**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *ajāśva* — O Pūṣan; *naḥ* — our; *asyāḥ sātaye* — for receiving this (praise or offering); *aheḷamānaḥ* — without anger (without disregard); *rarivān* — liberally giving; *su* — well; *upa bhuvaḥ* — be near us; *ajāśva* — O Pūṣan; *śravasyatām* — of us who desire food; *su* — … be close by; *dasma* — destroyer of foes, Pūṣan; *tvā* — you; *sādhubhiḥ* — to please you; *stomebhiḥ* — with hymns; *o ṣu* — well (taking refuge, restraining); *vavṛtīmahi* — (continued on p. 32).

### Printed p. 32  (PDF 50)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 138".)*

*(Pratipadārtha, concluded.)* *vavṛtīmahi* — we obtain (your) support; (and) *āghṛṇe* — O Pūṣan, who rain all around, or who accept the oblation; *nahi atimanye* — I surely do not disregard you; *te* — your; *sakhyam* — friendship; *na apahnuve* — I do not neglect and cast away (do not lose).

**Bhāvārtha.** O Pūṣan, whose steeds are goats [?], be near us, free from disregard and liberal in giving, to accept our worship; be near us who desire food. O destroyer of foes, with hymns able to please you we seek your support on every side. O Pūṣan, giver of rain, I surely do not disregard you; and I do not neglect your friendship or lose it.

**English Translation (as printed).** Free from anger, and liberal of gifts, be near to us, Ajaswa, for the acceptance of this our (offering); be near to those, Ajaswa, who solicit food: we have recourse to you, destroyer of enemies, with pious hymns. I never cease, Pushan, accepter of offerings, to think of you; I never disregard your friendship.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

***ajāśva.*** हरी इन्द्रस्य । रोहितौ अग्नेः । अजाः पूष्णः [?] (*harī indrasya | rohitau agneḥ | ajāḥ pūṣṇaḥ [?]*) (Ni. 2-[?]) — in this way Yāska lists in order the vehicles of Indra and the other gods; *ajāśva* means Pūṣan, whose vehicle is the goat. Explaining the present Ṛk, Yāska shows that *asyā naḥ sātaye upabhuvaḥ*, *aheḷamāno 'krudhyan*, *ririvān* (*rātiḥ* …) etc. are addressed to *ajāśva* [?]; the Kannada says that in this way he has said that Pūṣan, with the goats as his steeds, is so addressed. *Ririvān*: Yāska explains the word: the root *rā* of giving, reduplicated (that is, doubled), becomes *ririvān*; "one who gives liberally" is the sense (Ni. 4-[?]).

***dasma.*** *Śatrūṇām upakṣayitā* — "destroyer of foes"; Pūṣan is so addressed. The word *dasma* has two senses: one, destroyer of foes; the other, "beautiful" … (continues on p. 33).

### Printed p. 33  (PDF 51)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga numeral unclear.)*

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 4, continued from p. 32.)* [*dasma*, continued:] …"one possessing beauty" is the other sense. Derived from the root *dasi darśanadaṃśanayoḥ* the word means "worth seeing, charming"; derived from *dasu upakṣaye* it means "destroyer (of foes)". Since gods such as Indra possess both kinds of power, it is shown that *dasma* may be taken in either of the two senses. For example:

> जुजोषदिन्द्रो दस्मवर्चा नासत्येव सुग्म्यो रथेषाः [?] ।

> *jujoṣadindro dasmavarcā nāsatyeva sugmyo ratheṣāḥ [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] [?].)

> त्वं भगो न आ हि रत्नमिषे परिज्मेव क्षयसि दस्मवर्चाः [?] ।

> *tvaṃ bhago na ā hi ratnamiṣe parijmeva kṣayasi dasmavarcāḥ [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?] [?].)

> पूषा सुबन्धुर्दिव आ पृथिव्या इळस्पतिर्मघवा दस्मवर्चाः [?] ।

> *pūṣā subandhurdiva ā pṛthivyā iḷaspatirmaghavā dasmavarcāḥ [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?] [?].) In such Ṛks, in the first place *śatrūpakṣayaṇabalaḥ* — "one whose strength destroys foes"; in the second, *varcaḥ* is a name for form: *dasmaṃ darśanīyaṃ varcaḥ yasya tādṛśaḥ* — "one whose form is charming", is shown to be the sense. As the adjective *dasma* is applied in many places of the Ṛksaṃhitā to Indra and other gods, in the Ṛk at hand it is applied to Pūṣan, describing his foe-destroying power and his lovely form.

***āghṛṇe.*** *Sarvato vṛṣṭeḥ kṣārayituḥ*; or *haviṣām āhartaḥ svīkartaḥ* — Sāyaṇa explains that Pūṣan is addressed as "one who pours down rain on all sides" or "one who receives oblations". That Pūṣan has this epithet is a matter of discussion among critics. His qualities are of many kinds, and as they show various aspects of his nature it is hard to decide what his original nature is; for recent critics it is a difficult question. Yāska counts Pūṣan among the gods of the sky region [sic, *dyusthāna*]; the scholar Bloomfield, following Yāska, on the strength of the epithet *āghṛṇi* in Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?], 6-[?]-[?], 6-[?]-[?] and the like, maintains that Pūṣan is the Sun who gives light. Some oppose this: they say the word *āghṛṇi* relates only to radiance and may be used of any radiant deity, with no rule that it must be the Sun; for example in Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?] [?] it is also an epithet of Agni; so from this one epithet it cannot be decided that Pūṣan is the Sun. Yāska, the author of the Bṛhaddevatā and other followers of the Vedic tradition (continued on p. 34)

### Printed p. 34  (PDF 52)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 138".)*

…have shown clearly that *āghṛṇi* is an epithet showing only Pūṣan's distinction. Yāska, giving the derivation of the word in the Nirukta, explains *āgatahṛṇiḥ* ("one whose *hṛṇi* has come") and cites the Ṛk in which the word occurs:

> एहि वां विमुचो नपादाघृणे सं सचावहै । रथीर्ऋतस्य नो भव [?] ॥

> *ehi vāṃ vimuco napādāghṛṇe saṃ sacāvahai | rathīrṛtasya no bhava [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?] [?].) The Kannada says: *hṛṇi* is read both among words for radiance (Ni. 3-[?]) and among names of anger (Ni. 2-[?]); so Durgācārya, commenting on the word, says *āghṛṇi-śabdo dīptivācakaḥ; dīptikarmasu ca paṭhito vinā 'yaṃ hṛṇiḥ iti* ("the word *āghṛṇi* means radiance; *hṛṇi* is read among words of radiance") — "radiant" is one sense — and *krodho 'pi hṛṇir ity ucyate* ("anger too is called *hṛṇi*"), so another sense is possible: "the one whose wrath is directed at us — may we appease him". In sum, it is an epithet showing Pūṣan's distinction. The authors of the Bṛhaddevatā, in the verses

> त्रैको विश्वेषां देवानां पूष्ण आघृणये त्र्यचे [?] । [… rest of the quotation not legible at this resolution …] ॥

> *traiko viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ pūṣṇa āghṛṇaye tryace [?] | [… rest of the quotation not legible at this resolution …] ‖*

(Bṛ. De. [?]-[?]-[?] [?]) show that because a leather bag filled with *ghṛṇi* (an intoxicating substance) is tied to his chariot he is called *āghṛṇi*, and that the poets, singers of praise, therefore praised Pūṣan as *āghṛṇi*. Sāyaṇa gives the sense given above — *vṛṣṭeḥ kṣārayituḥ* or *haviṣām āhartuḥ* — only in the present Ṛk, but in all the other Ṛks where the word occurs (3-[?]-[?], 6-[?]-[?] and others) he explains it as *āgate dīpte pūṣan*. In 6-[?]-[?] alone is the epithet used of Agni; elsewhere it is always Pūṣan's, and shows his distinction.

## Sūkta 139

### Printed p. 36 (continued; PDF 54)

*(The Kannada heading reads "The 139th Sūkta".)*

*(Anukramaṇī, Sanskrit; not rendered in English. Gist: "Astu śrauṣaṭ", the sixth sūkta of the twentieth anuvāka, has eleven Ṛks; Parucchepa is the ṛṣi; Viśvedevāḥ the deity of the whole sūkta, with separate deities for individual Ṛks; the last Ṛk is Triṣṭubh, the fifth Bṛhatī, the rest Atyaṣṭi; its use in the Daśarātra rite is cited from the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra. Small type; doubtful words marked.)*

> अस्तु श्रौषडेकादशर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तम् । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । अस्तु श्रौषळेकादश वैश्वदेवो मैत्रावरुणाश्विनस्तिस्र ऐन्द्राग्नेय [?] बार्हस्पत्या वैश्वदेव्यन्त्या त्रिष्टुप्पञ्चमी बृहती वैश्वदेवमेतदेवमनुन्नासामि [?] सूक्तप्रयोगे वैश्वदेवत्वं सूक्तभेदप्रयोगे यल्लिङ्गं सा देवतेति । परुच्छेप ऋषिः । अन्त्या त्रिष्टुप् पञ्चमी बृहती । अन्या अत्यष्टयो निशेषाभावात् [?] । कृत्स्नं सूक्तं वैश्वदेवम् । तत्राद्यायां विश्वे देवा देवता । द्वितीयाया मित्रावरुणौ । अथ तिस्रोऽश्विदेवताकाः । ऐन्द्री षष्ठी । सप्तम्याग्नेयी । अष्टमी मारुती । नवम्यैन्द्राग्नी । दशमी बार्हस्पत्या । एकादशी वैश्वदेवी । सूक्तविनियोगो लैङ्गिकः । दशरात्रस्य षष्ठेऽहनि प्रउगशस्त्र आद्यं वैश्वदेवं तृचे प्रथमा षष्ठस्येति खण्डे सूत्रम् । अस्तु श्रौषळो सू नो अग्ने । आ. [?] इति ॥

> *astu śrauṣaḍekādaśarcaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ sūktam | atrānukramaṇikā | astu śrauṣaḷekādaśa vaiśvadevo maitrāvaruṇāśvinastisra aindrāgneya [?] bārhaspatyā vaiśvadevyantyā triṣṭuppañcamī bṛhatī vaiśvadevametadevamanunnāsāmi [?] sūktaprayoge vaiśvadevatvaṃ sūktabhedaprayoge yalliṅgaṃ sā devateti | parucchepa ṛṣiḥ | antyā triṣṭup pañcamī bṛhatī | anyā atyaṣṭayo niśeṣābhāvāt [?] | kṛtsnaṃ sūktaṃ vaiśvadevam | tatrādyāyāṃ viśve devā devatā | dvitīyāyā mitrāvaruṇau | atha tisro 'śvidevatākāḥ | aindrī ṣaṣṭhī | saptamyāgneyī | aṣṭamī mārutī | navamyaindrāgnī | daśamī bārhaspatyā | ekādaśī vaiśvadevī | sūktaviniyogo laiṅgikaḥ | daśarātrasya ṣaṣṭhe 'hani praugaśastra ādyaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ tṛce prathamā ṣaṣṭhasyeti khaṇḍe sūtram | astu śrauṣaḷo sū no agne | ā. [?] iti ‖*

*Anuvāda (Kannada).* The sūkta "*Astu śrauṣaṭ*" is the sixth sūkta in the twentieth anuvāka; it has eleven Ṛks. The Anukramaṇī says what is quoted above. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Parucchepa. The last Ṛk has the metre Triṣṭubh; the fifth is Bṛhatī; the other Ṛks are of the metre called Atyaṣṭi. For the whole sūkta, taken together, the deities are the Viśvedevas. Taken separately: the first Ṛk has the Viśvedevas as deity; the second, Mitra and Varuṇa; the next three Ṛks have the Aśvins; the sixth, Indra; the seventh, Agni; the eighth, the Maruts; the ninth, Indra and Agni; the tenth, Bṛhaspati; the eleventh, the Viśvedevas. The application (*viniyoga*) of the sūkta is *laiṅgika* (by the indication of the text). Though on the whole the sūkta is addressed to the Viśvedevas, a separate application is stated for each Ṛk in relation to its deity. In the sacrifice called *Daśarātra*, performed over ten days, on the sixth day, when the *Praüga-śastra* is recited, a *tṛca* (triplet) addressed to the Viśvedevas is recited; that the first Ṛk of this sūkta is so applied is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, in the section beginning *ṣaṣṭhasya*, by the sūtra *astu śrauṣaḷ… sū no agne* (continued on p. 37).

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** (*aham* — I); *puraḥ* — in front, on the northern altar; *agnim* — the Āhavanīya-form Agni; *dadhe* — I have established; *divyam* — born in the heavenly world; *tat śardhaḥ* — that Agni-power (the Agni with power), or the power that is the combined form of the Maruts; *nu* — quickly (we); *ā vṛṇīmahe* — we resort to, with worship; *indravāyū* — Indra and Vāyu; *vṛṇīmahe* — we serve; *yat ha* — which (cause of our devotion); *vivasvati* — in the radiant; *nābhā* — at the navel of the earth, the altar, or at the sacrifice which is the navel of the world; *navyasī* — (our) fresh praise; *krāṇā* — doing, making its own light known; *saṃdāyi* — (offered to the gods) the speed… (continued on p. 39).

### Printed p. 39  (PDF 57)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

*(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 1, concluded.)* *… (of that Agni)*; *astu śrauṣaṭ* — may our praise be heard by all the gods; *adha* — thereafter; *naḥ dhītayaḥ* — our praise-acts; *pra su upa yantu* — may they go well and in order to the gods; (*naḥ*) *dhītayaḥ* — our sacrificial rites also; *devān* — Agni and the other gods; *acchā na* — going towards them, may they reach them.

**Bhāvārtha.** I have established Agni, of the Āhavanīya form, on the northern altar in front. Let us resort to that divine might of Agni; likewise let us resort to Indra and Vāyu. Because we, full of devotion, have offered our fresh praise at this sacrifice, which is the navel of the earth, may this our praise reach the ears of the gods. May our praise-acts and the other rites of sacrifice go and reach the gods with the utmost faith.

**English Translation (as printed).** May our prayers be heard. I place before (me) Agni with reverence; we have recourse to his celestial might; we have recourse to Indra and to Vayu: which doing, a new (hymn) has been addressed (by us) to the radiant navel (of the earth); and thereupon may our pious rites attain the gods; may our pious rites attain the presence of the gods.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

***tac chardhaḥ.*** *Tādṛśaṃ balavantaṃ vā agniṃ; yadvā tac chardhaḥ tādṛśaṃ marutāṃ svarūpaṃ balam* — Sāyaṇa shows two senses to be possible: the powerful Agni, or the natural, collective power of the Maruts. The word *śardha* is read among the names of strength (Ni. 2-[?]); ordinarily it is used of the Maruts, meaning the power of their company. From such statements as

> सप्त सप्त हि मारुतो गणस्तस्मान्मारुतः सप्तकपालः [?] ।

> *sapta sapta hi māruto gaṇastasmānmārutaḥ saptakapālaḥ [?] |*

(Śa. Brā. 3-[?]-[?]-[?] [?])

> सप्त सप्त हि मारुतो गणः सर्वमेव्येतेन रथं प्रीणाति [?] ।

> *sapta sapta hi māruto gaṇaḥ sarvamevyetena rathaṃ prīṇāti [?] |*

(Śa. Brā. 5-[?]-[?]-[?] [?]) it is known that the Maruts always keep in a band; in such a band a kind of victorious power is natural. The word *śardhaḥ* is also used in the masculine; in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?]; 1-[?]-[?]; 6-[?]-[?] and others it is *a*-ending (continued on p. 40).

### Printed p. 40  (PDF 58)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 139".)*

…and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] and others it is *s*-ending [?]. Though the word is ordinarily used of the Maruts, it sometimes denotes the company of other gods as well:

> शृणोतु नो दैव्यं शर्धो अग्निः शृण्वन्तु विश्वे महिषा अमूराः [?] ।

> *śṛṇotu no daivyaṃ śardho agniḥ śṛṇvantu viśve mahiṣā amūrāḥ [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?] [?].)

> स आ वह देवताति यविष्ठ शर्धो यदद्य दिव्यं यजासि [?] ।

> *sa ā vaha devatāti yaviṣṭha śardho yadadya divyaṃ yajāsi [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?] [?].) Everywhere *daivyaṃ śardhaḥ*, *divyaṃ śardhaḥ* means the collective power consisting of gods. In the same way the word is used when speaking of an ordinary, worldly company. For example

> तं वः शर्धं रथानां त्वेषं गणं मारुतं नव्यसीनाम् [?] ।

> *taṃ vaḥ śardhaṃ rathānāṃ tveṣaṃ gaṇaṃ mārutaṃ navyasīnām [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-[?]-[?] [?]) where it means the collective power of chariots; and

> अवासां मघवञ्जहि शर्धो यातुमतीनाम् [?] ।

> *avāsāṃ maghavañjahi śardho yātumatīnām [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] [?]) where it also means the power of weapons, or of harmful beings. In the Ṛk at hand it means Agni's power or the Maruts' power.

***nābhā.*** *Bhūmyā nābhisthāne devayajane vedirūpe* — the place of sacrifice that is the navel-place of the earth and has the form of an altar; or *nābhau sarvaphalasya saṃbandhake yajñe* — the sacrifice that gives every fruit: Sāyaṇa explains both. With

> विश्वायुरसि पृथिवीं दृंह ध्रुवक्षिदसि [?] ।

> *viśvāyurasi pṛthivīṃ dṛṃha dhruvakṣidasi [?] |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] [?]) the northern altar is praised, so the first sense fits; and if "sacrifice" is meant, that sense too is supported by

> इयं वेदिः परो अन्तः पृथिव्या अयं यज्ञो भुवनस्य नाभिः [?] ।

> *iyaṃ vediḥ paro antaḥ pṛthivyā ayaṃ yajño bhuvanasya nābhiḥ [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-[?] [?])

> यज्ञमाहुर्भुवनस्य नाभिम् [?] ।

> *yajñamāhurbhuvanasya nābhim [?] |*

(Tai. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?] [?]) and similar texts of the Saṃhitā. Either sense may be given.

***vivasvati.*** *Dīptimati* — "radiant"; an epithet of *nābhā*. The word *vivasvat* is used in the Ṛksaṃhitā in different senses: besides "possessing radiance" and "man", it is also a proper name of a person (continued on p. 41).

### Printed p. 44  (PDF 62)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 139".)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *mitrāvaruṇau* — O Mitra and Varuṇa; *svena manyunā* — by your own greatness; *dakṣasya* — of the capable; *svena* — your own; *manyunā* — by the mighty power of the mind; *ṛtāt* — from the sun; *anṛtam* — the water that dries away and is unenduring; *tat* — that well-known; *yat ha* — for which reason; *adhi* — abundantly; *ādadāthe* — you bring (from it); *yuvoḥ* — your two; *hiraṇyayam* — golden-formed; *itthā* — in this manner; *sadmasu* — in the sacrificial halls; *dhībhiḥ* — by rites directed to you; *manasā cana* — by a mind attached (to you); *svebhir akṣabhiḥ* — by our own eyes and other senses, with no attention elsewhere; *apaśyāma* — we behold, with a fixed gaze; *svebhiḥ akṣabhiḥ* — by our own eyes and other senses; *somasya* — also the Soma (that is to be offered to you) (we behold).

**Bhāvārtha.** O Mitra and Varuṇa, by your own capable might you bring down abundantly the water that is in the world of the sun and, when it is poured on the earth, dries away and is unenduring; therefore we behold you, through our sacrifices and the like, with a mind attached to you alone and with our eyes and other senses fixed on nothing else. And we attend to the Soma that is to be offered to you.

**English Translation (as printed).** Mitra and Varuna, bestow (upon us) abundantly that unenduring water which you obtain from the sun, through your own energy; through the inherent energy of the vigorous: may we thus behold your golden (forms) in our balls [sic] of sacrifice, (brought thither) by our sacred rites, and by our thoughts and senses (intent upon you); by our senses (intent upon offering) the Soma libation.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

***ṛtād adhy anṛtam ādadāthe.*** *Ṛtāt* — from the sun (*ādityāt*); *anṛtam* — *śoṣaṇasvabhāvam*, "of the nature of drying up" (water). Sāyaṇa takes the word *ṛta* as the sun and *anṛta* as water; he explains that the epithet *anṛta* shows the impermanent state of water. The Kannada notes that the word *ṛta* reflects a principle that signifies the physical and moral order of the universe, as was said briefly earlier (in the Pīṭhike of Part [?] [?]). These two orders of Mitra and Varuṇa (continued on p. 45).

### Printed p. 45  (PDF 63)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued from p. 44.)* …[these two orders] are carried out by them is explained later, in the sūkta addressed to Mitra and Varuṇa themselves. Here one must understand how Mitra and Varuṇa obtained the *anṛta* from the *ṛta* and how they supplied it to the world.

Here *ṛta* may be said to mean "that which has an eternal state", and *anṛta* "that which has a non-eternal state, since water dries up and disappears". As the Upaniṣads and others say, *satya* and *anṛta* also mean "true" and "untrue". In this Ṛk *ṛta* also means the orb of the sun, which has an eternal state: in the Ṛksaṃhitā it is customary to call the radiant orb, which keeps to its rule in moving through the quarters of the sky, *ṛta*.

> द्वादशारं नहि तज्जराय वर्वर्ति चक्रं परि द्यामृतस्य ।
> आ पुत्रा अग्ने मिथुनासो अत्र सप्त शतानि विंशतिश्च तस्थुः [?] ॥

> *dvādaśāraṃ nahi tajjarāya varvarti cakraṃ pari dyāmṛtasya |*
> *ā putrā agne mithunāso atra sapta śatāni viṃśatiśca tasthuḥ [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-11.) The wheel of *ṛta* with twelve spokes revolves round the sky; the description that its seven hundred and twenty sons stand in pairs, each occupying its place, indicates the twelve spokes as twelve months and the 360 days and nights [as printed]. It is described, with other examples, how Uṣas too follows this path of *ṛta* by rule, without a break. To show the relation between the sun and this wheel of *ṛta*, it is fitting in the Ṛk at hand to take *ṛta* as the sun.

> अदर्शि गातुरुरवे वरीयसी पन्था ऋतस्य समयंस्त रश्मिभिश्चक्षुर्भगस्य रश्मिभिः [?] ।

> *adarśi gātururave varīyasī panthā ṛtasya samayaṃsta raśmibhiścakṣurbhagasya raśmibhiḥ [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] [?].) In the description that for the sun, of vast form, the still wider path of *ṛta* is made with the help of his rays, the wide path of *ṛta* in the sky is indicated. This same path of *ṛta*

> अग्निर्गन्धर्वीं पथ्यामृतस्य [?] … आ निषत्ता [?] ।

> *agnirgandharvīṃ pathyāmṛtasya [?] … ā niṣattā [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?] [?]) is described as the very lofty, wide *gandharva*-path. And

> उरु त्यच्चक्षुर्महि मित्रयोरा [?] एति प्रियं वरुणयोरदब्धम् ।
> ऋतस्य शुचि दर्शतमनीकं रुक्मो न दिव उदिता व्यद्यौत् [?] ।

> *uru tyaccakṣurmahi mitrayorā [?] eti priyaṃ varuṇayoradabdham |*
> *ṛtasya śuci darśatamanīkaṃ rukmo na diva uditā vyadyaut [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?])

> ऋतस्य पदे अधि दीद्यानं गुहा रघुष्यद्रघुयद्विवेद [?] ।

> *ṛtasya pade adhi dīdyānaṃ guhā raghuṣyadraghuyadviveda [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?] [?]) (continued on p. 46).

### Printed p. 46  (PDF 64)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 139".)*

In these Ṛks the sun, rising at the "face" of *ṛta* (in the sky), shines most beautifully; and in

> परि श्रिता पितरा पूर्वजावरी ऋतस्य योना क्षयतः समोकसा [?] ।
> द्यावापृथिवी वरुणाय सव्रते घृतवत्पयो महिषाय पिन्वतः [?] ॥

> *pari śritā pitarā pūrvajāvarī ṛtasya yonā kṣayataḥ samokasā [?] |*
> *dyāvāpṛthivī varuṇāya savrate ghṛtavatpayo mahiṣāya pinvataḥ [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?] [?]) it is described that the sun moves in the middle, the "womb" of *ṛta*, looking upon heaven and earth. Likewise in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-[?], 10-[?]-[?] and others, the sun is described as shining in the region of *ṛta*. Therefore in this Ṛk *ṛtāt* means "from the sun in the orb of *ṛta*".

But that *anṛta* here is an epithet of water is a point worth some thought. The word *ṛta* is read among the names of water in the Nirukta (Ni. [?]-[?]); in the Ṛksaṃhitā too, in about twenty Ṛks, *ṛta* means water. So how does *anṛta* come to mean water here? If *ṛta* is taken as "truth", the view of some philosophers that water is the first principle of the universe is understood as "water, which is of the nature of truth". In the Nirukta the words *ṛtam*, *yoniḥ*, *ṛtasya yoniḥ*, *satyam*, *nīram* are all put together among the names of water. And water, whose nature is to sink away in streams and the like, is impermanent and so momentary in its form of truth. Therefore Sāyaṇa explains *anṛtaṃ naśvaraṃ śoṣaṇasvabhāvam*. The sense is: Mitra and Varuṇa, taking the water, here called *anṛta*, from the sun, here called *ṛta*, poured it on the world.

***manyunā.*** The word *manyu* is used in the Ṛksaṃhitā in two or three senses. In the Nirukta the word is explained: *manyur manyater dīptikarmaṇaḥ krodhakarmaṇo vadhakarmaṇo vā* (Ni. 10-[?]) — from the root *man* meaning shining, or being angry, or smiting. Here *svena manyunā* means "by their own radiance, by their own power".

> वर्धयेतामोषधीः पिन्वतं गा अव वृष्टिं सृजतं जीरदानू [?] ।
> चित्रेभिरभ्रैरुप तिष्ठथो रवं द्यां वर्षयथो असुरस्य मायया [?] ।

> *vardhayetāmoṣadhīḥ pinvataṃ gā ava vṛṣṭiṃ sṛjataṃ jīradānū [?] |*
> *citrebhirabhrairupa tiṣṭhatho ravaṃ dyāṃ varṣayatho asurasya māyayā [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-[?]-[?] [?]) (continued on p. 47).

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?] [?]) as said in this Ṛk, Dakṣa's power also abides in Mitra and Varuṇa; since this is proper, it may also be taken as "by the *manyu* related to Dakṣa".

***hiraṇyayam.*** *Hiraṇyarūpam* — "having a golden form".

[?]-[?]) | aśvino rathasya madhupūrṇatvaṃ trayyāḥ pavayo madhupātrāḥ [?] (ṛ. 1-[?]-[?]) ityādiṣu prasiddham | kiñca tādṛśe hiraṇyaye rathe madhuraṃ havirvāhanamiti śeṣaḥ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *aśvinā* — O Aśvins; *yuvām* — you; *stomebhiḥ* — with hymns; *devayantaḥ* — desiring to win (you); *yuvām* — you; *havyā* — with oblations in the form of ghee and the like; *abhi āyavaḥ* — approaching; *āyavaḥ* — men; *ślokam* — praise-words (that praise you); *āśrāvayanta iva* — recite as if making them fall upon your ears; (then) *viśvavedasā* — O Aśvins, lords of all wealth; *yuvoḥ* — belonging to you; *viśvā śriyaḥ* — all riches; *pṛkṣaḥ ca* — and also food; *adhi* — in great measure (they enjoy); *dasrā* — O Aśvins, destroyers of foes; *vām* — your; *hiraṇyaye rathe* — in the golden chariot; *pavayaḥ* — the wheels of the chariot; *pruṣāyante* — let drip honey; *hiraṇyaye* — in that golden chariot, of wondrous work (carrying the oblation, come and go).

**Bhāvārtha.** O Aśvins, the sacrificers who wish to win you with hymns offer you oblations, approach you, and recite the hymns that praise you so that they fall upon your ears. O Aśvins, lords of all wealth, your worshippers who have praised you enjoy all the wealth and food that belongs to you. In your golden chariot, joined with fellies that make honey flow, full of honey and of wondrous work, come and carry off the oblation offered by us.

### Printed p. 50  (PDF 68)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 139".)*

**English Translation (as printed).** Aswins, men who desire to glorify you with (their) hymns, cause, as it were, their praises to be heard, propitiating you with oblations; for, from you, who are possessed of all opulence, (they obtain) every kind of wealth and abundant food. Dasras, the fellies (of the wheels) of your honey-laden car drop honey, (carried) in your golden (car).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

***stomebhiḥ.*** By the sentence एकं साम तृचे क्रियते तस्य च तृचस्यावृत्त्या ऋचां संख्या वर्धनीया भवति या स्तोमशब्देनोच्यते [?] (*ekaṃ sāma tṛce kriyate tasya ca tṛcasyāvṛttyā ṛcāṃ saṃkhyā vardhanīyā bhavati yā stomaśabdenocyate [?]*) the characteristic of the *stoma* is told. Among *stomas* there are nine kinds — *trivṛt*, *pañcadaśa*, *saptadaśa*, *ekaviṃśa*, *caturviṃśa*, *triṇava*, *trayastriṃśa*, *catuścatvāriṃśa*, *aṣṭācatvāriṃśa* — which, with their *viṣṭutis*, have been set out very fully in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, Part [?], pp. [?]–[?] (as printed "13th part, pp. 131–136" [?]); so here only the benefits to be obtained by reciting those *stomas* are told.

Of the *stomas*, the nine kinds mentioned above can be increased by sub-varieties such as *trayodaśa*, *caturdaśa*, *ṣoḍaśa*. For example:

> वसवस्त्रयोदशाक्षरेण त्रयोदशग्ं स्तोममुदजयन् [?] उद्राक्षश्चतुर्दशाक्षरेण चतुर्दशग्ं स्तोममुदजयन्नादित्याः पञ्चदशाक्षरेण पञ्चदशग्ं स्तोममुदजयन्नदितिः षोडशाक्षरेण षोडशग्ं स्तोममुदजयत् प्रजापतिः सप्तदशाक्षरेण सप्तदशग्ं स्तोममुदजयत् [?] ।

> *vasavastrayodaśākṣareṇa trayodaśagṃ stomamudajayan [?] udrākṣaścaturdaśākṣareṇa caturdaśagṃ stomamudajayannādityāḥ pañcadaśākṣareṇa pañcadaśagṃ stomamudajayannaditiḥ ṣoḍaśākṣareṇa ṣoḍaśagṃ stomamudajayat prajāpatiḥ saptadaśākṣareṇa saptadaśagṃ stomamudajayat [?] |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?]-[?] [?].) From these Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentences the order in which the Vasus, Rudras [?], Ādityas, Aditi and Prajāpati won the *stomas* of thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen and seventeen is told. The power of the *stomas* is very great, and that by reciting them all desired ends may be attained is made clear in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā itself:

> प्रातःसवने वै गायत्रेण छन्दसा त्रिवृते स्तोमाय ज्योतिर्दधेति त्रिवृता ब्रह्मवर्चसेन पञ्चदशाय ज्योतिर्दधाति पञ्चदशेनोजसा वीर्येण सप्तदशाय ज्योतिर्दधाति सप्तदशेन प्राजापत्यैन प्रजननेनैकविंशाय ज्योतिर्दधाति स्तोम एव तत्स्तोमाय ज्योतिर्दधात्यथो स्तोम एव स्तोममभि प्रणयति यावन्तो वै स्तोमास्तावन्तः कामास्तावन्तो [?] …

> *prātaḥsavane vai gāyatreṇa chandasā trivṛte stomāya jyotirdadheti trivṛtā brahmavarcasena pañcadaśāya jyotirdadhāti pañcadaśenojasā vīryeṇa saptadaśāya jyotirdadhāti saptadaśena prājāpatyaina prajananenaikaviṃśāya jyotirdadhāti stoma eva tatstomāya jyotirdadhātyatho stoma eva stomamabhi praṇayati yāvanto vai stomāstāvantaḥ kāmāstāvanto [?] …*

(Tai. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?]-[?] [?]; the quotation runs on to p. 51.)

### Printed p. 51  (PDF 69)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

*(The Taittirīya Saṃhitā quotation on the powers of the* stomas*, concluded from p. 50.)*

> लोकास्तावन्ति ज्योतींष्यावते वै स्तोमा एतावतः कामा एतावन्तो लोका एतावन्ति ज्योतींष्यवरुन्धे [?] ।

> *lokāstāvanti jyotīṃṣyāvate vai stomā etāvataḥ kāmā etāvanto lokā etāvanti jyotīṃṣyavarundhe [?] |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?]-[?] [?].) These sentences show the powers of the four kinds of *stoma* used in the Agniṣṭoma. At the morning pressing the sacrificer, by the *trivṛt* *stoma* in the Gāyatrī metre, is placed in a place of greatness [?]. In the same way, by the *trivṛt*, which is of the nature of light, he makes the *pañcadaśa* *stoma* [rich in light]; by the *pañcadaśa*, which is full of vigour, the *saptadaśa*; by the *saptadaśa*, which is connected with Prajāpati and makes for procreation, the *ekaviṃśa* — he makes them radiant. So each kind of *stoma* gives power and radiance to another kind. As many kinds as there are of *stoma*, so many are the worlds, so many the kinds of radiance, so many the kinds of desired ends; and the sacrificer, by reciting the *stomas*, obtains so many worlds, radiances and desired ends. Having told the power of the *stoma*, the text goes on to tell the loss that comes from not reciting it:

> ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति स त्वै [?] यजेत योऽग्निष्टोमेन यजमानोऽथ सर्वस्तोमेन यजेतेति यस्य त्रिवृतमन्तर्यन्ति प्राणांस्तस्यान्तर्यन्ति प्राणेषु मेऽस्यसदिति [?] खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यस्य पञ्चदशमन्तर्यन्ति वीर्यं तस्यान्तर्यन्ति वीर्ये मेऽस्यसदिति खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यस्य सप्तदशमन्तर्यन्ति प्रजां तस्यान्तर्यन्ति प्रजायां मेऽस्यसदिति खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यस्यैकविंशमन्तर्यन्ति प्रतिष्ठां तस्यान्तर्यन्ति प्रतिष्ठायां मेऽस्यसदिति खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यस्य त्रिणवमन्तर्यन्ति [?] ऋतुषु मेऽस्यसन्नक्षत्रियां च विराजं च [?] खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यस्य त्रयस्त्रिंशमन्तर्यन्ति देवतास्तस्यान्तर्यन्ति देवतासु मेऽस्यसदिति खलु वै यज्ञेन यजमानो यजते यो वै स्तोमानां परमतां गच्छन्तं वेद परमतामेव गच्छति त्रिवृद्वै स्तोमानामवमस्त्रिवृत्परमो य एवं वेद परमतामेव गच्छति [?] ।

> *brahmavādino vadanti sa tvai [?] yajeta yo 'gniṣṭomena yajamāno 'tha sarvastomena yajeteti yasya trivṛtamantaryanti prāṇāṃstasyāntaryanti prāṇeṣu me 'syasaditi [?] khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yasya pañcadaśamantaryanti vīryaṃ tasyāntaryanti vīrye me 'syasaditi khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yasya saptadaśamantaryanti prajāṃ tasyāntaryanti prajāyāṃ me 'syasaditi khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yasyaikaviṃśamantaryanti pratiṣṭhāṃ tasyāntaryanti pratiṣṭhāyāṃ me 'syasaditi khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yasya triṇavamantaryanti [?] ṛtuṣu me 'syasannakṣatriyāṃ ca virājaṃ ca [?] khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yasya trayastriṃśamantaryanti devatāstasyāntaryanti devatāsu me 'syasaditi khalu vai yajñena yajamāno yajate yo vai stomānāṃ paramatāṃ gacchantaṃ veda paramatāmeva gacchati trivṛdvai stomānāmavamastrivṛtparamo ya evaṃ veda paramatāmeva gacchati [?] |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?] [?].) The scholars have ordained that those who sacrifice with the Agniṣṭoma should do so with every *stoma*. In this rule, if the *trivṛt* *stoma* is left out, the principal breath is lost; so the sacrificer performs the *trivṛt* *stoma* with the intention that this sacrifice may be included in his principal breath. In the same way, if the *pañcadaśa* *stoma* is left out, vigour is lost; if the *saptadaśa* (continued on p. 52)

### Printed p. 52  (PDF 70)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 139".)*

…is left out, progeny is lost; if the *ekaviṃśa* is left out, the very support of his life is torn away; if the *triṇava* is left out, the seasons and constellations that are there for his benefit and the powers of his foes are no longer helpful to his side; if the *trayastriṃśa* is left out, the presence of the chief deities is lacking. Hence the sacrificer performs the sacrifice with the *pañcadaśa* *stoma* for acquiring strength, with the *saptadaśa* for progeny, with the *ekaviṃśa* for support of life, with the *triṇava* for the benefit of the influence of the seasons and constellations, and with the recitation of the *trayastriṃśa* for the presence of his chief deities. The sacrificer who knows the greatness of the *trivṛt* *stoma*, which holds first place among all *stomas*, obtains the first place among sacrificers.

Likewise, describing the greatness of the *stomas* beginning with *trivṛt*, which must be recited in order on the six days of the *Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha* sacrifices:

> त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमो भवति तेज एवाव रुन्धे पञ्चदशो भवतीन्द्रियमेवाव रुन्धे सप्तदशो भवत्यन्नाद्यस्यावरुद्ध्या [?] अथो प्रैव तेन जायन्ते [?] एकविंशो भवति प्रतिष्ठित्यै [?] अथो [?] आत्मन्धत्ते [?] त्रिणवो भवति विजित्यै त्रयस्त्रिंशो भवति प्रतिष्ठित्यै [?] ।

> *trivṛdagniṣṭomo bhavati teja evāva rundhe pañcadaśo bhavatīndriyamevāva rundhe saptadaśo bhavatyannādyasyāvaruddhyā [?] atho praiva tena jāyante [?] ekaviṃśo bhavati pratiṣṭhityai [?] atho [?] ātmandhatte [?] triṇavo bhavati vijityai trayastriṃśo bhavati pratiṣṭhityai [?] |*

(Tai. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?] [?].) By the *trivṛt*-Agniṣṭoma *tejas*, by the *pañcadaśa* *indriya* [vigour], by the *saptadaśa* food and offspring, by the *ekaviṃśa* a firm footing, by the *triṇava* victory and by the *trayastriṃśa* firm establishment are obtained; the Kannada thus states the benefits of reciting the *stomas*. In the Upaniṣads too the greatness of the *stoma* is shown and the way it brings spiritual fruit:

> स्तोममहदुरुगायं प्रतिष्ठां दृष्ट्वा धीरो नचिकेतोऽत्यस्राक्षीः [?] ।

> *stomamahadurugāyaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhīro naciketo 'tyasrākṣīḥ [?] |*

(Kaṭha Up. [?]-[?]-[?] [?].) By this sentence the greatness of the *udgītha* and the spiritual way of attaining it are shown. In the Chāndogya Upaniṣad:

> येन छन्दसा स्तोष्यन् स्यात्तच्छन्द उपधावेदेन स्तोमेन स्तोष्यमाणः स्यात्तं स्तोममुपधावेत् [?] ।

> *yena chandasā stoṣyan syāttacchanda upadhāvedena stomena stoṣyamāṇaḥ syāttaṃ stomamupadhāvet [?] |*

(Chā. Up. [?]-[?]-[?] [?].) By this sentence, describing the greatness of the *udgītha*, it is ordained that one should meditate on that *stoma* by which, being of the right qualities [?], the *stotra* becomes complete. In the same way, in the sūkta at hand, *stomebhiḥ* means a *stotra* that is of the nature of song and gives exceeding benefit.

***devayantaḥ.*** *Yuvām ātmana icchantaḥ* — "wishing to have you, the gods, as our own", that is, wishing to obtain your complete regard.

***āyavaḥ.*** It has been told earlier that *āyu* may mean "men", "life", a particular deity representing life, or a proper name of a person. In this Ṛk it means "we men".

***pṛkṣaḥ.*** The word *pṛkṣa* means battle (Ni. 2-[?]), a swift horse, and food. Here it means abundant food.

***dasrā.*** *Śatrūṇām upakṣayitārau* or *darśanīyau* — "those whose power destroys foes" or "those of beautiful form"; the peculiarity of the name *dasra* was told earlier.

***pavayaḥ.*** The word *pavi* is read among the names of speech (Ni. 3-[?]) and of the thunderbolt (Ni. 2-[?]); besides, *pavi rathanemir bhavati yad vipunāti bhūmim* (Ni. [?]-[?]-[?]) — "the *pavi* is the felly of the chariot, because it scours the earth": Yāska takes it as the name of a chariot wheel, citing

> उते पव्या रथानामद्रिं भिन्दन्त्योजसा [?] ।

> *ute pavyā rathānāmadriṃ bhindantyojasā [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-[?]-[?] [?]) where he shows that *pavi* means the felly of a chariot; in the Ṛk at hand too the sense is the wheel of the Aśvins' chariot. Showing that *pavi* also means an arrow-head (*śalya*):

> पावीरवी तन्यतुरेकपादजो दिवो धर्ता सिन्धुरापः समुद्रियः [?] ।

> *pāvīravī tanyaturekapādajo divo dhartā sindhurāpaḥ samudriyaḥ [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?] [?]) — citing which, (Ni. [?]-[?]) *paviḥ śalyo bhavati yad vipunāti kāyaṃ tadvajraṃ pavīravān*: "the *pavi* is an arrow-head, because it pierces the body"; because Indra has it, he is called *pavīravān*; and he explains with

> यो जनान्महिषा इवातितस्थौ पवीरवान् । उतापवीरवान् युधा [?] ।

> *yo janānmahiṣā ivātitasthau pavīravān | utāpavīravān yudhā [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?] [?]) …he has cited this Ṛk.

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *dasrā* — O Aśvins; *acheti* — (your purpose) is made known (*acheti* means "it is known"); *nākam* — towards the heaven; *vi ṛṇvathaḥ* — you go; *diviṣṭiṣu* — (to the world of heaven) in the journeys heavenward, or in the sacrifice; *u* — ; *adhvasmānaḥ* — (not injured, i.e. unhurt) the horses; *vām* — your; *rathayujaḥ* — the charioteers; *diviṣṭiṣu* — for travelling to heaven; *yuñjate* — (harnessing the horses) fasten them to the chariot; *dasrā* — O Aśvins; *pātheva* — as on a road; *yantau* — going; *anuśāsatā* — punishing the foes; *rajaḥ* — to the heaven; *yantau* — going; *rajaḥ* — the water of the sky; *añjasā* — straightly; *śāsatā* — those who make [?] rain; *vām* — you; *bandhure* — with the three-shafted [?] and well-made; *hiraṇyaye* — golden; *rathe* — in the chariot; *adhi sthāma* — we place [you / mount] …

**Bhāvārtha.** O Aśvins, we make known your purpose: you are willing to go towards heaven. Unsupported in the sky, your charioteers yoke the car to the horses for your journey to heaven; and you, going by the excellent road, punishing the foes and sending the rain, we place you in your golden, three-shafted car.

**English Translation (as printed).** Dasras, your purpose is known: you would repair to heaven: your charioteers harness (your steeds) for your heavenward journey; the horses that injure not (the car) on your journey to heaven. We have placed you, Dasras, in your golden three-shafted chariot, going by an (easy) road to heaven, humiliators (of enemies), and principal regulators of the rain.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

***nākam; ṛṇvathaḥ.*** *Nākaṃ svargaṃ svargalokam* — "to the world of heaven; *ṛṇvathaḥ* you go and reach"; or *nākam* — "you come towards the sacrifice and reach it": Sāyaṇa has given two senses of *nāka*. That *nāka* means "sacrifice" by derivation of the word is seen to be a traditional sense; "heaven" is the sense in more common use. The word is also used as a synonym of the sun. The Nirukta-author classes the word among the *sādhāraṇa* ("common") names, and, explaining its sense as common, says *sādhāraṇāny uttarāṇi ṣaṭ dinasthādityaś ca* [?] … *dyuloke kyo…* (continues on p. 57).

[?]-[?]) — "*nāka* is the sun, the leader of lights, of radiances"; *ka* is a name for happiness, *a-ka* its absence, and *nāka* what is without the absence of happiness: "that which is free from unhappiness" is the sense. (Kāṭhaka Saṃ. [?]-[?]) and the sentence *na vā amuṃ lokaṃ gacchate kiñca nāsukhaṃ, puṇyakṛto hy eva tatra gacchanti* [?] — "no unhappiness goes to that world; only doers of good go there" — to show the meaning of *nāka*. In the Ṛksaṃhitā this word is used in some places as a synonym of the sun, in others of heaven:

> तिस्रः पृथिवीरुपरि प्रवा दिवो नाकं रक्षेथे द्युभिरक्तुभिर्हितम् ।

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-34-8 [?].)

> ये नाकस्याधि रोचने दिवि देवास आसते ।

> *ye nākasyādhi rocane divi devāsa āsate |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-19-6 [?].) In such Ṛks it is a synonym of the sun;

> *tve vardhanta svatavaso mahitvanā nākaṃ tasthururu cakrire sadaḥ [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].)

> ते ह नाकं महिमानः सचन्त यत्र पूर्वे साध्याः सन्ति देवाः ।

> *te ha nākaṃ mahimānaḥ sacanta yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ santi devāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-90-16 [?].) In such Ṛks it is also a synonym of heaven;

> वृषैव कपिलो भूत्वा यन्नाकमधिरोहति [?] ।

> *vṛṣaiva kapilo bhūtvā yannākamadhirohati [?] |*

(Bṛ. De. [?]-[?]) in this Bṛhaddevatā sentence it is plainly the sky (*antarikṣa*) [?];

> इतोऽसावादित्यो द्वाविंशेन परमादित्याज्जयति तन्नाकं तद्विशोकम् [?] ।

> *ito 'sāvādityo dvāviṃśena paramādityājjayati tannākaṃ tadviśokam [?] |*

(Chā. Up. [?]-[?]-[?] [?].) In this Chāndogya Upaniṣad sentence the world of heaven, free from sorrow, is said to be beyond the sun's world. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa and the Taittirīya Upaniṣad the name *Nāka* is also famous for the knower of Brahman, Mudgalaputra [?]; the sense is "free from sorrow".

### Printed p. 58  (PDF 76)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 139".)*

***rajaḥ.*** The word *rajaḥ* is repeated. Sāyaṇa takes the first *rajaḥ* as "heaven", which delights (*rañjanātmaka*), and the second as "water"; both senses have the Nirukta's support — *rajaḥ: rajo rajater jyotir vā raja ucyate; udakaṃ raja ucyate; lokā rajāṃsy ucyante* (Ni. [?]-[?]): the word *rajas*, derived from the root *rañj* ("to colour, to shine"), means light, water and the worlds. Besides, *ahas sragahane rajasī ucyete* [?] — it is also a synonym of "blood" and "day". Yāska cites

> रजांसि चित्रा वि चरन्ति तन्यवो दिवः संव्रजा पयसा न उक्षतम् [?] ।

> *rajāṃsi citrā vi caranti tanyavo divaḥ saṃvrajā payasā na ukṣatam [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?] [?]) and shows that *rajāṃsi* here means "worlds" (Ni. 11-[?]); and

> अज्मामुक्थै रहिं [?] गृणीषे बुध्ने नदीनां रजःसु षीदन् [?] ।

> *ajmāmukthai rahiṃ [?] gṛṇīṣe budhne nadīnāṃ rajaḥsu ṣīdan [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-[?]-[?] [?]) where *rajaḥsu* means "in the waters"; and

> पिता उ त्वा उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमञ्जते [?] ।

> *pitā u tvā uṣasaḥ ketumakrata pūrve ardhe rajaso bhānumañjate [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] [?]) where *rajasaḥ* is taken as the sky; and

> त्रीणि भाति रजांस्यस्य यत्त्राणि तु तेजसा [?] ।

> *trīṇi bhāti rajāṃsyasya yattrāṇi tu tejasā [?] |*

(Bṛ. De. [?]-[?]) where the Bṛhaddevatā author says that Viṣṇu, who took the three strides, made the three worlds shine with his feet, thus giving the sense of the word *rajāṃsi*. In the Ṛk at hand the first *rajaḥ* means the delightful sky, and the second the rain-water.

***hiraṇyaye rathe.*** *Hiraṇmaye madhupūrṇe rathe* — "in the golden chariot full of honey": a description of the Aśvins' chariot. Sāyaṇa cites

> त्रयः पवयो मधुवाहने रथे सोमस्य वेनामनु विश्व इद्विदुः [?] ।

> *trayaḥ pavayo madhuvāhane rathe somasya venāmanu viśva idviduḥ [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] [?]) to show that the Aśvins' chariot is described as full of honey.

***bandhure.*** *Bandhuratrayayukte* — the chariot with three seats [?] (or shafts). In Ṛks such as रथो यो वां त्रिबन्धुरः [?] (*ratho yo vāṃ tribandhuraḥ [?]*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?]) the Aśvins' chariot is described as having three *bandhuras*, so here too it is called a three-*bandhura* chariot.

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> शचीभिर्नः शचीवसू दिवा नक्तं दशस्यतम् ।
> मा वां रातिरुप दसत्कदा चनास्मद्रातिः कदा चन ॥ ५ ॥

> *śacībhirnaḥ śacīvasū divā naktaṃ daśasyatam |*
> *mā vāṃ rātirupa dasatkadā canāsmadrātiḥ kadā cana ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> शचीभिः । नः । शचीवसू इति शचीऽवसू । दिवा । नक्तम् । दशस्यतम् ।
> मा । वाम् । रातिः । उप । दसत् । कदा । चन । अस्मत् । रातिः । कदा । चन ॥ ५ ॥

> *śacībhiḥ | naḥ | śacīvasū iti śacī 'vasū | divā | naktam | daśasyatam |*
> *mā | vām | rātiḥ | upa | dasat | kadā | cana | asmat | rātiḥ | kadā | cana ‖ 5 ‖*

### Printed p. 61  (PDF 79)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

*(Gist, mine: Aśvins, whose wealth is our rites, give us by day and night the wealth that our rites deserve; may your gifts and ours never fail.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *O Aśvins, rich in our rites, by day and night give us what our rites deserve; may neither your gift nor ours ever fail.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> हे शचीवसू शचीति कर्मनाम । अस्मदनुष्ठितैर्ज्योतिष्टोमादिकर्मधनौ युवां शचीभिरस्मदीयैः कर्मभिः [?] निमित्तभूतैः अनुग्रहीतव्यम् [?] दिवा नक्तं दिने रात्रौ च दशस्यतम् [?] [… ] अभिमतं देयम् । वां युवयोः रातिर्दानं कदा चन सर्वदा मा उपदसत् मोपक्षीणं भूत् । उपक्षये दसु उपक्षये [?] । न केवलं युष्मदीयं दानमस्मदीयमपि [?] रातिर्दानं हविरादिप्रदानं सर्वदापि कदा चन सर्वदा मोप दसत् [?] । उपक्षीणं मा भूत् । सर्वदा वर्तेताम् [?] । अहमपि सर्वदा युष्मदर्थं [?] … मित्यर्थः ॥

> *he śacīvasū śacīti karmanāma | asmadanuṣṭhitairjyotiṣṭomādikarmadhanau yuvāṃ śacībhirasmadīyaiḥ karmabhiḥ [?] nimittabhūtaiḥ anugrahītavyam [?] divā naktaṃ dine rātrau ca daśasyatam [?] [… ] abhimataṃ deyam | vāṃ yuvayoḥ rātirdānaṃ kadā cana sarvadā mā upadasat mopakṣīṇaṃ bhūt | upakṣaye dasu upakṣaye [?] | na kevalaṃ yuṣmadīyaṃ dānamasmadīyamapi [?] rātirdānaṃ havirādipradānaṃ sarvadāpi kadā cana sarvadā mopa dasat [?] | upakṣīṇaṃ mā bhūt | sarvadā vartetām [?] | ahamapi sarvadā yuṣmadarthaṃ [?] … mityarthaḥ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *śacīvasū* — O Aśvins, whose wealth is the rites performed by us; *naḥ* — our; *śacībhiḥ* — on account of our rites (wealth that is to be bestowed as a favour); *divā naktam* — by day and by night (continuously); *daśasyatam* — give; *vām* — your (that is to be given by you); *rātiḥ* — gift; *kadā cana* — ever; *mā upa dasat* — let it not fail; *asmat* — from us (that is to be offered); *rātiḥ* — the gifts of oblations and the like also; *kadā cana* — ever (let them not cease).

**Bhāvārtha.** O Aśvins, whose wealth is the rites we perform, give us continuously, by day and by night, the wealth that is to be bestowed on account of our rites. May your gift never cease; and we, for our part, shall never cease to offer you oblations and other gifts.

**English Translation (as printed).** Enriched by holy rites, grant us, by day and night, (all good things) on account of our pious acts; never may your donation, never may our (donations) be witheld [sic].

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

***śacīvasū.*** *Śacīti karmanāma; asmadanuṣṭhitair jyotiṣṭomādikarmadhanau* — the Aśvins are addressed as "those whose wealth is the *jyotiṣṭoma* and other rites performed by us, the sacrificers". The oblations and the like offered in sacrifices are the gods' wealth, and in return they give wealth to the sacrificers; this is a mutual dependence (continued on p. 62).

### Printed p. 62  (PDF 80)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 139".)*

***mā upadasat; asmadrātiḥ kadā cana.*** It is prayed that the gifts of both, mutually nourishing — ours and yours — may be carried on without a break. The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa describes a story: men on earth, devoid of the knowledge of the prescribed rites, let sacrifices lapse, and the gods, who live by offerings, became anxious and grieved at this:

> ते [?]श्रद्धा मनुष्यान्निवेद [?] …. ते इतो देवा हविर्न जग्मुस्ते प्रदानाद्धि देवा उपजीवन्ति [?] ।

> *te [?]śraddhā manuṣyānniveda [?] …. te ito devā havirna jagmuste pradānāddhi devā upajīvanti [?] |*

(Śa. Brā. [?]-[?]-[?] [?].) Because the gods live by the gifts of oblations and the like, and the gifts had stopped through lack of rites, the gods consulted one another, and Bṛhaspati taught the Aṅgirases the way in which rites might be perfectly performed in future. In the same way, it is known from many sentences that the gods' wealth of food is possible only through the performance of rites, and that rites and the praises that belong to them are the gods' food:

> यज्ञो वो अन्नम् [?] ।

> *yajño vo annam [?] |*

(Śa. Brā. 3-[?]-[?]-[?] [?].)

> अर्को वै देवानामन्नमन्नं यज्ञो [?] …

> *arko vai devānāmannamannaṃ yajño [?] …*

(Śa. Brā. [?]-[?]-[?].) From such sentences it follows that, since the gods are called *śacīvasu*, in the Ṛk at hand the sacrificer prays to the Aśvins, "rich in our rites", that he will perform the rites and offer oblations, and that their gift, the fruit of this, may continue in the same way unbroken. This mutual dependence is shown in

> यत्पृथिव्यै प्रतिगृणाति [?] अमुष्मा एव तदद्युर्जयन्तीति तिष्ठतीव ह्यसाना [?] … तस्मादितः प्रदानं मनुष्या उपजीवन्ति यत्प्रतिगृणाति तस्मादमुतः प्रदानं मनुष्या उपजीवन्ति [?] ।

> *yatpṛthivyai pratigṛṇāti [?] amuṣmā eva tadadyurjayantīti tiṣṭhatīva hyasānā [?] … tasmāditaḥ pradānaṃ manuṣyā upajīvanti yatpratigṛṇāti tasmādamutaḥ pradānaṃ manuṣyā upajīvanti [?] |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?] [?].) The Taittirīya Saṃhitā explains that the gods live by the praise and oblations offered from the earth, and in return men live by the wealth that the gods grant. Therefore, desiring that the two actions of both sides never stop —

***naktam.*** *Naktety rātrināma — nakti bhūtāny avyaktāni vā naktāvyaktavarṇā* [?]: "because it makes all beings enveloped as if by mist, it is named *nakta*", or "because its colour is indistinct"; derived from the root *añj* "to shine", the word *akta*, with the negative *na*: *na* + *akta*; thus *nakta* means "that of indistinct colour": two senses are given by Yāska (Ni. [?]-[?]). The Bṛhaddevatā authors also … (continues on p. 63).

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 5, concluded from p. 62.)* …The Bṛhaddevatā authors also (give the sense of *nakta*):

***mā upa dasat.*** *Das* is the negative of a root *das* meaning "to waste away"; "let it not diminish" is the sense — "let it go on without decrease".

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> वृषन्निन्द्र वृषपाणास इन्दव इमे सुता अद्रिषुतास उद्भिदस्तुभ्यं सुतास उद्भिदः ।
> ते त्वा मन्दन्तु दावने महे चित्राय राधसे ।
> गीर्भिर्गिर्वाहः स्तवमान आ गहि सुमृळीको न आ गहि ॥ ६ ॥

> *vṛṣannindra vṛṣapāṇāsa indava ime sutā adriṣutāsa udbhidastubhyaṃ sutāsa udbhidaḥ |*
> *te tvā mandantu dāvane mahe citrāya rādhase |*
> *gīrbhirgirvāhaḥ stavamāna ā gahi sumṛḷīko na ā gahi ‖ 6 ‖*

### Printed p. 65  (PDF 83)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *vṛṣan* — O showerer of desired things; *indra* — O Indra; *indavaḥ* — flowing; *vṛṣapāṇāsaḥ* — to be drunk by you, who grant what is wished; *udbhidaḥ* — that cause rain to fall; *adriṣutāsaḥ* — that are pressed and ground with stones; *ime* — these Soma juices; *sutāḥ* — have been pressed; *udbhidaḥ* — these Soma plants grown on mountains and the like; *tubhyam* — for you; *sutāsaḥ* — have been pressed and made ready; *te* — these juices; *dāvane* — at sacrificial times rich in gifts; *mahe* — great; *citrāya* — and of many kinds; *rādhase* — for the gain of wealth; *tvā* — you; *mandantu* — may they satisfy; *girvāhaḥ* — Indra, bearer of praise; *gīrbhiḥ* — by our hymns; *stavamānaḥ* — being praised; *ā gahi* — come (be gracious); *naḥ* — us; *sumṛḷīkaḥ* — giving us happiness; *ā gahi* — come here.

**Bhāvārtha.** O showerer of desired things, Indra, these Soma juices that flow, are to be drunk by you, the giver of what is wished, help to make rain fall, and are pressed and ground with stones, have been pressed. These Soma plants grown on the mountains have been pressed and made ready for you. At times of sacrifice rich in gifts, may these juices satisfy you, for the gain of great and manifold wealth. O Indra, bearer of praise, come, praised by our hymns. Come here, making us happy.

**English Translation (as printed).** Indra, showerer (of blessings) these effused juices, (expressed) by stones and which have sprung (from mountain plants), are for your drinking; these libations have burst forth for you: may they satisfy you as an offering presented (in the hope of receiving) great and wonderful riches. Accepter of laudations, come to us, glorified by our hymns; come to us well pleased.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

On the sixth day of the sacrifice called *Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, when the *Praüga-śastra* mantras are recited, a *tṛca* (three Ṛks) relating to Indra must be recited; the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra says so in the sūkta वृषन्निन्द्र वृषपाणास सुषुमा यातमद्रिभिः [?] (*vṛṣannindra vṛṣapāṇāsa suṣumā yātamadribhiḥ [?]*) (Āś. [?]-[?]); and at the morning pressing of the same sacrifice, before the *pṛṣṭhitayājyā* mantra is recited, the *hotṛ* priest joins this Ṛk with other Ṛks … (continues on p. 66).

### Printed p. 66  (PDF 84)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 139".)*

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 6, continued from p. 65.)* …makes the *hotṛ* priest offer the oblation; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra by the sūtra षष्ठस्य प्रातःसवने पृष्ठितेयाज्यानां पुरस्तादन्या कृत्वेभ्यामवनानन्तरो यजन्ति [?] (*ṣaṣṭhasya prātaḥsavane pṛṣṭhiteyājyānāṃ purastādanyā kṛtvebhyāmavanānantaro yajanti [?]*) (Āś. [?]-[?]).

***vṛṣan; vṛṣapāṇāsaḥ.*** Sāyaṇa explains *vṛṣan* as *kāmānāṃ varṣitaḥ* — "one who showers desired things" — and *vṛṣapāṇāsaḥ* as *abhimatavarṣaṇena tvayā pātavyāḥ* — "to be drunk by you, who shower what is wished". That is, the drinking of the Soma juice is the intent that gives Indra [joy] [?]:

> इति वा इति मे मनो गामश्वं सनुयामिति । कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥

> *iti vā iti me mano gāmaśvaṃ sanuyāmiti | kuvitsomasyāpāmiti ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-119-1 [?].) Indra says that he has drunk the Soma that encourages him to give cows and horses to the praisers. Likewise:

> कदा चन स्तरीरसि नेन्द्र सश्चसि दाशुषे । उपोपेन्नु मघवन्भूय इन्नु ते दानं देवस्य पृच्यते [?] । उपयाम गृहीतोऽस्यादित्येभ्यस्त्वा [?] । कदा चन प्रयुच्छसि [?] … सवनं त इन्द्रियामृतस्था [?] ।

> *kadā cana starīrasi nendra saścasi dāśuṣe | upopennu maghavanbhūya innu te dānaṃ devasya pṛcyate [?] | upayāma gṛhīto 'syādityebhyastvā [?] | kadā cana prayucchasi [?] … savanaṃ ta indriyāmṛtasthā [?] |*

(Tai. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?] [?].) In these Saṃhitā sentences too the drinking of the Soma juice is said to be the means of favouring the sacrificers who offer oblations; the same is said here.

***udbhidaḥ.*** *Balasya udbhedakāḥ, udbhinnā vā parvatādau tādṛśāḥ somāḥ* — "(Soma juices) that bring out strength", or "(plants) that have sprung up on mountains and the like": the commentator says the two senses are possible.

> प्र वाता इव दोधत उन्मा पीता अयंसत । कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥

> *pra vātā iva dodhata unmā pītā ayaṃsata | kuvitsomasyāpāmiti ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-119-3 [?].)

> न हि मे रोदसी उभे अन्यं पक्षं चन प्रति । कुवित्सोमस्यापामिति ॥

> *na hi me rodasī ubhe anyaṃ pakṣaṃ cana prati | kuvitsomasyāpāmiti ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-119-[?].) In such Ṛks, since there are the words of Indra that his strength grew through drinking Soma and that none with strength like his is found in heaven and earth, the first sense is correct. For the second, Sāyaṇa points out that the Soma plant grows on mountains and the like and so has the epithet *udbhid*. The growth, form, colour, taste and so on of the Soma plant are set out fully in Part [?] of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā. Recent critics have discussed the Soma plant and given their views; a summary of the articles written in the *Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society*, the *Indian Antiquary* and other journals is given briefly in the Pūrvapīṭhikā of this part. Whether those views are right or wrong the reader must judge for himself.

***dāvane.*** *Dāvati yāge* — "in the sacrifice that gives desired things"; an epithet of the sacrifice. The word is also used as an epithet of Indra and other gods, showing their giving nature.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar page, noted briefly).** *vṛṣan* (root *vṛṣu secane*; *kanin yuvṛṣi…* (U. Sū. 1-[?]) *kanin*; the *n* is not dropped in the vocative; as it is at the start of a *pāda*, no *nighāta*; *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-[?]) first-syllable accent), *vṛṣapāṇāsaḥ* (*vṛṣṇaḥ pānāḥ*; root *pā pāne*; *lyuṭ* in the passive sense; *yuvor anākau* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-[?]) *ana*; accent of the first member of a *kṛt*-compound; the *jas* with *ajjhalī…* *asuk* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-[?])), *adriṣutāsaḥ* (*adribhiḥ sutāḥ*; root *ṣuñ abhiṣave*; *kta* in the passive; *tṛtīyā karmaṇi* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-[?]) first-member accent; as before *asuk*), *udbhidaḥ* (root *bhidir vidāraṇe*; *kvip*; prefix compound; accent; nominative plural), *mandantu* (root *madi harṣaglepanayoḥ*; *iditaś ca* gives *num*; *loṭ* third person plural; *nighāta* as a *tiṅanta* follows a non-*tiṅanta*), *dāvane* (root *dudāñ dāne*; *āto maniṅ…* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-[?]) *vanip*; dative singular; Vedic non-*luk* of the *ṅe*), *mahe* (for *mahate*; Vedic loss of the *t*; *sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ* gives *udātta* to the case-ending), *girvāhaḥ* (*girāṃ vāhaḥ*; root *vah prāpaṇe*; *vahihādhāṅbhyaś chandasi* (U. Sū. 4-[?]) *asun*; vocative; *āmantritasya ca*), *stavamānaḥ* (root *ṣṭuñ stutau*; *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ*; *śānac* in the passive sense; *vyatyaya*: *śap*; *āne muk*), *gahi* (root *gamḷ gatau*; *loṭ* second person singular *sip* → *hi*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* *luk* of *śap*; the nasal of the root dropped), *sumṛḷīkaḥ* (*sukhaṃ mṛḷīkaṃ yasya saḥ*; *nañsubhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-[?]) accent of the last member's first syllable). ‖ 6 ‖ Sūtra numbers not read.

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *agne* — O Agni; *tvam* — you; *naḥ* — our; (*naḥ*) praise-form invocation; *īḷitaḥ* — praised by us; *o ṣu śṛṇuhi* — listen, turned towards us; (then) *rājabhyaḥ* — to the radiant; *yajñiyebhyaḥ* — worthy of the praise or the oblation connected with the sacrifice; *devebhyaḥ* — to the gods; *yajñiyebhyaḥ* — (the rite) considered by the sacrificer [?]; *bravasi* — tell; *yat tyām* — which well-known; *dhenum* — cow; *devāḥ* — the gods; *aṅgirobhyaḥ* — to the Aṅgirases; *adattana* — gave; *tām* — that cow; *aryamā* — Aryaman; *saṃyamisatakka karmavannu* [?]; *kartarī* — in you, the maker; *sacā* — together with the other gods; *vi duhre* — milked; (and) *eṣaḥ* — this Aryaman; *tām* — that cow; *me sacā* — together with me; *vede* — knows.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, praised by us, listen to this invocation of ours that takes the form of praise, turning towards us. Then tell the radiant gods, who deserve the praise and oblation of the sacrifice, of the rite performed by us, the sacrificers (continued on p. 70).

### Printed p. 70  (PDF 88)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 139".)*

*(Bhāvārtha, concluded.)* …Tell the gods who are worthy of oblations the rite performed by us, the sacrificers. In return for this rite the gods favour us; the cow well known [as given] by them to the Aṅgirases, Aryaman milked, together with those gods, for you [Agni]. That same Aryaman, even now, together with me, knows that cow as ready for the sacrifice.

**English Translation (as printed).** Agni, listen attentively when you are praised by us, and repeat (those praises) to the gods who are entitled to worship; to the royal (deities) entitled to worship: on which account the gods gave to the Angirasas the milch cow which Aryman milked for (you), the maker (of all), together with the gods; that cow (the nature of which you have said), be along wtih [sic] me, comprehends.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

On the sixth day of the sacrifice called *Daśarātra*, performed over ten days, at the morning pressing, before the priest called *Neṣṭṛ* recites the *pṛṣṭhitayājyā* mantra [?], this Ṛk *o ṣū ṇo agne* and the Ṛk *agniṃ hotāram* are joined and recited at the time of the sacrifice; so the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, in the section beginning *ṣaṣṭhasya*, sets out by the sūtra ओ षू णो अग्ने शृणुहि त्वमीळितोऽग्निं होतारम् (*o ṣū ṇo agne śṛṇuhi tvamīḷito 'gniṃ hotāram*) (Āś. [?]-[?]); and that when the *Praüga-śastra* mantras are recited at the same pressing, this Ṛk is to be recited as the second mantra, by the sūtra अस्तु श्रौषळो षू णो अग्ने (*astu śrauṣaḷo ṣū ṇo agne*) (Āś. [?]-[?]).

***yajñiyebhyo rājabhyo yajñiyebhyo bravasi.*** Here the first *yajñiyebhyaḥ* means, as an epithet of the gods, *yajñārhebhyo havirbhāgbhyaḥ stutibhāgbhyaś ca* — "to those worthy of sacrifice, who deserve a share of the oblation and of the praise". The second *yajñiyebhyaḥ* is an epithet of the sacrificers, *yajñārhebhyo yajamānebhyaḥ saṃbandhi karma* — the rite belonging to the sacrificers who are fit to sacrifice. The sense is: tell or convey to the gods, fit to receive the sacrifice, the praises and oblations of men fit to sacrifice. From this sentence it is understood that Agni, as the leader of the sacrifice, is a messenger who builds the relation between the sacrificers and the gods.

> त्वे अग्ने विश्वे अमृतासो अद्रुह आसा देवा हविरदन्त्याहुतम् ।
> त्वया मर्तासः स्वदन्त आसुतिं त्वं गर्भो वीरुधां जज्ञिषे शुचिः ॥

> *tve agne viśve amṛtāso adruha āsā devā haviradantyāhutam |*
> *tvayā martāsaḥ svadanta āsutiṃ tvaṃ garbho vīrudhāṃ jajñiṣe śuciḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-[?] [?].) As described in such Ṛks, and

> अग्निर्वै देवानां दूत आस [?] ।

> *agnirvai devānāṃ dūta āsa [?] |*

(Śa. Brā. 1-[?]-[?]-[?] [?]) (continued on p. 71).

### Printed p. 71  (PDF 89)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

> यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रति दधात्यग्निर्देवानां दूत आसीत् [?] ।

> *yajñasya śiraḥ prati dadhātyagnirdevānāṃ dūta āsīt [?] |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?]-[?] [?].) As said also in such sentences, Agni, being the messenger common to the gods and to the sacrificers, men, is addressed by the sacrificers with the prayer that he speak their praises before the gods.

***aṅgirobhyo dhenuṃ devā adattana.*** *Atretihāsam āhuḥ* — "here they tell a story: the great seers named Aṅgirases, in the past, praised the gods for the sake of a sacrifice and pleased them, and asked for cows. Pleased, they gave them the cow of desire. Unable to milk the milk of that cow, they prayed to the god Aryaman; and he, asked, milked the milk for the Agnihotra and so on." The Kannada gives it thus: the great seers called Aṅgirases, wishing to obtain cows for sacrifice, praised the gods and delighted them; the gods gave them the cow that grants all desires; then, unable to milk it, they prayed to the god Aryaman to help; and Aryaman milked for them the milk needed for the Agnihotra which the Aṅgirases were to perform — this story is hinted here. And that before all, the Aṅgirases made Agni shine in the Agnihotra sacrifice:

> अङ्गिरसः [?] ते ऽग्नेर्नाग्निमयजन्त ते स्वर्गं लोकमायन् [?] ।

> *aṅgirasaḥ [?] te 'gnernāgnimayajanta te svargaṃ lokamāyan [?] |*

(Ai. Brā. 1-[?]) and similar sentences say so. *Aṅgiras* is used in three ways: as a proper name; as the name of a line of seers; and as a name connected with a company of gods. By the epithet *aṅgirobhyaḥ*, *aṅgirasaḥ* it is shown, in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, Part 1, pp. 94–95 [?], that Indra and the Aṅgirases are closely related. Here the relation of Agni and the Aṅgirases is to be understood. Since this Ṛk has the plural *aṅgirobhyaḥ*, the line of the Aṅgiras seers is meant. Agni is the original ancestor of this line; from him the seer Aṅgiras himself came into being, and that line grew — a story told in

> त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अङ्गिरा ऋषिर्देवो देवानामभवः शिवः सखा ।

> *tvamagne prathamo aṅgirā ṛṣirdevo devānāmabhavaḥ śivaḥ sakhā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-[?] [?].) This same story (continues on p. 72).

> हे मरुतः वो युष्मत्सम्बन्धीनि तानि प्रसिद्धानि पौंस्या पौंस्यानि बलानि सना सदातनानि नित्यानि द्युम्नानि प्रकाशकयुक्तानि [?] । यद्वा । सना सम्भजनीयानि द्युम्नानि धनवन्ति यशोवन्ति वा [?] । मत्सङ्घातीयो [?] … । मो इति निपातद्वयसमुदायः [?] । अस्माकं नो [?] अभि भूवन् [?] सुष्ठु मा भूवन् । यद्वा । अस्मत्सकाशादभि मा भूवन् । उत अपि च । यद्वा । द्युम्नानि धनानि यशांसि वास्मदीयानि मा जारिषुः । क्षीणानि मा भूवन् । उतापि चास्मत्पुरा पुराणि लक्षणया तत्स्थाः प्राणिनो मा जारिषुः । जीर्णा नष्टा मा भूवन् । किञ्च वो युष्मत्सम्बन्धि चित्रं चायनीयं नानाविधं नव्यं नूतनं स्तोतव्यं वा अमर्त्यमरणधर्मकं [?] मर्त्येषु दुर्लभं यत् … घोषाद्घोषात् [?] शब्दोपेताः गवादयो घोषोपलक्षितः ग्रामः [?] नगरादयो वा ये सन्ति तैः सर्वं युगे युगे युगभेदोपलक्षिते काले [?] अस्मास्वेव भवत्विति शेषः । नान्यस्य । किञ्च हे मरुतः यच्च दुस्तरं दुःखेन तरणीयं सम्पादनीयं धनं दिद्धृत धारयत तदस्मासु [?] । किञ्च दुस्तरं शत्रुभिरुत्संपीडितं तद्धनमपि विशेषेणास्मासु स्थापयत ॥

> *he marutaḥ vo yuṣmatsambandhīni tāni prasiddhāni pauṃsyā pauṃsyāni balāni sanā sadātanāni nityāni dyumnāni prakāśakayuktāni [?] | yadvā | sanā sambhajanīyāni dyumnāni dhanavanti yaśovanti vā [?] | matsaṅghātīyo [?] … | mo iti nipātadvayasamudāyaḥ [?] | asmākaṃ no [?] abhi bhūvan [?] suṣṭhu mā bhūvan | yadvā | asmatsakāśādabhi mā bhūvan | uta api ca | yadvā | dyumnāni dhanāni yaśāṃsi vāsmadīyāni mā jāriṣuḥ | kṣīṇāni mā bhūvan | utāpi cāsmatpurā purāṇi lakṣaṇayā tatsthāḥ prāṇino mā jāriṣuḥ | jīrṇā naṣṭā mā bhūvan | kiñca vo yuṣmatsambandhi citraṃ cāyanīyaṃ nānāvidhaṃ navyaṃ nūtanaṃ stotavyaṃ vā amartyamaraṇadharmakaṃ [?] martyeṣu durlabhaṃ yat … ghoṣādghoṣāt [?] śabdopetāḥ gavādayo ghoṣopalakṣitaḥ grāmaḥ [?] nagarādayo vā ye santi taiḥ sarvaṃ yuge yuge yugabhedopalakṣite kāle [?] asmāsveva bhavatviti śeṣaḥ | nānyasya | kiñca he marutaḥ yacca dustaraṃ duḥkhena taraṇīyaṃ sampādanīyaṃ dhanaṃ diddhṛta dhārayata tadasmāsu [?] | kiñca dustaraṃ śatrubhirutsaṃpīḍitaṃ taddhanamapi viśeṣeṇāsmāsu sthāpayata ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *(he) marutaḥ* — O Maruts; *vaḥ* — your; *tāni* — those well-known; *pauṃsyā* — powers (strengths, capabilities); *sanā* — that last for ever (without decay); (and) *dyumnāni* — shining (excellent) [or: *sanā* — fit to be obtained; *dyumnāni* — that make wealth or fame]; (those powers of yours) *asmat* — us; *abhi mo ṣu bhūvan* — may they not turn against us (or: may they not leave us) [?]; *uta* — and; (*dyumnāni*) — our wealth or fame; *mā jāriṣuḥ* — let it not decay; *uta* — and; *asmat* — our; *purā* — towns (or the people and creatures in them); (*mā*) *jāriṣuḥ* — let them not perish; (and) *vaḥ* — yours (made for you); *yat citram* — whatever of many kinds, wonderful; *navyam* — new (or praiseworthy); *amartyam* — a thing hard to find among mortals; *yat* — whichever; *ghoṣāt* — [of the creatures that sound] and the people also; *tat* — that thing; *yuge yuge* — in every age; *asmāsu* — may it be among us (*asmāsu*; O) *marutaḥ* — Maruts; *dustaram* — hard to obtain, to be won with great effort; *yat ca* — whatever wealth there is; *didhṛtā* — set it in us (make us hold it); (and) *dustaram* — that cannot be taken by foes; *yat ca* — whatever things there are (make them dwell in us).

### Printed p. 75  (PDF 93)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

**Bhāvārtha.** O Maruts, may your well-known powers of protection not harm us. May our wealth not decay. May our towns (and the people and animals in them) not perish. Whatever is wonderful, excellent and imperishable, may it always be with us, with the creatures that make sound and with us men. May wealth that must be won with great hardship, and that cannot be taken by foes, remain with us.

**English Translation (as printed).** Never, Maruts, may your glorious energies be exerted against us; may our (riches) never diminish: never may our towns decay: and may whatever is wonderful, admirable, immortal, or (whatever is recognized to be living), from its sound, that has been yours from age to age, (devolve) upon us; whatever is most difficult (of attainment) bestow upon us; whatever is most difficult (to be attained).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

In the sacrifice called *Daśarātra*, spoken of before, this Ṛk *mo ṣu vo asmat* too is to be recited as a *pṛṣṭhitayājyā* mantra, as the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra sets out by the sūtra मो षु वो अस्मदभि तानि पौंस्या षू णो अग्ने (*mo ṣu vo asmadabhi tāni pauṃsyā ṣū ṇo agne*) (Āś. [?]-[?]).

***vaḥ tāni pauṃsyā.*** *Yuṣmatsaṃbandhīni balāni* — "your well-known powers": the collective power of the Maruts is praised (continued on p. 76).

### Printed p. 76  (PDF 94)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 20 Sū. 139".)*

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 8, continued from p. 75.)* ***sanā dyumnāni.*** These two words are epithets. Sāyaṇa explains *sanā* first as *sadātanāni*, *nityāni* — "eternal"; and *dyumnāni* as *prakāśayuktāni* — "radiant". Or *sanā* — *saṃbhajanīyāni*, "to be resorted to", and *dyumnāni* — "possessing wealth or fame": he gives this second sense too. Since the Maruts' powers have been famous and radiant from beginningless time, the first sense is fitting.

> प्र वेपयन्ति पर्वतान्वि विञ्चन्ति वनस्पतीन् [?] ।

> *pra vepayanti parvatānvi viñcanti vanaspatīn [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] [?].)

> वना चिदुग्रा जिहते नि वो भिया पृथिवी चिद्रेजते पर्वतश्चित् [?] ।

> *vanā cidugrā jihate ni vo bhiyā pṛthivī cidrejate parvataścit [?] |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] [?].) As described in such Ṛks, the mountains and the earth tremble through the might of the Maruts. Since earth and sky tremble, there is no one who does not know their power. Hence the second sense is also natural. Whoever moves in the sky cannot move without informing the Maruts; if one slights the Maruts, they are certain to bar the way.

> तासु पदमस्ति स्वस्ति रायो मरुतो दधातनेति मरुतो ह वै देवविशो [?] … तेरित्यभाजनान्यां [?] … स्वर्गं लोकमेतीश्वरा हैनं [?] निरोद्धोर्वा मथितोर्वा स यदाह स्वस्ति रायो मरुतो दधातनेति तं मरुद्भ्यो देवविद्भ्यो यजमानो निवेदयति न हैनं मरुतो देवविशः स्वर्गं लोकं यन्तं निरुन्धते [?] । स्वस्ति हैनं मर्त्यान्ति [?] स्वर्गं लोकमभि य एवं वेद ॥

> *tāsu padamasti svasti rāyo maruto dadhātaneti maruto ha vai devaviśo [?] … terityabhājanānyāṃ [?] … svargaṃ lokametīśvarā hainaṃ [?] niroddhorvā mathitorvā sa yadāha svasti rāyo maruto dadhātaneti taṃ marudbhyo devavidbhyo yajamāno nivedayati na hainaṃ maruto devaviśaḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ yantaṃ nirundhate [?] | svasti hainaṃ martyānti [?] svargaṃ lokamabhi ya evaṃ veda ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 1-[?]-[?] [?].) The Maruts, as the people of the gods, pervade all the sky. Those who go to heaven without informing them they surely stop or destroy. If, reciting the sentence *svasti rāye marutaḥ*, one worships them, they do not hinder. From the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and the like, in which it is said that he who knows this secret surely attains welfare, the Maruts' power, whether of favour or of restraint, is described. For this reason it is prayed: *asmat purā mā jāriṣuḥ* — "may our wealth and our sons and grandsons not decay; help us so".

***ghoṣāt.*** *Śabdopetā gavādayo ghoṣopalakṣitā grāmanagarādayo vā ye santi* — "those cows and others that make sound, or villages and towns characterized by sound, as there are": cows with their sounds, and villages and towns, are here indicated; the prayer is that these may be ours lastingly. The word *ghoṣa* is read among the names of speech (Ni. 1-[?]). Ordinarily this word means "sound"; it is used here in the sense of a sound that shows a distinctive power (continued on p. 77).

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

…In the Saṃhitās and in the Brāhmaṇas and the like, the word *ghoṣa* means a sound that carries an extraordinary power: *vi rodasī atapat ghoṣa viṣām* [?] (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?]), *āyāmi ghoṣa indra* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?]) and other Saṃhitā sentences; and

> ता वा एताः सर्वा ऋचः सर्वे वेदाः सर्वे घोषा एकैव व्याहृतिः [?] ।

> *tā vā etāḥ sarvā ṛcaḥ sarve vedāḥ sarve ghoṣā ekaiva vyāhṛtiḥ [?] |*

(Ai. Ā. 3-[?]-[?] [?].)

> मयि स्तोभो मयि स्तोमो [?] मयि श्लोको मयि घोषो मयि यशः [?] ।

> *mayi stobho mayi stomo [?] mayi śloko mayi ghoṣo mayi yaśaḥ [?] |*

(Brā. Ā. [?]-[?]-[?] [?].)

> येनेदमन्नं पच्यते यदिदमद्यते तस्यैष घोषो भवति [?] ।

> *yenedamannaṃ pacyate yadidamadyate tasyaiṣa ghoṣo bhavati [?] |*

(Śa. Brā. 14-[?]-[?]-[?] [?].)

> सर्वे स्वरा घोषवन्तो बलवन्तो वक्तव्याः [?] ।

> *sarve svarā ghoṣavanto balavanto vaktavyāḥ [?] |*

(Chā. Up. [?]-[?]-[?] [?].) In these and other places it is used with the sense of a sound that has extraordinary power. In the Ṛk at hand, though it has no such special sense, it means the sound of cows and the like, or of villages and towns, that causes exceeding delight. The prayer is: give us permanently wealth of cows and the like, accompanied by such joy-giving sounds.

***dustaram.*** The word is repeated. The first means the toil of acquiring wealth, the second the toil of guarding wealth. *Dustaram* — *duḥkhena taraṇīyaṃ saṃpādanīyam* — "to be obtained with great trouble"; and *dustaram* — *śatrubhir ahiṃsitam* — "not harmed by foes".

***yuge yuge.*** *Yugaśabdaḥ kālavacanaḥ* — "in the respective ages (times)"; it means either in the times of our sacrifices, or in the lifetimes of ourselves and our sons and grandsons.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; grammar page, noted briefly).** *mo ṣu* (*mā* and *u*: two particles), *suñaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-[?]) *ṣatva* of the *s* of *su*), *asmat* (ablative plural; *supāṃ sulak…*: the case-ending *luk* in the first-named [?]).

Sū. 6-4-[?]); *tiṅanta nighāta*), *jāriṣuḥ* (root *jṛṣ vayohānau*; *luṅ* third person plural, *jhi*; *cli* → *sic*; *jher jus* by *sijabhyastavidibhyaś ca* (Pā. **Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *dadhyañc ha* — the seer Dadhīci; *pūrvaḥ* — very ancient; *aṅgirāḥ* — the seer Aṅgiras; *priyamedhaḥ* — Priyamedha; *kaṇvaḥ* — Kaṇva; *atriḥ* — the seer Atri; *manuḥ* — and Manu (all these seers); *me januṣam* — my birth (of me, son of Divodāsa, named Parucchepa); *viduḥ* — have known; *pūrve* — the very ancient; *te* — these seers all; *manuḥ* — and Manu (my forefathers, father and grandfather); *me* — my; *viduḥ* — have known; *teṣām* — to those seers; *deveṣu* — with the other shining seers [?]; *āyatiḥ* — a long connection is there; *asmākam* — our; *nābhayaḥ* — chief vital breaths, or the sacrifices that are the place of birth and give fruit; *teṣu* — in them they lie (their help is sought); *teṣām* — of Dadhīci and the others; *padena* — for the sake of the greatness; *girā* — with a praising speech; *mahi* — exceedingly; *name* — I bow (and by their favour I have become fit for the sacrifice); *indrāgnī* — Indra and Agni; *girā* — with praising speech; *name* — I bow.

**Bhāvārtha.** The ancient seers Dadhīci, Aṅgiras, Priyamedha, Kaṇva, Atri, Manu and the like know well my forefathers and me, the son of Divodāsa. Since they are long-lived, they have a long connection with the gods and with other seers called by divine names. Our chief breaths and our states depend on them. To win [high] positions [?] I praise the gods; and with praises I worship Indra and Agni.

**English Translation (as printed).** The ancient Dadhyanch, Angiras, Priyamedha, Kanwa, Atri, Manu, have known my birth: they who were of old and Manu have known (my progenitors); for of them is long life amongst the gods, and in them is our existence: for the sake of their high station, I adore (the gods) with praise; I worship Indra and Agni with praise.

### Printed p. 81  (PDF 99)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

On the sixth day of the *Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha* sacrifice, at the midday pressing, the priest called *Acchāvāka* is to recite this Ṛk *dadhyaṅ ha me* as the introductory part of the *yājyā* mantra [?]; the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra sets this out by the sūtra दध्यङ् ह मे जनुषं पूर्वो अङ्गिरा इत्येवमेव माध्यंदिने (*dadhyaṅ ha me januṣaṃ pūrvo aṅgirā ityevameva mādhyaṃdine*) (Āś. [?]-[?]). In this Ṛk the seer Parucchepa, in connection with his own and his forefathers' acquaintance, indicates what his relation was with the ancient seers beginning with Dadhīci, and declares that he praises Indra and Agni in order to obtain a position as good as theirs.

***dadhyaṅ.*** *Atharvagotrotpanno dadhyaṅ etannāmako maharṣiḥ* — "the great seer of this name, born in the Atharva line" (he is also called son of Atharvan). He gained mastery of the *madhuvidyā* ("honey-lore"); he was Indra's direct pupil, and taught this lore also to the Aśvins. The story about this, which Sāyaṇa tells in the commentary on Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-12 [?], was given earlier in the Special Topics of that Ṛk. Without repeating it here, what is told is how the same story is narrated in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa and in the Upaniṣads and so on, the nature of the *madhuvidyā*, and how famous the name of Dadhīci became through that lore. The occasion on which Dadhīci taught this lore to the Aśvins is in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa as follows:

> दध्यङ् ह वा आथर्वणः । एतं शुक्रमेतं यज्ञं विदाञ्चकार । यथा यज्ञस्यैतस्य शिरः प्रतिधीयते यथैष कृत्स्नो यज्ञो भवति । स हेन्द्रेणोक्त आस । एतं चेदन्यस्मा अनुब्रूयास्तत एव ते शिरश्छिन्द्यामिति [?] ।

> *dadhyaṅ ha vā ātharvaṇaḥ | etaṃ śukrametaṃ yajñaṃ vidāñcakāra | yathā yajñasyaitasya śiraḥ pratidhīyate yathaiṣa kṛtsno yajño bhavati | sa hendreṇokta āsa | etaṃ cedanyasmā anubrūyāstata eva te śiraśchindyāmiti [?] |*

Dadhīci, son of Atharvan, learnt this bright lore of the sacrifice — how the head of the sacrifice is set in place and how the sacrifice becomes complete. Indra told him: "If you teach this to anyone else, I shall cut off your head."

> तेदु हाश्विनोरनुशुश्रुवामास [?] । दध्यङ् ह वा आथर्वण एतं शुक्रमेतं यज्ञं वेद यथा यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रतिधीयते यथैष कृत्स्नो यज्ञो भवति ।

> *tedu hāśvinoranuśuśruvāmāsa [?] | dadhyaṅ ha vā ātharvaṇa etaṃ śukrametaṃ yajñaṃ veda yathā yajñasya śiraḥ pratidhīyate yathaiṣa kṛtsno yajño bhavati |*

Then the Aśvins, hearing this, wished to obtain for themselves the knowledge of the sacrifice that Dadhīci possessed (continued on p. 82).

> ता हेमां चक्रतुः [?] । उप त्वायोवेति [?] कमनुवक्ष्यमाणाविति [?] एतं शुक्रमेतं यज्ञं यथा … कृत्स्नो यज्ञो भवतीति [?] ।

> *tā hemāṃ cakratuḥ [?] | upa tvāyoveti [?] kamanuvakṣyamāṇāviti [?] etaṃ śukrametaṃ yajñaṃ yathā … kṛtsno yajño bhavatīti [?] |*

Then they went to him, and said that they would become his pupils and learn that lore, asking him to instruct them also.

> स होवाच । इन्द्रेण वा उक्तोऽस्म्येतं चेदन्यस्मा अनुब्रूयास्तत एव ते शिरश्छिन्द्यामिति तस्माद्वै बिभेमि यद्वै मे स शिरो न छिन्द्यान्नेति वामुपवेयाम् इति [?] ।

> *sa hovāca | indreṇa vā ukto 'smyetaṃ cedanyasmā anubrūyāstata eva te śiraśchindyāmiti tasmādvai bibhemi yadvai me sa śiro na chindyānneti vāmupaveyām iti [?] |*

In reply he told them of the order Indra had given him, and said that he could not accept them as pupils.

> तौ होचतुः । आवां त्वा तस्मात्त्रायिष्यावह इति कथं मा त्रास्येथे इति यदा नावुपसेत्स्यस्येथ [?] तेरश्वस्य [?] शिर आहृत्य तेत्र [?] प्रतिधास्यावस्तेन नावनुशासिष्यसि [?] यदेन्द्रः शिरश्छेत्स्यते ते स्वं शिर आहृत्य तेत्र [?] प्रतिधास्याव इति ।

> *tau hocatuḥ | āvāṃ tvā tasmāttrāyiṣyāvaha iti kathaṃ mā trāsyethe iti yadā nāvupasetsyasyetha [?] teraśvasya [?] śira āhṛtya tetra [?] pratidhāsyāvastena nāvanuśāsiṣyasi [?] yadendraḥ śiraśchetsyate te svaṃ śira āhṛtya tetra [?] pratidhāsyāva iti |*

They answered, "We shall protect you." How? — they took his head off and put it safely away in another place, and in that place …; after Indra had cut off the head put on in its stead, they would bring back his own natural head. On this being said, Dadhīci agreed.

> तौ होपेनिस्ने । तौ यदोपेनिस्नेत्यास्य शिरश्छित्त्वान्यत्र निदधतुरश्वस्य शिर आहृत्यै तद्यास्य प्रतिदधतुस्तेन हाभ्यामनूवाच स यदाभ्यामनूवाचाथास्य तदिन्द्रः शिरश्छेदाथास्य शिर आहृत्यै तद्यास्य प्रतिदधतुः [?] ।

> *tau hopenisne | tau yadopenisnetyāsya śiraśchittvānyatra nidadhaturaśvasya śira āhṛtyai tadyāsya pratidadhatustena hābhyāmanūvāca sa yadābhyāmanūvācāthāsya tadindraḥ śiraśchedāthāsya śira āhṛtyai tadyāsya pratidadhatuḥ [?] |*

At once the two became pupils and took in the teaching; then Indra came and cut off that horse's head; and the Aśvins at once set in place Dadhīci's own natural head.

> तस्मादेतदृषिणाभ्यनूक्तम् । दध्यङ् ह यन्मध्वाथर्वणो वामश्वस्य शीर्ष्णा प्र यदीमुवाचेत्थायतं तदुवाचेति हैतदुक्तम् [?] ।

> *tasmādetadṛṣiṇābhyanūktam | dadhyaṅ ha yanmadhvātharvaṇo vāmaśvasya śīrṣṇā pra yadīmuvācetthāyataṃ taduvāceti haitaduktam [?] |*

(Śa. Brā. 14-[?]-[?]-[?] to [?].) Therefore it is famous that Dadhīci, the son of Atharvan, taught this *madhuvidyā* by means of the horse's head: so goes the story in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. This same story in the Bṛhaddevatā too:

(Bṛ. De. 3-[?] to [?].) These sentences tell the same story. There is no difference in the telling; only at the end it is added that the horse's head, cut off by Indra's thunderbolt, fell into the lake on the mountain called Śaryaṇāvat, and, rising from the water at every step, giving all beings the boons suited to them in abundance, remains submerged there to the end of the age.

That this same *madhuvidyā* is the "head of the sacrifice", the truth of the sacrifice, is stated in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka also, as in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, where, praising the greatness of other things, it says that this is the truth of the Supreme Person in the self; there the Ṛks तद्वां नरा सनये दंस उग्रम् [?] (*tadvāṃ narā sanaye daṃsa ugram [?]*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-12 [?]) and अथर्वणायाश्विना दधीचेऽश्व्यं शिरः [?] (*atharvaṇāyāśvinā dadhīce 'śvyaṃ śiraḥ [?]*) (1-119-[?]) are cited, and also

> रूपंरूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव तदस्य रूपं प्रतिचक्षणाय ।
> इन्द्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते युक्ता ह्यस्य हरयः शता दश ॥

> *rūpaṃrūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva tadasya rūpaṃ praticakṣaṇāya |*
> *indro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate yuktā hyasya harayaḥ śatā daśa ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-18 [?].) After citing this Ṛk it says इयं वै तन्मधु दध्यङ्ङाथर्वणोऽश्विभ्यामुवाच (*iyaṃ vai tanmadhu dadhyaṅṅātharvaṇo 'śvibhyāmuvāca*) [?] — "Dadhīci Ātharvaṇa taught the Aśvins that [lore]" — and that this brings one to the same supreme truth (Bṛ. U. 2-5-[?] to [?]).
