#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स संस्तिरो विष्टिरः सं गृभायति जानन्नेव जानतीर्नित्य आ शये ।
> पुनर्वर्धन्ते अपि यन्ति देव्यमन्यद्वर्पः पित्रोः कृण्वते सचा ॥ ७ ॥

> *sa saṃstiro viṣṭiraḥ saṃ gṛbhāyati jānanneva jānatīrnitya ā śaye |*
> *punarvardhante api yanti devyamanyadvarpaḥ pitroḥ kṛṇvate sacā ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । संस्तिरः । विस्तिरः । सम् । गृभायति । जानन् । एव । जानतीः । नित्ये । आ । शये ।
> पुनः । वर्धन्ते । अपि । यन्ति । देव्यम् । अन्यत् । वर्पः । पित्रोः । कृण्वते । सचा ॥ ७ ॥

> *saḥ | saṃstiraḥ | vistiraḥ | sam | gṛbhāyati | jānan | eva | jānatīḥ | nitye | ā | śaye |*
> *punaḥ | vardhante | api | yanti | devyam | anyat | varpaḥ | pitroḥ | kṛṇvate | sacā ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *Agni, now hidden, now spread out, seizes the fuel as if knowing the sacrificer's purpose; the flames, grown again, go to the divine, and together with it give another form to heaven and earth.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> सोऽग्निः संस्तिरः आच्छन्नः । संपूर्वात्स्तृणातेर्मूलविभुजादित्वात्कप्रत्ययः । [?] परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ तथा विस्तिरः कदाचिद्विस्तीर्णः सन् संगृभायति संगृह्णाति [?] । किंचाग्निः जानन्नेव यजमानार्थं प्रवृद्धेन भवितव्यमित्येवं ज्ञात्वैव [?] ज्वालाः जानतीः [?] नित्ये [?] सन् आ शये । आशेते । आश्रयतीत्यर्थः ॥ लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्विति तलोपः ॥ एवंभूता ज्वालाः पुनः पूर्वं [?] प्रवृद्धा एव पुनरपि यागयोग्या यथा भवन्ति तथा वर्धन्ते । देव्यं देवानां योग्यं [?] … यन्ति । [?] … अन्यत् वर्पः रूपं पित्रोः द्यावापृथिव्योः [?] सचा सह संभूय [?] कृण्वते कुर्वन्ति ॥ … [remainder of the small type not read]

> *so 'gniḥ saṃstiraḥ ācchannaḥ | saṃpūrvātstṛṇātermūlavibhujāditvātkapratyayaḥ | [?] parādiśchandasi bahulamityuttarapadādyudāttatvam ‖ tathā vistiraḥ kadācidvistīrṇaḥ san saṃgṛbhāyati saṃgṛhṇāti [?] | kiṃcāgniḥ jānanneva yajamānārthaṃ pravṛddhena bhavitavyamityevaṃ jñātvaiva [?] jvālāḥ jānatīḥ [?] nitye [?] san ā śaye | āśete | āśrayatītyarthaḥ ‖ lopasta ātmanepadeṣviti talopaḥ ‖ evaṃbhūtā jvālāḥ punaḥ pūrvaṃ [?] pravṛddhā eva punarapi yāgayogyā yathā bhavanti tathā vardhante | devyaṃ devānāṃ yogyaṃ [?] … yanti | [?] … anyat varpaḥ rūpaṃ pitroḥ dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ [?] sacā saha saṃbhūya [?] kṛṇvate kurvanti ‖ … [remainder of the small type not read]*

### Printed p. 128  (PDF 146)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 140".)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *saḥ* — Agni; *saṃstiraḥ* — (at one time) hidden, covered; *vistiraḥ* — (at another) spread out and coming into view; *saṃgṛbhāyati* — seizes (the fuel) by assailing it; *jānanneva* — as if knowing (the sacrificer's purpose) that he must grow; *jānatīḥ* — thus knowing, the flames; *nitye* — undying (?) [?]; *ā śaye* — takes refuge, lies down; *punaḥ* — again; *vardhante* — (these flames) grow by increase; *devyam* — the Agni who is divine, worthy of worship (by sacrifices etc.); *api yanti* — go and join; *sacā* — together with this sacrificial Agni; *pitroḥ* — their parents, or the protectors (of the world) heaven and earth; *anyat* — another, which was not before, wonderful; *varpaḥ* — (made of light) form; *kṛṇvate* — they make.

**Bhāvārtha.** Agni, at one time hidden, at another spread out and coming into view, seizes the fuel as if knowing that he must grow for the sacrificer, and takes refuge in the flames he knows. Though these flames have grown, they again grow in the same way. And they go to and join that Agni, who is worthy of worship and is useful in sacrifices and the like; together with this sacrificial Agni they make another, unprecedented form of light for their parents, heaven and earth, the protectors of the world.

**English Translation (as printed).** Now hidden, now displayed, he seizes (on the fuel), as if understanding (the purpose of the worshipper), and even reposes amidst the conscious (flames): again they break forth, and repair to the divine (fire of sacrifice), blending with which they give a different (luminous) form to their parent (heaven and earth).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** By the epithet *durgṛbhiḥ* in the previous Ṛk Agni's unobstructed power was shown; here the word *saṃgṛbhāyati* indicates the unobstructed spreading, and the epithets *saṃstiraḥ* and *vistiraḥ* explain the order of that spreading.

***jānanneva*** — *yajamānārthaṃ pravṛddhena bhavitavyam* [?] …: the sense is that he grows, knowing that he must be grown for the sacrificer. (continues on p. 129)

### Printed p. 129  (PDF 147)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 6 [?].)*

> जनस्य गोपा अजनिष्ट जागृविरग्निः सुदक्षः सुविताय नव्यसे । घृतप्रतीको बृहता दिविस्पृशा द्युमद्वि भाति भरतेभ्यः शुचिः ॥

> *janasya gopā ajaniṣṭa jāgṛviragniḥ sudakṣaḥ suvitāya navyase | ghṛtapratīko bṛhatā divispṛśā dyumadvi bhāti bharatebhyaḥ śuciḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?]; Tai. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?].) As described in these passages, so here too the favourable growth of Agni is praised.

***pitroḥ*** — *jagatpālayitroḥ*: the two protectors of the world, i.e. Heaven and Earth, or his own parents, Heaven and Earth.

> उत मन्ये पितुरद्रुहो मनो मातुर्महि स्वतवस्तद्धवीमभिः । सुरेतसा पितरा भूम चक्रतुरुरु प्रजाया अमृतं वरीमभिः [?] ॥

> *uta manye pituradruho mano māturmahi svatavastaddhavīmabhiḥ | suretasā pitarā bhūma cakratururu prajāyā amṛtaṃ varīmabhiḥ [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In many Ṛks like this, since Heaven and Earth are called the parents of the world (*jagatpitṛ*), the first sense is clear; and for the second sense:

> स रोचयज्जनुषा रोदसी उभे स मात्रोरभवत्पुत्र ईड्यः । हव्यवाळग्निरजरश्चनोहितो दूळभो [?] विशामतिथिर्विभावसुः ॥

> *sa rocayajjanuṣā rodasī ubhe sa mātrorabhavatputra īḍyaḥ | havyavāḷagnirajaraścanohito dūḷabho [?] viśāmatithirvibhāvasuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?].)

> अग्ने दिवः सूनुरसि प्रचेतास्तना पृथिव्या उत विश्ववेदाः । ऋधग्देवाँ इह यजा चिकित्वः ॥

> *agne divaḥ sūnurasi pracetāstanā pṛthivyā uta viśvavedāḥ | ṛdhagdevā~ iha yajā cikitvaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-25-1.) In these Ṛks Agni is said to be the son of Heaven and Earth; hence the second sense is stated; so too this very idea:

> स जातो गर्भो असि रोदस्योरग्ने चारुर्विभृत ओषधीषु । चित्रः शिशुः परि तमांस्यक्तून्प्र मातृभ्यो अधि कनिक्रदद्गाः ॥

> *sa jāto garbho asi rodasyoragne cārurvibhṛta oṣadhīṣu | citraḥ śiśuḥ pari tamāṃsyaktūnpra mātṛbhyo adhi kanikradadgāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-1-2.) is said; and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā too this Ṛk is cited as an illustration and Agni is praised.

***anyat varpaḥ kṛṇvate*** — they make an unprecedented form which was not there before. The sense is that, owing to the Mantra's power, Agni, with an exceeding brightness of his light, adorns the sacrificial ground.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar page, begun).** *saṃstiraḥ* — root *stṛñ ācchādane*; with the prefix *sam*, by the statement *ka prakaraṇe mūlavibhujādīnām upasaṃkhyānam* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-5 [?]), the suffix *ka*; … (continues on p. 130)

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तमग्रुवः केशिनीः सं हि रेभिर ऊर्ध्वास्तस्थुर्मम्रुषीः प्रायवे पुनः ।
> तासां जरां प्रमुञ्चन्नेति नानददसुं परं जनयञ्जीवमस्तृतम् ॥ ८ ॥

> *tamagruvaḥ keśinīḥ saṃ hi rebhira ūrdhvāstasthurmamruṣīḥ prāyave punaḥ |*
> *tāsāṃ jarāṃ pramuñcanneti nānadadasuṃ paraṃ janayañjīvamastṛtam ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तम् । अग्रुवः । केशिनीः । सम् । हि । रेभिरे । ऊर्ध्वाः । तस्थुः । मम्रुषीः । प्र । आयवे ।

> लोके काश्चन रमण्यो रमणेन सह निर्भरं क्रीडित्वा पश्चात्प्रोषिते तस्मिन्विरहेण जीर्णा म्रियमाणाः पश्चात्तस्मिन्नागते सति स्वप्राबल्यमगमयित्वा [?] संकोचेन [?] परिष्वङ्गाय चेष्टन्ते । स भर्ता मन्त्रोच्चारणेन जरामपनीयोचितप्रदानेन [?] प्राणयन् रक्षतीत्ययं भावोऽत्रानुसंधेयः [?] ॥

> *loke kāścana ramaṇyo ramaṇena saha nirbharaṃ krīḍitvā paścātproṣite tasminviraheṇa jīrṇā mriyamāṇāḥ paścāttasminnāgate sati svaprābalyamagamayitvā [?] saṃkocena [?] pariṣvaṅgāya ceṣṭante | sa bhartā mantroccāraṇena jarāmapanīyocitapradānena [?] prāṇayan rakṣatītyayaṃ bhāvo 'trānusaṃdheyaḥ [?] ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *tam* — Agni, (the husband); *agruvaḥ* — standing in front, or straight like fingers; *keśinīḥ* — dark like the hair on the head, those flames; *saṃrebhire hi* — they embrace, indeed; *mamruṣīḥ* — though they have gone out and are as if dead; *āyave* — to Agni, the husband coming to them; *punaḥ* — again (not noticing their own hardship); *ūrdhvāḥ* — rising upward; *pratasthuḥ* — stand facing him; *tāsām* — of those flames, so filled with love; *jarām* — the old-age-like slackness of body; *pramuñcan* — loosening; *nānadat* — sounding (as a husband murmurs a mantra to remove his wife's decrepitude); *param* — exceedingly; *asum* — vital energy; *astṛtam* — unimpaired; *jīvam* — the power of sustaining life; *janayan* — producing; *eti* — he joins (those flames).

**Bhāvārtha.** The beautiful flames, curving like the hair on the head and dark in their upper part, though extinguished and as if dead, rise upward like loving wives, not heeding their own hardship, as their husband Agni comes toward them, face him and embrace him. Loosening the slackness of body, like old age, of those loving flames, and making a sound as a husband murmurs a mantra to remove his wife's decrepitude, Agni produces in them exceeding energy and an unimpaired power of sustaining life, and joins the flames.

**English Translation (as printed).** The curving tresses (of the flames) embrace him (Agni), and when expiring spring aloft again to (greet) their coming (lord); rescuing them from decrepitude, he comes sounding aloud, generating (in them) intenser animation and unimpaired vitality.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***agruvaḥ*** — this word is read both in the names of rivers (Ni. 1-[?]-[?]) and in the names of fingers (Ni. 2-[?]-[?]); in both senses the word is used in the Ṛk-saṃhitā. (continues on p. 133)

> तमीं हिन्वन्त्यग्रुवो धमन्ति बाकुरं दृतिम् । त्रिधातुं वारणं मधु ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?]; this Ṛk is only partly legible at this resolution.)

> स्वध्वरा वि दुरो देवयन्तोऽश्रिश्रयू रथयुर्देवताता । पूर्वी शिशुं न मातरा रिहाणे समग्रुवो न समनेष्वञ्जन् ॥

> *svadhvarā vi duro devayanto 'śriśrayū rathayurdevatātā | pūrvī śiśuṃ na mātarā rihāṇe samagruvo na samaneṣvañjan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?].) In these Ṛks, "*agruvaḥ* is a river-name" — *agragāminīḥ nadīḥ*, rivers that spread and flow forward; hence the river is called *agru*, as the etymology says. And not only this:

> वस्त्रेभिः पुत्रमग्रुवो अदानं निवेशनाद्धरिव आ जभर्थ [?] । व्यङ्गो अख्यदहिमादादानो निर्भूदुखिच्छ्र [?] मुन्ते [?] सर्पः ॥

> *vastrebhiḥ putramagruvo adānaṃ niveśanāddhariva ā jabhartha [?] | vyaṅgo akhyadahimādādāno nirbhūdukhicchra [?] munte [?] sarpaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?].) In these Ṛks *agruvaḥ* appears to mean (the possessor of) a woman named *agrū* [?].

In the present Ṛk *agruvaḥ* is the epithet of the flames: either *agre sthitāḥ*, "spreading in front", or *aṅgulaya iva akuṭilāḥ*, "like fingers straight, not curved, stretched out". In this Ṛk Agni is compared to the husband and his flames to the wives. Sāyaṇa has described this comparison as follows:

> यथा लोके काश्चन रमण्यो रमणेन सह निर्भरं क्रीडित्वा पश्चात्प्रोषिते तस्मिन्विरहेण जीर्णा म्रियमाणाः पश्चात्तस्मिन्नागते सति स्वप्राबल्यमगमयित्वा [?] संकोचेन [?] परिष्वङ्गाय चेष्टन्ते । स भर्ता मन्त्रोच्चारणेन जरामपनीयोचितप्रदानेन [?] प्राणयन् रक्षतीत्ययं भावोऽत्रानुसंधेयः [?] ॥

> *yathā loke kāścana ramaṇyo ramaṇena saha nirbharaṃ krīḍitvā paścātproṣite tasminviraheṇa jīrṇā mriyamāṇāḥ paścāttasminnāgate sati svaprābalyamagamayitvā [?] saṃkocena [?] pariṣvaṅgāya ceṣṭante | sa bhartā mantroccāraṇena jarāmapanīyocitapradānena [?] prāṇayan rakṣatītyayaṃ bhāvo 'trānusaṃdheyaḥ [?] ‖*

In the world, women who have enjoyed their husbands' company and then, when the husbands go abroad, grow thin with grief, forget their own exhaustion on the husbands' return and strive eagerly to embrace them. In the same way the thinned flames of Agni, when fuel comes, embrace Agni. The husbands then recite mantras that remove the wives' emaciation and old age and fill them with new life; so too Agni, making a sound, removes the weakness of the flames and makes them grow: this is the sense. (continues on p. 134)

### Printed p. 136  (PDF 154)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 140".)*

*Bhāṣya of Ṛk 9 (concluding lines, small type).*

> … [?] सचते । सेवते । यत्र यत्राग्निर्गच्छति तत्र तत्र मार्गोऽपि कृष्णो भवति । अहेति प्रसिद्धौ ॥

> *… [?] sacate | sevate | yatra yatrāgnirgacchati tatra tatra mārgo 'pi kṛṣṇo bhavati | aheti prasiddhau ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *mātuḥ* — of the earth, the mother (of all beings); *adhīvāsam* — the grass, thickets and so on that lie like a covering over her; *pari* — all round; *rihan aha* — as if licking (invading); or: *mātuḥ* — for Mother Earth; *adhīvāsam* — an upper covering; *pari* — all round; *rihan* — procuring (by invading); *tuvigrebhiḥ* — making great noise (from fear); *satvabhiḥ* — together with the creatures; *jrayaḥ* — swiftly; *vi yāti* — spreads in various directions; *padvate* — (to all creatures with two or four feet); *vayaḥ* — food; *dadhat* — providing; *sadā* — always; *rerihat* — burning (the grass etc.); *śyenī* — dark-coloured; *vartanīḥ* — (this Agni's) path; *anu sacate aha* — follows (Agni), does it not?

**Bhāvārtha.** This forest-fire spreads swiftly in all directions: invading, as if licking, all the grass and thickets that lie like a covering over Mother Earth; providing food to all the creatures that move about; always burning the grass and the like; and joined by the creatures that cry out loudly in terror. The dark-coloured path follows Agni's path alone.

**English Translation (as printed).** Licking up the (verdant) vesture of the mother (of all things, earth) the rapid (Agni) proceeds with resounding existences: granting sustenance to (every) footed (creature): ever consuming (fuel), so that a blackened track follows (his path).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***mātuḥ adhīvāsaṃ pari rihan*** — Sāyaṇa shows that this can be explained in two ways. First: *mātuḥ* = *bhūtānāṃ nirmātuḥ bhūmeḥ*, of the earth, the maker of all beings; *adhīvāsam* = *uparyācchādanasthānīyaṃ tṛṇagulmauṣadhyādikam*, the grass, thickets and plants lying over her like a covering; *pari paritaḥ rihan lihan*, licking all round, i.e. invading. Second: *mātuḥ* = *bhūmeḥ*; *adhīvāsam* = *upari dhāryamāṇaṃ vastraṃ* (a garment worn over); *pari paritaḥ rihan saṃpādayan*: by his invasion all round procuring a covering for Mother Earth.

***padvate*** — *pādavate, dvipade catuṣpade ca*: for all creatures with two feet and four feet. (continues on p. 137)

### Printed p. 137  (PDF 155)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 6 [?].)*

It is customary to use the word *padvat* to denote living beings in general, and the word *apāt* to denote snakes and the like. For example —

> द्वे वै [?] अक्षरे भवत उभयोरन्नाद्ययोरुपाप्त्यै यच्च पद्वच्च [?] द्विपाच्च [?] पादाभ्यामिति [?] ।

> *dve vai [?] akṣare bhavata ubhayorannādyayorupāptyai yacca padvacca [?] dvipācca [?] pādābhyāmiti [?] |*

(Ai. Āraṇyaka 1-[?]-[?].) In this passage *padvat* is explained as animals with feet, and *apāt* as snakes and the like, without feet. But in the Ṛk-saṃhitā, in some Ṛks the word *padvat* is used only of creatures that walk on feet, while birds that fly are separately named, as is clear from these:

> आ घा योषेव सूनर्युषा याति प्रभुञ्जती । जरयन्ती वृजनं पद्वदीयत उत्पातयति पक्षिणः ॥

> *ā ghā yoṣeva sūnaryuṣā yāti prabhuñjatī | jarayantī vṛjanaṃ padvadīyata utpātayati pakṣiṇaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-48-[?].) Because *pakṣiṇaḥ* is separately named in this Ṛk, the word *padvat* is evidently meant only of creatures that move on feet. Likewise —

> नि ग्रामासो अविक्षत नि पद्वन्तो नि पक्षिणः । नि श्येनासश्चिदर्थिनः ॥

> *ni grāmāso avikṣata ni padvanto ni pakṣiṇaḥ | ni śyenāsaścidarthinaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) Here too *padvantaḥ* and *pakṣiṇaḥ* are separately named.

***tuvigrebhiḥ*** — the word *tuvi* is read among the names of the many (Ni. 3-1 [?]): *prabhūtaṃ śabdayadbhiḥ*, those making great noise; as an epithet of *satvabhiḥ*, the creatures that cry out loudly in terror at the spread of the forest-fire. Or, *prabhūtagamanaiḥ*, as creatures that run in all directions (Sāyaṇa says it can also be so explained).

***jrayaḥ*** — *jrayasā javena*, swiftly. In the lists of verbs of motion (*gatikarmanāmāni*) the roots *vartate*, *ayate*, *loṭate* etc. are read, among which *jrayati* "goes" is also read (Ni. 2-[?]); so *jraya* is "motion". But the word is used for the speed that marks a particular kind of motion. For example:

> यावृग्वैव देव्यते तान्यग्मं [?] ते सं थायया दधिरे सिप्रयोप्ताः [?] । महीमेषामुरुषामुरुज्रयो बृहत्कवीरमनपत्यकं सहः [?] ॥

> *yāvṛgvaiva devyate tānyagmaṃ [?] te saṃ thāyayā dadhire siprayoptāḥ [?] | mahīmeṣāmuruṣāmurujrayo bṛhatkavīramanapatyakaṃ sahaḥ [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?]; this Ṛk is garbled at this resolution and is given only as far as read.)

> अवितासि सुन्वतो वृक्तबर्हिषः पिबा सोमं मदाय कं शतक्रतो । यं ते भागमधारयन्विश्वाः सेहानः पृतना उरु ज्रयः समप्सुजिन्मृत्येन्द्र सत्पते [?] ॥

> *avitāsi sunvato vṛktabarhiṣaḥ pibā somaṃ madāya kaṃ śatakrato | yaṃ te bhāgamadhārayanviśvāḥ sehānaḥ pṛtanā uru jrayaḥ samapsujinmṛtyendra satpate [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?].) (continues on p. 138)

### Printed p. 138  (PDF 156)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 140".)*

In these and similar Ṛks the word *jrayaḥ* is explained as "speed". And again —

> प्रतिभद्रा अदृक्षत गवां सर्गा न रश्मयः । ओषा अप्रा उरु ज्रयः ॥

> *pratibhadrā adṛkṣata gavāṃ sargā na raśmayaḥ | oṣā aprā uru jrayaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?].) Here the word *jraya* means great brilliance (*mahattvāda tejas*); but the speed of power is suggested here too. In the present Ṛk also, the speed of the creatures running in all directions in utmost fear at the time of the forest-fire's spread is what is stated.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 9; grammar pages 138–139, noted briefly).** Headwords: *adhīvāsam* (root *vasa ācchādane*, suffix *ghañ*; *vṛddhi* of the penultimate by *ata upadhāyāḥ*; lengthening of the earlier member by *anyeṣām api dṛśyate*; accent), *mātuḥ* (root *māṅ māne*; suffix *tṛc*; *cita*: last-syllable accent), *rihan* (root *rihi* [?], *tudādi*; *śatṛ*; the *śa* suffix), *tuvigrebhiḥ* (*bahulaṃ chandasi*: no *ais* for *bhis*; accent), *yāti* (root *yā prāpaṇe*, *adādi*; *tiṅ*, hence *nighāta*), *jrayaḥ* (root *jri abhibhave*; *sarvadhātubhyo 'sun*; *nit*, first-syllable accent), *dadhat* (root *dudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*, *juhotyādi*; *śatṛ*; *abhyastānām ādiḥ*), *padvate* (*padasyāsti ity padvat*; *matup*, its *m* becomes *v*; dative singular; accent). #### Ṛk 10

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अस्माकमग्ने मघवत्सु दीदिह्यध श्वसीवान्वृषभो दमूनाः ।
> अवास्या [?] शिशुमतीरदीदेर्वर्मेव युत्सु परिजर्भुराणः ॥ १० ॥

> *asmākamagne maghavatsu dīdihyadha śvasīvānvṛṣabho damūnāḥ |*
> *avāsyā [?] śiśumatīradīdervarmeva yutsu parijarbhurāṇaḥ ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अस्माकम् । अग्ने । मघवत्ऽसु । दीदिहि । अध । श्वसीऽवान् । वृषभः । दमूनाः ।
> अव । अस्य [?] । शिशुऽमतीः । अदीदेः । वर्मऽइव । युत्ऽसु । परिऽजर्भुराणः ॥ १० ॥

> *asmākam | agne | maghavat 'su | dīdihi | adha | śvasī 'vān | vṛṣabhaḥ | damūnāḥ |*
> *ava | asya [?] | śiśu 'matīḥ | adīdeḥ | varma 'iva | yut 'su | pari 'jarbhurāṇaḥ ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *O Agni, shine in our wealthy houses; vivifying us, showering boons, be bountiful; forsaking the infant flames, blaze, and like armour in battles ward off the blows.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> हे अग्ने अस्माकं मघवत्सु स्वसंबन्धिषु धनवत्सु यागेषु गृहेषु वा दीदिहि दीप्यस्व । अथानन्तरं श्वसीवान् श्वसनवान् ज्वालाभिः प्राणवान् अस्मान् [?] … वृषभो वर्षिता अभिमतानां दमूनाः दानमनाः दमना दान्तमना वा सर्वत्र भव । स उक्तलक्षणस्त्वं शिशुमतीः [?] … तदवस्थाः लक्ष्यन्ते श्वसनवतीर्ज्वाला [?] … विहायादीदेः भृशं दीप्यस्व [?] … युत्सु

> *he agne asmākaṃ maghavatsu svasaṃbandhiṣu dhanavatsu yāgeṣu gṛheṣu vā dīdihi dīpyasva | athānantaraṃ śvasīvān śvasanavān jvālābhiḥ prāṇavān asmān [?] … vṛṣabho varṣitā abhimatānāṃ damūnāḥ dānamanāḥ damanā dāntamanā vā sarvatra bhava | sa uktalakṣaṇastvaṃ śiśumatīḥ [?] … tadavasthāḥ lakṣyante śvasanavatīrjvālā [?] … vihāyādīdeḥ bhṛśaṃ dīpyasva [?] … yutsu*

### Printed p. 140  (PDF 158)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 140".)*

*Bhāṣya (continued, small type).*

> संग्रामेषु वर्मेव परिजर्भुराणो भव ॥ हरतेर्यङ्लुगन्ताच्छानच् [?] । अभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ उक्तगुणको भवानस्माकं मघवत्सु यज्ञेषु दीप्यस्व ॥

> *saṃgrāmeṣu varmeva parijarbhurāṇo bhava ‖ harateryaṅlugantācchānac [?] | abhyastānāmādirityādyudāttatvam ‖ uktaguṇako bhavānasmākaṃ maghavatsu yajñeṣu dīpyasva ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *agne* — O Agni; *asmākam* — of us; *maghavatsu* — in our sacrificial houses, filled with food; *dīdihi* — shine; *adha* — afterwards; *śvasīvān* — burning with flames, that is, making us full of life; *vṛṣabhaḥ* — the one who showers desired objects; *damūnāḥ* — be generous, or of a self-controlled mind; *śiśumatīḥ* — the young (dim) flames; *avāsya* — leaving off, leaving off; *adīdeḥ* — blaze exceedingly; *yutsu* — in battles; *varmeva* — as armour protects; *pari jarbhurāṇaḥ* — warding off (the repeated blows of enemies) again and again, protect us.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, shine exceedingly in our sacrificial houses, filled with food. Then, making us full of life with your flames, be both the one who showers desired objects and the generous one. Leaving off the dim young flames, shine with your fierce flames. As a coat of mail protects in battles, ward off the repeated blows of enemies and protect us.

**English Translation (as printed).** Shine, Agni, in our opulent (abodes), vivifying, showering (blssings [sic]) bounteous, casting off infantine (glimmerings): blaze (fiercely), repelling repeatedly like a coat of mail, (our enemies) in combats.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***asmākam*** — this word is used ordinarily only in the sense of the genitive (*ṣaṣṭhī*); but there are also places where it is used by way of a mere indication of the other cases (*vibhakti*). Many such uses will be noted; in some places it has the sense of a verbal modifier.

> नू नो अग्न ऊतये सबाधसश्च रातये । अस्माकासश्च सूरयो विश्वा आशास्तरीषणि ॥

> *nū no agna ūtaye sabādhasaśca rātaye | asmākāsaśca sūrayo viśvā āśāstarīṣaṇi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-10-[?].) In this the word *sūrayaḥ* is used with *asmākāsaḥ* in the nominative (*prathamā*),

### Printed p. 141  (PDF 159)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 6 [?].)*

> स रथेन रथीतमोऽस्माकेनाभियुग्वना । जेषि जिष्णो हितं धनम् ॥

> *sa rathena rathītamo 'smākenābhiyugvanā | jeṣi jiṣṇo hitaṃ dhanam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?].) and here in the instrumental (*tṛtīyā*). So the word *asme* also is used with all case endings, as the Nirukta author shows with examples (Ni. [?]-[?]); the particulars are given in the Special Topics of Ṛk 1-10-3.

***damūnāḥ*** — *damūnā damanā vā, dānamanā vā, dāntamanā vā; api vā dama iti gṛhanāma tanmanāḥ syāt* (Ni. [?]). The epithet *damūnāḥ* is either because he has a mind full of compassion (*dayāpūrita*) [?], or one that gives, or because he is given to self-control; or, as *dama* is a synonym of "house", the word can mean one whose mind is attached to the house (Ni. [?]). Therefore Sāyaṇa too explains it as: "be of a giving mind, a mind of self-control, a house-loving mind, everywhere", and so prays to Agni.

***varma iva*** — *kavacam iva*: like armour; the protection to be had from Agni is compared with armour.

> न तस्य मायया चन रिपुरीशीत मर्त्यः । यो अग्नये ददाश हव्यदातिभिः ॥

> *na tasya māyayā cana ripurīśīta martyaḥ | yo agnaye dadāśa havyadātibhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].) In these Ṛks it is said that no enemy, however powerful, can harm one who has obtained Agni's shelter; such protection is prayed for here for ourselves as well.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 10; grammar pages 141–142, noted briefly).** Headwords: *maghavatsu* (*maghaṃ eṣām asti*; suffix *matup*; *pit*; locative plural), *dīdihi* (root *dīdī dīptau*, Vedic; *loṭ* second person singular; *śap* lost by *luk*), *adha* (Vedic change of the letter: *tha* → *dha*), *śvasīvān* (root *śvasa prāṇane*; *matup*; *pit*: the root accent is lost), *vṛṣabhaḥ* (root *vṛṣu secane*; suffix *abhac* by *ṛśivṛṣibhyāṃ kit* (Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]); *kit*, so no *guṇa*; *cita*, last-syllable accent). (continues on p. 142)

#### Ṛk 11

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> इदमग्ने सुधितं दुर्धितादधि प्रियादु चिन्मन्मनः प्रेयो अस्तु ते ।
> यत्ते शुक्रं तन्वो रोचते शुचि तेनास्मभ्यं वनसे रत्नमा त्वम् ॥ ११ ॥

> *idamagne sudhitaṃ durdhitādadhi priyādu cinmanmanaḥ preyo astu te |*
> *yatte śukraṃ tanvo rocate śuci tenāsmabhyaṃ vanase ratnamā tvam ‖ 11 ‖*

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 6 [?].)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> इदम् । अग्ने । सुऽधितम् । दुःऽधितात् । अधि । प्रियात् । ऊं इति । चित् । मन्मनः ।
> प्रेयः । अस्तु । ते । यत् । ते । शुक्रम् । तन्वः । रोचते । शुचि । तेन । अस्मभ्यम् । वनसे । रत्नम् । आ । त्वम् ॥ ११ ॥

> *idam | agne | su 'dhitam | duḥ 'dhitāt | adhi | priyāt | ūṃ iti | cit | manmanaḥ |*
> *preyaḥ | astu | te | yat | te | śukram | tanvaḥ | rocate | śuci | tena | asmabhyam | vanase | ratnam | ā | tvam ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *O Agni, may this oblation, well placed on hard fuel, be dearer to you than anything dear; with the pure brightness of your body, bring us treasure.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> हे अग्ने इदमस्मदीयं सोमादिरूपं हविः । कीदृशं तत् । दुर्धितात् दुःस्थापितात् [?] काष्ठादेः अधि उपरि सुधितं सुहितं सुस्थापितं वर्तते । मन्मनः मननीयं [?] प्रियादु चित् यदपि तव प्रियाद्वस्तुनोऽपि [?] … प्रेयः प्रियतरं अस्तु ते तव । … यत्ते तव तन्वः शरीरस्य ज्वालात्मकस्य [?] … शुक्रं शुक्लं निर्मलं शुचि दीप्तं … तेजो रोचते तेन सह रत्नं रमणीयं मणिमुक्तादिकं इतरत् … अस्मभ्यं वनसे त्वमा सम्भजस्व । वनतेर्व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं ॥ [partly unread]

> *he agne idamasmadīyaṃ somādirūpaṃ haviḥ | kīdṛśaṃ tat | durdhitāt duḥsthāpitāt [?] kāṣṭhādeḥ adhi upari sudhitaṃ suhitaṃ susthāpitaṃ vartate | manmanaḥ mananīyaṃ [?] priyādu cit yadapi tava priyādvastuno 'pi [?] … preyaḥ priyataraṃ astu te tava | … yatte tava tanvaḥ śarīrasya jvālātmakasya [?] … śukraṃ śuklaṃ nirmalaṃ śuci dīptaṃ … tejo rocate tena saha ratnaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ maṇimuktādikaṃ itarat … asmabhyaṃ vanase tvamā sambhajasva | vanatervyatyayenātmanepadaṃ ‖ [partly unread]*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *agne* — O Agni; *durdhitāt adhi* — upon hard fuel and the like; *sudhitam* — placed with care; *idam* — this oblation of Soma and the like; *manmanaḥ* — worthy of praise; *priyādu cit* — than all things beneficial (and dear); *preyaḥ* — most dear; *astu* — be; *te* — to you; *tanvaḥ* — of the body (blazing as flames with the ghee); *śuci* — pure; *śukram* — shining; *yat* — which brightness; *rocate* — shines; *tena* — with that; *tvam* — you; *ratnam* — delightful wealth; *asmabhyam* — to us; *ā vanase* — fill (and give).

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, may this oblation of Soma and the like, placed with care upon hard fuel, worthy of praise and beneficial, be dearer to you than all other things. Coming with the pure, shining brightness of your flame-body, kindled by ghee, give us delightful wealth, fully.

**English Translation (as printed).** May this oblation, Agni, carefully placed upon the rugged but agreeable (pile of fuel), be most acceptable to you, so that the pure radiance of your person may shine brightly, and you may grant us wealth.

### Printed p. 144  (PDF 162)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 140".)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***durdhitāt adhi sudhitam*** — the prayer to Agni is that, though the fuel is hard, the oblations placed on it be both well placed and beneficial.

***manmanaḥ*** — *manma* is explained as "worthy of thought, of meditation"; in the sense of "praiseworthy, worshipful" this word is used in many Ṛks, e.g. 1-[?]-[?]; 1-[?]-[?]; 1-[?]-[?]. In these and many other Ṛks the words *manmanā*, *manmabhiḥ* denote the mental activity (*manaḥpravṛtti*) that is full of praise and worthy of praise. The Nirukta author cites three Ṛks in which the word *manma* is used. First —

> उप प्रागात्सुमन्मेधायि मन्म देवानामाशा उप वीतपृष्ठाः [?] । अन्वेनं विप्रा ऋषयो मदन्ति देवानां पुष्टे चकृमा सुबन्धुम् ॥

> *upa prāgātsumanmedhāyi manma devānāmāśā upa vītapṛṣṭhāḥ [?] | anvenaṃ viprā ṛṣayo madanti devānāṃ puṣṭe cakṛmā subandhum ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk the Nirukta author explains *manma* as *mantra* (Ni. 6-[?]); the sense is "a mantra worthy of meditation". Sāyaṇa explains it as "a fruit worthy of meditation". Second —

> तनूनपात्पथ ऋतस्य यानान्मध्वा समञ्जन्त्स्वदया सुजिह्व । मन्मानि धीभिरुत यज्ञमृन्धन्देवत्रा च कृणुह्यध्वरं नः ॥

> *tanūnapātpatha ṛtasya yānānmadhvā samañjantsvadayā sujihva | manmāni dhībhiruta yajñamṛndhandevatrā ca kṛṇuhyadhvaraṃ naḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-[?].) Here Sāyaṇa explains *asmadabhipretāni stotrāṇi*, "the hymns desired by us". Likewise the Nirukta author cites 1-[?]-[?] (Ni. 11-[?]) and shows that the same sense results there. In the present Ṛk the sense "worthy of praise" results.

***te tanvaḥ śuci śukram*** — "the pure and shining brightness of the flame-form body, kindled by the ghee": thus, on the offering of the oblation, the peculiarity of Agni's brightness is described.

> अग्निः शुचिव्रततमः शुचिर्विप्रः शुचिः कविः । शुची रोचत आहुतः । उदग्ने शुचयस्तव शुक्रा भ्राजन्त ईरते । तव ज्योतींष्यर्चयः ॥

> *agniḥ śucivratatamaḥ śucirvipraḥ śuciḥ kaviḥ | śucī rocata āhutaḥ | udagne śucayastava śukrā bhrājanta īrate | tava jyotīṃṣyarcayaḥ ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-3-[?].) As this is described in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, so Agni's pure brightness is described here.

***ratnam*** — the word *ratna* is read among the names of wealth (Ni. 2-[?]); "delightful wealth" is the sense. (continues on p. 145)

#### Ṛk 12

### Printed p. 146  (PDF 164)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 140".)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> रथाय नावमुत नो गृहाय नित्यारित्रां पद्वतीं रास्यग्ने ।
> अस्माकं वीराँ उत नो मघोनो जनाँश्च या पारयाच्छर्म या च ॥ १२ ॥

> *asmākaṃ vīrā~ uta no maghono janā~śca yā pārayāccharma yā ca ‖ 12 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अस्माकम् । वीरान् । उत । नः । मघोनः । जनान् । च । या । पारयात् । शर्म । या । च ॥ १२ ॥

> *rathāya | nāvam | uta | naḥ | gṛhāya | nitya 'aritrām | pat 'vatīm | rāsi | agne |*
> *asmākam | vīrān | uta | naḥ | maghonaḥ | janān | ca | yā | pārayāt | śarma | yā | ca ‖ 12 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *O Agni, give our sacrificer the boat that carries across worldly existence — the Soma-sacrifice, equipped with oars and feet — which makes our heroic sons rich and bears our people across to the bliss of Brahma's world.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> हे अग्ने उतापि च रथाय रंहणाय गृहाय सर्वस्याश्रयभूताय [?] नोऽस्माकं यजमानानां नावं संसारोत्तारिकां सोमयागात्मिकां नावं । यज्ञो वै सुतमः [?] नौरित्यादिषु श्रुतिषु नौरूपेण स्तुतत्वात् । कीदृशीं तां । नित्यारित्रां नियतैरित्रैः [?] … पद्वतीं … ह्रस्वस्येत्यादिना मतुपः उदात्तत्वम् ॥ … [middle lines of the small type not read] … यो नः शर्म सुखं निरतिशयं ब्रह्म [?] प्रापयेत् … कृतसर्वाणाम् [?] … [remainder not read]

> *he agne utāpi ca rathāya raṃhaṇāya gṛhāya sarvasyāśrayabhūtāya [?] no 'smākaṃ yajamānānāṃ nāvaṃ saṃsārottārikāṃ somayāgātmikāṃ nāvaṃ | yajño vai sutamaḥ [?] naurityādiṣu śrutiṣu naurūpeṇa stutatvāt | kīdṛśīṃ tāṃ | nityāritrāṃ niyatairitraiḥ [?] … padvatīṃ … hrasvasyetyādinā matupaḥ udāttatvam ‖ … [middle lines of the small type not read] … yo naḥ śarma sukhaṃ niratiśayaṃ brahma [?] prāpayet … kṛtasarvāṇām [?] … [remainder not read]*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *agne* — O Agni; *nityāritrām* — having ever-ready oars [?]; *padvatīm* — having feet in the form of the substances, deities, mantras and so on; *uta* — and; *yā* — that which; *asmākam* — our; *vīrān* — heroic sons; *maghonaḥ* — rich ones (makes); *uta* — and; *naḥ* — our; *janān ca* — sacrificers too; *pārayāt* — carries across (from worldly existence); *yā* — which; *śarma* — (gives) the bliss (of the supreme world of Brahma); *nāvam* — the boat (consisting of the Soma-sacrifice); *rathāya* — to the dear one [?]; *gṛhāya* — to him who is a shelter like a house; *naḥ* — to our sacrificer; *rāsi* — give.

### Printed p. 147  (PDF 165)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 6 [?].)*

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, grant to our sacrificer, who is dear and a shelter like a house, the boat — consisting of the Soma-sacrifice — whose oars are the everlasting priests, and which has feet in the form of substances, deities, mantras and the like; which makes our heroic sons rich; which carries (us, the performers of the sacrifice, or our sacrificers) across worldly existence and gives the supreme bliss of Brahma's world.

**English Translation (as printed).** Bestow, Agni, upon our excellent patron a boat ever fitted with oars and feet, (one that may render) our posterity prosperous, and may bear mankind across (the ocean of life) to felicity.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** In this Ṛk the sacrifice is compared to a boat, worldly existence (*saṃsāra*) to the ocean, and the priests (*ṛtvijaḥ*) to the oars. Poverty, fear of enemies and other kinds of sorrow are the dreadful circumstances of the ocean of worldly existence. If one is to cross this ocean, it cannot be done without the boat as a stout means; this boat must carry the sacrificer safely across the ocean; and the boat cannot do so without its oars. Hence the prayer is that the boat of the Soma-sacrifice, driven by the excellent priests as oars, may carry us safely across worldly existence.

In the Ṛks it is commonly seen that poverty and similar sorrows, the sin that causes them, an enemy, are compared to a deep flood of water, and the help of the gods to a boat; this is a most fitting comparison. For example —

> जातवेदसे सुनवाम सोममरातीयतो नि दहाति वेदः । स नः पर्षदति दुर्गाणि विश्वा नावेव सिन्धुं दुरितात्यग्निः ॥

> *jātavedase sunavāma somamarātīyato ni dahāti vedaḥ | sa naḥ parṣadati durgāṇi viśvā nāveva sindhuṃ duritātyagniḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-99-1.)

### Printed p. 148  (PDF 166)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 140".)*

> नू नो इन्द्रावरुणा गृणाना पृङ्क्तं रयिं सौश्रवसाय देवा । इत्था गृणन्तो महिनस्य शर्धोऽपो न नावा दुरिता तरेम ॥

> *nū no indrāvaruṇā gṛṇānā pṛṅktaṃ rayiṃ sauśravasāya devā | itthā gṛṇanto mahinasya śardho 'po na nāvā duritā tarema ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?].) In these and other Ṛks, just as one crosses a river easily by boat, so the prayer is that by the help of Agni, Indra and other gods we may cross over sin (*durita*); and so here Agni is prayed to bestow the boat consisting of the sacrifice. Here it is said that the service of the boat consisting of the Soma-sacrifice is threefold: first, it makes the sacrificers and their sons wealthy; second, it carries the sacrificers across worldly existence; third, it gives the bliss of Brahma's world — thus Sāyaṇa has explained the passage *asmākaṃ vīrān maghonaḥ; uta no janāṃś ca pārayāt; yā śarma nāvam*. Not only in the Ṛk-saṃhitā but also in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa the same comparison is well known. For example —

> नौर्ह वा एषा स्वर्ग्या यद्बहिष्पवमानं तस्या ऋत्विज इव स्फ्याश्चारित्राणि [?] स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य संपारणाय [?] तस्या एक एव मज्जयिता य एव निन्द्यः [?] स यथा पूर्णामभ्यारुह्य मज्जयेदेवं हैनां समज्जयति केद्वे सर्व एव यज्ञो नः स्वर्ग्या तस्मादु सर्वस्मादेव यज्ञानिन्द्यं परिबिबाधिषेत ।

> *naurha vā eṣā svargyā yadbahiṣpavamānaṃ tasyā ṛtvija iva sphyāścāritrāṇi [?] svargasya lokasya saṃpāraṇāya [?] tasyā eka eva majjayitā ya eva nindyaḥ [?] sa yathā pūrṇāmabhyāruhya majjayedevaṃ haināṃ samajjayati kedve sarva eva yajño naḥ svargyā tasmādu sarvasmādeva yajñānindyaṃ paribibādhiṣeta |*

(Śa. Brā. 4-[?]-[?]-[?].) The Soma-sacrifice, and the *bahiṣpavamāna* hymn that is to be recited on the first day of the Soma-sacrifice, are boats that carry one to heaven; the priests themselves are their oarsmen. If even one of these priests is of a blameworthy way of life, he will cause this boat to sink. Therefore such a one must be kept away from the sacrificial act: so says the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa; and likewise —

> यज्ञो वै सुशर्मा नौः ।

> *yajño vai suśarmā nauḥ |*

(Ai. Brā. 1-[?].)

> नावमिवारुहेमेति सम् एव नावमेतदधिरोहति स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य समृत्यै । संपत्त्यै संगत्यै ॥

> *nāvamivāruhemeti sam eva nāvametadadhirohati svargasya lokasya samṛtyai | saṃpattyai saṃgatyai ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 4-[?].) Thus in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa also this comparison is well known. And as the fruit of this sacrifice is exceedingly great, even the gods desire it and are devoted to sacrifice; so, following them, men too should be devoted to sacrificial work: thus it is taught — (continues on p. 149)

### Printed p. 149  (PDF 167)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 6 [?].)*

> ते आसते श्रियं गच्छेमा यशः स्यामान्नादाः स्यामेति । ते होचुः । यो नः श्रमेण तपसा श्रद्धया यज्ञस्योद्देशं पूर्वो वा गच्छात्स नः श्रेष्ठोऽसत् सर्वेषां सहेति । तद्विष्णुः प्रथमः प्राप । स देवानां श्रेष्ठो [?] भवत्तस्मादाहुर्विष्णुर्देवानां श्रेष्ठ इति ।

> *te āsate śriyaṃ gacchemā yaśaḥ syāmānnādāḥ syāmeti | te hocuḥ | yo naḥ śrameṇa tapasā śraddhayā yajñasyoddeśaṃ pūrvo vā gacchātsa naḥ śreṣṭho 'sat sarveṣāṃ saheti | tadviṣṇuḥ prathamaḥ prāpa | sa devānāṃ śreṣṭho [?] bhavattasmādāhurviṣṇurdevānāṃ śreṣṭha iti |*

(Śa. Brā. [?]-[?]-[?]-[?]; the passage is garbled at this resolution and is given only as read.) By the practice of sacrifice, fruit and the place of the boat and birth-wealth are obtained [?]; so the gods wished for it and performed sacrifice. Since Viṣṇu among them attained the first place, he became the best among the gods: thus the fruit of sacrifice is praised. And likewise —

> तस्माद्धाहुः पुण्यलोक ईजान इति ।

> *tasmāddhāhuḥ puṇyaloka ījāna iti |*

(Śa. Brā. [?]-[?]-[?]-[?].) What this says — that the sacrificer becomes lord of the world of merit — is just what is suggested in the present Ṛk by the word *śarma*. For the word *śarma* Sāyaṇa gives *sukhaṃ niratiśayaṃ brahma prāpayet*, "may it bring the unsurpassed bliss of Brahma's world", and cites, to explain the word *śarma*, the sentence of the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad:

> विविदिषन्ति यज्ञेन दानेन ।

> *vividiṣanti yajñena dānena |*

(Bṛ. U. 4-4-22.) Thus the boat that bestows so excellent a fruit, consisting of the Soma-sacrifice, is prayed of Agni for the sacrificer.

***rathāya*** — *raṃhaṇāya yajamānāya*: the word is thus shown to be an epithet of the sacrificer. For the word *ratha* the Nirukta author says: *ratho raṃhater gatikarmaṇaḥ; sthirater vā syād viparītasya; ramater vā; rasater vā* (Ni. 9-[?]): that is, from the root *raṃh* meaning going or speed; or, with a change of letters, from *sthira*; or from the root *ram*, "those who sit in it rejoice"; or from the root *ras*, "it makes a sound"; and the Nirukta author shows this derivation of *ratha* under the Ṛk *vanaspate vīḍvaṅgo* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-4[?]-[?]). But in the present Ṛk the word must be an epithet of the sacrificer, and so one of these senses must be shown: the sacrificer is eager for the performance of the sacrifice and active; or, he is of steady mind when he is initiated (*dīkṣita*); or, he utters sounds of praise. Since the epithet *rāsmanasya* [?] (1-[?]-[?]) is given him, the epithet *rathāya* may belong to the sacrificer in any of the senses stated by the Nirukta author. (continues on p. 150)

### Printed p. 150  (PDF 168)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 140".)*

***rathāya, gṛhāya*** — the two epithets suggest the greatness of the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice, and his divine position, which produces good for the whole world. Because he is the cause of the origin and continuance of the sacrifice, and the cause of the sacrifice, in many places identity (*tādātmya*) is declared between the two; hence identity is also declared between the sacrificer and Prajāpati. In explaining the sacrificer's supernatural power the Taittirīya Saṃhitā says that he becomes the acquirer of a dwelling in heaven, the support of the greatest bliss:

> नाकसद्भिर्वै देवास्स्वर्गं लोकमायन्नाकसदां नाकसत्त्वं यन्नाकसद उपदधाति नाकसद्भिरेव तद्यजमानस्स्वर्गं लोकमेति सुवर्गो वै लोको नाकः [?] … नास्मा अकं भवति यजमानायतनं वै नाकसदो यन्नाकसद उपदधात्यायतनमेव तद्यजमानः कुरुते पृष्ठानां वा एते तेजः संभृतं यन्नाकसदो यन्नाकसद [?] …

> *nākasadbhirvai devāssvargaṃ lokamāyannākasadāṃ nākasattvaṃ yannākasada upadadhāti nākasadbhireva tadyajamānassvargaṃ lokameti suvargo vai loko nākaḥ [?] … nāsmā akaṃ bhavati yajamānāyatanaṃ vai nākasado yannākasada upadadhātyāyatanameva tadyajamānaḥ kurute pṛṣṭhānāṃ vā ete tejaḥ saṃbhṛtaṃ yannākasado yannākasada [?] …*

(Tai. Saṃ. 5-3-[?]-[?]; garbled in part at this resolution.) In these sentences the nature of the sacrificer's house (*gṛha*) and its special features are described in detail — what excellent dwelling the sacrificer, skilled in the work of building the altar and in the piling of the fire (*agnicayana*), brings about; hence the epithet *gṛhāya* in the present Ṛk gathers the same point. The word *gṛha* here may mean a worldly house with every kind of wealth, or a dwelling in heaven with exceeding good fortune.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 12; grammar pages 150–151, noted briefly).** *nāvam* (root *ṇud preraṇe*; suffix *ḍau* by *glānudibhyāṃ ḍau* (Uṇ. Sū. 2-[?]); by the power of *ḍit* the *ṭi* of the root is dropped; final-syllable accent; accusative singular, *am* for *am*), *gṛhāya* (root *graha upādāne*; *loṭ* second person singular; *hi* substitution; *chandasi śāyajapi* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-[?]), *śāyac* for *śap*; *ato heḥ* gives *luk*; by *vyatyaya* no *bhava*), *nityāritrām* (*nityaṃ niyataṃ aritraṃ yasyāḥ sā*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*: the earlier member keeps its accent). (continues on p. 151)

#### Ṛk 13

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अभी नो अग्न उक्थमिज्जुगुर्या द्यावाक्षामा सिन्धवश्च स्वगूर्ताः ।
> गव्यं यव्यं यन्तो दीर्घाहेषं वरमरुण्यो वरन्त ॥ १३ ॥

> *abhī no agna ukthamijjuguryā dyāvākṣāmā sindhavaśca svagūrtāḥ |*
> *gavyaṃ yavyaṃ yanto dīrghāheṣaṃ varamaruṇyo varanta ‖ 13 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अभि । नः । अग्ने । उक्थम् । इत् । जुगुर्याः । द्यावाक्षामा । सिन्धवः । च । स्वऽगूर्ताः ।
> गव्यम् । यव्यम् । यन्तः । दीर्घाहा । इषम् । वरम् । अरुण्यः । वरन्त ॥ १३ ॥

> *abhi | naḥ | agne | uktham | it | juguryāḥ | dyāvākṣāmā | sindhavaḥ | ca | sva 'gūrtāḥ |*
> *gavyam | yavyam | yantaḥ | dīrghāhā | iṣam | varam | aruṇyaḥ | varanta ‖ 13 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *O Agni, approve our hymn by praising it; may heaven and earth and the self-flowing rivers bring us milk and barley-cakes; may the ruddy dawns bring us food through the long days.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> हे अग्ने नः उक्थं शस्त्रमभि जुगुर्याः । अभिमुखेन स्तुहि प्रोत्साहय । सम्यक् शस्त्रमिति अंगीकुरु इति । गृ शब्दे । लिङि छन्दसि [?] … बहुलं छन्दसीत्यादिना [?] प्रोत्साहयताम् । तथा द्यावाक्षामा द्यावापृथिव्यौ यज्ञसाधनसंपादनेन प्रोत्साहयताम् । तथा सिन्धवः स्यन्दनशीला नद्यश्च स्वगूर्ताः स्वयमेव गामिन्यः गव्यं गोसमूहं क्षीरादिकं गवां तृणाम्भस्संपादनद्वारा यव्यं । उपलक्षणमेतत् । यवव्रीह्यादिजन्यं पुरोडाशादिकं यन्तः प्रापयन्तः प्रोत्साहयन्तु । तथा अरुण्यः अरुणवर्णगोयुक्ता मत्स्यर्थो [?] उषसः [?] … आरुण्यसाधनभूता उषसः तद्देषु [?] दीर्घाहा सर्वाण्यहानि सर्वकालमिष्यमाणमन्नमरादिकं वरं वरणीयं श्रेष्ठमन्नमपि [?] यागसाधनं वरन्त वृण्वन्तु । प्रापयन्तु । वृञ् संभक्तौ । अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थः [?] … छान्दसो लङ् [?] … प्रसादादित्यग्नेरेव स्तुतित्वादग्नेरेवात्र [?] … ॥ [partly unread]

> *he agne naḥ ukthaṃ śastramabhi juguryāḥ | abhimukhena stuhi protsāhaya | samyak śastramiti aṃgīkuru iti | gṛ śabde | liṅi chandasi [?] … bahulaṃ chandasītyādinā [?] protsāhayatām | tathā dyāvākṣāmā dyāvāpṛthivyau yajñasādhanasaṃpādanena protsāhayatām | tathā sindhavaḥ syandanaśīlā nadyaśca svagūrtāḥ svayameva gāminyaḥ gavyaṃ gosamūhaṃ kṣīrādikaṃ gavāṃ tṛṇāmbhassaṃpādanadvārā yavyaṃ | upalakṣaṇametat | yavavrīhyādijanyaṃ puroḍāśādikaṃ yantaḥ prāpayantaḥ protsāhayantu | tathā aruṇyaḥ aruṇavarṇagoyuktā matsyartho [?] uṣasaḥ [?] … āruṇyasādhanabhūtā uṣasaḥ taddeṣu [?] dīrghāhā sarvāṇyahāni sarvakālamiṣyamāṇamannamarādikaṃ varaṃ varaṇīyaṃ śreṣṭhamannamapi [?] yāgasādhanaṃ varanta vṛṇvantu | prāpayantu | vṛñ saṃbhaktau | antarbhāvitaṇyarthaḥ [?] … chāndaso laṅ [?] … prasādādityagnereva stutitvādagnerevātra [?] … ‖ [partly unread]*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *agne* — O Agni; *naḥ* — our; *uktham* — hymn; *abhi jugurāḥ* — praise as excellent [say the word of approval]; may heaven and earth also praise; *sindhavaḥ* — those of flowing form; *svagūrtāḥ ca* — rivers that flow of their own nature, too; *gavyam* — (by growing grass and feeding them) the milk and the like of cows; *yavyam* — barley-made offerings such as *purodāśa*; *yantaḥ* — bringing (may they praise our hymn); *aruṇyaḥ* — the dawns, accompanied by golden-hued cows; *dīrghāhā* — on all days; *varam* — excellent; *iṣam* — food; *varanta* — may they bring.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, praise our hymn as excellent, and speak the word of approval. May heaven and earth likewise praise it. May the rivers, flowing of their own nature, also, by raising the grass that is the food of cows and so providing us with the milk and the like of cows and with barley-made offerings such as *purodāśa*, praise our hymn. May the dawns, with their golden-hued cows, bring excellent food on all days.

**English Translation (as printed).** Agni, be propitiated by this our earnest praise, and may heaven and earth, and the spontaneously-flowing (streams), provide for us the produce of the herd, and of the field; and may the purple coursers (of the dawn) bestow upon us abundant food through a length of days. [continued on p. 153: "…the herd, and of the field; …" — the printed English runs over the page break.]

### Printed p. 153  (PDF 171)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 6 [?].)*

*(Printed English continued from p. 152: "the herd, and of the field; and may the purple coursers (of the dawn) bestow upon us abundant food through a length of days.")*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***uktham abhi jugurāḥ*** — the prayer to Agni is: "praise our *uktha* as excellent". Here Sāyaṇa explains *uktha* as *śastra*. Pointing out the fine difference between *śastra* and *stotra* that holds in some places, Sāyaṇa, in the Śatapatha [?] Brāhmaṇa [?] 4-[?]-[?]-[?], takes the word *uktha* to mean "hymn" (*stotra*) by the sentence there [?]; in the sentences 1-[?]-[?] the senses of the word *uktha* are shown. Here, since the sacrificer's *uktha* is to be praised by Agni and Heaven and Earth, one must understand what good effect (*suphala*) this *uktha*, which gladdens the gods, has [?].

Since the power of the *uktha* is surpassing, increase will certainly come to all who know it. The story is in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa: once the Asuras took refuge in the *uktha* and they too gained surpassing strength and increase; then Indra came and, praising [Varuṇa], sought to drive them out.

> ते वा असुरा मैत्रावरुणमुक्थमाश्रयन्ते [?] सोऽब्रवीदिन्द्रः कः [?] साहं क्वेमानितोऽसुरानोत्स्यानहा [?] इत्थं चेत् [?] ब्रवीद्वरुणस्त्वा [?] … मैत्रावरुणस्य तृतीयसवने शंसन्तीन्द्रश्च हि तान्वरुणश्च ततो नुदेताम् [?] ।

> *te vā asurā maitrāvaruṇamukthamāśrayante [?] so 'bravīdindraḥ kaḥ [?] sāhaṃ kvemānito 'surānotsyānahā [?] itthaṃ cet [?] bravīdvaruṇastvā [?] … maitrāvaruṇasya tṛtīyasavane śaṃsantīndraśca hi tānvaruṇaśca tato nudetām [?] |*

(Ai. Brā. [?]-[?].) [The passage is given only as far as read.] The Asuras entered the Maitrāvaruṇa *uktha*. Then Indra asked who among them would help him drive the Asuras out of this *uktha*, and Varuṇa said that he would help. At that time the Maitrāvaruṇa, who is the helper of the *hotṛ*, at the time of the third pressing —

> इन्द्रावरुणा युवमध्वराय नो विशे जनाय महि शर्म यच्छतम् ।

> *indrāvaruṇā yuvamadhvarāya no viśe janāya mahi śarma yacchatam |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-82-[?].) — recited the *sūkta* that begins with this Ṛk, and praised Indra and Varuṇa. Then Indra and Varuṇa drove those Asuras out of the Maitrāvaruṇa *śastra*.

> ते वै ते [?] असुरा ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन उक्थमाश्रयन्ते सोऽब्रवीदिन्द्रः कः [?] साहं क्वेमानितोऽसुरानोत्स्यानहा [?] इत्थं चेत् [?] ब्रवीद्बृहस्पतिस्त्वा [?] ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनस्तृतीयसवने शंसन्तीन्द्रश्च हि तान्बृहस्पतिश्च ततो नुदेताम् [?] ।

> *te vai te [?] asurā brāhmaṇācchaṃsina ukthamāśrayante so 'bravīdindraḥ kaḥ [?] sāhaṃ kvemānito 'surānotsyānahā [?] itthaṃ cet [?] bravīdbṛhaspatistvā [?] brāhmaṇācchaṃsinastṛtīyasavane śaṃsantīndraśca hi tānbṛhaspatiśca tato nudetām [?] |*

(Ai. Brā. [?]; given as far as read; the account of it follows on p. 154.)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 140".)*

The Asuras driven out from there entered the *uktha* of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. Then Indra rose and asked who would help him drive these Asuras out of it; Bṛhaspati rose and said he would help. Then the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, at the time of the third pressing —

> उदप्रुतो न वयो रक्षमाणा वावदतो अभ्रियस्येव घोषाः । गिरिभ्रजो नोर्मयो मदन्तो बृहस्पतिमभ्यर्का अनावन् ॥

> *udapruto na vayo rakṣamāṇā vāvadato abhriyasyeva ghoṣāḥ | giribhrajo normayo madanto bṛhaspatimabhyarkā anāvan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-68-1.) — recited the *sūkta* beginning with this Ṛk and praised Indra and Bṛhaspati; and then Indra and Bṛhaspati drove the Asuras out from there.

> ते वै ते ऽसुरा अच्छावाकस्योक्थमाश्रयन्ते सोऽब्रवीदिन्द्रः कः साहं क्वेमानितोऽसुरानोत्स्यामहा [?] इत्थं चेत् [?] अब्रवीद्विष्णुस्त्वा [?] … अच्छावाकस्तृतीयसवने शंसेदिन्द्रश्च हि तान्विष्णुश्च ततो नुदेताम् ।

> *te vai te 'surā acchāvākasyokthamāśrayante so 'bravīdindraḥ kaḥ sāhaṃ kvemānito 'surānotsyāmahā [?] itthaṃ cet [?] abravīdviṣṇustvā [?] … acchāvākastṛtīyasavane śaṃsedindraśca hi tānviṣṇuśca tato nudetām |*

(Ai. Brā. 13-[?] [?]; garbled in part.) The Asuras driven out of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's *uktha* took refuge in the Acchāvāka's *uktha*. Then Indra rose and asked which of them would help him drive them out from there; Viṣṇu said he would help. At that time the Acchāvāka —

> सं वां कर्मणा समिषा हिनोमीन्द्राविष्णू अपसस्पारे अस्य । जुषेथां यज्ञं द्रविणं च धत्तमरिष्टैर्नः पथिभिः पारयन्ता ॥

> *saṃ vāṃ karmaṇā samiṣā hinomīndrāviṣṇū apasaspāre asya | juṣethāṃ yajñaṃ draviṇaṃ ca dhattamariṣṭairnaḥ pathibhiḥ pārayantā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-69-[?].) — recited the *sūkta* beginning with this Ṛk and praised Indra and Viṣṇu; and then they drove the Asuras out from there too. So runs the story in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (13-[?]). From it the power of the *uktha*, and the benefit that comes by it to the sacrificer who protects it, are known.

As the power of the *uktha* is described at the time of sacrificial rites, so, in the same way, at the time of teaching spiritual knowledge, the greatness of this hymnic *uktha* is praised. In the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad:

> उक्थं प्राणो वा उक्थं प्राणो हीदं सर्वमुत्थापयत्युद्धास्मादुक्थविद्वीरस्तिष्ठत्युक्थस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां जयति य एवं वेद ।

> *ukthaṃ prāṇo vā ukthaṃ prāṇo hīdaṃ sarvamutthāpayatyuddhāsmādukthavidvīrastiṣṭhatyukthasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda |*

(Bṛ. U. 5-13-1.)

> उक्थं त्वोपासनान्तरम् [?] । उक्थं शस्त्रम् । तद्धि प्रधानं महाव्रते क्रतौ [?] ।

> *ukthaṃ tvopāsanāntaram [?] | ukthaṃ śastram | taddhi pradhānaṃ mahāvrate kratau [?] |*

(Śāṅkarabhāṣya.) (continues on p. 155)

### Printed p. 155  (PDF 173)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

In the sacrifice called Mahāvrata the *uktha*, the chief *śastra*, is the breath (*prāṇa*): from it comes rising up (*utthāna*); therefore a son who knows the *uktha* is born, and obtains standing (*tattvamānatā* [?]) and equal honour: so the greatness of the *uktha* is told. When such a great *uktha* is praised, the sense is "knowing its other greatness, praise it" [?]: that is, "may it give you joy, and be worthy of your praise".

***abhi jugurāḥ*** — *abhimukhena stuhi; protsāhaya; samyak śastram ity aṅgīkuru*: "praise facing it; encourage; accept, saying 'well recited'": the sense is "with special affection speak the word of acceptance praising it". Or —

> प्र स्तोषदुप गासिषच्छ्रवत्साम गीयमानम् । अभि राधसा जुगुरत् ॥

> *pra stoṣadupa gāsiṣacchravatsāma gīyamānam | abhi rādhasā jugurat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk the verb *abhi jugurat* means *abhigṛṇātu*, "may he accept (approve)"; here too the sense "accept" may result, and the purport agrees.

***svagūrtāḥ*** — *svayam eva gāminyaḥ*: Sāyaṇa explains it as "flowing of their own nature". But the word *gūrta* ordinarily has the sense "praiseworthy, famed"; it also has the sense "praisers, those who commend". For example —

> तं गूर्तयो नेमन्निषः परीणसः समुद्रं न संचरणे सनिष्यवः । पतिं दक्षस्य विदथस्य नू सहो गिरिं न वेना अधि रोह तेजसा ॥

> *taṃ gūrtayo nemanniṣaḥ parīṇasaḥ samudraṃ na saṃcaraṇe saniṣyavaḥ | patiṃ dakṣasya vidathasya nū saho giriṃ na venā adhi roha tejasā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-56-[?].) In this Ṛk *gūrtayaḥ* is explained as *stotāraḥ*;

> तं वः सखायो मदाय पुनानमभि गायत । शिशुं न यज्ञैः स्वदयन्त गूर्तिभिः ॥

> *taṃ vaḥ sakhāyo madāya punānamabhi gāyata | śiśuṃ na yajñaiḥ svadayanta gūrtibhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-104-1.) here *gūrtibhiḥ* is explained as *stutibhiḥ*, "with hymns"; and in other places too the sense "praiseworthy, famed" is found. So in the present Ṛk also the meaning may be: rivers "worthy of praise", or "having abundant flow".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 13; grammar pages 155–156, noted briefly).** *abhi* (an indeclinable; the *saṃhitā* lengthening in *abhī* by *nipātasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-[?])), *jugurāḥ* (root *gṝ śabde*; *liṅ*, second person singular, *sip*; *itaś ca* gives loss of the *i*; the suffix is dropped by *bahulaṃ chandasi*; reduplication). (continues on p. 156)

## Sūkta 141

### Printed p. 157 (continued; PDF 175)

*(The Kannada heading reads "The 141st Sūkta".)*

*(Anukramaṇī, Sanskrit; not rendered in English. Gist: the second sūkta of the twenty-first anuvāka, "Baḷitthā", of thirteen Ṛks, is Dairghatamasa; its metre is Jagatī, the last two Ṛks Triṣṭubh; the deity is Agni; its use at the Prātaranuvāka and the Aśvina-śastra is stated.)*

> बळित्थेति त्रयोदशर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तं दैर्घतमसं जागतम् । अन्त्ये त्रिष्टुभौ । अग्निर्देवता । प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोरुक्तो विनियोगः ॥

> *baḷittheti trayodaśarcaṃ dvitīyaṃ sūktaṃ dairghatamasaṃ jāgatam | antye triṣṭubhau | agnirdevatā | prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayorukto viniyogaḥ ‖*

*Anuvāda (Kannada).* The sūkta *Baḷitthā* is the second sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has thirteen Ṛks. Its ṛṣi is Dīrghatamas. Agni is the deity. The last two Ṛks have the metre Triṣṭubh; the remaining Ṛks have the metre Jagatī. The use of this sūkta at the time of reciting the mantras of the Prātaranuvāka and of the mantras of the Aśvina-śastra is stated (by the Anukramaṇī).

---

**॥ ओम् ॥**

**Sūkta 141** — Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 21, Sūkta 141; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?7, 8 — 'as read']. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 13. Ṛṣi: Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Devatā: Agni. Chandas: 1–11 Jagatī; 12–13 Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> बळित्था तद्वपुषे धायि दर्शतं देवस्य भर्गः सहसो यतो जनि ।
> यदीमुप ह्वरते साधते मतिर्ऋतस्य धेना अनयन्त सस्रुतः ॥ १ ॥

> *baḷitthā tadvapuṣe dhāyi darśataṃ devasya bhargaḥ sahaso yato jani |*
> *yadīmupa hvarate sādhate matirṛtasya dhenā anayanta sasrutaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

### Printed p. 158  (PDF 176)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> बट् । इत्था । तत् । वपुषे । धायि । दर्शतम् । देवस्य । भर्गः । सहसः । यतः । जनि ।
> यत् । ईम् । उप । ह्वरते । साधते । मतिः । ऋतस्य । धेनाः । अनयन्त । सस्रुतः ॥ १ ॥

> *baṭ | itthā | tat | vapuṣe | dhāyi | darśatam | devasya | bhargaḥ | sahasaḥ | yataḥ | jani |*
> *yat | īm | upa | hvarate | sādhate | matiḥ | ṛtasya | dhenāḥ | anayanta | sasrutaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *the visible brightness of the shining Agni is held by all for the body, being born of strength; my mind approaches it and accomplishes its aim; the speech of the sacrifice, flowing together, leads on his praise.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> देवस्य द्योतनशीलस्याग्नेः दर्शतं सर्वैर्दर्शनीयं तत् प्रसिद्धं भर्गः तेजः इत्थं सर्वैर्दृश्यमानप्रकारेण वपुषे शरीरव्यवहाराय दार्ढ्याय धायि धार्यते सर्वैः । बळित्थेत्युभे अपि सत्यनामनी । बट् शृत् सत्येत्येकं [?] तन्नामसु पाठात् । जाराग्निना भुक्तानां जरणेन शरीरधारणं प्रसिद्धम् [?] । के ऽग्रेपतिमाहः [?] । यतः सहसो जनि यतः कारणात् सहनकाले बलेनोत्पन्नः । अतो बलाय धार्यते इत्यर्थः । यदीमुप यदेतत्तेजः [?] … लोकोपकारकं … मतिर्बुद्धिः … उपह्वरते उपगच्छति [?] । ह्वृ कौटिल्ये । साधते च येनैव तेजसा साधयति स्वाभीष्टम् । किंच ऋतस्य यज्ञसाधकस्याग्नेस्तेजसा धेनाः [?] वाचः सस्रुतः समानं गच्छन्त्यः [?] ऋत्विजः … अनयन्ते नयन्ति [?] निर्वहन्ति जगद्व्यवहारं … व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदम् ॥ यद्वा ऋतस्य धेना यज्ञस्य सम्बन्धिन्यो मन्त्ररूपा वाचः सस्रुतो होत्रादिमुखेन समानं प्रवर्तमाना अनयन्ते नयन्ति । अग्नेः स्तोत्रं निर्वहन्ति । अग्नेस्तेजसा वा यज्ञं निर्वहन्ति । तेजोमयी वागिति श्रुतेः (भा. उ. ३-१-३ [?]) । अतः कारणात् तिरुपस्करे [?] इत्यर्थः । धेनेति वाङ्नाम धेना ग्ना इति तन्नामसु पाठात् ॥ [partly unread]

> *devasya dyotanaśīlasyāgneḥ darśataṃ sarvairdarśanīyaṃ tat prasiddhaṃ bhargaḥ tejaḥ itthaṃ sarvairdṛśyamānaprakāreṇa vapuṣe śarīravyavahārāya dārḍhyāya dhāyi dhāryate sarvaiḥ | baḷitthetyubhe api satyanāmanī | baṭ śṛt satyetyekaṃ [?] tannāmasu pāṭhāt | jārāgninā bhuktānāṃ jaraṇena śarīradhāraṇaṃ prasiddham [?] | ke 'grepatimāhaḥ [?] | yataḥ sahaso jani yataḥ kāraṇāt sahanakāle balenotpannaḥ | ato balāya dhāryate ityarthaḥ | yadīmupa yadetattejaḥ [?] … lokopakārakaṃ … matirbuddhiḥ … upahvarate upagacchati [?] | hvṛ kauṭilye | sādhate ca yenaiva tejasā sādhayati svābhīṣṭam | kiṃca ṛtasya yajñasādhakasyāgnestejasā dhenāḥ [?] vācaḥ sasrutaḥ samānaṃ gacchantyaḥ [?] ṛtvijaḥ … anayante nayanti [?] nirvahanti jagadvyavahāraṃ … vyatyayenātmanepadam ‖ yadvā ṛtasya dhenā yajñasya sambandhinyo mantrarūpā vācaḥ sasruto hotrādimukhena samānaṃ pravartamānā anayante nayanti | agneḥ stotraṃ nirvahanti | agnestejasā vā yajñaṃ nirvahanti | tejomayī vāgiti śruteḥ (bhā. u. 3-1-3 [?]) | ataḥ kāraṇāt tirupaskare [?] ityarthaḥ | dheneti vāṅnāma dhenā gnā iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt ‖ [partly unread]*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *devasya* — of the shining Agni; *darśatam* — which is visible (to all); *tat* — that well-known; *bhargaḥ* — brightness; *itthā* — in this manner; *yataḥ* — for which reason; *sahasaḥ* — from strength; *jani* — was born (kaṃtapa [?]); *vapuṣe* — for the firmness of the body; *dhāyi* — is held (by all); *yadīm* — which well-known brightness, beneficial to the world; *matiḥ* — my intellect; *upahvarate* — approaches (with effort); *sādhate* — accomplishes (its desired aim); *ṛtasya* — (with the brightness) of Agni, the accomplisher of the sacrifice; *dhenāḥ* — the speech of all creatures; *sasrutaḥ* — flowing together, joining; *anayante* — carry on (the business of the world); [or: *ṛtasya* — pertaining to the sacrifice; *dhenāḥ* — these speeches in the form of mantras; *sasrutaḥ* — issuing from the mouths of the *hotṛ* and others; *anayante* — carry through (Agni's praise)].

### Printed p. 159  (PDF 177)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

**Bhāvārtha.** The well-known brightness of Agni, which is visible to all, has been produced from strength in order to give all creatures firmness of body. For the sake of that firmness all people hold this brightness. My intellect also takes up this well-known brightness, beneficial to the world, and accomplishes its desired aim. At the time of the sacrifice the mantric speech issuing from the mouths of the *hotṛ* and others carries through the praise of this Agni.

**English Translation (as printed).** Verily, that visible radiance of the divine (Agni) has been so apprehended (by all, that it may be) for (the support of) the body, for which end it has been generated by (bodily) strength: and that my mind may apprehend and apply (that radiance), they address the sacred prayers associated with oblations (to Agni).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***bhargaḥ*** — *tejaḥ*: the word *bharga* is customarily used only of the brightness of Agni (in the form of the Āditya). Sāyaṇa, in the Ṛk

> तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि । धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् ॥

> *tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi | dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-62-10.) explains the word *bharga* as *avidyā-tatkāryayor bharjanād bhargaḥ*: "because it burns up ignorance and its effects, desire, delusion and the like, it is *bharga*" — showing that the nature of Savitṛ is declared by the word *bharga*.

***sahasaḥ jani*** — "born of strength": at the time of the churning of the *araṇi* sticks he is born of strength; so it is described as *sahasaḥ jani*.

***ṛtasya dhenāḥ*** — here the word *ṛta* means sacrifice. Showing the construction as "of *ṛta*, i.e. of the sacrifice-related (or sacrifice-accomplishing) Agni, the *dhenāḥ*", Sāyaṇa explains *dhenāḥ* as *sarvaprāṇināṃ vācaḥ*; or, *yajñasya sambandhinyaḥ mantrarūpā vācaḥ*, and cites the Upaniṣad sentence *tejomayī vāk* (Bhā. U. 3-[?]-[?] [?]). From this very example the word *dhenā* is understood not as ordinary speech but as supernatural and luminous [?] … (continues on p. 160)

### Printed p. 160  (PDF 178)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

*(Continued from p. 159.)* … [the word *dhenā* is thus shown to be] speech accompanied by mantra. Since Sāyaṇa has in some places given a different sense, it has to be examined whether this word has one clear sense or the sense varies with the context.

> सम्यक्स्रवन्ति सरितो न धेना अन्तर्हृदा मनसा पूयमानाः । एते अर्षन्त्यूर्मयो घृतस्य मृगा इव क्षिपणोरीषमाणाः ॥

> *samyaksravanti sarito na dhenā antarhṛdā manasā pūyamānāḥ | ete arṣantyūrmayo ghṛtasya mṛgā iva kṣipaṇorīṣamāṇāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-58-6.)

> क्रीळन्निन्द्र [?] प्रवितेव [?] अपस्यः परिष्ठिता अहिना शूर पूर्वीः । … द्वावक्रे [?] रथ्यो न धेना रेजन्ते विश्वा कृत्रिमाणि भीषा ॥

> *krīḷannindra [?] praviteva [?] apasyaḥ pariṣṭhitā ahinā śūra pūrvīḥ | … dvāvakre [?] rathyo na dhenā rejante viśvā kṛtrimāṇi bhīṣā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-30-[?]; the Ṛk is only partly legible at this resolution.) In these Ṛks Sāyaṇa explains *dhenā* as "flowing river";

> मादयस्व हरिभिर्ये त इन्द्र वि ष्यस्व शिप्रे वि सृजस्व धेने । आ त्वा सुशिप्र हरयो वहन्तूशन्हव्यानि प्रति नो जुषस्व ॥

> *mādayasva haribhirye ta indra vi ṣyasva śipre vi sṛjasva dhene | ā tvā suśipra harayo vahantūśanhavyāni prati no juṣasva ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-101-10.) in this Ṛk he explains *jihvopajihvike*, "the tongue and the uvula (?), the instruments of drinking" [?]. The Nirukta author cites this very Ṛk (1-101-10) and shows the derivation *dhenā dadhāteḥ* … [and explains it as … ] (Ni. 6-[?]). Apart from these, in the other Ṛks Sāyaṇa gives the sense "speech". If one examines the contexts of this word in the Saṃhitā and elsewhere, there seems no reason for any sense other than "speech in the form of praise". In this matter, too, the passages used in the Śrauta Sūtras give more room for this very sense.

In the Śrauta Sūtras, when the wives of the gods are named, *senendrasya, dhenā bṛhaspateḥ* — the name *dhenā* is well known for Bṛhaspati's wife; in these places there is no room for the sense "speech in the form of praise" [?]. In the other places, where the Ṛks cited above are concerned, it would be no mistake to give this very sense. For example, in Ṛk 4-58-6, *samyak sravanti sarito na dhenā antarhṛdā manasā pūyamānāḥ*: "like rivers flowing unchecked, the *dhenāḥ*, purified in the heart and by the mind" — to take them as speeches in the form of praise, coming forth naturally from the heart and with purity of mind, is fitting, and not wrong. Besides, the words *manasā* and *antarhṛdā pūyamānāḥ* agree naturally with *dhenāḥ*. Sāyaṇa joins those words with the others [?] (continues on p. 161)

### Printed p. 161  (PDF 179)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 7 [?].)*

… *ghṛtasya ūrmayaḥ* — that does not give a living sense. Likewise in Ṛk 1-101-10 the dual *dhene* may point to the two senses "praise" and "oblation". Thus —

> पितुश्चिदूधर्जनुषा विवेद व्यस्य धारा असृजद्वि धेनाः । गुहा चरन्तं सखिभिः शिवेभिर्दिवो यह्वीभिर्न गुहा बभूव ॥

> *pituścidūdharjanuṣā viveda vyasya dhārā asṛjadvi dhenāḥ | guhā carantaṃ sakhibhiḥ śivebhirdivo yahvībhirna guhā babhūva ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-1-[?].) In this Ṛk *ūdhaḥ* is explained as "the atmosphere", *dhārā* as "stream of rain", and *dhenā* as … [?]. Apart from these few examples, in the remaining ones —

> विश्रन्तिशं [?] मघोना पर्यायते जनानां धेना अवचाकशद्वृषा । यस्मादा शक्रः सवनेषु रण्यति स तीव्रैः सोमैः सहते पृतन्यतः ॥

> *viśrantiśaṃ [?] maghonā paryāyate janānāṃ dhenā avacākaśadvṛṣā | yasmādā śakraḥ savaneṣu raṇyati sa tīvraiḥ somaiḥ sahate pṛtanyataḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-43-[?]; read with doubt.)

> वीरेण्यः क्रतुरिन्द्रः सुशस्तिरुतापि धेना पुरुहूतमीट्टे । आर्दयद्वृत्रमकृणोदु लोकं ससाहे शक्रः पृतना अभिष्टिः ॥

> *vīreṇyaḥ kraturindraḥ suśastirutāpi dhenā puruhūtamīṭṭe | ārdayadvṛtramakṛṇodu lokaṃ sasāhe śakraḥ pṛtanā abhiṣṭiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-104-10 [?].) In all such Ṛks Sāyaṇa has explained it as *prīṇayitrī stutivāk*, "gladdening speech of praise". In the same way the *dhene* of 1-101-10 above —

> स्त्रियो हि दास आयुधानि चक्रे किं मा करन्नबला अस्य सेनाः । अन्तर्ह्यख्यदुभे अस्य धेने अथोप प्रैद्युद्धयये दस्युमिन्द्रः ॥

> *striyo hi dāsa āyudhāni cakre kiṃ mā karannabalā asya senāḥ | antarhyakhyadubhe asya dhene athopa praidyuddhayaye dasyumindraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-30-9.) — in the first half of this Ṛk, too, there are duals in two places, so the senses "praise" and "oblation" may be given. In 5-30-9 Sāyaṇa explains *asya* (the Asura's) *dhene ubhe antarakhyat*: "the two women of the Asura stood in the middle of the house; then Indra fought Namuci face to face" — taking *dhenā* in the sense "woman". It fits better to say: when Namuci produced an army in the form of women, praise and oblation entered the heart of Indra and roused him for the fight.

So in the present Ṛk too, for *ṛtasya dhenāḥ sasrutaḥ*, rather than Sāyaṇa's first interpretation, (continues on p. 162)

### Printed p. 162  (PDF 180)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

the speeches in the form of praise, connected with the sacrifice and flowing from the mouths of the *hotṛ*s — that is, Sāyaṇa's second sense — appears clear and correct.

***itthā*** — *baṭ* and *itthā* are both read among the names of truth (Ni. 3-10): "truly, certainly".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar pages 162–163, noted briefly).** Headwords: *itthā* (from *idam*; suffix *thamu* by *idamas thamuḥ*; case-ending changed by *vyatyaya*), *dhāyi* (root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *luṅ* by *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-6) in the present sense; *ciṇ* in the passive; *luk* of the ending; *yuk* after the *ā*; by *bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi* no *aḍ*; *tiṅ*, *nighāta*), *darśatam* (root *dṛśir prekṣaṇe*; *bhṛmṛdṛśi*… (Uṇ. Sū. 3-[?]) suffix *ata*; *guṇa*; *cit*: last-syllable accent), *sahasaḥ* (root *saha marṣaṇe*; suffix *asun*; *nit*: first-syllable accent), *jani* (root *janī prādurbhāve*; as before, *luṅ* in the Vedic sense; third person singular; because of the connected *yat*, no *nighāta*), *hvarate* (root *hvṛ kauṭilye*; *laṭ*, third person singular; *śap*; *guṇa*; *raparatva*; because of *yad* no *nighāta*), *sādhate* (root *sādha saṃsiddhau*; *ṇic* by *hetumati ca*; *śap* by *chandasy ubhayathā* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-117); *ṇeraniṭi* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-51) drops *ṇic*; no *nighāta*; the root accent remains). Sūtra numbers as read; [?] where small type was not legible.

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> पृक्षो वपुः पितुमान्नित्य आ शये द्वितीयमा सप्तशिवासु मातृषु ।
> तृतीयमस्य वृषभस्य दोहसे दशप्रमतिं जनयन्त योषणः ॥ २ ॥

> *pṛkṣo vapuḥ pitumānnitya ā śaye dvitīyamā saptaśivāsu mātṛṣu |*
> *tṛtīyamasya vṛṣabhasya dohase daśapramatiṃ janayanta yoṣaṇaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> पृक्षः । वपुः । पितुऽमान् । नित्यः । आ । शये । द्वितीयम् । आ । सप्तऽशिवासु । मातृषु ।
> तृतीयम् । अस्य । वृषभस्य । दोहसे । दशऽप्रमतिम् । जनयन्त । योषणः ॥ २ ॥

> *pṛkṣaḥ | vapuḥ | pitu 'mān | nityaḥ | ā | śaye | dvitīyam | ā | sapta 'śivāsu | mātṛṣu |*
> *tṛtīyam | asya | vṛṣabhasya | dohase | daśa 'pramatim | janayanta | yoṣaṇaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *Agni, the food-giver and body-builder, rests first on the earth; second among the seven auspicious mothers; third, the ten quarters bring him forth in the shower-bringing Āditya.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> अयमग्निः पृक्षः अन्नस्य [?] साधकः पाकादिना वपुः पुष्ट्यर्थं शरीराभिवृद्धिहेतुः पितुमान् पितु इत्यन्ननाम तद्वान् नित्यः शाश्वतः । ईश्वरः सन् प्रथमं पृथिवीस्थाने सन्ना शये आशेते । दापसाकादि [?] लौकिकं कर्म यज्ञादि दैविकं कर्म च निर्वर्तयन् … वर्तते । तथा सप्तशिवासु सप्तलोकेषु शिवासु हितकरीषु मातृषु मातृस्थानीयासु वृष्टिषु द्वितीयमाशेते [?] … । अस्य वृषभस्य वर्षितुः आदित्यस्य … दोहसे दोग्ध्रे … अग्नेः सहायत्वेन संबन्धिने … दशप्रमतिम् दशदिक्षु प्रकृष्टमननं … पूज्यम् … जनयन्त उत्पादयन्ति … योषणः संयुक्ताः सर्वा दिशः … । [partly unread]

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** (*ayam agniḥ* — this Agni;) *pṛkṣaḥ* — as the food-giver by cooking and so on, [as the digestive faculty (*jaraṇa-kāraka*)]; *vapuḥ* — as the cause of growth of the body; *pitumān* — rich in food, in the form of oblations; *nityaḥ* — eternal; *ā śaye* — (first, in the form of Agni) he lies spread out on the earth; *dvitīyam* — secondly (in a second form); *saptaśivāsu* — in the seven worlds, the givers of auspiciousness; *mātṛṣu* — in the places of the mothers, the rains, that are mother-like; *ā* (*śaye*) — he lies spread out (in the form of lightning); *tṛtīyam* — thirdly (in yet another form); *asya vṛṣabhasya* — of the showerer, belonging to the Āditya; *dohase* — for the milking of rain; *daśaprematim* — worshipful, delightful through the rays of the ten quarters, or [the one] born by the ten fingers, in churning; *yoṣaṇaḥ* — all the quarters united; *janayante* — bring forth (cause to blossom).

**Bhāvārtha.** Agni, who is the digestive faculty and the cause of the growth of the body, and rich in food in the form of oblations, and everlasting, first performs worldly acts such as cooking and divine acts such as sacrifice, and lies spread out on the earth. Second, he is spread out among the seven worlds that give auspiciousness, the places of the mothers, as lightning (*vidyut*) in the regions of rain. Third, by the activity of the rays of the Āditya, associated with the one who showers rain, he is spread out in the heaven; and all the quarters, united, make this Agni, who is worthy of worship and gladdening to the ten quarters because of the light, to blossom.

**English Translation (as printed).** First, he reposes (on the earth) as the digestive (faculty), the embodied, the accepter of food, the eternal: secondly, (he dwells) among the seven

### Printed p. 165  (PDF 183)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 7 [?].)*

*(Printed English continued from p. 164:)* auspicious mothers (of fertility): thirdly, the associated (regions) generate him, delighting in the ten (quarters) of space, for the sake of milking this showerer (of rain).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** Three kinds of manifestation of Agni are described in this Ṛk. The Nirukta authors say that all the sages worship the deity Agni who is in the form of the Āditya in heaven, in the form of lightning in the atmosphere, and in the form of fire on earth; and then they have explained at length these three forms in the three places with examples from Saṃhitā passages. If the Nirukta passage is followed in the order of this Ṛk, first —

> स्तोमेन हि दिवि देवा अग्निमजनयन्नस्कृत [?] कर्मभिर्द्यावापृथिव्योः [?] । पूरणं तमकुर्वंस्त्रेधाभावाय पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे दिवीति शाकपूणिः ॥

> *stomena hi divi devā agnimajanayannaskṛta [?] karmabhirdyāvāpṛthivyoḥ [?] | pūraṇaṃ tamakurvaṃstredhābhāvāya pṛthivyāmantarikṣe divīti śākapūṇiḥ ‖*

(Ni. 7-[?]; read with doubt.) By this sentence the Nirukta authors, following Śākapūṇi's explanation, say that Agni appears in three forms in the three places — earth, atmosphere and heaven — as Agni, Jātavedas and Vaiśvānara. This order is shown in the Nirukta (Ni. 7-[?] to 7-[?]) on the basis of Ṛks such as *… mūrdhā bhuvo bhavati nakṣan …* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-6). The same division —

> अग्नये पवमानाय पुरोडाशमष्टाकपालं निर्वपेदग्नये पावकायाग्नये शुचये ।

> *agnaye pavamānāya puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapedagnaye pāvakāyāgnaye śucaye |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-[?].) — is stated in these Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentences in the order *pavamāna*, *śuci*, *pāvaka*. It is to be understood that this threefold existence of Agni, and the threefold manifestation corresponding to it, reflect the fundamental principle of the three worlds; so says the Bṛhaddevatā:

> भवद्भूतेष्वस्य भव्यस्य जङ्गमस्याध्रुवस्य च । अस्यैको सूर्यमेकैकं प्रभवनं प्रलयं विदुः ॥ एतेष्वेतेषु लोकेषु अग्निर्भूतं स्थितं भूतं [?] ऋषयो गीर्भिरर्चन्ति व्यञ्जितं नामभिस्त्रिभिः ॥

> *bhavadbhūteṣvasya bhavyasya jaṅgamasyādhruvasya ca | asyaiko sūryamekaikaṃ prabhavanaṃ pralayaṃ viduḥ ‖ eteṣveteṣu lokeṣu agnirbhūtaṃ sthitaṃ bhūtaṃ [?] ṛṣayo gīrbhirarcanti vyañjitaṃ nāmabhistribhiḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 1-[?]; 1-[?]; read with doubt.) In these verses the Bṛhaddevatā author, in describing the greatness of Agni, [says that] Prajāpati, the source of all beings, [and] all the beings, moving and unmoving, in the past, future and present … (continues on p. 166)

### Printed p. 166  (PDF 184)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

*(Continued from p. 165.)* … [Prajāpati,] the source of all beings, [and all moving and unmoving beings] in the past, future and present: from the origin of creation Agni, in three forms, holds his existence in three places; and the sages praise the manifestations of Agni by three names, as the same verses go on to say in praising Agni:

> त्रिस्थानं चैनमर्चन्ति होत्रायोग्यं [?] वृक्तबर्हिषः । इहैव पावमानोऽग्निर्मध्यमो [?] वैद्युतः [?] । अमुष्मिन्नेव [?] … लोके शुचिर्बृहत् [?] । इहाग्निर्भूतस्थो [?] … स्तुतिभिरीडितः । जातवेदाः स्तुतो मध्ये स्तुतो वैश्वानरो दिवि ॥

> *tristhānaṃ cainamarcanti hotrāyogyaṃ [?] vṛktabarhiṣaḥ | ihaiva pāvamāno 'gnirmadhyamo [?] vaidyutaḥ [?] | amuṣminneva [?] … loke śucirbṛhat [?] | ihāgnirbhūtastho [?] … stutibhirīḍitaḥ | jātavedāḥ stuto madhye stuto vaiśvānaro divi ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 1-[?] to 1-[?]; read with doubt.) Of these three forms, the Agni who appears on earth is called *pavamāna*; the Agni who goes in the middle world is called *vanasyati* [?]; the Agni of heaven is called *śuci*: so it is known. By the same sentence —

> दिवस्परि प्रथमं जज्ञे अग्निरस्मद्द्वितीयं परि जातवेदाः । तृतीयमप्सु नृमणा अजस्रमिन्धान एनं जरते स्वाधीः ॥

> *divaspari prathamaṃ jajñe agnirasmaddvitīyaṃ pari jātavedāḥ | tṛtīyamapsu nṛmaṇā ajasramindhāna enaṃ jarate svādhīḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-45-1; Vā. Saṃ. 12-[?]; Tai. Saṃ. 4-2-[?]-[?].) — it is explained in all the Saṃhitās.

***pṛkṣaḥ*** — the word *pṛkṣa* is read among the names of food (Ni. 2-7); here *annasādhakaḥ pākādinā*: one who supports food by cooking and so on.

***pitumān*** — *havirlakṣaṇānnayuktaḥ*: one provided with food in the form of oblations.

***saptaśivāsu mātṛṣu*** — *saptalokaśivakarīṣu mātṛsthānīyāsu hitakarīṣu vṛṣṭiṣu*: in the rains that bring good to the seven worlds [and are mother-like]; … he is in the middle region, or is in the form of lightning (*vidyut*).

***daśapramatim*** — *daśasu dikṣu prakṛṣṭamananavantaṃ pūjyatāyai*: one who is revered and meditated on in the ten quarters, is one sense; or, *mathanakāle daśabhir aṅgulībhir utpannaṃ lokatraye daśadikṣu ca vyāptam*: one born at the time of churning by the ten fingers, and spread through the three worlds and the ten quarters, is another sense. Both senses have *śruti* authority. The account of the generation of Agni, [in which] the subtle Agni is made to appear on earth and in the atmosphere — (continues on p. 167)

### Printed p. 167  (PDF 185)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 7 [?].)*

> यं त्वा द्यावापृथिवी यं त्वापस्त्वष्टा यं त्वा सुजनिमा जजान । पन्थामनु प्रविद्वान्पितृयाणं द्युमदग्ने समिधानो वि भाहि ॥

> *yaṃ tvā dyāvāpṛthivī yaṃ tvāpastvaṣṭā yaṃ tvā sujanimā jajāna | panthāmanu pravidvānpitṛyāṇaṃ dyumadagne samidhāno vi bhāhi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-2-7 [?].) In such passages it is explained that Heaven and Earth, containing the ten quarters, are the source of Agni's birth. And again —

> द्विर्यं पञ्च जीजनन्त्संवसानाः स्वसारो अग्निं मानुषीषु विक्षु । उषर्बुधमथर्यो न दन्तं शुक्रं स्वासं परशुं न तिग्मम् ॥

> *dviryaṃ pañca jījanantsaṃvasānāḥ svasāro agniṃ mānuṣīṣu vikṣu | uṣarbudhamatharyo na dantaṃ śukraṃ svāsaṃ paraśuṃ na tigmam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-6-8 [?].) In such Ṛks it is explained that the ten fingers of the two hands begot Agni — the manner of Agni's birth. Therefore in this context the word *daśa* may be taken as the ten quarters, in which earth and atmosphere are included, or as the ten fingers engaged in the work of churning.

***yoṣaṇaḥ*** — *miśraṇaśīlāḥ sarvā diśaḥ*: all the quarters, joined together, is one sense; or *ekasmin pāṇau saṃhatya avasthitāḥ*: the ten fingers gathered together in one hand and standing in one place, is another sense.

***vṛṣabhasya dohase*** — because it has the power of shedding rain, the lightning-fire has the epithet *vṛṣabha*; the derivation of this word has been shown in detail before. Sāyaṇa explains the word *dohase* as follows: *ādityaraśmayaḥ gharmakāle bhūmisthamudakamākṛṣya sūryaṃ prāpya tatra cirakālaṃ dhṛtvā punar antarikṣaṃ prāpya megheṣu sthitvā varṣakāle pravarṣantīti prasiddham; ato raśmidogdhṛtvam*: "it is well known that in the hot season the rays of the sun draw the water on earth up to the sun, hold it there for a long time, bring it again to the atmosphere, and, remaining in the clouds, rain in the rainy season; hence the sun's rays are the milkers"; so the word *dohase* shows the milking-power of the sun's rays.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar pages 167–168, noted briefly).** *śaye* (root *śīṅ svapne*; *laṭ*, third person singular; *ṭe* → *e*; *lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu*; *ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ* drops *śap*; *sārvadhātukamapit*… *guṇa*; *ay*; because it follows an *ati-jñanta*, *nighāta*), *pṛkṣaḥ* (root *pṛcī samparke*; suffix *asun*; *coḥ kuḥ* gives *k*, *ṣatva*; nominative singular; accent [?]), *pitumān* (the word *pitu*, with *matup*; *hrasvanudbhyāṃ matup* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-[?]) gives the *udātta*; nominative singular) …

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

*Grammar (Ṛk 2, concluded; noted briefly):* *nityaḥ* (*tyap* suffix for the indeclinable *ni* by *nityaṃ svaraṃ vā*… [?]; being *pit*, it is *anudātta*), *dvitīyam* (*dvestīyaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 5-2-54) suffix *tīya*; the accent of the suffix is *ādyudātta*, the *ī* is *udātta*), *tṛtīyam* (*trayasya saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca*; the *tṛ* by *saṃprasāraṇa*; *igyaṇaḥ saṃprasāraṇam*: *ṛ* for the *r*; the accent as before), *dohase* (root *duha prapūraṇe*; *sarvadhātubhya asun* in the agent sense; *pugantalaghūpadhasya ca* gives *guṇa*; dative singular), *janayanta* (root *janī prādurbhāve*; *ṇic* by *hetumati ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-26); *upadhāvṛddhi*, *mitām hrasvaḥ* by *janivadhyoś ca*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* gives *laṅ* in the present sense; third person plural; *bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi*: no *aḍ*; *tiṅ*, *nighāta*). ‖ 2 ‖
