**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *īm* — this Agni; *yat* — for what reason; *mahiṣasya* — of the great sacrifice; *budhnāt* — from the time of the setting up of the fire onward; *varpasaḥ* (the form that undertakes and ends) — to obtain the form fit to receive the oblation; *īśānāsaḥ* — those competent in their duties; *sūrayaḥ* — the wise sacrificial priests; *śavasā* — by the strength of their mantras, or by the power of the body; *niḥ krānta* — bring forth (cause to arise) from the kindling-wood; [or: *budhnāt* — by the (first) effort of churning in the body; *mahiṣasya varpasaḥ* — to gain a vast form fit to receive the oblations; *niḥ krānta* — cause to arise from the wood] (and) *guhā santam yadīm* — this Agni, hidden in the kindling-sticks; *pradivaḥ* — from the beginningless time; *madhvaḥ ādhave* — for casting in the offering, like honey; *mātariśvā* — the wind that moves in the atmosphere; *mathāyati* — blows and kindles; [or *mātariśvā* — the sacrificer, a performer of the sacrifice; *mathāyati* — causes to be kindled (by the sticks)] (the sacrificer, so that this Agni, praiseworthy, ...).

### Printed p. 170  (PDF 188)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

**Bhāvārtha.** In the great sacrifice, from the time of the setting up of the fire onward, in order to obtain a form fit for receiving the oblation, the wise priests, competent in their own duties, bring forth this Agni from the kindling-wood by the power of their mantras and by the strength of the body. And from the beginningless time, in the same way, in order to cast into him the honey-like oblation, the wind, moving in the atmosphere, blows upon this Agni, hidden in the sticks, and makes him blaze. Therefore this Agni is worthy of praise.

**English Translation (as printed).** As powerful priests extract by the force (of prayer), this Agni from his primitive seat, (for the evolvement) of his mighty form; as the wind arouses him lurking in the hiding-place (of the altar), for the sake of offering oblations now as of old.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***mahiṣasya*** — the word *mahiṣa* is read among the names of the great (Ni. 3-[?]). The Nirukta authors cite

> अपामुपस्थे महिषा अगृभ्णत विशो राजानमुप तस्थुर्ऋग्मियम् । आ दूतो अग्निमभरद्विवस्वतो वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वा परावतः ॥

> *apāmupasthe mahiṣā agṛbhṇata viśo rājānamupa tasthurṛgmiyam | ā dūto agnimabharadvivasvato vaiśvānaraṃ mātariśvā parāvataḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-8-4.) and for the word *mahiṣāḥ* there show the sense "greatness", or "the great Maruts", and show that the sense of the present Ṛk is as in the Ṛk cited [?].

In the present Ṛk the commentator has connected the word *mahiṣasya* with *budhnāt* in one construction, and with *varpasaḥ* in another. By the first construction *mahiṣasya budhnāt* is "from the time of setting up the fire of the great sacrifice"; by the second, *mahiṣasya varpasaḥ* is "of the vast form". (continues on p. 171)

### Printed p. 171  (PDF 189)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 7 [?].)*

To learn the particulars of this context one must understand correctly the meaning of the word *budhnāt*. For *budhnāt* the commentator has given the sense *mūlāt, ādhānād ārabhya*. In the Ṛk-saṃhitā the word *budhna* is used for the most part as a synonym of "atmosphere"; but even when it gives the sense "atmosphere", it is because *baddhā asmin dhṛtā āpaḥ* — "in it the waters are held and fixed"; being the support of the waters, the atmosphere is called *budhna* (Ni. 10-44).

> इन्द्राय गिरो अनिशितसर्गा अपः प्रैरयत्सगरस्य बुध्नात् । यो अक्षेणेव चक्रिया शचीभिर्विष्वक्तस्तम्भ पृथिवीमुत द्याम् ॥

> *indrāya giro aniśitasargā apaḥ prairayatsagarasya budhnāt | yo akṣeṇeva cakriyā śacībhirviṣvaktastambha pṛthivīmuta dyām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-89-4.) In this Ṛk *sagarasya budhnāt* is "from the support of the atmosphere, the deep root region of the atmosphere". In the present Ṛk, too, this very sense is to be taken. Then the deep root of the sacrifice is either the time of setting up the fire, or the churning of the causes (the two sticks). The sense is that from such a beginning the wise priests, by their effort, caused Agni to arise and be favourable to the sacrifice.

***īśānāsaḥ*** — *svakīyavyāpārasamarthāḥ*: those able in fulfilling their own duty. The word *īśāna* means "lord, master".

> आर्वाच्यग्ने [?] अवर्तो [?] … [rest unread] ईशानासो पित्वैस्य रायो वि सूरयः शतहिमा नो अर्कः [?] ॥

> *ārvācyagne [?] avarto [?] … [rest unread] īśānāso pitvaisya rāyo vi sūrayaḥ śatahimā no arkaḥ [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-82-6 [?]; this Ṛk is garbled at this resolution.)

> ईशानमस्य जगतः स्वर्दृशम् ।

> *īśānamasya jagataḥ svardṛśam |*

(Ai. Brā. 17-[?] [?].)

> ईशानं भूतभव्यस्य ।

> *īśānaṃ bhūtabhavyasya |*

(Ka. U. 4-12.) In all such passages the sense "lord" is clear; so here too the sense is that the sacrificer is lord of his acts. Since it says *īśānāsaḥ sūrayaḥ*, the sense is that the wise priests will perform their duty without fault. Such wise priests, by prayerful means, cause the wind Mātariśvan to kindle the Agni, himself hidden in sleep [?]; this is said by *mātariśvā mathāyati*. (continues on p. 172)

### Printed p. 172  (PDF 190)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

*(Continued from p. 171.)* … Agni's supernatural manifestation and his worldly origin are described in many ways. That Agni, the father of the sacrifice, was first manifested in the form of lightning by the wind, the Ṛk-saṃhitā says:

> अग्ने प्रथमो मातरिश्वने [?] आविर्भव सुक्रतो [?] … विवस्वते । अरेजेतां रोदसी होतृवूर्ये [?] … भारमयजो महो वसो [?] ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-3 [?]; the verse is only partly legible.) As said in such Ṛks, how Mātariśvan, for the benefit of the sacrificers Bhṛgu and Manu, brought to earth the Agni who was hidden in a far place, and did good to all the creatures on earth, has been told in detail before. In the present Ṛk also, by the epithet *guhā santam* the same point is stated. Here the word *mātariśvā* has, besides the sense *antarikṣe ceṣṭamāno vāyuḥ* "the wind moving in the atmosphere", a second sense: *mātari yoge śvasiti ceṣṭate iti mātariśvā yajamānaḥ*, "he who breathes, strives in the *mātṛ*, the arrangement of the rite, is *mātariśvā*, the sacrificer"; he churns the Agni *guhā santam araṇyor nigūḍham santam*, hidden in the two kindling-sticks. Because the sacrificer acts in the sacrifice that produces every kind of fruit, he is called Mātariśvan, and it is said that by effort he blows and kindles the Agni hidden in the sticks: so the second sense is given.

***pradivaḥ*** — the word *pradiva* is read among the names of the ancient (Ni. 3-[?]). The Nirukta authors cite —

> मरुत्वां इन्द्र वृषभो रणाय पिबा सोममनुष्वधं मदाय । आ सिञ्चस्व जठरे मध्व ऊर्मिं त्वं राजासि प्रदिवः सुतानाम् ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-47-1.) and explain the word *pradivaḥ* there as *pūrveṣv ahaḥsu*, "in the former days (as before)". In the present Ṛk also the sense is: for offering now, in the same way, the oblation that has been offered since beginningless time.

Sū. 1-[?]) suffix *iṣac*; *cita*: last-syllable accent), *varpasaḥ* (root *vṛja sambhaktau*; *vṛjaśīṅbhyāṃ rūpasyāṅgayoḥ puṭ ca* (Uṇ. **Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *yat* — for what reason; *pituḥ* — the food in the form of beasts; *paramāt* — for the sake of its excellent [obtaining]; *pra pari nīyate* — (this Agni) is carried round, in the sunwise direction (*pradakṣiṇa*) …

### Printed p. 175  (PDF 193)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 7 [?].)*

*Pratipadārtha (continued).* Or: [*paramāt* — excellent; *pituḥ* — the one who is the root-cause; and as the Gārhapatya fire is carried from (*pra pari nīyate*, led round)] the Āhavanīya (to the vicinity of the Āhavanīya) exceedingly; *pṛkṣudhaḥ* — (the flames) eager to eat the oblations, those that stand up in the form of burning on the beast-offerings and the *purodāśa*; and *vīrudhaḥ* — (the Agni) of the plants, in the form of creepers, standing upright, rising upwards; *daṃsu* — amidst the flames, resembling teeth; *rohati* — ascend upwards; *yat* — for which reason; *ubhā* — the *adhvaryu* and the sacrificer, or the two kindling-sticks, both together; *asya* — of this Agni; *januṣam* — the birth; *invate* — bring about (spread); *ādit* — then; *śucīḥ* — he is of pure form; *ghṛṇā* — (to the sacrificer) gracious, or bright with the light of flame; *yaviṣṭhaḥ* — extremely youthful; *abhavat* — came to be.

**Bhāvārtha.** In order that food in the form of beasts may be obtained in excellent measure, this Agni is led round in procession. The flames of Agni, eager to eat the oblations, those that stand up burning in the *purodāśa* and beast-offerings, and those that stand rising up in the form of creepers, rise upward amid the flames like teeth. The *adhvaryu* and the sacrificer together bring about the birth of this Agni. For all these reasons Agni is born as pure, as gracious to the sacrificer, and as exceedingly youthful and radiant.

**English Translation (as printed).** As for securing the perfection of food (Agni) is generated and the consumable branches rise amidst (the flames); and as both (the institutor of the rite and the priest) combine for his generation, therefore has he been generated, pure, youthful, and radiant.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***pituḥ*** — the word *pitu* is read among the names of food (Ni. 2-9). While giving the derivation of the word *pitu*, the Nirukta author cites

> पितुं नु स्तोषं महो धर्माणं तविषीम् । यस्य त्रितो व्योजसा वृत्रं विपर्वमर्दयत् ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-187-1.) and says *pituḥ pitur ity annanāma; pāter vā pibater vā pyāyater vā*: from the root *pā* "to protect", or from the root *pā* "to drink", or (continues on p. 176)

### Printed p. 176  (PDF 194)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

from the root *pyai* "to grow"; "I praise the food that is exceedingly strong and strength-giving", is the sense of the cited Ṛk. In the present Ṛk Sāyaṇa takes *pituḥ* in one sense as "food" and in another as "father". By the first, *pituḥ* is nominative and an adverb to *paramāt*: "in order that food in the form of beasts may be obtained excellently, this Agni is led round (*pra pari nīyate*)". By the second, *pituḥ* is ablative, an epithet of *paramāt*: "from the excellent Gārhapatya fire, which is the support of all and protector of the sacrifice, he is led forth and round (*pra pari nīyate*)".

***pṛkṣudhaḥ*** — *prakarṣeṇa bubhukṣitā bhoktum icchamānāḥ*: those eager to eat the oblations; or, another sense is possible: those that stand up burning in the midst of beast-offerings, *purodāśa* and so on. [?] It is an epithet of *vīrudhaḥ*.

***vīrudhaḥ*** — *vīrudha oṣadhayo bhavanti virohaṇāt*: "plants (creepers) are called so because they grow in a special way": so the derivation is given (Ni. 6-3), citing —

> ओषधीः प्रति मोदध्वं पुष्पवतीः प्रसूवरीः । अश्वा इव सजित्वरीर्वीरुधः पारयिष्णवः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-97-3.) — and the aptness of the word *vīrudhaḥ* here is shown.

***daṃsu*** — amid the flames, which are like teeth.

***invate*** — *invati, nakṣati* and others are read among the names of verbs of pervading (Ni. 2-10): "they cause to pervade".

***ghṛṇā*** — the word *ghṛṇi* is read among the names suggesting shining by flame: *jamat*, *arciḥ*, *śociḥ* and others (Ni. 2-[?]); so the word may mean "shining", or, since *ghṛṇā* means compassion, "one who shows kindness to the sacrificer"; either way it is an epithet of Agni.

The description in this Ṛk that Agni, as soon as kindled, becomes pure, gracious and most youthful —

> अग्निर्होता नि ससादा यजीयानुपस्थे मातुः सुरभावु लोके । युवा कविः पुरुनिष्ठ ऋतावा धर्ता कृष्टीनामुत मध्य इद्धः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?]; read with doubt.) (continues on p. 177)

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-3-[?].) In such Saṃhitā sentences too the primacy of Agni is shown.

Sū. 1-[?]); by *kit*, *ghumāsthā*… the root's *ā* becomes *i*; by *vyatyaya* the sixth case-ending is nominative), *nīyate* (root *ṇīñ prāpaṇe*; *laṭ*, third person singular in the passive; *nighāta* barred by *yadvṛttān nityam* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39): the dual *au* takes *ā*), *inyate* (here *invate*) (root *invi vyāptau*; *laṭ*, dual *tas*; *idito num dhātoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-58) gives *num*; *śap*; the suffix-accent *rut*, *visarga*; *nighāta* barred by *yadvṛttān nityam* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66); *tāsyanudāttet*: the root accent remains), *yaviṣṭhaḥ* (*atiśayena yuvā yaviṣṭhaḥ*; *tuśchandasi* …; *iṣṭhan* by *ātiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-55); *sthūladūra*… (Pā. Sū. 6-4-156) loss of *van*; *guṇa*; *ājñāt*…; *ñnityādir nityam*: first-syllable accent), *ghṛṇā* (the *matup* is dropped in Vedic; *supāṃ sulug…*: *ā* for the case-ending). (continues on p. 178)

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> आदिन्मातॄराविशद्यास्वा शुचिरहिंस्यमान उर्विया वि वावृधे ।
> अनु यत्पूर्वा अरुहत्सनाजुवो नि नव्यसीष्ववरासु धावते ॥ ५ ॥

> *ādinmātṝrāviśadyāsvā śucirahiṃsyamāna urviyā vi vāvṛdhe |*
> *anu yatpūrvā aruhatsanājuvo ni navyasīṣvavarāsu dhāvate ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आत् । इत् । मातॄः । आ । अविशत् । यासु । आ । शुचिः । अहिंस्यमानः । उर्विया । वि । ववृधे ।
> अनु । यत् । पूर्वाः । अरुहत् । सनाऽजुवः । नि । नव्यसीषु । अवरासु । धावते ॥ ५ ॥

> *āt | it | mātṝḥ | ā | aviśat | yāsu | ā | śuciḥ | ahiṃsyamānaḥ | urviyā | vi | vavṛdhe |*
> *anu | yat | pūrvāḥ | aruhat | sanā 'juvaḥ | ni | navyasīṣu | avarāsu | dhāvate ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *Agni, bright and praised, entered the ten quarters, his mothers, in which he grew unharmed; then he ascends the old branches in order and runs among the newer, inferior ones.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> अयमग्निः शुचिर्दीप्तः सन् आदित् पूर्वमन्त्रे यविष्ठो भवदित्युक्तत्वात्तदनन्तरमेव मातॄः उपादयित्रीर्मातृस्थानीया दश दिशः [?] आविशत् । सर्वतः प्राविशत् [?] । पूर्वत्र दशप्रमतिं जनयन्त योषण इत्युक्तत्वात् दिशां मातृत्वम् । दिक्षु प्रकाशेन व्याप्त इत्यर्थः । मातरो विशेष्यन्ते । यासु मातृषु अहिंस्यमानः परिपीड्यमान उर्विया उरु [?] अतिप्रभूतं नि [?] … वि ववृधे विविधं प्रवृद्धो ऽभवत् तास्वाविशदित्यन्वयः । यथा लोके कश्चित्त्रैजन्य [?] … सनाजुवः सनातनाः … [rest of the small type not read]

> *ayamagniḥ śucirdīptaḥ san ādit pūrvamantre yaviṣṭho bhavadityuktatvāttadanantarameva mātṝḥ upādayitrīrmātṛsthānīyā daśa diśaḥ [?] āviśat | sarvataḥ prāviśat [?] | pūrvatra daśapramatiṃ janayanta yoṣaṇa ityuktatvāt diśāṃ mātṛtvam | dikṣu prakāśena vyāpta ityarthaḥ | mātaro viśeṣyante | yāsu mātṛṣu ahiṃsyamānaḥ paripīḍyamāna urviyā uru [?] atiprabhūtaṃ ni [?] … vi vavṛdhe vividhaṃ pravṛddho 'bhavat tāsvāviśadityanvayaḥ | yathā loke kaścittraijanya [?] … sanājuvaḥ sanātanāḥ … [rest of the small type not read]*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** (*ayam agniḥ* — this Agni;) *ā śuciḥ* — extremely bright; *ādit* — at once, having been praised in the preceding Ṛk; *yat* — when; *sanājuvaḥ* — [those] [?] ... of long standing; *pūrvāḥ* — the earlier, [dried] and excellent plants and the like; *anu* — in order, one after another; *aruhat* — mounts and burns; *navyasīṣu* — new; *avarāsu* — inferior (not so dry) plants and the like; *ni dhāvate* — enters and burns; then *yāsu* — in which ten quarters; *ahiṃsyamānaḥ* — unharmed (by others); *urviyā* — exceedingly; *vi vavṛdhe* — grew with flames of many kinds; *mātṝḥ* — the ten quarters standing in the places of mothers; *ā aviśat* — has entered, enveloping them on all sides.

### Printed p. 179  (PDF 197)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

**Bhāvārtha.** This extremely brilliant Agni, as soon as he is praised in the preceding mantra, mounts successively the very ancient and excellent plants and the like, and also the new and not so excellent plants and the like, and burns them. Then, unharmed by others and exceedingly abundant, he grows with flames of many kinds in the ten quarters, and, entering them on all sides — the ten quarters standing in the places of mothers — he shines.

**English Translation (as printed).** Therefore has the brilliant Agni entered the maternal (quarters of space), amidst which, pure and unharmed he had evolved into magnitude so that he mounted (the bushes) placed before him, as he had (consumed others) prior to them, and runs rapidly among the more recent and inferior branches.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***vi vavṛdhe*** — *vividhaṃ pravṛddho 'bhavat*: he grew great, covering the world with forms of many kinds; thus Agni's growth is described.

***ādit*** — by this word the time and cause of Agni's growth are stated. In the previous mantra it was said "*yaviṣṭho 'bhavat*" (he became youthful); the sense is that as soon as he became youthful he grew; or, as soon as he was praised in the preceding mantra. The description that he entered all the plants and the like, both those well dried and favourable to the kindling of fire and those not well dried but green, and spread, is given in many places as the very manner of Agni's pervading.

***sanājuvaḥ*** — though ancient, existing from a long time [?]; hence, the sense is that they were fit at the time of Agni's attack.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar page 180, noted briefly).** *āviśat* (root *viśa praveśane*; *laṅ*, third person singular; *tiṅ*, *nighāta*), *ahiṃsyamānaḥ* (root *hisi hiṃsāyām*; *idito num dhātoḥ* gives *num*; *śānac* in the passive; *sārvadhātuke yak*; *anemuk*; *nañ*-compound, *tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīya…* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2): the accent of the first member of a negated compound), *urviyā* (*iyāḍiyājīkārāṇām upasaṃkhyānam*: *iyāt* for the case-ending; *cit*: last-syllable accent), *vāvṛdhe* (root *vṛdhu vṛddhau*; *liṭ*, third person singular; in Vedic, lengthening of the reduplicate in the *saṃhitā*; *ati-jñanta*, *nighāta*), *aruhat* (root *ruha bījajanmani prādurbhāve ca*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* gives *laṅ* in the present sense; *tip*; *itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu*; *kṛmṛdṛruhibhyaś chandasi* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-59) gives *aṅ* for *cli*; no *aḍ*; because of *yat*, *nighāta* is barred by *yadvṛttān nityam* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66), and the augment *aḍ* is *udātta*, so *ādyudātta*), *navyasīṣu* (*nava*; *īyasun* in the sense of excess; *ugitaś ca* gives *ṅīp*; *yasyeti ca* drops the final *a*; *chāndasa* loss of the *ī* of *īyasun*; *nit*, first-syllable accent by *ñnityādir nityam*), *dhāvate* (root *dhāvu gatiśuddhyoḥ*; *laṭ*, third person singular; *ati-jñanta*, no *nighāta*). ‖ 5 ‖

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *papracānāsaḥ* — the priests and the sacrificers who worship (with oblations and with hymns); *hotāram* — Agni, who accomplishes the oblation or who gives the invitation to the gods; *diviṣṭiṣu* — for the gratification of the gods; *vṛṇate* — they worship; *ādit* — thereafter; *bhagam iva* — as one worships and adorns the sun in the form of Bhaga, or a king; *ṛñjate* — they adorn; *yat* — because; *puruṣṭutaḥ* — praised in many ways (or by many); *viśvadhā* — Agni, who protects and upholds all; *kratvā* — by the sacrificial act in the form of sacrifices and the like; *majmanā* — with bodily strength; *devān* — the gods, or the priests; *śaṃsam* — the praiser; *martam* — the sacrificer also; *veti* — brings together; *dhāyase* — for food in the form of oblations.

### Printed p. 182  (PDF 200)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

**Bhāvārtha.** The priests and the sacrificers worship Agni, who accomplishes the oblation, with the aim of gratifying the gods. As many adorn a king and worship him, so they adorn this one. Agni, praised by many and upholding the whole world, brings together, by sacrificial act and bodily strength, the gods, or the priests, and the devoted sacrificer, for the sake of food in the form of oblations.

**English Translation (as printed).** Pious worshippers then adore the invoker (of the gods), for (the propitiation of) the dwellers in heaven, as (such men) adore a powerful prince, since the manylauded, and all-upholding (Agni) knows how by (holy) act and (bodily) strength to bring together the gods and their mortal worshippers for the sake of obtaining (mutual) sustenance.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***papracānāsaḥ*** — formed from the root *pṛc*, which gives the sense "to come in contact". It is an epithet of the priests and of the sacrificer: it means that the priests and sacrificers who worship Agni were joined with the oblations and the hymns, which are the means of worship. This word is used in contexts where identification is attained (*tādātmya*). For example —

> अद्भिः सोम पप्रचानस्य ते रसोऽव्यो वारं वि पवमान धावति । स मृज्यमानः कविभिर्मदिन्तम स्वदस्वेन्द्राय पवमान पीतये ॥

> *adbhiḥ soma papracānasya te raso 'vyo vāraṃ vi pavamāna dhāvati | sa mṛjyamānaḥ kavibhirmadintama svadasvendrāya pavamāna pītaye ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?]; read with doubt.) In this Ṛk *papracānasya te* addresses the Soma that is to be mixed with purified water. Here the word is used because of the aptness of the mingling of Soma juice and water. In the present Ṛk also an inseparable relation between the priests and the oblations, which they hold with undivided mind and worship with the utmost devotion and faith, is suggested.

***hotāram*** — *homaniṣpādakam āhvātāraṃ vā*: the one who accomplishes the oblation by offering substances, or the one who gives the invitation to the gods: thus the word *hotṛ* has two senses, since there are two kinds of acts. The same view in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa — (continues on p. 183)

> यज्ञो वै देवेभ्य उदक्रामत्तमन्विच्छन्भिः प्रैषैः प्रैषमैच्छन् [?] … अनुवित्त्वा [?] यज्ञो राधेनैति [?] … आहुतिर्वै नाम्नाम् [?] … यजमानस्य … ऊतयः खलु वै ता नाम यद्भिर्देवा यजमानस्य जवनायन्ति ये वै पन्थानो यः स्रुतयस्ता वा ऊतयस्त [?] …

> *yajño vai devebhya udakrāmattamanvicchanbhiḥ praiṣaiḥ praiṣamaicchan [?] … anuvittvā [?] yajño rādhenaiti [?] … āhutirvai nāmnām [?] … yajamānasya … ūtayaḥ khalu vai tā nāma yadbhirdevā yajamānasya javanāyanti ye vai panthāno yaḥ srutayastā vā ūtayasta [?] …*

(Ai. Brā. 1-[?]; this passage is garbled at this resolution.) Once the sacrifice went away from the gods. Then, offering oblations, they got it back. *Āhuti*, "oblation", means the offering by the invocation, pronouncing the name of the deity. If it is said that one who offers such an oblation is called *hotṛ*, then another question arises —

> तेदामयज्ञेन [?] जुहोत्यथ यो नु चाहि यजति च कस्मात्तं होतेत्याचक्षते इति यद्यावानस तत्र यथाभजनं देवता अमुमावहामुमावहेत्यावापयति तदेव होतुर्होतृत्वं होता भवति । होतेत्येनमाचक्षते य एवं वेद ॥

> *tedāmayajñena [?] juhotyatha yo nu cāhi yajati ca kasmāttaṃ hotetyācakṣate iti yadyāvānasa tatra yathābhajanaṃ devatā amumāvahāmumāvahetyāvāpayati tadeva hoturhotṛtvaṃ hotā bhavati | hotetyenamācakṣate ya evaṃ veda ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 1-[?].) The one who offers the oblation is one, and the one who gives the invitation for the offering and recites the mantra is another; how does the name *hotṛ* apply to the one who recites the mantra? — to this question: since the reciter of this mantra calls the various deities in accordance with each offering's outcome, the name *hotṛ* is rightly his. After this explanation, the Brāhmaṇa gives —

> मनो वै यज्ञस्य मैत्रावरुणो वाग्यज्ञस्य होता ।

> *mano vai yajñasya maitrāvaruṇo vāgyajñasya hotā |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-[?].) — in this sentence it says that there is identity between the speech reciting the mantra and the *hotṛ*. And again —

> सीद होतः स्व उ लोके चिकित्वान्त्सादया यज्ञं सुकृतस्य योनौ । … अग्निर्वै देवानां होता तस्यैष स्वो लोको यदुत्तरवेदिनाभिः [?] … नि होता होतृषदने विदान इत्यग्निर्वै देवानां होता तस्यैतत्स्वं होतृषदनं यदुत्तरवेदिनाभिः ॥

> *sīda hotaḥ sva u loke cikitvāntsādayā yajñaṃ sukṛtasya yonau | … agnirvai devānāṃ hotā tasyaiṣa svo loko yaduttaravedinābhiḥ [?] … ni hotā hotṛṣadane vidāna ityagnirvai devānāṃ hotā tasyaitatsvaṃ hotṛṣadanaṃ yaduttaravedinābhiḥ ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 1-[?]; read with doubt.) Such sentences address Agni, the accomplisher of oblations, as the *veda-hotṛ* [?]. Hence in the present Ṛk, for the word *hotāram*, the commentator has given the sense *homaniṣpādakam āhvātāraṃ vā* and shown it to be an epithet of Agni.

***diviṣṭiṣu*** — *diviṣṭiṣu diva iṣaṇeṣu* (Ni. 6-[?]); the Nirukta authors say the sense is "the sacrifices that procure the road to heaven", and cite

> स्थूरं राधः शताश्वं कुरुङ्गस्य दिविष्टिषु । राज्ञस्त्वेषस्य सुभगस्य रातिषु तुर्वशेष्वमन्महि ॥

> *sthūraṃ rādhaḥ śatāśvaṃ kuruṅgasya diviṣṭiṣu | rājñastveṣasya subhagasya rātiṣu turvaśeṣvamanmahi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-4-19 [?].) to show the right sense of the word. Sāyaṇa also explains this word: *divaḥ svargasyaiṣaṇeṣu prāptihetubhūtāsu yāgakriyāsu*, "in the sacrificial acts that are the means of obtaining heaven".

***ṛñjate*** — *ṛñjatiḥ prasādhanakarmā* (Ni. 6-31): the Nirukta authors say it means "adorn", citing

> आ व ऋञ्जस ऊर्जां व्युष्ट्विन्द्रं मरुतो रोदसी अनक्तन । उभे यथा नो अहनी सचाभुवा सदःसदो वरिवस्यात उद्भिदा ॥

> *ā va ṛñjasa ūrjāṃ vyuṣṭvindraṃ maruto rodasī anaktana | ubhe yathā no ahanī sacābhuvā sadaḥsado varivasyāta udbhidā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) — the Ṛk containing *ṛñjase*. Sāyaṇa too explains this word as *prasādhayanti, alaṅkurvanti*.

***majmanā*** — this word is read among the names of strength (Ni. 2-9): *śārīreṇa balena*, "with bodily strength", Sāyaṇa explains.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar pages 184–185, noted briefly).** *hotāram* (root *hu dānādanayoḥ*; suffix *tṛn* in the agent sense; *guṇa* by the suffix; *nit*, first-syllable accent; accusative singular), *vṛṇate* (root *vṛñ sambhaktau*; *laṭ*, third person plural; *ati-jñanta*, hence *tiṅ-nighāta*), *diviṣṭiṣu* (*diva iṣṭayaḥ* — in the locative; by *divi-ṣṭiṣu* … *sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante* gives *vivalut* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-[?]) which does not apply here; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*: the first member's accent), *papracānāsaḥ* (root *pṛcī saṃparke*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* gives *liṭ* in the present sense; *liṭaḥ kānac* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-106); the root takes reduplication; …). (continues on p. 185)

#### Ṛk 7

### Printed p. 186  (PDF 204)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> वि यदस्थाद्यजतो वातचोदितो ह्वारो न वक्वा जरणा अनाकृतः ।
> तस्य पत्मन्दक्षुषः कृष्णजंहसः शुचिजन्मनो रज आ व्यध्वनः ॥ ७ ॥

> *vi yadasthādyajato vātacodito hvāro na vakvā jaraṇā anākṛtaḥ |*
> *tasya patmandakṣuṣaḥ kṛṣṇajaṃhasaḥ śucijanmano raja ā vyadhvanaḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> वि । यत् । अस्थात् । यजतः । वातऽचोदितः । ह्वारः । न । वक्वा । जरणा । अनाकृतः ।
> तस्य । पत्मन् । दक्षुषः । कृष्णऽजंहसः । शुचिऽजन्मनः । रजः । आ । विऽअध्वनः ॥ ७ ॥

> *vi | yat | asthāt | yajataḥ | vāta 'coditaḥ | hvāraḥ | na | vakvā | jaraṇā | anākṛtaḥ |*
> *tasya | patman | dakṣuṣaḥ | kṛṣṇa 'jaṃhasaḥ | śuci 'janmanaḥ | rajaḥ | ā | vi 'adhvanaḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *When Agni, urged by wind, spreads unchecked in many directions like a roving, crooked talker, the world is intent on the sacrificial way of this all-burning, dark-pathed one.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> यद्यदायमग्निर्वातचोदितो वायुना प्रेरितः । तृतीया कर्मणीति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । यजतः सर्वैर्यष्टव्यो यष्टुं योग्यः सन् व्यस्थात् विविधं तिष्ठति [?] सर्वतो व्याप्तो भवति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । अनाकृतः [?] अनिवारितोऽप्रहतप्रसरः । वक्वा बहुवक्ता ॥ वचेरन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यत इति वनिप् । दृशिग्रहणात्कन्प्रत्ययः [?] ॥ ह्वारो न कुटिल इव [?] । ह्वरतेर्ण्यन्ताच्चाद्यच् [?] । स यथा जरणा स्तुतीर्विशिष्टा [?] विविधं कुर्वन् वर्तते तद्वदयमप्यनाकृतोऽप्रतिबद्धप्रसरो व्यवस्थितः [?] । कदा । तस्याग्नेः सर्वत्र पत्मन् पतने मार्गे यज्ञरूपे रजो रञ्जनात्मके [?] लोके आ [?] … तस्य दक्षुषः दहतः कृष्णजंहसः कृष्णमार्गस्य । पुनःपुनर्गम्यते इति जंहा मार्गः । हन्तेरञ्लुगन्तात्मणसुन् [?] … शुचिजन्मनः मन्त्रसहिताभ्यामरणिभ्यामुत्पन्नत्वात् [?] … विविधजन्मस्य … व्यध्वनः नानामार्गस्य … [partly unread]

> *yadyadāyamagnirvātacodito vāyunā preritaḥ | tṛtīyā karmaṇīti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | yajataḥ sarvairyaṣṭavyo yaṣṭuṃ yogyaḥ san vyasthāt vividhaṃ tiṣṭhati [?] sarvato vyāpto bhavati | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | anākṛtaḥ [?] anivārito 'prahataprasaraḥ | vakvā bahuvaktā ‖ vaceranyebhyo 'pi dṛśyata iti vanip | dṛśigrahaṇātkanpratyayaḥ [?] ‖ hvāro na kuṭila iva [?] | hvaraterṇyantāccādyac [?] | sa yathā jaraṇā stutīrviśiṣṭā [?] vividhaṃ kurvan vartate tadvadayamapyanākṛto 'pratibaddhaprasaro vyavasthitaḥ [?] | kadā | tasyāgneḥ sarvatra patman patane mārge yajñarūpe rajo rañjanātmake [?] loke ā [?] … tasya dakṣuṣaḥ dahataḥ kṛṣṇajaṃhasaḥ kṛṣṇamārgasya | punaḥpunargamyate iti jaṃhā mārgaḥ | hanterañlugantātmaṇasun [?] … śucijanmanaḥ mantrasahitābhyāmaraṇibhyāmutpannatvāt [?] … vividhajanmasya … vyadhvanaḥ nānāmārgasya … [partly unread]*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *anākṛtaḥ* — he who has unchecked flow of speech; *hvāraḥ na* — like a deceitful man; *vakvā* — as a babbler; *jaraṇāḥ* — (without discrimination of rank) extends his talk with praises of many kinds, so (this Agni); *vātacoditaḥ* — impelled by the wind; *yajataḥ* — worthy of the worship of all; *yat* — when; *vi asthāt* — [he], with unchecked spread, spreads in many directions (then); *dakṣuṣaḥ* — the all-consuming; *kṛṣṇajaṃhasaḥ* — whose path is dark; *śucijanmanaḥ* — of pure birth (by mantra); *vyadhvanaḥ* — whose flames spread by many paths; *tasya agneḥ* — of that Agni; *patman* — in the way of worship in the form of sacrifice; *rajaḥ* — the world; *ā (asthāt)* — remains intent.

### Printed p. 187  (PDF 205)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

**Bhāvārtha.** As a babbler with unchecked flow of speech, a deceiver, extends his talk with praises of many kinds, with no sense of due order, so this Agni too — impelled by the wind, worthy of the worship of all, spreading with unchecked flow in many directions, consuming everything, of the dark path, of pure birth by mantra, with flames spread along many paths — in the way of worship that is the sacrifice of this Agni the whole world is intent.

**English Translation (as printed).** Since the adorable (Agni), impelled by the wind, spreads, in various directions, like an insincere and unrestrained chatterer, (who utters indiscriminate) praises, therefore the world is assiduous in the worship of him, the consumer of all, whose way is dark, who is pure of birth, and follows various paths.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** In this Ṛk the growth of Agni, with his unchecked spreading, is compared to the growth of an unbroken talker's words.

***anākṛtaḥ*** — *anivāritaḥ apratihataprasaraḥ*: Sāyaṇa explains it as "having unobstructed flow". The other derivation can be arrived at in two ways. *Anā* and *kṛtaḥ*: "made without obstruction" — the derivation can be shown suitably in this context. Thus —

> अभ्रातृव्यो अना त्वमनापिरिन्द्र जनुषा सनादसि । युधेदापित्वमिच्छसे ॥

> *abhrātṛvyo anā tvamanāpirindra januṣā sanādasi | yudhedāpitvamicchase ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-21-13.) In this Ṛk Sāyaṇa explains the word *anā* as *aniyantrake*, "unrestrained"; for the word *anā* other senses also are given — *āsyena* (1-12-3), *prāṇarūpeṇa balena* (4-30-3) — but those senses are not apt here. Hence *anā-kṛtaḥ* means "a talker who keeps going without check" [?].

***hvāraḥ*** — *kuṭila*: not straight, that is, one without a truthful feeling and conduct, a deceiver. The babbler, because he rambles beyond measure, has no straight and definite object; because he is crooked the epithet *hvāraḥ* is used. This epithet is also used of a thief. For example (continues on p. 188)

### Printed p. 188  (PDF 206)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

> युवं पयो उस्रियायामधत्तं पक्वमामायामव पूर्व्यं गोः । अन्तर्यद्वनिनो वामृतस्पृशा ह्वारो न शुचिर्यजते हविष्मान् [?] ॥

> *yuvaṃ payo usriyāyāmadhattaṃ pakvamāmāyāmava pūrvyaṃ goḥ | antaryadvanino vāmṛtaspṛśā hvāro na śuciryajate haviṣmān [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-180-3.) In this Ṛk the vigilance of the sacrificer is compared to the vigilance of a thief; here *hvāro na* means "like a thief". The senses "thief" and "deceiver" for the word *hvāra* came by tradition; the root sense of this word is "crooked, curved".

> क्रत्वा हि द्रोणे अज्यसेऽग्ने वाजी न कृत्व्यः । परिज्मेव स्वधा गयोऽत्यो न ह्वार्यः शिशुः ॥

> *kratvā hi droṇe ajyase 'gne vājī na kṛtvyaḥ | parijmeva svadhā gayo 'tyo na hvāryaḥ śiśuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk the word *hvāryaḥ* shows the crooked gait of a young horse; and

> उत स्म दुर्गृभीयसे पुत्रो न ह्वार्याणाम् । पुरू यो दग्धासि वनाग्ने पशुर्न यवसे ॥

> *uta sma durgṛbhīyase putro na hvāryāṇām | purū yo dagdhāsi vanāgne paśurna yavase ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-4-[?].) in this Ṛk the word *hvāryāṇām* shows *kuṭilaṃ gacchatāṃ sarpāṇām*, the crooked movement of snakes moving crookedly. In the present Ṛk, the epithet *hvāraḥ* is used to show the crooked way of a babbler who talks merely for the sake of talking, with no definite aim, and to show his deceitful dealing.

***vakvā*** — *bahuvaktā*, "a great talker": saying this, Sāyaṇa shows that it is formed from the root *vac*. But it appears more correct to say that its root is the verb *vaki* (*kauṭilye gatau ca*). The sense of this word is "crooked", or "crookedness". To show the derivation *vakvā* from *vac* does not seem fit [?]; the sense also agrees with the second root. But since the word *vakvā* is used in all the contexts of making great noise, one has to say that there it comes from the root *vac*. For example —

> असर्जि वक्वा रथ्ये यथाजौ धिया मनोता प्रथमो मनीषी । दश स्वसारो अधि सानो अव्ये जिन्वन्ति वह्निं सदनान्यच्छ ॥

> *asarji vakvā rathye yathājau dhiyā manotā prathamo manīṣī | daśa svasāro adhi sāno avye jinvanti vahniṃ sadanānyaccha ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?].) in this Ṛk it is an epithet of Soma, "making a sound", and

> श्रुधी हवमिन्द्र शूर पृथ्या उत स्तवसे वेन्यस्यार्कैः । आ यस्ते योनिं घृतवन्तमस्वारूर्मिर्न निम्नैर्द्रवयन्त वक्वाः ॥

> *śrudhī havamindra śūra pṛthyā uta stavase venyasyārkaiḥ | ā yaste yoniṃ ghṛtavantamasvārūrmirna nimnairdravayanta vakvāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].) (continues on p. 189)

### Printed p. 189  (PDF 207)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

in this Ṛk as an epithet of the sounding praisers; and,

> प्राग्रुवो नभन्वो न वक्वा ध्वस्रा अपिन्वन्युवतीर्ऋतज्ञाः [?] । धन्वान्यज्रा अपृणक् तृषाणा अधोगिन्द्रः स्त्रो [?] … दंसुपुष्टीः [?] ॥

> *prāgruvo nabhanvo na vakvā dhvasrā apinvanyuvatīrṛtajñāḥ [?] | dhanvānyajrā apṛṇak tṛṣāṇā adhogindraḥ stro [?] … daṃsupuṣṭīḥ [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?]; read with doubt.) in this Ṛk, since it is an epithet of the sounding army, one has to say that the root is *vac*. In the present Ṛk, since both qualities, sound and crookedness, are present, it may be formed from either root. "A babbler" is the sense.

***jaraṇāḥ*** — this word is ordinarily formed from the root *jṝ* (*vayohānau*) and indicates old age and decay [as used in Ṛks 1-[?]-[?]; 10-[?]-[?] and others]. But in the Ṛk

> अध प्र जज्ञे तरणिर्ममत्तु प्र रोच्यस्या उषसो न सूरः । इन्दुर्येभिराष्ट स्वेदुहव्यैः स्रुवेण सिञ्चञ्जरणाभि धाम ॥

> *adha pra jajñe taraṇirmamattu pra rocyasyā uṣaso na sūraḥ | induryebhirāṣṭa sveduhavyaiḥ sruveṇa siñcañjaraṇābhi dhāma ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?]; read with doubt.) it is also used in the sense of praise. Sāyaṇa, showing another derivation, explains *jarati stutikarmā* (Ni. 3-[?]), *asmāt karmaṇi lyuṭ*, and explains *jaraṇā* as *stotavyaḥ* in the explanation of Ṛk 1-66-1. The Nirukta authors

> जराबोध तद्विविड्ढि विशेविशे यज्ञियाय । स्तोमं रुद्राय दृशीकम् ॥

> *jarābodha tadviviḍḍhi viśeviśe yajñiyāya | stomaṃ rudrāya dṛśīkam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-27-10.) citing this Ṛk, showing the derivation of the word *jarābodha*, indicate the sense of this word thus: *jarā jaratiḥ stutikarmā* (Ni. 10-[?]). Accordingly in the present Ṛk also *jaraṇā* means "a praiser". The common quality between the babbler and the praisers here is that both extend their sentences without measure.

Thus the epithets *anākṛtaḥ*, *hvāraḥ*, *jaraṇāḥ*, as they tell the nature of *vakvā na*, also become epithets of Agni and tell his unobstructed, crooked and noise-filled spread.

***kṛṣṇajaṃhasaḥ*** — *kṛṣṇamārgasya*: "of the dark path" is an epithet of Agni. Showing the derivation of the word *jaṃha* as *punaḥpunargamyate iti jaṃhā mārgaḥ*, Sāyaṇa explains it as "path". (continues on p. 190)

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> रथो न यातः शिक्वभिः कृतो द्यामङ्गेभिररुषेभिरीयते ।
> आदस्य ते कृष्णासो दक्षि सूरयः शूरस्येव त्वेषथादीषते वयः ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 192  (PDF 210)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> रथः । न । यातः । शिक्वऽभिः । कृतः । द्याम् । अङ्गेभिः । अरुषेभिः । ईयते ।
> आत् । अस्य । ते । कृष्णासः । दक्षि । सूरयः । शूरस्यऽइव । त्वेषऽथात् । ईषते । वयः ॥ ८ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *Agni, set up by us, goes to the sky with his moving flame-limbs like a chariot bound with ropes; his paths turn black with smoke, and beasts and birds flee from his radiance as from a hero's might.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> अयमग्निः शिक्वभी रज्जुभिः कृतो बद्धो रथो न रथ इव । स यथा स्वैर्नाद्भिः [?] अङ्गैरीयते तद्वत् [?] … ज्वालादिरूपैरवयवैर्द्यामन्तरिक्षं [?] स्पृष्ट्वा सन्नीयते । गच्छति । ईङ् गतौ ॥ आत् प्रवृद्ध्यनन्तरमस्याग्नेस्ते सूरयः सरणयो मार्गाः कृष्णासः कृष्णवर्णा भवन्ति । यते [?] एवं भवन्ति तदेवाह । दक्षि दहति काष्ठानि [?] । छान्दसः शपो लुक् [?] । किंच ज्वलितस्याग्नेस्त्वेषथात् दीप्त्यात् [?] तेजसः सकाशाद्यज्ञोपकारार्थं [?] वयः पक्ष्यादि ईषते गच्छन्ति । ईष गतौ । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । पलायन्ते । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । शूरस्य त्वेषथादिव कस्यचिदाक्रान्तस्य दीप्त्या तेजसः सकाशादित्यपलायमानाः [?] … एवमन्तरिक्षं स्पृशन् सर्वतो दहतीति सर्वदा दावाग्निरूपेण स्तूयते ॥ [partly unread]

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *śikvabhiḥ* — with ropes; *kṛtaḥ* — bound; *ratho na* — as a chariot moves easily; *yātaḥ* — Agni, established (by us); *aruṣebhiḥ* — having the nature of moving about; *aṅgebhiḥ* — with the limbs in the form of flames; *dyām* — to the atmosphere; *īyate* — goes; *āt* — as soon as he has grown thus; *asya* — of this Agni; *sūrayaḥ* — the paths; *dakṣi* — by burning (the fuel); *kṛṣṇāsaḥ* — become black (with smoke); *śūrasya iva* — like an enemy that flees, terrified by the radiance of a hero; *tveṣathāt* — from the brilliant radiance (of this Agni); *vayaḥ* — all the beasts and birds that move about; *īṣate* — flee far away.

**Bhāvārtha.** As a chariot bound with ropes moves easily, so Agni, established by us, goes to the atmosphere with his limbs in the form of flames that have the nature of moving about. As soon as he has grown thus, his paths, because they burn fuel and the like, become black with smoke. And as enemies, terrified by the radiance of a valiant hero, flee far away, so all the beasts and birds moving about, terrified by the brilliant radiance of this Agni, flee far away.

### Printed p. 193  (PDF 211)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 8 [?].)*

**English Translation (as printed).** Like a chariot drawn by ropes, Agni, set in movement by his own revolving members (his flames) proceeds to the heavens; the paths he traverses are blackened by smoke, as he consumes (the fuel), and (beasts and) birds fly from his radiance as (enemies) fly from the prowess of a hero.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***śikvabhiḥ*** — for this word in this Ṛk Sāyaṇa gives the sense *rajjubhiḥ*, "with ropes". The scholar Monier Williams, in his Sanskrit–English Dictionary, first gives for this word the sense "Skilful, clever, artistic", and afterwards (the English text reads: "accord. say. — Rajju and tejas") gives Sāyaṇa's view. Sāyaṇa too, except at this one place, has in all other places explained *śikva* as "strength" (*śakti*) or "brilliance" (*tejas*). For example —

> प्र ये मे बन्धुवेशे गां वोचन्त सूरयः पृश्निं वोचन्त मातरम् । अथा पितरमिष्मिणं रुद्रं वोचन्त शिक्वसः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-52-[?].)

> व्यक्रन्द्रा [?] व्यहानि शिक्वसो व्यन्तरिक्षं वि रजांसि धूतयः । वि यदज्रान् अजथ नाव ईं यथा वि दुर्गाणि मरुतो नाह रिष्यथ [?] ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-54-[?].)

> त्वं त्या चिदच्युताग्ने पशुर्न यवसे । धामा ह यत्ते अजर वना वृश्चन्ति शिक्वसः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-3-[?].) In these Ṛks Sāyaṇa explains *śikvasaḥ* as *śaktāḥ*, "the powerful"; and in

> तमस्मेरा युवतयो युवानं मर्मृज्यमानाः परि यन्त्यापः । स शुक्रेभिः शिक्वभी रेवदस्मे दीदायानिध्मो घृतनिर्णिगप्सु ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-35-4.) it is "shining" (*dīptasya prakāśamānasya*); and in this Ṛk *śikvabhiḥ* means *tejobhiḥ*, "with brilliances". All these senses support the sense given by Monier Williams. Only in this one place has the sense *rajjubhiḥ* been given. This sense also is suitable to this context. (continues on p. 194)

### Printed p. 194  (PDF 212)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

***aruṣebhiḥ*** — for this word Sāyaṇa gives *gamanaśīlaiḥ*, "of a moving nature", and shows it as an epithet of *aṅgebhiḥ*. Or, since the word *aruṣa* has many senses, those that fit the context can be noticed. The Nirukta authors have counted this word among the names of the horse (Ni. 1-[?]), among the names of motion (Ni. 2-[?]) and as a synonym of "Uṣas" (Ni. 3-[?]). Also —

> विता उ त्या उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमञ्जते । निष्कृण्वाना आयुधानीव धृष्णवः प्रति गावोऽरुषीर्यन्ति मातरः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-1.) citing this Ṛk, *aruṣīḥ* there is an epithet of Uṣas, in the sense *ārocamānā*, "radiant, brilliant". Thus this word is used in some places as an epithet and in others as the subject, giving different senses. For example —

> युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नमरुषं चरन्तं परि तस्थुषः । रोचन्ते रोचना दिवि ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-6-1.) If one examines the word *aruṣa* in this Ṛk, the sage here describes sunrise. Indra is conceived as the radiant deity desired, the Sun as his horse, the Maruts as his companions. Though the word *aruṣa* gives the sense "reddish-brown", here it is a synonym of "horse" or of "sun" as a synonym of horse; *bradhna* is an epithet of *aruṣa*. In the same manner, there are many contexts where *aruṣa* gives an independent and conventional sense as the subject. For example —

> ये [?] ते अग्ने हरितो घृतस्ना रोहितास ऋजुअञ्चः स्वञ्चः । अरुषासो वृषण ऋजुमुष्का आ देवताति मिमृक्षन्त दस्माः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk the colour-words *haritaḥ*, *rohitāsaḥ*, *aruṣāsaḥ* denote horses of those colours. And —

> आ वर्धयन्त्सुभगं सप्त यह्वीः श्वेतं जज्ञानमरुषं महित्वा । शिशुं न जातमभ्यारुरश्वा देवासो अग्निं जनिमन्वपुष्यन् ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-1-[?].) here it is an epithet of Agni; and

> त्वं नृचक्षा वृषभानु पूर्वीः कृष्णास्वग्ने अरुषो वि भाहि । वसो नेषि च पर्षि चात्यंहः कृधी नो राय उशिजो यविष्ठ ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-15-3.) here it is an adverb (*kriyāviśeṣaṇa*). In this way in Ṛks 4-[?]-[?]; 1-[?]-[?]; 4-[?]-[?]; 4-[?]-[?] and many others it is used as an epithet. In some places one can see it used as a name denoting the visible deity himself — (continues on p. 195)

### Printed p. 195  (PDF 213)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 8 [?].)*

— taking just two Ṛks as examples:

> अप स्वसुरुषसो नग्जिहीते रिणक्ति कृष्णीररुषाय पन्थाम् । अश्वामघा गोमघा वां हुवेम दिवा नक्तं शरुमस्मद्युयोतम् ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-65-1 [?].) Here Sāyaṇa himself has not given a settled sense for the word *aruṣāya*; he has given both *ārocamānāya agnaye sūryāya vā*, "to the radiant Agni or to the Sun", as alternatives. In explaining this Ṛk the view of the scholar Max Müller is noteworthy. He says:

> *Here Arusha shares the same half-mythological character as Ushas, where we should speak of Dawn and morning as mere periods of time, the Vedic poet speaks of them as living and intelligent beings, half human, half divine, as powers of nature capable of understanding his prayers and powerful enough to reward his praises. I do not think that we need hesitate to take Arusha in this passage as a proper name of the morning, or of the morning sun to whom the dark Goddess, the Night, yields the path when he rises in the East.* (The Sacred Books of the East, Vol. XXXII, p. 21.)

In the same way —

> विरोचिष्ट [?] … दिवः शिशुं सहसः सूनुमग्निं यज्ञस्य केतुमरुषं यजध्यै ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?]; the first line is garbled at this resolution.) in this Ṛk too, although it is clear that *aruṣam* is an epithet of Agni, it would be no mistake to say that the word *aruṣa* is itself another proper name that is a synonym of Agni and indicates his nature. In explaining this Ṛk too the scholar Max Müller indicates his view of this word in this way:

> *… … But I return to my original translation, and I prefer to see in Arusha the representative of the rising Sun and, at the same time, of the sacrificial fire of the morning, but nevertheless as having in the mind of the poet a personality of his own. He is the child of Dyu, originally the offspring of heaven. He is the son of strength, originally generated by the strong rubbing of the Aranis. He is the light of the sacrifice, whether as reminding man that the time for the morning sacrifice has come, or as himself lighting the sacrifice on the eastern altar of the sky. He is Arusha, originally as clothed in bright red colour, but gradually changed into the representative of the morning.* (S. B. E. Vol. 32, pp. 25–6.)

Besides, since there are also passages in which the feminine word *aruṣī* is used [?] … if one considers the senses, (continues on p. 196)

### Printed p. 196  (PDF 214)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

*(Continued from p. 195.)*

> वयं हि ते अमन्महि [?] आन्तादा [?] पराकात् । अश्वे न चक्रे अरुषी [?] ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] [?].) In such Ṛks *aruṣī* denotes Uṣas as the deity; and

> युक्ष्वा ह्यरुषी रथे हरितो देव रोहितः । ताभिर्देवाँ इहा वह ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-14-12 [?].)

> अधि श्रियं नि दधुश्चारुमस्मिन्दिवो यदक्षी अमृता अकृण्वन् । अध क्षरन्ति सिन्धवो न सृष्टाः प्र नीचीरग्ने अरुषीरजानन् ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-71-10 [?].) In such Ṛks *aruṣī* is understood as the golden-hued mare of Agni; in the others, 1-14-12 and the like, as an ordinary mare. Regarding the special senses of the word *aruṣī* used in the feminine, Max Müller says again:

> *Further on, where the meanings attributed to Arushi in the Veda are collected, it is said: that Arushi means a red horse, also the teams of Agni and Ushas. Now, here surely, a distinction should have been made between those passages in which Arushi means a real horse and those where it expresses the imaginary steeds of Agni. The former, it should be observed, occur in one Mandala only, and in places of somewhat doubtful authority. Again, two passages are set apart where Arushi is supposed to mean flames. Now, it may be perfectly true that the red horses of Agni are meant for flames, just as the red horses of Indra may be the rays of the Sun. But, in that case, the red horses of Agni should always have been thus translated, or rather interpreted, and not in one passage only.* (S. B. E. XXXII, p. 27.)

In the present Ṛk, for the word *aruṣebhiḥ* one may give the sense "of moving nature" or "golden-hued".

***sūrayaḥ*** — *saraṇayaḥ mārgāḥ*: Sāyaṇa explains it as "paths that spread". Ordinarily the word *sūri* is used in the sense "wise"; the purport is "a wise praiser". *Rebhaḥ*, *jaritā* and the like are read in the Nirukta among the names of praisers (Ni. 3-[?]).

> उषो ये ते प्र यामेषु युञ्जते मनो दानाय सूरयः । अत्राह तत्कण्व एषां कण्वतमो नाम गृणाति नृणाम् ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-48-4.)

### Printed p. 197  (PDF 215)

> इदं नमो वृषभाय स्वराजे सत्यशुष्माय तवसेऽवाचि । अस्मिन्निन्द्र वृजने सर्ववीराः स्मत्सूरिभिस्तव शर्मन्त्स्याम ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-23-6 [?].) In such Ṛks *vipraḥ*, *vidvadbhiḥ* is the sense. In the present Ṛk, and in a few others also, as said above, "paths" — the paths of Agni's spreading — are suggested.

#### Ṛk 9

### Printed p. 198  (PDF 216)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वया ह्यग्ने वरुणो धृतव्रतो मित्रः शाशद्रे अर्यमा सुदानवः ।
> यत्सीमनु क्रतुना विश्वथा विभुररान्न नेमिः परिभूरजायथाः ॥ ९ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वया । हि । अग्ने । वरुणः । धृतऽव्रतः । मित्रः । शाशद्रे । अर्यमा । सुऽदानवः ।
> यत् । सीम् । अनु । क्रतुना । विश्वऽथा । विऽभुः । अरान् । न । नेमिः । परिऽभूः । अजायथाः ॥ ९ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *By you, Agni, Varuṇa keeps his vows, Mitra and Aryaman are bountiful and strong; you, pervading all like a felly encircling the spokes, were born through all rites.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> हे अग्ने त्वया खलु वरुणो रात्र्यभिमानी देवो धृतव्रतः स्वीकृतवर्षादिकर्मा भवति । तथा मित्रोऽहरभिमानी देवः शाशद्रे शातयति तमः । शद्लृ शातने । छान्दसो लिट् । बहुलं छन्दसीति रुट् । तुजादित्वादभ्यासदीर्घः [?] ॥ तथार्यमोभयोर्मध्यवर्ती देवः सुदानवः शोभनदानो भवति । व्यत्ययेन बहुवचनम् ॥ यद्वा । एते वरुणादयः सुदानवः शोभनदानाः स्वस्वकार्यकर्तारस्सन्त्यो [?] …

### Printed p. 199  (PDF 217)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 8 [?].)*

> … हि शाशद्रे । शात्रे [?] … तीक्ष्णीक्रियन्ते [?] । … मन्त्रात्मक … श्रेयमग्ने [?] वरुणो जायसे । … इति रेभ्यभावे [?] … । हि चेति निघातभावः ॥ वरुणादीनामनुग्रहाय [?] यत् यस्मात्कारणात् हे अग्ने सीम् सर्वतः क्रतुना कर्मणा विश्वथा विश्वे इव विश्वात्मके इव विभुर्मित्रायामात्मना सर्वव्यापी परिभूः स्वतेजसा सर्वतः परिवर्तिता सन् अजायथाः जायसे प्रादुर्भवसि । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । अरान्नेमिः [?] इव नेमिरिव वाह्यवलयं इव । स यथा व्याप्य तस्मिन् तत्पदेयमग्निर्वरुणादीनां व्याप्य तिष्ठसि [?] ॥ [partly unread]

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *agne* — O Agni; *tvayā hi* — by you alone (by your help); [*varuṇaḥ* — Varuṇa; *dhṛtavrataḥ* — carries out (his duties of rain and so on) correctly; *mitraḥ* — Mitra, the deity presiding over the day; *śāśadre* — destroys the darkness [?]; *āryamā* — Aryaman; *sudānavaḥ* — becomes an excellent giver]; or [*dhṛtavrataḥ* — he who fulfils his duties, *varuṇaḥ* — Varuṇa; *sudānavaḥ* — those of generous gifts, *mitraḥ* — Mitra (and) *āryamā* — Aryaman too; *tvayā hi* — by you alone; *śāśadre* — acquire keen intelligence]; *yat* — because; *sīm* — everywhere; *kratunā* — by all rites; *viśvathā* — as of universal nature; *arān nemiḥ na* — as the felly of a chariot-wheel surrounds the spokes (surrounding all rites); *vibhuḥ* — all-pervading; *paribhūḥ* — (by your radiance) surpassing all; *ajāyathāḥ* — you are born.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, Varuṇa, who correctly fulfils his duties, and Mitra and Aryaman, generous givers, acquire keen intelligence by your help alone. And for that very reason you, as the felly of a chariot-wheel surrounds the spokes, by all your rites too are born as of universal nature, all-pervading, and, by your radiance, encompassing everywhere.

**English Translation (as printed).** By you Agni, Varuna, observant of his duties, and Mitra and Aryaman, bountiful divinities, are animated, so that you have been born comprehending them all universally in all (their) functions, and encompassing (them all) as the circumference (encompasses) the spokes (of a wheel).

### Printed p. 200  (PDF 218)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of construction to the first half of this Ṛk. By the first construction, assigning individual qualities and duties to these deities, Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman, and saying that all of them perform their qualities and duties only by Agni's help, he makes it end in the praise of Agni. According to this construction Varuṇa is *dhṛtavrata*; Mitra is the destroyer of darkness; and Aryaman is a generous giver; this construction has the support of *śruti* sentences.

That Varuṇa is *dhṛtavrata* is well known in the Ṛk-saṃhitā. In many places he is praised as the leader and teacher in every kind of moral conduct.

> त्वमग्ने राजा वरुणो धृतव्रतस्त्वं मित्रो भवसि दस्म ईड्यः । त्वमर्यमा सत्पतिर्यस्य सम्भुजं त्वमंशो विदथे देव भाजयुः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-4.) As in this Ṛk it is said that Varuṇa of firm vows, Mitra the worthy of praise, and Aryaman the true lord are all Agni himself, so in this Ṛk also, in *tvayā hy agne varuṇo dhṛtavrataḥ* and so on, it is said that Agni is the root cause of all the activity of Varuṇa and the others. And further —

> सोऽग्नेरेको भागो यद्वारुणो यमेवामुष्मिन्नंभूर्भवति यो ऽपि वरुणः । सोऽग्निः सोऽग्नेर्द्वितीयो भागः ॥ [?]

(Śa. Brā. 3-4-4-[?]; read with doubt.) Such sentences declare identity between Agni and Varuṇa. And of Mitra and Varuṇa, who are Agni's own, whose functions in worldly affairs are fixed —

> क्रतोदक्षौ वा अस्य मित्रावरुणौ । वितेन्न्याध्यात्मं [?] स यदेव मनसा कामयत इदं मे स्यादिदं कुर्वीयेति स एव क्रतुरथ यदस्यै तत्समृद्ध्यते स दक्षो मित्र इव क्रतुर्वरुणो दक्षो ब्रह्मैव मित्रः क्षत्रं वरुणः ॥ [?]

(Śa. Brā. 4-1-4-[?]; read with doubt.) In such sentences the relation of each to the other is told: Mitra is the maker of the resolve, and Varuṇa the agent that carries out that resolve.

***mitraḥ śāśadre*** — *aharabhimānī devaḥ tamaḥ śātayati*: Mitra is the deity presiding over the day, who destroys all the darkness of night: his work and nature are stated. In the same way it is said in many places that Varuṇa is the deity presiding over the night.

### Printed p. 201  (PDF 219)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 8 [?].)*

> प्राणापानौ [?] वा एतौ यदुपांश्वन्तर्यामौ मित्रो ऽहरजनयद्वरुणो रात्रिं ततो वा इदं व्यैच्छद्यन्मैत्रावरुणो गृह्यते व्युष्ट्यै ॥ [?]

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-[?]-[?]; read with doubt.) What is said in these Saṃhitā sentences and in the Brāhmaṇas will be set out later, in the explanation of Sūktas 151–153 of this same adhyāya.

By the second construction, *mitraḥ śāśadre* is "Mitra destroys the enemies with Agni's help", and one has to address Agni thus: "By you alone are Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman invigorated, all these deities."

> उषसो हि वसो अग्रमेषि त्वं यमयोरभवो विभावा । ऋताय सप्त दधिषे पदानि जनयन्मित्रं तन्वे स्वायै ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks, because Agni is the cause of the birth of Mitra and the others, it is said that he is their invigorator; so the second construction too is possible.

In the second half of the Ṛk the epithets *vibhuḥ* and *paribhūḥ* indicate Agni's all-pervasiveness and all-surpassing. And since the sacrificial acts and Agni are compared to the nave and the felly of a chariot, the identity of the sacrificial rites and Agni, and their dear, inseparable relation, are understood.

The sacrifice mirrors the principle of the universe. The altar is the navel of the sacrifice, and so is the navel of the universe. Agni, established in this navel, is the centre of all the principles of the world and the all-pervader. The sun, moon and all the planets rest their movements on this centre.

> द्यौर्ह वै [?] … एष्योऽग्निः [?] । तस्यापः एव परिश्रयो यथा ह वा इदं कोशे समुब्जिते [?] एवमिमे लोका अप्स्वन्तः … इमान् लोकान् … आपः परिश्रिताः … देवा यजुष्मत्यः इष्टका यदेनैस्मिल्लोके … पूर्णेष्टकानि पुरीष्या … । यद्वा अस्मिल्लोकं … तद्वा वितत्सर्वमादित्यमेवाभिसंपद्यते तस्मात्सर्वोऽग्निः ॥ [?]

(Śa. Brā. 10-[?]-[?]-[?]; garbled at this resolution.)

> सर्वाणि ह श्वेव भूतानि । सर्वे देवा एषो ऽग्नौ चित आपो वै सर्वे देवास्ता हैता आप एवाग्नेः परिश्रिताः [?] … त्रीणि च शतानि भवन्ति … योऽसावादित्यो हिरण्मयः पुरुषः ॥ [?]

(Śa. Brā. 10-[?]-[?]-[?].)

### Printed p. 202  (PDF 220)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

*(Continued from p. 201.)* In these sentences Agni, set upon the altar, is described as pervading all the worlds, and as the centre on which all the rites and all the cosmic workings are based; the sense is that all the activity of the *adhvaryu* proceeds on this basis. Hence Agni's Viśvātmaka nature is shown in the present Ṛk. Agni himself is *hotṛ*, Agni himself is *adhvaryu*, Agni himself is the sacrifice; and since all the parts of the sacrifice and all the sacrificial acts find their support and stability in Agni, this simile of the felly of the chariot-wheel is apt.

> दिवि क्षयं [?] बृहतो जातवेदो वैश्वानर प्र रिरिचे महित्वम् । राजा कृष्टीनामसि मानुषीणां युधा देवेभ्यो वरिवश्चकर्थ ॥

> *divi kṣayaṃ [?] bṛhato jātavedo vaiśvānara pra ririce mahitvam | rājā kṛṣṭīnāmasi mānuṣīṇāṃ yudhā devebhyo varivaścakartha ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-59-5 [?].)

> वैश्वानर तव धामान्या चके येभिः स्वर्विदभवो विचक्षण । जात आपृणो भुवनानि रोदसी अग्ने ता विश्वा परिभूरसि त्मना ॥

> *vaiśvānara tava dhāmānyā cake yebhiḥ svarvidabhavo vicakṣaṇa | jāta āpṛṇo bhuvanāni rodasī agne tā viśvā paribhūrasi tmanā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-8-2.) In such Ṛks Agni's all-pervasiveness (*vibhutva*) and all-surpassing (*paribhāvukatva*) are described, and the point, that Agni surpasses all the deities by his own radiance, is stated in the present Ṛk also.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 9; grammar pages 202–203, noted briefly).** *agne* (vocative; *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19): *nighāta*), *dhṛtavrataḥ* (*dhṛtaṃ vrataṃ yena saḥ*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1): the first member's accent), *śāśadre* (root *śadḷ śātane*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-6): *liṭ* in the present sense; third person singular; *liṭas tajhayor eśirec* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-81): *eś*; reduplication; *tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-7): lengthening of the reduplicate; *bahulaṃ chandasi*: *ruṭ* augment to the suffix; because of the *ṭit*, *ādyudātta*-position [?]; because of the connected *hi*, *hica* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-34) barring *nighāta*; accent of the suffix, the final syllable *udātta*), *sudānavaḥ* (*śobhanaṃ dānaṃ yasya saḥ sudānuḥ*; root *dāñ dāne*; *dābhyāṃ nuḥ* (Uṇ. Sū. 3-[?]): suffix *nu*; final-syllable accent; compound: *nañsubhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172): the final accent; *vyatyayo bahulam*: the plural suffix for the singular).

#### Ṛk 10

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वमग्ने शशमानाय सुन्वते रत्नं यविष्ठ देवतातिमिन्वसि ।
> तं त्वा नु नव्यं सहसो युवन्वयं भगं न कारे महिरत्न धीमहि ॥ १० ॥

> *tvamagne śaśamānāya sunvate ratnaṃ yaviṣṭha devatātiminvasi |*
> *taṃ tvā nu navyaṃ sahaso yuvanvayaṃ bhagaṃ na kāre mahiratna dhīmahi ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वम् । अग्ने । शशमानाय । सुन्वते । रत्नम् । यविष्ठ । देवऽतातिम् । इन्वसि ।
> तम् । त्वा । नु । नव्यम् । सहसः । युवन् । वयम् । भगम् । न । कारे । महिऽरत्न । धीमहि ॥ १० ॥

> *tvam | agne | śaśamānāya | sunvate | ratnam | yaviṣṭha | deva 'tātim | invasi |*
> *tam | tvā | nu | navyam | sahasaḥ | yuvan | vayam | bhagam | na | kāre | mahi 'ratna | dhīmahi ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *O youngest Agni, for the sacrificer who praises you and presses Soma, you convey the precious oblation to the gods; O son of strength, we place you, ever new and rich in treasure, in our hymn, as men praise a king.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *yaviṣṭha* — extremely youthful; *agne* — O Agni; *tvam* — you; *śaśamānāya* — (to you) who praises; *sunvate* — (for you) who presses the Soma-juice, the sacrificer; *ratnam* — delightful oblation; *devatātim* — pleasing to the gods; *inyasi* — you cause to reach; *sahasaḥ yuvan* — [O you] born of strength, or ever young by strength; *mahiratna* — O Agni, possessed of vast wealth (to be bestowed on us); *navyam* — new-born, or worthy of praise; *tam* — that oblation, well known; *tvā* — you; *vayam* — we, the sacrificers; *kāre* — in the hymn in the form of praise; *bhagam na* — as one would a Bhaga, or a great king; *nu* — quickly; *dhīmahi* — we place [you] in praiseworthy fashion (we make you the subject of a hymn).

**Bhāvārtha.** O most youthful Agni, for the sacrificer who praises you and presses Soma for you, you carry the delightful oblation, so that it may be pleasing to the gods. O Agni, born of strength, ever youthful, possessing abundant wealth, new-born and worthy of the sacrificer's oblation, we sacrificers earnestly make you the subject of praise in the hymn, as men eulogize a mighty prince.

**English Translation (as printed).** Most youthfull Agni, for the good of him who praises you and offers you libations, you make the precious (offering) acceptable to the gods: new-born of strength, we glorify you who is to be lauded: to whom rich offerings (are to be presented:) we glorify you in (our) hymn as (men eulogize) a powerful prince.

### Printed p. 205  (PDF 223)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 9 [?].)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***śaśamānāya*** — citing the Nirukta sentence *śaśamānaḥ śaṃsamānaḥ* (Ni. 3-8), Sāyaṇa explains it as *stuvate*, "to the sacrificer who praises". The Nirukta authors, citing —

> यो वां यज्ञैः शशमानो ह दाशति कविर्होता यजति मन्मसाधनः । उपाह तं गच्छथो वीथो अध्वरमच्छा गिरः सुमतिं गन्तमस्मयू ॥

> *yo vāṃ yajñaiḥ śaśamāno ha dāśati kavirhotā yajati manmasādhanaḥ | upāha taṃ gacchatho vītho adhvaramacchā giraḥ sumatiṃ gantamasmayū ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) — explain the sense of the word *śaśamānaḥ* (Ni. 3-8).

In the first half of the Ṛk, the favour that Agni does to the sacrificer is described: he takes the delightful oblation and carries it to the gods and offers it.

***inyasi*** — *invatiḥ vyāptikarmā* (Ni. 2-18): *asmadīyaṃ havir devān prāpayasi*: "you make our oblation reach the gods"; the word suggests the sense of distributing it among all the gods and gratifying them all.

***navyam*** — *nava, nūtana* and the like are read among the names of the new (Ni. 3-[?]): *kṣipropapannaṃ nūtanam*: "just now come into being"; therefore "worthy of praise".

***kāre*** — *stotralakṣaṇe śabde*: "in the word that is a hymn". *dhīmahi* is "we place": we make you the subject of a splendid hymn. Since the word *kāra* shows *kriyate iti kāraḥ*, "what is done", it may be the act of sacrifice, the act of battle, or the act of praise; the meaning of this word must be understood according to each context. For example —

> सहावा पृत्सु तरणिर्नार्वा व्यानशे रोदसी मेहनावान् । भगो न कारे हव्यो मतीनां पितेव चारुः सुहवो वयोधाः ॥

> *sahāvā pṛtsu taraṇirnārvā vyānaśe rodasī mehanāvān | bhago na kāre havyo matīnāṃ piteva cāruḥ suhavo vayodhāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?] [?].) in this Ṛk the word *kāra* is given the sense "sacrifice" (*kriyate iti kāraḥ yajñādiḥ; tasmin yajñe*), and

> जयेम कारे पुरुहूत कारिणोऽभि तिष्ठेम दूढ्यः । नृभिर्वृत्रं हन्याम शूशुयाम चावेरिन्द्र प्र णो धियः ॥

> *jayema kāre puruhūta kāriṇo 'bhi tiṣṭhema dūḍhyaḥ | nṛbhirvṛtraṃ hanyāma śūśuyāma cāverindra pra ṇo dhiyaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-21-12 [?].) (continues on p. 206)

### Printed p. 206  (PDF 224)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

in this Ṛk *kāre* is *kīryante āyudhāny atra iti kāraḥ yuddhaṃ tasmin jayema*: "the battle, in which weapons are sharply discharged, is called *kāra*; in this battle may we conquer." The word *kāra* suggests the prayer for victory. In the present Ṛk it means the act of praise.

***bhagaṃ na*** — here the word *bhaga* is said to mean either the god Bhaga, one of the Ādityas, or a great king. *Bhago bhajateḥ* (Ni. 1-2): since it expresses the sense of worship, either of these two senses may be given. As the god Bhaga, or the worshipful king, becomes the subject of praise, so we make Agni too the subject of praise: so it is compared.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 10; grammar pages 206–207, noted briefly).** *śaśamānāya* (*śaṃsamānaḥ* (Niru. 3-8) says Yāska; root *śasu stutau*; *śānac* in the present sense; *cit*: last-syllable accent; dative singular), *sunvate* (root *ṣuñ abhiṣave*; *dhātor ādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64): initial *ṣ* → *s*; *laṭ*-sense *śatṛ*; *svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-73): *śnu*; *sārvadhātukamapit*: no *guṇa*; *yaṇ*; dative singular, *num*-less since the suffix is without *num*; *śatuḥ anumo nadyajādī* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-173): the case-ending *udātta*), *ratnam* (*ramayatīti ratnam*; *rameś ca* (Uṇ. Sū. 3-[?]): suffix *na*; *m* of the root → *t*; *nit*, first-syllable accent), *yaviṣṭha* (*atiśayena yuvā yaviṣṭhaḥ*; *yuvan*; *ātiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-55): suffix *iṣṭhan*; *sthūladūra*… (Pā. Sū. 6-4-156): loss of *van*; *guṇa* of *u*; *av*; vocative: *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19): *nighāta*), *devatātim* (*sarvadevāt tātil* (Pā. Sū. 4-4-142): suffix *tātil*; *lit*, so *litaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193): the accent of the syllable before the suffix *udātta*), *inyasi* (root *invi vyāptau*; *invati, nakṣati* are read as verbs of pervading (Niru. 2-[?]); *iditaḥ num*: *num*; *laṭ* second person singular; as it follows an *ati-jñanta*, *nighāta*).

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** (*agne* — O Agni; *tvam* — you;) *asme* — to us; *rayiṃ na* — as you give wealth; *svartham* — one greatly desired; *damūnasam* — [a gentle one]; *bhagam* — a beloved one; *dakṣam* — a capable one; *dharṇasim* — one fit to hold learning: (such) a son; *papracāsi* — you graciously give; *yaḥ* — who, that Agni; *raśmīn iva* — as he spreads his rays; *ubhe janmanī* — the two worlds of his birth; *yamati* — he controls and extends (so too); *sukratuḥ* — Agni of excellent works; *ṛte* — in our sacrifice; *devānām* — directed to the gods; *śaṃsaṃ ca* — the hymn also; *ā (yamati)* — controls and extends.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, as you give us wealth, you graciously give us a son who is greatly desired, gentle, beloved, capable, and fit to hold learning. That Agni, as he extends his rays, also extends his two birthplaces, the two worlds (heaven and earth). In the same way Agni of excellent deeds extends, in our sacrifice, the hymns directed to the gods, regularly.

**English Translation (as printed).** In like manner as you confer upon us riches, (so you bestow upon us) a well-disposed, obedient, and energetic (son); the receptacle (of

### Printed p. 209  (PDF 227)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 9 [?].)*

*(Printed English continued from p. 208:)* learning and other merits), one who is the performer of holy rites. Agni, who regulates as it were his own rays, (and the condition of) both (his) births, (or heaven and earth), he regulates at (our) sacrifice the adoration of the gods.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** In this Ṛk Agni, who gives wealth such as a son, is described as generous, as having the power to extend heaven and earth, and as one who regulates and extends the priests' hymns.

***svartham*** — *suṣṭhu araṇīyam* [?]: one who pursues an excellent aim, or one with the power of excellent conduct: it is an epithet of the son. [The explanation of the word *svartha*, from the root *ṛ* "to go", and of the sense of *artha* as "purpose" is garbled at this resolution and is given only in outline] [?].

***damūnasam*** — *damanīyam upājyam* [?]: the sense is "one who is gentle". The explanation of the Nirukta authors for the word *damūnāḥ* — *damanā vā dānamanā vā dāntamanā vā; api vā dama iti gṛhanāma tanmanāḥ syāt* (Ni. 4-4) — and the particular senses of this word have been given in the Special Topics of Ṛk 1-140-10 of this same part. In the present Ṛk it may be taken as "a son endowed with self-control and modesty".

***bhagam*** — *bhago bhajateḥ*: citing the sentence of the previous Ṛk, [it is said that] the word gives the sense "worshipful". Here it must be said "a beloved son".

***dharṇasim*** — the Nirukta authors read the word *dharṇasi* among the names of strength (Ni. 2-9). Ordinarily the word is used in the sense "supporting power". For example —

> आ धर्णसिर्बृहद्दिवो रराणो विश्वेभिर्गन्त्वोमभिर्हुवानः । ग्ना वसान ओषधीरमृध्रस्त्रिधातुशृङ्गो वृषभो वयोधाः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?] [?].) here as *sarvasya dhārakaḥ*, "supporter of all", an epithet of Agni; and

> आ वच्यस्व महि प्सरो वृषेन्दो द्युमत्तमः । आ योनिं धर्णसिः सदः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?].) here *dhartā tvam*, "you, the supporter", addressed to Soma; so in other places too it is used with the sense that indicates supporting power. In the present Ṛk (continues on p. 210)

### Printed p. 210  (PDF 228)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

Sāyaṇa explains *vidyādhidhāraṇakuśalaṃ putram*: a son with the power fit to grasp learning and to hold it.

***papracāsi*** — earlier it was said that the word *papracānāsaḥ* has the sense of an undivided relation. Here too: "make the excellent son related to us", that is, the prayer is "bestow a son worthy of great regard"; or the assurance is suggested that "you will certainly give to the sacrificers".

> अग्निं स्तोमं विश्रवस्तमं सुविब्रह्माणमुत्तमम् । आतोत्रं [?] श्रावयेत्त्विति [?] पुत्रं ददाति दाशुषे ॥ [?]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?] [?]; read with doubt.) On the basis of the sentences in such Ṛks — that to the sacrificer who offers oblations Agni gives a son who is best, noblest, and who brings good fame to his father and the rest — the same assurance is given in the present Ṛk.

***ubhe janmanī yamati*** — *janānādhārabhūtau ubhau lokau yamati niyacchati*: "he controls, restrains, the two worlds that are the support of beings"; the sense is that he controls and extends the sky and the earth, the causes of his own origin.

> अजो न क्षां दाधार पृथिवीं तस्तम्भ द्यां मन्त्रेभिः सत्यैः । प्रिया पदानि पश्वो नि पाहि विश्वायुरग्ने गुहा गुहं गाः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-67-3.) As described in such Ṛks, the purport is that he upheld heaven and earth, and, like extending his rays, so made these worlds shine and expand.

***śaṃsaṃ ca ā yamati*** — *stavaṃ ca āyacchati sarvadā dadāti*: "he gives continually the invocation-hymn to the gods". Because Agni is the *hotṛ* of the sacrifice —

> वाग्वै यज्ञस्य होता तद्येयं वाक्सोऽयमग्निः स होता सा मुक्तिः । साशमुक्तिः [?] ॥

(Bṛ. U. 1-[?]-[?] [?]; read with doubt.) such sentences state the identity of the speech of praise and the *hotṛ*; and since Agni is both *hotṛ* and the presiding deity of speech, the purport is that he makes the praise extend.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 11; grammar pages 210–211, noted briefly).** *asme* (the word *asmad*; when the case-ending follows, *supāṃ sulug…* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) gives *śe* for it; loss of the *a* by *pararūpa* [?]). (continues on p. 211)

#### Ṛk 12

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उत नः सुद्योत्मा जीराश्वो होता मन्द्रः शृणवच्चन्द्ररथः ।

### Printed p. 212  (PDF 230)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

> स नो नेषन्नेषतमैरमूरोऽग्निर्वामं सुवितं वस्यो अच्छ ॥ १२ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उत । नः । सुऽद्योत्मा । जीरऽअश्वः । होता । मन्द्रः । शृणवत् । चन्द्रऽरथः ।
> सः । नः । नेषत् । नेषऽतमैः । अमूरः । अग्निः । वामम् । सुवितम् । वस्यः । अच्छ ॥ १२ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *May Agni, bright, swift-horsed, joyous, golden-chariot'd hotṛ, hear us and lead us by his best leadings to the desirable, accessible heaven.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> उतशब्दोऽर्थः [?] । स च संभावनायां । सोऽग्निरस्मदीयमाह्वानमुतापि शृणवत् । अपि नामाशृणुयात् । यद्वा नोऽस्मान् श्रावयेत् । देवेषु मध्ये प्रख्यापयेत् । श्रुनोतेर्लेट्यडागमः । कीदृशोऽयं । सुद्योत्मा सुद्योतमानः । द्युत दीप्तौ । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते इति मनिन् । जीराश्वः शीघ्रगमनाश्वः । होता देवानामाह्वाता । मन्द्रो मदनशीलः । चन्द्ररथः सुवर्णमयरथः । किंचायमग्निरमूढबलो [?] वस्योवसनीयः [?] सः प्रसिद्धोऽग्निः नेषतमैर्नेतृतमैः कर्मभिः स्तोत्रैर्वा नोऽस्मान् नेषत् । अपि नयेत् । यज्ञस्य पारं प्रापयेत् । नयतेर्लेट्यडागमः । सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् । किमर्थं । वामं वननीयं सुवितं सुष्ठु प्राप्यं सर्वैः काङ्क्षणीयं स्वर्गमच्छाभिमुख्येन प्रापयितुं नेषत् ॥ [partly unread]

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *sudyotmā* — extremely bright; *jīrāśvaḥ* — having swift horses; *hotā* — the one who invites the (gods); *mandraḥ* — joyous by nature; *candrarathaḥ* — having a golden chariot, that Agni; *naḥ* — our (invocation); *uta śṛṇavat* — may he hear; *amūraḥ* — of unfailing strength; *vasyaḥ* — dispenser of dwelling [?]; *saḥ* — that well-known; *agniḥ* — Agni; *neṣatamaiḥ* — the best leaders, with the best leading acts of the sacrifice or with hymns; *naḥ* — us; *vāmam* — desirable; *suvitam* — easily to be entered, favourable; *accha* — facing; *neṣat* — may he take us.

**Bhāvārtha.** May Agni, extremely bright, with swift horses, the invoker of the gods, joyous, with a golden chariot, hear our call; may he, of unfailing strength, the well-known Agni, lead us, with the best of leading rites and hymns, to the desirable and easily entered heaven and take us forward.

### Printed p. 213  (PDF 231)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 9 [?].)*

**English Translation (as printed).** May he who is one with light, who has fleet horses, the invoker (of the gods), full of joy, and borne in a golden chariot, listen to us: may that irresistible, yet placable Agni, conduct us, by the most efficacious (means), to that desirable and accessible (heaven).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** In the first half of the Ṛk Agni is described by epithets such as *jīrāśvaḥ*.

***jīrāśvaḥ*** — the word *jīra* is read among the names of the swift (Ni. 2-15); *jīra* or *jīram* occurs separately, and in compounds such as *jīrāśva*, *jīrādvara*, *jīradānu*, in many places.

> दिवस्पृशं यज्ञमस्माकमश्विना जीराध्वरं कृणुतं सुम्नमिष्टये । प्राचीनरश्मिमाहुतं घृतेन तद्देवानामवो अद्या वृणीमहे ॥ [?]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk the Aśvins are prayed to make our rite *jīrādhvara*; here *jīrādhvara* means: "not obstructed by hindrances, free from injury, quickly completed — complete it for us".

> प्र क्षे तु [?] विश्वा भुवना ववक्षिरे मित्राय वा सदमा जीरदानवः । प्रपन्वशासो अनभ्रराधस उज्ज्यासो न वयोनेषु धूषहे [?] ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?]; read with doubt.) here *jīradānavaḥ* is an epithet of the Maruts: they who fulfil the sacrificer's wishes most swiftly. In the same way the compounds *jīrāśvaḥ*, *jīrāśvam* are also epithets of Agni and other deities; or they are sometimes epithets of their chariot. For example —

> आ वां रथं पुरुमायं मनोजुवं जीराश्वं यज्ञियं जीवसे हुवे । सहस्रकेतुं वनिनं शतद्वसुं श्रुष्टीवानं वरिवोधामभि प्रयः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].)

### Printed p. 214  (PDF 232)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

*(Continued from p. 213.)* In some Ṛks of this kind, the chariot of the Aśvins is described as drawn by swiftly running horses. In the present Ṛk the word *jīrāśva* describes Agni as one who has horses of a moving nature; and not only the epithet *jīrāśva*, but also epithets such as *ghṛtapṛṣṭha*, *vātajūta*, *svañca* tell the nature of his vehicles.

***sudyotmā*** — *sudyotamānaḥ*: an epithet of Agni, "shining supremely and excessively".

> अग्निः शुचिव्रततमः शुचिर्विप्रः शुचिः कविः । शुची रोचते आहुतः । उदग्ने शुचयस्तव शुक्रा भ्राजन्त ईरते । तव ज्योतींष्यर्चयः । आयुर्दा अग्नेऽस्यायुर्मे देहि वर्चोदा अग्नेऽसि वर्चो मे देहि [?] … सं श्वे [?] मग्ने सूर्यस्य वर्चसागथाः [?] स्वर्णं [?] स्तुतेन सं प्रियेण धाम्ना ॥ [?]

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-3-14 [?].) In such sentences the description of Agni tells of his brightness and power: the chief quality of Agni, who is self-luminous and the illuminator of the whole world, is stated.

***mandraḥ*** — the word *mandra* is read among the names of speech (Ni. 1-11): sweet and delighting speech. The word *mandrajihva* is used as an epithet both of Agni and of Bṛhaspati and describes the nature of each; but the sense differs a little. For example —

> आ नो बर्हिणं वृषभं मन्द्रजिह्वं बृहस्पतिं वर्धया नव्यमर्कैः । गाथान्यः सुरुचो यस्य देवा आशृण्वन्ति नवमानस्य मर्ताः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-190-1.) In this Ṛk, as an epithet of Bṛhaspati, it means "having delightful speech". When the same epithet is used of Agni, in 1-[?]-[?] and 3-[?]-[?], it means "having tongues in the form of flames that are lovely and delighting". In the present Ṛk, the word *mandra* means Agni, whose nature is lovely and joyous.

***candrarathaḥ*** — the word *candra* is read among the names of gold (Ni. 1-10). *Candraratha* means "one having a golden chariot", or, since *candraḥ kānteḥ kāntikarmaṇaḥ* (Ni. 11-3), as it gives the sense "radiant and beautiful", the word *candra* may be formed from the root *cand*; following the Nirukta authors' derivation, Sāyaṇa in the Ṛk 6-32-1 [?] (continues on p. 215)

### Printed p. 215  (PDF 233)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 9 [?].)*

has explained *candrarathāḥ*, an epithet of the dawns, as *kāntirathāḥ*. Likewise —

> चन्द्रमग्निं चन्द्ररथं हरिव्रतं वैश्वानरमप्सुषदं स्वर्विदम् । विगाहं तूर्णिं तविषीभिरावृतं भूर्णिं देवास इह सुश्रियं दधुः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-2-4 [?].) in this Ṛk Sāyaṇa explains *candraratha*, an epithet of Vaiśvānara Agni, as *āhlādake rathe yasya*, "one with a gladdening chariot". Here too the sense may be so taken.

***śṛṇavat*** — *śṛṇuyāt*, or *śrāvayet, deveṣu madhye prakhyāpayet*: may Agni himself attend to and hear our invocation, or may he make the gods hear it; that is, may our invocation be proclaimed before them.

***vasyaḥ*** — formed from the root *vas*, meaning radiance, *vasanīyaḥ* [?]: "one of a gentle form".

***amūraḥ*** — Sāyaṇa explains it as *amūḍhabalaḥ*, "of unfailing strength". Ordinarily *mūra* means "the foolish", and *amūra*, "not foolish", that is, "wise". The Nirukta authors —

> मूरा अमूर न वयं चिकित्वो महित्वमग्ने त्वमङ्ग विद्से [?] । शये वव्रिश्चरति जिह्वयादन्नेरिहाणः [?] युवतिं विश्पतिः सन् ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-4-4 [?].) citing this Ṛk, explain it as *mūḍhā vayaṃ tvam amūḍhas tvam asi*, "we are foolish, you are wise". Likewise here too one may give the sense "wise", as an epithet of Agni.

***neṣatamaiḥ*** — *asmadarthaṃ netṛbhiḥ karmabhiḥ stotrair vā*: "by the best leading acts or hymns", that is, by guiding and excellent acts or hymns.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 12; grammar pages 215–216, noted briefly).** *sudyotmā* (root *dyuta dīptau*; *anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-75) gives *manin*; the guṇa of the light penultimate by *pugantalaghūpadhasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86); *kratvādayaś ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-118): *ādyudātta* for the second member). (continues on p. 216)

#### Ṛk 13

### Printed p. 217  (PDF 235)
