**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अस्तावि अग्निः शिमीवद्भिरर्कैः साम्राज्याय प्रतरं दधानः ।
> अमी च ये मघवानो वयं च मिहं न सूरो अति निः तत्न्युः ॥ १३ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अस्ताविः । अग्निः । शिमीवत्ऽभिः । अर्कैः । साम्ऽराज्याय । प्रऽतरम् । दधानः ।
> अमी इति । च । ये । मघवानः । वयम् । च । मिहम् । न । सूरः । अति । निः । तत्न्युः ॥ १३ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *Agni has been praised by us with hymns and sacrificial acts, holding the highest sovereignty; may these rich patrons and we thunder his praise as the sun makes a rain-cloud thunder.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> अयमग्निः शिमीवद्भिर्हविष्प्रदानादिकर्मवद्भिरर्कैरर्चनसाधनैर्मन्त्रैश्च अस्तावि स्तुतोऽस्माभिर्यजमानैः । शिमी शमीति कर्मनाम शमी शक्तिरिति तन्नामसु पाठात् । कीदृशोऽयं । साम्राज्याय साम्राज्यं सम्यक् राजमानत्वं तस्मै प्रतरं प्रकृष्टतरमैश्वर्यं दधानः धारयन् । अमू च [?] छान्दस इत्यसौ उपप्रत्ययः [?] । किंचेमग्निमिमा च पुरोवर्तमाना ऋत्विजः पुत्रादयो वा । ये वयं च पूर्वं स्तोतृत्वेन प्रसिद्धा वयमप्यस्मत्कर्तृकं निष्टतन्युः [?] । शब्दयन्तु । निष्पूर्वः स्तनतिः शब्दकर्मा । इतः परमपुष्यप्रस्ताव [?] … वयं चागम्य स्तुमः इत्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । मिहं न सूरः । मिहं मेघं मेहनशीलं मेढं सूरः सूर्यः वृष्ट्यर्थं शब्दयति तद्वत् । लिङ् छान्दसो विकरणस्य श्लुः [?] । अभिनिः स्तनः शब्दसंज्ञायां । पा. ८-४-[?] इति षत्वम् ॥ [partly unread]

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *sāmrājyāya* — for the sake of supreme sovereignty; *prataram* — the most excellent dignity (*ārhatā*); *dadhānaḥ* — possessing; *agniḥ* — Agni; *śimīvadbhiḥ* — with acts such as offering oblations; *arkaiḥ* — with mantras worthy of worship; *astāvi* — has been praised (this Agni); *amī ca* — those who stand before him, the priests or our sons and the rest; *ye maghavānaḥ* — (by his favour) rich; *vayaṃ ca* — we also; *sūraḥ* — the sun; *mihaṃ na* — as (for rain) he makes the cloud thunder; *ati* — with deep (grave) sound; *niṣṭatanyuḥ* — let us praise (him).

### Printed p. 218  (PDF 236)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 141".)*

**Bhāvārtha.** We praise this Agni, who has attained the supreme sovereignty, with offerings of oblations and other acts and with mantras fit for worship. Moreover, these priests and sons standing before him, and we, enriched by his favour, praise him with deep and grave sound, as the sun makes the cloud thunder for rain.

**English Translation (as printed).** Agni, possessing eminent (fitness) for supreme sovereignty, has been glorified by us with holy rites, and with hymns: Let all who are present, as well as we ourselves, enriched (by his favour), shout aloud (the praise of Agni), as (loudly as) the sun (causes) the rain-cloud to thunder.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***sāmrājyāya prataram*** — *sāmrājyāya prakṛṣṭataram aiśvaryaṃ dadhānaḥ*: the word that should be in the genitive, *sāmrājyasya*, stands in the dative in this place; Agni is praised as one who has attained a position of supreme sovereignty.

> प्र साम्राजो असुरस्य प्रशस्तिं पुंसः कृष्टीनामनुमाद्यस्य । इन्द्रस्येव प्र तवसस्कृतानि वन्दे दारुं वन्दमानो विवक्मि ॥ [?]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?] [?].) And in such Ṛks too,

> अग्निर्ह दैवीनां विशां पुर एत्यग्निर्हि देवतानां मुखम् । [?]

(Śa. Brā. 3-[?]-[?]-10 [?].) as described in such Brāhmaṇa sentences too, the power of Agni, the sovereign over even the gods, is expressed by the phrase *sāmrājyāya prataram*.

***śimīvadbhiḥ*** — *śimīti karmanāma; śimī śaktiḥ* (Ni. 2-1): since it is so read among those names. *Haviṣpradānādi karmavadbhiḥ*: Sāyaṇa explains it as "with acts such as the giving of oblations", on the authority of the Nirukta sentence.

***arkaiḥ*** — *arcanasādhanair mantraiḥ*: "with mantras, the means of worship": thus it is explained here.

### Printed p. 219  (PDF 237)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 9 [?].)*

> अर्को देवो भवति यदेनमर्चन्ति । अर्को मन्त्रो भवति यदेनेनार्चन्ति । अर्कमन्नं भवत्यर्चति भूतानि । अर्को वृक्षो भवति संवृत्तः कटुकिम्ना ॥

(Ni. 5-4.) The Nirukta authors give different senses: as it is the object of worship, *arka* is a god; as a means of worship, *arka* is a mantra; as it gives vitality to beings, *arka* is food; as it is pungent, *arka* is a tree (the *arka* plant); and then —

> गायन्ति त्वा गायत्रिणोऽर्चन्त्यर्कमर्किणः । ब्रह्माणस्त्वा शतक्रत उद्वंशमिव येमिरे ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-10-1.) citing this Ṛk, they explain the nature of *arka*. The *arka* is of surpassing power, and its greatness is praised in many places. In the Aitareya Āraṇyaka —

> अथातः शिरः । तद्गायत्रीषु भवत्यग्रं वै छन्दसां गायत्र्यग्रमङ्गानां शिरः । तेनार्कवतीषु भवत्यर्को वा अर्कः [?] । ता नव भवन्ति नव कपालं शिरः ॥ [?]

(Ai. Ār. 1-4-1 [?].) And by *indram id gāthino bṛhad indram arkebhir arkiṇaḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-7-1), it is said that the nine Ṛks beginning with it are *arka* mantras, that they are the mantras that are the head; and that since these mantras, as the principal principle in the form of the Gāyatrī, are in the form of Gāyatrī, the *arka* mantras hold the principal place among all mantras [?].

***mihaṃ na*** — *mehanaśīlaṃ meghaṃ yathā*: "like the cloud, which sheds rain": the sacrificer's deep and sonorous praise is compared to the thunder of the cloud.

Sū. 3-1-66): *ciṇ* for *cli*; *acaḥ ñniti* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-115): *vṛddhi*; *ciṇo luk* (Pā. ## Sūkta 142

### Printed p. 221 (continued; PDF 239)

*(The Kannada heading reads "The 142nd Sūkta".)*

*(Anukramaṇī, Sanskrit; not rendered in English. Gist: the sūkta of thirteen Ṛks beginning "Samiddho" is an Āprī-sūkta; the first Ṛk is addressed to Samiddha Agni; the second and following to Tanūnapāt, Narāśaṃsa, Iḍā, Barhis, Devīdvāra, Uṣāsānaktā, the two divine Hotṛs, the three goddesses Sarasvatī–Iḍā–Bhāratī, Tvaṣṭṛ, Vanaspati, Svāhākṛti; the last to Indra; Śākapūṇi's and Kātthakya's views on the deities are given. Small type; only partly read.)*

> समिद्ध इति त्रयोदशर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तमाप्रीसूक्तम् [?] । प्रथमायाः समिद्धोऽग्निर्देवता [?] । द्वितीयादीनां तनूनपान्नराशंस इळो बर्हिर्देवीद्वार उषासानक्ता दैव्या होतारौ प्रचेतसौ तिस्रो देव्यः सरस्वतीळाभारत्यः त्वष्टा वनस्पतिः स्वाहाकृतय इति । अन्त्याया इन्द्रः [?] । … [remainder of the small type not read]

> *samiddha iti trayodaśarcaṃ tṛtīyaṃ sūktamāprīsūktam [?] | prathamāyāḥ samiddho 'gnirdevatā [?] | dvitīyādīnāṃ tanūnapānnarāśaṃsa iḷo barhirdevīdvāra uṣāsānaktā daivyā hotārau pracetasau tisro devyaḥ sarasvatīḷābhāratyaḥ tvaṣṭā vanaspatiḥ svāhākṛtaya iti | antyāyā indraḥ [?] | … [remainder of the small type not read]*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta *Samiddho agne* is the third sūkta of the twenty-first anuvāka. It has thirteen Ṛks. The deity of the first Ṛk is Samiddha Agni (the kindled fire) [?]. From the second to the twelfth the deities are, in order, Tanūnapāt, Narāśaṃsa, Iḍā, Barhis, Devīdvāraḥ, Uṣāsānaktā, the two divine Hotṛs Pracetasau, the three goddesses Sarasvatī, Iḍā, Bhāratī, Tvaṣṭṛ, Vanaspati, Svāhākṛtis. The deity of the last Ṛk is Indra. "*Tisro devyaḥ*" means the three goddesses Sarasvatī, Iḍā and Bhāratī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: "*samiddhe āprī anuṣṭubhaṃ antyendrī*" [?]. Since *idhma*, *tanūnapāt* and the like are names of the limbs of the sacrifice, all these denote the sacrifice itself; so the opinion of Kātthakya is that the deity of this sūkta is the sacrifice (*yajña*) itself. Since the words *samidh* and the rest apply to Agni, Śākapūṇi's opinion is that Agni alone is the deity of this sūkta [?]. In the Nirukta — "*kiṃ devatāḥ prayājānuyājāḥ*", "what deities have the *prayājas* and *anuyājas*?" — the oblations called *prayāja* and *anuyāja* are described as the deities of this sūkta, and Brāhmaṇa sentences are cited in support. In the Ṛks … (continues on p. 222)

### Printed p. 222  (PDF 240)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

*(Anuvāda continued.)* … the Ṛks give grounds (*pakṣāntara*) in agreement with the sense told above, that all these Ṛks relate to Agni. In the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra (Ā. 3-[?]) the use of this Āprī-sūkta is stated in the section called *ekādaśa prayāja*, in the case of the *paśuhoma* offering, for those born in the line of the sage Aṅgiras — *samiddho 'gna ity ābrūyāt sarveṣāṃ yathāyajuṣaṃ* — and by the word *yathā-yajuṣam* in it, the Āprī-sūktas are of three kinds: the four Āprī-sūktas seen by the sages Vasiṣṭha, Atri, Vādhryaśva and Gṛtsamada are concerned with Narāśaṃsa; the two seen by Medhātithi and by Dīrghatamas are concerned with both Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt; the remaining Āprī-sūktas are concerned with Tanūnapāt. Hence this sūkta, seen by Dīrghatamas, belongs to the group concerned with both Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt.

**॥ ओम् ॥**

**Sūkta 142** — **Āprī-sūktam**. Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 21, Sūkta 142; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 10, 11 [?]. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 13. Ṛṣi: Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Devatā: 1. Samit; 2. Tanūnapāt; 3. Narāśaṃsa; 4. Iḍā; 5. Barhis; 6. Devīdvāraḥ; 7. Uṣāsānaktā; 8. Daivyā Hotārau Pracetasau; 9. Tisro devyaḥ Sarasvatī–Iḍā–Bhāratyaḥ; 10. Tvaṣṭā; 11. Vanaspati; 12. Svāhākṛtayaḥ; 13. Indra. Chandas: Anuṣṭubh.

**The Āprī-sūktas.** We have given an account of the Āprī-sūktas in the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, part 3, pages 73–74 and 528 [?]. In the Ṛgveda there are ten Āprī-sūktas in all. In them are mantras whose deities are: *idhma* (or *samiddha*), *tanūnapāt*, *narāśaṃsa*, *iḍā*, *barhis*, *devīdvāraḥ*, *uṣāsānaktā*, *daivyā hotārau pracetasau*, *tisro devyaḥ sarasvatīḍābhāratyaḥ*, *tvaṣṭā*, *vanaspati*, *svāhākṛtayaḥ*. But, as regards the deities Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt, in some sūktas only a single deity called Narāśaṃsa is praised, (continues on p. 223)

### Printed p. 223  (PDF 241)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 10 [?].)*

in some others only the single deity Tanūnapāt, and in some both Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt. In accordance with this arrangement these Āprī-sūktas have been divided into three groups. Those seen by the sages Vasiṣṭha, Atri, Vādhryaśva and Gṛtsamada are:

1) *Juṣasvana samidham agne* — Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-[?] (Maitrāvaruṇi Vasiṣṭha);
2) *Susamiddhāya śociṣe* — Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-5 [?] (Vasuśruta Ātreya);
3) *Imāṃ me agne samidham* — Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?] (Sumitra Vādhryaśva);
4) *Samiddho agnir nihite* — Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3 [?] (Gṛtsamada).

These four sūktas belong to one group. In each of them there is one Ṛk whose deity is Narāśaṃsa. Hence these four sūktas are named *narāśaṃsavanti sūktāni*, "Āprī-sūktas that praise only the deity Narāśaṃsa".

1) *Susamiddho na ā vaha* — Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13 (Medhātithi Kāṇva); 2) *Samiddho agna ā vaha* — Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-142 (Dīrghatamas Aucathya): these two Āprī-sūktas belong to the second group. In each of these there is one Ṛk for each of the two deities, Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt. Hence these Āprī-sūktas are well known as those having both deities, Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt. Since both deities are in these sūktas (except Indra in the present sūkta) [?], the twelve *prayāja* offerings come to be twelve offerings [?].

(1) *Samiddho adya rājasi* — Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188 (Agastya Maitrāvaruṇi); (2) *Samit-samit sumanāḥ* — Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4 [?] (Gādhina Viśvāmitra); (3) *Samiddho viśvatas patiḥ* — Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-5 (Kāśyapa Asita or Devala); (4) *Samiddho adya manuṣaḥ* — Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110 (Jāmadagnya Rāma Bhārgava): these sūktas belong to the third group. In these there are Ṛks whose deity is Tanūnapāt alone (there are no Ṛks with the deity Narāśaṃsa). Hence these are named *tanūnapātvanti sūktāni*, Āprī-sūktas with mantras (Ṛks) whose deity is Tanūnapāt.

These Āprī-sūktas are recited in the *paśuhoma* for performing the eleven *prayāja* oblations. There is a sentence of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā: *ekādaśa prayājān anvāha; daśa vai paśoḥ prāṇā ātmaikādaśaḥ* (Tai. Saṃ. 6-3-[?]-[?]), "he recites eleven *prayājas*; the ten vital airs of the animal, and the self is the eleventh". When these Āprī-sūktas are recited and the *paśuhoma* done, there is a special rule: (continues on p. 224)

### Printed p. 224  (PDF 242)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

the sacrificers, who are of various *gotra*-sages, must recite at the sacrifice the very Āprī-sūktas seen by their own sage (Ā. 3-3 [?]). The present Āprī-sūkta is to be recited by those born in the line of the sage Aṅgiras.

To know the nature of the Āprī-sūktas and the place they hold in the performance of rites, we have two kinds of authority: first, the *śruti*-sentences of the Brāhmaṇas and the like; second, the sentences of derivation (*nirvacana*) in the Nirukta and the like. Of these two kinds, the Nirukta-type sentences are more reasoned and are also accompanied by a more scientific explanation.

If one considers the derivation of the word *āprī* given in the Brāhmaṇas, such as the Aitareya, it may be said that those texts have understood and explained this word from the standpoint of the performance of rites such as sacrifice. For example —

> तद्यदाप्रीणाति तस्मादाप्रियो नाम [?] ।

> *tadyadāprīṇāti tasmādāpriyo nāma [?] |*

(Kauṣ. Brā. 10-3 [?].) so the name arises from its being a means of gratifying; and in the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa, and

> आप्रीभिराप्नुवन् [?] । तदाप्रीणामाप्रित्वम् ।

> *āprībhirāpnuvan [?] | tadāprīṇāmāpritvam |*

(Tai. Brā. 3-2-8-6 [?].) says the same idea, as does the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, and —

> यदेवैतान्याप्रिय आज्यानि भवन्ति । आत्मानमेवैतैराप्रीणाति ।

> *yadevaitānyāpriya ājyāni bhavanti | ātmānamevaitairāprīṇāti |*

(Tā. Brā. 3-9-8-3 [?].) so the Tāṇḍya Brāhmaṇa too tells the nature of the word *āprī*.

In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, in indicating the duties the *hotṛ* must perform at the time of the Agniṣomīya sacrifice, the explanation of the Āprīs is given. After the description of the animal, to be offered to Agni and Soma (2-3), eleven *prayāja* mantras are stated (2-4). In that context —

> आप्रीभिराप्रीणाति । तेजो वै ब्रह्मवर्चसमाप्रियस्तेजस्यैनं ब्रह्मवर्चसेन समर्धयति ॥

> *āprībhirāprīṇāti | tejo vai brahmavarcasamāpriyastejasyainaṃ brahmavarcasena samardhayati ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 2-4.) the Āprī Ṛks are full of radiance and with *brahmavarcas*; by such Ṛks the (hotṛ) becomes a cause of gratification: thus it shows that they are a means for one's own gratification. Afterwards (continues on p. 225)

### Printed p. 225  (PDF 243)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 10 [?].)*

it tells that the deities *samidh*, *tanūnapāt* and so on are identified with the vital airs and the like.

The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, saying of these sūktas that are given in different maṇḍalas, and of their fruit, first of all gives the matter of the sages who recited them —

> ताभिर्ऋषयः प्रीणायोद्यथा [?] ऋषयः प्रीणाति यजमानमेव तद्बन्धुतायाः उत्सृजति [?] ॥

> *tābhirṛṣayaḥ prīṇāyodyathā [?] ṛṣayaḥ prīṇāti yajamānameva tadbandhutāyāḥ utsṛjati [?] ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 2-4.) This tells the fruit of reciting these sūktas: that by reciting those sūktas of the sages, the sacrificer is freed from the bond of the sacrifice and protected. Different sages saw these sūktas on their own happy occasions; yet the nature of the sūktas, and the fruit of reciting them, appear as the same in all.

It is known from the explanation of the Nirukta author that from the time of the Brāhmaṇas and the like there has been a difference of opinion about these Āprī-sūktas and about their deities.

> अथातो ऽऽप्रियः । आप्रियः कस्मादाप्नोतेः प्रीणातेर्वा । आप्रीभिराप्रीणातीति च ब्राह्मणम् ॥

> *athāto ' 'priyaḥ | āpriyaḥ kasmādāpnoteḥ prīṇātervā | āprībhirāprīṇātīti ca brāhmaṇam ‖*

(Ni. 8-4.) By this the Nirukta author shows that the opinion of the Brāhmaṇas and the like regarding the Āprī-sūktas is different from his own. And he has cited from time to time the opinions of sages such as Kātthakya, Śākapūṇi and Mādhyamika. Though Kātthakya and the rest were *yājñikas*, it is shown in the particulars of each Ṛk that in many specific contexts they do not agree with what is said in the Brāhmaṇas and the like. Having set out all these opinions, Yāska at last states his own settled view. For instance, as to the Āprī deities, he first records that the Brāhmaṇas and the rest say so and so, and collects them all —

> इतीमा आप्रीदेवता अनुक्रान्ताः । अथ किं देवताः प्रयाजानुयाजाः । आग्नेया इत्येके । आग्नेया वै प्रयाजा आग्नेया अनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणम् । छन्दोदेवता इत्यात्मपरम् । छन्दांसि वै प्रयाजाश्छन्दांस्यनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणम् । ऋतुदेवता इत्यात्मपरम् । ऋतवो वै प्रयाजा ऋतवोऽनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणम् । पशुदेवता इत्यात्मपरम् । पशवो वै प्रयाजाः पशवोऽनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणम् । प्राणदेवता इत्यात्मपरम् । प्राणा वै प्रयाजाः [continues on p. 226]

> *itīmā āprīdevatā anukrāntāḥ | atha kiṃ devatāḥ prayājānuyājāḥ | āgneyā ityeke | āgneyā vai prayājā āgneyā anuyājā iti ca brāhmaṇam | chandodevatā ityātmaparam | chandāṃsi vai prayājāśchandāṃsyanuyājā iti ca brāhmaṇam | ṛtudevatā ityātmaparam | ṛtavo vai prayājā ṛtavo 'nuyājā iti ca brāhmaṇam | paśudevatā ityātmaparam | paśavo vai prayājāḥ paśavo 'nuyājā iti ca brāhmaṇam | prāṇadevatā ityātmaparam | prāṇā vai prayājāḥ [continues on p. 226]*

### Printed p. 226  (PDF 244)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

*(Continuation of the Nirukta passage on the Āprī deities. Top of page, the end of the Brāhmaṇa quotations; small type, doubtful words marked.)*

> प्राणा वा अनुयाजाः इति च ब्राह्मणम् । आत्मा देवता इत्येवरं [?] । आत्मा वै प्रयाजा आत्मा वा अनुयाजा इति च ब्राह्मणम् । आग्नेयो [?] इति तु स्थितिः । भक्तिमात्रमितरम् ।

> *prāṇā vā anuyājāḥ iti ca brāhmaṇam | ātmā devatā ityevaraṃ [?] | ātmā vai prayājā ātmā vā anuyājā iti ca brāhmaṇam | āgneyo [?] iti tu sthitiḥ | bhaktimātramitaram |*

(Ref. [?].) Saying thus the several opinions, Yāska first cites a Ṛk:

> तव प्रयाजा अनुयाजाश्च केवल ऊर्जस्वन्तो हविष्मन्तो [?] सन्तु भागाः ।
> तवाग्ने यज्ञोऽयमस्तु सर्वस्तुभ्यं नमन्तां प्रदिशश्चतस्रः ॥

> *tava prayājā anuyājāśca kevala ūrjasvanto haviṣmanto [?] santu bhāgāḥ |*
> *tavāgne yajño 'yamastu sarvastubhyaṃ namantāṃ pradiśaścatasraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) Having cited this Ṛk, Yāska says that, as stated in it, the *prayāja* and *anuyāja* mantras are addressed to Agni alone. After giving his own explanation he states the other opinions too. Of these, this same opinion is supported by the Brāhmaṇa sentence. But some say that the Chandas-deities are meant (Śa. Brā. 1-[?]-[?]-[?]); some, that the deities of the Ṛtus [?] are meant; others, that the *yogahaviṣ* (the oblation proper) is meant (Kau. Brā. [?]); others, that the Prāṇa-deities are meant (Ai. Brā. [?], Śa. Brā. [?]); still others, that Ātman is meant (Tai. Saṃ. [?]). Having gathered all that is said, he states his own straightforward opinion: that the sound view is that at the beginning the sūkta is addressed to Agni.

In Kātyāyana's Sarvānukramaṇī the difference between *āpra* and *āprī* is pointed out (this difference is given at the end of the sūkta facing the Āprī-sūkta [?]): the Ṛks addressed to the deity Narāśaṃsa are known as *āpra* mantras, and those addressed to the deity Tanūnapāt as *āprī* mantras. In the Bṛhaddevatā (the verses below):

> *dvitīyo dvādaśarce tu pṛkṣaicaṃ [?] yāstu devatāḥ |*

### Printed p. 228  (PDF 246)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

In these sentences (Yāska's), if the Praiṣa-sūkta is counted there are eleven Āprī-sūktas in all, otherwise ten. According to the very same Nirukta sentences, the deities **Narāśaṃsa** and **Tanūnapāt** and others are the deities of the Ṛks seen by the sages, and the order of the sūktas is given.

The Praiṣa-sūkta, being in an orderly sequence, gives a pictorial description (a "picture" in outline) that contains, in a fixed order, the beginnings of all the Āprī-sūktas. In the Āprī-sūktas the particular qualities of the deities are mentioned; the Praiṣa-sūkta gathers all of them and, taking the nature of the deities and the agent of each, divides and shows them. Before each deity the formula *hotā yakṣat* ("the Hotṛ shall sacrifice") is recited: one fixed mantra-part, and then the deities are invoked. After examining the qualities, the deity and the doer described in the Praiṣa-sūkta, one can learn the agreement or the difference of opinions as to the purpose of the Āprī mantras of this kind, their characteristics and their effects.

*(Table, "number — deity — epithets", as printed; small type read with doubt.)*

|---|---|---|
| 1 | अग्निः (समित्) (*agniḥ (samit)*) | समिधा, सुसमिद्धः, समिद्धः (*samidhā, susamiddhaḥ, samiddhaḥ*) |
| 2 | अग्निः (तनूनपात्) (*agniḥ (tanūnapāt)*) | अदितेः गर्भं भुवनस्य गोपाम् (*aditeḥ garbhaṃ bhuvanasya gopām*) |
| 3 | अग्निः (नराशंसः) (*agniḥ (narāśaṃsaḥ)*) | वृषणं नः प्रयेतारम् (*vṛṣaṇaṃ naḥ prayetāram*) [?] |
| 4 | अग्निः (इळः) (*agniḥ (iḷaḥ)*) | ईळितो देवः, हव्यवाट्, अमूरः (*īḷito devaḥ, havyavāṭ, amūraḥ*) |
| 5 | बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*) | सुस्तरीम, ऊर्णम्रदः, देवेभ्यः, स्वासस्थम् (*sustarīma, ūrṇamradaḥ, devebhyaḥ, svāsastham*) |
| 6 | देवीर्द्वारः (*devīrdvāraḥ*) | कुष्पाः, कवष्यः, कोषधानः (*kuṣpāḥ, kavaṣyaḥ, koṣadhānaḥ*) [?] |
| 7 | उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) | बृहती, सुवर्चसः, पतिभ्यः, योनिं कृण्वाने, संस्यमाने (*bṛhatī, suvarcasaḥ, patibhyaḥ, yoniṃ kṛṇvāne, saṃsyamāne*) [?] |
| 8 | दैव्या होतारा (*daivyā hotārā*) | मन्द्रा, प्रोथारा, कवी, प्रचेतसा (*mandrā, prothārā, kavī, pracetasā*) [?] |
| 9 | तिस्रो देवीः (*tisro devīḥ*) | अपसाम् अपस्तमा देवी (*apasām apastamā devī*) |

| 11 | वनस्पतिः (*vanaspatiḥ*) | धियो जैत्र, स्पन्दः, स्वधितिः [?], देवेभ्यः, घृतं घृतपाट् [?], यज्ञस्य, आयुः कल्पमानः (*dhiyo jaitra, spandaḥ, svadhitiḥ [?], devebhyaḥ, ghṛtaṃ ghṛtapāṭ [?], yajñasya, āyuḥ kalpamānaḥ*) |
| 12 | अग्निः (स्वाहा) (*agniḥ (svāhā)*) | आज्यस्य मेदः स्वाहा (*ājyasya medaḥ svāhā*) |

Thus the Praiṣa-sūkta gives a connected picture that gathers up the whole of the Āprī-sūktas.

Their purposes, their poetic nature and the opinions of modern scholars about them will likewise be stated at the end of this sūkta, after the explanation of Ṛk 13.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> समिद्धो अग्न आ वह देवाँ अद्य यतस्रुचे ।
> तन्तुं तनुष्व पूर्व्यं सुतसोमाय दाशुषे ॥ १ ॥

> *samiddho agna ā vaha devā~ adya yatasruce |*
> *tantuṃ tanuṣva pūrvyaṃ sutasomāya dāśuṣe ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सम्ऽइद्धः [?] । अग्ने । आ । वह । देवान् । अद्य । यतऽस्रुचे । तन्तुम् । तनुष्व । पूर्व्यम् । सुतऽसोमाय । दाशुषे ॥ १ ॥

> *sam 'iddhaḥ [?] | agne | ā | vaha | devān | adya | yata 'sruce | tantum | tanuṣva | pūrvyam | suta 'somāya | dāśuṣe ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *O Agni, called Samiddha, bring today to the sacrificer with raised ladle the gods who enjoy the oblations; for the one who has pressed Soma and gives the oblation, extend the ancient sacrifice.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> हे अग्ने समिद्धः सम्यग्दीपितः एतन्नामकः [?] त्वं अद्य अस्मिन् यज्ञदिने देवान् हविषां भोक्तॄन् अग्न्यादीन् वह अस्मद्यज्ञं प्रति प्रापय । यतस्रुचे यागाय उद्यतस्रुचे यजमानाय तदर्थं । आ वह च । सुतसोमाय यागार्थमभिषुतसोमाय दाशुषे हविर्दात्रे । यद्वा [?] … पूर्व्यं पूर्वेभ्यो यज्ञेभ्यो हितं पूर्वकालीनं वा तन्तुं यज्ञं तनुष्व विस्तारय ॥

> *he agne samiddhaḥ samyagdīpitaḥ etannāmakaḥ [?] tvaṃ adya asmin yajñadine devān haviṣāṃ bhoktṝn agnyādīn vaha asmadyajñaṃ prati prāpaya | yatasruce yāgāya udyatasruce yajamānāya tadarthaṃ | ā vaha ca | sutasomāya yāgārthamabhiṣutasomāya dāśuṣe havirdātre | yadvā [?] … pūrvyaṃ pūrvebhyo yajñebhyo hitaṃ pūrvakālīnaṃ vā tantuṃ yajñaṃ tanuṣva vistāraya ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *agne* — O Agni; *samiddhaḥ* — you, who are famed as "Samiddha" (well kindled, blazing); *adya* — at this time of the sacrifice; *yatasruce* — for the sacrificer who holds up the ladle for the sacrifice; *devān* — the gods (who accept the oblation); *ā vaha* — bring and bring together; (and) *sutasomāya* — for him who has the soma juice [?]; *dāśuṣe* — who offers the oblation, the sacrificer; *pūrvyam* — the ancient; *tantum* — sacrifice; *tanuṣva* — extend and complete.

### Printed p. 230  (PDF 248)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, famed as Samiddha, kindled well! At this time of the sacrifice bring and bring together the gods who accept the oblation, which has been got ready with the ladle, for the sacrificer who is ready for the sacrifice. And for the sacrificer who has the soma juice and who offers the oblation, extend and complete the ancient sacrifice.

**English Translation (as printed).** Agni, who is Samiddha, bring the gods to-day (to the worshipper), whose ladle is uplifted : extend (the merit of) former sacrifice to the giver (of the Soma libation) is poured forth [sic: the sentence is as printed, evidently with a misprint].

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***samiddhaḥ*** — समिद्धः—सम्यग्दीप्तितः एतन्नामकस्त्वम् (*samiddhaḥ—samyagdīptitaḥ etannāmakastvam*) [?]: Sāyaṇa explains that the Agni famed by the name *samiddha*; in the Āprī-sūkta this refers to the Samit-Agni who holds the first place. The Bṛhaddevatā says:

> इध्मो यः सर्वमेवाग्निरयं हीद्धः समिध्यते ।
> धातेर्वैतत्कृतं रूपं हीध्म समिध्यते ॥

> *idhmo yaḥ sarvamevāgnirayaṃ hīddhaḥ samidhyate |*
> *dhātervaitatkṛtaṃ rūpaṃ hīdhma samidhyate ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-[?]; read with doubt.) The *idhma* of the same bodily form, and Agni, who is all-pervading, are given identity here. By the root *dhā* [?] the word *idhma* is derived from *idh*, that is, "being kindled". The author of the Bṛhaddevatā has given the derivations of the words *idhma* and *samit*; this derivation follows the account of the Nirukta author. In the Nirukta also:

> तासामिध्मः प्रथमागामी भवति । इध्मः समिन्धनात् ।

> *tāsāmidhmaḥ prathamāgāmī bhavati | idhmaḥ samindhanāt |*

(Ni. 8-[?].) so is said regarding the first deity of the Āprī-sūkta. In the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa also, at the beginning of the Praiṣa-sūkta:

> होता यक्षदग्निं समिधा सुसमिधा समिद्धं नाभा पृथिव्याः सङ्गथे वामस्य ।

> *hotā yakṣadagniṃ samidhā susamidhā samiddhaṃ nābhā pṛthivyāḥ saṅgathe vāmasya |*

(Tai. Brā. 3-[?]-[?]-[?].) Agni, thus called *samit* and appearing with the first *prayāja* deity, is addressed in this sense and called to the sacrifice.

### Printed p. 231  (PDF 249)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

Here one more matter must be noticed. The name *idhma* (as a deity name) does not occur in the Āprī-sūktas, nor does this name occur in the Praiṣa-sūktas. Only in the Sarvānukramaṇī:

> सुसमिद्धमितीध्मं समिद्धो वा अग्निः …… इति प्रत्यृचं देवताः ।

> *susamiddhamitīdhmaṃ samiddho vā agniḥ …… iti pratyṛcaṃ devatāḥ |*

(Ref. [?].) so it is said. Since the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa also has this usage in this context, the Nirukta author, Śaunaka [?] and Kātyāyana [?] take the deity to be Agni [?; the Kannada words are small and partly unclear]. Moreover, the adjective *samiddha* or *susamiddha* occurs in these sūktas, and the adjective *samidh* is used in three other sūktas, Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?]; 2-[?]-[?]; 10-[?]-[?]; hence these are used for the Āprī-sūktas [?].

These deities are to be invoked first. In the opening Ṛks of these sūktas, the first-in-order is the doer: *susamiddho na ā vaha devāṃ agne haviṣmate* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?]; as printed, with several reference numerals [?]) — the prayer with which the duty of Agni is indicated; he is asked to bring the oblation-takers, and nothing more.

On whether this deity is Agni alone, there is from ancient times a disagreement; Yāska, having stated it, then states his own opinion:

यज्ञद्धे (*yajñaddhe*) [?] इति कात्थक्यः (*iti kātthakyaḥ*); अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः (*agniriti śākapūṇiḥ*) (Ni. 8-[?]) — thus giving the opinions of the respective sages — and then आग्नेय इति तु स्थितिः (*āgneya iti tu sthitiḥ*) (Ni. 8-[?]), thus stating his own opinion. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

> समिधो यजति । प्राणा वै समिधः । प्राणा हीदं सर्वं समिन्धते यदिदं किञ्चित् प्राणानेव तत्प्रीणाति प्राणान् यजमाने दधाति ।

> *samidho yajati | prāṇā vai samidhaḥ | prāṇā hīdaṃ sarvaṃ samindhate yadidaṃ kiñcit prāṇāneva tatprīṇāti prāṇān yajamāne dadhāti |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-[?].) From sentences such as these, equating *samidh* and *prāṇa*, and from many other grounds, this deity must be Agni alone.

***tantum*** — by the word *tantu* the commentator here means "sacrifice". It is *anusyūta* (strung through, continuous) even when it is *vicchinna* (broken up into parts), and being spread out in manifold offerings of oblations, from "stretching" it is called *tantu*. These two qualities apply to other objects too, and *tantu* is their name. For example:

> तन्तुं तन्वन् रजसो भानुमन्विहि ज्योतिष्मतः पथो रक्ष धिया कृतान् ।
> अनुल्बणं वयत जोगुवामपो मनुर्भव जनया दैव्यं जनम् ॥

> *tantuṃ tanvan rajaso bhānumanvihi jyotiṣmataḥ patho rakṣa dhiyā kṛtān |*
> *anulbaṇaṃ vayata joguvāmapo manurbhava janayā daivyaṃ janam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-53-6.) Having cited this Ṛk, in the Aitareya [?] Brāhmaṇa … *(continues on p. 232)*

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> *ghṛta 'vantam | upa | māsi | madhu 'mantam | tanūnapāt | yajñam | viprasya | māvataḥ | śaśamānasya | dāśuṣaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *O Tanūnapāt, you measure out (arrange) the sacrifice of the wise, praising, oblation-giving sacrificer like me, full of ghee and sweetness; the name is explained as ghee or as the fire born of the waters and plants.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> हे तनूनपात् । तनूनपादाज्यमिति काठ्कपक्षे [?] तनूः गावः भोगानां ताः सु जायमानत्वात् [?] ताभ्यः उत्पन्नं क्षीरं क्षीरात् सर्पिः इत्याज्यस्य तनूनपात्वं [?] तदाज्यम् । अग्निपक्षे अपस्तु [?] ओषधिवनस्पतयः तेभ्योऽग्निरिति तनूनपात्वम् [?] । अरणिभ्यामिति भावः । हे तनूनपात्नामक हे अग्ने विप्रस्य मेधाविनः शशमानस्य शंसमानस्य स्तुवतः दाशुषो हविर्दत्तवतो मावतो मत्सदृशस्य यजमानस्य ॥ घृतवन्तं क्षरदाज्योपेतं मधुमन्तं माधुर्योपेतं सोमादिमधुरद्रव्येण तद्वन्तं यज्ञमुपमासि निर्मिमीषे । मिञ् [?] भवसि वा । सम्पूर्तिपर्यन्तं तिष्ठसीत्यर्थः । मा मानेऽ । आदादिकः ॥

> *he tanūnapāt | tanūnapādājyamiti kāṭhkapakṣe [?] tanūḥ gāvaḥ bhogānāṃ tāḥ su jāyamānatvāt [?] tābhyaḥ utpannaṃ kṣīraṃ kṣīrāt sarpiḥ ityājyasya tanūnapātvaṃ [?] tadājyam | agnipakṣe apastu [?] oṣadhivanaspatayaḥ tebhyo 'gniriti tanūnapātvam [?] | araṇibhyāmiti bhāvaḥ | he tanūnapātnāmaka he agne viprasya medhāvinaḥ śaśamānasya śaṃsamānasya stuvataḥ dāśuṣo havirdattavato māvato matsadṛśasya yajamānasya ‖ ghṛtavantaṃ kṣaradājyopetaṃ madhumantaṃ mādhuryopetaṃ somādimadhuradravyeṇa tadvantaṃ yajñamupamāsi nirmimīṣe | miñ [?] bhavasi vā | sampūrtiparyantaṃ tiṣṭhasītyarthaḥ | mā māne ' | ādādikaḥ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *tanūnapāt* — O Agni, famed by the name "Tanūnapāt"; *viprasya* — of the wise one; *śaśamānasya* — who praises (you); *dāśuṣaḥ* — who offers the oblation; *māvataḥ* — who is like me (full of faith), of such a sacrificer; *ghṛtavantam* — which is filled with ghee; *madhumantam* — which is full of sweet things such as soma; *yajñam* — to the sacrifice; *upa māsi* — be pleased to come (and stay) up to the completion of the sacrifice.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, famed by the name Tanūnapāt! For the sacrifice of the wise one who praises you, who offers oblations, and who is like me full of faith, which is filled with ghee and full of sweet things such as soma, be pleased to be present up to the completion of the sacrifice.

### Printed p. 234  (PDF 252)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

*(The Bhāvārtha ends: "… up to the completion of the sacrifice.")*

**English Translation (as printed).** Tanunapat, be present at this well-flavoured and butter-fed sacrifice, (the offering) of a pious offerer (of oblations) ; glorifying you.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***tanūnapāt*** — here Sāyaṇa gives two kinds of meaning, on the authority of the Nirukta. First: तनूनपादाज्यमिति काठ्कपक्षे तनूर्गावो भोगानां ताः सु जायमानत्वात् (*tanūnapādājyamiti kāṭhkapakṣe tanūrgāvo bhogānāṃ tāḥ su jāyamānatvāt*) [?]; the "bodies" (*tanu*) are the cows, being (the producers) of the enjoyments; from them is produced milk, from milk ghee (*ājya*): thus, in the view of the Kāṭhaka [?] school, *tanūnapāt* is ghee, and the *yajña* is that ghee. Taking *tanūnapāt* as meaning *ājya* (ghee), according to Kātthakya, the word *tanu* means "cow"; from it ghee is produced by way of milk; *tanūnapāt* means ājya, or the sacrifice that has ghee. Second: अग्निपक्षे अपस्तु (*agnipakṣe apastu*) [?] — in the Agni view, from the waters the plants and trees (*oṣadhi-vanaspati*) are produced, from them (the churning sticks, *araṇi*) Agni is born; hence the name *tanūnapāt*. *Tanu* here means "water". The Bṛhaddevatā says:

> अयं तनूनपाद्ग्निरसौ हि तनूनपात् नः [?] ।
> ततस्तु मध्यमो जज्ञे स्थाने यं मध्यमात्रतः [?] ॥
> अनन्तरं प्रजामाहुर्नपादित्यपदं नवः [?] ।
> नपादेमुष्य चैवायम् अग्निस्त्रेन तनूनपात् ॥

> *ayaṃ tanūnapādgnirasau hi tanūnapāt naḥ [?] |*
> *tatastu madhyamo jajñe sthāne yaṃ madhyamātrataḥ [?] ‖*
> *anantaraṃ prajāmāhurnapādityapadaṃ navaḥ [?] |*
> *napādemuṣya caivāyam agnistrena tanūnapāt ‖*

> तनूनपादयं त्वेन नामा यच्चेष्ट तनूनम् [?] ।
> नपादिति प्रजा माहुरमुतोऽस्य च सम्भवम् ॥

> *tanūnapādayaṃ tvena nāmā yacceṣṭa tanūnam [?] |*
> *napāditi prajā māhuramuto 'sya ca sambhavam ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-[?] to 3-[?], and 3-[?]; these verses are only partly legible and are given with doubt.) The sense of these Bṛhaddevatā verses, as the Kannada explains: the *nap(āt)* word in *tanūnapāt* means "grandson" (*pautra*) in the sense of progeny; the "celestial" fire of the heavenly world is, by its spreading power, called *tanūnapāt*, hence *tanūnapāt* is its synonym. From this the Agni of the atmosphere (the lightning) and the terrestrial Agni are also born from the *tanū* of the waters; so for the earthly Agni too the name *tanūnapāt* …

… has been explained as meaning "the name *tanūnapāt*". The relation of this form of Agni with the Agni *Narāśaṃsa* and the differences between them will be explained in the Special Topics that follow.

***māsi*** — निर्मिमीषे मिमीते भवसि वा । सम्पूर्तिपर्यन्तं तिष्ठसीति वा (*nirmimīṣe mimīte bhavasi vā | sampūrtiparyantaṃ tiṣṭhasīti vā*) [?]: "you prepare, or you are; or you remain until the sacrifice is completely finished" — the meaning is "stay until the complete completion of the sacrifice".

***viprasya*** — the word *vipra* is read among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-[?]-[?]); "of the wise, one possessing intelligence, and of the praising [?]": of the sacrificer.

***māvataḥ*** — मत्सदृशस्य यजमानस्य (*matsadṛśasya yajamānasya*): of a sacrificer who is like me, "who is endowed with the same faith [?]".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly).** *ghṛtavantam* (*ghṛtam asyāsti*; suffix *matup*; *tadasyāsti*…; *pit*, hence *anudātta*), *māsi* (root *mā māne*, *adādi*; *laṭ*, second person singular; *sip* ending; *ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ* drops *śap* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72); *lopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. [?]): *ati̇ṅ*, *nighāta* accent), *tanūnapāt* (*āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 4-3-[?]): suffix *vatup* after *asmad*; *pratyayottarapadayoś ca* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-98): replaced by *ma*; *ā sarvanāmnaḥ* (Pā. **॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> शुचिः पावको अद्भुतो मध्वा यज्ञं मिमिक्षति ।
> नराशंसस्त्रिरा दिवो देवो देवेषु यज्ञियः ॥ ३ ॥

> *śuciḥ pāvako adbhuto madhvā yajñaṃ mimikṣati |*
> *narāśaṃsastrirā divo devo deveṣu yajñiyaḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> शुचिः । पावकः । अद्भुतः । मध्वा । यज्ञम् । मिमिक्षति ।
> नराशंसः । त्रिः । आ । दिवः । देवः । देवेषु । यज्ञियः ॥ ३ ॥

> *śuciḥ | pāvakaḥ | adbhutaḥ | madhvā | yajñam | mimikṣati |*
> *narāśaṃsaḥ | triḥ | ā | divaḥ | devaḥ | deveṣu | yajñiyaḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *Agni Narāśaṃsa, among the gods pure, purifying, wonderful, shining and fit for the sacrifice, praised by the priests, comes from heaven and thrice sprinkles our sacrifice with sweet fruit; the alternative view of Kātthakya takes Narāśaṃsa as the sacrifice-presiding deity.* Small type; doubtful words marked)

> देवेषु मध्ये शुचिः शुद्धो दीप्तो वा पावकोऽन्नस्य पूतस्य [?] शोधयिता अद्भुतोऽद्भुत इव [?] भवति । आश्चर्यभूत इत्यर्थः । देवो द्योतनशीलो यज्ञियो यज्ञसम्पादनार्हः । नराशंसो नर्यः कर्मनेतृभिर्ऋत्विग्भिः शंसनीयोऽग्निर्दिवो द्युलोकादागत्य मध्वा मधुरेण रसेन यज्ञमस्मदीयं त्रिरा मिमिक्षति । त्रिवारं समन्तात् सिञ्चति । स्वदेयमित्यर्थः । यद्वा मधुरेण फलेन त्रिरा मिमिक्षति । योजयतीत्यर्थः । नराशंसो यज्ञ इति कात्थक्यपक्षे यज्ञाभिमानी देवो द्योतमानो द्युलोकादागत्यास्मदीयं यज्ञं त्रिरा मिमिक्षति [?] । उपसर्गव्यवहितयोगः [?] क्रियाध्याहारः [?] । त्रिवारमागच्छति । त्रिराहरति [?] वा फलम् । अवशिष्टं पूर्ववन्नेयम् ॥

> *deveṣu madhye śuciḥ śuddho dīpto vā pāvako 'nnasya pūtasya [?] śodhayitā adbhuto 'dbhuta iva [?] bhavati | āścaryabhūta ityarthaḥ | devo dyotanaśīlo yajñiyo yajñasampādanārhaḥ | narāśaṃso naryaḥ karmanetṛbhirṛtvigbhiḥ śaṃsanīyo 'gnirdivo dyulokādāgatya madhvā madhureṇa rasena yajñamasmadīyaṃ trirā mimikṣati | trivāraṃ samantāt siñcati | svadeyamityarthaḥ | yadvā madhureṇa phalena trirā mimikṣati | yojayatītyarthaḥ | narāśaṃso yajña iti kātthakyapakṣe yajñābhimānī devo dyotamāno dyulokādāgatyāsmadīyaṃ yajñaṃ trirā mimikṣati [?] | upasargavyavahitayogaḥ [?] kriyādhyāhāraḥ [?] | trivāramāgacchati | trirāharati [?] vā phalam | avaśiṣṭaṃ pūrvavanneyam ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *deveṣu* — among the gods; *śuciḥ* — the pure one; *pāvakaḥ* — who purifies (the food); *adbhutaḥ* — wonderful; *devaḥ* — shining; *yajñiyaḥ* — fit for obtaining the sacrifice; *narāśaṃsaḥ* — Agni, famed as Narāśaṃsa (praised by the priests); *divaḥ* — having come from the heavenly world; *madhvā* — with sweet juice or fruit; *yajñam* — the sacrifice; *triḥ* — thrice; *ā mimikṣati* — sprinkles all round, or brings the fruit thrice at the three sacrifice-times.

**Bhāvārtha.** Agni, who is pure among the gods, who purifies the food, wonderful, shining, fit for obtaining the sacrifice and famed as Narāśaṃsa, comes from the heavenly world and thrice joins this our sacrifice with a sweet fruit.

### Printed p. 237  (PDF 255)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 10 [?].)*

**English Translation (as printed).** The pure, purifying, wonderful Narasansa, an adorable god among gods, (having come) from heaven, thrice mixes the sacrifice with the sweet (juice of the Soma).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***narāśaṃsaḥ*** — नर्यैः शंसनीयः (अग्निः) (*naryaiḥ śaṃsanīyaḥ (agniḥ)*): "Agni, who is praised by men", and (it is also said) the name of "the sacrifice". Or नराशंसोऽग्निर्यज्ञो वा (*narāśaṃso 'gniryajño vā*): *narāśaṃsa* is either Agni or the sacrifice. This is the view meant by the commentator that the word *narāśaṃsa* means either Agni or the sacrifice, and the Nirukta passage supports these two opinions:

> नराशंसो यज्ञ इति कात्थक्यः । नरा अस्मिन्नासीनाः शंसन्ति । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः । नर्यैः प्रशस्यो भवति ।

> *narāśaṃso yajña iti kātthakyaḥ | narā asminnāsīnāḥ śaṃsanti | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ | naryaiḥ praśasyo bhavati |*

(Ni. 8-[?].) "*Narāśaṃsa* is the sacrifice, says Kātthakya; men sit in it and recite praise; Agni, says Śākapūṇi: he is praised by men." After pointing out these two opinions it says (Yāska):

> नराशंसस्य महिमानमेषामुपस्तोषाम यजतस्य यज्ञैः ।
> ये सुक्रतवः शुचयो धियन्धाः स्वदन्ति देवा उभयानि हव्या ॥

> *narāśaṃsasya mahimānameṣāmupastoṣāma yajatasya yajñaiḥ |*
> *ye sukratavaḥ śucayo dhiyandhāḥ svadanti devā ubhayāni havyā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2-2 [?].) Citing this Ṛk, "in this Ṛk the meaning 'Agni' is appropriate". In the Nighaṇṭu, the deity *narāśaṃsa* is understood to be one of the forms of Agni [?]. The author of the Bṛhaddevatā says the same:

> नराशंसस्त्रिस्थानमेनमेवाग्निः [?] त्रिष्टुः [?] ।
> बर्हिर्द्वारश्च देव्योऽग्निमेनमेव तु संश्रिताः [?] ॥

> *narāśaṃsastristhānamenamevāgniḥ [?] triṣṭuḥ [?] |*
> *barhirdvāraśca devyo 'gnimenameva tu saṃśritāḥ [?] ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 1-[?]; read with doubt.) In this verse *narāśaṃsa* is said to be inherent in Agni, like the other deities mentioned here. And:

> पृथक्त्वेन समासैस्तु यज्ञे यच्च स्तुतिर्नृभिः [?] ।
> स्तुत्यन्ताप्रीषु तेनेमं नराशंसं तु कारवः [?] ॥

> *pṛthaktvena samāsaistu yajñe yacca stutirnṛbhiḥ [?] |*
> *stutyantāprīṣu tenemaṃ narāśaṃsaṃ tu kāravaḥ [?] ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-[?].) Since in the sacrifice he is separately praised, also in combination, by all men, the poets [?] have called this (Agni) "Narāśaṃsa" in the Āprī-sūktas; thus the author of the Nirukta, giving a different view …

> नरैः प्रशस्य आसीनैः [?] … नरः ॥

> *narāśaṃsamihaike tu agnimāhurbhetare [?] |*
> *naraiḥ śaṃsanti sarve 'sminnāsīnā iti nādhvare [?] |*
> *etamevāhuragniṃ narāśaṃso 'dhvare hyayam |*
> *naraiḥ praśasya āsīnaiḥ [?] … naraḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-3 to 3-6 [?]; partly legible.) Some say that Narāśaṃsa is Agni; since men gather in the sacrifice and praise, others say it is the sacrifice itself. A third group says that, since Agni is praised by the men gathered in the sacrifice, Narāśaṃsa is Agni himself; this is the opinion of still others. The third is a reconciliation of the first and second opinions. Along with these two meanings Sāyaṇa has also given a third, in explaining Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?] in his bhāṣya:

> नराशंस इत्येतन्नामकं देवविशेषं यद्वा अनयार्थवृत्त्या सदसस्पतिदेवताप्रकारोऽयं शब्दः । अत्र अग्निवत् सदसस्पतेरपि नर्यैः शस्यमानत्वात् नराशंसस्त्वम् [?] । एतमेवाभिष्टुवन्तो [?] हृदि निधाय ब्राह्मणमेवामान्नायते — प्रजा वै नरो वाक् शंसः । (ऐ. ब्रा. २-[?]) इति ।

> *narāśaṃsa ityetannāmakaṃ devaviśeṣaṃ yadvā anayārthavṛttyā sadasaspatidevatāprakāro 'yaṃ śabdaḥ | atra agnivat sadasaspaterapi naryaiḥ śasyamānatvāt narāśaṃsastvam [?] | etamevābhiṣṭuvanto [?] hṛdi nidhāya brāhmaṇamevāmānnāyate — prajā vai naro vāk śaṃsaḥ | (ai. brā. 2-[?]) iti |*

The word *narāśaṃsa* can then mean either a deity of this name, or the deity Sadasaspati; and the idea that it means the latter is signalled by the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa passage quoted. Yet in the Ṛks in this context the sense seems to be Agni throughout, and none can say otherwise.

> नराशंसः प्रति धामान्यञ्जन् तिस्रो दिवः प्रति मह्ना स्वर्चिः ।
> घृतप्रुषा मनसा हव्यमुन्दन् मूर्धन्यज्ञस्य समनक्तु देवान् ॥

> *narāśaṃsaḥ prati dhāmānyañjan tisro divaḥ prati mahnā svarciḥ |*
> *ghṛtapruṣā manasā havyamundan mūrdhanyajñasya samanaktu devān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3-2 [?].) In this and such Ṛks too, the sense is Agni.

In the ten Āprī-sūktas the deity Narāśaṃsa is addressed six times and the deity Tanūnapāt six times [?]. In the first Maṇḍala, in the two sūktas, they are both addressed together. How these two deities have been treated, the contradiction found in them, how it has been explained and how scholars have discussed this matter, is the topic of the discussion that follows.

Regarding the *prayāja* principle the main point to be noted is that there is no necessity to invoke these two deities together, since …

### Printed p. 239  (PDF 257)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

… these two deities are portions of Agni, and the first fruit of Agni is called *āprī*; therefore it is not proper to address them. Haug (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa translator) says that these are two distinct deities; but that opinion is not sound. Here the following should be noted: in the Āprī-sūktas where it occurs, the word *tanūnapāt*, as vocative, is an epithet of Agni; likewise, among the epithets of Narāśaṃsa, *kavi*, *sujihva*, *śuci*, *deva*, *devatama* and others belong to Agni too; the sense is that Narāśaṃsa is known to the priests as dear, terrestrial Agni in form, and *tanūnapāt* as the one who has, from the other heavenly form, been invited here; (it is held that) in person, he is the one who, on the prayer of the sacrificers, has accepted the oblation and delivers it to the gods. This opinion of some scholars is valid, and in its explanation truth is mixed with fancy. *(This paragraph is read at low confidence; the Kannada print is small and dense.)*

By their sweet tongue they make the sacrifice rich in honey; both these deities have the nature of the performer. *Prathidhāmāni añjan* (Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]); by such epithets Narāśaṃsa shows the sacrifice to the men:

> तनूनपात्पथ ऋतस्य यानान्मध्वा समञ्जन् स्वदया सुजिह्व ।
> मन्मानि धीभिरुत यज्ञमृन्धन् देवत्रा च कृणुह्यध्वरं नः ॥

> *tanūnapātpatha ṛtasya yānānmadhvā samañjan svadayā sujihva |*
> *manmāni dhībhiruta yajñamṛndhan devatrā ca kṛṇuhyadhvaraṃ naḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-2.) As described in such Ṛks, Tanūnapāt makes the paths of the sacrifice sweet and pleasant; thus his nature is told. These descriptions are given thus in the Praiṣa-sūkta:

> होता यक्षत्तनूनपातमदितेर्गर्भं भुवनस्य गोपाम् । मध्वाद्य देवो देवेभ्यो देवयानान् [?] पथोऽनक्तु [?] … होतर्यज [?] ।

> *hotā yakṣattanūnapātamaditergarbhaṃ bhuvanasya gopām | madhvādya devo devebhyo devayānān [?] patho 'naktu [?] … hotaryaja [?] |*

(Tai. Brā. 2-[?]-[?]-[?].)

> होता यक्षन्नराशंसं नृशंसं [?] स्वर्गं [?] प्रयेतारम् । गोभिर्वसावान्नः [?] … शक्रीवान् [?] प्रथमयावा हिरण्यैः … होतर्यज [?] ।

> *hotā yakṣannarāśaṃsaṃ nṛśaṃsaṃ [?] svargaṃ [?] prayetāram | gobhirvasāvānnaḥ [?] … śakrīvān [?] prathamayāvā hiraṇyaiḥ … hotaryaja [?] |*

(Tai. Brā. 3-[?]-[?]-[?]; the quotations are only partly legible and are given with doubt.) By these sentences Tanūnapāt is called "the son of Aditi" and the lighter of the gods' path; Narāśaṃsa is called "the first to go" (*prathamayāvan*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?]) — as the representative of the deities, the first to go for men; it is described that he is the guide of men. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> ईळितो अग्न आ वहेन्द्रं चित्रमिह प्रियम् ।
> इयं हि त्वा मतिर्ममाच्छा सुजिह्व वच्यते ॥ ४ ॥

> *īḷito agna ā vahendraṃ citramiha priyam |*
> *iyaṃ hi tvā matirmamācchā sujihva vacyate ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> ईळितः । अग्ने । आ । वह । इन्द्रम् । चित्रम् । इह । प्रियम् ।
> इयम् । हि । त्वा । मतिः । मम । अच्छ । सुऽजिह्व । वच्यते ॥ ४ ॥

> *īḷitaḥ | agne | ā | vaha | indram | citram | iha | priyam |*
> *iyam | hi | tvā | matiḥ | mama | accha | su 'jihva | vacyate ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *O Agni, called Iḷā, praised by all, bring here to us Indra, wonderful and dear, to accept the oblation; O bright-tongued one, this my praise, a meditation, is spoken towards you; the sacrificer's purpose and the Soma-offering are also explained.* Small type; many words doubtful)

> हे अग्ने ईळितः सर्वैः स्तुत्य इळनामकस्त्वमिहास्मिन्यज्ञे चित्रं चायनीयं [?] प्रियं प्रीणयितारमस्मान् हविः स्वीकर्तुं वा प्रीतियुक्तमिन्द्रमा वह । आहर । हे सुजिह्व घृतपानेन [?] श्रेष्ठजिह्व [?] … इयं हि मम मतिर्मननीयोक्तिः [?] स्तुतिरूपा वाक् त्वामच्छाभिमुखेन प्राप्तुं वच्यते । मतिर्मननसाधना [?] ईळितोऽग्न [?] पूर्वार्धे [?] वर्जयित्वा [?] … वा छन्दसीति विकल्पेन … अत्र पुरोडाशादिभिर्नानयज्ञ [?] … यज्ञसम्बन्धिदेवताभिश्च यज्ञः प्रवर्त्यते इति स्पष्टत्वेन व्याख्येयम् ॥

> *he agne īḷitaḥ sarvaiḥ stutya iḷanāmakastvamihāsminyajñe citraṃ cāyanīyaṃ [?] priyaṃ prīṇayitāramasmān haviḥ svīkartuṃ vā prītiyuktamindramā vaha | āhara | he sujihva ghṛtapānena [?] śreṣṭhajihva [?] … iyaṃ hi mama matirmananīyoktiḥ [?] stutirūpā vāk tvāmacchābhimukhena prāptuṃ vacyate | matirmananasādhanā [?] īḷito 'gna [?] pūrvārdhe [?] varjayitvā [?] … vā chandasīti vikalpena … atra puroḍāśādibhirnānayajña [?] … yajñasambandhidevatābhiśca yajñaḥ pravartyate iti spaṣṭatvena vyākhyeyam ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *agne* — O Agni; *iḷitaḥ* — you who are famed by the name Iḷā (praised by all); *iha* — in this sacrifice; *citram* — the one who causes wonder; *priyam* — the one who is dear (to us); *indram* — Indra; *ā vaha* — bring; *suj̈ihva* — O Agni with the bright tongue (radiant with the ghee you drink); *iyaṃ hi mama matiḥ* — this my praise, which is thoughtful; *tvā acchā* — towards you; *vacyate* — is recited.

### Printed p. 242  (PDF 260)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, praised by all and famed by the name Iḷā! Bring to us in this sacrifice Indra, the one who causes wonder and is dear to us. O Agni, bright with the ghee you drink, this my praise, full of meditation, is being recited before you.

**English Translation (as printed).** Agni, who is Ilita, bring hither Indra, the wonderful, the beloved; this my praise is recited, bright-tongued, before you.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***iḷitaḥ*** — ईळितः—सर्वैः स्तुत्यः इळ नामकः त्वम् (*īḷitaḥ—sarvaiḥ stutyaḥ iḷa nāmakaḥ tvam*): "you who are praised by all and are known by the name *iḷā*": this is the sense given. *Iḷa* is the root *īḍ stutau* (*īḍe stutikarmaṇi*; *indhate vā*, "he is kindled"); the word *iḷā* is explained as derived from the root *īḍ* in the sense of praise, or from the root *indh* in the sense of kindling: Ni. 8-[?], and the Nirukta author, showing the derivation of this word, has explained the true sense of the word in Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-8 [?]. Like *prathama* and *samiddha*, this word too has no distinct deity-name in this context; it appears to be used only as an adjective of Agni. In the order of the sacrificial rites, Agni is the helper and, being completely present with the ladle, he is naturally praised. At the beginning (1) Agni is to be *samiddha*; then (2) as *tanūnapāt* or *narāśaṃsa*, to make the oblations rich in sweetness; afterwards (3) he is to bring the gods to the sacrifice. For that work he must be praised; hence at this juncture he is addressed as (3) *iḷita* (a prayer).

In the Āprī-sūktas this word, derived from the root *iḍ*, occurs in eight places either as meaning "praised" or as an epithet "praise-worthy" [?], and in one place the same is used for Agni to show his radiant nature; in nine places it is used for Agni's power. And in the Ṛk of Viśvāmitra:

> प्र दीधितिर्विश्ववारा जिगाति होतारमिळः प्रथमं यजध्यै ।
> अच्छा नमोभिर्वृषभं वन्दध्यै स देवान् यक्षदिषितो यजीयान् ॥

> *pra dīdhitirviśvavārā jigāti hotāramiḷaḥ prathamaṃ yajadhyai |*
> *acchā namobhirvṛṣabhaṃ vandadhyai sa devān yakṣadiṣito yajīyān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-3.) In this Ṛk alone *iḷa* is understood as food (*anna*); both that and the chief deity Agni of the Ṛk are connected; this meaning differs from the Āprī-sūktas' tradition. But in the Praiṣa-sūkta alone the sense is Agni.

### Printed p. 243  (PDF 261)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 10 [?].)*

> होता यक्षदग्निमिळ ईळितो देवो देवानां [?] आवक्षद्द्वारो हव्यवाडमूरः [?] ।
> उपेमं यज्ञमुपेमां [?] देवो देवपूतमवतु वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥

> *hotā yakṣadagnimiḷa īḷito devo devānāṃ [?] āvakṣaddvāro havyavāḍamūraḥ [?] |*
> *upemaṃ yajñamupemāṃ [?] devo devapūtamavatu vetvājyasya hotaryaja ‖*

(Tai. Brā. 3-[?]-[?]-[?]; partly legible.) On this sentence the commentator says: "*iḷā ity etan nāmakam agniṃ tṛtīyaprayājadevam*", giving Agni as the synonym. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

> इळो यजत्यन्नं वा इळान्नमेव तत्प्रीणात्यन्नं यजमाने दधाति ।

> *iḷo yajatyannaṃ vā iḷānnameva tatprīṇātyannaṃ yajamāne dadhāti |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-[?].) *Iḷā* means the offering-substance that is the sacrifice's food; it says that by this food, as the beneficial fruit, there is food for the sacrificer himself.

As explained above, Yāska also shows the connection of this word with the root *indh*, but not rightly interpreted. Here Kātthakya's opinion is presented to us by Yāska. In the Bṛhaddevatā:

> इळस्त्वेधिकेनं [?] रूपमिळेत्थं स्तुतिकर्मणः ।
> इळावांस्तेन वोक्तोऽग्निरिडिना वृद्धिकर्मणा ॥

> *iḷastvedhikenaṃ [?] rūpamiḷetthaṃ stutikarmaṇaḥ |*
> *iḷāvāṃstena vokto 'gniriḍinā vṛddhikarmaṇā ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-[?].) By these sentences it is shown that this word means *ārcīya* ("worthy of worship") and synonym of Agni; and the word *iḷāvān* is also an epithet of Agni:

> गोमाँ अग्नेविमाँ अश्वी यज्ञो नृवत्सखा सदमिदप्रमृष्यः ।
> इळावाँ एषो असुर प्रजावान् दीर्घो रयिः पृथुबुध्नः सभावान् ॥

> *gomā~ agnevimā~ aśvī yajño nṛvatsakhā sadamidapramṛṣyaḥ |*
> *iḷāvā~ eṣo asura prajāvān dīrgho rayiḥ pṛthubudhnaḥ sabhāvān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-2-5 [?].) In this Ṛk, the word *iḷāvān* is an adjective of Agni, hence the Bṛhaddevatā indicates this portion.

Such different traditions, appearing in the explanations, are all taken as saying that the fourth place in the Āprī-sūktas is held by Agni as the deity.

***matiḥ*** — मनननसाधना स्तुतिरूपा वाक् (*manananasādhanā stutirūpā vāk*): speech that is a means of thought and takes the form of praise. The meaning: speech which is thoughtful and in the form of praise.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar page, begun; noted briefly).** *iḷitaḥ* (root *iḍa stutau*; suffix *kta* by *niṣṭhā*; *ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-35): the augment *iṭ*; by the suffix-accent the end is *udātta*) …

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स्तृणानासो यतस्रुचो बर्हिर्यज्ञे स्वध्वरे ।
> वृञ्जे देवव्यचस्तममिन्द्राय शर्म सप्रथः ॥ ५ ॥

> *stṛṇānāso yatasruco barhiryajñe svadhvare |*
> *vṛñje devavyacastamamindrāya śarma saprathaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> स्तृणानासः । यतऽस्रुचः । बर्हिः । यज्ञे । सुऽअध्वरे ।
> वृञ्जे । देवऽव्यचःऽतमम् । इन्द्राय । शर्म । सऽप्रथः ॥ ५ ॥

> *stṛṇānāsaḥ | yata 'srucaḥ | barhiḥ | yajñe | su 'adhvare |*
> *vṛñje | deva 'vyacaḥ 'tamam | indrāya | śarma | sa 'prathaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

### Printed p. 245  (PDF 263)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga [?].)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *In the well-ordered soma sacrifice the priests with ladles raised strew the barhis; they prepare for Indra the wide house, a comfort, which most pleases the gods.* Small type; a few words doubtful)

> स्वध्वरे शोभनप्रायणीयोदयनीयाद्यनुयागवति [?] यज्ञे सोमयागे बर्हिर्दर्भान् स्तृणानासः आस्तृण्वन्तो यतस्रुचो नियमितजुहूपात्राः ऋत्विजो देवव्यचस्तमम् अतिशयेन देवानामिमं [?] सप्रथः सर्वतो विस्तीर्णं शर्म सुखसाधनं गृहमिन्द्राय वृञ्जे । विवर्जयन्ति [?] सम्पादयन्तीत्यर्थः ॥

> *svadhvare śobhanaprāyaṇīyodayanīyādyanuyāgavati [?] yajñe somayāge barhirdarbhān stṛṇānāsaḥ āstṛṇvanto yatasruco niyamitajuhūpātrāḥ ṛtvijo devavyacastamam atiśayena devānāmimaṃ [?] saprathaḥ sarvato vistīrṇaṃ śarma sukhasādhanaṃ gṛhamindrāya vṛñje | vivarjayanti [?] sampādayantītyarthaḥ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *svadhvare* — in this soma sacrifice, which is excellent and preceded by preliminary rites such as the *prāyaṇīya*; *yajñe* — in the sacrifice; *barhiḥ* — the seats of *darbha* grass; *stṛṇānāsaḥ* — strewing; *yatasrucaḥ* — those priests who hold the ladles and vessels such as *juhū* for the sacrifice; *devavyacastamam* — which most pleases (invites) the gods; *saprathaḥ* — wide; *śarma* — the sacrificial house, a means of comfort; *indrāya* — for Indra; *vṛñje* — they prepare.

**Bhāvārtha.** The priests who hold the ladles and vessels such as the *juhū* for the sacrifice, in this soma sacrifice, which is excellent and endowed with preliminary rites such as the *prāyaṇīya*, strew the *darbha* seats and prepare for Indra the sacrificial house, wide, a means of comfort, and one which pleases the gods in the highest degree by calling them.

**English Translation (as printed).** The priests, bearing ladles, are strewing the sacred grass in this holy sacrifice, to prepare a god-frequented and well-spread abode for Indra.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***barhiḥ*** — "Like the ideas *idhma* and *iḷā*, this implement is much more of a concrete, material form. *Barhis* means the seat of *darbha* grass. Unlike the doors in *devīr dvāraḥ*, to which a divine element is ascribed, no such element was ascribed to the *barhis*; only the sense 'seat of the gods' is suggested. Moreover, the doors are asked to open of themselves, without other help, and make a way for the arrival of the gods: the doors being inanimate, they cannot make a wide way for themselves without some divine power; in the case of the *barhis* alone, no such power is ascribed. The priests must spread it. And not only in this Ṛk but in the other Ṛks of the Āprī-sūktas too it is stated plainly that the *barhis* is to be spread with the help of the priests and others. For instance —" *(the example, a Ṛk, stands at the head of the next page.)*

### Printed p. 246  (PDF 264)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

> प्राचीनं बर्हिरोजसा सहस्रवीरमस्तृणन् । यत्रादित्या विराजथ ॥

> *prācīnaṃ barhirojasā sahasravīramastṛṇan | yatrādityā virājatha ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, and likewise in Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-5-4 [?] (*prācīnaṃ barhiḥ pavamāno stṛṇan hariḥ* [?]), the priests are described as spreading the *barhis*. So in the Ṛks of the other Āprī-sūktas too the *barhis* is called an earthly thing and inanimate, but yet a place that is holy to the gods. In the Praiṣa-sūkta:

> होता यक्षद्बर्हिः सुष्वरीर्णोर्णम्रदा अस्मिन्यज्ञे वि च प्र च प्रथताम् [?] स्वासस्थं देवेभ्यः । ऐमेनमद्य वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याः सदन्तु [?] प्रियमिन्द्रस्य … होतर्यज [?] ॥

> *hotā yakṣadbarhiḥ suṣvarīrṇorṇamradā asminyajñe vi ca pra ca prathatām [?] svāsasthaṃ devebhyaḥ | aimenamadya vasavo rudrā ādityāḥ sadantu [?] priyamindrasya … hotaryaja [?] ‖*

(Tai. Brā. 3-[?]-[?]-[?].) Here the commentator says that the *barhis* is, as a synonym of Agni, the fourth *prayāja* deity, with the character of a deity, and a seat. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

> बर्हिर्यजति पशवो वै बर्हिः पशूनेव तत्प्रीणाति पशून्यजमाने दधाति ।

> *barhiryajati paśavo vai barhiḥ paśūneva tatprīṇāti paśūnyajamāne dadhāti |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-[?].) here the *barhis* is explained as the animal that grazes grass and is soft [?]; but it is understood that there is no scope at all for this meaning here.

The Nirukta author says: *barhiḥ paribarhaṇāt* — "*barhis*, from growing quickly" — since *darbha* grass grows fast it is called *barhis* (Ni. 8-[?]). In the Bṛhaddevatā:

> बर्हिरेवायमग्निस्तु सर्वं हि परिबर्हितम् ।
> अन्नेन यद्वृतो वा सन्नीयमानेन परिबर्हितः ॥

> *barhirevāyamagnistu sarvaṃ hi paribarhitam |*
> *annena yadvṛto vā sannīyamānena paribarhitaḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-[?].) "Because it is surrounded by food, and because after the *ājya*-offering it is filled by the *idhma*, it is Agni himself in the form of *barhis*", thus it says of the identity.

In many matters the author of the Bṛhaddevatā follows the Nirukta, but in this context he shows a little difference; the author of the Nirukta takes *barhis* simply as the seat of the gods, while he explains it as being at once the divine, a synonym of Agni, and a seat.

***stṛṇānāsaḥ*** — *āstṛṇate*: "spreading" — those who spread them.

***saprathaḥ*** — *saprathāḥ sarvataḥ pṛthuḥ*: "spread out on all sides"; the Nirukta author explains it as "widely extended" (Ni. 8-[?]).

### Printed p. 247  (PDF 265)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 10 [?].)*

> त्वमग्ने सप्रथा असि जुष्टो होता वरेण्यः । त्वया यज्ञं वितन्वते ॥

> *tvamagne saprathā asi juṣṭo hotā vareṇyaḥ | tvayā yajñaṃ vitanvate ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-13-4 [?].) Having cited this Ṛk, he explains the meaning of the word *saprathāḥ* there. As in this case, in the other Ṛks too the epithet *saprathāḥ* is applied to the divine sacrificial houses, which are extended on all sides.

***yatasrucaḥ*** — *bhāratāḥ, vṛktabarhiṣaḥ, yatasrucaḥ* and similar words are read among the names of priests (Ni. [?]). The meaning is "priests who are ready, holding the ladles such as *juhū*, for the sake of the sacrifice".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar page, noted briefly).** *stṛṇānāsaḥ* (root *stṛñ ācchādane*, *kryādi*; *śānac* in the present sense; *kryādibhyaḥ śnā* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-81): the *śnā* vikaraṇa; *prādīnāṃ [?]*: *pratyayasvara*, the suffix *śānac* being *cit*, last-syllable accent; *jas* with *ājjaser asuk* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50): *asuk* augment; *s* becomes *ru*, *visarga*), *yatasrucaḥ* (*yatā sruk yeṣāṃ te*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1): first member keeps its accent; nominative plural), *svadhvare* (*śobhano 'dhvaro yasmin saḥ svadhvaraḥ*; *nañsubhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172): the last member is *udātta*; locative singular), *vṛñje* (root *vṛjī varjane*, *adādi*; the nasal augment because of the *it*; *laṭ*, third person plural; by *vyatyaya* a plural becomes singular, ending *ta*; hence *e*; *lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-41): loss of *t* of the ending; as *pādādi* there is no *nighāta*; by the suffix-accent the last syllable is *udātta*), *saprathaḥ* (root *prathaḥ prakhyāne*; *sarvadhātubhya asun* (Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]): suffix *asun*; *prathanena saha vartate iti saprathaḥ*; *tena saheti tulyayoge* (Pā. Sū. 2-2-28): compound; *vopasarjanasya* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-82): *saha* becomes *sa* [?]; *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139): the *kṛdanta* keeps its natural accent). ‖ 5 ‖

#### Ṛk 6

### Printed p. 248  (PDF 266)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> वि श्रयन्तामृतावृधः प्रयै देवेभ्यो महीः ।
> पावकासः पुरुस्पृहो द्वारो देवीरसश्चतः ॥ ६ ॥

> *vi śrayantāmṛtāvṛdhaḥ prayai devebhyo mahīḥ |*
> *pāvakāsaḥ puruspṛho dvāro devīrasaścataḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> वि । श्रयन्ताम् । ऋतऽवृधः । प्रऽयै । देवेभ्यः । महीः ।
> पावकासः । पुरुऽस्पृहः । द्वारः । देवीः । असश्चतः ॥ ६ ॥

> *vi | śrayantām | ṛta 'vṛdhaḥ | pra 'yai | devebhyaḥ | mahīḥ |*
> *pāvakāsaḥ | puru 'spṛhaḥ | dvāraḥ | devīḥ | asaścataḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *Let the divine doors, presiding deities of the doors of the sacrificial house, open wide, separate, to let the gods enter; they increase the sacrifice, are great, purify, are much desired, and cling not to one another.* Small type)

> द्वारो देवीर्यज्ञस्य द्वाराभिमानिन्यो देवताः वि श्रयन्ताम् । विविधं श्रयन्तु । विवृता भवन्तु । किमर्थं देवेभ्यः प्रयै प्रयातुं देवानां प्रपत्त्यै [?] । प्रयै [?] रोहिष्यै [?] (Pā. 6-4-[?]) इति निपातितः । कीदृश्यः । ऋतवृधो यज्ञस्य वर्धयित्र्यः पूज्या मही [?] महत्यः पावकासः शोधयित्र्यः पुरुस्पृहो बहुस्पृहणीयाः असश्चतो [?] असज्जमानाः परस्परमविप्रकृष्टाः [?] इत्यर्थः ॥

> *dvāro devīryajñasya dvārābhimāninyo devatāḥ vi śrayantām | vividhaṃ śrayantu | vivṛtā bhavantu | kimarthaṃ devebhyaḥ prayai prayātuṃ devānāṃ prapattyai [?] | prayai [?] rohiṣyai [?] (Pā. 6-4-[?]) iti nipātitaḥ | kīdṛśyaḥ | ṛtavṛdho yajñasya vardhayitryaḥ pūjyā mahī [?] mahatyaḥ pāvakāsaḥ śodhayitryaḥ puruspṛho bahuspṛhaṇīyāḥ asaścato [?] asajjamānāḥ parasparamaviprakṛṣṭāḥ [?] ityarthaḥ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *ṛtavṛdhaḥ* — those who make the sacrifice grow; *mahīḥ* — of great form; *pāvakāsaḥ* — having the power of purifying; *puruspṛhaḥ* — those desired by the people [?]; *asaścataḥ* — those who, without clinging, stand separate (to each other); *dvāro devīḥ* — the deities who preside over the doors (of the sacrificial house); *devebhyaḥ* — for the gods; *prayai* — for entering; *viśrayantām* — let them, separately, move apart and make the way.

**Bhāvārtha.** May the deities who preside over the doors of the sacrificial house — those who cause the sacrifice to grow, of great form, who have the power to purify, desired by many, and who stand separate without clinging to each other — move aside separately and open the way for the entrance of the gods.

**English Translation (as printed; heading printed "English Tranlation" [sic]).** Let the bright, separable doors, the augmenters of sacrifice, the purifiers of rites, the desired of many, be set open for the gods to enter.

### Printed p. 249  (PDF 267)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 10 [?].)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***dvāro devīḥ*** — यज्ञगृहस्य द्वाराभिमानिन्यो देवताः (*yajñagṛhasya dvārābhimāninyo devatāḥ*) (Sāyaṇa: "the deities presiding over the doors of the sacrificial house"). There is a difference of opinion as to whether these doors are the doors of the sacrificial house itself or merely a figurative (poetic) usage. If the word here does not mean house-doors, then, in the matter of the deities of the Āprī-sūktas too, we must imagine points that differ from those stated.

From the point of view of ritual procedure, only the *barhis* and the *svāhākṛti* lack a deity-form [?] and are merely earthly things, yet, because they belong to the sacrifice, qualities that are beyond the ordinary are spoken of. In *tisro devīḥ*, since Sarasvatī has a pure divine element, and the other two rivers are added together with her, they are called deities counted together [?]. Likewise in *daivyā hotārau* the earthly *hotṛ*, being connected with the Vedic Agni, is addressed as a deity. But in *devīr dvāraḥ* alone this has no room. If these doors were the doors of the sacrificial house, the question arises why they should have the special place that the *barhis* and *svāhākṛti* have. If only some of the implements that are limbs of the sacrifice are to be viewed as deities, then the most important of them all, the *vedī*, has no name here at all. *(Read at low confidence.)*

One more point to be noticed: the word *dvāraḥ* ("doors") is in the plural. And:

> सप्त होत्राणि मनसा वृणाना इन्वन्तो विश्वं प्रति यन्नृतेन ।
> नृपेशसो विदथेषु प्र जाता अभीमं यज्ञं वि चरन्त पूर्वीः ॥

> *sapta hotrāṇi manasā vṛṇānā invanto viśvaṃ prati yannṛtena |*
> *nṛpeśaso vidatheṣu pra jātā abhīmaṃ yajñaṃ vi caranta pūrvīḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-[?].) in this Ṛk of the Āprī-sūkta the adjective *pūrvīḥ* ("former") is likewise in the plural. And in the duties of these deities we notice:

1) *vi śrayantām ṛtāvṛdho dvāro devīr asaścataḥ* — "they take them separately for the work of the sacrifice" (this Ṛk, 1-142-6) and in the Ṛk (1-[?]-[?]);
2) *[?]* — "they poured out waters" (1-188-5 [?]);
3) *pra pra yajñaṃ pṛṇītana* [?] — "they fill the sacrifice with the fruit" (5-5-5 [?]);
4) *invanto viśvaṃ prati yanty ṛtena* — "they carry all water-resources as the ritual path requires" (3-4-[?]).

### Printed p. 250  (PDF 268)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 6 on *dvāro devīḥ*.)*

Thus many kinds of functions of these (door-deities) are mentioned. In these duties many actions are attributed to them only figuratively (*aupacārika*), as an ornament of speech; some hold that there is no substantial truth in them. For instance,

> समिद्धो अस्य मनुषो दुरोणे देवो देवान् यजसि जातवेदः ।
> आ च वह मित्रमहश्चिकित्वान्त्वं दूतः कविरसि प्रचेताः ॥

> *samiddho asya manuṣo duroṇe devo devān yajasi jātavedaḥ |*
> *ā ca vaha mitramahaścikitvāntvaṃ dūtaḥ kavirasi pracetāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-1.) In this Ṛk, *manuṣo duroṇe* ("in the house of the man") — since what is faced is the man's sacrificial house, these house-doors are said to have only a worldly (*laukika*) sense and to be figuratively (*aupacārika*) spoken of; but the epithets *nṛpeśasaḥ*, *ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*, *pāvakāḥ* and the like are not suitable to them, say some critics. Whether these views are to be supported or refuted must be understood in the light of the earlier Vedic scholars' opinions.

> स्वाध्यो वि दुरो देवयन्तोऽशिश्रयू रथयुर्देवताता ।
> पूर्वी शिशुं न मातरा रिहाणे समग्रुवो न समनेष्वञ्जन् ॥

> *svādhyo vi duro devayanto 'śiśrayū rathayurdevatātā |*
> *pūrvī śiśuṃ na mātarā rihāṇe samagruvo na samaneṣvañjan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3-5 [?].) In this Ṛk of the Āprī-sūkta, *yajñagṛhadvārāṇi* ("the doors of the sacrificial house") is the sense. Some scholars, for the verb *[?]* in the Ṛk, take *yajamānaḥ* as the subject (doer) and construe that they stand resorting to the doors of the sacrificial house [?]. The English scholars Oldenberg, Grassmann and Ludwig have also accepted this explanation. In:

> विराट् सम्राड्विभ्वीः प्रभ्वीर्बह्वीश्च भूयसीश्च याः । दुरो घृतान्यक्षरन् ॥

> *virāṭ samrāḍvibhvīḥ prabhvīrbahvīśca bhūyasīśca yāḥ | duro ghṛtānyakṣaran ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?]; as read.) the words *virāṭ* and *samrāṭ* are two names. Max Müller, the scholar, says that these deities are doors of heaven [?: the Kannada words are *… upasargadiṃ iḍiduberuva svargadvāragaḷeṃdiddāne*] (History of Ancient Sanskrit Literature, p. 245). In the Praiṣa-sūkta:

> होता यक्षद्दुरः कुष्पाः कवष्यः कोषधानीर् [?] … वि पक्ष्मोभिः श्रयन्तामं [?] सुप्रायणा अस्मिन्यज्ञे विश्रयन्तामृतावृधो वियन्तु [?] आज्यस्य होतर्यज ।

> *hotā yakṣadduraḥ kuṣpāḥ kavaṣyaḥ koṣadhānīr [?] … vi pakṣmobhiḥ śrayantāmaṃ [?] suprāyaṇā asminyajñe viśrayantāmṛtāvṛdho viyantu [?] ājyasya hotaryaja |*

(Tai. Brā. 3-[?]-[?]-[?]; partly legible.)

### Printed p. 251  (PDF 269)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 11 [?].)*

By these sentences the commentator explains, with *duro dvārasaṃjñāḥ pañcamaprayājadevatāḥ…* (the doors, the deities of the fifth *prayāja*), *…hotā yajatu*. These sentences, it is said, are in conflict with the foregoing opinion of Sāyaṇa [?]; hence the idea that "doors" are a poetic figure is one that some would hold [?]; (read at low confidence). In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

> दुरो यजति वृष्टिर्वै दुरो वृष्टिमेव तत्प्रीणाति वृष्टिमन्नाद्यं यजमाने दधाति ।

> *duro yajati vṛṣṭirvai duro vṛṣṭimeva tatprīṇāti vṛṣṭimannādyaṃ yajamāne dadhāti |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-[?].) Thus the sense of *dvāraḥ* is taken as *vṛṣṭi* ("rain"); how this can be is not made clear. The Nirukta author:

> द्वारो जवतेर्वा [?] द्रवतेर्वा [?] वृणोतेर्वा [?] ।

> *dvāro janatervā [?] pravṛtervā [?] pātayatervā [?] |*

(Ni. [?].) — thus the Nirukta author, as the Kannada explains, derives *dvāra* either from the root *ju* (giving a sense of pressing on [?]), or from the root *dru* (giving the sense of running [?]), or from the root *vṛ* (giving the sense of separating [?]); the Sanskrit words are read with doubt. And:

> व्यचस्वतीरुर्विया वि श्रयन्तां पतिभ्यो न जनयः शुम्भमानाः ।
> देवीर्द्वारो बृहतीर्विश्वमिन्वा देवेभ्यो भवत सुप्रायणाः ॥

> *vyacasvatīrurviyā vi śrayantāṃ patibhyo na janayaḥ śumbhamānāḥ |*
> *devīrdvāro bṛhatīrviśvaminvā devebhyo bhavata suprāyaṇāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-5.) Citing this Ṛk, while explaining the meaning of the word *dvār*, the Nirukta author says: "*gṛhadvāra* (house-door), says Kātthakya; Kātthakya's opinion is *gṛhadvāra*; Agni, says Śākapūṇi" (Ni. 8-[?]) — he gives the different views, the second being that the deity is Agni. The Bṛhaddevatā:

> द्वारस्तु देव्यो याः प्रोक्ता विश्वेषां [?] ताः तासु पत्न्यः ।
> अग्नायीमनुवर्तन्ते तेथाग्नाय्यग्निमेव च [?] ।
> अग्नेः ध्रुवं स्थितास्तासु संस्तुत्यन्तेऽग्निना सह ।
> प्राधान्यं तासु चैवाग्नेः स्तुतिष्वेव च [?] ॥

> *dvārastu devyo yāḥ proktā viśveṣāṃ [?] tāḥ tāsu patnyaḥ |*
> *agnāyīmanuvartante tethāgnāyyagnimeva ca [?] |*
> *agneḥ dhruvaṃ sthitāstāsu saṃstutyante 'gninā saha |*
> *prādhānyaṃ tāsu caivāgneḥ stutiṣveva ca [?] ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-[?] to 2-[?]; partly legible.) "These doors are the wives of the gods, and they follow Agni's wife [?], who is Agni himself; being firmly in Agni they are praised along with Agni; the chief of them is Agni": thus it is said. This explanation is quite reasonable.

***asaścataḥ*** — *asajjamānāḥ*: "not clinging to each other, standing separate" (*parasparam vipraṛkṛṣṭāḥ* [?]), the sense is "separate".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar page, noted briefly).** *śrayantām* (root *śriñ sevāyām*; *loṭ*, third person plural, form *śrayantām*; being in a word with *ati*… the *nighāta* accent), *ṛtāvṛdhaḥ* (*ṛtaṃ vardhayanti iti ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*; root *vṛdhu vṛddhau*; used in the causative sense, the root is *aṇyarthānvarthādhātu* [?]; suffix *kvip ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-76); *upapada* compound; *anveṣām api dṛśyate* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-136 [?]): lengthening of the former member in the Saṃhitā; *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139): the natural accent of the *kṛdanta*), *prayai* (root *yā prāpaṇe*; *prayai rohiṣyai avyathiṣyai* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-10): formed as an *avyaya* infinitive; *kṛnmejantaḥ* [?]: the name *avyaya*), *mahīḥ* (*mahatī*; the *t* of *mahatī* is dropped by Vedic usage; *vibhakti* following, *supāṃ sulukpūrvasavarṇa…* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39): *pūrvasavarṇa* lengthening), *pāvakāsaḥ* (*jas* following; *ājjaser asuk* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50): *asuk* augment), *puruspṛhaḥ* (root *spṛha īpsāyām*; suffix *kvip*; the natural accent of the *kṛdanta* in the last member), *asaścataḥ* (root *ṣaścā gatau* [?]; the *ca* is changed to *ka* by *vyatyaya* [?]; *śatṛ* in the present sense; *na vidyate saścantaḥ gacchantaḥ yeṣu te asaścantaḥ*; *nañsubhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172): the final of the last member is *udātta*). ‖ 6 ‖

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> आ भन्दमाने उपाके नक्तोषासा सुपेशसा ।
> यह्वी ऋतस्य मातरा सीदतां बर्हिरा सुमत् ॥ ७ ॥

> *ā bhandamāne upāke naktoṣāsā supeśasā |*
> *yahvī ṛtasya mātarā sīdatāṃ barhirā sumat ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आ । भन्दमाने इति । उपाके इति । नक्तोषसा । सुऽपेशसा ।
> यह्वी इति । ऋतस्य । मातरा । सीदताम् । बर्हिः । आ । सुऽमत् ॥ ७ ॥

> *ā | bhandamāne iti | upāke iti | naktoṣasā | su 'peśasā |*
> *yahvī iti | ṛtasya | mātarā | sīdatām | barhiḥ | ā | su 'mat ‖ 7 ‖*
