*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 11.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *the goddesses Night and Dawn, praised by all, close to each other, beautiful, great, makers of the sacrifice, are asked to come of their own accord and sit on the spread grass.* Small type; only partly legible)

> भन्दमाने सर्वैः स्तूयमाने उपाके परस्परं सन्निहिते सुपेशसा शोभनरूपे [?] पेश इति रूपनाम । यह्वी महत्क्यौ [?] अत्यन्तरूपे वा प्रतिदिनं [?] जायमानत्वात् । यह्वीति महन्नाम [?] । ऋतस्य मातरा यज्ञस्य निर्मात्र्यौ ताभ्यामागन्तुना [?] यज्ञस्य सम्पूर्तेः यज्ञमात्रत्वमुपचर्यते [?] । तथाभूतयोः यद्वा अहोरात्रादीनामहोरात्रत्वं साधयितृत्वात् [?] । नक्तोषासा उक्तगुणविशिष्टे अहोरात्रे एते वा सुमत् स्वयमेव अस्माभिरप्रार्थिते इत्यर्थः । यद्वा सुमद् [?] विस्तृतं बर्हिः सीदतां स्वयमेवा सीदतां [?] ॥

> *bhandamāne sarvaiḥ stūyamāne upāke parasparaṃ sannihite supeśasā śobhanarūpe [?] peśa iti rūpanāma | yahvī mahatkyau [?] atyantarūpe vā pratidinaṃ [?] jāyamānatvāt | yahvīti mahannāma [?] | ṛtasya mātarā yajñasya nirmātryau tābhyāmāgantunā [?] yajñasya sampūrteḥ yajñamātratvamupacaryate [?] | tathābhūtayoḥ yadvā ahorātrādīnāmahorātratvaṃ sādhayitṛtvāt [?] | naktoṣāsā uktaguṇaviśiṣṭe ahorātre ete vā sumat svayameva asmābhiraprārthite ityarthaḥ | yadvā sumad [?] vistṛtaṃ barhiḥ sīdatāṃ svayamevā sīdatāṃ [?] ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *bhandamāne* — those praised by all; *upāke* — those who are close to each other; *supeśasā* — of charming form; *yahvī* — of great form, or (since they are born daily) of the form of offspring [?]; *ṛtasya* — of the sacrifice; *mātarā* — the makers; *naktoṣāsā* — the deities Night and Dawn themselves; *sumat* — (even though we have not prayed) of their own accord; *barhiḥ* — on the *darbha* seat; *ā sīdatām* — come and sit facing; or *sumat* — on the *barhis* spread out widely, *ā sīdatām* — come and sit.

**Bhāvārtha.** O deities of Night and Day, praised by all, close to each other, of charming form, of great form, makers of the sacrifice! Even though we have not prayed, be pleased, of your own accord, to sit on our *darbha* seats spread out widely.

**English Translation (as printed).** Beautiful night and morning, ever hymned, ever associated, progeny (of time), parents of sacrifice, sit down of your own good-will on the sacred grass.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** (a) ***bhandamāne*** — सर्वैः स्तूयमाने (*sarvaiḥ stūyamāne*): "praised by all"; this is an epithet of the deities *naktoṣāsā*. In the Nirukta-list of names of the verbs of worship (Ni. 3-[?]) *arcati* and *gāyati* ("worships", "sings") are read, and *bhandanā* — from the root *bhand* — "worship". *Bhandanā*:

---

### Printed p. 254  (PDF 272)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

भन्दना भन्दतेः स्तुतिकर्मणः (*bhandanā bhandateḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ*) (Ni. 6-[?]): *bhandanā* is from the root *bhand*, meaning praise, says the Nirukta author, who cites these two Ṛks:

> आ विवेश रोदसी भूरिवर्पसा पुरुप्रियो भन्दते धामभिः कविः ।

> *ā viveśa rodasī bhūrivarpasā purupriyo bhandate dhāmabhiḥ kaviḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-5-4 [?].)

> स भन्दना उदियर्ति प्रजावतीर्विश्वायुर्विश्वाः सुभरा अहर्दिवि ।

> *sa bhandanā udiyarti prajāvatīrviśvāyurviśvāḥ subharā ahardivi |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-61-7 [?].) By citing these two Ṛks he shows the propriety of the use of this word in the passages where excellent praise is made (Ni. 6-[?]).

(b) ***sumat*** — स्वयमेव (*svayameva*) ("of their own accord"; Sāyaṇa: "even though not prayed by us"): this indicates the deities' self-motivation and respect. The Nirukta author explains *sumat* as "*svayam*", i.e. "of oneself" (Ni. 6-[?]). Besides this, the word is found in the sense *kalyāṇa* ("auspicious"), *śobhana* ("beautiful") or *bhadra* ("good"); to see it, look at the many words that are used with it — *sumadgaṇaḥ*, *sumadrathaḥ*, *sumadaṃśaḥ* etc.:

> आमेनं सुदुघा आ हि गन्तेन नि बर्हिषि सदतना रणिष्टन ।
> अथा मन्दस्व जुजुषाणो अन्धसस्त्वष्टर्देवेभिर्जनिभिः सुमद्गणः ॥

> *āmenaṃ sudughā ā hi gantena ni barhiṣi sadatanā raṇiṣṭana |*
> *athā mandasva jujuṣāṇo andhasastvaṣṭardevebhirjanibhiḥ sumadgaṇaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk the word *sumadgaṇaḥ* is explained as "*śobhanagaṇaḥ*" ("of fine retinue"); and:

> विभावा देवः सुरणः परि क्षितीरग्निर्बभूव शवसा सुमद्रथः ।
> तस्य व्रतानि भूरिपोषिणो वयमुप भूषेम दम आ सुवृक्तिभिः ॥

> *vibhāvā devaḥ suraṇaḥ pari kṣitīragnirbabhūva śavasā sumadrathaḥ |*
> *tasya vratāni bhūripoṣiṇo vayamupa bhūṣema dama ā suvṛktibhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].) in this the word *sumadrathaḥ* means "of a beautiful chariot". Here too *sumat* is a synonym of the words "auspicious" and "beautiful". Therefore here, too, this word, when applied to the deities Night and Dawn who are pleasing, bright and auspicious, is seen to be proper.

(c) ***upāke*** — this word is read among the names of the "near" (*antika*) (Ni. 3-[?]): "close to each other"; the sense is "near one another".

(d) ***supeśasā*** — पेश इति रूपनाम । पिंशतेर्विपिशितं भवति (*peśa iti rūpanāma | piṃśatervipiśitaṃ bhavati*) [?]: "*peśas* means 'form' (*rūpa*); it is related to the root *piś*, 'to be shaped'"; and, because the word *piś* gives the sense "adorned" and "made beautiful", the Nirukta author explains "*supeśasā*" in this very Ṛk (Ni. 4-[?]): "of extremely beautiful form".

---

### Printed p. 255  (PDF 273)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 3 [?], Varga 11.)*

(e) ***yahvī*** — महात्मा अपत्यरूपे वा (*mahātmā apatyarūpe vā*) [?]: "of very great form, or of the form of offspring"; the word is among the names of the great (*mahat*) in the Nirukta (Ni. 3-[?]), and (also) *tuk*, *tokam* (offspring) are read in it (Ni. 3-[?]). These two kinds of nature are described in the Ṛks; for instance:

> उप वो हविषे वन्द्येभिः शूषैः प्र यह्वी दिवश्चितयद्भिरर्कैः ।
> उषासानक्ता विदुषीव विश्वमा हा वहतो मर्त्याय यज्ञम् ॥

> *upa vo haviṣe vandyebhiḥ śūṣaiḥ pra yahvī divaścitayadbhirarkaiḥ |*
> *uṣāsānaktā viduṣīva viśvamā hā vahato martyāya yajñam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].)

> उते योषणे [?] दिव्ये महीन उषासानक्ता सुमृघेव [?] धेनुः ।
> बर्हिषदा पुरुहूते मघोनी आ यज्ञिये सुविताय श्रयेताम् ॥

> *ute yoṣaṇe [?] divye mahīna uṣāsānaktā sumṛgheva [?] dhenuḥ |*
> *barhiṣadā puruhūte maghonī ā yajñiye suvitāya śrayetām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3-6 [?].) In such Ṛks the greater form of the deities Uṣāsānaktā is described. And:

> द्वे विरूपे चरतः स्वर्थे अन्यान्या वत्समुप धापयेते ।
> हरिरन्यस्यां भवति स्वधावाञ्छुक्रो अन्यस्यां ददृशे सुवर्चाः ॥

> *dve virūpe carataḥ svarthe anyānyā vatsamupa dhāpayete |*
> *hariranyasyāṃ bhavati svadhāvāñchukro anyasyāṃ dadṛśe suvarcāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-95-1.)

> पुनः पुनर्जायमाना पुराणी समानं वर्णमभिशुम्भमाना ।
> श्वघ्नीव कृत्नुर्विज आमिनाना मर्तस्य देवी जरयन्त्यायुः ॥

> *punaḥ punarjāyamānā purāṇī samānaṃ varṇamabhiśumbhamānā |*
> *śvaghnīva kṛtnurvija āminānā martasya devī jarayantyāyuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-10.) In such Ṛks, since night and dawn are born again and again, it is also described that they have the form of children. Therefore, for the word *yahvī* either of the two above meanings can be given.

(f) ***naktoṣāsā*** — together with the other epithets of these deities, the epithet *ṛtasya mātarā* is very important.

> द्रवतां त उषसा वाजयन्ती अग्ने वातस्य पथ्याभिरच्छ ।
> यत्सीमञ्जन्ति [?] पूर्व्यं परिभ्रा [?] बन्धुरेव तस्थतुर्दुरोणे [?] ॥

> *dravatāṃ ta uṣasā vājayantī agne vātasya pathyābhiraccha |*
> *yatsīmañjanti [?] pūrvyaṃ paribhrā [?] bandhureva tasthaturduroṇe [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?]; the Ṛk is partly legible.) In this Ṛk the permanent connection of these deities with the sacrifice is described. All the Ṛks that invite them (there are some twenty-five such Ṛks) pray that they should come with the other deities and sit on the *darbha* seat. Moreover, at the time of dawn and also at evening they have a very close relation with the kindled Agni. Hence it is that they are described figuratively as bearing Agni among themselves *(continues on p. 256)*.

### Printed p. 256  (PDF 274)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 7, on *naktoṣāsā*.)*

> नक्तोषासा वर्णमामेम्याने धापयेते शिशुमेकं समीची ।
> द्यावाक्षामा रुक्मो अन्तर्वि भाति देवा अग्निं धारयन् द्रविणोदाम् ॥

> *naktoṣāsā varṇamāmemyāne dhāpayete śiśumekaṃ samīcī |*
> *dyāvākṣāmā rukmo antarvi bhāti devā agniṃ dhārayan draviṇodām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-96-5.) Such Ṛks tell us that these goddesses help in nourishing Agni, who is of the form of a child. Because of this relation they are said to be near to the sacrificers. In the Āprī-sūktas in general the description of this point recurs. For example —

> आ सुष्वयन्ती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योनौ ।
> दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं शुक्रपिशं दधाने ॥

> *ā suṣvayantī yajate upāke uṣāsānaktā sadatāṃ ni yonau |*
> *divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatī surukme adhi śriyaṃ śukrapiśaṃ dadhāne ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-6.) In this Ṛk of the Āprī-sūkta too, the same subject is stated. From this it is understood that the deities Uṣāsānaktā have not a secondary place in the sacrificial acts, but a most important place. This eminence is hinted in the mantra of the Praiṣa-sūkta:

> होता यक्षदुषासानक्ता बृहती सुपेशसा नृग्मं [?] पतिभ्यो योनिं कृण्वाने ।
> सग्मंस्यमाने [?] इन्द्रेण देवैरिदं बर्हिः सीदतां वीतामाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥

> *hotā yakṣaduṣāsānaktā bṛhatī supeśasā nṛgmaṃ [?] patibhyo yoniṃ kṛṇvāne |*
> *sagmaṃsyamāne [?] indreṇa devairidaṃ barhiḥ sīdatāṃ vītāmājyasya hotaryaja ‖*

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-3 [?]; partly legible.) in which Uṣāsānaktā are prayed not only along with Agni but also with Indra and the other deities to sit on the *darbha* seat. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa they are addressed as *ahorātre* ("day and night"). The Nirukta authors have explained the nature of these deities (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?]) [?]; the derivation of the two words *uṣas* and *naktā*, and the nature of these deities, as explained by the Nirukta authors, was told earlier. In the Bṛhaddevatā too they are described thus:

> नक्तोषासा च ये देव्याग्नेय्यो वेव ते स्मृते ।
> श्याव्याग्नेयी हि कालस्य तस्यैषोषाः कलेव तु ॥

> *naktoṣāsā ca ye devyāgneyyo veva te smṛte |*
> *śyāvyāgneyī hi kālasya tasyaiṣoṣāḥ kaleva tu ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-[?].) Both these deities, Uṣas and Naktā, are known to be related to Agni. Of them, Śyāvī (night) (Ni. 1-17 [?]) has a close relation to Agni, and by the Nirukta sentence *uṣaḥ kasmād ucchatīti satyā rātreranta kāle* (Ni. 2-19 [?]) it is known that Uṣas is the last time of the night.

> तमे [?] उच्चैस्तृषा नक्ता नक्तेमां हिमबिन्दुभिः [?] ।
> अपि नामाक्तवर्णेति नैद्ध [?] पूर्वाह्णैरेदं भनेत् [?] ॥

> *tame [?] uccaistṛṣā naktā naktemāṃ himabindubhiḥ [?] |*
> *api nāmāktavarṇeti naiddha [?] pūrvāhṇairedaṃ bhanet [?] ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-[?]; the verse is garbled at this resolution.)

### Printed p. 257  (PDF 275)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 11.)*

Of these two, Uṣas drives away the darkness; Night makes all things wet and pervaded with dew-drops. Or, since it has no definite colour (*varṇa*), the root *añj* is joined in the word *naktā* and gives the sense "of an unmanifest colour" [?].

> सा हि दोषा भवत्याद्यौ निशीथे सा तमस्वते [?] ।
> नाम्ना भवत्युषाश्चैव सैषा प्राग्गुदयाद्रात्रेः ॥

> *sā hi doṣā bhavatyādyau niśīthe sā tamasvate [?] |*
> *nāmnā bhavatyuṣāścaiva saiṣā prāggudayādrātreḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-10.) At the beginning of the night this goddess is called *(pra)doṣā*, at midnight *tamasvatī*, and before sunrise *uṣas*. *Doṣā*, *tamasvatī*, *śyāvī*, *naktā*: all these are read as names of Night in the Nighaṇṭu (Nigh. 1-7 [?]). In the Ṛks and in other places, by the epithet *tantuṃ tatena saṃnayantī* (3-[?]-[?]) [?] and the like, the help of Uṣāsānaktā in the extension of the sacrifice is described.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar page, noted briefly).** *bhandamāne* (root *bhadi kalyāṇe sukhe ca*, *bhvādi*; *laṭ*, *śānac*; *idito num dhātoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-58): *num* augment; *śap* vikaraṇa; *ānaṅ muk* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-82): *muk* augment; the *anudātta* accent of the vikaraṇa is lost since it comes after *ati…*; *tāsyanudāttet* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186): the root accent remains; dual, loc. of *seṭ* [?]), *upāke* (the *antodātta* accent being expected, it becomes *ādyudātta* by *vyatyaya*), *naktoṣasā* (*naktaṃ ca uṣāḥ ca*, *naktoṣasā*; dual; *supāṃ sulug*… (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39): *ākāra* replaces the case-ending; *pūrvasya makārasya lopaḥ* (the *m* of the first member is dropped) and the final of the latter member is lengthened by Vedic usage), *supeśasā* (*śobhanaṃ peśo rūpaṃ yayos te*; *piśi avayave* [?]; *nañsubhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172): the final is *udātta*; *ādyudāttaś ca chandasi* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-[?]): first-syllable *udātta*, hence the accent is first-syllable *udātta*), *mātarā* (*supāṃ sulug*: *ā* replaces the case-ending), *sīdatām* (root *ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*; *loṭ*, third person dual, *tām*; the *ādeśa*; *pāghrādhmā…* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-78): *sīda* replaces *sad*; the accent is *anudātta* by *tāsyanudāttet* … ; since it stands at the beginning of the pāda, there is no *nighāta*). ‖ 7 ‖

#### Ṛk 8

### Printed p. 258  (PDF 276)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> मन्द्रजिह्वा जुगुर्वणी होतारा दैव्या कवी ।
> यज्ञं नो यक्षतामिमं सिध्रमद्य दिविस्पृशम् ॥ ८ ॥

> *mandrajihvā jugurvaṇī hotārā daivyā kavī |*
> *yajñaṃ no yakṣatāmimaṃ sidhramadya divispṛśam ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> मन्द्रऽजिह्वा । जुगुर्वणी इति । होतारा । दैव्या । कवी इति ।
> यज्ञम् । नः । यक्षताम् । इमम् । सिध्रम् । अद्य । दिविऽस्पृशम् ॥ ८ ॥

> *mandra 'jihvā | jugurvaṇī iti | hotārā | daivyā | kavī iti |*
> *yajñam | naḥ | yakṣatām | imam | sidhram | adya | divi 'spṛśam ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *the two divine hotṛs, whose tongues delight the gods, who favour the praising sacrificers, wise, are to perform today this our fruit-bearing sacrifice that touches heaven.* Small type; many words doubtful)

> मन्द्रजिह्वा देवानां मादयित्र्यौ जिह्वे ज्वाले ययोस्तौ [?] । जुगुर्वणी भृशं गृणतां स्तुवतां यजमानानाम् [?] गृणातेर्यङ्लुगन्तात् क्विप् छान्दसो रूपसिद्धिः [?] । कस्मिन्नुपपदे वनसे [?] … छन्दसि वनसनरक्षमथानीत्य [?] प्रत्ययः । कवी मेधाविनौ क्रान्तदर्शिनौ दैव्या होतारा देवसम्बन्धिनौ होतारौ अयं च मध्यमस्थानेऽन्तेभ्यो [?] सिध्रं फलसाधकभूतम् । सिधेः स्वायतमित्यादिना रक् [?] । दिविस्पृशं द्युलोकवासिनो देवान् स्पृशन्तं [?] त्रैदशीषु स्वीक्रियमाणत्वादिति भावः [?] । उद्दशं [?] नोऽस्मदीयमिमं यज्ञमद्य यक्षतां अनुतिष्ठतां पूजयतां [?] । सम्यग्भूर्वाहयतामित्यर्थः ॥

> *mandrajihvā devānāṃ mādayitryau jihve jvāle yayostau [?] | jugurvaṇī bhṛśaṃ gṛṇatāṃ stuvatāṃ yajamānānām [?] gṛṇāteryaṅlugantāt kvip chāndaso rūpasiddhiḥ [?] | kasminnupapade vanase [?] … chandasi vanasanarakṣamathānītya [?] pratyayaḥ | kavī medhāvinau krāntadarśinau daivyā hotārā devasambandhinau hotārau ayaṃ ca madhyamasthāne 'ntebhyo [?] sidhraṃ phalasādhakabhūtam | sidheḥ svāyatamityādinā rak [?] | divispṛśaṃ dyulokavāsino devān spṛśantaṃ [?] traidaśīṣu svīkriyamāṇatvāditi bhāvaḥ [?] | uddaśaṃ [?] no 'smadīyamimaṃ yajñamadya yakṣatāṃ anutiṣṭhatāṃ pūjayatāṃ [?] | samyagbhūrvāhayatāmityarthaḥ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *mandrajihvā* — those whose flames (tongues) give delight to the gods; *jugurvaṇī* — who favour the praising sacrificers; *kavī* — the wise; *daivyā hotārā* — the two forms of Agni who call the gods (to the sacrifice); *sidhram* — fruit-giving; *divispṛśam* — touching the world of heaven (joining the gods); *naḥ imaṃ yajñam* — this our sacrifice; *adya* — now; *yakṣatām* — let them perform.

**Bhāvārtha.** May the two forms of Agni, whose flames give delight to the gods, who favour the praising sacrificers, and who are fruit-giving, now perform this our sacrifice, which touches heaven and joins the gods.

### Printed p. 259  (PDF 277)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 11.)*

**English Translation (as printed).** May the two pleasing-tongued receivers of praise, the divine and sage invokers (of the gods), officiate to-day at this our sacrifice, which confers (rewards) and attains heaven.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***daivyā hotārā*** — देवसम्बन्धिनौ होतारौ । अयं च मध्यमः (*devasambandhinau hotārau | ayaṃ ca madhyamaḥ*) [?]: "the two *hotṛs* related to the gods; one is Agni of the earth and the other the Agni of the middle region (atmosphere)", Sāyaṇa has explained. Some scholars, following their own opinions, have shown different views of the meaning: Geldner takes the two as the sacrificer's *hotṛ* and his Agni; Haug as the *hotṛ* and the *adhvaryu*; Oldenberg as the *hotṛ* and his assistant the Maitrāvaruṇa. None of these is harmonious.

The principal duty of these *hotṛs* is the performance of the sacrifice, as told in *yajñaṃ no yakṣatām imam* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-142-8) and in *devāṃ yajantāv ṛtuthā* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?]). This duty is attributed to the human *hotṛ*, in the case of whom, who is fit for praise, and to Agni, who is addressed in a figurative sense. In the same way —

> देव्या होतारा प्रथमा सुवाचा मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै ।
> प्रचोदयन्ता विदथेषु कारू प्राचीनं ज्योतिः प्रदिशा दिशन्ता ॥

> *devyā hotārā prathamā suvācā mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai |*
> *pracodayantā vidatheṣu kārū prācīnaṃ jyotiḥ pradiśā diśantā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-7.) In this Ṛk, by "those who impel the sacrifice, or who promote it", the opinion of some scholars is hinted that these are human *hotṛs*. Likewise (they say) both epithets in the pair of epithets apply equally to both, and certain epithets also apply to both together; but those that apply to the divine *hotṛ* Agni describe the duties of Agni. For example —

> देव्या होतारा प्रथमा न्यञ्जे सप्त पृक्षासः स्वधया मदन्ति ।
> ऋतं शंसन्त ऋतमित्त आहुरनु व्रतं व्रतपा दीध्यानाः ॥

> *devyā hotārā prathamā nyañje sapta pṛkṣāsaḥ svadhayā madanti |*
> *ṛtaṃ śaṃsanta ṛtamitta āhuranu vrataṃ vratapā dīdhyānāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-[?].) In this Ṛk there is no doubt that the epithet *prathamā* belongs to the divine *hotṛ* Agni, as the Kannada says.

### Printed p. 260  (PDF 278)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

In Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?] [?], "*hotā manurhitaḥ*" is an epithet of Agni. The difference [?] between these two *hotṛs* is stated in the Praiṣa-sūkta as follows:

> होता यक्षद्दैव्या होतारा मन्द्रा पोतारा कवी प्रचेतसा । स्पृष्टम् [?] … इषा स्थिभिर्गोर्तमन्य ऊर्जा सवेस्नेमं यज्ञं दिवि देवेषु धत्तां वीतामाज्यस्य होतर्यज ।

> *hotā yakṣaddaivyā hotārā mandrā potārā kavī pracetasā | spṛṣṭam [?] … iṣā sthibhirgortamanya ūrjā savesnemaṃ yajñaṃ divi deveṣu dhattāṃ vītāmājyasya hotaryaja |*

(Tai. Brā. 3-[?]-[?]-[?]; partly legible.) In this sentence one *hotṛ* is to accept the sacrifice with the oblation in the form of food, and the other to establish this sacrifice among the gods in heaven; the difference between the human *hotṛ* and the divine *hotṛ* Agni is thus shown, it says. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

> दैव्या होतारा यजति प्राणापानौ वै दैव्या होतारा प्राणापानावेव तत्प्रीणाति प्राणापानौ यजमाने दधाति ।

> *daivyā hotārā yajati prāṇāpānau vai daivyā hotārā prāṇāpānāveva tatprīṇāti prāṇāpānau yajamāne dadhāti |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-[?].) Having thus told the identity of these *hotṛs* with *prāṇa* and *apāna*, it says that the one who recites this mantra gives the sacrificer a long life, the satisfaction of *prāṇa* and *apāna*. In the Nirukta:

> दैव्या होतारा दैव्यौ होतारावयं चाग्निरसौ च मध्यमः [?] ।

> *daivyā hotārā daivyau hotārāvayaṃ cāgnirasau ca madhyamaḥ [?] |*

(Ni. 8-[?].) Thus, by the basis-sentences supporting Sāyaṇa's meaning, the *hotṛs* are the earthly Agni and the Agni of the atmosphere. The Bṛhaddevatā too gives the same meaning:

> दैव्याविति तु होतारावग्निः पार्थिवमध्यमौ ।
> दिव्यादग्नेर्हि जज्ञाते दैव्यौ तेनेह जन्मना ॥

> *daivyāviti tu hotārāvagniḥ pārthivamadhyamau |*
> *divyādagnerhi jajñāte daivyau teneha janmanā ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-11.) These two *hotṛs* are said to be the earthly and the middle (atmospheric) Agnis.

***jugurvaṇī*** — भृशं गृणतां यजमानानां संभक्तारौ (*bhṛśaṃ gṛṇatāṃ yajamānānāṃ saṃbhaktārau*) ("who favour the praising sacrificers abundantly"): meaning "those who favour the sacrificers that praise".

***sidhram*** — फलसाधनभूतम् (*phalasādhanabhūtam*): "that which gives fruit" (*phaladāyaka*). The Nirukta author:

> द्यावा नः पृथिवी इमं सिध्रमद्य दिविस्पृशम् । यज्ञं देवेषु यच्छताम् ॥

> *dyāvā naḥ pṛthivī imaṃ sidhramadya divispṛśam | yajñaṃ deveṣu yacchatām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].)

### Printed p. 261  (PDF 279)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 12 [?].)*

Citing this Ṛk, he explains the word *sidhram* as "means" (*sādhana*). In the Ṛk in hand it means "the sacrifice, which brings fruit".

***mandrajihvā*** — देवानां मादयित्र्यौ जिह्वे ज्वाले (*devānāṃ mādayitryau jihve jvāle*): "those whose flames delight the gods". The words *mandra* and *mandrajihvā* have been explained in the Special Topics of Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?]. Since the word *mandrajihvā* cannot be an epithet of the human *hotṛ*, it indicates that the *daivyā hotārā* must be two forms of Agni; only then is this epithet in harmony.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; grammar page, noted briefly).** *mandrajihvā* (root *madi stutimodamadasvapnakāntigatiṣu* [as printed *madi harṣe*?]; *sphāyitañcivañci…* (Uṇ. Sū. 2-[?]): suffix *rak*; by the suffix-accent the end is *udātta*; *mandrā jihvā yayoḥ te mandrajihvau*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1): the first member keeps its accent; *supāṃ sulug* gives *ā* for the case-ending), *jugurvaṇī* (root *gṝ śabde*; in the repeated sense *yaṅ*; *dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-22); *yaṅ* is *luk*-dropped in Vedic usage [?], and by *chandasi* *jugur* results; the root *van saṃbhaktau*; when *jugur* is the *upapada*, *chandasi vanasana…* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-27 [?]): suffix *iṇ*; the form *jugurvaṇī*; *āṭ kuṣṇājjāt* [?]: the root takes *ṇatva*; dual), *hotārā* (root *hu dānādanayoḥ*; suffix *tṛc* in the agent sense; *nityād vā* [?]: first-syllable *udātta*; dual; *supāṃ sulug*), *daivyā* (*devasya idaṃ daivyam*; suffix *yat* in the sense of *devād yañ…*; *taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ* (Pā. #### Ṛk 9

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> शुचिर्देवेष्वर्पिता होत्रा मरुत्सु भारती ।
> इळा सरस्वती मही बर्हिः सीदन्तु यज्ञियाः ॥ ९ ॥

> *śucirdeveṣvarpitā hotrā marutsu bhāratī |*
> *iḷā sarasvatī mahī barhiḥ sīdantu yajñiyāḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> शुचिः । देवेषु । अर्पिता । होत्रा । मरुत्ऽसु । भारती ।
> इळा । सरस्वती । मही । बर्हिः । सीदन्तु । यज्ञियाः ॥ ९ ॥

> *śuciḥ | deveṣu | arpitā | hotrā | marut 'su | bhāratī |*
> *iḷā | sarasvatī | mahī | barhiḥ | sīdantu | yajñiyāḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *Bhāratī, pure and fixed among the shining gods, the praisers, the Maruts or the priests, with Iḷā (terrestrial speech) and Sarasvatī (speech of the middle region), the great ones fit for sacrifice, are to sit on the spread grass.* Small type; many words doubtful)

> शुचिः शुद्धा मरुत्सु विरुद्धलक्षणेषु [?] देवेषु द्योतनशीलेषु स्तोतृषु मरुत्सु ऋत्विक्षु वा अर्पिता नियता होत्रा होमनिष्पादिका भारती भरतस्यादित्यस्य सम्बन्धिनी द्युस्थाना वाक् [?] तथेळा पार्थिवी प्रैषादिरूपा मही सरस्वती । सर इत्युदकनाम [?] तद्वती स्तनितादिरूपा माध्यमिका च वाक् । … स्थानवागभिमानिदेवता यज्ञिया यज्ञार्हाः सत्त्वो [?] बर्हिः स्तीर्णं सीदन्तु । उपविशन्तु ॥

> *śuciḥ śuddhā marutsu viruddhalakṣaṇeṣu [?] deveṣu dyotanaśīleṣu stotṛṣu marutsu ṛtvikṣu vā arpitā niyatā hotrā homaniṣpādikā bhāratī bharatasyādityasya sambandhinī dyusthānā vāk [?] tatheḷā pārthivī praiṣādirūpā mahī sarasvatī | sara ityudakanāma [?] tadvatī stanitādirūpā mādhyamikā ca vāk | … sthānavāgabhimānidevatā yajñiyā yajñārhāḥ sattvo [?] barhiḥ stīrṇaṃ sīdantu | upaviśantu ‖*

### Printed p. 263  (PDF 281)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 11 [?].)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *marutsu* — among the immortal; *deveṣu* — among the shining ones, (that is) either among the praisers, or among the Maruts, or among the priests; *arpitā* — fixed; *śuciḥ* — pure; *hotrā* — accomplisher of the offering; *bhāratī* — the goddess of speech belonging to the world of heaven and to the Āditya; *iḷā* — the goddess of speech belonging to the earth; *mahī* — of great form; *sarasvatī* — the goddess of speech belonging to the middle, that is the atmospheric, world; *yajñiyāḥ* — fit for the sacrifice; *barhiḥ* — on the *darbha* seat; *sīdantu* — let them sit.

**Bhāvārtha.** May the three goddesses of speech — Bhāratī, of heaven and of the Āditya; Iḷā, of the earth; and Sarasvatī, of the middle world — pure, fixed among the immortal, shining praisers, Maruts or priests, the accomplisher of the offering, of great form, come fit for the sacrifice and sit on our *darbha* seat in the sacrificial house.

**English Translation (as printed).** May the pure Hotra, placed among the gods, and Bharati, among the Maruts, and may the adorable Ila, Saraswati, and Mahi, sit down upon the sacred grass.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** In this Ṛk a group of three goddesses is addressed and prayed to favour the sacrifice. Except the present sūkta and Sūkta 188 of this Maṇḍala, all the other Āprī-sūktas also place these goddesses together and name them collectively as *tisro devīḥ*. The three are *Iḷā*, *Sarasvatī* and *Bhāratī*. There is considerable disagreement about the nature of these goddesses. In this sūkta the goddess Bhāratī has the epithets *hotrā*, *śuciḥ* and *arpitā* (*marutsu, deveṣu*), and the goddess Sarasvatī the word *mahī*. In some sūktas the word *mahī* is not an epithet but is used as a synonym of the goddess Bhāratī. Whether the nature of these goddesses can now be determined precisely may be considered by taking the Veda and the like as authority. If we look at the mantra in the Praiṣa-sūkta, which gathers the main points of the Āprī-sūktas and addresses these goddesses —

### Printed p. 264  (PDF 282)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

> होतायक्षत्तिस्रो देवीरपसामपस्तमा अच्छिद्रमद्यैदमुपस्तन्वतां [?] ।
> देवेभ्यो देवीर्देवमपो नियन्त्याज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥

> *hotāyakṣattisro devīrapasāmapastamā acchidramadyaidamupastanvatāṃ [?] |*
> *devebhyo devīrdevamapo niyantyājyasya hotaryaja ‖*

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-[?]-[?]; partly legible.) In the original it is only *tisro devīḥ*. Explaining it, the commentator says: इडा सरस्वती भारतीत्येवमुपास्त्रीः [?] अनुप्रयाजदेव्यस्त्रिरूपमग्निं दैव्यो होता यजतु (*iḍā sarasvatī bhāratītyevamupāstrīḥ [?] anuprayājadevyastrirūpamagniṃ daivyo hotā yajatu*) [?]: Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī, the three *anuprayāja* goddesses, reflect Agni; and *apasām apastamā* — "the most active of the active ones" (*karmavatīnām madhye atiśayena karmavatī*), says the epithet, "exceedingly active". In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

> तिस्रो देवीर्यजति प्राणो वा अ[पा]नो [?] व्यानस्तिस्रो देव्यस्ता एव तत्प्रीणाति ता यजमाने दधाति ।

> *tisro devīryajati prāṇo vā a[pā]no [?] vyānastisro devyastā eva tatprīṇāti tā yajamāne dadhāti |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-[?].) Thus it declares the identity of these three deities with the three life-principles *prāṇa*, *apāna* and *vyāna*. The Nirukta author, citing the Ṛk *ā no yajñam* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-8), gives this explanation:

> आ भारती भारतीभिः [?] … भरत आदित्यस्तस्य भा इळा च मनुष्यवती चेतयन्ती तिस्रो देव्यो बर्हिरिदं सुखं सरस्वती च सुकमाना [?] आसीदन्ते [?] ।

> *ā bhāratī bhāratībhiḥ [?] … bharata ādityastasya bhā iḷā ca manuṣyavatī cetayantī tisro devyo barhiridaṃ sukhaṃ sarasvatī ca sukamānā [?] āsīdante [?] |*

(Ni. 8-[?].) "Bhāratī: the radiance of Bharata (the sun); Iḷā; Sarasvatī: these three come and adorn the *barhis*." In the Bṛhaddevatā:

> तिस्रस्तु देव्यो याः प्रोक्तास्त्रिस्थानेष्वेव सा तु वाक् [?] ।
> त्रिविधेनैव सैतेन नाम्ना ज्योतिष्मतीश्विनि [?] ।
> अग्नेर्मेनानुगेळा तु मध्यमा प्राप्ता सरस्वती ।
> अमूर्तिस्त्वाथ लोकं तु भारती भवति ह्यसौ [?] ।
> स्यैषा तु त्रिविधा वाग्वै दिवि भूम्यां च [?] …
> व्यस्ता चैव समस्ता च भजन्ते [?] ह्यग्निमानसि [?] ॥

> *tisrastu devyo yāḥ proktāstristhāneṣveva sā tu vāk [?] |*
> *trividhenaiva saitena nāmnā jyotiṣmatīśvini [?] |*
> *agnermenānugeḷā tu madhyamā prāptā sarasvatī |*
> *amūrtistvātha lokaṃ tu bhāratī bhavati hyasau [?] |*
> *syaiṣā tu trividhā vāgvai divi bhūmyāṃ ca [?] …*
> *vyastā caiva samastā ca bhajante [?] hyagnimānasi [?] ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-[?] to 2-[?].) *Tisro devīḥ* are the goddesses of speech who are in the three worlds. [The three forms of speech are explained in Bṛ. De. 2-7 to 2-8 [?].]

> आयं प्रयोगस्त्वेतेषां ज्योतिषां त्रिषु वर्तताम् [?] ।

> *āyaṃ prayogastveteṣāṃ jyotiṣāṃ triṣu vartatām [?] |*

(Bṛ. De. 2-[?].)

### Printed p. 265  (PDF 283)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 11 [?].)*

So the different goddesses in the three worlds are the manifestations of one goddess of speech. Of these Iḷā followed the earthly Agni; Sarasvatī passed through the middle world; and Bhāratī is established in heaven. Yet —

> देव्यस्तिस्रः श्रितास्त्वग्निं त्वष्टा चैत्वेदाश्रयः [?] ।

> *devyastisraḥ śritāstvagniṃ tvaṣṭā caitvedāśrayaḥ [?] |*

(Bṛ. De. 1-106 [?].) as this sentence says, the goddesses of the three worlds all serve the earthly Agni; thus everything is brought to a close with reference to Agni.

***mahī*** — *mahatī*, "of great form"; an epithet of Sarasvatī. In some places *mahī* has been interpreted as a separate deity; in the opinion of others it is a common epithet of the three goddesses. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3-8 and 9-5-8 [?] (Āprī-sūktas) it is an epithet of *uṣāsānaktā*. Moreover,

> इळा सरस्वती मही तिस्रो देवीर्मयोभुवः ।
> बर्हिः सीदन्त्वस्रिधः ॥

> *iḷā sarasvatī mahī tisro devīrmayobhuvaḥ |*
> *barhiḥ sīdantvasridhaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-9.) In this Ṛk and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-31 [?] likewise, since there is no mention of *bhāratī* [in the same sequence], Sāyaṇa says that *mahī* is a synonym of the goddess Bhāratī. In the Ṛk in hand and in —

> भारती पवमानस्य सरस्वतीळा मही ।
> इमं नो यज्ञमा गमन्तिस्रो देवीः सुपेशसः ॥

> *bhāratī pavamānasya sarasvatīḷā mahī |*
> *imaṃ no yajñamā gamantisro devīḥ supeśasaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-5-8 [?].) it is likewise an epithet.

***iḷā*** — in the Bṛhaddevatā, *agnim evānugeḷā* (2-13 [?]): "Iḷā followed the earthly Agni"; and in the Ṛk —

> प्र दीधितिर्विश्ववारा जिगाति होतारमिळः प्रथमं यजध्यै ।
> अच्छा नमोभिर्वृषभं वन्दध्यै स देवान् यक्षदिषितो यजीयान् ॥

> *pra dīdhitirviśvavārā jigāti hotāramiḷaḥ prathamaṃ yajadhyai |*
> *acchā namobhirvṛṣabhaṃ vandadhyai sa devān yakṣadiṣito yajīyān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-3.) the word *iḷā* is taken as food in the form of oblation; and since in Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-1-4 [?] the epithet *ghṛtahastā* and in 10-70 [?] the epithet *ghṛtapadī* occur, it appears that the meaning "cow" can be given to *iḷā*. Perhaps for this very reason,

---

### Printed p. 266  (PDF 284)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

> उत्तानायामव भरा चिकित्वान्त्सद्यः प्रवीता वृषणं जजान ।
> अरुषस्तूपो रुशदस्य पाज इळायास्पुत्रो वयुने ऽजनिष्ट ॥

> *uttānāyāmava bharā cikitvāntsadyaḥ pravītā vṛṣaṇaṃ jajāna |*
> *aruṣastūpo ruśadasya pāja iḷāyāsputro vayune 'janiṣṭa ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-29-3.) in this Ṛk Agni is called the son of Iḷā.

***bhāratī*** — the Nirukta says "the radiance of Āditya" (*bharata ādityaḥ tasya bhāḥ*). The scholar Macdonell, in his *Vedic Mythology*, says (p. 87) that it is the oblation resorted to by the Bharata clan, and Grassmann that it is the goddess of speech; it may also be taken as belonging to Agni.

> तस्मा अग्निर्भारतः शर्म यंसज्ज्योक्पश्यात्सूर्यमुच्चरन्तम् ।
> य इन्द्राय सुनवामेत्याह नरे नर्याय नृतमाय नृणाम् ॥

> *tasmā agnirbhārataḥ śarma yaṃsajjyokpaśyātsūryamuccarantam |*
> *ya indrāya sunavāmetyāha nare naryāya nṛtamāya nṛṇām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-25-4.) since in this Ṛk *bhārataḥ* is an epithet of Agni, some think that the deity related to him may be named *bhāratī*.

***sarasvatī*** — सर इत्युदकनाम । तद्वती स्तनितादिरूपा माध्यमिका च वाक् (*sara ityudakanāma | tadvatī stanitādirūpā mādhyamikā ca vāk*): "*sara* means water; the possessor of it, in the form of thunder and the like, is the speech of the middle region". The sense of *sara* is "water"; the goddess of speech belonging to the atmosphere, who has water and sounds such as thunder, is explained as a form (of the three). Some say *sarasvatī* is a grouping of the deities. Or (others) because *devyas tisraḥ śritās tv agnim* (Bṛ. De. 1-106) says that these three resort to Agni, and Agni has three forms in earth, atmosphere and heaven; since Bhāratī is said to be the sun's radiance and Sarasvatī the deity of thunder and lightning, and Iḷā has a direct relation to Agni, some hold that these three are forms of Agni. About *traidrūpam agnim* in the explanation of the Praiṣa-sūkta, it was said above.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 9; grammar page, noted briefly).** *arpitā* (*umbhādīnāṃ ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-170) [?]: first-syllable *udātta* accent), *iḷā* (root *iḍa stutau*; by Vedic usage the root takes *ḷa*; *kvip ca*: suffix *kvip*; the root accent; *ṭāp* even after a consonant-ending stem, as in *yathā vācā diśā* [?]), *sarasvatī* (root *sṛ gatau*; suffix *asun*; since *saras* ends in the *sit* suffix it is *ādyudātta*; *saraḥ asyāsti iti*, *tadasyāsti*: suffix *matup*; by *tasau matvarthe* [?] the stem has the *bha* designation, so *rutva* and the like do not apply) …

> अरम् अलम् । त्मनात्मना । पुरु बहुक्रियाविशेषणमेतत् । … उदकं त्वष्टा वृष्ट्यादेः कर्ता [?] । त्वष्टा तोर्णमत्स्य [?] … नाभा नाभ्यां वृष्टेर्बन्धके [?] मेघस्य नाभिस्थाने [?] … पुष्पये … पोषाय … वि ष्यतु उत्कृलक्षणमुदकं वृष्टिं मुञ्चतु [?] । विविधं गमयतु ॥

> *aram alam | tmanātmanā | puru bahukriyāviśeṣaṇametat | … udakaṃ tvaṣṭā vṛṣṭyādeḥ kartā [?] | tvaṣṭā torṇamatsya [?] … nābhā nābhyāṃ vṛṣṭerbandhake [?] meghasya nābhisthāne [?] … puṣpaye … poṣāya … vi ṣyatu utkṛlakṣaṇamudakaṃ vṛṣṭiṃ muñcatu [?] | vividhaṃ gamayatu ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *tvaṣṭā* — Agni, who is of the form of lightning (*vidyud-rūpa*) and brings about rain [?]; *asmayuḥ* — being kindly disposed to us; *naḥ* — for our; *poṣāya* — nourishment; *rāye* — prosperity; *nābhā* — from the middle (navel) of the cloud; (or *naḥ* — our; *nābhā* — at the *uttaravedi*, the navel of the sacrifice); *rāye* — for wealth such as cattle; *poṣāya* — for protection; *tat* — that well-known; *turīpam* — quickly falling; *adbhutam* — wonderful; *puru vāram* — sufficient for many creatures, or very abundant; *tmanā puru* — doing much good of itself, the rain; *vi syatu* — let him send down in many ways.

**Bhāvārtha.** May Agni, who is in the form of lightning, being kindly disposed to us, send down in abundance, for our nourishment and for our prosperity, the rain, famous and from the centre of the cloud, quickly falling, wonderful, needed by many creatures, and very abundant.

**English Translation (as printed).** May Twashtri, favourably disposed towards us, send to us, for our nourishment and prosperity, the quick (falling) wonderful, abundant (water), in the centre (of the cloud, effecting) of itself much (good).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***tvaṣṭā*** — *tvaṣṭā* is explained in the account of the *navana-prayāja* [?]; in the Praiṣa-sūkta, the nature of this deity is told by four or five epithets.

### Printed p. 269  (PDF 287)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 12 [?].)*

The passages of the Praiṣa-sūkta that give his individual views about the deity Tvaṣṭṛ are these. It addresses only the deity concerned with the Āprī-sūkta:

> होता यक्षत्त्वष्टारमजिष्ट्वाम् [?] अपाकं रेतोधां विश्वरूपं यशोधां ।
> पुरुरूपमकामकर्शनं सुपोषैः पोषैः स्यात्त्वष्टा वीरो वीर्येणास्य होतर्यज ॥

> *hotā yakṣattvaṣṭāramajiṣṭvām [?] apākaṃ retodhāṃ viśvarūpaṃ yaśodhāṃ |*
> *pururūpamakāmakarśanaṃ supoṣaiḥ poṣaiḥ syāttvaṣṭā vīro vīryeṇāsya hotaryaja ‖*

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-6-3 [?]; partly legible.) In this mantra the epithets are *ajiṣṭnu* [?], *apākam*, *retodhām*, *viśvarūpam*, *yaśodhām*, *pururūpam* and *akāmakarśanam*. Of these:

*ajiṣṭnum* — "without *jaiṣṭnya*"; without fickleness, steady, not fickle but steady.

*apākam* — *abālam, prājñam*: "not a child, but wise".

*retodhām* — *putrādibījasya yajamāne dhārayitāram*: "who plants the seed of sons and the like in the sacrificer".

*viśvavasum* [as printed; the Praiṣa has *viśvarūpam*] — *vividhakīrtiyuktam*: "endowed with manifold fame".

*yaśodhām* — *yajamānasya yaśaso dhārayitāram*: "who makes the sacrificer a sharer of glory".

*pururūpam* — *bahurūpam*: "having many kinds of form".

*akāmakarśanam* — *kāmānām anāśayitāram*: "who does not destroy desires; who fulfils the sacrificer's desires".

These epithets show the individual nature of Tvaṣṭṛ. The Nirukta author, showing the derivation of the word *tvaṣṭṛ* (Ni. 8-[?]) says: *tvaṣṭā tūrṇam aśnuta iti nairuktāḥ; tviṣer vā syād dīptikarmaṇaḥ; tvakṣater vā syāt karotikarmaṇaḥ* [?] — "he pervades quickly: so say the etymologists; or from *tviṣ*, 'to shine'; or from *tvakṣ* [?], 'to do'". From these derivations it is understood that Tvaṣṭṛ is one who pervades quickly, who shines, and who is the maker. To show to which world this deity belongs he says: माध्यमिकस्त्वष्टेत्याहुर्मध्यमे च स्थाने समाम्नातेः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः (*mādhyamikastvaṣṭetyāhurmadhyame ca sthāne samāmnāteḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ*) [?] — some say he belongs to the group of the deities of the atmosphere (*mādhyamika*), and Śākapūṇi says he is Agni; he gives these opinions. In the Bṛhaddevatā, approving the first view,

> त्वष्टा रूपविकर्ता च योऽसौ माध्यमिके गणे ।
> स्तुतः स च निपातेन सूक्तं तस्य विद्यते ॥

> *tvaṣṭā rūpavikartā ca yo 'sau mādhyamike gaṇe |*
> *stutaḥ sa ca nipātena sūktaṃ tasya vidyate ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-33 [?].) this verse says that he belongs to the group of the deities of the middle world. Before it:

> त्वष्टा तु यस्यायमेव पार्थिवोऽग्निरिति स्तुतिः [?] ।
> पार्थिवस्यास्य वर्चः स्यात् कस्माद्भ्यक्तं चात्मवेषु च [?] ।
> त्विषेस्तु च त्विषेर्वा स्यात् तोर्णमत्स्न्वेव [?] वा ।
> कर्मसत्त्वारोऽवेति तेन नाम्नैतदुच्यते [?] ।
> येनः सहस्रतमो रश्मीरिनेद्रमुपाश्रिताः [?] ।
> सोऽपि त्वष्टारमेवाग्निं परं तेहज्ञ [?] यज्ञ्ञदु [?] ॥

> *tvaṣṭā tu yasyāyameva pārthivo 'gniriti stutiḥ [?] |*
> *pārthivasyāsya varcaḥ syāt kasmādbhyaktaṃ cātmaveṣu ca [?] |*
> *tviṣestu ca tviṣervā syāt torṇamatsnveva [?] vā |*
> *karmasattvāro 'veti tena nāmnaitaducyate [?] |*
> *yenaḥ sahasratamo raśmīrinedramupāśritāḥ [?] |*
> *so 'pi tvaṣṭāramevāgniṃ paraṃ tehajña [?] yajññadu [?] ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-[?] to 2-[?]; garbled at this resolution.) What the Kannada says of these verses: "whatever praise there is of the earthly Agni is addressed to Tvaṣṭṛ; there is also a suggestion in some places that he is a deity related to the earth. Moreover the authors of the Bṛhaddevatā describe him as a part of Agni [?]. Then the Nirukta's derivation of the word *tvaṣṭṛ* is stated [?]. It is also described that he pervades the thousand-rayed honey [?] of the sun and the other world and the earth [?]. In the matter of this deity the Bṛhaddevatā mainly approves the opinion of Śākapūṇi given in the Nirukta. In the Nighaṇṭu, Tvaṣṭṛ is classed first with the Āprī deities (Nigh. 1-[?]), then with the deities of the atmosphere (5-4) and also with those of heaven (5-6)." *(This paragraph read at low confidence.)*

The story of Tvaṣṭṛ and the sage Dadhyañc has been given in the Special Topics of Sūkta 1-116. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

> त्वष्टारं यजति वाग्वै त्वष्टा वाग्घीदं सर्वम् । क्षाप्नोति [?] वाचेवेन [?] तत्प्रीणाति वाचं यजमाने दधाति ।

> *tvaṣṭāraṃ yajati vāgvai tvaṣṭā vāgghīdaṃ sarvam | kṣāpnoti [?] vācevena [?] tatprīṇāti vācaṃ yajamāne dadhāti |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-[?].) this sentence shows the identity of Tvaṣṭṛ and Speech (*vāc*): this is one opinion.

> ये इमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भुवनानि विश्वा ।
> तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान् देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् ॥

> *ye ime dyāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpairapiṃśadbhuvanāni viśvā |*
> *tamadya hotariṣito yajīyān devaṃ tvaṣṭāramiha yakṣi vidvān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-9.) In this Ṛk it is told that this deity has a divine birth, and that therefore even at the time of creation he is praised as "former, ancient". The idea that Tvaṣṭṛ is very ancient —

### Printed p. 271  (PDF 289)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 12 [?].)*

> इह त्वष्टारमग्रियं विश्वरूपमुपह्वये ।
> अस्माकमस्तु केवलः ॥

> *iha tvaṣṭāramagriyaṃ viśvarūpamupahvaye |*
> *asmākamastu kevalaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-10.)

> त्वष्टारमग्रजां गोपां पुरोयावानमा हुवे ।
> इन्दुरिन्द्रो वृषा हरिः पवमानः प्रजापतिः ॥

> *tvaṣṭāramagrajāṃ gopāṃ puroyāvānamā huve |*
> *indurindro vṛṣā hariḥ pavamānaḥ prajāpatiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-5-9 [?].) By such Ṛks it is understood through the epithets *agriya* and *agraja* ("first-born").

> त्वष्टा रूपाणि हि प्रभुः पशून्विश्वान्त्समानजे ।
> तेषां नः स्फातिमा यज ॥

> *tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi hi prabhuḥ paśūnviśvāntsamānaje |*
> *teṣāṃ naḥ sphātimā yaja ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-64-9 [?].)

> त्वष्टा रूपाणि विकरोति ।

> *tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi vikaroti |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-3-7-1 [?].) By such sentences the role of Tvaṣṭṛ as the maker of forms is declared. Of these, for him the epithet *viśvarūpa* ("having all forms") is also there (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-10).

***turīpam*** — considering only the derivation of the word *turīpa*, it is *tūrṇaṃ vyāpi*: "that which pervades quickly"; the meaning is "what is quick, falls swiftly or pervades". According to the commentator it is "rain" or "seed": in this Ṛk the commentator makes it an epithet of rain. And Ṛ. Saṃ.

> तन्न स्तुरीपमध पोषयित्नु देव त्वष्टर्वि रराणः स्यस्व ।
> यतो वीरः कर्मण्यः सुदक्षो युक्तग्रावा जायते देवकामः ॥

> *tanna sturīpamadha poṣayitnu deva tvaṣṭarvi rarāṇaḥ syasva |*
> *yato vīraḥ karmaṇyaḥ sudakṣo yuktagrāvā jāyate devakāmaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].) in this Ṛk the commentator explains the word *turīpa* as "seed" (*retas*). In the Praiṣa-sūkta the epithet *retodhām* is used of Tvaṣṭṛ, which gives the same sense. For example:

> त्वष्ट्रे स्वाहा । त्वष्ट्रे तुरीपाय स्वाहा । त्वष्ट्रे पुरुरूपाय स्वाहा ।

> *tvaṣṭre svāhā | tvaṣṭre turīpāya svāhā | tvaṣṭre pururūpāya svāhā |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-3-[?].) In such Saṃhitā sentences the identity of Tvaṣṭṛ and *turīpa* is declared; the commentator takes *turīpa* as "seed". The scholar Keith translates this mantra "To Tvashtra, the Seminal". Or, since he belongs to the middle world, it may be said that he is the cause of the falling of rain.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 10; grammar page, noted briefly).** *aram* (*vālamūla…* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-[?]): *ra* is the substitute for the *la*; *alam* is the natural form), *tmanā* (*ātmanā*; in mantras *tmanātmanā*… *ātmanaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-141): the *a* of *ātman* is dropped), *tvaṣṭā* (root *tviṣ dīptau*, or *tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe*; suffix *tṛn* in the agent sense; being *nit* it is *ādyudātta*; *skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-29) drops the *k*; nominative singular), *poṣāya* (root *puṣa puṣṭau*; *halaś ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-121): suffix *ghañ*; *pugantalaghūpadhasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86): *guṇa*; by the suffix, the first-syllable *udātta*; dative singular), *vi syatu* (root *ṣo antakarmaṇi*; *loṭ*, third person singular, ending *ti*; *ṭi*, *tu*; *ṣatva*… *vyatyaya*: *śyan* vikaraṇa [*divādibhyaḥ śyan*]; *oter ... śyati* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-67): loss of the root vowel; *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64): *sa*; hence *syatu*; the prefix *vi* causes *ṣatva* by *upasargāt sunoti…* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-65): *ṣa*; standing after *ati…* the *tiṅ* has *nighāta* accent; in the second explanation, *upasargeṇa dhātvarthe balād anyaḥ pratīyate* (the sense of the root is changed by the prefix), since *vi* is joined the sense is "release, letting go"), *rāye* (*rai*, dative singular; *ūḍidam padādi…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171): the case-ending gets the *udātta*; in the second explanation it is dative in the sense of the fourth case), *nābhā* (*supāṃ sulug*… (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39): *ā* replaces the case-ending; *ṭi* loses [*ṭe*] *lopa*), *asmayuḥ* (*asmān ātmanaḥ icchati*; *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-8): *kyac*; *kyāc chandasi* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-170): suffix *u* after the *kyac*-ending; *ato lopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-48): the *a* is dropped; by the suffix-accent the last syllable is *udātta*). ‖ 10 ‖

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अवसृजन्नुप त्मना देवान्यक्षि वनस्पते ।
> अग्निर्हव्या सुषूदति देवो देवेषु मेधिरः ॥ ११ ॥

> *avasṛjannupa tmanā devānyakṣi vanaspate |*
> *agnirhavyā suṣūdati devo deveṣu medhiraḥ ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अवऽसृजन् । उप । त्मना । देवान् । यक्षि । वनस्पते ।
> अग्निः । हव्या । सुऽसूदति । देवः । देवेषु । मेधिरः ॥ ११ ॥

> *ava 'sṛjan | upa | tmanā | devān | yakṣi | vanaspate |*
> *agniḥ | havyā | su 'sūdati | devaḥ | deveṣu | medhiraḥ ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *O Vanaspati (Agni presiding over the sacrificial post), setting the priests each to their tasks, come of yourself to the gods and sacrifice; the shining, wise Agni among the gods graciously accepts the oblations.* Small type; some words doubtful)

> हे वनस्पते वनानां पालक [?] यूपाभिमानिदेवाग्ने अवसृजन् स्वरं [?] ऋत्विजः स्वस्वकर्मसु व्यापारयन् त्मना आत्मना देवान् विभर्ज [?] उप यक्षि । उपेत्य यज । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । देवो द्योतमानो मेधिरो मेधावान् अग्निर्देवेषु मध्ये येषां मध्ये [?] हव्या हवींषि सुषूदति सुष्ठु स्वीकरोति । षूद क्षरणे । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लुः । लेटोऽडाटावित्यडागमः । यद्वा यूपाग्निरेव परोक्षे …स्त्वा [?] उच्यते । सोऽग्निर्हवींषि सुष्ठु स्वीकरोति ॥

> *he vanaspate vanānāṃ pālaka [?] yūpābhimānidevāgne avasṛjan svaraṃ [?] ṛtvijaḥ svasvakarmasu vyāpārayan tmanā ātmanā devān vibharja [?] upa yakṣi | upetya yaja | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | devo dyotamāno medhiro medhāvān agnirdeveṣu madhye yeṣāṃ madhye [?] havyā havīṃṣi suṣūdati suṣṭhu svīkaroti | ṣūda kṣaraṇe | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ śluḥ | leṭo 'ḍāṭāvityaḍāgamaḥ | yadvā yūpāgnireva parokṣe …stvā [?] ucyate | so 'gnirhavīṃṣi suṣṭhu svīkaroti ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *vanaspate* — O Agni, the deity presiding over the sacrificial post; *avasṛjan* — (setting the priests) each to their own duty; *tmanā* — yourself (having come); *devān* — the gods; *upa* — approaching; *yakṣi* — sacrifice; *devaḥ* — shining; *medhiraḥ* — wise; *agniḥ* — Agni; *deveṣu* — among the gods; *havyā* — the oblations; *suṣūdati* — accepts; or (distributes the oblations to the gods).

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, the deity presiding over the sacrificial post! Setting the priests each to their duty, come of yourself to the sacrificial house and perform the sacrifice addressing the gods. The shining, wise Agni takes the oblations and distributes them among the gods.

### Printed p. 274  (PDF 292)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

**English Translation (as printed).** Vanaspati, here present of your own accord, convey our offerings to the gods ; the divine and intelligent Agni accepts (the oblations) for the deities.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***vanaspate*** — what the nature of *vanaspati* is must be understood after much deliberation. On the basis of this word, some modern Western scholars have concluded that in Vedic times the violent animal sacrifice was strong, and that the Āprī-sūktas are *prayāja* mantras belonging to such a sacrifice. Looked at in a gross way, *vanaspati* means the sacrificial post (*yūpa-stambha*) to which the sacrificial animal is tied. But whether this is a post for binding the sacrificial animal or not may be determined by attending to the Śruti sentences and then reasoning from them. In the Praiṣa-sūkta:

> होता यक्षद्वनस्पतिमुपावसृक्षद्धियो जोष्टारं [?] शशमानं नरि [?] स्वदात्त्वधितिः [?]
> ऋतुथाद्य देवो देवेभ्यो हव्यवाडन्येऽन्यस्य [?] होतर्यज ॥

> *hotā yakṣadvanaspatimupāvasṛkṣaddhiyo joṣṭāraṃ [?] śaśamānaṃ nari [?] svadāttvadhitiḥ [?]*
> *ṛtuthādya devo devebhyo havyavāḍanye 'nyasya [?] hotaryaja ‖*

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-[?]-[?]; partly legible.) The commentator's gloss on this mantra is of this kind: वनस्पतिं योऽसाधारणभूतं दशमप्रयाजदेवतात्मकमग्निं दैव्यो होता यजतु (*vanaspatiṃ yo 'sādhāraṇabhūtaṃ daśamaprayājadevatātmakamagniṃ daivyo hotā yajatu*) [?]: "the *vanaspati* is the support of the post, and is the tenth *prayāja* deity, Agni; let the divine Hotṛ sacrifice to him". To this *vanaspati* are applied the epithets *dhiyo joṣṭā*, *svadāt svadhitiḥ*, *devebhyaḥ ṛtuthā havyavāṭ*, *yajñasya āyuḥ kalpamānaḥ* and so on. Of these, *dhiyo joṣṭā* is "one who pleases the intellect" [?]; *svadhitiḥ* — with the axe [?], a divider; *ṛtuthā* — at the proper time (*kālaviśeṣe*) *adya*, in this rite, he makes sweet the oblation given by us [?]; and *yajñasya āyuḥ kalpamānaḥ* means "one who prolongs the life of the sacrificer". By such epithets the Praiṣa-sūkta states the identity of Agni and *vanaspati*. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa *prāṇo vai vanaspatiḥ* (2-[?]) is said. The Nirukta author first gives the derivation and then in the Āprī-sūkta … *(this paragraph read at low confidence)*

### Printed p. 275  (PDF 293)

… tells us the nature of *vanaspati*. While explaining the Ṛk 3-[?]-[?] he shows the derivation of the word *vanaspati* (Ni. 8-[?]): *vanānāṃ pā vā pālayitā vā* — "the protector or guardian of the forests (*vana*)" — and says that, since Agni is the lord (*prabhu*) of the *vana*s, he is called *vanaspati*; and *vanoti* [?], from the root *van* meaning "to take, to obtain", he is called *vanaspati*. Then in discussing the nature of the deities of the Āprī-sūkta (Ni. 8-[?]) he says *tat ko vanaspatiḥ; yūpa iti kātthakyaḥ; agnir iti śākapūṇiḥ* — giving the two opinions, "he is the post (*yūpa*)", say Kātthakya, "he is Agni", says Śākapūṇi — and to support Kātthakya's view he cites:

> आञ्जन्ति त्वामध्वरे देवयन्तो वनस्पते मधुना दैव्येन ।
> यदूर्ध्वस्तिष्ठा द्रविणेह धत्तादद्वा क्षयो मातुरस्या उपस्थे ॥

> *āñjanti tvāmadhvare devayanto vanaspate madhunā daivyena |*
> *yadūrdhvastiṣṭhā draviṇeha dhattādadvā kṣayo māturasyā upasthe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-1.) In this Ṛk Sāyaṇa has addressed *vanaspati* as *yūpa*. Then, to support Śākapūṇi's view the Nirukta author cites:

> वनस्पते रशनया नियूया देवानां पाथ उप वक्षि विद्वान् ।
> स्वदाति देवः कृणवद्धवींष्यवताद्द्यावापृथिवी हवं मे ॥

> *vanaspate raśanayā niyūyā devānāṃ pātha upa vakṣi vidvān |*
> *svadāti devaḥ kṛṇavaddhavīṃṣyavatāddyāvāpṛthivī havaṃ me ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-70-10.) Sāyaṇa has taken even this as *yūpa*; but Durgācārya, in his Nirukta commentary, explaining this Ṛk and *yat punarvanaspatiḥ* [?], says: यूपान्तर्गतो ऽग्निः (*yūpāntargato 'gniḥ*) — "the Agni within the post", and *atra bravīti: agnir evāsau yūpāntargato yūpātmanā vartamāno yūpa-jañjanīyo vanaspatiśabdenocyate* [?]: "Agni residing within the post, being in the post's form, is called *vanaspati*". Here *vanaspati* means the Agni within the post, and not another; the Nirukta author, he says, has established. The author of the Bṛhaddevatā says:

> वनस्पतिं तु यं प्राहुरयं सोऽग्निर्वनस्पतिः ।
> अयं वनानां हि पतिः पाता पालयितेति वा ।
> अग्निर्गृह्णमदेनायं वनस्पतिरितीरितः [?] ।
> मन्दस्त्वेकस्य सूक्तस्य पल्यचस्य [?] तृतीयया ।
> यूपवर्त्मोपवच्चैव स्तुतिरस्य प्रसङ्गजा ।
> सर्वेणाञ्जाति सूक्तेन तृतीये सा तु मण्डले [?] ॥

> *vanaspatiṃ tu yaṃ prāhurayaṃ so 'gnirvanaspatiḥ |*
> *ayaṃ vanānāṃ hi patiḥ pātā pālayiteti vā |*
> *agnirgṛhṇamadenāyaṃ vanaspatiritīritaḥ [?] |*
> *mandastvekasya sūktasya palyacasya [?] tṛtīyayā |*
> *yūpavartmopavaccaiva stutirasya prasaṅgajā |*
> *sarveṇāñjāti sūktena tṛtīye sā tu maṇḍale [?] ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-48 to 3-50 [?]; partly legible.)

### Printed p. 276  (PDF 294)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

By these sentences, the nature of the Āprī deity aimed at in Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?] is discussed. Here *vanaspati* is simply "Agni", and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-[?] a Ṛk in the third Maṇḍala … having accepted *yūpa*, Durga, on the strength of *gṛhyamadena* [?] and *vanaspati* word, says that it means Agni; in the third Maṇḍala, in certain Ṛks only, *yūpa* or the "tree" is the meaning, he shows, and *prasaṅgaja* ("incidental"). In the same way —

> इहैव पवमानोऽग्निर्मध्यमोऽग्निर्वनस्पतिः ।
> अमुष्मिन्नेव लोकेऽग्निः [?] … रुच्यते [?] ॥

> *ihaiva pavamāno 'gnirmadhyamo 'gnirvanaspatiḥ |*
> *amuṣminneva loke 'gniḥ [?] … rucyate [?] ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 1-44 [?].) In this verse *vanaspati* is the Agni of the middle world, and in the Ṛks, leaving aside certain places, it is clearly said that in many places this word is applied to Agni alone.

In the Ṛk 10-70-10 cited above, *rasanayā niyūya devānām upavakṣi*, it is a prayer that the oblation be carried to the gods tied firmly, as it were with a rope; there, it is not at all necessary that a sacrificial animal be tied to the *yūpa* ... [?]. In the Āprī-sūktas, when examined all together, in no Ṛk is the binding of the sacrificial animal indicated. And in Ṛks 1-188-10, 3-4-10, 7-2-10 the word *havyāni*, the oblations, and in the present sūkta *havyā* [?], in 10-110-10 and the like the words *haviṣī*, *havyam* are used, and the oblations are appropriately indicated by words of common sense and meaning (*sāmānya*); words that relate to the offerings (*ājya*, *haviṣ*) are indicated.

The word *śamitā* applied to *vanaspati* occurs, in worldly usage, in the sense of "one who kills" or "who destroys" (*nāśa*). In the Āprī-sūktas, in four Ṛks besides this one of the other places, this word is used. In 1-[?]-[?] and 10-[?] the general meaning "who makes" [?] appears. In the Ṛk 3-[?]-[?] "who cuts the soma-creeper" and in 3-[?]-[?] "who cuts the skin", it is only a word applying to the officiating priest [?], and only those who rely on the sacrificial animal take this word, in general, for them (the animal-slaughter school). If we take only the Ṛks of the Āprī-sūktas in which this word is used —

> वनस्पतिरवसृजन्नुपस्थादग्निर्हविः सूदयाति प्रधीभिः ।
> त्रिधा समक्तं नयतु प्रजानन् देवेभ्यो दैव्यः शमितोप हव्यम् ॥

> *vanaspatiravasṛjannupasthādagnirhaviḥ sūdayāti pradhībhiḥ |*
> *tridhā samaktaṃ nayatu prajānan devebhyo daivyaḥ śamitopa havyam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-10.)

In this Ṛk, *śamitā* is "the purifier (*saṃskartā*)" of the oblation [?], or the divine *śamitā* named Agni [?]: "Agni is the *śamitā* of the gods, so it is said" [?]. And:

> उपावसृज त्मन्या समञ्जन् देवानां पाथ ऋतुथा हवींषि ।
> वनस्पतिः शमिता देवो अग्निः स्वदन्तु हव्यं मधुना घृतेन ॥

> *upāvasṛja tmanyā samañjan devānāṃ pātha ṛtuthā havīṃṣi |*
> *vanaspatiḥ śamitā devo agniḥ svadantu havyaṃ madhunā ghṛtena ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-10.) In this Ṛk, since Sāyaṇa explains *śamitā* as the god named Agni (or, "named *śamitṛ*"), the word *śamitā* there has not been taken as "slaughterer of the sacrificial animal"; accordingly the word *vanaspati*, the sacrificial post in which the animal is bound, is not meant as the *yūpa-stambha*.

***avasṛjan*** — स्वरं वर्तयन् ऋत्विजः स्वस्वकर्मसु न्यापारयन् (*svaraṃ vartayan ṛtvijaḥ svasvakarmasu nyāpārayan*): "setting the priests to their own acts"; the meaning is "putting the priests to their several duties".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 11; grammar page, noted briefly).** *avasṛjan* (root *sṛja visarge*; in the present sense *śatṛ*; *tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ*: vikaraṇa *śa*; here there is no *guṇa* because of *ṅit* [?]; *tiṅ ca* … (Pā. #### Ṛk 12

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> पूषण्वते मरुत्वते विश्वदेवाय वायवे ।
> स्वाहा गायत्रवेपसे हव्यमिन्द्राय कर्तन ॥ १२ ॥

> *pūṣaṇvate marutvate viśvadevāya vāyave |*
> *svāhā gāyatravepase havyamindrāya kartana ‖ 12 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> पूषण्ऽवते । मरुत्ऽवते । विश्वऽदेवाय । वायवे ।
> स्वाहा । गायत्रऽवेपसे । हव्यम् । इन्द्राय । कर्तन ॥ १२ ॥

> *pūṣaṇ 'vate | marut 'vate | viśva 'devāya | vāyave |*
> *svāhā | gāyatra 'vepase | havyam | indrāya | kartana ‖ 12 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *O priests, make the offering with "svāhā" to Indra, in the form of the Gāyatra, accompanied by Pūṣan, the Maruts, the whole assembly of gods, and Vāyu.* Small type)

> पूषण्वते पूषा तदस्यास्ति । अनो नुडिति नुट् । ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुबिति मतुप उदात्तत्वम् ॥ मरुत्वते मरुद्भिः सह वर्तमानाय विश्वदेवाय सर्वदेवसंघाय वायवे गमनशीलाय च तथा गायत्रवेपसे । वेप इति रूपनाम । गायत्रशब्द इतरसामोपलक्षणः । गायत्रस्य वेपो रूपं यस्य ताद्दृशायेन्द्राय हव्यं हविः प्रदातुं स्वाहा कर्तन स्वाहाकारं कुरुत ऋत्विजः । करोतेर्लोटि तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चेति तनबादेशः ॥

> *pūṣaṇvate pūṣā tadasyāsti | ano nuḍiti nuṭ | hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matubiti matupa udāttatvam ‖ marutvate marudbhiḥ saha vartamānāya viśvadevāya sarvadevasaṃghāya vāyave gamanaśīlāya ca tathā gāyatravepase | vepa iti rūpanāma | gāyatraśabda itarasāmopalakṣaṇaḥ | gāyatrasya vepo rūpaṃ yasya tāddṛśāyendrāya havyaṃ haviḥ pradātuṃ svāhā kartana svāhākāraṃ kuruta ṛtvijaḥ | karoterloṭi taptanaptanathanāśceti tanabādeśaḥ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *pūṣaṇvate* — accompanied by Pūṣan; *marutvate* — by the Maruts, the gods; *viśvadevāya* — to the assembly of all the gods; *vāyave* — to Vāyu; *gāyatravepase* — who has the Gāyatra form; *indrāya* — to Indra; *havyam* — the oblation; *svāhākartana* — make the *svāhā*-call (to offer it).

### Printed p. 279  (PDF 297)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 12.)*

**Bhāvārtha.** Make the call *svāhā* and offer the oblation to Indra, who is accompanied by Pūṣan, who is with the Maruts, the assembly of all the gods, and Vāyu, and who has the Gāyatra form.

**English Translation (as printed).** (Priests), present the oblation with Swaha to Indra, in the form of the Gayatra, along with Pushan and the Maruts ; also the assembled gods, and to Vayu.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***gāyatravepase*** — वेप इति रूपनाम । गायत्रशब्द इतरसामोपलक्षणः (*vepa iti rūpanāma | gāyatraśabda itarasāmopalakṣaṇaḥ*) ("*vepa* is a name for form; the word *gāyatra* indicates the other *sāmans* also"): "to Indra, who has the form of *gāyatra*"; Sāyaṇa explains it as "for Indra, who has the form of the Gāyatra [Sāman]; the one who is pleased by song and who has a form that is supreme by song". The meaning is that he is the praised by song, and has a beautiful form. In the epithet —

> आ त्वेहि [?] सबर्दुघां हुवे गायत्रवेपसम् ।
> इन्द्रं धेनुं सुदुघामन्यामिषमुरुधारामरंकृताम् ॥

> *ā tvehi [?] sabardughāṃ huve gāyatravepasam |*
> *indraṃ dhenuṃ sudughāmanyāmiṣamurudhārāmaraṃkṛtām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-6-10 [?].) in this Ṛk the nature of Indra is told. But Sāyaṇa there has made *gāyatravepasam* an epithet of *dhenum* (cow) and explained *praśastavegām* "of excellent speed [?]". Here some hold that the epithet is applicable to Indra. In the Ṛk 8-[?]-[?], the word *gāthaśravasam* is an epithet of Indra, and given the sense *gāthayā kīrtivantam* ("famed through song"); likewise here also the word *gāyatravepase* has the same sense and is an epithet of Indra.

***svāhā kartana*** — स्वाहाकारं कुरुते (*svāhākāraṃ kurute*) ("make the *svāhā*-call"). Its further particulars will be given in the next Ṛk.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 12; grammar page, noted briefly).** *pūṣaṇvate* (*pūṣā tasyāsti* [= *pūṣā asya asti*]; *tadasyāsti*… gives suffix *matup*; *ano nuḍ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-[?]) gives *nuṭ* augment; *hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-176): *matup* is *udātta*; dative singular), *viśvadevāya* (*viśve devā yasya saḥ viśvadevaḥ*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1): the first member keeps its natural accent).

#### Ṛk 13

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स्वाहाकृतान्या गह्युप हव्यानि वीतये ।
> इन्द्रा गहि श्रुधी हवं त्वां हवन्ते अध्वरे ॥ १३ ॥

> *svāhākṛtānyā gahyupa havyāni vītaye |*
> *indrā gahi śrudhī havaṃ tvāṃ havante adhvare ‖ 13 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> स्वाहाऽकृतानि । आ । गहि । उप । हव्यानि । वीतये ।
> इन्द्र । आ । गहि । श्रुधि । हवम् । त्वाम् । हवन्ते । अध्वरे ॥ १३ ॥

> *svāhā 'kṛtāni | ā | gahi | upa | havyāni | vītaye |*
> *indra | ā | gahi | śrudhi | havam | tvām | havante | adhvare ‖ 13 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *O Indra, come near to eat the oblations offered with the call "svāhā"; come and hear our invocation, since the priests call you at the non-violent sacrifice.* Small type; a few words doubtful)

> हे इन्द्र स्वाहाकृतानि । स्वाहेत्येवंपूर्वा कृतिः करणमुच्चारणं यस्यां [?] यज्यमानदेवतानां ताः स्वाहाकृतयः । तद्वन्ति हव्यानि हवींषि । अत्र प्रयाजेषु वषट्कारप्रदानात् स्वाहाकृतं हविरित्यर्थः [?] । तद्वा उप समीपे गहि आगच्छ । वीतये भक्षणाय । गहि आगच्छ [?] । तथा हे इन्द्र आ गहि स्तोत्राण्यभिलक्ष्य गच्छ [?] । आगत्य अस्मदीयमाह्वानं श्रुधि शृणु । यतस्त्वा अध्वरे हिंसात्मके [?] योगे अह्वयन्ति ऋत्विजः । अतः श्रुधि । श्रुतेर्बहुलं छन्दसीति सम्प्रसारणम् ॥

> *he indra svāhākṛtāni | svāhetyevaṃpūrvā kṛtiḥ karaṇamuccāraṇaṃ yasyāṃ [?] yajyamānadevatānāṃ tāḥ svāhākṛtayaḥ | tadvanti havyāni havīṃṣi | atra prayājeṣu vaṣaṭkārapradānāt svāhākṛtaṃ havirityarthaḥ [?] | tadvā upa samīpe gahi āgaccha | vītaye bhakṣaṇāya | gahi āgaccha [?] | tathā he indra ā gahi stotrāṇyabhilakṣya gaccha [?] | āgatya asmadīyamāhvānaṃ śrudhi śṛṇu | yatastvā adhvare hiṃsātmake [?] yoge ahvayanti ṛtvijaḥ | ataḥ śrudhi | śruterbahulaṃ chandasīti samprasāraṇam ‖*

### Printed p. 281  (PDF 299)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 13 [?].)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *indra* — O Indra; *svāhākṛtāni* — offered with the call *svāhā*; *havyāni* — the oblations; *vītaye* — to eat; *upa* — near; *ā gahi* — come, be pleased; *tvām* — you; *adhvare* — in the non-violent sacrifice; *havante* — (the priests) call; (therefore) *ā gahi* — come (and); *havam* — our invocation; *śrudhi* — hear.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Indra, come near us to eat the oblations offered with the call *svāhā*. Since the priests call you in the non-violent sacrifice, come, and hear our invocation.

**English Translation (as printed).** Approach, Indra, to partake of the oblations consecrated with Swaha ; approach and hear the invocation, as they invoke you to the sacrifice.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***svāhākṛtāni*** — स्वाहा इत्येवंपूर्वा कृतिः करणमुच्चारणं यासां ताः स्वाहाकृतयः (*svāhā ityevaṃpūrvā kṛtiḥ karaṇamuccāraṇaṃ yāsāṃ tāḥ svāhākṛtayaḥ*): "the oblations which have the call *svāhā* as their utterance"; and *havyāni* is the epithet of the oblations (*havis*) joined with the mantra *svāhā*. This word occurs mostly at the end of the Āprī-sūktas. In some sūktas it is used in a more particular sense: in 1-[?]-[?] *svāhā kṛṇotana*, in 1-[?]-[?] *svāhā kartana*; in 1-[?]-[?]; 3-4-[?] as the epithet of *kṛtis* (the acts); in 1-[?]-[?] as an epithet of *havyam*; in 10-110-[?] as an epithet of *haviḥ*; and in the present sūkta *havyāni* is an epithet. In this word, since the deity of the term is the divine *svāhākṛti*, some have taken the deity here to be not Agni; others hold that Agni is meant. In the Praiṣa-sūkta:

> होता यक्षदग्निग्ं स्वाहाज्यस्य … वीयन्तु [?] होतर्यज ।

> *hotā yakṣadagnigṃ svāhājyasya … vīyantu [?] hotaryaja |*

(Tai. Brā. 3-6-[?]-[?]; partly legible.) The commentator on this explains: ओयुं स्वाहाशब्दोदिते [?] उत्तमप्रयाजदेवः अग्निः (*oyuṃ svāhāśabdodite [?] uttamaprayājadevaḥ agniḥ*) — "the last *prayāja* deity, Agni, called by *svāhā*" — thus explaining it as a synonym of Agni. The Nirukta author:

---

### Printed p. 282  (PDF 300)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

> स्वाहाकृतयः स्वाहेत्येतत् सु आहेति वा स्वा वागाहेति वा स्वं प्राहेति वा स्वाहुतं हविर्जुहोतीति वा ।

> *svāhākṛtayaḥ svāhetyetat su āheti vā svā vāgāheti vā svaṃ prāheti vā svāhutaṃ havirjuhotīti vā |*

(Ni. 8-21 [?].) The sense given is: either that it is *su-āha* — spoken well; or in the manner of "well-spoken" (*svāha*), the word being so pronounced in speech; or "the offerer of *svāhā*" that is, the *mantra* with which an oblation is purified (*pūta*) and well offered, as famed. He then cites Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-11 and explains this sense in detail. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

> स्वाहाकृतीर्यजति प्रतिष्ठा वै स्वाहाकृतयः प्रतिष्ठयैवैनं [?] तद्यज्ञमन्ततः प्रतिष्ठापयति ।

> *svāhākṛtīryajati pratiṣṭhā vai svāhākṛtayaḥ pratiṣṭhayaivainaṃ [?] tadyajñamantataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayati |*

(Ai. Brā. 2-9 [?].) It is explained that, since the oblation is made by *svāhā*, it is the end of the rite and the sacrifice is thereby set on a right foundation. In the Bṛhaddevatā:

> स्वाहाकृतयोऽनेकाश्च विदुषां मतेऽभवन् [?] ।
> कृत्स्नवर्गं [?] त्रयीमेनमग्निं विनिश्चयः ।
> अयं हि कर्ता स्वाहानां कृतिस्त्रा [?] सामिधेन्यकेजा [?] ।
> आयं प्रसूतिर्भूतानां सर्वेषामव्ययः [?] ॥

> *svāhākṛtayo 'nekāśca viduṣāṃ mate 'bhavan [?] |*
> *kṛtsnavargaṃ [?] trayīmenamagniṃ viniścayaḥ |*
> *ayaṃ hi kartā svāhānāṃ kṛtistrā [?] sāmidhenyakejā [?] |*
> *āyaṃ prasūtirbhūtānāṃ sarveṣāmavyayaḥ [?] ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-9 to 2-10 [?]; partly legible.) On the subject of the *svāhākṛtis*, there are different opinions of the learned; all the ideas are indicated by this term, in order to indicate this earthly Agni. "This Agni is the doer of the *svāhās*; he is called the maker; by all other makers too, therefore, he is thus remembered; hence the earthly Agni alone is the begetter of all"; thus, following the opinion of the Nirukta author, *āgneya iti tu sthitiḥ* (Ni. 8-22) the Bṛhaddevatā states its own opinion.

In the last Ṛks of the Āprī-sūktas, which conclude with *svāhā*, Dawn (Uṣas), the Maruts, Vāyu, Sūrya, Indra, Varuṇa and others are addressed; but above all (Agni):

> पुरोगा अग्निर्देवानां गायत्रेण समज्यते । स्वाहाकृतीषु रोचते ॥

> *purogā agnirdevānāṃ gāyatreṇa samajyate | svāhākṛtīṣu rocate ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188-11.)

> सद्यो जातो व्यमिमीत यज्ञमग्निर्देवानामभवत्पुरोगाः ।
> अस्य होतुः प्रदिश्यृतस्य वाचि स्वाहाकृतं हविरदन्तु देवाः ॥

> *sadyo jāto vyamimīta yajñamagnirdevānāmabhavatpurogāḥ |*
> *asya hotuḥ pradiśyṛtasya vāci svāhākṛtaṃ haviradantu devāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-11.)

### Printed p. 283  (PDF 301)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 13 [?].)*

In such Ṛks it is praised that from the time of his birth Agni is the leader of the gods; and, explaining the greatness of the *svāhākṛti*:

> आ याह्यग्ने समिधानो अर्वाङिन्द्रेण देवैः सरथं तुरेभिः ।
> बर्हिर्न आस्तामदितिः सुपुत्रा स्वाहा देवा अमृता मादयन्ताम् ॥

> *ā yāhyagne samidhāno arvāṅindreṇa devaiḥ sarathaṃ turebhiḥ |*
> *barhirna āstāmaditiḥ suputrā svāhā devā amṛtā mādayantām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-11.)

> अग्ने वह वरुणमिष्टये न इन्द्रं दिवो मरुतो अन्तरिक्षात् ।
> सीदन्तु बर्हिर्विश्व आ यजत्राः स्वाहा देवा अमृता मादयन्ताम् ॥

> *agne vaha varuṇamiṣṭaye na indraṃ divo maruto antarikṣāt |*
> *sīdantu barhirviśva ā yajatrāḥ svāhā devā amṛtā mādayantām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-11.) In these Ṛks (and so on) it is signalled that the sacrificial offering of oblations is made with *svāhā*, which delights the gods.

**(Āprī-sūktas) — Concluding Remarks (*upasaṃhāra*)**

On the necessity of the Āprī-sūktas and their purpose, the scholar Max Müller first says that those deities were hymns for the appeasement of families or kinsmen [?], and, after that, said of the interpretation of their mystery, thus:

"It is possible that Apri hymns may have been the songs of reconciliation and that they were called Apri, i.e., appeasing hymns, not because of their appeasing the anger of Gods but the enmities of the members of the same or different families. However it may be, they indeed prove an active intercourse between the ancient families of India long before the final collection of the ten books.......The original purpose of the Apri hymns and the motive for allowing the priests to choose, are difficult to discover" (Ancient Sanskrit Literature P. 246-7; English as printed).

Regarding the places of the Āprī-sūktas in sacrificial rites and the deities, although there is disagreement even among scholars of the East and West, there are many common features in all the Āprī-sūktas; since the composition of the sūktas and the subjects each have a fixed pattern, it is said that all of them are seen to be composed together or to be connected with one another. Except the sages of the fourth [?] and sixth Maṇḍalas, all the others …

---

### Printed p. 284  (PDF 302)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 142".)*

… the sages of the other Maṇḍalas all have the traditional Āprī-sūktas of their own families. In the eighth Maṇḍala the descendants of Kaṇva [?] have no separate Āprī-sūkta, yet it is famous that they use [Sūkta 1-13] (the Kāṇva Sūkta); the sages of the fourth and the sixth Maṇḍalas have no need of them, and the reason cannot be said [?]; or the descendants of Vāmadeva and Bhāradvāja may have used some other mantras (since Bharadvāja was born in the Āṅgirasa gotra, the well-known sūkta) in this place [?].

*Mantras indicated by the terms Āprī and Āpra* — Kātyāyana in the Sarvānukramaṇī: विकदाप्रीसूक्तं … नाराशंसानि अप्रशब्दोक्तानि आतेनूनपात्रान्ति (*vikadāprīsūktaṃ … nārāśaṃsāni apraśabdoktāni ātenūnapātrānti*) [?] — the mantras addressed to the deity Narāśaṃsa are called *āpra*, although the mantras addressed to Tanūnapāt are famous as *āprī*; his sentences show this difference in the Nirukta and the like. Whether the term *āprī* belongs to the deity or to the sūkta also is a question; looking at the sūkta, it can be said that it is a sūkta for the deity, and the others are mantras of the deities [?].

*Nature of the rite* — the sacrificial rite accomplished by the Āprī-sūktas, though it might be said to hold a secondary place, as an accessory to Brāhmaṇa-type rites, can in truth be said to have held the principal place. Its connection with the *prayāja* is known in many places: in the Ṛks 1-13-[?]; 1-142-[?]; 10-[?]-[?]; 3-4-[?]; 5-5-[?]; 7-2-[?] the mantra *imaṃ yajñam* occurs, in 3-4-[?]; 7-2-11 *no yajñam*, and in 1-142-[?]; 10-110-[?] *asmin yajñe* occurs, which indicate the sacrificial rite itself; and in the *prayāja* and other sūktas no rite whatever is seen to be treated as being of secondary place.

*tridhā ā mimikṣati* (1-142-3); *tri-ṣadhasthāya* [?] (3-4-5): from these mantras it is understood that this rite is to be performed in the three periods of the day; and from *samiddho adya manuṣo duroṇe* (10-110-1) that there was a separate house for it, but that Agni can be installed in an ordinary house.

> समिध्द्वमित्थुना [?] बोध्यस्मे शुचा शुचा सुमतिं रासि वस्वः ।
> आ देव देवान्यजथाय वक्षि सखा सखीन्त्सुमना यक्ष्यग्ने ॥

> *samidhdvamitthunā [?] bodhyasme śucā śucā sumatiṃ rāsi vasvaḥ |*
> *ā deva devānyajathāya vakṣi sakhā sakhīntsumanā yakṣyagne ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-9-4 [?].)

### Printed p. 285  (PDF 303)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 13 [?].)*

In this Ṛk, and in this one that follows, the sage Viśvāmitra describes poetically the blazing of Agni and its being —

> जुषस्व नः समिधमग्ने अद्य शोचा बृहद्यजतं धूममृण्वन् ।
> उप स्पृश दिव्यं सानु स्तूपैः सं रश्मिभिस्ततनः सूर्यस्य ॥

> *juṣasva naḥ samidhamagne adya śocā bṛhadyajataṃ dhūmamṛṇvan |*
> *upa spṛśa divyaṃ sānu stūpaiḥ saṃ raśmibhistatanaḥ sūryasya ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3-1 [?].) in this Ṛk the description of the flame of Agni and the rays of the sun spreading together also shows the poetic form of the mantras. These very descriptions show that the sacrifice is performed at the beginning of the morning.

The mantra *pūrvyaṃ tantuṃ tanuṣva* (1-142-1) shows that the sacrifice is ancient. Since this sacrifice is performed by the priests, together with the help of Agni, the divine *hotṛ*, the oblation of ghee is first to be offered to Agni. After the kindling of Agni the offering [of praise] goes towards the atmosphere (1-[?]-3), and then he brings the gods; Agni performs this service as the helper of men (3-4-5).

*Artistry* [heading as read: *kṛtikauśalya* [?]] — Although the Āprī-sūktas were composed apart from one another, at different times, and are related to different families of sages, the sentence structure and the usage of words are of the same kind in all these sūktas, and so their special excellence shows a greater harmony and certainty than other sūktas.

(Except two sūktas [?]) all the sūktas have eleven Ṛks, begin with the word *samidh* and end with *svāhā*, which shows a regular pattern from the point of view of poetry and art alike.

As to metre there is no such restriction. The sūktas 1-13; 1-188; 5-5 and 9-5 [as read] are in the Gāyatrī metre; Sūkta 1-142 in Anuṣṭubh; and 3-4; 7-2; 2-3; 10-70 and 10-110 in Triṣṭubh. The mantra-parts *devān āvaha*, *devān yakṣi*, *viprā yajñeṣu mānuṣeṣu kāravaḥ* and so on are repeated.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 13; grammar page, begun; noted briefly).** *gahi* (root *gamḷ gatau*; *loṭ*, second person singular, *sip*, *hi*; *bahulaṃ chandasi*: *śap* is *luk*; *anudāttopadeśa…* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-37): loss of the nasal *m* of the root; *asiddhavat…* …) *(continues on p. 286)*.

*Grammar (Ṛk 13, concluded; noted briefly).* *gahi* (…; *āto heḥ* [?]: because of this the *luk* does not apply; standing after an *ati…* word, *nighāta*), *vītaye* (root *vī gatiprajananakāntyasanakhādaneṣu*; *mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā udāttaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-96) [?]: *ktin* is *udātta*; dative singular), *indra* (being at the head of the pāda there is no *nighāta*; *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198): the first syllable is *udātta*), *śrudhi* (root *śru śravaṇe*; *loṭ*, second person singular, *sip*; *bahulaṃ chandasi*: *luk* of the vikaraṇa; *śṛṇuhi*… (Pā. Sū. 6-4-102): *hi* becomes *dhi*; as it has no [*ati*]… the *guṇa* does not occur; since it stands after an *ati…* word it has the *nighāta* but *atiṅ* … is not prohibited [?]; by the *apit* rule for the suffix, the last syllable is *udātta*), *havam* (root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *ap* suffix in the abstract sense; *samprasāraṇa* of the root; *pūrvarūpa*; *guṇa* of the root vowel; *avādeśa*; the suffix is *pit*, so the root accent remains), *havante* (the same root as before; *loṭ*, third person plural, *jhi*; *e* [for *ṭi*]; *ghvoḥ* … (Pā. Sū. 7-1-[?]): *anta* substitution; *bahulaṃ chandasi*: *samprasāraṇa* of the root; *pūrvarūpa*; the *śap* vikaraṇa; *guṇa* of the *u* before it; *avādeśa*; standing after an *ati…* word, *nighāta*), *adhvare* (*na vidyate dhvaro hiṃsā yatra saḥ adhvaraḥ*, tasmin; *nañsubhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172): the final of the last member is *udātta*; locative singular). ‖ 13 ‖

*Here the 142nd Sūkta ends.*

## Sūkta 143

### Printed p. 287 (continued; PDF 305)

*(The Kannada heading reads "The 143rd Sūkta".)*

*(Anukramaṇī, Sanskrit; partly legible, not rendered in English. Gist: the sūkta of eight Ṛks beginning "Pra tavyasīm" is the fourth sūkta; ṛṣi Dīrghatamas; "from this sūkta on, eight sūktas are addressed to Agni"; the last Ṛk is Triṣṭubh and the others Jagatī [as the text reads]; its use at the Prātaranuvāka, the Āśvina-śastra, and, as a *nivid* for Jātavedas, in the Āgnimāruta-śastra of the Agniṣṭoma, with the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra cited.)*

> प्र तव्यसीमिति अष्टर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं दैर्घतमसं । तथा चानुक्रान्तं प्र तव्यसीमष्टाग्नेयं तु त्रिष्टुबन्तमिति । तु तदितिकृत्वा [?] आद्यं सूक्तप्रभृत्यष्टाग्निदेवता [?] । अन्त्यं त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टाः [?] जगत्यः । प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोरुक्तो विनियोगः । अग्निष्टोमे आग्निमारुते शस्त्रे (अग्निः) सूक्तं जातवेदस्यनिविद्धानीयम् [?] । अथ यथेतमुक्ते खण्डे सूत्रितम् — प्र तव्यसीं नव्यसीमपो हि ष्ठेति तिस्रः [?] (आ. श्रौ. ३-१०) इति । वरोरात्रस्य [?] प्रथमेऽहनि जातवेदस्यनिविद्धानं अश्वमेधिके मध्यमेऽहनि च निविद्धानं । तथा चाज्ञायोतिदेशः [?] । एकाहिकान्युपसंशस्य तेषु निविदो दध्यादेवमेवाग्निमारुते (आ. १०-१०) इति ॥ [?]

> *pra tavyasīmiti aṣṭarcaṃ caturthaṃ sūktaṃ dairghatamasaṃ | tathā cānukrāntaṃ pra tavyasīmaṣṭāgneyaṃ tu triṣṭubantamiti | tu taditikṛtvā [?] ādyaṃ sūktaprabhṛtyaṣṭāgnidevatā [?] | antyaṃ triṣṭup śiṣṭāḥ [?] jagatyaḥ | prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayorukto viniyogaḥ | agniṣṭome āgnimārute śastre (agniḥ) sūktaṃ jātavedasyanividdhānīyam [?] | atha yathetamukte khaṇḍe sūtritam — pra tavyasīṃ navyasīmapo hi ṣṭheti tisraḥ [?] (ā. śrau. 3-10) iti | varorātrasya [?] prathame 'hani jātavedasyanividdhānaṃ aśvamedhike madhyame 'hani ca nividdhānaṃ | tathā cājñāyotideśaḥ [?] | ekāhikānyupasaṃśasya teṣu nivido dadhyādevamevāgnimārute (ā. 10-10) iti ‖ [?]*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta *pra tavyasīm* is the fourth sūkta of the twenty-first anuvāka; it has eight Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Dīrghatamas. The Anukramaṇī says "*pra tavyasīm aṣṭāgneyaṃ tu triṣṭubantam*"; from the use of the words *tu* and *tat* here it is to be understood that this and the following sūktas, eight in number, have Agni as their deity. The last Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Triṣṭubh metre and the rest in Jagatī. These sūktas are also employed as mantras of the *pātrānuṣavaṇa* [?] and the Āśvina-śastra; and, when the mantras of the Āgnimāruta-śastra are recited at the Agniṣṭoma, this sūkta is used as the *nivid* mantras relating to Jātavedas. The Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section *yathetam*, explains it with the sūtra *pra tavyasīṃ navyasīm apo hi ṣṭheti tisraḥ* (Āś. [?]-10) [?]; and further: "on the first day of the *ahorātra*, the *nivid* for Jātavedas; and in the Aśvamedha, on the middle day, the *nivid* too" — and in the Āśvalāyana the teacher states that in the *ekāhika* rites, in the Āgnimāruta the *nivid* is to be inserted (Āś. [?]-10).

**॥ ओम् ॥**

**Sūkta 143** — Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 21, Sūkta 143; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 13 [?]. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8. Ṛṣi: Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Devatā: Agni. Chandas: 1–2 Jagatī; 3–8 Triṣṭubh [as read].

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> प्र तव्यसीं नव्यसीं धीतिमग्नये वाचो मतिं सहसः सूनवे भरे ।
> अपां नपाद्यो वसुभिः सह प्रियो होता पृथिव्यां न्यसीददृत्वियः ॥ १ ॥

> *pra tavyasīṃ navyasīṃ dhītimagnaye vāco matiṃ sahasaḥ sūnave bhare |*
> *apāṃ napādyo vasubhiḥ saha priyo hotā pṛthivyāṃ nyasīdadṛtviyaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्र । तव्यसीम् । नव्यसीम् । धीतिम् । अग्नये । वाचः । मतिम् । सहसः । सूनवे । भरे ।
> अपाम् । नपात् । यः । वसुऽभिः । सह । प्रियः । होता । पृथिव्याम् । नि । असीदत् । ऋत्वियः ॥ १ ॥

> *pra | tavyasīm | navyasīm | dhītim | agnaye | vācaḥ | matim | sahasaḥ | sūnave | bhare |*
> *apām | napāt | yaḥ | vasu 'bhiḥ | saha | priyaḥ | hotā | pṛthivyām | ni | asīdat | ṛtviyaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *I offer to Agni, son of strength, the most vigorous and most new act of devotion and thoughtful speech of praise; he, the grandson of the waters, dear, the Hotṛ, takes his seat in due season on the earth (the altar) with the Vasus.* Small type; many words doubtful)

> अहमग्नये तव्यसीं तवीयसीमतिशयेन वर्धयित्रीं [?] । तवतिर्वृद्ध्यर्थः । सौत्रो धातुः । अस्मात् तृजन्तात् [?] छन्दसि ईयसुन् । तुरिष्ठमेयेष्ठेषु [?] इति तृलोपः । छान्दस ईकारलोपः । नव्यसीं नवतरामपूर्वां धीतिं योगलक्षणां [?] स्तुतिगुणकं कर्म प्र भरे । प्रकर्षेण करोमि । तथोक्तलक्षणां वाचो मतिं स्तुतिरूपं कर्म भरे । कीदृशायाग्नये । सहसो बलस्य सूनवे पुत्राय । कीदृशो योऽग्निरपां नपात् तासां नप्ता । अद्भ्य ओषधिभ्यः [?] … वा अपां नपाताद्वा [?] … यो ऽग्निः वसुभिः सह प्रियो यजमानस्य प्रीणयिता प्रियतमो वा तस्य होता होमनिष्पादकः ऋत्वियः [?] सोऽग्निः … पृथिव्यां वेदिलक्षणायां वसुभिर्वासनाश्रयोग्य [?] … न्यसीदत् । नितरां सीदति ॥

> *ahamagnaye tavyasīṃ tavīyasīmatiśayena vardhayitrīṃ [?] | tavatirvṛddhyarthaḥ | sautro dhātuḥ | asmāt tṛjantāt [?] chandasi īyasun | turiṣṭhameyeṣṭheṣu [?] iti tṛlopaḥ | chāndasa īkāralopaḥ | navyasīṃ navatarāmapūrvāṃ dhītiṃ yogalakṣaṇāṃ [?] stutiguṇakaṃ karma pra bhare | prakarṣeṇa karomi | tathoktalakṣaṇāṃ vāco matiṃ stutirūpaṃ karma bhare | kīdṛśāyāgnaye | sahaso balasya sūnave putrāya | kīdṛśo yo 'gnirapāṃ napāt tāsāṃ naptā | adbhya oṣadhibhyaḥ [?] … vā apāṃ napātādvā [?] … yo 'gniḥ vasubhiḥ saha priyo yajamānasya prīṇayitā priyatamo vā tasya hotā homaniṣpādakaḥ ṛtviyaḥ [?] so 'gniḥ … pṛthivyāṃ vedilakṣaṇāyāṃ vasubhirvāsanāśrayogya [?] … nyasīdat | nitarāṃ sīdati ‖*
