### Printed p. 289  (PDF 307)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 13 [?].)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *(ahaṃ — I)*; *sahasaḥ* — of strength; *sūnave* — to the son; *agnaye* — to Agni (addressing Agni); *tavyasīm* — the most invigorating; *navyasīm* — the very new; *dhītim* — the sacrificial act; *vācaḥ matim* — together with speech in the form of praise; *pra bhare* — I perform in a high degree; *yaḥ* — which Agni; *apāṃ napāt* — the grandson of the waters; *priyaḥ* — pleasing (to the sacrificer), or most dear; *hotā* — the accomplisher of the offering (that Agni); *ṛtviyaḥ* — being present in due time; *pṛthivyām* — on the earth called the altar; *vasubhiḥ* — with the Vasus [?]; *saha* — together; *ni asīdat* — sits down.

**Bhāvārtha.** Addressing Agni, the son of strength, I perform in a high degree, with speech in the form of praise, the sacrificial act, which is most invigorating and new. That Agni, the grandson of the waters, who pleases the sacrificer and accomplishes the offering, comes, at the proper time of the sacrifice, to the altar with the Vasus [?] and sits down.

**English Translation (as printed).** I offer devoutly to Agni, the son of strength, an invigorating and most new sacrifice, with words of adoration ; (that Agni), the grandson of the waters, who, (present) in due season, the friend and ministering priest (to the sacrificer) sits upon the alter [sic] with (many) good things.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** *(begins; the page ends after the first lines.)* The Sanskrit sentence *āgniṣṭome āgnimārute śastre idaṃ sūktaṃ jātavedasyanividdhānīyam* (as in the Anukramaṇī) is again quoted: *āgnimāruta*-related ... This sūkta, Sāyaṇa has said in his introduction, is of the nature of the *āgnimāruta-śastra* mantras; (and) *pra tavyasīṃ navyasīm apo hi ṣṭheti tisraḥ* [?].

### Printed p. 290  (PDF 308)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 143".)*

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 1 on the use of the sūkta in the Āgnimāruta-śastra.)*

He also cites the authority of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (5-30 [?]). It is well known as the *nivid* mantra of Jātavedas. Since the *vaiśvānara-nivid* mantra is a part of the Āgnimāruta-śastra, [the Sūtra] has said, to give it its due place, *jātavedasyanividdhānīyam* ("it is to be employed as the *nivid* of Jātavedas"). Of these, —

> प्र वैश्वानराय पृथुपाजसे विपो रत्ना विधन्त धरुणेषु गातवे ।
> अग्निर्हि देवाँ अमृतो दुवस्यत्यथा धर्माणि सनता न दूदुषत् ॥

> *pra vaiśvānarāya pṛthupājase vipo ratnā vidhanta dharuṇeṣu gātave |*
> *agnirhi devā~ amṛto duvasyatyathā dharmāṇi sanatā na dūduṣat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-1.) the sūkta beginning with this Ṛk relates to Vaiśvānara Agni. The present sūkta, and

> आपो हि ष्ठा मयोभुवस्ता न ऊर्जे दधातन । महे रणाय चक्षसे ॥

> *āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvastā na ūrje dadhātana | mahe raṇāya cakṣase ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-9-1.) the sūkta beginning with this Ṛk and the next two sūktas relate to the Agni called Jātavedas.

The story that is the cause (*hetubhūta*) of this Āgnimāruta and is its old tale is told in both the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. In the two there is a slight difference in the narration; so the two are explained separately here. Of these, the original story of the Vaiśvānara-related Āgnimāruta hymn is given in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa thus —

> वैश्वानरीयेणाग्निमारुतं प्रतिपद्यते वैश्वानरो वा एतद्रेतः सिक्त्वा [?] प्राच्यावयत्तस्माद्वैश्वानरीयेणाग्निमारुतं प्रतिपद्यते ।

> *vaiśvānarīyeṇāgnimārutaṃ pratipadyate vaiśvānaro vā etadretaḥ siktvā [?] prācyāvayattasmādvaiśvānarīyeṇāgnimārutaṃ pratipadyate |*

(Ai. Brā. 3-23 [?].) "Vaiśvānara made the seed that was poured fall away eastwards (?), therefore with the Vaiśvānara (hymn) the Āgnimāruta is begun" — thus, the sentence suggests the background of the sūktas' recitation, and that preceding context is this:

> प्रजापतिर्वै स्वां दुहितरमभ्यध्यायद् दिवमित्यन्य आहुरुषसमित्यन्ये तामृश्यो भूत्वा रोहितं भूतामभ्यैत् तं देवा अपश्यन्नकृतं वै प्रजापतिः करोतीति ते तमैच्छन् य एनमारिष्यत्येतमन्योऽस्मिन्नविन्दन्नेषां या एव घोरतमास्तन्वः आसन् ता एकधा समभरन् संभृता एष देवोऽभवत् तस्मा एतद्रूपमभवत् [?]

> *prajāpatirvai svāṃ duhitaramabhyadhyāyad divamityanya āhuruṣasamityanye tāmṛśyo bhūtvā rohitaṃ bhūtāmabhyait taṃ devā apaśyannakṛtaṃ vai prajāpatiḥ karotīti te tamaicchan ya enamāriṣyatyetamanyo 'sminnavindanneṣāṃ yā eva ghoratamāstanvaḥ āsan tā ekadhā samabharan saṃbhṛtā eṣa devo 'bhavat tasmā etadrūpamabhavat [?]*

(Ai. Brā. 3-33 [?]; partly legible, given as read.) On one occasion Prajāpati looked at his own daughter with desire, and, in the form of a roe-stag (*ṛśya*), approached her, she having become a doe (*rohit*); the Gods perceived this and said, "Prajāpati is doing what has not been done"; they sought one who would punish him; they could not find one in another; they gathered the most terrible bodies of themselves into one; thus gathered this god (Bhūtapati) came into being. Seeing it, the Kannada continues: the gods commanded him to punish Prajāpati. …

### Printed p. 291  (PDF 309)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 13 [?].)*

… [They said:] "He is to be punished; and the form he has taken is fearful; let it be a union of the most terrible forms of all", and so they made this *bhūta* (being) of the gathered fearful bodies. Him, as lord of beings (Bhūtapati), —

> तं देवा अब्रुवन्नयं वै प्रजापतिरकृतमकरिमं विध्येति स तथेत्यब्रवीत्स वै वो वरं वृणा इति वृणीष्वेति स एतमेव वरमवृणीत पशूनामाधिपत्यं तदस्यैतत्पशुमन्नाम ।

> *taṃ devā abruvannayaṃ vai prajāpatirakṛtamakarimaṃ vidhyeti sa tathetyabravītsa vai vo varaṃ vṛṇā iti vṛṇīṣveti sa etameva varamavṛṇīta paśūnāmādhipatyaṃ tadasyaitatpaśumannāma |*

(Ai. Brā. 3-33.) The gods told him, "This Prajāpati has done what is not done; pierce him"; he said "so be it"; "I choose a boon from you"; "choose"; and he chose this very boon, the lordship over animals: that is why he has the name Paśupati. Then, the gods understood Prajāpati's doing, and Bhūtapati took the lordship over the beasts, in the form of a boon, and the gods gave him the consent.

> तमभ्यायत्तात्वा [?] विध्यत् ऊर्ध्व उदस्पप्तत् [?] इते मृग इत्याचक्षते य उ एव मृगव्याधः स उ एव सा यो रोहित्सा रोहिणी यो एवेषुस्त्रिकाण्डा सो एवेषुस्त्रिकाण्डा [?]

> *tamabhyāyattātvā [?] vidhyat ūrdhva udaspaptat [?] ite mṛga ityācakṣate ya u eva mṛgavyādhaḥ sa u eva sā yo rohitsā rohiṇī yo eveṣustrikāṇḍā so eveṣustrikāṇḍā [?]*

(Ai. Brā. 3-33 [?]; partly legible.) Then Bhūtapati, in the form of a three-pointed arrow (*three-pointed arrow* is printed in English in the Kannada text), pierced Prajāpati with his hunting-spear. At once —

> तद्वा इदं प्रजापतेः रेतः सिच्यमानमधावत् तत्रोधं [?] पद्मत्ते [?] देवा अब्रुवन् नैदं प्रजापते रेतो मुषदिति तन्मादुषमभवत् तन्मादुषस्य मादुषत्वं माद्षं ह वै नामैतद्यन्नासुषमित्याचक्षते परोक्षेण परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवाः [?] ।

> *tadvā idaṃ prajāpateḥ retaḥ sicyamānamadhāvat tatrodhaṃ [?] padmatte [?] devā abruvan naidaṃ prajāpate reto muṣaditi tanmāduṣamabhavat tanmāduṣasya māduṣatvaṃ mādṣaṃ ha vai nāmaitadyannāsuṣamityācakṣate parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ [?] |*

(Ai. Brā. 3-33.) At once the seed of Prajāpati began to flow; and the gods, seeing the seed flowing, [said "let it not be lost"] … therefore called *mādhuṣa* [?]; the gods are fond of indirect speech. Then the gods collected the seed into a lake [*sarasa*]; —

> तेन्ग्निना निर्माविधुस्तुप्सुमरुतोऽधून्वस्तेऽग्निर्न प्राच्यावयन्न वैश्वानरेण सर्वान्दहत् [?] सा वैश्वानरो मन्त्रैः प्राच्यावयन्त्यस्य तेद्रेतसः प्रथममुदद्रुप्त तेजसादित्योऽभवत् [?] ……

> *tengninā nirmāvidhustupsumaruto 'dhūnvaste 'gnirna prācyāvayanna vaiśvānareṇa sarvāndahat [?] sā vaiśvānaro mantraiḥ prācyāvayantyasya tedretasaḥ prathamamudadrupta tejasādityo 'bhavat [?] ……*

(Ai. Brā. 3-33 [?]; heavily garbled at this resolution.) The gods then surrounded Agni with that seed, as it were with a lake; they made the Maruts shake it; but Agni could not be moved. Then it was said to be possible by the aid of Vaiśvānara to cause the Maruts to move. Therefore, with the mantra *pra vaiśvānarāya pṛthupājase* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-1) the Vaiśvānara *nivid* mantra begins, and Vaiśvānara Agni is praised. And —

### Printed p. 292  (PDF 310)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 143".)*

> जातवेदस्यं शंसति । प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत ताः सृष्टाः परान्वीभ्यो [?] विवायेनिनिर्वर्तन्त [?] ता अग्निना पर्यगृह्णात् ता अग्निमुपावर्तन्त तेनैवाद्यावृपास्वाप्त्वा [?] सोऽब्रवीज्जाता वै प्रजा अनेनायीमिति तज्जातवेदस्यमभवत्तज्जातवेदसो जातवेदस्त्वम् [?]

> *jātavedasyaṃ śaṃsati | prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ parānvībhyo [?] vivāyeninirvartanta [?] tā agninā paryagṛhṇāt tā agnimupāvartanta tenaivādyāvṛpāsvāptvā [?] so 'bravījjātā vai prajā anenāyīmiti tajjātavedasyamabhavattajjātavedaso jātavedastvam [?]*

(Ai. Brā. 3-34 [?]; partly legible.) Prajāpati created creatures; those created ran away, scattered; they did not return; then Agni enclosed them all round, and, being enclosed by Agni, they approached Agni. Prajāpati, because his creatures were thus brought back by Agni, gave him the name Jātavedas. Therefore, from the sūkta which begins with the Ṛk *pra tavyasīm* this Agni is praised, hence the Āgnimāruta *nivid* mantra; thus the Kannada concludes the origin of the recitation. The same thing is told in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa:

> प्रजापतिर्वै स्वां दुहितरमभ्यध्यायत् । दिवं वोषसं वा मिथुन्येनेयां [?] स्यामिति । तां संबभूव । तद्वै देवानामागस आस । य इत्थं स्वां दुहितरमस्माकं स्वसारं करोतीति । ते ह देवा ऊचुः । योऽयं देवः पशूनामीष्ट एतिसंधं [?] वा अयं चरति य इत्थं स्वां दुहितरमस्माकं स्वसारं करोति विध्यैनमिति तं रुद्रो भूत्वाभ्यायत्य विव्याध तस्य सा रेतः प्रासिञ्चत तदेवेतत् [?] । तस्मादेतद्विणिभ्यां [?] । पिता यस्त्वां दुहितरमधिष्कन् प्रजया रेतः संजग्मानो निषिञ्चत् [?] ॥

> *prajāpatirvai svāṃ duhitaramabhyadhyāyat | divaṃ voṣasaṃ vā mithunyeneyāṃ [?] syāmiti | tāṃ saṃbabhūva | tadvai devānāmāgasa āsa | ya itthaṃ svāṃ duhitaramasmākaṃ svasāraṃ karotīti | te ha devā ūcuḥ | yo 'yaṃ devaḥ paśūnāmīṣṭa etisaṃdhaṃ [?] vā ayaṃ carati ya itthaṃ svāṃ duhitaramasmākaṃ svasāraṃ karoti vidhyainamiti taṃ rudro bhūtvābhyāyatya vivyādha tasya sā retaḥ prāsiñcata tadevetat [?] | tasmādetadviṇibhyāṃ [?] | pitā yastvāṃ duhitaramadhiṣkan prajayā retaḥ saṃjagmāno niṣiñcat [?] ‖*

(Śa. Brā. 1-[?]-[?]-[?] to [?]; partly legible, given as read.) Prajāpati had desire for his own daughter, Heaven or Dawn; she, becoming a doe …; that was a sin of the gods: "who treats his own daughter as our sister?"; the gods said: "this god, lord of the beasts … goes about; pierce him". Rudra, taking the form, assailed him and pierced him; his seed fell. In the same matter —

> पिता यत्स्वां दुहितरमधिष्कन् क्ष्मया रेतः संजग्मानो नि षिञ्चत् ।
> स्वाध्योऽजनयन् ब्रह्म देवा वास्तोष्पतिं व्रतपां निरतक्षन् ॥

> *pitā yatsvāṃ duhitaramadhiṣkan kṣmayā retaḥ saṃjagmāno ni ṣiñcat |*
> *svādhyo 'janayan brahma devā vāstoṣpatiṃ vratapāṃ niratakṣan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-61-7.) In this Ṛk it is said: "the father (Prajāpati), uniting with his own daughter, poured his seed down on the earth" — thus; this mantra became famed as "Agnimāruta". In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, the Āgnimāruta śastra, which relates to Jātavedas and is prescribed by the sūkta of the present context, is further described, explaining its efficacy —

### Printed p. 293  (PDF 311)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 13 [?].)*

> जातवेदसे सुनवाम सोममिति जातवेदस्यां पुरस्तात्सूक्तस्य शंसति स्वस्त्ययनं वै जातवेदस्याः स्वस्तये । स्वस्त्ययनमेव तत्कुरुते [?] स्वस्ति संवत्सरस्य पारमश्नुते य एवं वेद ।

> *jātavedase sunavāma somamiti jātavedasyāṃ purastātsūktasya śaṃsati svastyayanaṃ vai jātavedasyāḥ svastaye | svastyayanameva tatkurute [?] svasti saṃvatsarasya pāramaśnute ya evaṃ veda |*

> प्र तव्यसीं नव्यसीं धीतिमग्नय इति जातवेदस्यां प्रति प्रथमेऽहनि प्रथमस्याह्नो रूपं । समानमाग्निमारुतं भवति यज्ञाग्निष्टोमे यद्येयज्ञे [?] समानं क्रियते तत्प्रजा अनु समनन्ति तस्मात्समानमाग्निमारुतं भवति ।

> *pra tavyasīṃ navyasīṃ dhītimagnaya iti jātavedasyāṃ prati prathame 'hani prathamasyāhno rūpaṃ | samānamāgnimārutaṃ bhavati yajñāgniṣṭome yadyeyajñe [?] samānaṃ kriyate tatprajā anu samananti tasmātsamānamāgnimārutaṃ bhavati |*

(Ai. Brā. 3-34 / 3-35 [?]; partly legible.) The Āgnimāruta-śastra, which relates to Jātavedas, is auspicious (*maṅgalātmaka*) and brings peace and well-being, and so on; thus it is described; therefore the greatness of the sūkta in hand is increased.

***apāṃ napāt*** — "*adbhya oṣadhayaḥ, oṣadhibhyo 'gniḥ*" (so on): from the waters the plants, and from the plants Agni is born; so Agni is called the "grandson" (*napāt*) of the waters. Or, *apāṃ na pātayitā* — he who does not cause the waters to fall [?]: in the form of lightning-Agni he "moves in front", and so Sāyaṇa explains this name, showing that derivation. The Nirukta author's explanation of *apāṃ napāt* is, like that of *tanūnapāt*:

> तनूनपादयं त्वेव नाम्ना यच्चेष्ट तनूनम् [?] ।
> नपादिति प्रजा माहुरमुतोऽस्य च सम्भवात् ॥

> *tanūnapādayaṃ tveva nāmnā yacceṣṭa tanūnam [?] |*
> *napāditi prajā māhuramuto 'sya ca sambhavāt ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-[?].) as *tanūnapāt* got his name because his own son was born from his own body [?], and as in many places it is said, *apāṃ napāt* too has this same explanation. This matter is told fully in the Special Topics of Ṛg Saṃhitā, part 10 [?], Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?]. Now whether the deity *apāṃ napāt* is distinct from Agni or is only Agni is the subject of a dispute. Earlier, in discussing the deity Tanūnapāt in the Āprī-sūkta (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-142), we cited the Bṛhaddevatā and others and said that the deity is Agni in form; it is also clear that Agni and Apāṃ Napāt are not distinct. Looking at the Ṛks, it appears that in the Ṛks the word *apāṃ napāt* is for some places given as a separate deity from Agni [?], and Agni too (2-[?]; 3-[?]) as an Āprī deity; but it is stated that when the two are combined they are the same deity. According to the Nirukta author, the deity *apāṃ napāt* and the deity Tanūnapāt are one; hence the same sort of explanation tells the nature of two deities. In the present context, it must be considered in which place the deity *apāṃ napāt* occurs in the Ṛk. In the sūktas to the Viśvedevas the deity *apāṃ napāt* is seen to be (referred to in) many *ārabdha* [?] places.

### Printed p. 294  (PDF 312)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 143".)*

> प्र नः पूषा चरथं विश्वदेव्योऽपां नपादवतु वायुरिष्टये ।
> आत्मानं वस्यो अभि वातमर्चत तदश्विना सुहवा यामनि श्रुतम् ॥

> *pra naḥ pūṣā carathaṃ viśvadevyo 'pāṃ napādavatu vāyuriṣṭaye |*
> *ātmānaṃ vasyo abhi vātamarcata tadaśvinā suhavā yāmani śrutam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk Pūṣan, then Apāṃ Napāt, are prayed for, among the Viśvedevas. In the third Ṛk of this sūkta (10-[?]-3) Agni is praised as the increaser of the sacrifice. In the second Maṇḍala, Ṛks in the sūkta 2-[?]-[?] say *ajaikapāt*, *ahirbudhnya*, *samudra*, *apāṃ napāt* and *pṛśni*; these deities are taken together; and in the first Ṛk of the same, Indra and Agni; and in the fourth Ṛk, Agni. In the Ṛk of the earlier sūkta, 2-[?]-[?], *apāṃ napāt* and Agni, and of the 3rd Ṛk and the 2nd, *apāṃ napāt* as protector and Mitra as well are mentioned [?]. In the seventh Maṇḍala, in the sūkta 7-[?]-[?], in the 2nd Ṛk with *apāṃ napāt* other deities are invoked; and in the 4th Ṛk and in the 2nd Agni is prayed for. In this way, in 2-[?] and in 7-[?] sūktas, both Agni and Apāṃ Napāt are mentioned separately. In none of these Ṛks is it found that Agni and Apāṃ Napāt are one deity. In the whole of the sūkta 2-[?], *apāṃ napāt* is the sole deity; only in the [?]th Ṛk is Agni addressed; from there to the end no Ṛk names Agni; yet it must be interpreted as being about Agni; only the 2nd and 4th Ṛks are explicit (…); even there the description does not make Agni evident. Taking these examples, the scholar Bloomfield has given his opinion thus —

"While Agni became more and more conspicuous, Apam Napat seems to have waned in popularity, until he was so far forgotten that a confusion arose concerning the two uses of the expression (अपां नपात्) and Apam Napat, "the son of the waters" was swallowed up in Agni, a "son of the waters" as he was occasionally (twice in the Rik) called, since he too, because of his original lightning nature, was supposed to have been born of the rain-clouds. To the same source is to be traced the myth of his hiding in the waters, for this myth probably had no connection originally with Apam Napat, beyond the mere fact that both he and Agni were forms of lightning which, appearing when the thunderstorm was at its height, seemed to disappear in the clouds from which they came.

The conclusion seems to be warranted, therefore, that Agni and Apam Napat were once distinct Gods—Gods, of the lightning, who were, however, associated with each other and

were much alike in certain particulars, and that this association, and resemblance ultimately resulted, possibly at the close of the Vedic Period, in a confusion and Union of the two, as a result of which Apam Napat was absorbed by Agni."

(Journal of American Oriental Society. Vol. XIX. (2) p. 144. — English as printed.)

***tavyasīm*** — तवीयसीमतिशयेन वर्धयित्रीं तवतिर्वृद्ध्यर्थः (*tavīyasīmatiśayena vardhayitrīṃ tavatirvṛddhyarthaḥ*): "the one who increases exceedingly; the root *tavati* has the sense of growth"; it is an epithet of *dhītim*, "giving strength" or "bringing about growth"; so too *matim*. For instance,

> स शेवृधमधि धा द्युम्नमस्मे महि क्षत्रं जनाषाळिन्द्र तव्यम् ।
> रक्षा च नो मघोनः पाहि सूरीन्राये च नः स्वपत्या इषे धाः ॥

> *sa śevṛdhamadhi dhā dyumnamasme mahi kṣatraṃ janāṣāḷindra tavyam |*
> *rakṣā ca no maghonaḥ pāhi sūrīnrāye ca naḥ svapatyā iṣe dhāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?].) in this Ṛk *tavyam kṣatram* has the sense of "strength" (*balam*) and "possessing power" (*prabhūta*, *śaktiyukta*), both meanings being indicated.

***dhītim*** — यागफलानामुत्कृष्टगुणकं कर्म (*yāgaphalānāmutkṛṣṭaguṇakaṃ karma*): "an act that has the excellent quality of the fruits of sacrifice"; the sacrificial act, the one in the form of sacrifice. *Dhīti* has two meanings, *karma* and *prajñā*. [In the Nirukta it is read among names of action, Ni. 2-[?], and among names of intelligence]. The Nirukta author, citing two Ṛks in support, —

> इयं शुष्मेभिर्बिसखा इवारुजत्सानु गिरीणां तविषेभिरूर्मिभिः ।
> पारावतघ्नीमवसे सुवृक्तिभिः सरस्वतीमा विवासेम धीतिभिः ॥

> *iyaṃ śuṣmebhirbisakhā ivārujatsānu girīṇāṃ taviṣebhirūrmibhiḥ |*
> *pārāvataghnīmavase suvṛktibhiḥ sarasvatīmā vivāsema dhītibhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-61-2.) in this Ṛk *dhītibhiḥ* is explained as *karmabhiḥ* ("by actions");

> ऋतस्य हि शुरुधः सन्ति पूर्वीरृतस्य धीतिर्वृजिनानि हन्ति ।
> ऋतस्य श्लोको बधिरा ततर्द कर्णा बुधानः शुचमान आयोः ॥

> *ṛtasya hi śurudhaḥ santi pūrvīrṛtasya dhītirvṛjināni hanti |*
> *ṛtasya śloko badhirā tatarda karṇā budhānaḥ śucamāna āyoḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-23-8.) in this *dhīti* is explained as *prajñā*. In many places this word is used also in the sense of "praise". In the Ṛk in hand it means "the act that is the sacrifice".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar page, noted briefly).** *tavyasīm* (the root *tavati*, formed by the sūtras, is used in the sense of growth; *ṇvultṛcau* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-133): suffix *tṛc*; *[chandasi…]* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-[?]): the suffix *īyasun* after *tṛc*; *turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-154): loss of *tṛc*; *yasyeti ca* drops the *a*; Vedic …) *(continues on p. 296)*.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1, concluded; grammar page, noted briefly).** *tavyasīm* (continued: the suffix-*ī* is dropped; since *īyasun* is *nit*, by *ñnityādir nityam* the first syllable is *udātta*), *navyasīm* (when *īyasun* comes in the sense of excess, the *a* is dropped as before; the accent as before), *matim* (*mantre vṛṣeṣa…* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-96): *ktin* is *udātta*; accusative singular), *bhare* (root *bhṛñ bharaṇe*; *laṭ*, first person singular; *tiṅ*-*nighāta* accent), *apām* (*ūḍidaṃ padādi…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171): the case-ending is *udātta*), *napāt* (root *pā rakṣaṇe*; with *śatṛ* the form is *pāt*; with *nañ* prefixed in the compound, *nabhrāṇnapāt…* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-75): formed irregularly with non-loss of *n* [i.e. *na* is retained]), *pṛthivyām* (the word *pṛthivī* is *jas*-ending [?: ṅīṣ-ending, *antodātta*]; when a case-ending follows, *yaṇ* is the substitute, and as the case-ending after it is *anudātta*, *udāttayaṇo…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-174) gives it the *udātta* accent), *asīdet* (root *ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-6): *laṅ* in the present sense; third person singular, *tip*; *itaś ca*: loss of *i*; *śap*; *pāghrādhmā…* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-78): *sīda* for the root; because of the connection with *yaḥ* (the relative) there is no *nighāta*; the augment *aṭ* is *udātta*, so the first syllable is *udātta*), *ṛtviyaḥ* (*ṛtu*; *yajñartvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau* (Pā. Sū. 5-1-71): suffix *gha*; *āyaneyī…* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-2): *iya*; *yasyeti ca* drops the *a*; by the first-syllable *udātta* of the suffix the *i* is *udātta*). ‖ 1 ‖

#### Ṛk 2

### Printed p. 297  (PDF 315)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 14 [?].)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स जायमानः परमे व्योमन्याविरग्निरभवन्मातरिश्वने ।
> अस्य क्रत्वा समिधानस्य मज्मना प्र द्यावा शोचिः पृथिवी अरोचयत् ॥ २ ॥

> *sa jāyamānaḥ parame vyomanyāviragnirabhavanmātariśvane |*
> *asya kratvā samidhānasya majmanā pra dyāvā śociḥ pṛthivī arocayat ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । जायमानः । परमे । विऽओमनि । आविः । अग्निः । अभवत् । मातरिश्वने ।
> अस्य । क्रत्वा । सम्ऽइधानस्य । मज्मना । प्र । द्यावा । शोचिः । पृथिवी इति । अरोचयत् ॥ २ ॥

> *saḥ | jāyamānaḥ | parame | vi 'omani | āviḥ | agniḥ | abhavat | mātariśvane |*
> *asya | kratvā | sam 'idhānasya | majmanā | pra | dyāvā | śociḥ | pṛthivī iti | arocayat ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *That Agni, as soon as born from the two fire-sticks, appeared before Mātariśvan (the wind) in the highest atmosphere; kindled by mighty effort, his flame lit up heaven and earth; an alternative: Mātariśvan is the sacrificer and the "firmament" is the altar.* Small type; some words doubtful)

> स पूर्वोक्तोऽग्निर्जायमानोऽरणिभ्यामुत्पद्यमानः काष्ठेषु वा प्रादुर्भूतः सन् तदानीमेव परमे उत्कृष्टे व्योमनि विविधरक्षणवति [?] नेदिदेशे [?] मातरिश्वने अन्तरिक्षसंचारिणे वायवे प्रथममाविरभवत् । प्रत्यक्षोऽभूत् । श्रूयते च — अग्ने प्रथमो मातरिश्वन आविर्भव (ऋ. १-३१-३) इत्यादि प्रत्यन्तरप्रसिद्धेः । वायुसंयोगात् प्रज्वलतीत्यर्थः । अथवा मातरि फलस्य निर्मात्र्यां यज्ञे श्वसिति चेष्टते इति मातरिश्वा यजमानः । तदर्थं कृतं [?] किंचित् समिधानस्येन्धनैः सम्यग्गृह्यमाणस्याग्नेर्मज्मना बलनामैतत् । बलवता क्रत्वा कर्मणा ज्वालनाव्यापारेण शोचिर्द्युलोकं पृथिवीं च प्रारोचयत् । प्रकर्षेण दीपयत् ॥ मज्मना क्रत्वा समिधानस्येति वा योज्यं । प्रबलेन समिन्धनाध्यापारेण समिद्ध्यमानस्येत्यर्थः ॥

> *sa pūrvokto 'gnirjāyamāno 'raṇibhyāmutpadyamānaḥ kāṣṭheṣu vā prādurbhūtaḥ san tadānīmeva parame utkṛṣṭe vyomani vividharakṣaṇavati [?] nedideśe [?] mātariśvane antarikṣasaṃcāriṇe vāyave prathamamāvirabhavat | pratyakṣo 'bhūt | śrūyate ca — agne prathamo mātariśvana āvirbhava (ṛ. 1-31-3) ityādi pratyantaraprasiddheḥ | vāyusaṃyogāt prajvalatītyarthaḥ | athavā mātari phalasya nirmātryāṃ yajñe śvasiti ceṣṭate iti mātariśvā yajamānaḥ | tadarthaṃ kṛtaṃ [?] kiṃcit samidhānasyendhanaiḥ samyaggṛhyamāṇasyāgnermajmanā balanāmaitat | balavatā kratvā karmaṇā jvālanāvyāpāreṇa śocirdyulokaṃ pṛthivīṃ ca prārocayat | prakarṣeṇa dīpayat ‖ majmanā kratvā samidhānasyeti vā yojyaṃ | prabalena samindhanādhyāpāreṇa samiddhyamānasyetyarthaḥ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *saḥ* — that, described before; *agniḥ* — Agni; *jāyamānaḥ* — as soon as he was born; *parame* — in the highest; *vyomani* — in the atmosphere; *mātariśvane* — before the wind; *āviḥ abhavat* — became manifest; [*vyomani* — on the altar; *mātariśvane* — before the sacrificer; *āviḥ abhavat* — became manifest]; (and) *majmanā* — of great power; *kratvā* — by his act of blazing and the like; *samidhānasya asya* — of this Agni who is kindled by fuel; *śociḥ* — the radiance; *dyāvā* — heaven; *pṛthivī* — and earth; *pra arocayat* — lit up.

### Printed p. 298  (PDF 316)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 143".)*

**Bhāvārtha.** As soon as he was born, Agni became manifest before the wind in the excellent atmosphere. And the radiance of this Agni, kindled by fuels, with the power of blazing and so on, lit up heaven and earth.

**English Translation (as printed).** As soon as born, was that (Agni) manifested to Matarishwan in the highest atmosphere, and his radiance, kindled by vigorous effort, spread through heaven and earth.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** In this Ṛk it is described that Agni, as soon as he was born, became manifest in the sky (*vyoman*) before Mātariśvan, and that thereafter his kindled radiance lit up heaven and earth. Here two kinds of construction of the first half are possible. First: *vyomani* — in the atmosphere; *mātariśvane* — before Mātariśvan; *āvir abhavat* — became manifest. Second: *vyomani* — on the sacrificial altar; *mātariśvane* — before the sacrificer; *āvir abhavat*.

(1) That Agni became manifest to Mātariśvan in the *vyoman* is well known. The word *vyoman* is read among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 1-[?]): it is derived from the root *vī + om*, "to pervade, to cover"; the meaning is "the pervading atmosphere".

> त्वमग्ने प्रथमो मातरिश्वन आविर्भव सुक्रतो यो विवस्वते ।
> अरेजेतां रोदसी होतृवूर्ये सहोभिर्भारमयजो महो वसो ॥

> *tvamagne prathamo mātariśvana āvirbhava sukrato yo vivasvate |*
> *arejetāṃ rodasī hotṛvūrye sahobhirbhāramayajo maho vaso ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-3.) In such Ṛks it is well known that the manifestation of Agni, first to the wind, is in the form of lightning. Moreover,

> वह्निं यशसं विदथस्य केतुं सुप्राव्यं दूतं सद्योअर्थम् ।
> द्विजन्मानं रयिमिव प्रशस्तं रातिं भरद्भृगवे मातरिश्वा ॥

> *vahniṃ yaśasaṃ vidathasya ketuṃ suprāvyaṃ dūtaṃ sadyoartham |*
> *dvijanmānaṃ rayimiva praśastaṃ rātiṃ bharadbhṛgave mātariśvā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-60-1.) in such Ṛks it is said in many places that Mātariśvan brought the hidden Agni from a far-off place and gave him to the earth, for the use of Bhṛgu and Manu, the performers of sacrifice, and for the benefit of all creatures on earth.

### Printed p. 299  (PDF 317)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 14 [?].)*

Hence there is ample support for stating the first meaning. 

(2) In stating the second meaning, what ground there is, and whether it suffices, are to be considered. *Vyomani* — here *vedīdeśe* ("in the region of the altar") is Sāyaṇa's sense of the word *vyoman*: the root *vi* + *avati* (to protect) gives *vi-oman*, "a place endowed with various kinds of protection, the altar (*vedī*)": this is the explanation. In the Ṛks too, this word is seen to have this meaning in many places. For instance —

> इयं वेदिः परो अन्तः पृथिव्या अयं यज्ञो भुवनस्य नाभिः ।
> अयं सोमो वृष्णो अश्वस्य रेतो ब्रह्मायं वाचः परमं व्योम ॥

> *iyaṃ vediḥ paro antaḥ pṛthivyā ayaṃ yajño bhuvanasya nābhiḥ |*
> *ayaṃ somo vṛṣṇo aśvasya reto brahmāyaṃ vācaḥ paramaṃ vyoma ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-35.) in this Ṛk *vyoma* means "the highest place that protects", and

> ऋतेन ऋतं धरुणं धारयन्त यज्ञस्य शाके परमे व्योमन् ।
> दिवो धर्मन् धरुणे सेदुषो नॄञ्जातैरजातां अभि ये ननक्षुः ॥

> *ṛtena ṛtaṃ dharuṇaṃ dhārayanta yajñasya śāke parame vyoman |*
> *divo dharman dharuṇe seduṣo nṝñjātairajātāṃ abhi ye nanakṣuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-39-2 [?].) in this Ṛk *utkṛṣṭe sthāne* ("in the highest place") is *uttaravedī* (the northern altar): "in the *utkṛṣṭa uttaravedī*" is the meaning. Here, in the present Ṛk, if *vyoman* is taken as the *vedī*, then *mātariśvā* [would be] *mātari phalasya nirmātryāṃ yajñe śvasiti ceṣṭate iti mātariśvā*, "the one who moves in the sacrifice, the maker of the fruit"; so, since he conducts himself in the sacrifice that gives all kinds of fruit, *mātariśvā* means the sacrificer. Hence the sense: "Agni, as soon as kindled, became manifest on the altar for the sacrificer". The Brāhmaṇa sentence

> व्योमसदसि वै व्योमसद् [?] व्योमा वै पशुः [?] ।

> *vyomasadasi vai vyomasad [?] vyomā vai paśuḥ [?] |*

(Ai. Brā. 1-[?]; read with doubt.) supports this meaning.

As in the first sense, if *mātariśvan* means the wind, then Agni and this *mātariśvan* have relations that are to be considered as distinct, and Agni being manifest as having been brought by him will mean that the two are separate beings. Yet in the history stated here, if looked at carefully, there are some grounds for their identity —

> उदु ष्टुतः समिधा यज्ञो अद्यौद्वर्ष्मन् दिवो अधि नाभा पृथिव्याः ।
> मित्रो अग्निरीड्यो मातरिश्वा दूतो वक्षद्यजथाय देवान् ॥

> *udu ṣṭutaḥ samidhā yajño adyaudvarṣman divo adhi nābhā pṛthivyāḥ |*
> *mitro agnirīḍyo mātariśvā dūto vakṣadyajathāya devān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].)

### Printed p. 300  (PDF 318)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 143".)*

In this Ṛk, for the word *mātariśvā*, Sāyaṇa gives the sense of *mātari antarikṣe śvasiti*, "he who breathes in the atmosphere", that is *prāṇiti* (lives): "he who moves as the sun in the atmosphere", or *mātṛ-araṇye* "in the forest-mother (the fire-sticks)" he moves — in the atmosphere, or in the *araṇi*s; as Agni is moving in them, he is called by this name; the Nirukta authors too show this very derivation and explain it as Agni; so Sāyaṇa shows the basis of his own derivation. In the same way —

> तं शुभ्रमग्निमवसे हवामहे वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वानमुक्थ्यम् ।
> बृहस्पतिं मनुषो देवताताये विप्रं श्रोतारमतिथिं रघुष्यदम् ॥

> *taṃ śubhramagnimavase havāmahe vaiśvānaraṃ mātariśvānamukthyam |*
> *bṛhaspatiṃ manuṣo devatātāye vipraṃ śrotāramatithiṃ raghuṣyadam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-26-2.) in this Ṛk, and in *sa mātariśvā puruvārapuṣṭiḥ* ("that Mātariśvan of abundant nourishment") in the Ṛk 1-[?]-[?], the identity of Agni and Mātariśvan is declared; and in the Ṛk in the present context (1-143-2):

> उदस्तम्भीत्समिधा नाकमृष्वो ऽग्निर्भवन्नुत्तमो रोचनानाम् ।
> यदी भृगुभ्यः परि मातरिश्वा गुहा सन्तं हव्यवाहं समीधे ॥

> *udastambhītsamidhā nākamṛṣvo 'gnirbhavannuttamo rocanānām |*
> *yadī bhṛgubhyaḥ pari mātariśvā guhā santaṃ havyavāhaṃ samīdhe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].) in this Ṛk it is clear that the two are said to be separate. [But this is itself a sentence of Ṛk 3-9-4 [?], which says that Agni and Mātariśvan are identical, or that the word *mātariśvā* is an epithet of Agni.]

The other qualities and powers of Mātariśvan will be told later at the suitable contexts.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly).** *jāyamānaḥ* (root *janī prādurbhāve*; *śānac* in the present sense; *śyan* vikaraṇa; *jñājanor jā* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-79): *jā* substituted; *āne muk* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-82): the augment *muk* of the suffix; being after an *ati…* [word] *tāsyanudāttet* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) makes it *anudātta*; since *śyan* is *śit* [*sit*], first-syllable *udātta*), *mātariśvane* (*mātari śvayati iti mātariśvā*; *śvannukṣan…* (Uṇ. Sū. 1-[?]): formed by the suffix *kani*; dative singular; by the suffix-accent the *i* is *udātta*).

### Printed p. 301  (PDF 319)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 14 [?].)*

*kratvā* — *kratu* + *ā*; being followed by *ā*, *jasādiṣu chandasi vāvacanam* gives the non-occurrence of *nābhāva* [?]; *yaṇ* substituted.

*samidhānasya* — root *iñdhī dīptau*; *śānac* in the present sense; *bahulaṃ chandasi*: *luk* of the vikaraṇa; the suffix being *cit*, *anidītāṃ…* drops the nasal [of the root]; *śānac* being *cit*, the accent is last-syllable *udātta* by *citaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163); genitive singular.

*majmanā* — root *ṭumasjo śuddhau*; with *ṣoḍaśādika* [?] *manin* suffix; by the suffix-accent it is last-syllable *udātta* [?].

*dyāvāpṛthivī* — *dyauś ca pṛthivī ca dyāvāpṛthivyau*; *divo dyāvā* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-29) [?]: *dyāvā* for the former member; by Vedic usage *dyāvā* is used, and the word *śociḥ* becomes [?]; by *supāṃ sulug* the second case-ending gets *pūrvasavarṇa* lengthening.

*arocayat* — root *ruca dīptau*; *hetumati ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-26): *ṇic* indicating the causal action; *pugantalaghūpadhasya ca*: *guṇa* of the penultimate short vowel; *laṅ*, third person singular; being after an *ati…* word, the *tiṅ*-*nighāta* accent. ‖ 2 ‖

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अस्य त्वेषा अजरा अस्य भानवः सुसंदृशः सुप्रतीकस्य सुद्युतः ।
> भात्वक्षसो अत्यक्तुर्न सिन्धवोऽग्ने रेजन्ते असन्तो अजराः ॥ ३ ॥

> *asya tveṣā ajarā asya bhānavaḥ susaṃdṛśaḥ supratīkasya sudyutaḥ |*
> *bhātvakṣaso atyakturna sindhavo 'gne rejante asanto ajarāḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अस्य । त्वेषाः । अजराः । अस्य । भानवः । सुऽसंदृशः । सुऽप्रतीकस्य । सुऽद्युतः ।
> भात्वक्षसः । अति । अक्तुः । न । सिन्धवः । अग्नेः । रेजन्ते । असन्तः । अजराः ॥ ३ ॥

> *asya | tveṣāḥ | ajarāḥ | asya | bhānavaḥ | su 'saṃdṛśaḥ | su 'pratīkasya | su 'dyutaḥ |*
> *bhātvakṣasaḥ | ati | aktuḥ | na | sindhavaḥ | agneḥ | rejante | asantaḥ | ajarāḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Ṛk 3; Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *The blazing, undecaying rays of this lovely-faced Agni spread everywhere, bright, piercing the darkness of night, and never cease from their work; like the streams of a river, or the rays of the sun, they are never idle.* Small type, only partly read)

> अस्य स्तूयमानस्याग्नेस्त्वेषा दीप्तयोऽजरा जरारहिता अजीर्णाः । अविरीताः [?] इत्यर्थः । नीलो [?] जरमारेतादि [?] … कथा सुप्रतीकस्य शोभनमुखस्याग्नेर्भानवो रश्मयः । दीप्तेरुक्तत्वादत्र विष्णुलिङ्गा [?] … ते च सुसंदृशः सुष्ठु सम्यग्द्रष्टारः [?] सर्वतो व्याप्ता इत्यर्थः । सुद्युतः सुष्ठु सर्वतो द्योतमानाः । त्वक्षः इति बलनाम त्वक्षः शर्धः इति बलनामसु पाठात् । भासमानं बलम् । अक्तूरिति रात्रिनामैतत् । अक्तून् [?] … । द्वितीयोर्थे प्रथमा । अक्तुं जगद्व्यञ्जकं नैकं तमोऽतिक्रम्य सिन्धवः स्यन्दमानाः सर्वत्र व्याप्नुवन्तोऽसन्तः स्वव्यापारेष्वसन्तोऽविरीताः । अतएव अजरा न रेजन्ते । न कम्पन्ते । दाहपाकादिषु न चलन्ति न चाल्यन्ते वान्यैः । यद्वा [?] … भात्वक्षसो भा इव त्वक्षो बलं यस्य ताद्वशस्यादित्यस्य सिन्धवो न रश्मय इव । ते यथा स्यन्दनशीला व्याप्तिमन्तः ॥ [?]

> *asya stūyamānasyāgnestveṣā dīptayo 'jarā jarārahitā ajīrṇāḥ | avirītāḥ [?] ityarthaḥ | nīlo [?] jaramāretādi [?] … kathā supratīkasya śobhanamukhasyāgnerbhānavo raśmayaḥ | dīpteruktatvādatra viṣṇuliṅgā [?] … te ca susaṃdṛśaḥ suṣṭhu samyagdraṣṭāraḥ [?] sarvato vyāptā ityarthaḥ | sudyutaḥ suṣṭhu sarvato dyotamānāḥ | tvakṣaḥ iti balanāma tvakṣaḥ śardhaḥ iti balanāmasu pāṭhāt | bhāsamānaṃ balam | aktūriti rātrināmaitat | aktūn [?] … | dvitīyorthe prathamā | aktuṃ jagadvyañjakaṃ naikaṃ tamo 'tikramya sindhavaḥ syandamānāḥ sarvatra vyāpnuvanto 'santaḥ svavyāpāreṣvasanto 'virītāḥ | ataeva ajarā na rejante | na kampante | dāhapākādiṣu na calanti na cālyante vānyaiḥ | yadvā [?] … bhātvakṣaso bhā iva tvakṣo balaṃ yasya tādvaśasyādityasya sindhavo na raśmaya iva | te yathā syandanaśīlā vyāptimantaḥ ‖ [?]*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *asya* — of this Agni; *tveṣāḥ* — the radiances; *ajarāḥ* — free from decay; *supratīkasya* — who has an excellent face; *asya* — of this Agni; *bhānavaḥ* — the rays (sparks); *susaṃdṛśaḥ* — which spread so as to be visible to all; *sudyutaḥ* — most bright; *agneḥ* — of Agni; [*bhātvakṣasaḥ* — the powers of brilliant form]; *aktūn* — the darkness that pervades (the world); *ati* — crossing over (piercing); *sindhavaḥ* — flowing; *asantaḥ* — without breaks (in their work); *ajarāḥ* — not wasting away; *na rejante* — (in their tasks) they do not hesitate; [(or) *bhātvakṣasaḥ* — the sun, with brilliant strength; *sindhavaḥ na* — like rays; *aktūn ati* — piercing the darkness; *asantaḥ* — [and] without breaks (in their duties); *rejante* — they spread in the form of vibration].

**Bhāvārtha.** The radiances of Agni do not decay. The rays — the fire-crown — of this Agni of excellent face spread so as to be seen by all and are most bright. The radiance of this Agni, like the rays of the sun whose strength is brilliant, pierces the darkness that pervades the world, and without a break, undiminished in their work, they pervade the world.

### Printed p. 303  (PDF 321)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 14 [?].)*

**English Translation (as printed).** His radiance is undecaying ; the rays of him who is of pleasing aspect, are everywhere visible and bright : the intensely shining, all-pervading, unceasing, undecaying (rays) of Agni, desist not (from their functions).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** In this Ṛk the radiance of Agni and his power in the form of radiance, which pierce the darkness, are described as ever pursuing their work.

***supratīkasya*** — *pratīkam* means "face" (*mukha*), or "radiant" (*prakāśāḍhyam*), or "appearance" (*darśana*). The word *pratīka* means a face, or an appearance, in a body of brightness. The Nirukta author:

> यावन्नात्रमुषसो न प्रतीकं सुसंकाशं [?] … मातरिश्वा ।
> तावद्दधात्मन्युप यज्ञमायन् ब्राह्मणो होतुरवरो निषीदन [?] ॥

> *yāvannātramuṣaso na pratīkaṃ susaṃkāśaṃ [?] … mātariśvā |*
> *tāvaddadhātmanyupa yajñamāyan brāhmaṇo hoturavaro niṣīdana [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-[?]; partly legible.) Citing this Ṛk, he explains *pratīka* as "an appearance (*ābhāsa*) that has brightness (*kānti*)". In this Ṛk the word is used by combining the two meanings, "a shining appearance" and "face".

***bhānavaḥ*** — the word *bhānu* has two meanings, "sun" and "rays".

> उदपप्तन्नरुणा भानवो वृथा स्वायुजो अरुषीर्गा अयुक्षत ।
> अक्रन्नुषासो वयुनानि पूर्वथा रुशन्तं भानुमरुषीरशिश्रयुः ॥

> *udapaptannaruṇā bhānavo vṛthā svāyujo aruṣīrgā ayukṣata |*
> *akrannuṣāso vayunāni pūrvathā ruśantaṃ bhānumaruṣīraśiśrayuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-2.) In this Ṛk the "rays" of the ruddy dawns are being described, [rising] ……; their ruddy forms [are said to have been united with the sun / worked] …; thus for the word *bhānu* both meanings are seen in one and the same Ṛk. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

> कविरस्तो बृहता भानुनागा हव्या जुषस्व ।

> *kavirasto bṛhatā bhānunāgā havyā juṣasva |*

(Ai. Brā. 3-[?].) "with his great splendour, come; accept the offerings": thus great Agni is prayed to come with his radiance. In the same way here the word means "rays", the radiating light of Agni.

***susaṃdṛśaḥ*** — *suṣṭhu samyag draṣṭāraḥ* [?]: "seen well by all"; the meaning is "pervading so as to be visible to all".

### Printed p. 304  (PDF 322)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 143".)*

***aktūn*** — this word is read among the names of Night, in the list beginning with *śyāvī*, *kṣapā*, *śarvarī* (Ni. 1-[?]). In many places the word *aktu* means "night"; it has also the meanings "ray", "weapon" and the like. The root *añj* gives the sense of "to cover", "to anoint", "to be bright", and so "to pervade"; from this, "night" (as it covers); "ray" (as it spreads); "weapon" (as it covers the body): these are the meanings. For example —

> घनेव विष्वग्वि जह्यराव्णस्तपुर्जम्भ यो अस्मध्रुक् ।
> यो मर्त्यः शिशीते अत्यक्तुभिर्मा नः स रिपुरीशत ॥

> *ghaneva viṣvagvi jahyarāvṇastapurjambha yo asmadhruk |*
> *yo martyaḥ śiśīte atyaktubhirmā naḥ sa ripurīśata ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-36-[?].) In this Ṛk *aktubhiḥ* is explained as *āvarakair āyudhaiḥ* ("with covering weapons"). It is thus that in this meaning the word has been employed in the plural; the use of the meanings "night", "ray" and "darkness (that spreads with night)" is greater.

> उत्तानायामजनयन्सुषूतं भुवदग्निः पुरुपेशासु गर्भः ।
> शिरिणायां चिदक्तुना महोभिरपरीवृतो वसति प्रचेताः ॥

> *uttānāyāmajanayansuṣūtaṃ bhuvadagniḥ purupeśāsu garbhaḥ |*
> *śiriṇāyāṃ cidaktunā mahobhiraparīvṛto vasati pracetāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-1-[?].) In such Ṛks *aktunā* is *añjanādiguṇakena tamasā*, "by the darkness that has the quality of covering". As explained here also in the present Ṛk, the meaning of *aktūn* is "the darkness that pervades the world": the Agni, radiance, is said to pierce such darkness.

***asantaḥ*** — *svavyāpāreṣu asajjantaḥ aviratāḥ* ("not clinging, ceaseless, in their own tasks"): without sloth, with unbroken activity in their own tasks, "endowed with ceaseless activity", the meaning. The Nirukta author —

> अति वायोः ससतो याहि शश्वतो यत्र ग्रावा वदति तत्र गच्छतं गृहमिन्द्रश्च गच्छतम् ।
> वि सूनृता ददृशे रीयते घृतमा पूर्णया नियुता याथो अध्वरमिन्द्रश्च याथो अध्वरम् ॥

> *ati vāyoḥ sasato yāhi śaśvato yatra grāvā vadati tatra gacchataṃ gṛhamindraśca gacchatam |*
> *vi sūnṛtā dadṛśe rīyate ghṛtamā pūrṇayā niyutā yātho adhvaramindraśca yātho adhvaram ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-135-2.) citing this Ṛk, explains the word *sasataḥ* as "those who sleep" (*ālasyādinā nidrāṃ kurvataḥ*): such sloth and sleep do not exist for them (the rays), who are constantly engaged in their tasks.

***bhātvakṣasaḥ*** — *tvakṣaḥ*, *śardhaḥ* are read as names of strength (Ni. 2-[?]; Nigh. 2-9 [?]) so *bhāsamānabalāḥ*: "those whose strength shines": the word *tvakṣa* is read among the names of strength, the meaning is "the shining power"…

### Printed p. 305  (PDF 323)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 14 [?].)*

> इन्द्रियं वीर्यमात्मन्धत्ते तेजो वा अग्निरिन्द्रियं वीर्यमिन्द्र उभे वीर्ये [?] ।

> *indriyaṃ vīryamātmandhatte tejo vā agnirindriyaṃ vīryamindra ubhe vīrye [?] |*

(Śa. Brā. 3-[?]-[?]-1.) By such Brāhmaṇa sentences the powers of Agni in the form of brilliance are described here.

In this Ṛk Sāyaṇa has shown two modes of construction for the second half. First —

*sindhavaḥ, asantaḥ, ajarāḥ* are epithets of *bhātvakṣasaḥ*: the powers (*śakti*), in the form of brilliance, which flow, which have no break in their tasks, and which do not waste away; *na rejante* is taken [as a negative], "they do not tremble": so that in their works they do not shiver; second:

> न शब्दो दृष्टान्तवचनः । भात्वक्षसो भा इव त्वक्षो बलं यस्य ताद्दृशस्यादित्यस्य सिन्धवो न रश्मय इव । ते यथा स्यन्दनशीला व्याप्तिमन्तः । अक्तूरति अञ्जनं तमोऽतिक्रम्यासन्तो रेजन्ते तद्वद्भात्वक्षसोऽस्याग्नेरुक्तलक्षणा दीप्तयोऽपि सर्वत्र रेजन्ते कम्पन्ते । व्याप्नुवन्तीत्यर्थः ।

> *na śabdo dṛṣṭāntavacanaḥ | bhātvakṣaso bhā iva tvakṣo balaṃ yasya tāddṛśasyādityasya sindhavo na raśmaya iva | te yathā syandanaśīlā vyāptimantaḥ | aktūrati añjanaṃ tamo 'tikramyāsanto rejante tadvadbhātvakṣaso 'syāgneruktalakṣaṇā dīptayo 'pi sarvatra rejante kampante | vyāpnuvantītyarthaḥ |*

Here the *na* is "a word of comparison": "the rays of Āditya, of whom the strength is, as it were, brilliance (*bhā*): *sindhavaḥ na*, like rays; as they are flowing and pervading, and, crossing the darkness, unceasing they shake [spread]; so likewise the radiances of this Agni, described before, everywhere shake [spread]": the meaning is that they pervade. This is a *dṛṣṭānta* ("simile"); the author, taking the rays of the sun that pierce the darkness and pervade the world without interruption in their action, explains that the flames of Agni pervade in the same way.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar page, noted briefly).** *tveṣāḥ* (root *tviṣ dīptau*; *pāṭādiṣu* …: since it is in the *pāṭādi* list, *ac* suffix; the root has *guṇa* by *laghūpadha*; since *cit* the end is *udātta*), *ajarāḥ* (*na vidyate jarā yeṣāṃ te ajarāḥ*; *nañsvara*: the *nañ* …; *nañsubhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172): the last member's final is *udātta*), *asya* (*ūḍidam padādi…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171): the case-ending is *udātta*), *bhānavaḥ* (root *bhā dīptau*; *bhābhyāṃ nuḥ* (Uṇ. Sū. 3-[?]): suffix *nu*; the suffix-accent gives the last syllable *udātta*), *susaṃdṛśaḥ* (*su* + *saṃ* + root *dṛśir prekṣaṇe*; suffix *kvip*; *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139): the natural accent of the *kṛdanta*; nominative plural), *supratīkasya* (*śobhanaṃ pratīkaṃ yasya saḥ supratīkaḥ*, genitive; *krtvāyeddha…* (Pā. Sū. 6-[?]-[?]): by *uttarapada* the first-syllable *udātta*) *(continues on p. 306)*.

*bhātvakṣasaḥ* (*bhā eva tvakṣaḥ balaṃ yasya saḥ bhātvakṣāḥ*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1): the first member keeps its accent), *rejante* (root *reja kampane*; *laṭ*, third person plural; being after an *ati…* word, the *nighāta* accent), *asantaḥ* (*na sasantaḥ asantaḥ*; root *pasa spṛṣṭau* [?: *ṣasa*]; *śatṛ* in the present sense; nominative plural; *tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2): the *nañ* has its natural accent). ‖ 3 ‖

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यमेरिरे भृगवो विश्ववेदसं नाभा पृथिव्या भुवनस्य मज्मना ।
> अग्निं तं गीर्भिर्हिनुहि स्व आ दमे य एको वस्वो वरुणो न राजति ॥ ४ ॥

> *yamerire bhṛgavo viśvavedasaṃ nābhā pṛthivyā bhuvanasya majmanā |*
> *agniṃ taṃ gīrbhirhinuhi sva ā dame ya eko vasvo varuṇo na rājati ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यम् । आऽईरिरे । भृगवः । विश्वऽवेदसम् । नाभा । पृथिव्याः । भुवनस्य । मज्मना ।
> अग्निम् । तम् । गीःऽभिः । हिनुहि । स्वे । आ । दमे । यः । एकः । वस्वः । वरुणः । न । राजति ॥ ४ ॥

> *yam | ā 'īrire | bhṛgavaḥ | viśva 'vedasam | nābhā | pṛthivyāḥ | bhuvanasya | majmanā |*
> *agnim | tam | gīḥ 'bhiḥ | hinuhi | sve | ā | dame | yaḥ | ekaḥ | vasvaḥ | varuṇaḥ | na | rājati ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *The Agni whom the Bhṛgus established on the navel of the earth, the lord of all wealth, ruling alone like Varuṇa: bring him by praises to our own house.* Small type; many words doubtful)

> विश्ववेदसं सर्वधनं । वेद इति धननाम वेदो वरिव इति तेन्नामसु पाठात् । तादृशं यमग्निं भृगवो भृगुगोत्रोत्पन्नाः पाप्त्य [?] भर्जकाः [?] पृथिव्या वेद्याः एकदेशे कृत्स्नशब्दः । यद्वा [?] स्थिता वै पृथिवीत्यादिश्रुतेर्वेद्याः [?]

> *viśvavedasaṃ sarvadhanaṃ | veda iti dhananāma vedo variva iti tennāmasu pāṭhāt | tādṛśaṃ yamagniṃ bhṛgavo bhṛgugotrotpannāḥ pāptya [?] bharjakāḥ [?] pṛthivyā vedyāḥ ekadeśe kṛtsnaśabdaḥ | yadvā [?] sthitā vai pṛthivītyādiśrutervedyāḥ [?]*

### Printed p. 307  (PDF 325)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 14 [?].)*

*(Continuation of the bhāṣya.)*

> पृथिवीत्वम् [?] । तस्मान्नाभावुत्तरवेद्यां भुवनस्य भूतजातस्य मज्मना बलेन निमित्तेन [?] तमग्निं स्वे स्वकीये दमे गृहे उत्तरवेद्यां गीर्भिः स्तुतिभिर्हिनुहि [?] प्रापय । हि गतौ वृद्धौ च । उत्तरवेद्यां इत्यादि । स्थितः पृष्ठे [?] यद्वा । उत्तरवेद्याः इत्यादि प्रत्ययानुवादेन [?] योऽग्निर्द्वन्द्वादीनां [?] एकः एकमात्रः सन् । एकैव वा वस्वो वसूनो गवादिधनस्य राजति ईश्वरो भवति । प्रदातुमिति शेषः । राजतिरैश्वर्यकर्मा [?] क्रियायुक्ताद्राजति राजतीति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । वरुणो न वारकः आदित्य इव । स यथा सर्वस्येशे तद्वत् ॥

> *pṛthivītvam [?] | tasmānnābhāvuttaravedyāṃ bhuvanasya bhūtajātasya majmanā balena nimittena [?] tamagniṃ sve svakīye dame gṛhe uttaravedyāṃ gīrbhiḥ stutibhirhinuhi [?] prāpaya | hi gatau vṛddhau ca | uttaravedyāṃ ityādi | sthitaḥ pṛṣṭhe [?] yadvā | uttaravedyāḥ ityādi pratyayānuvādena [?] yo 'gnirdvandvādīnāṃ [?] ekaḥ ekamātraḥ san | ekaiva vā vasvo vasūno gavādidhanasya rājati īśvaro bhavati | pradātumiti śeṣaḥ | rājatiraiśvaryakarmā [?] kriyāyuktādrājati rājatīti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | varuṇo na vārakaḥ āditya iva | sa yathā sarvasyeśe tadvat ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *yaḥ* — which Agni; *varuṇaḥ na* — like Āditya; *ekaḥ* — having sole lordship; *vasvaḥ* — of the cattle and other wealth; *rājati* — is the lord; (and) *viśvavedasam* — who possesses all wealth; *yam* — which Agni; *bhṛgavaḥ* — the sages born in the lineage of Bhṛgu; *pṛthivyāḥ* — of the altar; *nābhā* — in the northern part (of the altar); *bhuvanasya* — of all beings; *majmanā* — with strength; *īrire* — established; *taṃ agnim* — that Agni; *sve dame* — into your own house (the *uttaravedi*); *gīrbhiḥ* — with praises; *ā hinuhi* — bring.

**Bhāvārtha.** Bring, with praises, into the northern part of your own house, the altar, that Agni who rules alone, like Āditya, with sole lordship over the cattle and other wealth, and who is the possessor of all wealth, and whom the sages born in the lineage of Bhṛgu have established with the strength of all beings at the navel of the earth.

**English Translation (as printed).** Bring to his own abode with hymns that Agni, the possessor of all riches, whom the descendants of Bhrigu placed by the strength of all beings upon the navel of the earth : for, like Veruna [sic], he reigns sole (monarch) over (all) treasure.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** In this Ṛk, after praising Agni as the sole lord and as the owner of all wealth, the sacrificer is told to bring such a *viśvavedas* (all-wealthy) Agni, established on the northern part of the altar.

### Printed p. 308  (PDF 326)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 143".)*

***varuṇo na*** — here the commentator explains the word *varuṇa* as *vāraka*, "the restrainer", i.e. the Āditya. Agni's lordship is compared with the sole lordship of Āditya.

***rājati*** — *rājṛ dīptau* ("to shine"); *rājati* and the like are read among the names of the activity of lordship (*aiśvaryakarma*; Ni. 2-[?]). *Īśvaro bhavati*: he is the lord of all wealth.

> सप्त क्षरन्ति शिशवे मरुत्वते पित्रे पुत्रासो अप्यवीवतन्नृतम् ।
> उभे इदस्योभयस्य राजत उभे यतेते उभयस्य पुष्यतः ॥

> *sapta kṣaranti śiśave marutvate pitre putrāso apyavīvatannṛtam |*
> *ubhe idasyobhayasya rājata ubhe yatete ubhayasya puṣyataḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-13-[?].) In this Ṛk the word *rājate* is the illustration, the Nirukta author has shown, of the sense *īśate*, "rules"; here too the sense is the same.

***bhṛgavaḥ, īrire*** — भृगुगोत्रोत्पन्नाः (*bhṛgugotrotpannāḥ*): "sages born in the lineage of Bhṛgu established Agni first in the sacrificial house": this indicates the earlier story.

> अयमिह प्रथमो धायि धातृभिर्होता यजिष्ठो अध्वरेष्वीड्यः ।
> यमप्नवानो भृगवो विरुरुचुर्वनेषु चित्रं विभवं विशेविशे ॥

> *ayamiha prathamo dhāyi dhātṛbhirhotā yajiṣṭho adhvareṣvīḍyaḥ |*
> *yamapnavāno bhṛgavo virurucurvaneṣu citraṃ vibhavaṃ viśeviśe ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-3-[?]-[?].) In such Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentences it is told that the Bhṛgus first established Agni, who is the Hotṛ. In the Ṛk-saṃhitā too —

> दधुष्ट्वा भृगवो मानुषेष्वा रयिं न चारुं सुहवं जनेभ्यः ।
> होतारमग्ने अतिथिं वरेण्यं मित्रं न शेवं दिव्याय जन्मने ॥

> *dadhuṣṭvā bhṛgavo mānuṣeṣvā rayiṃ na cāruṃ suhavaṃ janebhyaḥ |*
> *hotāramagne atithiṃ vareṇyaṃ mitraṃ na śevaṃ divyāya janmane ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-58-6.)

> द्विता यदीं कीस्तासो अभिद्यवो नमस्यन्त उपवोचन्त भृगवो मथ्नन्तो दाशा भृगवे ।
> अग्निरीशे वसूनां शुचिर्यो धर्णिरेषां । प्रियाँ अपिधीर्वनिषीष्ट मेधिर आ वनिषीष्ट मेधिरः ॥

> *dvitā yadīṃ kīstāso abhidyavo namasyanta upavocanta bhṛgavo mathnanto dāśā bhṛgave |*
> *agnirīśe vasūnāṃ śuciryo dharṇireṣāṃ | priyā~ apidhīrvaniṣīṣṭa medhira ā vaniṣīṣṭa medhiraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks it is said, in many places, that the Bhṛgus, by churning, established Agni in the sacrificial house, and that, again, by Mātariśvan Agni was brought from a far-off place and praised. This context is indicated in the Ṛk in hand also.

### Printed p. 309  (PDF 327)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 14 [?].)*

***bhṛgave*** — भृज्जतो [?] हविषां पाकानां भर्जका वा (*bhṛjjato [?] haviṣāṃ pākānāṃ bharjakā vā*): "those who roast oblations (the cooked), or the roasters of the cooked"; since the Bhṛgus roast the oblations offered (*arpisuvavaru*), or since they remove sin, that is, they destroy sin, this name has been given to these sages by both kinds of power, Sāyaṇa explains. The Nirukta author:

"आर्चिति [?] भृगुः संभूतो भृगुर्भ्रज्यमानो न देहे" (Nirukta 3-[?]),

so, showing the derivation of the word *bhṛgu* ("Bhṛgu, sprung from the flame, was not consumed in the fire": having arisen from fire, he was not burnt in it), that sage is of this name. These two kinds of power, of Agni, are of great help to the sacrificial rites and also to destroying sin. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa —

> अथाङ्गारेभ्यो भृहति [?] । भृगूणामङ्गिरसां तेजसा तस्यैतन्नमुक्ते [?] भृग्वङ्गिरसां तेजसा तेजो यद्भृग्वङ्गिरसां सुकृप्तान्य सन्ति तस्मादेनमभ्यूहति [?] ।

> *athāṅgārebhyo bhṛhati [?] | bhṛgūṇāmaṅgirasāṃ tejasā tasyaitannamukte [?] bhṛgvaṅgirasāṃ tejasā tejo yadbhṛgvaṅgirasāṃ sukṛptānya santi tasmādenamabhyūhati [?] |*

(Śa. Brā. 1-3-[?]-[?]; partly legible.) By such sentences it is said that Bhṛgu and the Aṅgirasas are, by their connection with *vāk* [?], endowed with great radiance; and also —

> अयमिह प्रथमो धायि धातृभिर्होता यजिष्ठो अध्वरेष्वीड्य इत्यादि [?]

> *ayamiha prathamo dhāyi dhātṛbhirhotā yajiṣṭho adhvareṣvīḍya ityādi [?]*

(Tai. Brā. 3-[?]-[?]-[?]; and Tai. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].)

> द्वे अग्नेर्ज्योती [?] । द्विपाद्यजमानो यजमानोऽग्निर्यावान्नग्निर्यावत्यस्य मात्रा तावत्यैवैतद्यज्ञं संस्थापयतीष्टो यज्ञो भृगुभिराहुतोऽग्निरायुः [?] पिपर्ति [?] इति ।

> *dve agnerjyotī [?] | dvipādyajamāno yajamāno 'gniryāvānnagniryāvatyasya mātrā tāvatyaivaitadyajñaṃ saṃsthāpayatīṣṭo yajño bhṛgubhirāhuto 'gnirāyuḥ [?] piparti [?] iti |*

(Śa. Brā. 1-2-[?]-[?]; partly legible.) By such sentences the order in which the Bhṛgus honoured Agni and performed the sacrifice is also described.

***pṛthivyā nābhā bhuvanasya majmanā īrire*** — by this mantra the order in which the Bhṛgus established Agni is told. Here the word *pṛthivyā nābhā* is taken as meaning *uttaravedi*.

> उत्तरं परिग्राहं परि गृह्णात्येतावती वै पृथिवी यावती वेदिस्तस्या एतावत एव ।

> *uttaraṃ parigrāhaṃ pari gṛhṇātyetāvatī vai pṛthivī yāvatī vedistasyā etāvata eva |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-4-3 [?].) In such Saṃhitā sentences, as is said, *pṛthivī* is the *vedi*; here too it has been given the same sense. Thus on the *vedi* of the earth form, in the strength of all beings, the Bhṛgus established Agni.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar page, noted briefly).** *īrire* (root *īra gatau preraṇe ca*; *liṭ*, third person plural; *liṭas tajhayoḥ* … *irec* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-81): *ire* is the substitute; being after an *ati…* word, the *nighāta* accent), *viśvavedasam* (*viśvaṃ vedo yasya saḥ viśvavedāḥ*, tam; in the *bahuvrīhi* the first member keeps its natural accent), *nābhā* (*supāṃ sulug…* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39): *ā* replaces the case-ending), *majmanā* (root *ṭumasjo śuddhau*; *ṣoḍaśādika* suffix *manin*; by the suffix-accent first-syllable *udātta*; instrumental singular), *gīrbhiḥ* (root *gṝ śabde*; *kvip ca*: suffix *kvip*; *ṛta iddhātoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-100): the root vowel becomes *i*, *gir*; *bhis* following: *halī ca* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-77): lengthening of the penultimate), *hinuhi* (root *hi gatau vṛddhau ca*; *loṭ*, second person singular *sip*, *hi*; *svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ*: vikaraṇa *śnu*; *utaś ca pratyayāc chandasi vā vacanam* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-106): *hi* is *luk* [here not]; *sārvadhātukam apit*: since the suffix is *apit* the *guṇa* does not occur; being after an *ati…* word, the *tiṅ*-*nighāta* accent), *vasvaḥ* (the word *vasu*; with a *ṣaṣṭhī* case-ending following, by *jasādiṣu chandasi vā vacanam* the *num* is not added and *guṇa* etc. do not occur; *yaṇ* substitution).

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> न यो वराय मरुतामिव स्वनः सेनेव सृष्टा दिव्या यथाशनिः ।
> अग्निर्जम्भैस्तिगितैरत्ति भर्वति योधो न शत्रून्त्स वना नि ऋञ्जते ॥ ५ ॥

> *na yo varāya marutāmiva svanaḥ seneva sṛṣṭā divyā yathāśaniḥ |*
> *agnirjambhaistigitairatti bharvati yodho na śatrūntsa vanā ni ṛñjate ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> न । यः । वराय । मरुताम्ऽइव । स्वनः । सेनाऽइव । सृष्टा । दिव्या । यथा । अशनिः ।
> अग्निः । जम्भैः । तिगितैः । अत्ति । भर्वति । योधः । न । शत्रून् । सः । वना । नि । ऋञ्जते ॥ ५ ॥

> *na | yaḥ | varāya | marutām 'iva | svanaḥ | senā 'iva | sṛṣṭā | divyā | yathā | aśaniḥ |*
> *agniḥ | jambhaiḥ | tigitaiḥ | atti | bharvati | yodhaḥ | na | śatrūn | saḥ | vanā | ni | ṛñjate ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *The Agni who cannot be checked or restrained, like the roaring of the Maruts, like an army let loose, like a thunderbolt of heaven, consumes with his sharp jaws the forests as a warrior destroys his foes.* Small type, partly legible)

> योऽग्निर्वराय वरणाय निग्रहाय न शक्यो न भवति [?] । तत्र दृष्टान्तैर्योऽ… मरुतां स्वन इव । स यथा ग्राह्यः स्यात् तथा सृष्टा [?] पैरिकार्थं [?] प्रबलेनातिस्पष्टं [?] सेनेव । सा यथा ग्रहणं [?] तथा दिव्या [?] अशनिर्यथा [?] … निवार्यते [?] । अग्निः तीक्ष्णैर्जम्भैर्दन्तस्थानीयाभिज्वालाभिः । अत्ति । अस्मद्विरोधिनो भक्षयति । तथा भर्वति । हिंसति । भर्व हिंसायाम् । यास्कः [?] … भवतिरर्कर्मेति (नि. ३-२१ [?]) । यद्वा [?] … । योधो न योद्धा यथा शत्रून् भक्षयति तद्वत् । किंच [?] सोऽग्निः वनान्यरण्यानि वृक्षादिसमूहान् ऋञ्जते । निकरां प्रसाधयति । दहतीत्यर्थः ॥ ऋञ्जते प्रसाधनकर्मेति यास्कः [?] ॥

> *yo 'gnirvarāya varaṇāya nigrahāya na śakyo na bhavati [?] | tatra dṛṣṭāntairyo '… marutāṃ svana iva | sa yathā grāhyaḥ syāt tathā sṛṣṭā [?] pairikārthaṃ [?] prabalenātispaṣṭaṃ [?] seneva | sā yathā grahaṇaṃ [?] tathā divyā [?] aśaniryathā [?] … nivāryate [?] | agniḥ tīkṣṇairjambhairdantasthānīyābhijvālābhiḥ | atti | asmadvirodhino bhakṣayati | tathā bharvati | hiṃsati | bharva hiṃsāyām | yāskaḥ [?] … bhavatirarkarmeti (ni. 3-21 [?]) | yadvā [?] … | yodho na yoddhā yathā śatrūn bhakṣayati tadvat | kiṃca [?] so 'gniḥ vanānyaraṇyāni vṛkṣādisamūhān ṛñjate | nikarāṃ prasādhayati | dahatītyarthaḥ ‖ ṛñjate prasādhanakarmeti yāskaḥ [?] ‖*

### Printed p. 312  (PDF 330)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 143".)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *yaḥ* — which Agni; *marutāṃ svanaḥ iva* — like the roar of the Maruts; *varāya na* — not to be checked (not suppressible); *sṛṣṭā* — let loose (to destroy enemies); *senā iva* — like a mighty army; *divyā* — born in the sky (heaven); *aśaniḥ yathā* — like the thunderbolt; *varāya na* — not to be checked (unobstructible, with a spreading that is unrestrained); *agniḥ* — this Agni; *jambhaiḥ* — with his teeth, sharp; *yodhaḥ* — a warrior; *śatrūn na* — as he destroys enemies; *tigitaiḥ* — with the keen flames that are his teeth; *atti* — (our) enemies; *bhurvati* — destroys, causes loss; (and) *saḥ* — that Agni; *vanā* — the trees of the forests; *ni ṛñjate* — burns up completely.

**Bhāvārtha.** The roar of the Maruts is as unstoppable as, to destroy enemies, a mighty army let loose, or the thunderbolt born in heaven; likewise is the spread of this Agni, unstoppable; as a warrior destroys enemies, so this Agni destroys our enemies with his keen flames that are his teeth; and he burns up the trees of the forests entirely.

**English Translation (as printed).** Agni, who, like the roaring of the winds, like a victorious host, like the thunderbolt in heaven, is not to be arrested, devours and destroys (our foes) with sharpened teeth, and, as a warrior (annihilates his enemies) he, (Agni), lays waste the woods.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** In this Ṛk, the unrestrained spreading of Agni's flames is compared with the roar of the Maruts, the speed of a mighty army, and the thunderbolt that is not to be checked; and Agni is said to destroy the enemies as a warrior does, and to consume the trees. It is a description that is frightening in one way, and attractive in another. The same description is noticed, appearing as attractive and frightful, in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā —

> तव भ्रमास आशुया पतन्त्यनु स्पृश धृषता शोशुचानः ।
> तपूंष्यग्ने जुह्वा पतङ्गानसन्दितो वि सृज विष्वगुल्काः ॥

> *tava bhramāsa āśuyā patantyanu spṛśa dhṛṣatā śośucānaḥ |*
> *tapūṃṣyagne juhvā pataṅgānasandito vi sṛja viṣvagulkāḥ ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 4-2-[?]-[?].)

> ऋतावा भर्ता कृष्टीनामुत मध्य इद्वः । साधिमानां [?] कर्देवात्रेतं [?] … स आयुरानत्कुर्वि नासानो भद्राणि भद्रंकर्देवहूतिं नो अद्य ॥
> अक्रन्दद्ग्निः स्तनयन्निव द्यौः क्षामा रेरिहद्वीरुधः समञ्जन् ।
> सद्यो जज्ञानो वि हीमिद्धो अख्यदा रोदसी भानुना भात्यन्तः ॥

> *ṛtāvā bhartā kṛṣṭīnāmuta madhya idvaḥ | sādhimānāṃ [?] kardevātretaṃ [?] … sa āyurānatkurvi nāsāno bhadrāṇi bhadraṃkardevahūtiṃ no adya ‖*
> *akrandadgniḥ stanayanniva dyauḥ kṣāmā rerihadvīrudhaḥ samañjan |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-5-[?]-[?]; partly legible.)

> सप्त्रितानसन्नतुरोचनस्ताऽअजरेभिर्नानद्दद्भिर्यविष्ठ [?] ।
> यः पावकः पुरुतमः पुरूणि पृथून्यग्निरनुयाति भर्वन् ॥

> *saptritānasannaturocanastā 'ajarebhirnānaddadbhiryaviṣṭha [?] |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?]-[?]; partly legible.) In such sentences it is the case that Agni, like the roaring of the clouds in the atmosphere, makes a sound; with his radiant flames spreads like beautiful cloth; devours the trees and creepers caught around; and spreads all over with his flames that are the cause of fire in the atmosphere. As described in the Ṛk in hand, such a form of Agni, both attractive and terrible, is shown.

***varāya*** — *varaṇāya*, *nigrahāya* (*na*): "to check, to restrain". The word is derived both from the root *vṛñ* (*varaṇe*) giving the sense "to wish, to choose", and from the root *vṛ* (*āvaraṇe*) giving the sense "to check, to hide"; so it has been used in both meanings.

> यस्ता चकार स कुह स्विदिन्द्रः कमा जनं चरति कासु विक्षु ।
> कस्ते यज्ञो मनसे शं वराय को अर्क इन्द्र कतमः स होता ॥

> *yastā cakāra sa kuha svidindraḥ kamā janaṃ carati kāsu vikṣu |*
> *kaste yajño manase śaṃ varāya ko arka indra katamaḥ sa hotā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-30-[?].) In this Ṛk *varāya* is *tava varaṇāya* ("for choosing you") *kaḥ kīdṛśaḥ arkaḥ mantraḥ samarho bhavati*: "for the choice of you, what mantra will be capable of making you favourable?": the root *vṛñ* gives the sense "to choose, to select". Moreover, in the sūkta 8-44-22 [?], *varāya* is "to the excellent one (*śreṣṭhāya*), to the very self"; the meaning is thus obtained.

> इषा मन्दस्वादु तेऽरं वराय मन्यवे ।
> भुवत्त इन्द्र शं हृदे ॥

> *iṣā mandasvādu te 'raṃ varāya manyave |*
> *bhuvatta indra śaṃ hṛde ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].)

### Printed p. 314  (PDF 332)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 143".)*

*(Continuation of the Special Topics of Ṛk 5.)*

In such Ṛks, *varāya* is also used in the sense of "to restrain, to check"; as in *śatrunivārakāya manyave krodhāya* ("to wrath, which restrains enemies"), where the sense "restraining, obstructing" (*nivāraka*) is given; and the Ṛk in hand too gives the senses "to hold back", "to restrain" (*asādhya*, "one that cannot be mastered"), like the thunderbolt (*aśani*) which cannot be stopped from falling swiftly, so that Agni's spreading too cannot be checked; this is what the word expresses.

***tigitaiḥ*** — *niśitaiḥ, tīkṣṇaiḥ*: "sharp"; a word meaning "much", generally used as an epithet of weapons. For example —

> यो नः सनुत्य उत वा जिघत्नुरभिख्याय तं तिगितेन विध्य ।
> बृहस्पत आयुधैर्जेषि शत्रून्द्रुहे रीषन्तं परि धेहि राजन् ॥

> *yo naḥ sanutya uta vā jighatnurabhikhyāya taṃ tigitena vidhya |*
> *bṛhaspata āyudhairjeṣi śatrūndruhe rīṣantaṃ pari dhehi rājan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-30-8.) In this Ṛk *tigitena* ("sharp") shows the nature of a weapon. In the Ṛk in hand also, since it is an epithet of *jambhaiḥ* ("teeth"), and since the teeth of a boar and the like are keen as weapons, Agni's flames are compared with them, and so this epithet is fit.

***bhurvati*** — *avayāti*, *bhurvati* are read among the names of the activity of oppressing (*atti-karma*; Ni. 2-[?]); the sense is "devours" (*bhakṣayati*). The same sense is given in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], as Sāyaṇa too has cited, *bhurvan agnir ayasayāti* [?] and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā passages too. The sense is "Agni consumes with his flames all the creepers and trees".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar page, noted briefly).** *varāya* (*vriyate iti varaḥ*; root *vṛñ varaṇe*; *grahavṛdṛniścigamaś ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-58): suffix *ap*; *guṇa* of the *ṛ* because of the suffix; since *ap* is *pit* the root accent remains; dative singular), *sṛṣṭā* (root *sṛja visarge*; *niṣṭhā*: *kta* in the passive; *vraścabhrasja…*: *ṣatva* of the *j*; by *ṣṭutva* the *ta* of the suffix becomes *ṭa*; the feminine intended, *ṭāp* by *ajādyatas ṭāp*), *divyā* (*divi bhavā divyā*; *daṇḍādigaṇapaṭhitatvāt* [?] (Pā. Sū. 5-1-[?]): suffix *ya*; by the suffix-accent the last syllable is *udātta*; in the feminine, *ṭāp* by *ajādyatas ṭāp*), *aśaniḥ* (root *aśa bhojane*; *arti-stu-sṛ…* (Uṇ. Sū. 2-[?]): suffix *ani*; by the suffix-accent the middle is *udātta*) …

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> कुविन्नो अग्निरुचथस्य वीरसद्वसुष्कुविद्वसुभिः कामुमावरत् [?] ।
> चोदः कुवित्तुतुज्यात्सातये धियः शुचिप्रतीकं तमया धिया गृणे ॥ ६ ॥

> *kuvinno agnirucathasya vīrasadvasuṣkuvidvasubhiḥ kāmumāvarat [?] |*
> *codaḥ kuvittutujyātsātaye dhiyaḥ śucipratīkaṃ tamayā dhiyā gṛṇe ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> कुवित् । नः । अग्निः । उचथस्य । वीः । असत् । वसुः । कुवित् । वसुऽभिः । कामम् । आऽवरत् ।

> *kuvit | naḥ | agniḥ | ucathasya | vīḥ | asat | vasuḥ | kuvit | vasu 'bhiḥ | kāmam | ā 'varat |*

> अयमग्निर्नोऽस्माकमुचथस्य स्तोत्रस्य कुविद्बहुवारं वीः कामयितासत् । भवतु । अस्त्रेर्लेट्याडागमः ॥ यद्वा । उचथस्येत्यन्नामकस्य [?] महर्षेर्गोत्रप्रभवस्य नः इति सम्बन्धः । तथा वसुर्वासयिता सर्वेषां वसुस्थानीयो वा वसुभिर्धनैः [?] कामं कामयमर्थमभिमतं वा कुविदिति प्रभूतमावरत् । आवृणोतु । अभिमतप्रदानेन कामं निवर्तयतु इत्यर्थः । वृणोतेर्लेट्याडागमः । छान्दसो विकरणस्य लुक् । अयमग्निर्देवोऽस्माकं कर्मसु प्रेरकः सन् धियः कर्मणां लाभाय कुविद्बहु तुतुज्यात् । त्वरयतु । प्रेरयतु इत्यर्थः । तुज हिंसायाम् [?] । छान्दसः शपः श्लुः । शुचिप्रतीकं शोभनमुखं शोधनज्वालं [?] तमग्निमया धियानया स्तुतिरूपया प्रज्ञया गृणे । उच्चारयामि । स्तौमीत्यर्थः ॥

> *ayamagnirno 'smākamucathasya stotrasya kuvidbahuvāraṃ vīḥ kāmayitāsat | bhavatu | astrerleṭyāḍāgamaḥ ‖ yadvā | ucathasyetyannāmakasya [?] maharṣergotraprabhavasya naḥ iti sambandhaḥ | tathā vasurvāsayitā sarveṣāṃ vasusthānīyo vā vasubhirdhanaiḥ [?] kāmaṃ kāmayamarthamabhimataṃ vā kuviditi prabhūtamāvarat | āvṛṇotu | abhimatapradānena kāmaṃ nivartayatu ityarthaḥ | vṛṇoterleṭyāḍāgamaḥ | chāndaso vikaraṇasya luk | ayamagnirdevo 'smākaṃ karmasu prerakaḥ san dhiyaḥ karmaṇāṃ lābhāya kuvidbahu tutujyāt | tvarayatu | prerayatu ityarthaḥ | tuja hiṃsāyām [?] | chāndasaḥ śapaḥ śluḥ | śucipratīkaṃ śobhanamukhaṃ śodhanajvālaṃ [?] tamagnimayā dhiyānayā stutirūpayā prajñayā gṛṇe | uccārayāmi | staumītyarthaḥ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *agniḥ* — Agni; *naḥ* — our; *ucathasya* — praise; *kuvit* — often; *vīḥ* — desirous; *asat* — let him be; *vasuḥ* — Agni, the giver of wealth, or the dwelling-place of all; *vasubhiḥ* — with riches; *kāmam* — our desired object; *kuvit* — in the utmost measure; *āvarat* — let him fill and satisfy; *codaḥ* — as the inspirer (of our rites for us); *dhiyaḥ* — our sacrificial rites; *sātaye* — for the gaining of the fruit; *kuvit* — in the utmost measure; *tutujyāt* — let him urge and cause to be completed; *śucipratīkam* — who has radiant flames; *tam agnim* — that Agni; *ayā dhiyā* — with this thoughtful praise; *gṛṇe* — I praise.

**Bhāvārtha.** May Agni be desirous of our praise; may Agni, the giver of wealth, satisfy our desired object abundantly with riches. May he, the inspirer of our rites, urge our sacrifice so that it is completed for the gaining of its fruit. I praise this Agni, of radiant flames, with this praise in the form of a meditative thought.

**English Translation (as printed).** May Agni be ever desirous of our praise ; may the giver of wealth satisfy our utmost expectation with riches ; may the inspirer of our devotion

### Printed p. 317  (PDF 335)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 15 [?].)*

hasten our rites fruition. I glorify him, the radiant-limbed (Agni), with this laudation.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***ucathasya*** — उक्थस्य स्तोत्रस्य । यद्वा उचथेत्यन्नामकस्य महर्षेर्गोत्रप्रभवस्य नः (*ukthasya stotrasya | yadvā ucathetyannāmakasya maharṣergotraprabhavasya naḥ*): "of praise (*uktha*, *stotra*); or of us, born in the lineage of the great sage named Ucatha (Ucathya)": the commentator gives these two meanings. Here the first meaning, "of the praise", is well suited and to be accepted.

***kuvit*** — this word is used in two senses in this sūkta: in the first pāda it means "many times" (*bahuvāram*); in the second pāda, "in abundance" (*atiprabhūtam*) — so Sāyaṇa explains; in the third sense, it is "abundantly" (*prabhūtam*).

The Nirukta author reads the word *kuvit* among the names of "many" (Ni. 3-[?]):

> उपेमसृक्षि वाजयुर्वचस्यां चनो दधीत नाद्यो गिरो मे ।
> अपां नपादाशुहेमा कुवित्स सुवेशसस्करति जोषिषद्धि ॥

> *upemasṛkṣi vājayurvacasyāṃ cano dadhīta nādyo giro me |*
> *apāṃ napādāśuhemā kuvitsa suveśasaskarati joṣiṣaddhi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-35-1.) and in such Ṛks the word means "much"; he also cites:

> ताँ आ रुद्रस्य मीळ्हुषो विवासे कुविन्नंसन्ते मरुतः पुनर्नः ।
> यत्सस्वर्ता जिहीळिरे यदाविरव तदेन ईमहे तुराणाम् [?] ॥

> *tā~ ā rudrasya mīḷhuṣo vivāse kuvinnaṃsante marutaḥ punarnaḥ |*
> *yatsasvartā jihīḷire yadāvirava tadena īmahe turāṇām [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-[?]-5 [?].) in such Ṛks the meaning "many times" (*bahukṛtvaḥ*, *punaḥpunaḥ*) is obtained.

***dhiyaḥ*** — *karmāṇi*: "rites"; "that our sacrificial rites may be completed". This word is read among the names of action (Ni. 2-[?]) and among the names of intelligence (*prajñā*). The Nirukta author:

> महो अर्णः सरस्वती प्र चेतयति केतुना । धियो विश्वा वि राजति ॥

> *maho arṇaḥ sarasvatī pra cetayati ketunā | dhiyo viśvā vi rājati ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3-12.) citing this Ṛk, "*sarvāṇi prajñānāni*" (Ni. [?]-[?]) he explains "all knowledges", "ideas of meditation (*dhyāna*)", for our whole intelligence.

> पथस्पथः परिपतिं वचस्या कामेन कृतो अभ्यानळर्कम् ।
> स नो रासच्छुरुधश्चन्द्राग्रा धियंधियं सीषधाति प्र पूषा ॥

> *pathaspathaḥ paripatiṃ vacasyā kāmena kṛto abhyānaḷarkam |*
> *sa no rāsacchurudhaścandrāgrā dhiyaṃdhiyaṃ sīṣadhāti pra pūṣā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-53-1.)

> पावीरवी तन्यतुरेकपादजो दिवो धर्ता सिन्धुरापः समुद्रियः ।
> विश्वे देवासः शृणवन् वचांसि मे सरस्वती सह धीभिः पुरंध्या ॥

> *pāvīravī tanyaturekapādajo divo dhartā sindhurāpaḥ samudriyaḥ |*
> *viśve devāsaḥ śṛṇavan vacāṃsi me sarasvatī saha dhībhiḥ puraṃdhyā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-66-13.) In these Ṛks the word *dhi* is explained as "rites such as sacrifice".

### Printed p. 318  (PDF 336)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 143".)*

***śucipratīkam*** — शोभनजालं शोभनावयवं (*śobhanajālaṃ śobhanāvayavaṃ*) [?]: "of radiant flames, of beautiful limbs"; "bright, fair of limb" — that is, Agni; Indra's epithet. Among the other epithets of Agni this is the principal one.

***tutujyāt*** — *tvarayatu, prerayatu*: "let him urge, impel"; the sense is "impel and cause our rites to be completed".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar page, noted briefly).** *vīḥ* (root *vī gatyādiṣu*; in the agent sense *kvip ca* gives suffix *kvip*; by the root-accent the *udātta* arises), *asat* (root *as bhuvi*; *leṭ*, third person singular, *tip*; *itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-97): loss of *i*; *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94): *aṭ* augment; *asat* is the form), *vasuḥ* (root *vasa nivāse*; *śvasyasnihi…* (Uṇ. Sū. 1-[?]): suffix *u*; by *vyatyaya* first-syllable *udātta*), *ā varat* (root *vṛñ varaṇe*; *āṅ* prefix; *leṭ*, third person singular; the loss of *i* of the ending and *aṭ*; *bahulaṃ chandasi*: *luk* of the vikaraṇa; by the *kuvit*-connection (*nipātair yadyadi…* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-30): prevention of *nighāta*; since the suffix is *pit* the root accent remains; *asat* … the first syllable has its own accent; *tiṅ cāniṅ…* gives the *anudātta* of the prefix), *codaḥ* (root *cud preraṇe*; *nandigrahipacādi*: *ac* suffix; *laghūpadha guṇa*; by *cit* the end is *udātta*), *tutujyāt* (root *tuja preraṇe*; *liṅ*, third person singular, *ti*; *itaś ca*: loss of *i*; *yāsuṭ* augment; *bahulaṃ chandasi*: *śap* becomes *ślu*; reduplication; since *kuvit* is connected there is no *nighāta*; the *a* of the suffix is *udātta*), *sātaye* (*ūtiyūti…* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-97): *ktin* formed irregularly), *śucipratīkam* (*śuciḥ pratīkaṃ yasya saḥ*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1): the first member's accent; accusative singular) …

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> घृतप्रतीकं व ऋतस्य धूर्षदमग्निं मित्रं न समिधान ऋञ्जते [?] ।
> इन्धानो अक्रो विदथेषु दीद्यच्छुक्रवर्णामुदु नो यंसते धियम् ॥ ७ ॥

> *ghṛtapratīkaṃ va ṛtasya dhūrṣadamagniṃ mitraṃ na samidhāna ṛñjate [?] |*
> *indhāno akro vidatheṣu dīdyacchukravarṇāmudu no yaṃsate dhiyam ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> घृतऽप्रतीकम् । वः । ऋतस्य । धूःऽसदम् । अग्निम् । मित्रम् । न । सम्ऽइधानाः [?] । ऋञ्जते । इन्धानः । अक्रः । विदथेषु । दीद्यत् । शुक्रऽवर्णाम् । उत् । ऊं इति । नः । यंसते । धियम् ॥ ७ ॥

> *ghṛta 'pratīkam | vaḥ | ṛtasya | dhūḥ 'sadam | agnim | mitram | na | sam 'idhānāḥ [?] | ṛñjate | indhānaḥ | akraḥ | vidatheṣu | dīdyat | śukra 'varṇām | ut | ūṃ iti | naḥ | yaṃsate | dhiyam ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; gist: *They kindle Agni, ghee-faced, the bearer of the sacrifice's yoke, like a friend; he, blazing at the sacrifices, will uplift our bright-hued prayer.* Small type, partly legible)

> घृतप्रतीकं घृतोपलक्षणं प्रयाजादिष्वाज्यैर्होयमानत्वात् । यद्वा । प्रतीकमङ्गं दीप्रज्वालमित्यर्थः । किंच वो युष्मत्सम्बन्धिन ऋतस्य यज्ञस्य धूर्षदं धुरि निर्वहणे सीदन्तं यज्ञनिर्वाहकमग्निं मित्रं न मित्रमिव समिधानाः इध्मैर्दीपयमाना ऋञ्जते । प्रसाधयन्ति । ऋञ्जतिः प्रसाधनकर्मा । इन्धानः सम्यग्दीप्यमानोऽक्रो ज्वालाभिराक्रान्तोऽथ्वैरनाक्रान्तो वा क्रमेः श्यन्दसो डः [?] । विदथेषु यज्ञेषु वेदयत्स्तोत्रेषु निमित्तेषु दीद्यत् स्वयं दीप्यमानोऽग्निः शुक्रवर्णां शुद्धवर्णां निर्मलवर्णां च धियं प्रज्ञां ज्योतिष्मदादिकर्म वा नो ऽस्माकमुद्यंसते उद्यमयतु [?] । … यमेर्लेट्याडागमः । सिप् । उशब्दो [?] धारणे । धीरिति कर्मनामसु पाठात् ॥

> *ghṛtapratīkaṃ ghṛtopalakṣaṇaṃ prayājādiṣvājyairhoyamānatvāt | yadvā | pratīkamaṅgaṃ dīprajvālamityarthaḥ | kiṃca vo yuṣmatsambandhina ṛtasya yajñasya dhūrṣadaṃ dhuri nirvahaṇe sīdantaṃ yajñanirvāhakamagniṃ mitraṃ na mitramiva samidhānāḥ idhmairdīpayamānā ṛñjate | prasādhayanti | ṛñjatiḥ prasādhanakarmā | indhānaḥ samyagdīpyamāno 'kro jvālābhirākrānto 'thvairanākrānto vā krameḥ śyandaso ḍaḥ [?] | vidatheṣu yajñeṣu vedayatstotreṣu nimitteṣu dīdyat svayaṃ dīpyamāno 'gniḥ śukravarṇāṃ śuddhavarṇāṃ nirmalavarṇāṃ ca dhiyaṃ prajñāṃ jyotiṣmadādikarma vā no 'smākamudyaṃsate udyamayatu [?] | … yamerleṭyāḍāgamaḥ | sip | uśabdo [?] dhāraṇe | dhīriti karmanāmasu pāṭhāt ‖*

### Printed p. 320  (PDF 338)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 143".)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *samidhānaḥ* — (with fuel) kindling Agni to blaze, the priest; *ghṛtapratīkam* — Agni, of ghee-marked (ghee-faced) form, with offerings of ghee; *vaḥ* — your; *ṛtasya* — of the sacrifice; *dhūrṣadam* — who sits at the yoke and bears the burden of the sacrifice; *agnim* — Agni; *mitraṃ na* — like a friend; *ṛñjate* — adorn and worship; *indhānaḥ* — Agni, who is blazing; *akraḥ* — (filled with fuel, i.e.) satisfied; *videṣu* — at the sacrifices; *dīdyat* — shining of himself; *dhiyam* — our sacrificial wisdom; *śukravarṇām* — the pure, bright act (radiant sacrifice and the like); *ud u yaṃsate* — (Agni) lifts up and brings to completion.

**Bhāvārtha.** The priest, with offerings of ghee and so on, adorns and worships Agni — who carries the burden of the sacrifice at the yoke — like a friend. Agni, blazing, filled with fuel and shining at sacrifices, makes our sacrificial wisdom and the pure, bright rites (of light and the like) complete and brings them to fulfilment.

**English Translation (as printed).** The kindler (of the sacrificial fire) propitiates Agni, of glistening form; the upholder of your ceremony, like a friend; well kindled and well supplied (with fuel); blazing brightly at holy rites, he illumines our pure and pious observances.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***samidhānaḥ*** — इध्मैर्दीपयमानः (*idhmairdīpayamānaḥ*): "kindling with fuel": the epithet of the priest (*ṛtvij*), who makes Agni blaze with fuel. This word is generally used as an epithet of Agni in the other places too; in the sense of *karmaṇi* (passive) it is also applied. For example —

> स नो रेवत्समिधानः स्वस्तये संददस्वान्रयिमस्मासु दीदिहि ।
> आ नः कृणुष्व सुविताय रोदसी अग्ने हव्या मनुषो देव वीतये ॥

> *sa no revatsamidhānaḥ svastaye saṃdadasvānrayimasmāsu dīdihi |*
> *ā naḥ kṛṇuṣva suvitāya rodasī agne havyā manuṣo deva vītaye ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-1-[?].) In this Ṛk also in the same way, and in 4-[?]-[?]; 7-[?]-[?]; 8-[?]-[?] and the like, in all of these the epithet *asmābhiḥ samyag-idhyamānaḥ sann*, "being well kindled by us" is applied to Agni. But in the Ṛk in hand alone, it is an epithet of the priest, who is the doer of the act.

### Printed p. 321  (PDF 339)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 15 [?].)*

***dhūrṣadam*** — धुरि निर्वहणे सीदन्तं यज्ञनिर्वाहकमग्निम् (*dhuri nirvahaṇe sīdantaṃ yajñanirvāhakamagnim*): "who sits at the yoke, that is, in the carrying through; the Agni who carries the sacrifice through". In the work of carrying through the sacrifice, "he takes the leading position": thus Agni's power and his main place in sacrificial work are shown. This epithet, like the other epithets, is used for another sense also in the Ṛk 1-[?]-[?] [?]; see that sūkta.

> यज्ञेन वर्धत जातवेदसमग्निं यजध्वं हविषा तना गिरा ।
> समिधानं सुप्रयसं स्वर्णरं द्युक्षं होतारं वृजनेषु धूर्षदम् ॥

> *yajñena vardhata jātavedasamagniṃ yajadhvaṃ haviṣā tanā girā |*
> *samidhānaṃ suprayasaṃ svarṇaraṃ dyukṣaṃ hotāraṃ vṛjaneṣu dhūrṣadam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, "the one who carries the sacrificial yoke (*dhūrṣad*) and the strong (*balasya kartā*)" is explained; "when Agni is lit, the body's strength becomes famous" is another explanation; by this it is shown that Agni is a deity of strength and work. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?] too, in *dhūrṣadaṃ dhurṣv…* it is an epithet of the chariot (*ratha*, referring to *dhūrṣadam*), and shows the sense "supported by the chariot-yoke as the wheels' support". In the Ṛk in hand it means "one who has the power of carrying through".

***ghṛtapratīkam*** — the word *pratīka* is generally of the sense "face", but here it is an "organ" (*aṅga*), explained as "shining flame (*dīptajvāla*) — bright flame": the meaning is "he who is made shining by an offering of ghee".

*ghṛta* (the word is read among names of water; Ni. 1-[?]); in the contexts the Nirukta authors show the sense of this word as it occurs in the Ṛks.

***akraḥ*** — *jvālāsamidādibhir ākrāntaḥ*, "covered by flames, fuel and so on", or *anākrāntaḥ*, "unattackable": spread over by flames, fuel and so on; or of unobstructed spreading, not overcome by other things. The Nirukta author gives it the name *akra* in the sense of *ākramaṇāt* ("coming upon") (Ni. 6-[?]): by his coming upon enemies. He has shown that it is a name for a hero (Nigh.).

> आक्रो ऽबभ्रिः समिथे महीनां दिव्यश्येनः सूनवे भाऋजीकः [?] ।
> अदुस्स्रियो जनिता यो जजानापां गर्भो नृतमो यह्वो अग्निः ॥

> *ākro 'babhriḥ samithe mahīnāṃ divyaśyenaḥ sūnave bhāṛjīkaḥ [?] |*
> *adussriyo janitā yo jajānāpāṃ garbho nṛtamo yahvo agniḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?].) Citing this Ṛk he compared Agni's power to a *prākāra* (rampart). Or Sāyaṇa explains it as, since *kranta* ("one who has gone across") is not possible, *prākāra* (rampart) is the meaning: as stated above, the sense is the spreading (*prasaraṇa*) of Agni, endowed with unobstructed power.

***videṣu*** — *yajñeṣu*: the places of sacrifices; the meaning is "in the sacrificial places" (*vedasthāna*); and *stotreṣu nimittabhūteṣu*, "when the praises are the cause"; thereby the word *vidatha* is explained by the Nirukta authors. Here ——
