### Printed p. 322  (PDF 340)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 143".)*

Among the explanations one is accepted: *yajña, vena* etc. are read among the names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-[?]) and *vidathāni vedanāni* — "the word *vidatha* [means] knowledge" (Ni. 3-[?]) is shown for the word *vidatha*:

> होता देवो अमर्त्यः पुरस्तादेति मायया । विदथानि प्रचोदयन् ॥

> *hotā devo amartyaḥ purastādeti māyayā | vidathāni pracodayan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-27-7 [?].) Citing this Ṛk, it is shown there that it is formed from the root *vid* in the sense of knowledge. Here Sāyaṇa has explained "*vidathāni vedanāni karmāṇi*": the actions which must be understood. As to the derivation of this word, a number of scholars have taken pains and each has given his own particular opinion; and, as each has shown a different derivation of this word and a different meaning, it is to be understood that all those meanings are not fixed. The scholar Max Müller says:

> आमादेषां भियसा भूमिरेजति नौर्न पूर्णा क्षरति व्यथिर्यती ।
> दूरेदृशो ये चितयन्त एमभिरन्तर्महे विदथे येतिरे नराः ॥

> *āmādeṣāṃ bhiyasā bhūmirejati naurna pūrṇā kṣarati vyathiryatī |*
> *dūredṛśo ye citayanta emabhirantarmahe vidathe yetire narāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-59-3.) In explaining this Ṛk he has taken the word *vidathe* to mean "the great sacrificial assembly (*yajña-sabhā*)"; and, giving the explanation of others, he has also indicated the meanings given by the other German scholars to this word. Max Müller's own English as printed:

"Vidatha may have been the name of a sacred act, as Veda is of sacred knowledge. But the fact remains that it is best translated by assembly, particularly an assembly for sacrificial purposes." (Sacred Books of the East. Vol. 32 P. 319-50 [sic]).

It is said that, just as *veda* means "sacred knowledge", so *vidatha* means "a sacred act"; but since it is understood to mean "sacrificial assembly", that is the one finally decided on.

Hermann Oldenberg, the scholar, in his *Vedic Hymns*, in explaining the word *vidatha* in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?] has given his own opinion; his words are quoted and his opinions then explained:

"On the derivation and meaning of विदथ Various opinions have been pronounced in the last years which have been collected by prof. Max Muller in his note on R.V. V.59,3 (S.B.E.

### Printed p. 323  (PDF 341)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 15 [?].)*

Vol. 32 P. 349 sq.) without trying to discuss here all different theories, I proceed to state my own opinion;

I propose to derive विदथ from वि+धा; The Verb वि+धा means 'to distribute, to arrange, to Ordain;' thus the original meaning of विदथ must be like the meaning of विधान, 'distribution, disposition, ordinance'. In V. 3-6, we read विदथेषु अज्मः: this phrase receives its explanation by VII. 66-11 we may call attention also to VI-51-2 within the sphere of the Vedic poets' thoughts, the most prominent example of something most artificially विहित was the sacrifice. यज्ञ and विदथ, 'Sacrifice' and 'ordinance' became nearly synonymous. (III 3-3) ......... finally विदथ seems to mean 'the act of disposing of any business' or the like; this meaning appears, I believe, in some passages like the well-known phrase, बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः—may we with Valiant men mightily raise our voice at the determining of ordinances. Thus the word विदथ and सभा approach each other in their meaning ; a person influential in council is called both विदथ्य and सभेय."

(Sacred Books of the East. Vol. 46 P. 27.) *(English as printed; the Devanagari words in it and the references are partly legible.)*

The gist of this writing is as follows. The word *vidatha* is formed from the root *dhā* by adding the prefix *vi*. *Vidhā* means "to distribute, to ordain"; the meaning "distribution, regulation" is obtained. It may be taken that *vidatha* and *vidhā* are one in sense. In the Ṛk —

> वयमग्ने वनुयाम त्वोता वसूयवो हविषा बुध्यमानाः ।
> वयं समर्ये विदथेष्वह्नां वयं राया सहसस्पुत्र मर्तान् ॥

> *vayamagne vanuyāma tvotā vasūyavo haviṣā budhyamānāḥ |*
> *vayaṃ samarye vidatheṣvahnāṃ vayaṃ rāyā sahasasputra martān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-5-6 [?].) the words *vidatheṣu āhnām* in this Ṛk and *vi dhāḥ* in

> वि ये दधुः शरदं मासमादहर्यज्ञमक्तुं चादृचम् ।
> अनाप्यं वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा क्षत्रं राजान आशत ॥

> *vi ye dadhuḥ śaradaṃ māsamādaharyajñamaktuṃ cādṛcam |*
> *anāpyaṃ varuṇo mitro aryamā kṣatraṃ rājāna āśata ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?].) the words *vi dadhuḥ* are, by similarity of meaning, understood to be of the same sense as other words; and *vihita* and *vidatha* [are of the same sense] and the sacrifice ordained by the Śāstra is called *vidatha*. The scholar explains how the meanings "sacrifice" or "sacrificial assembly" came to remain at the end.

By *vidatha* the sense "assembly" is not obtained; the meaning "*gṛha*" (house, home) is correct for domestic matters, say Bloomfield, both Max Müller and Oldenberg, who show faults in the meanings they have given. His opinion is this —

### Printed p. 324  (PDF 342)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 143".)*

"The word विदथ contains the root विद् in its ordinary sense of 'get, acquire'. Instead of this, the radical idea underlying the word was generally felt to be 'come-together, 'assemble'. Again, the false start from the notion of 'assemblage' resulted in an approximation of the word to other words for assemblage, especially to सभा with which विदथ was almost identified. We shall see that there are decided points of contact between the words विदथ and सभा but that the contact is that of extreme opposites in a way. विदथ refers to home matters, सभा to public matters.

In the interpretation of a term that figures prominently in the mystic-hieratic sphere of the Veda it is peculiarly necessary to search for its uses outside of that sphere, if there be such uses. In X-85-26, the bride after the wedding ceremony proper, as the newly married couple are about to travel to their new home is addressed with the words 'May Pushan taking thee by the hand lead thee house; may the Asvins lead thee forth on their car. Go to your house in order that thou mayst be mistress of the house'.

Now विदथ here, can but have one meaning, 'household' or something very like it. It certainly cannot refer to anything in the nature of a public gathering similar to the सभा. In the phrase बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः (R.V. 2-1-16), the word सुवीराः refers to family relations not to public life.

Thus far, it may not be doubted, the word appears in the language of ordinary life. But it is found to a very much greater extent in the sacerdotal sphere; indeed, as all interpreters from Yaska on, have agreed, it often has a meaning very close to Yagna 'Sacrifice' itself. This is as it should be. In as much as the sacrifice is a private, home affair, it is very natural विदथ the house the premises the establishment, should figure prominently in connection with the sacrifice." *(English as printed; partly legible at this resolution.)*

The summary of this writing is that the meaning "assembly" (*sabhā*) given by some to the word *vidatha* is not right; the meaning, "house", should be taken. In the Ṛks too this usage is noted at more than one place. For example —

> पूषा त्वेतो नयतु हस्तगृह्याश्विना त्वा प्र वहतां रथेन ।
> गृहान् गच्छ गृहपत्नी यथासो वशिनी त्वं विदथमा वदासि ॥

> *pūṣā tveto nayatu hastagṛhyāśvinā tvā pra vahatāṃ rathena |*
> *gṛhān gaccha gṛhapatnī yathāso vaśinī tvaṃ vidathamā vadāsi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-26.) in this Ṛk it is evident that Pūṣan and the Aśvins are said to invite her to the house of her husband.

> ये स्तोतृभ्यो गोअग्रामश्वपेशसमग्ने रातिमुपसृजन्ति सूरयः ।
> अस्माञ्चतांश्च प्र हि नेहि वस्य आ बृहद्वयेम विदथे सुवीराः ॥

> *ye stotṛbhyo goagrāmaśvapeśasamagne rātimupasṛjanti sūrayaḥ |*
> *asmāñcatāṃśca pra hi nehi vasya ā bṛhadvayema vidathe suvīrāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-10-6 [?].) In this Ṛk also, the word *suvīrāḥ*, "accompanied by good sons and so on" (*śobhanaputrādisahitāḥ*), means the *gṛha*, "house"; but in the household the sacrificial rites were performed; and in this very context it is *yajñagṛha* ("house of sacrifice"). The word *yajña* too is said by Yāska to be a synonym [?]. In this manner the Western scholars have given their individual opinions in great numbers.

Thus *gṛha*, *yajña* and *sabhā* have different senses, and since each is included in all, none of them can be said to be wrong. These meanings are all in Sāyaṇa's commentary itself. For example, in 10-[?]-[?] and 10-[?] the meaning "house" is given; in 10-[?]-[?]; 10-[?]-[?] and in many other Ṛks the meaning "sacrifice"; and the senses "sacrificial house" and "sacrificial assembly" both are obtained.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar page, noted briefly).** *ghṛtapratīkam* (*ghṛtāt pratīkaḥ yasya saḥ*, tam; in the *bahuvrīhi* the first member keeps its accent; accusative singular), *dhūrṣadam* (*dhuri sīdati iti dhūrṣat*; the root *ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*; *satsūdviṣadruhaduhayujavidabhidachidajinīrājām upasargeṣv api kvip* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-61): *kvip* when an *upapada*; *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139): the *kṛdanta* keeps its natural accent), *samidhānaḥ* (root *iñdhī dīptau*; *śānac* in the present sense; *anidītāṃ hal…*: loss of the nasal of the *upadhā*; by *cit* the end is *udātta*; in the compound the *kṛdanta*'s natural accent), *ṛñjate* (root *ṛñja bhartsane*; *laṭ*, third person singular; *nighāta* after an *ati…* word), *indhānaḥ* (root *iñdhī dīptau*; *rudhādi*: in the *rudhādi* class *śānac*; *rudhādibhyaḥ śnam* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-78): *śnam* vikaraṇa; since *anudātta* [*śnam*] stands after *ati…* the *tāsyanudāttet* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) leaves the root accent) *(continues on p. 326)*.

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अप्रयुच्छन्नप्रयुच्छद्भिरग्ने शिवेभिर्नः पायुभिः पाहि शग्मैः ।
> अदब्धेभिरदृपितेभिरिष्टेऽनिमिषद्भिः परि पाहि नो जाः ॥ ८ ॥

> *aprayucchannaprayucchadbhiragne śivebhirnaḥ pāyubhiḥ pāhi śagmaiḥ |*
> *adabdhebhiradṛpitebhiriṣṭe 'nimiṣadbhiḥ pari pāhi no jāḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अप्रऽयुच्छन् । अप्रऽयुच्छत्ऽभिः । अग्ने । शिवेभिः । नः । पायुऽभिः । पाहि । शग्मैः ।
> अदब्धेभिः । अदृपितेभिः । इष्टे । अनिमिषत्ऽभिः । परि । पाहि । नः । जाः ॥ ८ ॥

> *apra 'yucchan | apra 'yucchat 'bhiḥ | agne | śivebhiḥ | naḥ | pāyu 'bhiḥ | pāhi | śagmaiḥ |*
> *adabdhebhiḥ | adṛpitebhiḥ | iṣṭe | animiṣat 'bhiḥ | pari | pāhi | naḥ | jāḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

> *he agne aprayucchan apramādyan | yuccha pramāde | avicchinnapravṛttiḥ san aprayucchadbhirapramādarahitaiḥ [?] śivebhiḥ kalyāṇaiḥ śagmaiḥ sukhakaraiḥ pāyubhiḥ rakṣaṇaprakārairno 'smān pāhi | rakṣa | kiṃca he iṣṭe sarvairiṣṭe [?] yogye agne jāyamāno 'smadbhirhiṃsyamānaḥ san [?] adabdhebhirahiṃsaiḥ adṛpitebhiḥ kenacidapyaparibhūtaiḥ [?] animiṣadbhirnimeṣarahitaiḥ jaḍasvabhāvarahitaiḥ [?] … dṛpe dṛpta utkleśe [?] … jāḥ asmatsambandhinīḥ putrapautrarūpāḥ prajāḥ pari pāhi | parito rakṣa | na kevalamasmān kintu putrapautrādīnapi rakṣa ‖*

### Printed p. 327  (PDF 345)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 16.)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *agne* — O Agni; *aprayucchan* — (in respect of us) not heedless, ever vigilant; *aprayucchadbhiḥ* — not heedless; *śivebhiḥ* — auspicious; *śagmaiḥ* — comfort-giving; *pāyubhiḥ* — with protective means; *naḥ* — us; *pāhi* — guard; *iṣṭe* — O Agni, desired by all; *jāḥ* — born of us; *adabdhebhiḥ* — not to be injured; *adṛpitebhiḥ* — not to be overcome by others; *animiṣadbhiḥ* — never slumbering, with guards; *naḥ* — us; *pari* — all round; *pāhi* — protect; [or *naḥ* — to us; *jāḥ* — born, our sons and grandsons; *pari pāhi* — protect all round].

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, be ever watchful over us, and guard us with protections that are not heedless, auspicious and comfort-giving. O Agni, desired by all, guard all round, with guards that are not to be injured or overcome by others and never asleep, us and also our sons and grandsons born of us.

**English Translation (as printed).** Agni, never heedless (of us), guard us with never heedless, auspicious, and joy-bestowing cares : do you, who are desired (by all), protect us, and those born of us, with unobstructed, unovercome, and never-slumbering (vigilance).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** In this Ṛk the protection of Agni is prayed for. The nature of that protection is told by the epithets *aprayucchan* and the like.

***aprayucchan*** — *yucchaprāmāde*: *aprayucchan* = *asmatpraharṣe jāgarūkaḥ* [?]: "vigilant", from the root *yuccha* ("to be careless") with the prefix, giving the sense "ever vigilant, not careless".

> अग्ने तोकस्य नस्तने तनूनामप्रयुच्छन् दीद्यद्बोधि गोपाः ॥

> *tvaṃ dūtastvamu naḥ paraspāstvaṃ vasya ā vṛṣabha praṇetā |*
> *agne tokasya nastane tanūnāmaprayucchan dīdyadbodhi gopāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-4-9.) In such Ṛks, Agni is prayed to protect with watchfulness; here too the same sense is signified.

***śagmaiḥ*** — the word *śagma* is read among the names of happiness (Ni. 3-[?]); Sāyaṇa has generally given this word the sense "comfort" or "bringing comfort" everywhere. For example —

> तं शग्मासो अरुषासो अश्वा बृहस्पतिं सहवाहो वहन्ति ।
> सहश्चिद्यस्य नीलवत्सधस्थं नभो न रूपमरुषं वसानाः ॥

> *taṃ śagmāso aruṣāso aśvā bṛhaspatiṃ sahavāho vahanti |*
> *sahaścidyasya nīlavatsadhasthaṃ nabho na rūpamaruṣaṃ vasānāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-[?]-[?].) in this Ṛk, and

> एह हरी ब्रह्मयुजा शग्मा वक्षतः सखायम् ।
> गीर्भिः श्रुतं गिर्वणसम् ॥

> *eha harī brahmayujā śagmā vakṣataḥ sakhāyam |*
> *gīrbhiḥ śrutaṃ girvaṇasam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].) in this he has explained it as "bringing comfort" or "strength" (*śakti*). The Bhaṭṭabhāskara says —

> पवमानादा सरस्वती यजता गन्तो यज्ञं हवं देवी जुजुवाणा घृताची ।
> शग्मां नो वाजमुशती कृणोतु ॥

> *pavamānādā sarasvatī yajatā ganto yajñaṃ havaṃ devī jujuvāṇā ghṛtācī |*
> *śagmāṃ no vājamuśatī kṛṇotu ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-8-22-3 [?].) in such Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentences, and in

> तपसास्यानु वर्तये शिवेनास्मा उपवर्तये शग्मेनास्मा अभिवर्तये ॥

> *tapasāsyānu vartaye śivenāsmā upavartaye śagmenāsmā abhivartaye ‖*

(Tai. Brā. 1-1-3-[?].) in this Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa sentence, in the word *śagma* he has shown the meanings "able" or "possessing special power". From these explanations the word appears to be derived from the root *śak* ("to be able") and to mean "powerful" or "able". Among them —

> रथवाहनं हविरस्य नाम यत्रायुधं निहितमस्य वर्म ।
> तत्रा रथमुप शग्मं सदेम विश्वाहा वयं सुमनस्यमानाः ॥

> *rathavāhanaṃ havirasya nāma yatrāyudhaṃ nihitamasya varma |*
> *tatrā rathamupa śagmaṃ sadema viśvāhā vayaṃ sumanasyamānāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?].) in such Ṛks the meaning "bringing comfort" is the one to be taken. In the Ṛk in hand also the two senses "comfort-giving" and "able" are fitting.

***iṣṭe*** — *sarvaiḥ* [*viṣaṇīyaḥ*] सर्वैः विषणीयः (*sarvaiḥ viṣaṇīyaḥ*) [?]: "desired by all": addressing Agni, who is worthy to be sought by all, from the performance of the *devapūjā* and others.

---

### Printed p. 329  (PDF 347)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 16.)*

***adabdhebhiḥ*** — *ahiṃsitaiḥ*: "by those who are unharmed", from the root *dabh* ("to injure, to destroy"): in the Vedic language a word derived from the root *dabh*, with the sense of "injured" or "destroyed", is common; the word *adabha* is used more with this sense. The sense "unharmed, not subject to destruction". Ordinarily in prayers for the protection of Agni, the epithets *adabdhebhiḥ pāyubhiḥ* or *adabdhebhir gopābhiḥ* occur together.

> अदब्धेभिस्त्वं गोपाभिरिष्टेऽस्माकं पाहि त्रिषधस्थ सूरीन् ।
> रक्षा च नो ददुषां शर्धो अग्ने वैश्वानर प्र च तारीः स्तवानः ॥

> *adabdhebhistvaṃ gopābhiriṣṭe 'smākaṃ pāhi triṣadhastha sūrīn |*
> *rakṣā ca no daduṣāṃ śardho agne vaiśvānara pra ca tārīḥ stavānaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-8-[?].) In such Ṛks it is an epithet of *gopābhiḥ*; and as in the Ṛk in hand,

> अदब्धेभिः सवितः पायुभिस्त्वं शिवेभिरद्य परि पाहि नो गयम् ।
> हिरण्यजिह्वः सुवितायनन्मसे रक्षा माकिर्नो अघशंस ईशत ॥

> *adabdhebhiḥ savitaḥ pāyubhistvaṃ śivebhiradya pari pāhi no gayam |*
> *hiraṇyajihvaḥ suvitāyananmase rakṣā mākirno aghaśaṃsa īśata ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?].) in such Ṛks it is an epithet of *pāyubhiḥ*.

***adṛpitebhiḥ*** — *kenāpy aparibhūtaiḥ*: "unovercome by anyone, or by none to be mastered": the nature of the protection is told.

***animiṣadbhiḥ*** — *nimeṣarahitaiḥ* *udyuktaiḥ lakṣyaiḥ*: "without closing the eyes, ready, attentive"; the meaning is "not subject to the nature of inertness; speedily bringing fruit".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; grammar page, noted briefly).** *aprayucchan* (*yuccha prāmāde*; *śatṛ*; *pra* + *yuccha*; *na prayucchan*; *tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2): the first member *nañ* keeps its natural accent), *śivebhiḥ* (*bahulaṃ chandasi* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-10): in the instrumental plural *bhis*, *aisbhāva* is optional [*ais* not]; *bahuvacanasya ṅer yet* [?]: *e*), *pāyubhiḥ* (root *pā rakṣaṇe*; *kṛvāpājimisvadisādhyaśūbhyaḥ uṇ* (Uṇ. Sū. 1-1): suffix *uṇ*; *ātoyuk ciṇkṛtoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-33): *yuk* augment for the root; since *kit*… the end is *udātta* by the suffix), *pāhi* (root *pā rakṣaṇe*; *loṭ*, second person singular; *nighāta* after an *ati…* word).

*adabdhebhiḥ* (root *dambha dambhe*; *kta* suffix; *anidītāṃ hal…*: loss of the nasal; *jhaṣaḥ* … *dh*; *bhatva* of *bh* by *pūrvasya*; the first member's … *nañ* keeps its natural accent; by *bahulaṃ chandasi* as before the *aisbhāva* is optional), *adṛpitebhiḥ* (root *dṛpa dṛmpa utkleśe* [?]; *tudādi*; *niṣṭhā*: *kta*; *ardhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ*: *iṭ* in the suffix *kta*; *adṛpita* has *iṭ* in the *dṛpita* word, and by *kta*'s *anudātta*… the first member's natural accent; *bhisa*, as before, *aisbhāva* optional), *iṣṭe* (root *iṣu icchāyām*; *kta* suffix; *iṣyatekarmaṇi* [?]; *śvanyathā…*; *guṇa* by *pugantalaghūpadha* and *vṛddhi* [?]; the vocative, *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198): *nighāta*), *jāḥ* (root *janī prādurbhāve*; *kvip*, though *upasarga*-less, in the feminine [?]; by the strength of *ḍit* the root's *ṭi* is dropped; by the suffix-accent *udātta*). ‖ 8 ‖

## Sūkta 144

### Printed p. 330 (continued; PDF 348)

*(The Kannada heading reads "The 144th Sūkta".)*

*(Anukramaṇī, Sanskrit; not rendered in English. Gist: the sūkta of seven Ṛks beginning "Eti pra hotā" is the fifth sūkta, of Dīrghatamas, in Jagatī; Agni is the deity of it as of the preceding, with the same use at the Prātaranuvāka and Āśvina-śastra.)*

> एति प्र होतेति सप्तर्चं पञ्चमं सूक्तं दैर्घतमसं जागतम् । पूर्वत्राग्नेयं तु तदितिकृत्वादिमेऽप्याग्नेयम् [?] । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् — एति प्र सप्त जागतम् इति ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्विनियोग उक्तः ॥

> *eti pra hoteti saptarcaṃ pañcamaṃ sūktaṃ dairghatamasaṃ jāgatam | pūrvatrāgneyaṃ tu taditikṛtvādime 'pyāgneyam [?] | tathā cānukrāntam — eti pra sapta jāgatam iti ‖ prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayorviniyoga uktaḥ ‖*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta *eti pra hotā* is the fifth sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Dīrghatamas, the son of Ucathya. The metre is Jagatī. As said before, Agni is the deity of this sūkta. In the Anukramaṇī it is said "*eti pra sapta jāgatam*". It is employed as Agni-stotra mantras in the Prātaranuvāka and Āśvina-śastra.

### Printed p. 331  (PDF 349)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 16 [?].)*

**॥ ओम् ॥**

**Sūkta 144** — Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 21, Sūkta 144; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 16 [?]. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Ṛṣi: Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Devatā: Agni. Chandas: Jagatī.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> एति प्र होता व्रतमस्य मायया ऊर्ध्वां दधानः शुचिपेशसं धियम् ।
> अभि स्रुचः क्रमते दक्षिणावृतो या अस्य धाम प्रथमं ह निंसते ॥ १ ॥

> *eti pra hotā vratamasya māyayā ūrdhvāṃ dadhānaḥ śucipeśasaṃ dhiyam |*
> *abhi srucaḥ kramate dakṣiṇāvṛto yā asya dhāma prathamaṃ ha niṃsate ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> एति । प्र । होता । व्रतम् । अस्य । मायया । ऊर्ध्वाम् । दधानः । शुचिऽपेशसम् । धियम् ।
> अभि । स्रुचः । क्रमते । दक्षिणाऽआवृतः । याः । अस्य । धाम । प्रथमम् । ह । निंसते ॥ १ ॥

> *eti | pra | hotā | vratam | asya | māyayā | ūrdhvām | dadhānaḥ | śuci 'peśasam | dhiyam |*
> *abhi | srucaḥ | kramate | dakṣiṇā 'āvṛtaḥ | yāḥ | asya | dhāma | prathamam | ha | niṃsate ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** (Sanskrit, not rendered in English; the bhāṣya begins at the foot of p. 331 and continues on p. 332; gist: *This Hotṛ-adhvaryu, endowed with special insight into his duties, sets out to perform Agni's rite of oblation.* Small type)

> अयं होता होमनिष्पादकोऽध्वर्युरस्याग्नेर्व्रतं हविःप्रदानादिरूपं कर्म कर्तुं मायया कर्तव्यविशेषप्रज्ञया युक्तः सन् प्रैति । प्रकर्षेण गच्छति [continues]

> *ayaṃ hotā homaniṣpādako 'dhvaryurasyāgnervrataṃ haviḥpradānādirūpaṃ karma kartuṃ māyayā kartavyaviśeṣaprajñayā yuktaḥ san praiti | prakarṣeṇa gacchati [continues]*

### Printed p. 332  (PDF 350)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 144".)*

*(Continuation of the bhāṣya of Ṛk 1; small type, partly read.)*

> होतेम् [?] मायेति प्रज्ञानाम माया वयुनमिति तन्नामसु पाठात् । केदृशोऽयम् [?] ऊर्ध्वां उपरिस्थां [?] ऊर्ध्वसमारूढां शुचिपेशसं शोभनरूपोपेतां शुचिरूपां [?] पेश इति रूपनाम । धियं प्रज्ञां दधानः । चतुर्थ्यर्थे [?] … करिष्यतीत्येवंरूपां [?] । अनुग्रहं [?] च दक्षिणावृतः प्रादक्षिण्येन वर्तमानः स्रुचो जुहूप्रभृतीः क्रमते । गृह्णाति । कीदृश्यः स्रुचः । याः प्रथमं पात्रासादनकाले [?] स्वाग्नीध्रादिसमीप स्थानं निंसते चुम्बन्ति चुम्बन्ति इति धातुः । चुम्बन्ति भजन्ते इत्यर्थः । प्रथममनुप्रयाजक्रमं बुध्वा प्रति पश्चात् [?] क्रमते । हरतो [?] प्रसिद्धः । यद्वा । होता देवानामाह्वातायमग्निरस्य यजमानस्य व्रतं कर्म ज्योतिष्टोमादि प्रज्ञाविशेषेण युक्तः सन्नैति । यज्ञद्वेरं प्रत्याग्रछति । तीक्ष्णं लोकम् [?] ऊर्ध्वामूर्ध्ववर्ती शुचिपेशसं शोभनरूपोपेतं ज्वलनात्मकं कर्म दधानो धारयमाणः । आगत्य च दक्षिणावृत उक्तलक्षणः सन् स्रुचो ज्वालात्मना जुहूप्रभृतिका अभिक्रमते । आक्रमते । घृतं स्वीकर्तुं ज्वाला प्रसर्पतीत्यर्थः । याः स्रुचः प्रथमं पूर्वं हविरासादनकाले स्वाग्नीध्रादिस्थानं वेदिलक्षणं निंसते चुम्बन्ति प्राप्नुवन्ति । हरतः प्रसिद्धः । निसि चुम्बने । आदादित्यात् शपो लुक् । इदित्यनुनासिकम् ॥ [?]

> *hotem [?] māyeti prajñānāma māyā vayunamiti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | kedṛśo 'yam [?] ūrdhvāṃ uparisthāṃ [?] ūrdhvasamārūḍhāṃ śucipeśasaṃ śobhanarūpopetāṃ śucirūpāṃ [?] peśa iti rūpanāma | dhiyaṃ prajñāṃ dadhānaḥ | caturthyarthe [?] … kariṣyatītyevaṃrūpāṃ [?] | anugrahaṃ [?] ca dakṣiṇāvṛtaḥ prādakṣiṇyena vartamānaḥ sruco juhūprabhṛtīḥ kramate | gṛhṇāti | kīdṛśyaḥ srucaḥ | yāḥ prathamaṃ pātrāsādanakāle [?] svāgnīdhrādisamīpa sthānaṃ niṃsate cumbanti cumbanti iti dhātuḥ | cumbanti bhajante ityarthaḥ | prathamamanuprayājakramaṃ budhvā prati paścāt [?] kramate | harato [?] prasiddhaḥ | yadvā | hotā devānāmāhvātāyamagnirasya yajamānasya vrataṃ karma jyotiṣṭomādi prajñāviśeṣeṇa yuktaḥ sannaiti | yajñadveraṃ pratyāgrachati | tīkṣṇaṃ lokam [?] ūrdhvāmūrdhvavartī śucipeśasaṃ śobhanarūpopetaṃ jvalanātmakaṃ karma dadhāno dhārayamāṇaḥ | āgatya ca dakṣiṇāvṛta uktalakṣaṇaḥ san sruco jvālātmanā juhūprabhṛtikā abhikramate | ākramate | ghṛtaṃ svīkartuṃ jvālā prasarpatītyarthaḥ | yāḥ srucaḥ prathamaṃ pūrvaṃ havirāsādanakāle svāgnīdhrādisthānaṃ vedilakṣaṇaṃ niṃsate cumbanti prāpnuvanti | harataḥ prasiddhaḥ | nisi cumbane | ādādityāt śapo luk | idityanunāsikam ‖ [?]*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *ūrdhvām* — (the sacrifice) risen to the height; *śucipeśasam* — of a clear, deep form [?]; *dhiyam* — the insight; *dadhānaḥ* — possessing; *hotā* — the invoker of the gods, the Adhvaryu; *asya* — of Agni who has been referred to; *vratam* — the oblation-offering and similar acts; *māyayā* — with his special insight into his duties; *pra eti* — proceeds in front [of the altar]; (and) *yaḥ* — which ladles (*juhū* and others); *prathamam* — first; (at the time of setting down the vessels for the oblation); *asya* — of this; *dhāma* — to the place; *niṃsate* — they touch (reach); *dakṣiṇāvṛtaḥ* — circumambulating with the right side towards it; *srucaḥ* — the ladles *juhū* and the like; *kramate* — he takes up; [or *ūrdhvām* — the high; *śucipeśasam* — of a pleasant form; *dhiyam* — the flame; *hotā* — the summoner of the gods; *asya yajamānasya* — of this sacrificer; *vratam* — the acts such as Jyotiṣṭoma; *māyayā* — knowing it by his special insight; *pra eti* — comes forward;] *yaḥ srucaḥ* — the ladles that, at the time of laying down the oblations first (*prathamam*), reach *asya dhāma* — Agni's place, the altar; *abhi kramate* — he takes in front [of them].

### Printed p. 333  (PDF 351)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 16 [?].)*

**Bhāvārtha.** The Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu who conducts the sacrifice, possessing insight raised on high, with a deep and beautiful form, proceeds — endowed with the experience necessary to perform the offering of the oblations — to the performance of the sacrifice. Having first touched Agni's altar and circumambulated it with his right side towards it, he takes up the ladles used for offering the oblations.

**English Translation (as printed).** The ministering priest, (qualified by experience, and) possessing exalted and graceful devotion, proceeds (to celebrate) his (Agni's) worship, having circumambulated [?: read "cumbulated" at this resolution] (the altar), he takes up the ladles which are first to present the oblations.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

> एति प्र सप्त जागतम् (अनुक्रमणिका) प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्विनियोग उक्तः । (सा. भा. पीठिका)

> *eti pra sapta jāgatam (anukramaṇikā) prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayorviniyoga uktaḥ | (sā. bhā. pīṭhikā)*

The commentator has told in his Pīṭhikā that this sūkta is employed in the Āśvina-śastra. A story-context that suggests the connection of the Aśvina-śastra with the Agni-sūkta and other things, is told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa thus —

> प्रजापतिर्वै सोमाय राज्ञे दुहितरं प्रायच्छत्सूर्यां सावित्रीं तस्यै सर्वे देवा वरा आगच्छंस्तस्मा एतत् सहस्रं वहतुमन्वकरोद्यदेतदाश्विनमित्याचक्षतेऽश्विनं हैव तत्सहस्रं तस्मात् [?] त्रैसहस्रं [?] शंसेद्यो वा प्राश्वं फलं शंसेद्यथा ह वा इदमनो वा रथो वाक्रो वर्तत एवं हैवाक्रो वर्तते । शकुनिरो [?] तिष्ठेव्यन्नाजायते [?] ।

> *prajāpatirvai somāya rājñe duhitaraṃ prāyacchatsūryāṃ sāvitrīṃ tasyai sarve devā varā āgacchaṃstasmā etat sahasraṃ vahatumanvakarodyadetadāśvinamityācakṣate 'śvinaṃ haiva tatsahasraṃ tasmāt [?] traisahasraṃ [?] śaṃsedyo vā prāśvaṃ phalaṃ śaṃsedyathā ha vā idamano vā ratho vākro vartata evaṃ haivākro vartate | śakuniro [?] tiṣṭhevyannājāyate [?] |*

(Ai. Brā. 4-7 [?]; partly legible.) Formerly, when Prajāpati was ready to give his daughter Sūryā to King Soma in marriage, all the gods came wishing to wed her themselves. Then Prajāpati laid down a condition: the thousand mantras known as the Aśvina-śastra are to be recited, and not fewer. As in the world a chariot wheel moves easily after it has been oiled, so the mantras are to be recited easily; to do that one must first perform the *[phaitapana, as printed; the anointing?]* and then recite. And as a wife, when ready to fly [?], makes her body light, so the suitor who is to enchant her must have that quality. *(Read at low confidence.)*

*(Continuation of the Kannada account of the Āśvina-śastra legend: "first the smearing is done and then the recitation. And again the wife's quality …")*

> तस्मिन्नेना समजानते ममेदमस्तु ममेदमस्तीति ते संजानाना अब्रुवन्नाजिमस्यायामहे स यो न उज्जेष्यति तस्येदं भविष्यतीति तेऽस्य रे [?] … गृहपतेरादित्यं काष्ठामकुर्वत तस्मादाग्नेयेन प्रतिपद्यतेऽश्विनस्याग्निर्होता गृहपतिः स राजेति [?]

> *tasminnenā samajānate mamedamastu mamedamastīti te saṃjānānā abruvannājimasyāyāmahe sa yo na ujjeṣyati tasyedaṃ bhaviṣyatīti te 'sya re [?] … gṛhapaterādityaṃ kāṣṭhāmakurvata tasmādāgneyena pratipadyate 'śvinasyāgnirhotā gṛhapatiḥ sa rājeti [?]*

(Ai. Brā. 4-[?].) Then the gods contended with one another, each saying, "this is mine"; they gathered together at the race: "let whoever wins among us have it"; and in that running, the winner would take the bride. Then, starting with Agni, the Gṛhapati, they ran as far as Sūrya, as the goal. Therefore the first mantra —

> स त्वं दक्षस्याव्यको वृथो भूरर्थः परस्यान्तरस्य तरुषः ।
> रायः सूनो सहसो मर्त्येष्वा छर्दिर्यच्छ वीतहव्याय सप्रथो भरद्वाजाय सप्रथः ॥

> *sa tvaṃ dakṣasyāvyako vṛtho bhūrarthaḥ parasyāntarasya taruṣaḥ |*
> *rāyaḥ sūno sahaso martyeṣvā chardiryaccha vītahavyāya sapratho bharadvājāya saprathaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-15-[?].) is according to one view addressed to Agni; and also —

> अग्निं मन्ये पितरमग्निमापिमग्निं भ्रातरं सदमित्सखायम् ।
> अग्नेरनीकं बृहतः सपर्यं दिवि शुक्रं यजतं सूर्यस्य ॥

> *agniṃ manye pitaramagnimāpimagniṃ bhrātaraṃ sadamitsakhāyam |*
> *agneranīkaṃ bṛhataḥ saparyaṃ divi śukraṃ yajataṃ sūryasya ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-7-3.) Thus one view is that [the Āśvina-śastra] is to be begun with this mantra. But this is not accepted by others.

> तत्र [?] … तस्माद्गृहपतिर्होता गृहपतिः स राजेत्येव प्रतिपद्येत गृहपतिवती प्रजातिमती शान्ता सर्वायै । सर्वायुत्वाय । सर्वमायुरेति य एवं वेद ।

> *tatra [?] … tasmādgṛhapatirhotā gṛhapatiḥ sa rājetyeva pratipadyeta gṛhapativatī prajātimatī śāntā sarvāyai | sarvāyutvāya | sarvamāyureti ya evaṃ veda |*

(Ai. Brā. [?].) The sūkta beginning with the mantras *agnir hotā gṛhapatiḥ* and the like is the right order; such a one who knows this obtains all prosperity and long life, it says. And also —

> तासां वै देवतानामाजिं धावन्तीनामभिप्रस्थानमग्निर्मुखं प्रथमः प्रत्यपद्यत तमश्विनावन्वगच्छेतां तमब्रूतां [?] … वा इदं जेष्याम इति स तथेत्यब्रवीत्तस्य वै मे महोऽस्त्विति तथेति तस्मादाग्नेयाश्विने शस्यते [?]

> *tāsāṃ vai devatānāmājiṃ dhāvantīnāmabhiprasthānamagnirmukhaṃ prathamaḥ pratyapadyata tamaśvināvanvagacchetāṃ tamabrūtāṃ [?] … vā idaṃ jeṣyāma iti sa tathetyabravīttasya vai me maho 'stviti tatheti tasmādāgneyāśvine śasyate [?]*

(Ai. Brā. 4-[?]; partly legible.) Of those deities, as they ran the race, Agni, in the lead, was first; the Aśvins followed him; they said to him, "…" and asked for a share; he agreed. Therefore Agni's [sūkta] is recited in the Āśvina-śastra.

### Printed p. 335  (PDF 353)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 17 [?].)*

All the gods, when running in this race, Agni was ahead of everyone; the Aśvins approached Agni and asked for help in getting [the prize]; Agni gave consent; but he asked "give me also a share in the victory". Therefore in the Āśvina-śastra Agni too has a share; the share obtained by Agni and Uṣas and the like in the Āśvina-śastra is told in the part of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā that concerns the Pīṭhikā, in the Special Topics of Sūkta [?] (part 1 [?]).

On this occasion another objection is raised and answered —

> तदाहुर्यच्छंस्त्याग्नेयं शस्यते उषस्यं शस्यते इन्द्रमथ तस्मादेतदाश्विनमित्याचक्षतेऽश्विना हि तमजयतामश्विनावात्स्यातां यदश्विना वातं तस्मादेतदाश्विनमित्याचक्षते [?] ।

> *tadāhuryacchaṃstyāgneyaṃ śasyate uṣasyaṃ śasyate indramatha tasmādetadāśvinamityācakṣate 'śvinā hi tamajayatāmaśvināvātsyātāṃ yadaśvinā vātaṃ tasmādetadāśvinamityācakṣate [?] |*

(Ai. Brā. 4-7 to 4-8 [?].) On this occasion, since mantras addressed to Agni, Uṣas and Indra were used, the question is why the name *āśvina* is given; this was answered: the Aśvins are the winners; the name of the śastra is *āśvina* because it is chiefly concerned with the victory of the Aśvins.

***śucipeśasam*** — पेश इति रूपनाम (नि. ३-७ [?]) शोभनरूपोपेतां (*peśa iti rūpanāma (ni. 3-7 [?]) śobhanarūpopetāṃ*): "*peśa* is a name for form (Ni. 3-7); endowed with beautiful form": "of deep (grave) form" is the meaning of the word *dhiyam* for which it is an epithet. The Nirukta author —

> आ सुष्वयन्ती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योनौ ।
> दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं शुक्रपिशं दधाने ॥

> *ā suṣvayantī yajate upāke uṣāsānaktā sadatāṃ ni yonau |*
> *divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatī surukme adhi śriyaṃ śukrapiśaṃ dadhāne ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-6.) citing this Ṛk, "*śukrapeśasaṃ śriyaṃ śocitejarjvalatikamaṇīyāḥ* [?]" (Ni. 8-[?]) explains *peśa* as the name for form, as "bright appearance".

***dhiyam*** — *prajñām*: "knowledge". This word is read among the names of action (Ni. 2-1) and among names of knowledge (Ni. 3-[?]); the Nirukta author, citing Ṛks, explained both meanings; it was told earlier.

***māyayā*** — मायेति प्रज्ञानाम । माया वयुनमिति तन्नामसु पाठात् (*māyeti prajñānāma | māyā vayunamiti tannāmasu pāṭhāt*) (Ni. 3-9 [?]): "*māyā* is a name for knowledge: *māyā*, *vayunam* are read among its names". The Nirukta author:

> मूर्धा भुवो भवति नक्तमग्निस्ततः सूर्यो जायते प्रातरुद्यन् ।
> मायामु तु यज्ञियानामेतामपो यत्तूर्णश्चरति [?] प्रजानन् ॥

> *mūrdhā bhuvo bhavati naktamagnistataḥ sūryo jāyate prātarudyan |*
> *māyāmu tu yajñiyānāmetāmapo yattūrṇaścarati [?] prajānan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-6.)

Having cited this Ṛk, he explains the word *māyā* as "knowledge" (Ni. 7-[?]; "*sa eva prajñāṃ trīkāṃ manyante*" [?]). And again —

> शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यद्विषुरूपे अहनी द्यौरिवासि ।
> विश्वा हि माया अवसि स्वधावो भद्रा ते पूषन्निह रातिरस्तु ॥

> *śukraṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyadviṣurūpe ahanī dyaurivāsi |*
> *viśvā hi māyā avasi svadhāvo bhadrā te pūṣanniha rātirastu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-58-1.) citing this Ṛk (Ni. 12-[?]) he shows that the word *māyā* here too means knowledge. This word has also the meaning "deceit, cheating".

> आरोरुवीद्वृत्रो अस्य वज्रो मानुषो यन्नानुषो निजूर्वात् ।
> नि मायिनो दानवस्य माया अपादयत्स्वप्नान्सस्य [?] ॥

> *āroruvīdvṛtro asya vajro mānuṣo yannānuṣo nijūrvāt |*
> *ni māyino dānavasya māyā apādayatsvapnānsasya [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-30-6.) In such Ṛks *māyā* means the *māyāvin* (the deceiver) Dānava's deceits; the sense is *dānavasya māyāḥ* "the Dānava's arts of magic".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar page, noted briefly).** *eti* (root *iṇ gatau*; *laṭ*, third person singular; at the head of the pāda there is no *nighāta*; *tip* being *anudātta*, the root accent remains), *māyayā* (root *mā māne*; *māhāsthiyo yaḥ* (Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]): suffix *ya*; by the suffix-accent the end is *udātta*; instrumental singular), *dadhānaḥ* (root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *śānac* in the present sense; *ślu* vikaraṇa; *abhyastānām ādiḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-189): first-syllable *udātta*), *śucipeśasam* (*śuciḥ peśo yasya saḥ*, tam; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*: the first member's accent; accusative singular), *srucaḥ* (root *sru gatau*; *ticik ca* (Uṇ. Sū. 2-[?]): suffix *ciḥ* [?]; its *i* has the designation *it* so is dropped; *sruc*), *kramate* (root *kramu pādavikṣepe*; *laṭ*, third person singular, *nighāta*), *dakṣiṇāvṛtaḥ* (*dakṣiṇā* is an *ajanta* word; *ā* prefix; root *vṛñ varaṇe*; suffix *kta*; in the compound the *kṛdanta* keeps its natural accent).

### Printed p. 338  (PDF 356)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 144".)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *agniḥ* — Agni; *yat* — when; *apāṃ upasthe* — in the middle of the waters; *vibhṛtaḥ* — held with special regard (by them); *ā avasat* — abides, having taken possession (of them); (then) *ṛtasya* — of water; *dohanāḥ* — the streams; *yonau* — in their birth-place; *devasya* — of the shining Āditya; *sadane* — in the abode; *parivṛtāḥ* — enveloped (by his rays), having received a refinement; *abhi anūṣata* — become renewed with a new refinement; *adha* — thereafter; *yābhiḥ* — with which waters; *īyate* — (Agni in the form of lightning) joins; *svadhāḥ* — (such) waters of the rain, of nectar-like quality; *adhayat* — (the whole world) drinks.

**Bhāvārtha.** When Agni, held with special regard by the waters, abides in their midst having taken possession of them, then the streams of water, enveloped in the abode of the radiant Āditya, their place of origin, by his rays, receive a new refinement. Thereafter Agni in the form of lightning unites with the waters. Immediately the whole world drinks the nectar-like waters of the rain.

**English Translation (as printed).** The drops of rain, enveloped (by the solar rays), are renewed in the dwelling of the divine (sun), their birth-place: when he, (Agni), abides cherished on the lap of the waters, then (the world) drinks the nectareous rain, with which he, (as the lightning), associates.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** In this Ṛk the nature of the waters purified by the rays of the sun, and the nature of Agni, who is within the waters of the cloud and is in the form of lightning, are explained.

***apāṃ upasthe*** — उदकानामुत्सङ्गे अन्ते (*udakānāmutsaṅge ante*): "in the lap of the waters"; the sense is "within, in the midst of the waters". The Nirukta author:

> अपामुपस्थे महिषा अग्रभ्णत विशो राजानमुप तस्थुर्ऋग्मियम् ।
> आ दूतो अग्निमभरद्विवस्वतो वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वा परावतः ॥

> *apāmupasthe mahiṣā agrabhṇata viśo rājānamupa tasthurṛgmiyam |*
> *ā dūto agnimabharadvivasvato vaiśvānaraṃ mātariśvā parāvataḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-8-4.)

### Printed p. 339  (PDF 357)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 17 [?].)*

Citing this Ṛk, he explains *apām upasthe* as *mahat antarikṣaloke āsīnāḥ* — "being in the great atmospheric world"; Durgācārya, giving the explanation in the sense "*yatropagamya tiṣṭhanti sopasthaḥ*" (the place where they come and stay is the *upastha*), says: "*upasthe*: in the atmospheric world, *tasmin antarikṣaloke*, which is the place where all the waters meet and stay, as the middle region of the atmosphere (*nābhiyalli*) — the lap". Thus the sense is shown.

***ṛtasya*** — *udakasya*: "of water". The word *ṛta* was told before to mean "truth, sacrifice" and the like; since it also has the meaning "water", it must be given this sense here with attention to the context. The Nirukta author reads this word among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]) and (afterwards) *arṇas*, *kṣodaḥ*, etc.; and in the Ṛk

> रमध्वं मे वचसे सोम्याय ऋतावरीरुप मुहूर्तमेवैः ।
> प्र सिन्धुमच्छा बृहती मनीषावस्युरह्वे कुशिकस्य सूनुः ॥

> *ramadhvaṃ me vacase somyāya ṛtāvarīrupa muhūrtamevaiḥ |*
> *pra sindhumacchā bṛhatī manīṣāvasyurahve kuśikasya sūnuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-33-5.) the word *ṛtāvarīḥ* is explained: "full of the waters, with water" — thus explaining that this is the name of rivers.

***svadhāḥ*** — it is read among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]) and among the names of food (Ni. 6-[?]). Here the sense of water, which has the quality of nectar, is given.

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *tadit* — when Agni has blazed up; *savayasā* — those of equal strength (the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu); *samānam arthaṃ* — a common object, the same aim; *mithaḥ* — mutually; *vitaritratā* — striving with faith and by their own acts; [(or) *savayasā* — of equal strength, one in all in doing; *samānam arthaṃ* — a common object; *mithaḥ vitaritratā* — each achieving, in friendly acts]; *vapuḥ* — their own bodies; *yuyūṣataḥ* — (by embracing) wish to unite, as a wedded pair; *vapuḥ* — Agni's body; *yuyūṣataḥ* — they wish to join (by their acts); *ādīm* — immediately; *havyaḥ* — Agni, fit to receive the oblation; *asmat* — from us; *raśmīn* — like rays, the streams of ghee spread out in the *juhū* and the like; *bhagaḥ na* — like Bhaga, the sun; *sarvān* — the worship of all; *sārathiḥ* — like the charioteer; *vāhaḥ* — the reins of the horses that draw the chariot; *ā sam ayaṃsta* — gathers together and accepts in one.

### Printed p. 342  (PDF 360)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 144".)*

**Bhāvārtha.** When Agni has blazed up, the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu, of equal strength and each working with faith for the same common aim, desire to unite Agni's body with their own acts, as a wedded pair [embrace and] unite. Immediately thereupon, as the sun gathers up the worship of all, and as a charioteer gathers into one hand the reins of the horses that draw the chariot, so Agni, fit to receive the oblations, gathers together the streams of ghee spread out like rays, and accepts them.

**English Translation (as printed).** The two (priests, the Hotri and Adhwaryu), of equal honour, and alike assiduous, labouring mutually for a common object, combine the form of Agni ( with their respective functions ) ; whereupon he to whom the oblation is to be offered, collects the drops (of clarified butter), as Bhaga (accepts the worship of all), or as a charioteer (gathers the reins of the horses) that draw (the car).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** In this Ṛk the nature of the performance of the rite is told. Here two kinds of construction of the first half are possible, Sāyaṇa shows. First, *savayasā* — *vitaritratā* (*hotṛ-adhvaryū*) *vapuḥ yuyūṣataḥ*: "the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu, by their several acts, wish to combine Agni's body" (to unite it); the second: *dampatī*, the married couple, wish to join their bodies by embrace; in the same way the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu join their acts with Agni. That is the sense.

***savayasā*** — an epithet of the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu; here the word *vayas* must mean "strength"; the two are of equal strength; in the rite of the Hotṛ, after the *praiṣa*, the recitation of the *yājyā* and the like is the Hotṛ's function, and after the *vaṣaṭkāra* the offering is the Adhvaryu's duty; thus a division. Of the pair (*dampatī*), the epithet is *samānayasya* — "of equal [strength]".

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यमीं द्वा सवयसा सपर्यतः समाने योना मिथुना समोकसा ।
> दिवा न नक्तं पलितो युवाजनि पुरू चरन्नजरो मानुषा युगा ॥ ४ ॥

> *yamīṃ dvā savayasā saparyataḥ samāne yonā mithunā samokasā |*

> दिवा । न । नक्तम् । पलितः । युवा । अजनि । पुरु । चरन् । अजरः । मानुषा । युगा ॥ ४ ॥

> *yam | īm | dvā | savayasā | saparyataḥ | samāne | yonā | mithunā | sam 'okasā |*
> *divā | na | naktam | palitaḥ | yuvā | ajani | puru | caran | ajaraḥ | mānuṣā | yugā ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: Hotṛ and Adhvaryu, like a couple of equal age living together, worship Agni day and night; though "grey" as embers he is born young after kindling, and unageing he consumes much ghee.)*

> यमीमेनमग्निं द्वा द्वौ सवयसा समानवयस्कौ समानसामर्थ्यौ वा समाने योना योनौ फलस्योत्पत्तिस्थाने यज्ञे वर्तमानौ मिथुना मिथुनौ दम्पती इव ऐककार्योद्युक्तौ [?] समोकसा समानवासौ देवयजनस्थानौ [?] होत्रध्वर्यू सपर्यतः पूजयतः स्तुत्या हविष्प्रदानेन च प्रीणयतः । कदेत्याह । दिवा नाहनीव नक्तं रात्रावपि । सर्वदेत्यर्थः । एवं पूज्यमानोऽग्निः पलितः पूर्वमङ्गारावस्थायां जीर्णोऽपि समिन्धनानन्तरं युवा तरुणतेजसा सर्वस्य मिश्रयिता वा [?] अजनि । जायते । मानुषा युगा मनुष्यसम्बन्धीनि [?] युगानि जायापतिरूपाणि होत्रध्वर्युरूपाणि वा प्रीत्यै [?] पुरू बहून्याज्यादीनि चरन् भक्षयन् अजरोऽजीर्णो जराहितो वर्तते ॥ *[small type; several words doubtful]*

> *yamīmenamagniṃ dvā dvau savayasā samānavayaskau samānasāmarthyau vā samāne yonā yonau phalasyotpattisthāne yajñe vartamānau mithunā mithunau dampatī iva aikakāryodyuktau [?] samokasā samānavāsau devayajanasthānau [?] hotradhvaryū saparyataḥ pūjayataḥ stutyā haviṣpradānena ca prīṇayataḥ | kadetyāha | divā nāhanīva naktaṃ rātrāvapi | sarvadetyarthaḥ | evaṃ pūjyamāno 'gniḥ palitaḥ pūrvamaṅgārāvasthāyāṃ jīrṇo 'pi samindhanānantaraṃ yuvā taruṇatejasā sarvasya miśrayitā vā [?] ajani | jāyate | mānuṣā yugā manuṣyasambandhīni [?] yugāni jāyāpatirūpāṇi hotradhvaryurūpāṇi vā prītyai [?] purū bahūnyājyādīni caran bhakṣayan ajaro 'jīrṇo jarāhito vartate ‖ *[small type; several words doubtful]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada, p. 344 end – p. 345).** *savayasā* — of the same age or the same capacity; *samāne yonā* — staying in the sacrificial place that gives the same fruit; *mithunā* — joined together, performing (the one rite); *samokasā* — having the same dwelling; *dvā* — the two, Hotṛ and Adhvaryu (like a couple); *yam īm* — which (Agni); *divā na naktam* — at night as by day; *saparyataḥ* — worship with oblations and the like; *palitaḥ* — (in the first, ember stage) aged; *yuvā* — (after the fuel is fed) young; *ajani* — is born; (and) *mānuṣā yugā* — for the human couples or Hotṛ-Adhvaryus; *puru* — abundant ghee and the like; *caran* — eating; *ajaraḥ* — free of age (he grows).

### Printed p. 345  (PDF 363)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 18 [?].)*

**Bhāvārtha.** Hotṛ and Adhvaryu, of the same age and capacity, staying in the sacrificial place that gives the same fruit, performing one rite together, with the same dwelling like a married couple, worship this Agni by day and night. He, in the beginning aged by his ember stage, becomes young after the fuel is fed; and for the human couples or the Hotṛ-Adhvaryus he is born as one who eats much ghee and the like, ageless.

**English Translation (as printed).** He, whom the two, a pair of equal power, dwelling in the same place, and engaged in the same ceremony, worship night and day: he, whether old or young, has been engendered for the sake of mortal couples, accepting many (oblation), and exempt from decay.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***yonā*** — the word *yoni* is read among the names of water (Ni. 1-[?]) and of houses (Ni. 3-[?]); here it means the sacrificial place, *phalasyotpattisthāne yajñe* ("in the sacrifice, the place where the fruit arises"); the fruit's place of origin is also called a *yoni*; Sāyaṇa explains it thus. Another Brāhmaṇa passage:

> जनिष्ठा उग्रः सहसे तुरायेति सूक्तं शंसति तद्वै [?] यजमानजननमेव सूक्तं यजमानं ह वा एतेन यज्ञो [?] देवलोकस्यै [?] प्रजनयति ।

> *janiṣṭhā ugraḥ sahase turāyeti sūktaṃ śaṃsati tadvai [?] yajamānajananameva sūktaṃ yajamānaṃ ha vā etena yajño [?] devalokasyai [?] prajanayati |*

(Ai. Brā. 3-[?].) Sāyaṇa explains this: "*yajamānaṃ prajanayati*; *tasmād yajamānajananam*", i.e. the sacrificer is born by it for the sake of the divine world (*devalokasthānārtham*): the sacrifice's performer is accomplished in the place of the gods, and so the sacrificial place is a *yoni*. The text goes on to say that, from this, *yajña* is the birth-place of the fruit; other meanings of this word are also seen. The Nirukta author:

> योनिरन्तरिक्षं महानयवयुः [?] परिश्रितो वायुना । आयमयीतसो [?] योनिः रेतस्माद्योनिः परियुतो भवति [?] ॥

> *yonirantarikṣaṃ mahānayavayuḥ [?] pariśrito vāyunā | āyamayītaso [?] yoniḥ retasmādyoniḥ pariyuto bhavati [?] ‖*

(Ni. 3-[?].) "Because *antarikṣa* is great, with its parts pervaded by the wind, it is called *yoni*"; for the production of offspring a *yoni* is also said to be an etymological cause of the word — so they say.

### Printed p. 346  (PDF 364)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 144".)*

In the Ṛk-saṃhitā:

> ऋतस्य देवा अनु व्रता गुर्भुवत्पतिर्द्यौर्न [?] भूम [?] । वर्धन्तीमापः पन्नी [?] सुशिश्विमृतस्य योना गर्भे सुजातम् ॥

> *ṛtasya devā anu vratā gurbhuvatpatirdyaurna [?] bhūma [?] | vardhantīmāpaḥ pannī [?] suśiśvimṛtasya yonā garbhe sujātam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, *ṛtasya yonā* is read, where *yoni* is the name of water: *ṛtasya* — of the sacrifice or of food, because water is the cause of both, water is called *yoni*. And:

> देवं वो देवयज्याग्निमीळीत मर्त्यः । समिद्धः शुक्र दीदिह्यृतस्य योनिमासदः सस्य योनिमासदः ॥

> *devaṃ vo devayajyāgnimīḷīta martyaḥ | samiddhaḥ śukra dīdihyṛtasya yonimāsadaḥ sasya yonimāsadaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk *yoni* is "cause, source" (*kāraṇam*), and in:

> दुरोकशोचिः क्रतुर्न नित्यो जायेव योनावरं विश्वस्मै । चित्रो यदभ्राट्छ्वेतो न विक्षु रथो न रुक्मी त्वेषः समत्सु ॥

> *durokaśociḥ kraturna nityo jāyeva yonāvaraṃ viśvasmai | citro yadabhrāṭchveto na vikṣu ratho na rukmī tveṣaḥ samatsu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) *yoni* is "house" (*gṛham*), as in the other Ṛks quoted; and in the Ṛk in question, too, it means the sacrificial place (*yajñasthānam*). Hotṛ and Adhvaryu both have the same place; hence *samāne yonā*.

***samokasā*** — *samānanivāsau devayajanasthānau*: "the two having a common dwelling, the sacrificial place of the gods". *Hotṛ and Adhvaryu — oka iti nivāsanāma* (Ni. 3-[?]) "*oka* is a name for dwelling". But this word is not used for all dwelling-places. To show that a man has attachment (*abhimāna*) to his own house, the Nirukta author gives the example:

> नहि ग्रभायारणः सुशेवो अन्योदर्यो मनसा मन्तवा उ । अधा चिदोकः पुनरित्स एत्यानो वाज्यभीषाळेतु नव्यः ॥

> *nahi grabhāyāraṇaḥ suśevo anyodaryo manasā mantavā u | adhā cidokaḥ punaritsa etyāno vājyabhīṣāḷetu navyaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?].) citing it, and *atha sa okaḥ punar eva tad eti yata āgato bhavati* (Ni. 3-[?]): "he returns to the home from which he came"; accepted, since a son goes to his own house as it is where he has attachment. As in all sacrifices the fruit arises there and in the sacrificial place, and attachment is the same there, the word *oka* is used here with *sa* (*samokasā*).

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तमीं हिन्वन्ति धीतयो दश व्रिशो [?] देवं मर्तास ऊतये हवामहे ।
> धनोरधि प्रवत आ स ऋण्वत्यभिव्रजद्भिर्वयुना नवाधित ॥ ५ ॥

> *tamīṃ hinvanti dhītayo daśa vriśo [?] devaṃ martāsa ūtaye havāmahe |*
> *dhanoradhi pravata ā sa ṛṇvatyabhivrajadbhirvayunā navādhita ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तम् । ईम् । हिन्वन्ति । धीतयः । दश । व्रिशः [?] । देवम् । मर्तासः । ऊतये । हवामहे ।
> धनोः । अधि । प्रवतः । आ । सः । ऋण्वति । अभिव्रजत्ऽभिः । वयुना । नवा । अधित ॥ ५ ॥

> *tam | īm | hinvanti | dhītayaḥ | daśa | vriśaḥ [?] | devam | martāsaḥ | ūtaye | havāmahe |*
> *dhanoḥ | adhi | pravataḥ | ā | saḥ | ṛṇvati | abhivrajat 'bhiḥ | vayunā | navā | adhita ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: ten fingers please Agni, whom mortals invoke for protection; like an arrow from a bow he sends out his flames, and takes the new praises of the surrounding priests.)*

> देवं द्योतमानं तमेनमग्निं दश धीतयो दशसंख्याका अङ्गुलयो व्रिशः [?] विश [?] परस्परमिश्लिष्य हिन्वन्ति प्रीणयन्ति मिथुनकालेऽ [?] तथा मर्तासो मनुष्या वयं यजमाना ऊतये रक्षणाय हवामहे । अग्न्यमाणः [?] ... स देवो धनोर्धनुषः सकाशात् प्रवतः प्रवणदेशं प्र कर्षेण गच्छतो बाणानिव [?] तान्यथा शरोरुपरि मुञ्चन्ति । आ ऋण्वति ... *[the remainder of this small-type bhāṣya, including its grammatical tail, not legibly read; Sāyaṇa glosses *ṛṇvati* = *gacchati*, *vayunā* = *prajñānāni*, *navā* = *navāni*, *adhita* = *dhārayati/jñāpayati*, with alternative sense *abhivrajadbhiḥ* = *sarvataḥ sañcarad-ṛtvigbhiḥ*]*

> *devaṃ dyotamānaṃ tamenamagniṃ daśa dhītayo daśasaṃkhyākā aṅgulayo vriśaḥ [?] viśa [?] parasparamiśliṣya hinvanti prīṇayanti mithunakāle ' [?] tathā martāso manuṣyā vayaṃ yajamānā ūtaye rakṣaṇāya havāmahe | agnyamāṇaḥ [?] ... sa devo dhanordhanuṣaḥ sakāśāt pravataḥ pravaṇadeśaṃ pra karṣeṇa gacchato bāṇāniva [?] tānyathā śarorupari muñcanti | ā ṛṇvati ... *[the remainder of this small-type bhāṣya, including its grammatical tail, not legibly read; Sāyaṇa glosses *ṛṇvati* = *gacchati*, *vayunā* = *prajñānāni*, *navā* = *navāni*, *adhita* = *dhārayati/jñāpayati*, with alternative sense *abhivrajadbhiḥ* = *sarvataḥ sañcarad-ṛtvigbhiḥ*]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *devam* — the shining; *tam* — Agni; *daśa dhītayaḥ* — ten fingers; *vriśaḥ* [?] — mutually bound, joined together; *hinvanti* — satisfy; *martāsaḥ* — we mortals, the sacrificers; *ūtaye* — for protection; *havāmahe* — invoke (him); *dhanoḥ* — from the bow (released); *pravate ā* — with speed

### Printed p. 349  (PDF 367)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 18 [?].)*

moving, like arrows; *saḥ* — Agni; *ṛṇvati* — his own rays, with speed, makes spread (he sends out); *abhivrajadbhiḥ* — from the foes, moving around from all sides (the surrounding priests); *navā* — the new; *vayunāni* — (of the sacrifice) the knowable, the objects; *adhita* — he accepts. [Or *abhivrajadbhiḥ* — by the Hotṛs and others moving around the fire (purified); *navāni* — new; *vayunāni* — the hymns and the like; *adhita* — he accepts.]

**Bhāvārtha.** The ten fingers together satisfy the shining Agni; we mortals, too, invoke him for protection. As arrows released from a bow go with speed, Agni makes his flames spread with speed; and he accepts the new hymns, made new by the Hotṛs and others moving around him.

**English Translation (as printed).** The ten fingers intertwined propitiate that divine (Agni), whom we mortals invoke for protection: he darts (his rays) like swift (arrows) from a bow, and accepts the new praises (uttered) by those who crowd round the alter [sic].

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***daśadhītayaḥ*** — *dhīti* is the name of karma (action) and *prajñā* (understanding) as told before (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?]). This word is also read among the names of fingers (Ni. 2-[?]); here "ten fingers" is meant.

***vṛiśaḥ*** [?] — this word too is read among the names of fingers (Ni. 2-[?]); here, "though separate, joined together (*parasparaviśliṣya*)", Sāyaṇa has said, showing the etymological explanation as a qualification of *dhītayaḥ*.

***ṛṇvati*** — from the root meaning "to go"; "makes it go (spread), causes to move" is the sense. Other examples:

> क्राणा रुद्रेभिर्वसुभिः पुरोहितो होता निषत्तो रयिषाळमर्त्यः । रथो न विक्षु ऋञ्जसान आयुषु व्यानुषग्वार्या देव ऋण्वति ॥

> *krāṇā rudrebhirvasubhiḥ purohito hotā niṣatto rayiṣāḷamartyaḥ | ratho na vikṣu ṛñjasāna āyuṣu vyānuṣagvāryā deva ṛṇvati ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].)

### Printed p. 350  (PDF 368)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 144".)*

*(Ṛk 5, Special Topics continued.)* … in such Ṛks the sense is *gamayati* ("causes to go"); here too the sense is "makes his rays spread".

The latter half of this Ṛk admits two kinds of meaning, Sāyaṇa has explained: first, "Agni, as the sacrificial-ground fire, makes the priests who go round it on every side know what is to be known (the sacrificial materials)"; second, "he accepts the new hymns and the like of the Hotṛs and others who, going all round, have purified him".

***vayunā*** — it is read among the names of *prajñā* (understanding), *ketaḥ, ketuḥ* (Ni. 3-[?]); since it makes clear [?], this sense is given. *vayunaṃ vetes kāntir vā prajñā vā* (Ni. 3-[?]): derived from the root *vī* in the sense "to desire, wish", or of "understanding" — the Nirukta author shows this and cites:

> स इत्तमोऽवयुनं [?] तस्तन्वत्सूर्येण वयुनवच्चकार [?] । कदा ते मर्ता अमृतस्य धामेयक्षन्तो न मिनन्ति स्वधावः ॥

> *sa ittamo 'vayunaṃ [?] tastanvatsūryeṇa vayunavaccakāra [?] | kadā te martā amṛtasya dhāmeyakṣanto na minanti svadhāvaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?].) From this Ṛk, *sa tamo vayunaṃ tastanvat sūryeṇa vayunavac cakāra* (Ni. [?]): "in the form of the Sun, who has spread out [?] the dark, he made understanding [?]", is explained. The word in the present Ṛk means "(sacrificial) objects of understanding".

***adhita*** — *jñāpayati*: "makes (them) know" (in the first sense); *stotrādīni dhatte*: "accepts hymns and the like" (in the other sense).

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar page, noted briefly).** *hinvanti* (root *hivi prīṇane*; *lat* 3rd plural; *nu* [?]-affix; *idito num dhātoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-58) *num*; no *nighāta*-accent as after *tiṅanta* [?]); *dhītayaḥ* (root *dudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *kticc* [?] suffix; *ghumāsthāgāpā…* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-66) *ī* for the root; *citsvara*, final *udātta*); *vriśaḥ* [?] (Vedic *repha*-insertion; nom. pl.); *martāsaḥ* (*ajjhanagamāṃ*… no — *ajjhasīrasuk* [?] (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50) *asuk*)

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वं ह्यग्ने दिव्यस्य राजसि त्वं पार्थिवस्य पशुपा इव त्मना ।
> एनी त एते बृहती अभिश्रिया हिरण्ययी वक्वरी बर्हिराशाते ॥ ६ ॥

> *tvaṃ hyagne divyasya rājasi tvaṃ pārthivasya paśupā iva tmanā |*
> *enī ta ete bṛhatī abhiśriyā hiraṇyayī vakvarī barhirāśāte ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वम् । हि । अग्ने । दिव्यस्य । राजसि । त्वम् । पार्थिवस्य । पशुपाःऽइव । त्मना ।
> एनी इति । ते । एते इति । बृहती इति । अभिऽश्रिया । हिरण्ययी इति । वक्वरी इति ।
> बर्हिः । आशाते इति ॥ ६ ॥

> *tvam | hi | agne | divyasya | rājasi | tvam | pārthivasya | paśupāḥ 'iva | tmanā |*
> *enī iti | te | ete iti | bṛhatī iti | abhi 'śriyā | hiraṇyayī iti | vakvarī iti |*
> *barhiḥ | āśāte iti ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: Agni rules the heavenly and the earthly as a herdsman rules his herd by his own power; heaven and earth, bright, vast, golden, resounding, pervade his sacrificial grass.)*

> हे अग्ने त्वं दिव्यस्य दिवि भवस्य देवादेः [?] ... राजसि । ईशिषे ऐश्वर्यं ... तथा पार्थिवस्य पृथिवीसम्बन्धिनो मनुष्यादेः । किमिव । पशुपा इव पशुपालको यथा स्वसामर्थ्येनैव पशूनां निरोधनिर्गमनादिव्यापारेषु समर्थो भवति तद्वत् । *[the rest of this small-type bhāṣya — the explanation of *enī, ete, bṛhatī, abhiśriyā, hiraṇyayī, vakvarī, barhir āśāte* and its grammatical tail — is not legibly read; only fragments such as *dyāvāpṛthivyau barhir āśāte, vyāpnutaḥ, vakvarī* … *vacer* … *chāndasaṃ kutvaṃ* … are made out]*

> *he agne tvaṃ divyasya divi bhavasya devādeḥ [?] ... rājasi | īśiṣe aiśvaryaṃ ... tathā pārthivasya pṛthivīsambandhino manuṣyādeḥ | kimiva | paśupā iva paśupālako yathā svasāmarthyenaiva paśūnāṃ nirodhanirgamanādivyāpāreṣu samartho bhavati tadvat | *[the rest of this small-type bhāṣya — the explanation of *enī, ete, bṛhatī, abhiśriyā, hiraṇyayī, vakvarī, barhir āśāte* and its grammatical tail — is not legibly read; only fragments such as *dyāvāpṛthivyau barhir āśāte, vyāpnutaḥ, vakvarī* … *vacer* … *chāndasaṃ kutvaṃ* … are made out]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *agne* — O Agni; *tvam* — you; *paśupā iva* — as a herdsman, having his own independent power over the cattle; *tmanā* — by your own independent power; *divyasya* — of the dwellers in heaven, the gods and others; *rājasi hi* — you reign indeed [rest of this page is cut off by the Kannada page break].

### Printed p. 353  (PDF 371)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 19 [?].)*

*(Pratipadārtha continued.)* *tvam* — you; *pārthivasya* — of those on the earth, all the humans, who are lords (*īśvara*); *bṛhatī* — extremely vast (and); *abhiśriyā* — endowed with *aiśvarya* or served by all, worshipped; *hiraṇyayī* — beneficial to the world [hitakara], desirable; *vakvarī* — pleasing to the mind, resounding; *enī* — shining [prakāśamāna]; *ete* — these heaven and earth; *te* — your; *barhiḥ* — sacrifice; *āśāte* — pervading, spread.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, as a herdsman always reigns over the cattle with his own independent power, so you always, by your own power, reign over the gods and others in heaven, and over all the humans on earth. Extremely vast, worshipped, beneficial to the world, desirable, resounding, shining heaven and earth spread over your sacrifice.

**English Translation (as printed).** You Agni, reign over (the dwellers in) heaven, and over those of earth, according to your own (will), as a herdsman over his (herd) and those two, (heaven and earth), bright, vast, adorable, beneficent, and sounding (agreeably), partake of the oblation.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***abhiśriyā*** — *prāptaiśvaryau abhitaḥ sevyau vā*: "possessing attained lordship, or served on all sides"; Sāyaṇa says it shows the greatness of heaven and earth. As this qualifier it is generally used in the senses "worshipful, support or refuge"; it is the *dyāvāpṛthivī* that are the objects. In many places the greatness of the pair is shown in a special way, e.g.:

> प्रत्नवती भुवनानामभिश्रियोर्वी पृथ्वी मधुदुघे सुपेशसा । द्यावापृथिवी वरुणस्य धर्मणा विष्कभिते अजरे भूरिरेतसा ॥

> *pratnavatī bhuvanānāmabhiśriyorvī pṛthvī madhudughe supeśasā | dyāvāpṛthivī varuṇasya dharmaṇā viṣkabhite ajare bhūriretasā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?].) This Ṛk praises the earth as worshipped by all the worlds.

> प्रत्नं होतारमीड्यं जुष्टमग्निं कविक्रतुम् । अध्वराणामभिश्रियम् ॥

> *pratnaṃ hotāramīḍyaṃ juṣṭamagniṃ kavikratum | adhvarāṇāmabhiśriyam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk the quality of Agni being worshipped by the world is told.

***vakvarī*** — *atikuśalaṃ śabdayantyau*: "sounding very skilfully"; since the *dyāvāpṛthivī* are qualified, the adjective is applied to them (the source cites *Vakvarī*; *vaki kauṭilye*, *"ity asmād dhātoś chāndaso namabhāvaḥ"*, as Sāyaṇa says)

### Printed p. 354  (PDF 372)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 144".)*

… it becomes derived from *vacaḥ* (the sound-making root). *vaki kauṭilye*, says Sāyaṇa, from this *vakvarī* — but here, because it is a word referring to "making sound" and in all such contexts *vakvarī* and *vakvā* are used with the sense of sounding, one must say that these words are made from the root *vac* (*vacer*). Examples:

> शं पृच्छन्ति वज्रहस्तं रथेष्ठामिन्द्रं नेषि वक्वरी यस्य सू गीः । तुविग्राभं तुविकूर्मिं रभोदां गातुमिषे नक्षते तुम्रमच्छ ॥

> *śaṃ pṛcchanti vajrahastaṃ ratheṣṭhāmindraṃ neṣi vakvarī yasya sū gīḥ | tuvigrābhaṃ tuvikūrmiṃ rabhodāṃ gātumiṣe nakṣate tumramaccha ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, *vakvarī* is *guṇānāṃ vaktrī* (utterer of virtues) "such praise" (*gīḥ*, *stuti*): since it qualifies praise — "that which speaks out, praises merit" — the root *vac* is the source of the rest also. And of the form *vakvā*:

> असर्जि वक्वा रथ्ये यथाजौ धिया मनोता प्रथमो मनीषी । दश स्वसारो अधि सानो अव्ये जिग्र्यं [?] वह्निं सदनान्यच्छ ॥

> *asarji vakvā rathye yathājau dhiyā manotā prathamo manīṣī | daśa svasāro adhi sāno avye jigryaṃ [?] vahniṃ sadanānyaccha ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?].) here *vakvā* qualifies *śabdāyamānaḥ* "sounding" Soma; and

> श्रुधी हवमिन्द्र शूर पृथ्या उत स्रवसे विश्वस्मै [?] । आ यस्ते योनिं घृतवन्तमस्वारूर्मिर्न निम्नैर्द्रवयन्त वक्वाः ॥

> *śrudhī havamindra śūra pṛthyā uta sravase viśvasmai [?] | ā yaste yoniṃ ghṛtavantamasvārūrmirna nimnairdravayanta vakvāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) in this Ṛk *vakvāḥ* qualifies the sounding hymns; and

> प्राग्रुवो नभन्योः [?] न वक्वा ध्वसा अपिन्वद्युवतीर्ऋतज्ञाः । धन्वान्यज्राँ अपस्रोतसो [?] अधोगिन्द्रः स्रोत्री [?] इमस्य पत्नीः ॥

> *prāgruvo nabhanyoḥ [?] na vakvā dhvasā apinvadyuvatīrṛtajñāḥ | dhanvānyajrā~ apasrotaso [?] adhogindraḥ srotrī [?] imasya patnīḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?].) in this Ṛk, it qualifies the sounding streams; therefore the root *vac* is to be said the source of this word too.

***rājasi*** — this word is read among the names of lordship (Ni. 2-[?]): *īśvaro bhavasi*: "you are the lord", "you are the one who is able", is the sense.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar page, noted briefly).** *divyasya* (*divi bhavaṃ divyam* — *divyam*: *bhave chandasi* (Pā. Sū. 4-4-110) *yat*; accent from the suffix: final *udātta*; genitive sg.)

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अग्ने जुषस्व प्रति हर्य तद्वचो मन्द्र स्वधावन्नृतजात सुक्रतो ।
> यो विश्वतः प्रत्यङ्ङसि दर्शतो रण्वः संदृष्टौ पितुमाँ इव क्षयः ॥ ७ ॥

> *agne juṣasva prati harya tadvaco mandra svadhāvannṛtajāta sukrato |*
> *yo viśvataḥ pratyaṅṅasi darśato raṇvaḥ saṃdṛṣṭau pitumā~ iva kṣayaḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अग्ने । जुषस्व । प्रति । हर्य । तत् । वचः । मन्द्र । स्वधाऽवः । ऋतऽजात । सुऽक्रतो इति सुऽक्रतो ।
> यः । विश्वतः । प्रत्यङ् । असि । दर्शतः । रण्वः । सम्ऽदृष्टौ । पितुमान्ऽइव । क्षयः ॥ ७ ॥

> *agne | juṣasva | prati | harya | tat | vacaḥ | mandra | svadhā 'vaḥ | ṛta 'jāta | su 'krato iti su 'krato |*
> *yaḥ | viśvataḥ | pratyaṅ | asi | darśataḥ | raṇvaḥ | sam 'dṛṣṭau | pitumān 'iva | kṣayaḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: Agni, be pleased with the oblation and this hymn; you face everyone favourably, are lovely to see, delightful in sight, and a home like the owner of abundant food.)*

> हे अग्ने जुषस्व सेवस्व हविः प्रीतो भव वा स्तुत्या । किञ्चेत्येतादृशं प्रियकरं वचो वाग्रूपं स्तोत्रं प्रति हर्य पुनः कामयस्व । हे मन्द्र मादनशील स्तुत्य वा हे स्वधावो [?] हविर्लक्षणान्नवन् हे ऋतजात यज्ञार्थमुत्पन्न हे सुक्रतो शोभनकर्मन् शोभनप्रज्ञ वा । य एवंविधस्त्वं विश्वतः सर्वस्य स्थावरजङ्गमस्य जगतः प्रत्यङ्ङसि अभिमुखोऽनुकूलोऽसि । न पराङ्मुख इत्यर्थः । तथा दर्शतो दर्शनीयः सर्वैः किञ्च संदृष्टौ सम्यग्दर्शने रण्वो रमणशीलो रमयिता वा भवसि सर्वस्य । यद्वा । तव संदृष्टौ सतां सर्वेषां जनानां क्षयो निवासस्थानं भवति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । पितुमानिव अतिप्रभूतान्नस्वामी यथा सर्वैराश्रयणीयो [?] गन्तव्यश्च भवति तद्वत् ॥ *[small type; several words doubtful]*

> *he agne juṣasva sevasva haviḥ prīto bhava vā stutyā | kiñcetyetādṛśaṃ priyakaraṃ vaco vāgrūpaṃ stotraṃ prati harya punaḥ kāmayasva | he mandra mādanaśīla stutya vā he svadhāvo [?] havirlakṣaṇānnavan he ṛtajāta yajñārthamutpanna he sukrato śobhanakarman śobhanaprajña vā | ya evaṃvidhastvaṃ viśvataḥ sarvasya sthāvarajaṅgamasya jagataḥ pratyaṅṅasi abhimukho 'nukūlo 'si | na parāṅmukha ityarthaḥ | tathā darśato darśanīyaḥ sarvaiḥ kiñca saṃdṛṣṭau samyagdarśane raṇvo ramaṇaśīlo ramayitā vā bhavasi sarvasya | yadvā | tava saṃdṛṣṭau satāṃ sarveṣāṃ janānāṃ kṣayo nivāsasthānaṃ bhavati | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | pitumāniva atiprabhūtānnasvāmī yathā sarvairāśrayaṇīyo [?] gantavyaśca bhavati tadvat ‖ *[small type; several words doubtful]**

### Printed p. 357  (PDF 375)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 20 [?].)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *mandra* — gladdener or worshipful; *svadhāvaḥ* — having food in the form of oblation; *ṛtajāta* — born for the sacrifice; *sukrato* — of excellent action or of excellent understanding; *agne* — O Agni; *juṣasva* — partake of the oblation (or be pleased); (and) *tat* — that which is beneficial; *vacaḥ* — the praise in the form of speech; *pratiharya* — desire and accept; *yaḥ* — you who are such; *viśvataḥ* — to the whole world; *pratyaṅ asi* — you are favourable, facing it; *darśataḥ* — visible (to all); *saṃdṛṣṭau* — to behold well; *raṇvaḥ* — you are delightful; (and) *pitumān iva* — as the lord of abundant food is a refuge to all; *kṣayaḥ* — you are the dwelling-place.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, delighter of all, having food in the form of oblations, born for the sacrifice, of excellent action — partake of our oblation and accept our hymns. You are favourable to all the world, visible to all, delightful to behold; and like the lord of abundant food, you are the dwelling-place of all.

**English Translation (as printed).** Agni, you confer happiness, you accept oblations, you were born for sacrifice, and are the performer of good works ; be pleased (with this rite), attend to this prayer : for you are in presence of all (the world), are visible (to all) are pleasant in their sight, and are their refuge, like a (bountiful) distributor of food.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***raṇvaḥ*** — *ramaṇaśīlaḥ ramayitā vā*: "one who delights, or who makes (others) delight"; the sense is "he who himself delights in oblations and the like, or who makes gods, men and others delight by his own form".

***ṛtajāta*** — Agni is addressed as "born in the sacrifice" or "born for the sake of the sacrifice".

***pratiharya*** — *kāmayasva*, "desire", i.e. "accept, desiring". The Nirukta author:

> आ रुद्रास इन्द्रवन्तः सजोषसो हिरण्यरथाः सुविताय गन्तन । इयं वो अस्मत्प्रति हर्यते मतिस्तृष्णजे न दिव उत्सा उदन्यवे ॥

> *ā rudrāsa indravantaḥ sajoṣaso hiraṇyarathāḥ suvitāya gantana | iyaṃ vo asmatprati haryate matistṛṣṇaje na diva utsā udanyave ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-[?]-[?].)

### Printed p. 358  (PDF 376)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 144".)*

Citing this Ṛk, he explains *pratiharyate* as "desires, accepting" (Ni. [?]); the same meaning applies here.

***mandra*** — *mādanaśīla stutya vā*: "gladdening or praiseworthy"; it is an adjective of Agni in the sense "giver of joy or worshipful". The Nirukta author:

> देवीं वाचमजनयन्त देवास्तां विश्वरूपाः पशवो वदन्ति । सा नो मन्द्रेषमूर्जं दुहाना धेनुर्वागस्मानुप सुष्टुतैतु ॥

> *devīṃ vācamajanayanta devāstāṃ viśvarūpāḥ paśavo vadanti | sā no mandreṣamūrjaṃ duhānā dhenurvāgasmānupa suṣṭutaitu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk he explains *mandra* as *madana*, "joy-producing" (Ni. [?]); Sāyaṇa too, on this Ṛk, shows several senses of the word — *madayitrī*, "praiseworthy", *harṣayitrī* "delighting". The same word the Nirukta author has also listed among the names of food (*vāja*) (Ni. 2-[?]).

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar page, noted briefly).** *juṣasva* (root *juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*; *loṭ* 2nd sg. ātmanepada; the final-*udātta* … ); with *agne* as a vocative preceding, the verb being *saṃbuddhi*-governed, *āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-72) makes it as if the vocative did not exist, so the *nighāta*-accent of the *tiṅanta* does not occur because it is *pāda*-initial [?]; *tāsyanudāttet…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) the *lasārvadhātuka* is *anudātta*, so the *vikaraṇa* accent remains. *harya* (root *harya gatikāntyoḥ*; *loṭ* 2nd sg.; no *nighāta* after … ); *mandra* (root *madi stutimodamadasvapnakāntigatiṣu*; *sphāyitañcivañci…* (Uṇ. Sū. 2-[?]) *rak*; *idita*: *num*; vocative; no *nighāta* because *pāda*-initial; *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198) first *udātta*); *svadhāvaḥ* (*tadasyāsti*: *matup*; *mādupadhāyāś ca…* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-9) *va* for *ma*; *matuvasor ruḥ sambuddhau* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-1) *ru*; as the earlier word is a vocative that does not exist, first *udātta*); *ṛtajāta* (*ṛtāya yajñāya jātaḥ* — *ṛtajātaḥ*, *tatpuruṣa*; first-member accent).

Sū. 5-3-7) *tasil* in the ablative sense; *liti* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) [?] *udātta* before the suffix); *asi* (root *as bhuvi*; *laṭ* 2nd sg. *sip*; *tāsastyoḥ lopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-4-50) loss of *s* of the root; as *yat* is connected, *nighāta* is prevented, hence the root accent remains); *darśataḥ* (root *dṛśir prekṣaṇe*; *bhṛmṛdṛśi…* (Uṇ. Sū. 3-110) *atac*; *guṇa* of *i* on account of it; *ajiṣṭe* [?]; final *udātta*); *raṇvaḥ* (root *ravi gatau*; *kvan* [?] in the sense of agent; *idito num dhātoḥ* *num*; *aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi* (Pā. Sū. 8-4-2) *ṇatva*; final *udātta* from the suffix); *saṃdṛṣṭau* (root *dṛśir prekṣaṇe*; *striyāṃ ktin* [?]; *vraścabhrasja…* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-36) *ṣatva* of the root-ending; *tāḍau ca niti* … [?], *gati* (*sam*) keeps its natural accent). ‖ 7 ‖

*Here the 144th Sūkta ends.*

## Sūkta 145

### Printed p. 359 (continued; PDF 377)

*(The Kannada heading reads "The 145th Sūkta".)*

*(Anukramaṇī, Sanskrit; not rendered in English. Gist: the sūkta of five Ṛks beginning "Taṃ pṛcchata" is the fifth [?] sūkta, of Dīrghatamas, in Jagatī, the last Ṛk in Triṣṭubh; Agni is the deity; its use is at the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra.)*

> तं पृच्छतेति पञ्चर्चं पञ्चमं सूक्तम् । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । तं पृच्छत पञ्चान्त्या त्रिष्टुबिति । दीर्घतमा ऋषिः । पूर्वत्राग्नेयं [?] तु तदितिकृत्वादिमेऽप्याग्नेयम् [?] । अन्त्या त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टाः [?] जगत्यः [?] ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्विनियोग उक्तः ॥

> *taṃ pṛcchateti pañcarcaṃ pañcamaṃ sūktam | atrānukramaṇikā | taṃ pṛcchata pañcāntyā triṣṭubiti | dīrghatamā ṛṣiḥ | pūrvatrāgneyaṃ [?] tu taditikṛtvādime 'pyāgneyam [?] | antyā triṣṭup śiṣṭāḥ [?] jagatyaḥ [?] ‖ prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayorviniyoga uktaḥ ‖*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta *taṃ pṛcchata* is the fifth sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. In the Anukramaṇī it is said *taṃ pṛcchata pañcāntyā triṣṭub*. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Dīrghatamas. Agni is the deity. The last Ṛk is in Triṣṭubh metre; the remaining Ṛks are in Jagatī. This sūkta is used for the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra mantra recitals.

**॥ ओम् ॥**

**Sūkta 145** — Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 21, Sūkta 145; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 21 [?]. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Ṛṣi: Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Devatā: Agni. Chandas: 1–4 Jagatī, 5 Triṣṭubh [?].

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तं पृच्छता स जगामा स वेद स चिकित्वाँ ईयते सो न्वीयते [?] ।
> तस्मिन्त्सन्ति प्रशिषस्तस्मिन्निष्टयः स वाजस्य शवसः शुष्मिणस्पतिः ॥ १ ॥

> *taṃ pṛcchatā sa jagāmā sa veda sa cikitvā~ īyate so nvīyate [?] |*
> *tasmintsanti praśiṣastasminniṣṭayaḥ sa vājasya śavasaḥ śuṣmiṇaspatiḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तम् । पृच्छत । सः । जगाम । सः । वेद । सः । चिकित्वान् । ईयते । सः । नु । ईयते ।
> तस्मिन् । सन्ति । प्रऽशिषः । तस्मिन् । इष्टयः । सः । वाजस्य । शवसः । शुष्मिणः । पतिः ॥ १ ॥

> *tam | pṛcchata | saḥ | jagāma | saḥ | veda | saḥ | cikitvān | īyate | saḥ | nu | īyate |*
> *tasmin | santi | pra 'śiṣaḥ | tasmin | iṣṭayaḥ | saḥ | vājasya | śavasaḥ | śuṣmiṇaḥ | patiḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: sacrificers, ask Agni what you want; he goes everywhere, knows all, is resorted to; in him are the powers of command and the sacrifices; he is lord of food, strength and the mighty.)*

> हे यजमानाः तमग्निं पृच्छत । यत्र ग्रादि [?] विषयं प्रष्टव्यमस्ति तत् तस्यैव प्रष्टव्यमित्यतिशयमाह । स जगाम सः सर्वत्र गच्छति । अत एव स वेद स च प्रष्टव्यं जानाति । स चिकित्वान् । कुमितेरसाधारणत्वेन नेतृत्वात्रः । स विशेषज्ञः इत्यर्थः । स ईयते । ज्ञेयैकाकाशं गच्छति । पुनर्गतिरेव विशेष्यते । सः सोऽग्निर्जज्ञे ... स नु क्षिप्रमीयते । यद्वा यजमानस्य ज्ञेयमस्ति तमर्थं ज्ञातुं शीघ्रमेव गच्छतीत्यर्थः । यद्वा ज्ञानार्थमीयते सेव्यते । तथा शीघ्रमनुसेव्यते । यस्माद्वेदमुक्तरूपः तस्मात्तमेव पृच्छतेत्यर्थः । कर्तव्यापेक्षितानां कामानां संनीतानाह । तस्मिन्नग्नौ प्रशिषः प्रशासनानि नियमनसामर्थ्यानि सन्ति । असाध्यं नियमितुमपि साधयितुं शक्त इत्यर्थः । किञ्च तस्मिन्नेवाग्नौ इष्टयः इष्टव्या भोगाः सर्वफलसाधकाः यागा वा सन्ति । किञ्च सोऽग्निर्वाजस्यान्नस्य शवसो बलस्य च पतिः पालयिता दाता । किञ्च शुष्मिणो बलवतो राजादेरपि पतिः स्वामी । यस्मादयं महानुभावस्तस्मात्त्रमेव पृष्ट्वा पुरुषार्थं साधयतेति ॥ *[small type; several words doubtful]*

> *he yajamānāḥ tamagniṃ pṛcchata | yatra grādi [?] viṣayaṃ praṣṭavyamasti tat tasyaiva praṣṭavyamityatiśayamāha | sa jagāma saḥ sarvatra gacchati | ata eva sa veda sa ca praṣṭavyaṃ jānāti | sa cikitvān | kumiterasādhāraṇatvena netṛtvātraḥ | sa viśeṣajñaḥ ityarthaḥ | sa īyate | jñeyaikākāśaṃ gacchati | punargatireva viśeṣyate | saḥ so 'gnirjajñe ... sa nu kṣipramīyate | yadvā yajamānasya jñeyamasti tamarthaṃ jñātuṃ śīghrameva gacchatītyarthaḥ | yadvā jñānārthamīyate sevyate | tathā śīghramanusevyate | yasmādvedamuktarūpaḥ tasmāttameva pṛcchatetyarthaḥ | kartavyāpekṣitānāṃ kāmānāṃ saṃnītānāha | tasminnagnau praśiṣaḥ praśāsanāni niyamanasāmarthyāni santi | asādhyaṃ niyamitumapi sādhayituṃ śakta ityarthaḥ | kiñca tasminnevāgnau iṣṭayaḥ iṣṭavyā bhogāḥ sarvaphalasādhakāḥ yāgā vā santi | kiñca so 'gnirvājasyānnasya śavaso balasya ca patiḥ pālayitā dātā | kiñca śuṣmiṇo balavato rājāderapi patiḥ svāmī | yasmādayaṃ mahānubhāvastasmāttrameva pṛṣṭvā puruṣārthaṃ sādhayateti ‖ *[small type; several words doubtful]**

### Printed p. 361  (PDF 379)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 21 [?].)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *tam* — Agni; *pṛcchata* — (you) ask — all objects you want to know; *saḥ* — Agni; *jagāma* — he goes about in all regions; *saḥ* — he; *veda* — knows all; *saḥ* — he; *cikitvān* — is endowed with special understanding; *īyate* — goes to the neighbourhood of the object to be known; *saḥ* — he; *nu jāgṛtiḥ* [?] *yāgīya* [?] *īyate* — goes (towards the sacrificers); or (for the sake of knowledge) is resorted to; *tasmin* — in that Agni; *praśiṣaḥ* — the power of restraint also; *santi* — are; *tasmin* — in him; *iṣṭayaḥ* — all enjoyments or the sacrifices that give the fruit (are); *saḥ* — he; *vājasya* — of food; *śavasaḥ* — of strength; *patiḥ* — is the giver; *śuṣmiṇaḥ* — (of the king and others) he is the lord of the powerful, too.

**Bhāvārtha.** Agni goes about in all regions and knows everything. He is endowed with special understanding, and goes to the neighbourhood of the object to be known, for the sake of the sacrificer. In him is the power of restraint. He is the treasure of all enjoyments. He is the giver of food and of strength, and the lord even of the powerful.

**English Translation (as printed).** Ask (of Agni what you desire), for he goes (everywhere), he knows (all things): possessed of intelligence, he proceeds (to ascertain what is to be done), and is had recourse to (by his worshippers) ; for in him is the power of restraining (unreasonable desires), [in] him (is the power of granting) enjoyment ; he is the giver of food and of strength ; the protector of the mighty.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***praśiṣaḥ*** — this word is explained here as "the power of restraint, regulation (*niyamana*)"; it is said to be derived from the root *śās* in the sense of command. Further …

### Printed p. 362  (PDF 380)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 145".)*

*(Ṛk 1, Special Topics continued.)*

> स सूर्येण रश्मिभिः परि व्यत तन्तुं तन्वानस्त्रिवृतं यथा विदे । नयन्नृतस्य प्रशिषो नवीयसीः पतिर्जनीनामुप याति निष्कृतम् ॥

> *sa sūryeṇa raśmibhiḥ pari vyata tantuṃ tanvānastrivṛtaṃ yathā vide | nayannṛtasya praśiṣo navīyasīḥ patirjanīnāmupa yāti niṣkṛtam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk the word *praśiṣaḥ* is explained as *praśaṃsanā*, "praise" (the sense "approved praise" being intended), so the word here must be derived from the root *śaṃs*, "to praise".

> [?] सप्त सिन्धवः प्रशिषं सोमं सिस्रते । तुभ्यं धावन्ति धेनवः ॥

> *[?] sapta sindhavaḥ praśiṣaṃ somaṃ sisrate | tubhyaṃ dhāvanti dhenavaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?].) Here, where it is said that the seven rivers and the Soma follow the command (*ājñā*), *praśiṣaḥ* is *praśāsanam*, "command".

> य आत्मदा बलदा यस्य विश्व उपासते प्रशिषं यस्य देवाः । यस्य छायाऽमृतं यस्य मृत्युः कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥

> *ya ātmadā baladā yasya viśva upāsate praśiṣaṃ yasya devāḥ | yasya chāyā 'mṛtaṃ yasya mṛtyuḥ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-121-2.) Here too *praśiṣam* means *prakṛṣṭaṃ śāsanam*, "excellent command", the command of Prajāpati, he being the best of the gods. In the Ṛk at hand also the sense is "regulation" (*niyamana*), i.e. the power of regulation of Agni.

***iṣṭayaḥ*** — *iṣṭavyā bhogāḥ sarvaphalasādhakā yāgā vā*: "desired enjoyments, or sacrifices that accomplish all fruits"; Sāyaṇa explains: "enjoyments desired, or sacrifices that give all fruits". The word *iṣṭi*, though it occurs among the names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-[?]), in contexts like this it is derived from the root *iṣ*, or from *yaj*; there is discussion on this among some scholars (Oldenberg, Z. D. M. G. XXXII [?] 473). Its use in the *Ṛk-saṃhitā* in the senses of the two roots can be seen:

> नित्ये चिन्नु यं सदने जगृभ्रे प्रशस्तिभिर्दधिरे यज्ञियासः । प्र सू नयन्त गृभयन्त इष्टावश्वासो न रथ्यो राराहाणाः ॥

> *nitye cinnu yaṃ sadane jagṛbhre praśastibhirdadhire yajñiyāsaḥ | pra sū nayanta gṛbhayanta iṣṭāvaśvāso na rathyo rārāhāṇāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) Here *iṣṭau* "in the sacrifice, which brings about the desired objects"; and in

> न यस्य सातुर्जनितोरवारि न मातरापितरा नू चिदिष्टौ । अधा मित्रो न सुधितः पावकोऽग्निर्दीदाय मानुषीषु विक्षु ॥

> *na yasya sāturjanitoravāri na mātarāpitarā nū cidiṣṭau | adhā mitro na sudhitaḥ pāvako 'gnirdīdāya mānuṣīṣu vikṣu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?].)

### Printed p. 363  (PDF 381)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 21 [?].)*

here *yasya iṣṭau preṣaṇe* ("in whose sacrifice, in sending") — since the sense "sacrifice" is given, the root *iṣ* is the source here.

> यः सरूपा विरूपा एकरूपा यासामग्निरिष्ट्या नामानि वेद । या अङ्गिरसस्तपसेह चक्रुस्तेभ्यः परि [?] सर्जम [?] महि शर्म यच्छ ॥

> *yaḥ sarūpā virūpā ekarūpā yāsāmagniriṣṭyā nāmāni veda | yā aṅgirasastapaseha cakrustebhyaḥ pari [?] sarjama [?] mahi śarma yaccha ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) In these and other Ṛks, the word is shown to be derived from the root *yaj* in the sense "sacrifice". In the Ṛk at hand both meanings, "enjoyments" and "sacrifices", are given; so no derivation need be insisted on.

***cikitvān*** — *cetanāvān*: "possessing understanding, intelligent".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar page, noted briefly).** *pṛcchata* (root *pracchaṃ jñīpsāyām*; *loṭ* 2nd plural; because after a *tiṅanta*… *nighāta*-accent); *jagāma* (root *gamḷ gatau*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-6) *liṭ* in the present sense; 3rd sg.; *tiṅ*-*nighāta*); *veda* (root *vida jñāne*; *laṭ* 3rd sg.; *vido laṭo vā* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-83) *ṇal*-substitution; *pugantalaghūpadhasya ca* guṇa of the root; *nighāta*); *cikitvān* (root *kita jñāne*; by *chandasi* *liṭ*; *kvasu*; *kvasuś ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-107); nominative sg.; *vasu*-accent); *īyate* (root *īṅ gatau*, *divādi*; *laṭ* 3rd sg.; *nighāta*); *praśiṣaḥ* (root *śāsu anuśiṣṭau*; *kvip ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-76) *kvip*; *śāsa idaṅhaloḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-34) *i*; *śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-60) *ṣa*; *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) *kṛt*-accent of the later member of the compound); *iṣṭayaḥ* (root *iṣu icchāyām*; *ktin*; accent from the suffix; *ṭakāra* of *kta* → *mantre vṛṣeṣa…* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-96) *ktin* udātta). ‖ 1 ‖
