#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> तमित्पृच्छन्ति न सिमो वि पृच्छति स्वेनेव धीरो मनसा यदग्रभीत् ।
> न मृष्यते प्रथमं नापरं वचोऽस्य क्रत्वा सचते अप्रदृपितः ॥ २ ॥

> *tamitpṛcchanti na simo vi pṛcchati sveneva dhīro manasā yadagrabhīt |*
> *na mṛṣyate prathamaṃ nāparaṃ vaco 'sya kratvā sacate apradṛpitaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तम् । इत् । पृच्छन्ति । न । सिमः । वि । पृच्छति । स्वेनऽइव । धीरः । मनसा । यत् ।
> अग्रभीत् । न । मृष्यते । प्रथमम् । न । अपरम् । वचः । अस्य । क्रत्वा । सचते । अप्रऽदृपितः ॥ २ ॥

> *tam | it | pṛcchanti | na | simaḥ | vi | pṛcchati | svena 'iva | dhīraḥ | manasā | yat |*
> *agrabhīt | na | mṛṣyate | prathamam | na | aparam | vacaḥ | asya | kratvā | sacate | apra 'dṛpitaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: all ask Agni and none asks him wrongly; the wise one speaks what he has determined in his own mind; he brooks neither a speech before his nor an answer after it; the unarrogant is joined to his protective acts.)*

> पूर्वमन्त्रेऽग्निं पृच्छतेत्युक्तम् । अत्र तु सोऽनुनयेन [?] प्रष्टव्य इत्याह । तमित्तमेवाग्निं पृच्छन्ति सर्वे नान्यं [?] पृच्छन्ति प्रश्नसमये [?] । सिमः सर्वजनो न वि पृच्छति विशेषेण न पृच्छति । पृष्टोऽपि धीरो धीमानयं स्वेनेव मनसा यदग्रभीत् यदग्रहीत् [?] ... तदेवाग्निं पृच्छति न तु बहु भाषते इत्यर्थः । परवाक्यासहिष्णुत्वमाह । अयमग्निः प्रथमं वचः स्ववाक्यात् पूर्वभावि वचनं न मृष्यते न सहते । तथा अपरं वचः स्ववाक्यानन्तरभावि प्रतिवचनं न मृष्यते । यस्मादयमेवंविधस्तस्मादप्रदृपितः [?] अप्रदृप्तः यद्वा केन शिक्षितो ऽनुद्धतः सर्वो लोकोऽस्य महानुभावस्याग्नेः क्रत्वा क्रतुना रक्षणादिकर्मणा सह सचते संगच्छते [?] जीवतीत्यर्थः ॥ *[small type; several words doubtful]*

> *pūrvamantre 'gniṃ pṛcchatetyuktam | atra tu so 'nunayena [?] praṣṭavya ityāha | tamittamevāgniṃ pṛcchanti sarve nānyaṃ [?] pṛcchanti praśnasamaye [?] | simaḥ sarvajano na vi pṛcchati viśeṣeṇa na pṛcchati | pṛṣṭo 'pi dhīro dhīmānayaṃ sveneva manasā yadagrabhīt yadagrahīt [?] ... tadevāgniṃ pṛcchati na tu bahu bhāṣate ityarthaḥ | paravākyāsahiṣṇutvamāha | ayamagniḥ prathamaṃ vacaḥ svavākyāt pūrvabhāvi vacanaṃ na mṛṣyate na sahate | tathā aparaṃ vacaḥ svavākyānantarabhāvi prativacanaṃ na mṛṣyate | yasmādayamevaṃvidhastasmādapradṛpitaḥ [?] apradṛptaḥ yadvā kena śikṣito 'nuddhataḥ sarvo loko 'sya mahānubhāvasyāgneḥ kratvā kratunā rakṣaṇādikarmaṇā saha sacate saṃgacchate [?] jīvatītyarthaḥ ‖ *[small type; several words doubtful]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *tam it* — that very Agni; *pṛcchanti* — (all) ask (what they wish to know); *simaḥ* — all people (anyone at all); *na vi pṛcchati* — does not ask even an improper question; *dhīraḥ* — the intelligent Agni; *svena iva manasā* — by his own understanding; *yat* — whatever matter; *agrabhīt* — he has determined (to say), that alone he tells; [or *dhīraḥ* — the intelligent petitioner; *svena iva manasā* — by his own understanding; *yat* — (the question fit to be asked) which; *agrabhīt* — he has considered and determined — that question alone he asks;]

### Printed p. 365  (PDF 383)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 22 [?].)*

*(Pratipadārtha continued.)* (this Agni) *prathamaṃ vacaḥ* — a word preceding his own; *na mṛṣyate* — does not tolerate; *aparam* — a reply coming after his own word; *na* — does not tolerate; *apradṛpitaḥ* — one devoid of arrogance (alone), or one disciplined by him (alone); *asya* — of this Agni; *kratvā* — by the acts of protection and the like; *sacate* — is joined (is protected).

**Bhāvārtha.** All ask this Agni for what they want to know; no one asks an improper question. Agni, the wise, tells only what he has determined in his own mind. He does not tolerate a word that precedes his own, nor a reply that comes after; only one devoid of arrogance becomes fit for his protection.

**English Translation (as printed).** They ask of Agni, but no one asks improperly; for a sensible man (replies to solicitation) as he has determined in his own mind; Agni tolerates not a speech that anticipates (his reply), nor endures a rejoinder: he who is devoid of arrogance is favoured by his protection.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***simaḥ*** — "all people": the word *sima* is explained as "all". It has the sense *śreṣṭha* ("excellent") in many places:

> यदिन्द्र प्रागपागुदङ्न्यग्वा हूयसे नृभिः । सिमा पुरू नृषूतो अस्यानवेऽसि प्रशर्ध तुर्वशे ॥

> *yadindra prāgapāgudaṅnyagvā hūyase nṛbhiḥ | simā purū nṛṣūto asyānave 'si praśardha turvaśe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk Sāyaṇa explains this word's meaning: *sima iti vai śreṣṭhanāmā ucyate* ("*sima* is said to be a name of the excellent") — citing the views of other commentators, he explains "O Indra, the excellent (*śreṣṭha*)".

### Printed p. 366  (PDF 384)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 145".)*

> तेभ्यो गोधा आयुधं कर्षदेतद्ये ब्रह्मणः प्रतिपीयन्ति [?] अन्नैः । सिमु [?] ऋष्वो वस्पृप्पा [?] अदेन्तु [?] स्वयं बलानि तन्वः शृणानाः ॥

> *tebhyo godhā āyudhaṃ karṣadetadye brahmaṇaḥ pratipīyanti [?] annaiḥ | simu [?] ṛṣvo vaspṛppā [?] adentu [?] svayaṃ balāni tanvaḥ śṛṇānāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk *sima* — *simāṃ śreyān*, "the more excellent"; or *simaśabdaḥ sarvaśabdaparyāyaḥ*, "the word *sima* is synonymous with *sarva*" (Sāyaṇa), "all": he gives both meanings, *śreṣṭha* and *sarva*. In the Ṛk at hand the meaning *sarva* fits; thus "*simo na vi pṛcchati*" — "no one asks an improper question", is the sense.

*svenevadhīro manasā yadagrabhīt* — this sentence admits two kinds of meaning. First, taking *dhīraḥ* as an adjective of Agni: the wise Agni says only what he must say, according to his wisdom. Second, taking *dhīraḥ* as an adjective of the petitioner (*prārthī*): the petitioner asks only the proper question.

***dhīraḥ*** — *dhīmantaḥ prajñāvanto vā*: "the intelligent, or those possessed of understanding"; the many senses of the word *dhīra* have been explained before.

> पुरुप्रैषस्तुरिर्यज्ञसाधनोऽच्छिद्रोतिः शिशुरादत्त सं रभः ॥ ३ ॥

> *tamidgacchanti juhvastamarvatīrviśvānyekaḥ śṛṇavadvacāṃsi me |*

> *... rthamapi hūyamānaṃ ceti bhāvaḥ | kiñcārvatīḥ prāptimatyaḥ stutayastamit [?] gacchanti sarvadevatātmakatvādeva | sa evaiko 'yamagnirviśvāni me madīyāni vacāṃsi sarvāṇi śṛṇavat śṛṇoti | agnirhi sarvadevatātmakaḥ | tai. saṃ. [?] ... tathātraiva purastāt [?] ... tvamagne varuṇo jāyase yattvaṃ mitro [?] ... (ṛ. saṃ. [?]) ityādiko 'sya viśeṣa ityeke [?] | purupraiṣo bahupraiṣasaṃbhāk | yadvā bahupreṣaṇaḥ sarvasmai jñāpayitetyarthaḥ | turiḥ tārayitā | taraterṇarthāt [?] ... iti kinpratyayaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasītvam | yajñasādhano yajñasādhakaḥ | agnirhi [?] ... acchidrotiḥ acchinnarakṣaṇaḥ | śiśuḥ śiśuvatpriyakārī śocayitā vā śatrūṇām | evaṃbhūto 'gniḥ saṃ rabho yajñādisaṃrambhavān san ādatte | havirādikaṃ svīkaroti ‖ *[a Taittirīya-Saṃhitā citation and an Ṛg citation inside this bhāṣya are not legible; references left out]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *juhvaḥ* — the ladles such as the *juhū*, filled with ghee and the like, or the oblations of Soma and the like, or the ghee and the like in the vessels; *tam it* — towards that very Agni; *gacchanti* — go (facing him); *arvatīḥ* — all the hymns; *tam* — (reach) him alone; *ekaḥ* — Agni, the sole representative of all the deities; *me* — my; *viśvāni vacāṃsi* — all the hymn-words; *śṛṇavat* — hears; *purupraiṣaḥ* — the impeller of all; *turiḥ* — who carries (across the world); *yajñasādhanaḥ* — the cause of the sacrifice; *acchidrotiḥ* — whose protection is unbroken; *śiśuḥ* — he who is like a child (doing what is dear), or who makes (enemies) grieve — that Agni; *saṃ rabhaḥ* — together with the equipment (needed for the sacrifice and the like); *ā adatte* — accepts (the oblations).

**Bhāvārtha.** The ladles and other vessels filled with ghee and the like go facing that Agni. As the sole representative of all the gods he hears all my hymns, and the hymns too reach him alone. The impeller of all, who carries across worldly existence, the cause of the sacrifice, whose protection is unceasing, who is like a child to us and makes enemies grieve, Agni accepts the oblations together with the equipment needed for the sacrifice.

### Printed p. 369  (PDF 387)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 22 [?].)*

**English Translation (as printed).** To him the (sacrificial) ladles are directed ; to him (our) praises are addressed ; he alone hears all my prayers; he is the instigator of many, the transporter (across the world), the instrument of sacrifice, the unintermitting preserver (of mankind), and (gentle as) an infant: provided with the preparations (of sacrifice), he accepts the oblation.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***arvatīḥ*** — *prāptimatyaḥ stutayaḥ*: "hymns that reach"; here it means "hymns approaching Agni". In general *arvatī* means "mares"; since the hymns are said to go near Agni like mares being yoked [?], this word is used for hymns also.

***tāraḥ*** [*turiḥ*] — *tārayitā*: "one who carries across worldly existence".

***eko viśvāni vacaḥ śṛṇavat*** — "he alone hears all my hymn-words"; how Agni is the sole representative of all the gods Sāyaṇa explains by citing the Taittirīya-Brāhmaṇa [?]: *agnir vai sarvā devatāḥ* ("Agni is all the deities"), and *te devā bibhyatas tvāgniṃ prāviśan tasmād āhur agniḥ sarvā devatā iti* ("the frightened gods entered Agni; therefore they say Agni is all the deities"). The statement of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā that all the gods, being frightened, took refuge in Agni and that thus he alone is their sole representative is recalled here. In the Ṛk-saṃhitā too:

> यदीं गणस्य रशनामजीगः शुचिरङ्क्ते शुचिभिर्गोभिरग्निः । आद्दक्षिणा युज्यते वाजयन्त्यु [?] नामूर्ध्वो [?] अध्वयुः [?] ॥

> *yadīṃ gaṇasya raśanāmajīgaḥ śuciraṅkte śucibhirgobhiragniḥ | āddakṣiṇā yujyate vājayantyu [?] nāmūrdhvo [?] adhvayuḥ [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) the same sense is expressed. Hence *eko viśvāni vacāṃsi śṛṇavat*: it praises him.

***śiśuḥ*** — *śiśuvat priyakārī* ("doing what pleases, like a child") and *śocayitā vā śatrūṇām* ("or one who causes enemies to grieve") — Sāyaṇa gives two senses; both are possible with regard to Agni.

> हस्ताभ्यां ह्येनं मन्थन्ति शिशुं जातमिति शिशुरिव वा एष प्रथमजातो यदग्निः ।

> *hastābhyāṃ hyenaṃ manthanti śiśuṃ jātamiti śiśuriva vā eṣa prathamajāto yadagniḥ |*

(Ai. Brā. 1-[?].)

### Printed p. 370  (PDF 388)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 145".)*

Thus in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and in other places this quality of his is described. The word *śiśu* does not mean only "child"; to show that it also means "praiseworthy, yes", the Nirukta author says: *śiśuḥ śaṃsanīyo bhavati* (Ni. 10-[?]): "*śiśu* is called so from being fit for praise". Or —

> शिशीतेर्वा स्याद्धानकर्मणः । चिरलब्धो गर्भो भवति ।

> *śiśītervā syāddhānakarmaṇaḥ | ciralabdho garbho bhavati |*

(Ni. 10-[?].) Because of the form of a woman's being the abode of a long-obtained child, it is called *śiśu*; thus this word's derivation is shown.

> अन्यान्या वत्सम्[?] उपधापयेते तयोरेकैता वत्सा । अग्निश्चादित्यश्च । रात्रेर्वत्सः । श्वेत आदित्यः । अहोऽग्निः ।

> *anyānyā vatsam[?] upadhāpayete tayorekaitā vatsā | agniścādityaśca | rātrervatsaḥ | śveta ādityaḥ | aho 'gniḥ |*

(Tai. Ā. [?].) In such statements too this child-nature is praised.

In the second sense, *śocayitā vā śatrūṇām*, Agni consumes his foes entirely; hence this name.

> न तस्य मायया चन रिपुरीशीत मर्त्यः । यो अग्नये ददाश हव्यदातिभिः ॥

> *na tasya māyayā cana ripurīśīta martyaḥ | yo agnaye dadāśa havyadātibhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks, since "no enemy can win against Agni, nor conquer him", and since Agni is described as able to harm all, the second sense is also possible.

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उपस्थायं चरति यत्समारत सद्यो जातस्तत्सार यज्ञेभिः ।
> अभि श्वान्तं मृशते नान्द्ये मुदे यदीं गच्छन्त्युशतीरपिस्थितम् [?] ॥ ४ ॥

> *upasthāyaṃ carati yatsamārata sadyo jātastatsāra yajñebhiḥ |*
> *abhi śvāntaṃ mṛśate nāndye mude yadīṃ gacchantyuśatīrapisthitam [?] ‖ 4 ‖*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *yat* — whenever (the Adhvaryu); *upasthāyam* — (for the arising of Agni) a favourable activity; *carati* — performs; *samārate* — Agni appears (visibly); *sadyaḥ* — at once; *jātaḥ* — being born; *yajñebhiḥ* — joined with the proper powers (or with the means of fruit); *tatsāra* — moved among (the two fire-sticks) and; *yat* — when; *āsisthitam* — pervading (all round); *īm* — this Agni; *uśatīḥ* — the ladles of ghee or hymns that desire (his acceptance); *gacchanti* — approach (him) — then; *śrāntam* — (by the sacrificial acts) wearied, or the sacrificer made cheerful; *nāndye* — in the pleasing rite; *mude* — for the joy (of the sacrificer); *abhimṛśate* — he becomes joined, touched.

**Bhāvārtha (begins).** As soon as the Adhvaryu performs the act helpful to the arising of Agni, Agni appears. And at once, born, he moves about with his rays joined —

---

### Printed p. 373  (PDF 391)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 23 [?].)*

*(Bhāvārtha continued.)* — and as soon as the ladles of ghee, desiring him, reach the all-pervading Agni, he, for the joy of the sacrificer wearied by the sacrificial acts, is joined to the pleasing rite and becomes satisfying. (Reading of the last words, "*vṛddhi yāgutrāni*" [?], unclear.)

**English Translation (as printed).** When (the priest) proceeds to effect his development, he is (at once) manifested ; and as soon as engendered, is associated with his objects : he provides for the gratification ( of his worshipper ), placidly engaged in the agreeable (rite), when the (oblations) that desire (his acceptance) reach him present (at the sacrifice).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***upasthāyam*** — *upasthānam asti iti*; *utpattyanukūlavyāpāram*: "an activity favourable to the origin"; at the sacrificial altar the Adhvaryu performs, sitting, the activity favourable to the birth of Agni.

***samārate*** — *samāgacchate*, *mathanenāvirbhavat*: "comes together; appears by the churning"; the verb *ṛ* with the prefix *sam* gives this word. Thus:

> इन्द्रेषिते प्रसवं भिक्षमाणे अच्छा समुद्रं रथ्येव याथः । समारणे ऊर्मिभिः पिन्वमाने अन्या वामन्यामप्येति शुभ्रे ॥

> *indreṣite prasavaṃ bhikṣamāṇe acchā samudraṃ rathyeva yāthaḥ | samāraṇe ūrmibhiḥ pinvamāne anyā vāmanyāmapyeti śubhre ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].) here too the prefix *sam* with the root *ṛ* has the sense "come together"; thus "appear before (the sacrificer)" is the sense. In the Ṛk at hand: "appeared on the churning of the fire-sticks"; the origin of Agni from the *araṇi*s, is the point.

***yujyebhiḥ*** — *yoktuṃ sambandhuṃ samarthaiḥ phalaiḥ, mitrayutair [?] ... tejobhir vā*: "with the powers fit to be joined, or with the fruits; or with the brilliances". (*as being joined with abilities, that may be associated with their objects, or with energies fit to be connected with their consequences, or with his horses joined to his Car. Tr. Wilson*)

***tatsāra*** — from a root meaning "to go": it is derived from *sṛ*-root; "moved about" (*sañcacāra*, "moved"). Or *yajyebhir aśvair jātamātra iva sarvatra sañcacāra*: "as if, just born, he went about everywhere with his horses [?]" — he moved about with his chariot-horses, is the sense.

***āsisthitam*** — *vyāpya vartamānam*: "being present, pervading"; "Agni who pervades all places".

---

### Printed p. 374  (PDF 392)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 145".)*

*(Ṛk 4, Special Topics continued.)* ***śrāntam*** — *śrāntaṃ śāntaṃ vā yajamānam*: "the sacrificer, wearied by sacrificial acts or, being engaged in performing the rite, made tranquil", i.e. "one whose mind is pleased"; the word *śrānta* may also mean "pleased" (*prasanna*).

> अधा गाव उपमातिं कनायाः अनु श्वान्तस्य कस्य चित्परेयुः । श्रुधि त्वं सुद्रविणो नस्त्वं [?] याळाश्वस्य [?] ... सूनृताभिः ॥

> *adhā gāva upamātiṃ kanāyāḥ anu śvāntasya kasya citpareyuḥ | śrudhi tvaṃ sudraviṇo nastvaṃ [?] yāḷāśvasya [?] ... sūnṛtābhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, *śrāntasya* is explained in two senses, *pravṛddhasya śrāntasya vā*; likewise it may be said in the present Ṛk.

***uśatīḥ*** — *kāmayamānā ājyadhārāḥ stutayo vā*: "ghee-streams or hymns desiring to reach Agni".

***nāndye*** — *nandanīye karmaṇi*: "in a pleasing rite", "in the rite that gives joy"; since the rite gives joy to the body and, even though it troubles, to the mind as well, it is so said in this Ṛk, as in:

> त्रिर्वर्तिर्यातं त्रिरनुव्रते जने त्रिः सुप्राव्ये त्रेधेव शिक्षतम् । त्रिर्नान्द्यं वहतमश्विना युवं त्रिः पृक्षो अस्मे अक्षरेव पिन्वतम् ॥

> *trirvartiryātaṃ triranuvrate jane triḥ suprāvye tredheva śikṣatam | trirnāndyaṃ vahatamaśvinā yuvaṃ triḥ pṛkṣo asme akṣareva pinvatam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-34-[?].) Here too *nāndya* means *nandanīya, santoṣakara* "joy-giving"; the sacrifice, giving fruit for the sake of well-being, is meant.

***abhimṛśate*** — *abhimarśanaṃ karoti*: "touches". As in the world a teacher or father touches a wearied pupil or son with love, so Agni touches the wearied sacrificer in the joyous rite, with regard.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar page, noted briefly).** *upasthāyam* (*upasthāya* → *upasthāyam*; root *ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*; *abhyāśe* [?] ... *ṇamul* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-[?]); *āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-33) *yuk* for the root; in *ṇamul* the *m* [?] is a marker; *liti* …; *prādisamāsa*: *kṛdutarapada-prakṛtisvara*)

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स ईं मृगो अप्यो वनर्गुरुप त्वच्युपमस्यां नि धायि ।
> व्यब्रवीद्वयुना मर्त्येभ्योऽग्निर्विद्वाँ ऋतचिद्धि सत्यः ॥ ५ ॥

> *sa īṃ mṛgo apyo vanargurupa tvacyupamasyāṃ ni dhāyi |*
> *vyabravīdvayunā martyebhyo 'gnirvidvā~ ṛtaciddhi satyaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । ईम् । मृगः । अप्यः । वनर्गुः । उप । त्वचि । उपमस्याम् । नि । धायि ।
> वि । अब्रवीत् । वयुना । मर्त्येभ्यः । अग्निः । विद्वान् । ऋतऽचित् । हि । सत्यः ॥ ५ ॥

> *saḥ | īm | mṛgaḥ | apyaḥ | vanarguḥ | upa | tvaci | upamasyām | ni | dhāyi |*
> *vi | abravīt | vayunā | martyebhyaḥ | agniḥ | vidvān | ṛta 'cit | hi | satyaḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: Agni, the seeker, accessible, forest-dweller, is placed on the skin-like altar-surface; the knowing, truthful one declares to mortals their sacrificial duties.)*

> स ईं स एव अग्निः ... उपमस्यां [?] ... त्वचि उपमाने [?] निधायि निहितः । मृगः मार्जनीयः [?] ... अप्यः आपः कर्म तत्र साधुः [?] वनर्गुः वननामानि [?] ... व्यब्रवीत् विशेषेण ब्रवीति उपदिशति । वयुनमिति प्रज्ञानाम [?] ... ऋतचित् यज्ञस्य उदकस्य वा चेतिता ज्ञाता सत्यः सत् क्रियमाणं कर्म तत्र साधुः [?] ... सम्यक्फलप्रद इत्यर्थः । यस्मादयमुक्तसामर्थ्योपेतस्तस्मात्तेन [?] ज्ञानोपदेशो युक्तः । हिशब्दः प्रसिद्धौ ॥ *[small type; largely doubtful]*

> *sa īṃ sa eva agniḥ ... upamasyāṃ [?] ... tvaci upamāne [?] nidhāyi nihitaḥ | mṛgaḥ mārjanīyaḥ [?] ... apyaḥ āpaḥ karma tatra sādhuḥ [?] vanarguḥ vananāmāni [?] ... vyabravīt viśeṣeṇa bravīti upadiśati | vayunamiti prajñānāma [?] ... ṛtacit yajñasya udakasya vā cetitā jñātā satyaḥ sat kriyamāṇaṃ karma tatra sādhuḥ [?] ... samyakphalaprada ityarthaḥ | yasmādayamuktasāmarthyopetastasmāttena [?] jñānopadeśo yuktaḥ | hiśabdaḥ prasiddhau ‖ *[small type; largely doubtful]**

### Printed p. 377  (PDF 395)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 24 [?].)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *mṛgaḥ* — expert in seeking; *apyaḥ* — (being easily reached) one to be approached, or the one skilled (*śrīmanta* [?]) in the rite; *vanargu* — roaming in the woods; *saḥ īm* — that very Agni; *upamasyām* — like (in the form of) the skin that is in the similitude; *tvaci* — on the skin; *upa nidhāyi* — has been placed on the altar; *vidvān* — omniscient; *ṛtacit* — who knows the sacrifice, or who is understood by the sacrificer; *satyaḥ* — of truthful nature, or who is in the company of the good, or whose fruit is worthy; *agniḥ hi* — that very Agni; *martyebhyaḥ* — to the human sacrificers; *vayunā* — the (sacrificial) duties, knowledge of what is to be done; *vyabravīt* — has declared in a special way.

**Bhāvārtha.** Agni, skilled in seeking, easily reached, roaming in the woods, is placed on the altar like one lying on a skin. The omniscient, truthful Agni who knows the fitness of the sacrifice has taught the human sacrificers the knowledge of what is to be done.

**English Translation (as printed).** He, the searcher, the accessible, the dweller in woods, has been placed (amidst the fuel), as in the simlitude [sic] of (an enveloping) skin: the wise Agni, the appreciater of sacrifice, the veracious, has declared to mortals (the knowledge of) their religious duties.

*(The running heading of this English block on the printed page reads "English Trnalation" [sic].)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***mṛgaḥ*** — *mṛgo mārṣṭer gatikarmaṇaḥ* (Ni. [?]): "*mṛga* from the root *mṛj*, in the sense of going"; derived from the root *mṛj* of the sense "go", it means "one who goes always swiftly (*nityaṃ hṛṣṭaḥ* [?] *gacchati*)" — so it gives the sense of "constantly moving". Or *anveṣaṇaśīlo vā*: "one in the habit of seeking"; Sāyaṇa explains that, his own food being the trees and the like, he is skilled in seeking them, so. Therefore,

***vanargu*** — *vanagāmī*: "going in the woods".

> जामिः सिन्धूनां भ्रातेव स्वस्रामिभ्यान्नराजा [?] वनान्यत्ति । यद्वातजूतो वना व्यस्थादग्निर्ह दाति रोमा [?] पृथिव्याः ॥

> *jāmiḥ sindhūnāṃ bhrāteva svasrāmibhyānnarājā [?] vanānyatti | yadvātajūto vanā vyasthādagnirha dāti romā [?] pṛthivyāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) As in such Ṛks, it is described as moving in the woods and eating them; so these two adjectives show the nature of Agni. The Nirukta author:

---

### Printed p. 378  (PDF 396)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 145".)*

> क्नूथेव [?] कस्कर्रा [?] वनर्गू रशनाभिर्दशभिरभ्यध्वीतम् । इयं ते अग्ने नव्यसी मनीषा युक्ष्वा रथं न शुचयद्भिरङ्गैः ॥

> *knūtheva [?] kaskarrā [?] vanargū raśanābhirdaśabhirabhyadhvītam | iyaṃ te agne navyasī manīṣā yukṣvā rathaṃ na śucayadbhiraṅgaiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) Citing this Ṛk, he explains *vanargu* as *vanagāminau* (the two arms of the churner, *agnimanthanau bāhū*), the word being used for the two hands at the time of praising Agni (Ni. [?]).

***sa īm*** — *sa evāgnirūpam*, "that very Agni-form" is the determined sense; the word *īm* has no separate meaning. The Nirukta author:

> अथ ये प्रवृत्तेऽर्थेऽमिताक्षरेषु ग्रन्थेषु वाक्यपूरणा आगच्छन्ति पूरणास्ते मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमीमिद्धीति [?] ।

> *atha ye pravṛtte 'rthe 'mitākṣareṣu grantheṣu vākyapūraṇā āgacchanti pūraṇāste mitākṣareṣvanarthakāḥ kamīmiddhīti [?] |*

(Ni. 1-[?].) This Nirukta passage is thus: "In the case of words that come in a set sense in works of unmeasured syllables, such as the Brāhmaṇas, *īm* and the like are to be seen as filling out the sentence; and in verses of measured metre and syllables, they fill out the pāda: *kam īm* (*kam īm iddhi*) and the like." That is: words such as *īm* are used merely to fill out a sentence in prose of no fixed metre or syllable-count — the Brāhmaṇa and similar sentences — and to fill out the pāda in Ṛks of fixed metre and syllables.

***ṛtacit*** — *yajñasya udakasya vā cetitā jñātā*: "one who knows the sacrifice, or the water".

***vayunā*** — *vayunam iti prajñānāma*: "*vayuna* is a name of understanding"; the special meanings of the word have been given before with examples.

***agnir hi vayunā vyabravīt*** — "Agni taught the knowledge of duties."

> अथास्य हस्तं गृह्णाति । इन्द्रस्य ब्रह्मचार्यस्यग्निराचार्यस्तवाहमाचार्यस्तवासाविति [?] ।

> *athāsya hastaṃ gṛhṇāti | indrasya brahmacāryasyagnirācāryastavāhamācāryastavāsāviti [?] |*

(Śa. Brā. 11-[?]-[?].) From such sentences Agni is praised as a teacher; as it is said that all duties were taught by him, here too that matter is stated.

## Sūkta 146

### Printed p. 380 (continued; PDF 398)

*(The Kannada heading reads "The 146th Sūkta".)*

*(Anukramaṇī, Sanskrit; not rendered in English. Gist: the sūkta of five Ṛks beginning "Trimūrdhānam" is the sixth sūkta, of Dīrghatamas, Agni deity, in Triṣṭubh; its use at the Prātaranuvāka and Āśvina-śastra is told by the Āśvalāyana sūtra *abhyetasyā* — "*trimūrdhānam iti tisraḥ*".)*

> त्रिमूर्धानमिति पञ्चर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं दैर्घतमसम् । आग्नेयम् । पूर्वत्राग्नेयं तु तदित्येकपत्नित्वात् [?] । त्रिमूर्धानमित्यनुक्रमणिका । प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोस्त्रिष्टुब्भे छन्दसीदमादिसूक्तत्रयस्य विनियोगः । अथैतस्या इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । त्रिमूर्धानमिति तिस्र इति ॥ अ. ४-[?] इति ॥

> *trimūrdhānamiti pañcarcaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ sūktaṃ dairghatamasam | āgneyam | pūrvatrāgneyaṃ tu tadityekapatnitvāt [?] | trimūrdhānamityanukramaṇikā | prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayostriṣṭubbhe chandasīdamādisūktatrayasya viniyogaḥ | athaitasyā iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | trimūrdhānamiti tisra iti ‖ a. 4-[?] iti ‖*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta *trimūrdhānam* is the sixth sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Dīrghatamas Aucathya. As said before, the deity of this sūkta too is Agni. In the Anukramaṇī it begins with *trimūrdhānam*. For the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra mantra recitals the Ṛks in the Triṣṭubh metre are used; the use of these three sūktas together is described in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section beginning *athaitasyā*, by the sūtra *trimūrdhānam iti tisraḥ* (Aś. [?]).

---

**॥ ओम् ॥**

**Sūkta 146** — Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 21, Sūkta 146; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 24 [?]. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Ṛṣi: Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Devatā: Agni. Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्रिमूर्धानं सप्तरश्मिं गृणीषेऽनूनमग्निं पित्रोरुपस्थे ।
> निषत्तमस्य चरतो ध्रुवस्य विश्वा दिवो रोचनापप्रिवांसम् ॥ १ ॥

> *trimūrdhānaṃ saptaraśmiṃ gṛṇīṣe 'nūnamagniṃ pitrorupasthe |*
> *niṣattamasya carato dhruvasya viśvā divo rocanāpaprivāṃsam ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्रिऽमूर्धानम् । सप्तऽरश्मिम् । गृणीषे । अनूनम् । अग्निम् । पित्रोः । उपऽस्थे ।
> निऽसत्तम् । अस्य । चरतः । ध्रुवस्य । विश्वा । दिवः । रोचना । आऽपप्रिवांसम् ॥ १ ॥

> *tri 'mūrdhānam | sapta 'raśmim | gṛṇīṣe | anūnam | agnim | pitroḥ | upa 'sthe |*
> *ni 'sattam | asya | carataḥ | dhruvasya | viśvā | divaḥ | rocanā | ā 'paprivāṃsam ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: Agni, three-headed as the three savanas, seven-rayed as the seven metres, perfect, seated between heaven and earth, filling all the shining realms and all desires of the moving and the fixed — praise him.)*

> अनेनाग्निर्यज्ञरूपेण स्तूयते । त्रिमूर्धानं सवनत्रयरूपमूर्धत्रयोपेतम् ॥ [...] बहुव्रीहौ [?] पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । किञ्च सप्तरश्मिं नियामकसप्तच्छन्दोयुक्तं अनूनमविकलफलं सम्पूर्णफलम् अग्निमङ्गनादिगुणयुक्तं [?] वा पित्रोरुपस्थे द्यावापृथिव्योरुत्सङ्गे निषत्तं निषण्णं मध्ये वर्तमानमित्यर्थः । भूमिर्द्यौर्देवताभिश्च [?] साध्यत्वादिति [?] । किञ्च ध्रुवस्य निश्चलस्य चरतो हविःप्रक्षेपणादिना [?] ... अस्याग्नेः सम्बन्धिनं यज्ञं दिवो द्युलोकस्य विश्वा रोचनानि देवविमानान्याप्रिवांसं सर्वतः पूरयन्तं कामानाम् उक्तलक्षणविशिष्टमग्निं गृणीषे स्तुहि । किञ्च चरतः सर्वतो ज्वलनाभिर्गच्छतो ध्रुवस्य धृतत्वादचलितस्य दिवो द्योतमानस्याग्नेर्विश्वा रोचनानि तेजांसि सर्वत्र व्याप्नुवन्तीति शेषः । ... उद्यमतमग्निं स्तुहीत्यन्तरगतः प्रैषः ॥ *[small type; many words doubtful, several pieces left out]*

> *anenāgniryajñarūpeṇa stūyate | trimūrdhānaṃ savanatrayarūpamūrdhatrayopetam ‖ [...] bahuvrīhau [?] pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | kiñca saptaraśmiṃ niyāmakasaptacchandoyuktaṃ anūnamavikalaphalaṃ sampūrṇaphalam agnimaṅganādiguṇayuktaṃ [?] vā pitrorupasthe dyāvāpṛthivyorutsaṅge niṣattaṃ niṣaṇṇaṃ madhye vartamānamityarthaḥ | bhūmirdyaurdevatābhiśca [?] sādhyatvāditi [?] | kiñca dhruvasya niścalasya carato haviḥprakṣepaṇādinā [?] ... asyāgneḥ sambandhinaṃ yajñaṃ divo dyulokasya viśvā rocanāni devavimānānyāprivāṃsaṃ sarvataḥ pūrayantaṃ kāmānām uktalakṣaṇaviśiṣṭamagniṃ gṛṇīṣe stuhi | kiñca carataḥ sarvato jvalanābhirgacchato dhruvasya dhṛtatvādacalitasya divo dyotamānasyāgnerviśvā rocanāni tejāṃsi sarvatra vyāpnuvantīti śeṣaḥ | ... udyamatamagniṃ stuhītyantaragataḥ praiṣaḥ ‖ *[small type; many words doubtful, several pieces left out]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada, p. 381 end).** *trimūrdhānam* — having three heads in the form of the three savanas; (or) pervading the three worlds, earth, atmosphere and heaven; (or) having the three places, the Dakṣiṇāgni, Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya [continues on p. 382]

### Printed p. 382  (PDF 400)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 146".)*

*(Pratipadārtha continued.)* … the three places; *saptaraśmim* — having seven metres, or having seven flames; *anūnam* — without deficiency; *pitroḥ* — on the lap (in the middle) of heaven and earth; *niṣattam* — seated, (pervading); *āpapriāṃsam* — fulfilling (the desired aims); *agnim* — Agni; *gṛṇīṣe* — praise (him) in hymns; *carataḥ* — of him who moves (or who by his flames goes about all regions); *dhruvasya* — of him who is immovable; *divaḥ* — shining; *asya* — of this Agni; *viśvā rocanā* — all lights (spread everywhere).

**Bhāvārtha.** Praise, O priest, this Agni, who has three heads in the form of the three savanas, who is of the nature of the seven metres, free from deficiency, pervading the middle of heaven and earth, and fulfilling the desired aims. All the lights of this Agni, who moves everywhere by his flames, immovable and shining, spread everywhere.

**English Translation (as printed).** Glorify the three-headed, seven-rayed Agni; who is subject to no diminution, seated on the lap of his parents, (heaven and earth); and gratifying all (desires); as the universal radiance of the divine (Agni), whether moving or stationary, (spreads around).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***trimūrdhānam*** — *anenāgniryajñarūpeṇa stūyate*. This adjective and the adjective *saptaraśmim* are explained first in the sense of the sacrifice and afterwards in the sense of Agni himself. *trimūrdhānam* — *savanatrayarūpamūrdhatrayopetam*, "having three heads in the form of the three savanas"; or [?] *trimūrdhānaṃ lokatrayavyāptam*, "pervading the three worlds"; or *gārhapatyādisthānatrayopetam*, "having the three places beginning with the Gārhapatya". Thus the meaning is given in three ways: one who has three heads in the form of the three savanas; or one who pervades the three worlds, earth, atmosphere and heaven; or one who has the three places, Dakṣiṇāgni, Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya. Oldenberg, the German scholar, when translating this Ṛk into English and writing his notes, refers to these three meanings of Sāyaṇa and says:

Sayana refers the three heads of Agni to the three Savanas, or the three worlds, or the three sacrificial fires. The last explanation seems to be most probable.

"Of these three meanings, the third —  *he who has the three places Dakṣiṇāgni, Gārhapatya, Āhavanīya* —" [the Kannada continues on the next page].

---

### Printed p. 383  (PDF 401)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 24 [?].)*

*(Special Topics continued.)* "— the meaning is the more agreeable. Yet it is not possible to say that the first meanings are not agreeable (*samañjasa*)."

> दिवस्परि प्रथमं जज्ञे अग्निरस्मद्द्वितीयं परि जातवेदाः । तृतीयमप्सु नृमणा अजस्रमिन्धान एनं जरते स्वाधीः ॥

> *divaspari prathamaṃ jajñe agnirasmaddvitīyaṃ pari jātavedāḥ | tṛtīyamapsu nṛmaṇā ajasramindhāna enaṃ jarate svādhīḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk the origin of Agni in the heaven-world, the earth-world and the atmosphere, in order, is stated; and the Brāhmaṇa explains the same:

> दिवस्परि प्रथमं जज्ञे अग्निरिति । प्राणो वै दिवः प्राणाद्ध्येष प्रथमम[...] जायते [?] द्वितीयं परि जातवेदा इति यदेनमुदरो [?] द्वितीयं पुरुषा [...] तृतीयमप्सु नृमणा अजस्रमिति प्रजापतिर्वै नृमणा अग्निरजस्र इन्धान एनं जरते स्वाधीः ॥ [?]

> *divaspari prathamaṃ jajñe agniriti | prāṇo vai divaḥ prāṇāddhyeṣa prathamama[...] jāyate [?] dvitīyaṃ pari jātavedā iti yadenamudaro [?] dvitīyaṃ puruṣā [...] tṛtīyamapsu nṛmaṇā ajasramiti prajāpatirvai nṛmaṇā agnirajasra indhāna enaṃ jarate svādhīḥ ‖ [?]*

(Tai. Brā. 2-[?]-[?].) From these sentences it is explained that the three-fold origin said in the Ṛk is meant, and that, being *vyāpti* ("pervasion"), it refers to the three worlds; or in other Śruti passages too, the two meanings are possible.

***saptaraśmim*** — *niyāmakasaptachandoyuktam athavā saptajvālam*: "yoked with the seven metres that regulate, or having seven flames"; here too two meanings are told. Oldenberg here also gives his view:

*(English, as printed:)* The seven reins (rays) are, according to Sayana, the seven metres or the seven flames of Agni. The last explanation is recommended by III-6-2. But it is possible also to think of the seven Priests.

***sapta hotāraḥ*** [*saptahotā*] — of the two meanings given by Sāyaṇa, the second is the more probable; supporting this:

> आ रोदसी अप्र[...]ना जायमान उत प्र रिक्था अध नु प्रयज्यो । दिवश्चिदग्ने महिना पृथिव्या वच्यन्तां ते वह्नयः सप्तजिह्वाः ॥

> *ā rodasī apra[...]nā jāyamāna uta pra rikthā adha nu prayajyo | divaścidagne mahinā pṛthivyā vacyantāṃ te vahnayaḥ saptajihvāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-6-[?].) In this Ṛk too Agni is praised as having seven tongues. And here:

> आ यस्मिन्त्सप्त रश्मयस्तता यज्ञस्य नेतरि । मनुष्वद्दैव्यमष्टमं पोता विश्वं तदिन्वति [?] ॥

> *ā yasmintsapta raśmayastatā yajñasya netari | manuṣvaddaivyamaṣṭamaṃ potā viśvaṃ tadinvati [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) in this Ṛk, with the sense *saptaraśmivad vyāptā hotṛkāḥ svasvakarmabhiḥ*, "the Hotṛs, spread out like seven reins, each by his own acts, all around"; and since they are said to be always intent on their respective duties, here *sapta hotṛkaḥ* is the meaning.

### Printed p. 384  (PDF 402)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 146".)*

> सप्त ते अग्ने समिधः सप्त जिह्वाः सप्त ऋषयः सप्त धाम प्रियाणि । सप्त होत्राः सप्तधा त्वा यजन्ति सप्त योनीरा पृणस्वा घृतेन ॥

> *sapta te agne samidhaḥ sapta jihvāḥ sapta ṛṣayaḥ sapta dhāma priyāṇi | sapta hotrāḥ saptadhā tvā yajanti sapta yonīrā pṛṇasvā ghṛtena ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In this Taittirīya-saṃhitā sentence too this matter is specially praised. Likewise:

> काली कराली च मनोजवा च सुलोहिता या च सुधूम्रवर्णा । स्फुलिङ्गिनी विश्वरुची च देवी लेलायमाना इति सप्त जिह्वाः ॥

> *kālī karālī ca manojavā ca sulohitā yā ca sudhūmravarṇā | sphuliṅginī viśvarucī ca devī lelāyamānā iti sapta jihvāḥ ‖*

(Muṇḍaka 1-2-4.) In the Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad the names of Agni's seven tongues are described.

> पायूपस्थेऽपानं चक्षुःश्रोत्रे मुखनासिकाभ्यां प्राणः स्वयं प्रातिष्ठते मध्ये तु समानः । एष ह्येतद्भुतमन्नं समं नयति तस्मादेताः सप्तार्चिषो भवन्ति ॥

> *pāyūpasthe 'pānaṃ cakṣuḥśrotre mukhanāsikābhyāṃ prāṇaḥ svayaṃ prātiṣṭhate madhye tu samānaḥ | eṣa hyetadbhutamannaṃ samaṃ nayati tasmādetāḥ saptārciṣo bhavanti ‖*

(Praśna 3-[?].) In the Praśna Upaniṣad too the powers of the seven-formed Agni's flames — the (seven) organs — are described.

***pitroḥ*** — *dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ*: "of heaven and earth".

> स रोचयज्जनुषा रोदसी उभे स मात्रोरभवत्पुत्र ईड्यः । हव्यवाळग्निरजरश्चनोहितो दूळभो विशामतिथिर्विभावसुः ॥

> *sa rocayajjanuṣā rodasī ubhe sa mātrorabhavatputra īḍyaḥ | havyavāḷagnirajaraścanohito dūḷabho viśāmatithirvibhāvasuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-2-[?].) In this Ṛk,

> अग्ने दिवः सूनुरसि प्रचेतास्तना पृथिव्या उत विश्ववेदाः । ऋधग्देवाँ इह यजा चिकित्वः ॥

> *agne divaḥ sūnurasi pracetāstanā pṛthivyā uta viśvavedāḥ | ṛdhagdevā~ iha yajā cikitvaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].) and in Ṛks such as 10-1-2, 10-2-2, 10-1-5 [?] and many others, because Agni is said to be born of heaven and earth, *pitroḥ* is "of heaven and earth, the parents". "The two fire-sticks" is another sense that is also possible.

***ā papriavāṃsam*** — *sarvataḥ pūrayantaṃ kāmānām*: "fulfilling the desires on all sides"; at all times and in all rites fulfilling the desired objects; the root *pyā*, in the sense "to protect, to fill", gives the word *papriḥ* — "filling"; the sense is "one who fills".

> न सिक्ष्णा [?] एष दिवो मध्य आस्ते आपप्रिवान् रोदसी अन्तरिक्षम् । स विश्वाचीरभि चष्टे घृताचीरन्तरा पूर्वमपरं च केतुम् ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, as *āpaprivān svatejasā pūrayan* ("filling with his own splendour"), here *kāmānāṃ pūritāram*, "the filler of desires", is the sense.

***carataḥ dhruvasya*** — by these adjectives, qualities opposed to each other are described: both moving, in the form of flames, and unmoving, in the root-form, as unchanging, are praised.

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उक्षा महाँ अभि ववक्ष एने अजरस्तस्थावितऊतिर्ऋष्वः ।
> उर्व्याः पदो नि दधाति सानौ रिहन्त्यूधो अरुषासो अस्य ॥ २ ॥

> *ukṣā mahā~ abhi vavakṣa ene ajarastasthāvitaūtirṛṣvaḥ |*
> *urvyāḥ pado ni dadhāti sānau rihantyūdho aruṣāso asya ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उक्षा । महान् । अभि । ववक्षे । एने इति । अजरः । तस्थौ । अवितऽऊतिः । ऋष्वः ।
> उर्व्याः । पदः । नि । दधाति । सानौ । रिहन्ति । ऊधः । अरुषासः । अस्य ॥ २ ॥

> *ukṣā | mahān | abhi | vavakṣe | ene iti | ajaraḥ | tasthau | avita 'ūtiḥ | ṛṣvaḥ |*
> *urvyāḥ | padaḥ | ni | dadhāti | sānau | rihanti | ūdhaḥ | aruṣāsaḥ | asya ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: the showerer, great, bears heaven and earth, ageless, unfailing in protection; he sets his feet on the summit of the broad earth and the red ones lick the udder.)*

> उक्षा सेक्ता फलप्रदानसमर्थ इत्यर्थः । अत एव महान् महिम्ना स्वरूपेण [?] ... द्यावापृथिव्यावभि ववक्षे वहति [?] वहतेर्लिट् छान्दसं शपः श्लुः [?] ... सिब्बहुलमिति सिच् [?] ... वृष्ट्यादिप्रदानेन हविर्हवनेन च लोकद्वयस्य वासिनो देवान्मनुष्यांश्च रक्षतीत्यर्थः । किञ्चायमजरो जराहितः ऋष्वो महान् पूज्यः । महन्नामैतत् ऋष्व उक्ष इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तथैतेऽपि प्राप्तरक्षणः [?] ... तस्थौ स्थितो वर्तते । यद्वा । उक्षन्नोऽयमितऊतिरत इव गमनवान् [?] ... *[small type; largely illegible]*

> *ukṣā sektā phalapradānasamartha ityarthaḥ | ata eva mahān mahimnā svarūpeṇa [?] ... dyāvāpṛthivyāvabhi vavakṣe vahati [?] vahaterliṭ chāndasaṃ śapaḥ śluḥ [?] ... sibbahulamiti sic [?] ... vṛṣṭyādipradānena havirhavanena ca lokadvayasya vāsino devānmanuṣyāṃśca rakṣatītyarthaḥ | kiñcāyamajaro jarāhitaḥ ṛṣvo mahān pūjyaḥ | mahannāmaitat ṛṣva ukṣa iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt | tathaite 'pi prāptarakṣaṇaḥ [?] ... tasthau sthito vartate | yadvā | ukṣanno 'yamitaūtirata iva gamanavān [?] ... *[small type; largely illegible]**

> सानौ समुच्छ्रिते प्रदेशे वेदिलक्षणे सदो नि दधाति पदानि स्थापयति करोति [?] । किंच [?] ... अरुषासः आरोचमानाः [?] ... ऊधः उद्धृतोदकप्रदानस्थानीयम् [?] अन्तरिक्षं रिहन्ति लिहन्ति ... यद्वा । अस्याग्नेः ... अरुषा आरोचना ब्रह्मवर्चसेन यजमानाः रिहन्ति । अभिमतैः स्वर्गादीनि लिहन्ति ॥ *[several words doubtful]*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *ukṣā* — the showerer (of desired aims); *mahān* — Agni, endowed with greatness; *ene* — both heaven and earth; *abhi vavakṣe* — has pervaded; *ajaraḥ* — the ageless; *ṛṣvaḥ* — the adorable Agni; *itaūtiḥ* — joined with protections (or) coming hither to the sacrificial place; *tasthau* — stands; *urvyāḥ* — of the broad earth; *sānau* — on the lofty altar-place like a summit; *padaḥ* — feet; *ni dadhāti* — places; *asya* — of this Agni; *aruṣāsaḥ* — the shining lights; *ūdhaḥ* — the atmosphere that is like an udder; *rihanti* — touch (pervade); (or) *asya* — of this Agni; *ūdhaḥ* — the sacrifice that is like an udder; *aruṣāsaḥ* — the sacrificers shining with their splendour; *rihanti* — touch (heaven and the rest).

**Bhāvārtha.** Agni, the showerer of desired aims, endowed with greatness, has pervaded heaven and earth. The ageless, adorable Agni stands with his protections, and places his feet on the lofty altar-ground, which is like the summit of the broad earth; and the bright lights of this Agni pervade the atmosphere, which is like an udder.

**English Translation (as printed).** The great showerer (of benefits) has pervaded these two (worlds); undecaying and adorable, he is (ever) present, bestowing protection: he places his foot on the summit of the earth, and his radiant ( flames ) lick the udder (of the firmament).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***ukṣā*** — *sekta, phalapradātā ity arthaḥ*: "the sprinkler, the giver of fruit"; one who pours out the desired aims. *sec*, "to sprinkle", gives the sense of "sprinkling"; the word is derived from the root *ukṣ*, "to sprinkle"; the sense is the divinity that showers desired aims. The Nirukta author has listed *ukṣan* among the names of the great (Ni. 3-[?]), and:

---

### Printed p. 388  (PDF 406)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 146".)*

> वृषाकपायि रेवति सुपुत्र आदु सुस्नुषे । घसत्त इन्द्र उक्षणः प्रियं काचित्करं हविर्विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ॥

> *vṛṣākapāyi revati suputra ādu susnuṣe | ghasatta indra ukṣaṇaḥ priyaṃ kācitkaraṃ havirviśvasmādindra uttaraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-86-[?].) Citing this Ṛk, in explaining the word *ukṣaṇaḥ* occurring in it he says: *ukṣāṇa ukṣaṇaḥ, ukṣater vṛddhikarmaṇaḥ* ("*ukṣan* from the root *ukṣ*, of the sense of growth"), (Ni. [?]) — since the root *ukṣ* is of the sense "to increase", with *vṛddhi* [?], the meaning "bulls that sprinkle waters" is given in this context. In general the word *ukṣan* is used in the sense of strength, of capacity also; it has the sense of the power of sprinkling.

> ते जज्ञिरे दिव ऋष्वास उक्षणो रुद्रस्य मर्या असुरा अरेपसः । पावकासः शुचयः सूर्या इव सत्वानो न द्रप्सिनो घोरवर्पसः ॥

> *te jajñire diva ṛṣvāsa ukṣaṇo rudrasya maryā asurā arepasaḥ | pāvakāsaḥ śucayaḥ sūryā iva satvāno na drapsino ghoravarpasaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-[?]-[?].)

> यज्ञस्य केतुं प्रथमं पुरोहितं हविष्मन्त ईळते सप्त वाजिनम् । शृण्वन्तमग्निं घृतपृष्ठमुक्षणं पृणन्तं देवं पृणते सुवीर्यम् ॥

> *yajñasya ketuṃ prathamaṃ purohitaṃ haviṣmanta īḷate sapta vājinam | śṛṇvantamagniṃ ghṛtapṛṣṭhamukṣaṇaṃ pṛṇantaṃ devaṃ pṛṇate suvīryam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks the word *ukṣan* attains the sense of "sprinkling" or "the power of sprinkling". In the Ṛk at hand too, "one who has the power of sprinkling", i.e. who gives desired aims — Agni.

***abhi vavakṣe*** — *abhikramya vyāpya vahati*; *vyāpnotīty arthaḥ*: "having gone over, he bears, pervading"; "he pervades on all sides". The word *vavakṣe* may be derived from the root *vah* or from the root *vac paribhāṣaṇe*, says the Nirukta author:

> किमित्ते विष्णो परिचक्ष्यं भूत्प्र यद्ववक्षे शिपिविष्टो अस्मि । मा वर्पो अस्मदप गूह एतद्यदन्यरूपः समिथे बभूथ ॥

> *kimitte viṣṇo paricakṣyaṃ bhūtpra yadvavakṣe śipiviṣṭo asmi | mā varpo asmadapa gūha etadyadanyarūpaḥ samithe babhūtha ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-100-6.) Citing this, he explains *vavakṣe* here as *pra bravīṣi* ("you declare") — thus showing the root *vac* as the source of this. And:

> सद्यो जातो ओषधीभिर्ववक्षे यदी वर्धन्ति प्रस्वो घृतेन । आप इव प्रवता शुम्भमाना उरुष्यदग्निः पित्रोरुपस्थे ॥

> *sadyo jāto oṣadhībhirvavakṣe yadī vardhanti prasvo ghṛtena | āpa iva pravatā śumbhamānā uruṣyadagniḥ pitrorupasthe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].)

### Printed p. 389  (PDF 407)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 25 [?].)*

In such Ṛks, *vavakṣe* is "is carried (or: made to be borne)": *uhyate*, *vahyate*. 

> ववक्ष इन्द्रो अमितमृजिष्यु ऽ भे आ पप्रौ रोदसी महित्वा । अतश्चिदस्य महिमा वि रेच्यभि यो विश्वा भुवना बभूव ॥

> *vavakṣa indro amitamṛjiṣyu ' bhe ā paprau rodasī mahitvā | ataścidasya mahimā vi recyabhi yo viśvā bhuvanā babhūva ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, it gives the sense "he was borne (pervaded)": *uvāha* — so in the Ṛk in question too, the word is derived from the root *vah*, so that *abhi vavakṣe* means *vyāpnoti*, "pervades on all sides".

***ṛṣvaḥ*** — this word is read among the names of the great (Ni. 3-[?]). It is used in the sense "great" and in the sense "of beautiful form". The Nirukta author:

> उरुं नो लोकमनु नेषि विद्वान्स्वर्वज्ज्योतिरभयं स्वस्ति । ऋष्वा त इन्द्र स्थविरस्य बाहू उप स्थेयाम शरणा बृहन्ता ॥

> *uruṃ no lokamanu neṣi vidvānsvarvajjyotirabhayaṃ svasti | ṛṣvā ta indra sthavirasya bāhū upa stheyāma śaraṇā bṛhantā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-8.) Citing this Ṛk, he explains the word *ṛṣvā* as *darśanīyau*, "beautiful, of delightful form"; and in

> अनानुदो वृषभो दोधतो वधो गम्भीर ऋष्वो असमष्टकाव्यः । रध्रचोदः श्नथनो वीळितस्पृथुरिन्द्रः सुयज्ञ उषसः स्वर्जनत् ॥

> *anānudo vṛṣabho dodhato vadho gambhīra ṛṣvo asamaṣṭakāvyaḥ | radhracodaḥ śnathano vīḷitaspṛthurindraḥ suyajña uṣasaḥ svarjanat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?].) the word *mahān* is an adjective of Indra. In the Ṛk at hand this word is an adjective of Agni. As Agni has both these qualities, either of the two senses may be given for this word.

***urvyāḥ*** — *vistāyāḥ bhūmyāḥ*: "of the broad earth"; the word, as an adjective of the earth or of the atmosphere, shows the nature spread out broadly.

> ऊर्मिर्न पृथ्वी बहुला गभीरा मा वामेतौ [?] ।

> *ūrmirna pṛthvī bahulā gabhīrā mā vāmetau [?] |*

(Ai. Brā. 4-[?].) In such sentences, this word is shown as an adjective of heaven and earth, which spread very broadly.

***rihanty ūdho aruṣāso asya*** — Two kinds of meaning for this sentence have been shown by Sāyaṇa: first, *asya aruṣāsaḥ* — "the shining lights of this Agni *rihanti* (pervade) the atmosphere that is like an udder, *ūdhaḥ*"; second, *asya ūdhaḥ* — "the sacrifice of this Agni that is like an udder; *aruṣāsaḥ*, the sacrificers shining with their splendour, *rihanti*, touch heaven and the rest".

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> समानं वत्समभि संचरन्ती विष्वग्धेनू वि चरतः सुमेके ।
> अनपवृज्याँ अध्वनो मिमाने विश्वान्केताँ अधि महो दधाने ॥ ३ ॥

> *samānaṃ vatsamabhi saṃcarantī viṣvagdhenū vi carataḥ sumeke |*
> *anapavṛjyā~ adhvano mimāne viśvānketā~ adhi maho dadhāne ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> समानम् । वत्सम् । अभि । संचरन्ती इति सम्ऽचरन्ती । विष्वक् । धेनू इति । वि । चरतः ।
> सुमेके इति सुऽमेके ।
> अनपऽवृज्यान् । अध्वनः । मिमाने इति । विश्वान् । केतान् । अधि । महः । दधाने ।
> इति ॥ ३ ॥

> *samānam | vatsam | abhi | saṃcarantī iti sam 'carantī | viṣvak | dhenū iti | vi | carataḥ |*
> *sumeke iti su 'meke |*
> *anapa 'vṛjyān | adhvanaḥ | mimāne iti | viśvān | ketān | adhi | mahaḥ | dadhāne |*
> *iti ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: the two cows, heaven and earth [or the two priests], each moving to the one calf, Agni, feed him and travel in all directions, measuring faultless paths and bearing great wisdom.)*

> समानमेकमेव वत्सं वत्सस्थानीयं पुत्रं [?] ... अग्निं मुखीकृत्य [?] अभिमुखं संचरन्ती संचरन्त्यौ द्वे धेनू अग्निं हितकरेण [?] प्रीणयित्र्यौ पत्नीयजमानलक्षणे धेनू विष्वक् सर्वतः वि चरतः संचरतः । स्वसमानासाधारणेन [?] सम्यग्गच्छता [?] ... इत्यर्थः । कीदृश्यौ ते । सुमेके शोभनमेके शोभनमेकेन वा परिचरना- [?]

> *samānamekameva vatsaṃ vatsasthānīyaṃ putraṃ [?] ... agniṃ mukhīkṛtya [?] abhimukhaṃ saṃcarantī saṃcarantyau dve dhenū agniṃ hitakareṇa [?] prīṇayitryau patnīyajamānalakṣaṇe dhenū viṣvak sarvataḥ vi carataḥ saṃcarataḥ | svasamānāsādhāraṇena [?] samyaggacchatā [?] ... ityarthaḥ | kīdṛśyau te | sumeke śobhanameke śobhanamekena vā paricaranā- [?]*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *sumeke* — skilled in performing the rites; or skilled in the service; (and) *anapavṛjyān* — which have nothing to be avoided (free from faults); *adhvanaḥ* — the paths (of Agni); *mimāne* — those who accomplish; *viśvān ketān* — all the knowledges (that increase Agni); *mahaḥ* — to the great; *adhi dadhāne* — those who hold (in excess); *samānam* — (to both) a common, i.e. one worthy of love; *vatsam* — to the calf, the delight-giving Agni; *abhi saṃcarantī* — going facing (pleasing him); *dhenū* — those who show affection like cows, the sacrificer and his wife, both (or) the Hotṛ and Adhvaryu; *viṣvak* — together; *vi carataḥ* — move (with the equipment needed for the sacrifice).

**Bhāvārtha.** Skilled in service, free from faults, accomplishing the paths of Agni, increasing all the knowledges, endowed in excess with greatness, the two — going facing Agni, the delight-giving, who is, like a calf, the object of love for both, as cows show affection to the calf — the sacrificer and his wife, or the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu, together move about with the equipment needed for the sacrifice.

**English Translation (as printed).** (There are) two well-disposed milch cows together approaching their common progeny, and fully nourishing (him); pointing out the paths that are free from all that is to be avoided, and possessing more than the great intelligence (necessary for his development).

### Printed p. 393  (PDF 411)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 26 [?].)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 3).** ***sumeke*** — *śobhanakarmāṇau śobhanamehane vā, paricaraṇakuśale ity arthaḥ* — "having excellent actions, or excellent … ; skilled in service": Sāyaṇa here explains it thus. In general this word is used in many places in the sense of "firmly established" (*pratiṣṭhāpita*) [?]. Examples:

> अच्छिद्रा शर्म जरितः पुरूणि देवाँ अच्छा दीद्यानः सुमेधाः । रथो न सस्निरभि वक्षि वाजमग्ने त्वं रोदसी नः सुमेके ॥

> *acchidrā śarma jaritaḥ purūṇi devā~ acchā dīdyānaḥ sumedhāḥ | ratho na sasnirabhi vakṣi vājamagne tvaṃ rodasī naḥ sumeke ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks *sumeke* — *śobhanarūpopete svakīyaprabhābhiḥ prakāśayukte*: "endowed with beautiful form, shining with their own lustre"; i.e. "having beautiful form, shining with their own splendour". In the Ṛk at hand, the Hotṛ and Adhvaryu, or the sacrificer and his wife — the two (*dhenū*) — are praised for their excellent acts of service; this adjective probably belongs to them.

***mimāne*** — *sampādayitryau, parisṛtya saṃvādi-takartṛ* [?]: "the two who accomplish; having surrounded".

***viṣvak*** — *sarvataḥ*: "everywhere" or "together"; both meanings are possible.

> तव भ्रमास आशुया पतन्त्यनु स्पृश धृषता शोशुचानः । तपूंष्यग्ने जुह्वा पतङ्गानसंदितो वि सृज विष्वगुल्काः ॥

> *tava bhramāsa āśuyā patantyanu spṛśa dhṛṣatā śośucānaḥ | tapūṃṣyagne juhvā pataṅgānasaṃdito vi sṛja viṣvagulkāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks, everywhere *viṣvak* is given the sense "on all sides". In the Ṛk at hand it is the sense that the Hotṛ and Adhvaryu, together, serve him.

***dhenū*** — *īdṛśyau adhvaryuyajamānarūpe jāyāpatirūpe vā dhenū*: "the two cows, in the form of the Adhvaryu and sacrificer, or of the wife and husband": here Agni is the calf, and to the sacrificer and his wife (or the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu) as cows are likened. As for Agni and them there is such mutual relationship of affection, and as, to the cows, the arrival of the calf gives delight, so the arrival of Agni gives delight to them — such is the purport. This word is used in many places in the sense *prīṇayitryau harṣadāyakau*, "the two who please, the two who give delight":

> महास्त्वधस्थे ध्रुव आ निषत्तोऽन्तर्द्यावा माहिने हर्यमाणः । आस्क्रे सपत्नी अजरे अमृक्ते सबर्दुघे उरुगायस्य धेनू ॥

> *mahāstvadhasthe dhruva ā niṣatto 'ntardyāvā māhine haryamāṇaḥ | āskre sapatnī ajare amṛkte sabardughe urugāyasya dhenū ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].)

### Printed p. 394  (PDF 412)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 146".)*

In this Ṛk, *dhenū* is an adjective of heaven and earth. In the passage where Agni is described as of the form of a calf, the word *dhenū* is explained as *prīṇayitryau*, "the two who please".

> माता च यत्र दुहिता च धेनू सबर्दुघे धापयेते समीची । ऋतस्य ते सदसीळे अन्तर्महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकम् ॥

> *mātā ca yatra duhitā ca dhenū sabardughe dhāpayete samīcī | ṛtasya te sadasīḷe antarmahaddevānāmasuratvamekam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk too, it is an adjective of heaven and earth: *jagataḥ prīṇayitryau jagatsarvasya harṣadāyakau* — "the two who please the world, who give delight to the whole world". By this, in the Ṛk at hand too, the attribute *harṣadāyakatva* is the principal one. The Hotṛ and Adhvaryu — and the sacrificer and his wife — go out to meet and serve Agni, who is in the form of a calf, with affection, is the purport.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar page, noted briefly).** *vatsam* (root *vada vyaktāyāṃ vāci*; *vyatyayo bahulam* [?] (Uṇ. Sū. 3-[?]) *sa* suffix; *khari ca*: *takāra* substituted for the root's *dakāra*; final *udātta* from the suffix accent); *saṃcarantī* (root *cara gatibhakṣaṇayoḥ*; *śatṛ* in the sense of *laṭ*; feminine: *ugitaś ca* *ṅīp*; *śapśyanoḥ nityam* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-81) *num* augment; *lasārvadhātuka* *anudātta*, hence the root accent remains; *prādisamāsa*: *kṛdutarapada-prakṛtisvara*; dual: *supāṃ sulug* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) preceding-vowel lengthening); *viṣvak* (root *añcu gatipūjanayoḥ*; with *viṣu* as the *upapada*, *ṛtvik-dadhṛk…* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-59) *kvin* suffix; *anidītāṃ halaḥ…* (Pā. #### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> धीरासः पदं कवयो नयन्ति नाना हृदा रक्षमाणा अजुर्यम् ।
> सिषासन्तः पर्यपश्यन्त सिन्धुमाविरेभ्यो अभवत्सूर्यो नॄन् ॥ ४ ॥

> *dhīrāsaḥ padaṃ kavayo nayanti nānā hṛdā rakṣamāṇā ajuryam |*
> *siṣāsantaḥ paryapaśyanta sindhumāvirebhyo abhavatsūryo nṝn ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> धीरासः । पदम् । कवयः । नयन्ति । नाना । हृदा । रक्षमाणाः । अजुर्यम् ।
> सिषासन्तः । परि । अपश्यन्त । सिन्धुम् । आविः । एभ्यः । अभवत् । सूर्यः । नॄन् ॥ ४ ॥

> *dhīrāsaḥ | padam | kavayaḥ | nayanti | nānā | hṛdā | rakṣamāṇāḥ | ajuryam |*
> *siṣāsantaḥ | pari | apaśyanta | sindhum | āviḥ | ebhyaḥ | abhavat | sūryaḥ | nṝn ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: the wise priests bring the unageing Agni to the altar, guarding him in many ways in their hearts; wishing to serve, they worship him; as the Sun he becomes manifest to them.)*

> धीरासो धीरा धीमन्तः प्रयोगज्ञा अध्वर्य्वादयोऽजुर्य्यमजर्य्यं नारहितमग्निं पदं स्थानं वेदिलक्षणं नयन्ति । प्रापयन्ति । मथनदेशात् [?] गार्हपत्यादा... अथवा वक्ष्यमाणलक्षणा यजमानादयः पदमस्यदं [?] सर्वकामा... *[the remainder of this bhāṣya runs on to p. 396; small type, largely illegible]*

> *dhīrāso dhīrā dhīmantaḥ prayogajñā adhvaryvādayo 'juryyamajaryyaṃ nārahitamagniṃ padaṃ sthānaṃ vedilakṣaṇaṃ nayanti | prāpayanti | mathanadeśāt [?] gārhapatyādā... athavā vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇā yajamānādayaḥ padamasyadaṃ [?] sarvakāmā... *[the remainder of this bhāṣya runs on to p. 396; small type, largely illegible]**

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 146".)*

*(Ṛk 4 bhāṣya, continued.)*

> ...नामास्पदेनेनं गमयन्ति । कीदृशास्ते । कवयः क्रान्तदर्शिनो मेधाविनः । अनूचानाः वा । ये वा अनूचानास्ते कवयः इति श्रुतेः । किञ्च नाना हृदा बहुप्रकारया बुद्ध्या रक्षमाणा धारयमाणाः । किञ्चैतदूपास्ते सिन्धुं स्यन्दमानम् [?] यज्ञद्वारा फलानि स्रवन्तमग्निं सिषासन्तः सम्भक्तुमिच्छन्तः [?] । सनेतेः [?] सनिः सनिवन्तर्थेत्यादिना विकल्पनादिभावः । जनसनखनामित्यादिना [?] ... पर्यपश्यन्त परितः पश्यन्ति शुश्रूषन्त इत्यर्थः । किञ्च सूर्यः सर्वस्य प्रसवितायाग्निरेभ्य एवं कुर्वद्भ्य एभ्यो नॄन्नेतृभ्य आविरभवत् तेषामनुग्रहेण प्रत्यक्षोऽभवत् । नॄन् नेतॄन् [?] ... अनुग्रहीतुमिति वा योज्यम् ॥ *[small type; many words doubtful]*

> *...nāmāspadenenaṃ gamayanti | kīdṛśāste | kavayaḥ krāntadarśino medhāvinaḥ | anūcānāḥ vā | ye vā anūcānāste kavayaḥ iti śruteḥ | kiñca nānā hṛdā bahuprakārayā buddhyā rakṣamāṇā dhārayamāṇāḥ | kiñcaitadūpāste sindhuṃ syandamānam [?] yajñadvārā phalāni sravantamagniṃ siṣāsantaḥ sambhaktumicchantaḥ [?] | saneteḥ [?] saniḥ sanivantarthetyādinā vikalpanādibhāvaḥ | janasanakhanāmityādinā [?] ... paryapaśyanta paritaḥ paśyanti śuśrūṣanta ityarthaḥ | kiñca sūryaḥ sarvasya prasavitāyāgnirebhya evaṃ kurvadbhya ebhyo nṝnnetṛbhya āvirabhavat teṣāmanugraheṇa pratyakṣo 'bhavat | nṝn netṝn [?] ... anugrahītumiti vā yojyam ‖ *[small type; many words doubtful]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *kavayaḥ* — the wise; *dhīrāsaḥ* — the Adhvaryu and others, skilled in application, or the sacrificers and the rest; *ajuryam* — the imperishable Agni; *hṛdā* — in their hearts; *nānā* — in manifold ways; *rakṣamāṇāḥ* — cherishing; *padam* — to the altar; *nayanti* — bring and place [or *padam* — Agni, the resort of all desired aims; *nayanti* — carry (him)]. (And) *sindhum* — Agni who makes the fruits flow through the sacrifice; *siṣāsantaḥ* — desirous of serving; *paryapaśyanta* — they worship all round; (therefore) *sūryaḥ* — Agni in the form of the Sun; *ebhyaḥ nṝn* [?] — to these, the guides; *āvirabhavat* — became manifest, visible.

**Bhāvārtha.** The wise, skilled in application, the Adhvaryu and the rest, bring the imperishable Agni to the altar, cherishing him in manifold ways in their hearts. Desirous of serving him, who yields the fruits of the sacrifice, they worship him all round. Agni, who in the form of the Sun makes all things arise, becomes visible to these guides.

**English Translation (as printed).** Experienced sages bring the invincible (Agni) to his station (on the altar) ; cherishing him in manifold (ways) in their hearts : desirous of propitiating him they worship the (boon)-shedding (Agni) ; and to those men he is manifest as the Sun.

### Printed p. 397  (PDF 415)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 27 [?].)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 4).** ***dhīrāsaḥ*** — *dhīro dhīmān*; *prajñāvantaḥ* (Ni. 3-[?]) — "the wise; the possessors of understanding". This word is read among the names of the intelligent (Ni. 3-[?]); Sāyaṇa too, on this Ṛk, explains: *prayogajñā adhvaryvādayaḥ* — "the Adhvaryu and others who are skilled in application", "the Adhvaryu and the like who are skilled in the performance". From this we see that the word *dhīra* means "courageous", "steadfast, brave" (*dhairyavāna*). In the Vedic texts, too, in the Upaniṣads, "the wise, the discriminating" (*vivekī*) is the meaning that is shown; they are said to be firm and unshaken even in danger; quiet-minded, they remain firm even in a calamity — it is said — it is the purport that they have this kind of qualities.

> युना सुवासाः परिवीत आगात्स उ श्रेयान्भवति जायमानः । तं धीरासः कवय उन्नयन्ति स्वाधियो मनसा देवयन्तः ॥

> *yunā suvāsāḥ parivīta āgātsa u śreyānbhavati jāyamānaḥ | taṃ dhīrāsaḥ kavaya unnayanti svādhiyo manasā devayantaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-4.) In such Ṛks, and in

> श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतस्तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः । श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभिप्रेयसो वृणीते प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते ॥

> *śreyaśca preyaśca manuṣyametastau samparītya vivinakti dhīraḥ | śreyo hi dhīro 'bhipreyaso vṛṇīte preyo mando yogakṣemādvṛṇīte ‖*

(Kaṭha 2-2.)

> महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ॥

> *mahāntaṃ vibhumātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati ‖*

(Kaṭha 2-[?].) in such Upaniṣad statements too, the word *dhīra* gives the sense "intelligent, wise".

***ajuryam*** — *ajīrṇam*, *nārarahitam*: "one without decay"; it is an adjective of Agni.

***sindhum*** — *sindhuḥ syandanāt*: "*sindhu* from flowing"; hence the name; it is read also among the names of the river.

*prakṛtaḥ syandamānaṃ yajñadvārā phalāni* — "here the flowing, giving the fruits by the sacrifice" is the meaning of this adjective of Agni.

***padaṃ nayanti*** — for this the meaning has been given in two ways. First, *padaṃ sthānaṃ vedilakṣaṇaṃ nayanti* — "they bring to the place, the altar", i.e. they carry him to the altar; or second, *yajamānādayaḥ sarvakāmānām āspadam enaṃ nayanti* — "the sacrificers and others carry him, the resort of all desires" — the sense is "they bring Agni, the resort of all desired aims".

***paryapaśyanta*** — *paritaḥ paśyanti, śuśrūṣante ity arthaḥ*: "they look all round — they wait upon", i.e. worship on all sides.

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> दिदृक्षेण्यः परि काष्ठासु जेन्य ईळेन्यो महो अर्भाय जीवसे ।
> पुरुत्रा यदभवत्सूरहैभ्यो गर्भेभ्यो मघवा विश्वदर्शतः ॥ ५ ॥

> *didṛkṣeṇyaḥ pari kāṣṭhāsu jenya īḷenyo maho arbhāya jīvase |*
> *purutrā yadabhavatsūrahaibhyo garbhebhyo maghavā viśvadarśataḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> दिदृक्षेण्यः । परि । काष्ठासु । जेन्यः । ईळेन्यः । महः । अर्भाय । जीवसे ।
> पुरुऽत्रा । यत् । अभवत् । सूः । अह । एभ्यः । गर्भेभ्यः । मघवा । विश्वऽदर्शतः ॥ ५ ॥

> *didṛkṣeṇyaḥ | pari | kāṣṭhāsu | jenyaḥ | īḷenyaḥ | mahaḥ | arbhāya | jīvase |*
> *puru 'trā | yat | abhavat | sūḥ | aha | ebhyaḥ | garbhebhyaḥ | maghavā | viśva 'darśataḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: Agni is to be seen in all ten quarters, victorious, worthy of praise; for the life of great and small he has become the begetter of these embryos, the opulent, visible to all.)*

> अयमग्निः काष्ठासु परस्परं क्रान्तास्व [?] वर्तमानासु दशसु दिक्षु दिदृक्षेण्यः अनुग्रहयुक्तैः दर्शनयुक्तो भवति । यद्वा प्रसृत्य [?] ... दर्शनेच्छाविषयीभूतः । दृशेः सनन्तात् [?] ... कन् [?] प्रत्ययः । अत एव जेन्यः सर्वत्र प्रादुर्भवनशीलो भवति जयशीलो वा । किञ्च प्रदानसमये ईळेन्यः स्तुत्यो भवति । किमर्थमित्याह । महो देवादेरर्भायार्भकस्याल्पस्य यजमानादेर्वा जीवसे जीवनाय । हविर्हननेन धनप्रदानेनेति विवेकः । तत्रोपपत्तिमाह । यदह यस्माद्बहुषु देशेषु पुरुत्रा बहुषु देशेषु ... देवमनुष्येत्यादिना त्रा प्रत्ययः । मघवा हविर्लक्षणान्न [?] ... विश्वदर्शतः सर्वविषयैर्दृश्य ... गर्भेभ्यः गर्भवत् ... *[small type; the sentence continues on p. 400; many words doubtful]*

> *ayamagniḥ kāṣṭhāsu parasparaṃ krāntāsva [?] vartamānāsu daśasu dikṣu didṛkṣeṇyaḥ anugrahayuktaiḥ darśanayukto bhavati | yadvā prasṛtya [?] ... darśanecchāviṣayībhūtaḥ | dṛśeḥ sanantāt [?] ... kan [?] pratyayaḥ | ata eva jenyaḥ sarvatra prādurbhavanaśīlo bhavati jayaśīlo vā | kiñca pradānasamaye īḷenyaḥ stutyo bhavati | kimarthamityāha | maho devāderarbhāyārbhakasyālpasya yajamānādervā jīvase jīvanāya | havirhananena dhanapradāneneti vivekaḥ | tatropapattimāha | yadaha yasmādbahuṣu deśeṣu purutrā bahuṣu deśeṣu ... devamanuṣyetyādinā trā pratyayaḥ | maghavā havirlakṣaṇānna [?] ... viśvadarśataḥ sarvaviṣayairdṛśya ... garbhebhyaḥ garbhavat ... *[small type; the sentence continues on p. 400; many words doubtful]**

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 146".)*

*(Ṛk 5 bhāṣya, continued.)*

> ... यजमानादेर्वा जीवसे जीवनाय । हविर्हननेन धनप्रदानेनेति विवेकः । तत्रोपपत्तिमाह । यदह यस्माद्बहुषु देशेषु [?] ... मघवा हविर्लक्षणान्नवानेवमुपयोगिधनवान् [?] ... सूः प्रसवितोत्पादयिताभवत् भवति । तस्मान्नाना हृदा रक्षमाणाः कवयः पदं नयन्तीति पूर्वत्र सम्बन्धः ॥ *[small type; many words doubtful]*

> *... yajamānādervā jīvase jīvanāya | havirhananena dhanapradāneneti vivekaḥ | tatropapattimāha | yadaha yasmādbahuṣu deśeṣu [?] ... maghavā havirlakṣaṇānnavānevamupayogidhanavān [?] ... sūḥ prasavitotpādayitābhavat bhavati | tasmānnānā hṛdā rakṣamāṇāḥ kavayaḥ padaṃ nayantīti pūrvatra sambandhaḥ ‖ *[small type; many words doubtful]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *(Agni —)* *mahaḥ* — (by carrying the oblation) of those great, the powerful gods; *arbhāya* — and of the small, the humans; *jīvase* — for the sake of life; *kāṣṭhāsu* — in the ten quarters; *pari dideṛkṣeṇyaḥ* — he who is to be seen by all, as he is wished to be seen (by himself too); *jenyaḥ* — (everywhere) manifest, or victorious; *īḷenyaḥ* — worthy of praise (is praised); *yat aha* — since indeed; *purutrā* — in many places; *maghavā* — in the form of oblation, the bearer of food; *viśvadarśataḥ* — Agni, visible to all; *ebhyaḥ garbhebhyaḥ* — like an embryo (child) the child in the womb, to these hymns and the rest, which are fit to be protected; *sūḥ abhavat* — has become the begetter.

**Bhāvārtha.** Agni, by carrying the oblations, is propitious to the powerful gods and, by giving wealth, for the life of the small humans; by his favour, in the ten quarters, all desire to see him; therefore he is manifest and victorious everywhere and worthy of praise. And since he, in many places, in the form of oblation, in the form of food, visible to all, is the begetter of these hymns and the rest, which are like embryos to be protected.

**English Translation (as printed).** He his [sic] willing to be seen in the (ten) regions (of space); the victorious, the adorable, the source of life to great and small: inasmuch as in many places the opulent (possessor of sacrificial food), who is visible to all, s [sic] the parent of that (pious) progeny.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***arbhāya*** — *arbhakasya alpasya yajamānādeḥ*: "of the small one, of the sacrificer and the like"; the word *arbhaka* is read among the names of the small (Ni. 3-[?]); the Nirukta author —

### Printed p. 401  (PDF 419)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 27 [?].)*

> कनिनकेव विद्रधे नवे द्रुपदे अर्भके । बभ्रू यामेषु शोभेते ॥

> *kaninakeva vidradhe nave drupade arbhake | babhrū yāmeṣu śobhete ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) Citing this Ṛk, he explains *arbhake* as *avadde* [?] — in the sense that "in the youthful state which is small (*anu*) …" (Ni. [?]). Agni, in comparison with the greatness of the gods, is *alpa*, "small" — the sacrificer, the sacrificer-like man — is the meaning.

***kāṣṭhāsu*** — this word is read among the names of directions (Ni. [?]). *tatra kāṣṭhā ity etad anekasyāpi sattvasya nāma bhavati* [?]:

> काष्ठा हि शो भवन्ति क्रान्त्वा स्थिता भवन्ति ।
> काष्ठा उपशिशो भवन्तीतरेतरं क्रान्त्वा स्थिता भवन्ति ।
> आदित्योऽपि काष्ठोच्यते क्रान्त्वा स्थितो भवति ।
> आपोऽपि काष्ठा उच्यन्ते क्रान्त्वा स्थिता भवन्तीति [?] ॥

> *kāṣṭhā hi śo bhavanti krāntvā sthitā bhavanti |*
> *kāṣṭhā upaśiśo bhavantītaretaraṃ krāntvā sthitā bhavanti |*
> *ādityo 'pi kāṣṭhocyate krāntvā sthito bhavati |*
> *āpo 'pi kāṣṭhā ucyante krāntvā sthitā bhavantīti [?] ‖*

(Ni. [?].) Because, having gone across all the regions, it spreads, it is called *kāṣṭhā*, "direction"; and because they, spreading, going across one another, remain, they are called *kāṣṭhā*; the sun, going across all regions, remains; and *Āditya*, "who stands having gone across his own course" — thus the sense is obtained. And "the distance that must be crossed", the goal of going, is also called *kāṣṭhā*.

> त्वामिद्धि हवामहे सातौ वाजस्य कारवः । त्वां वृत्रेष्विन्द्र सत्पतिं नरस्त्वां काष्ठास्वर्वतः ॥

> *tvāmiddhi havāmahe sātau vājasya kāravaḥ | tvāṃ vṛtreṣvindra satpatiṃ narastvāṃ kāṣṭhāsvarvataḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?].)

> उपो ह यद्विदथं वाजिनो गुर्भिर्विप्राः प्रमतिमिच्छमानाः । अर्वन्तो न काष्ठां नक्षमाणा इन्द्राग्नी जोहुवतो नरस्ते [?] ॥

> *upo ha yadvidathaṃ vājino gurbhirviprāḥ pramatimicchamānāḥ | arvanto na kāṣṭhāṃ nakṣamāṇā indrāgnī johuvato naraste [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks the word *kāṣṭhā* is explained as a place (*pradeśa*; "destination") to be reached, i.e. the ground that is the goal of the racers.

> तं वा एतमाहुरतिपितामहो [?] ... परमां काष्ठां प्राप्य [?] यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन ॥

> *taṃ vā etamāhuratipitāmaho [?] ... paramāṃ kāṣṭhāṃ prāpya [?] yaśasā brahmavarcasena ‖*

(Bṛ. U. 4-[?]-[?].)

---

### Printed p. 402  (PDF 420)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 146".)*

> महतः परमव्यक्तमव्यक्तात्पुरुषः परः । पुरुषान्न परं किञ्चित्सा काष्ठा सा परा गतिः ॥

> *mahataḥ paramavyaktamavyaktātpuruṣaḥ paraḥ | puruṣānna paraṃ kiñcitsā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ ‖*

(Kaṭha 3-11.) In such statements, *kāṣṭhā* means "the place that is to be reached — the highest place". The *kāṣṭhāsu* in the Ṛk in question means "in the ten quarters".

***jenyaḥ*** — *sarvatra prādurbhavanaśīlo bhavati jayaśīlo vā*: "he becomes one who appears everywhere, or one given to victory": the two meanings are given as synonyms: "manifest everywhere or victorious". According to the commentator it is derived either from the root *jani prādurbhāve* or from *ji jaye*, "to conquer"; this word is used in both these senses.

> जनिष्वा हि जेन्यो अग्रे अह्नां हितो हितेष्वरुषो वनेषु । दमेदमे सप्त रत्ना दधानोऽग्निर्होता नि षसादा यजीयान् ॥

> *janiṣvā hi jenyo agre ahnāṃ hito hiteṣvaruṣo vaneṣu | damedame sapta ratnā dadhāno 'gnirhotā ni ṣasādā yajīyān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk *jenya* is explained as *utpādanīyaḥ*, "to be produced", as an adjective of Agni; and

> होता जनिष्ट चेतनः पिता पितृभ्य ऊतये । प्रयक्षज्जिन्यं वसु शकेम वाजिनो यमम् ॥

> *hotā janiṣṭa cetanaḥ pitā pitṛbhya ūtaye | prayakṣajjinyaṃ vasu śakema vājino yamam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?].) in such Ṛks *jainyam* means "wealth to be won"; and

> ते हिन्विरे अरुणं जेन्यं वस्वेकं पुत्रं तिसृणाम् । ते धामान्यमृता मर्त्यानामद्वषो अभि चक्षते ॥

> *te hinvire aruṇaṃ jenyaṃ vasvekaṃ putraṃ tisṛṇām | te dhāmānyamṛtā martyānāmadvaṣo abhi cakṣate ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].) in such Ṛks it is understood as "victory-bearing" or "means of victory". In the Ṛk in question either meaning agrees with Agni.

***garbhebhyaḥ*** — by Agni's action in the interval, the self-nature of these [hymns] is produced; therefore the arising of these hymns and the like is such that Agni is the cause, it is explained.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar page, noted briefly).** Words treated, with the *san* desiderative of *dṛś* and a *kenya* suffix in *didṛkṣeṇyaḥ*; sūtra numbers small-type, not read [?].

*(Ṛk 5 grammar, continued, noted briefly.)* *didṛkṣeṇyaḥ* (continued: *kenya* suffix, loss of the final *a*, *ṇatva*, suffix accent); *jenyaḥ* (root *janī prādurbhāve* with *kenya*, or root *ji jaye*; "*kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam*" cited for the agent sense; guṇa of the root vowel; first *udātta*); *īḷenyaḥ* (root *iḍa stutau*; *kenya*; first *udātta*); *mahaḥ* (genitive sg. of *mahat* with loss of *ta* in Vedic, or root *maha pūjāyām* with *kvip*); *jīvase* (root *jīva prāṇadhāraṇe*; suffix *ase* in the infinitive sense; suffix accent); *purutrā* (*puru* + suffix *trā*; final *udātta*); *abhavat* (no *nighāta* because of *yat*; *aṭ* augment is *udātta*, so first-syllable *udātta*); *sūḥ* (root *ṣūṅ prasave*; *kvip*); *ebhyaḥ* (a dative sense with a case-ending substituted); *viśvadarśataḥ* (*viśvaiḥ darśataḥ*; root *dṛś*; *atac* suffix, *Uṇ.* 3-110 as printed [?]; in the *marudvṛdhādi* class, first member accent). ‖ 5 ‖

## Sūkta 147

### Printed p. 404 (continued; PDF 422)

*(The Kannada heading reads "The 147th Sūkta"; page header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 147".)*

*(Anukramaṇī, Sanskrit; not rendered in English. Gist: the sūkta of five Ṛks beginning "Kathā te" is the seventh sūkta, of Dīrghatamas, Agni deity, in Triṣṭubh; "kathā" is the Anukramaṇī word; its use at the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra was stated by the sūtra "trimūrdhānam iti trīṇi".)*

> कथा त इति पञ्चर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तं दैर्घतमसमाग्नेयं त्रैष्टुभम् । कथेत्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोरस्य सूक्तस्य विनियोगस्त्रिमूर्धानमिति त्रीणीत्यनेनोक्तः ॥

> *kathā ta iti pañcarcaṃ saptamaṃ sūktaṃ dairghatamasamāgneyaṃ traiṣṭubham | kathetyanukramaṇikā ‖ prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayorasya sūktasya viniyogastrimūrdhānamiti trīṇītyanenoktaḥ ‖*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta *kathā te* is the seventh sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Agni is the deity. The metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said to begin with *kathā*. As already said, the three sūktas beginning with the sūkta *trimūrdhānam* (Sūktas 146, 147 and 148) are used for the Prātaranuvāka and Āśvina-śastra mantra recitals.

**॥ ओम् ॥**

**Sūkta 147** — Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 21, Sūkta 147; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 28 [?]. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Ṛṣi: Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Devatā: Agni. Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> कथा ते अग्ने शुचयन्त आयोर्ददाशुर्वाजेभिराशुषाणाः ।
> उभे यत्तोके तनये दधाना ऋतस्य सामन्रणयन्त देवाः ॥ १ ॥

> *kathā te agne śucayanta āyordadāśurvājebhirāśuṣāṇāḥ |*
> *ubhe yattoke tanaye dadhānā ṛtasya sāmanraṇayanta devāḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> कथा । ते । अग्ने । शुचयन्तः । आयोः । ददाशुः । वाजेभिः । आशुषाणाः ।
> उभे इति । यत् । तोके इति । तनये । दधानाः । ऋतस्य । सामन् । रणयन्त । देवाः ॥ १ ॥

> *kathā | te | agne | śucayantaḥ | āyoḥ | dadāśuḥ | vājebhiḥ | āśuṣāṇāḥ |*
> *ubhe iti | yat | toke iti | tanaye | dadhānāḥ | ṛtasya | sāman | raṇayanta | devāḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: how do your shining rays, quickly pervading, give food and life; so that the gods/worshippers, having both sons and grandsons, rejoice in the sacrificial chants?)*

> हे अग्ने ते तव सम्बन्धिनो रश्मयः शुचयन्तो दीप्तिं सर्वत्र चेष्टमानाः [?] प्रकटयन्ते [?] आशुषाणाः आशु शीघ्रं सम्भक्तारः आशुसम्भक्तारो वा । वायुदेरपि [?] शीघ्रं सम्भक्तार इत्यर्थः । यद्वा । समन्ताद्व्याप्नुवन्तः [?] ... आयोः ... ददाशुः दाश्वांसः [?] ... कथा केन प्रकारेण ... देवाः ... *[small type; largely illegible; the grammatical tail is on the same page and is not read]*

> *he agne te tava sambandhino raśmayaḥ śucayanto dīptiṃ sarvatra ceṣṭamānāḥ [?] prakaṭayante [?] āśuṣāṇāḥ āśu śīghraṃ sambhaktāraḥ āśusambhaktāro vā | vāyuderapi [?] śīghraṃ sambhaktāra ityarthaḥ | yadvā | samantādvyāpnuvantaḥ [?] ... āyoḥ ... dadāśuḥ dāśvāṃsaḥ [?] ... kathā kena prakāreṇa ... devāḥ ... *[small type; largely illegible; the grammatical tail is on the same page and is not read]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada, begins).** *agne* — O Agni; *yat* — by the help of whose (your) helping rays; *ubhe* — both food and life; … (the page ends here; continues on p. 406).

### Printed p. 406  (PDF 424)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 147".)*

*(Pratipadārtha continued.)* *dadhānāḥ* — having obtained; *devāḥ* — the devout sacrificers; *ṛtasya* — belonging to the sacrifice; *sāman* — in the *Rathantara* and other chants (by reciting the chants); *raṇayante* — they show joy; *te* — your; *śucayantaḥ* — spreading light (on all sides); *āśuṣāṇāḥ* — rays which quickly pervade (the wind and the rest) as in *aviya* [?]; *vājebhiḥ* — joined with food; *āyoḥ* — life; *kathā* — in what manner; *dadāśuḥ* — do they bestow? [the order and exact glossing of the opening words of this Pratipadārtha is partly unclear in the print as read]

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, it is by the help of your rays — which spread light everywhere and pervade the wind and the rest quickly — that the sacrificers obtain food and life and cause these to be obtained also by their sons, grandsons and the rest; and, enjoying these good fortunes, they show their joy in the chants like the *Rathantara* and sing your praises. By what means do your rays thus bestow food and life? Tell us too these means.

**English Translation (as printed).** How have your shining and evaporating (rays), Agni, supported life ( and supplied ) food ; so that, enjoying both, the devout (worshippers), possessing sons and grandsons, may repeat the hymns of the sacrifice.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***toke tanaye*** — *tuk*, *tokam*, *tanayaḥ* (Ni. 3-[?]): these are read among the names of offspring (Ni. 3-[?]); both words mean "son". But viewed by ordinary usage the two words have one sense, yet in practice they are taken as a pair, "sons and grandsons and the rest". The Nirukta author shows the difference between the two in the passage beginning *tokaṃ tuvyate*, *tanayaṃ tanoteḥ*, and the commentators explain it: *toka* is derived as "(the son) who is instructed — 'do this, do not do that' — [?]" (the father making a rule thereby and having him lead the family life [?]); and *tanaya* from *tan*, "to spread, extend", i.e. one who extends the family; so it is explained that *tanaya* means "grandson" (Ni. 10-[?]).

***raṇayante*** — *ramayanti*, "they delight"; or *śabdayanti*, "they sound": the sense of delighting is given by the Sāyaṇa commentary, and also "making sound" (root *raṇ śabde*, "to sound"). The word is also used in the sense of *raṇa*, "battle": [continued on p. 407]

---

### Printed p. 407  (PDF 425)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 28 [?].)*

… the word is also given as a synonym of "fighting" (*raṇa*, "battle"): since, when the gods fight together there is joy in the certainty of victory, this word suggests that the battle-ground too is delightful.

> प्रति व एना नमसाहमेमि सूक्तेन भिक्षे सुमतिं तुराणाम् । रराणता मरुतो वेद्याभिर्नि हेळो धत्त वि मुचध्वमश्वान् ॥

> *prati va enā namasāhamemi sūktena bhikṣe sumatiṃ turāṇām | rarāṇatā maruto vedyābhirni heḷo dhatta vi mucadhvamaśvān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-171-1.)

> कृते चिदत्र मरुतो रणन्तानवद्यासः शुचयः पावकाः । प्र णोऽवत सुमतिभिर्यजत्राः प्र वाजेभिस्तिरते पुष्यसे नः ॥

> *kṛte cidatra maruto raṇantānavadyāsaḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāḥ | pra ṇo 'vata sumatibhiryajatrāḥ pra vājebhistirate puṣyase naḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks this word is used to indicate *harṣaṇīya* ("what causes joy"). So in the Ṛk at hand too, it is meant that, as the Hotṛs and others, joined with the *Rathantara* and other chants, they make known the joy, "delighting" is the sense.

***āśuṣāṇāḥ*** — *āśu śīghraṃ sambhaktāraḥ*; *vāyvāderapi śīghraṃ sambhaktāra ity arthaḥ*: "quickly associating; those who quickly associate even with the wind and the like": "swiftly joined with the wind and the rest, spreading as vapour (*aviya*) [?]" is the sense.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar page, noted briefly).** *kathā* (*kim* + *thāl*; *kimaḥ kaḥ* — *kim* → *ka* by *kimaḥ kaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-103); *thāl ca chandasi* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-26); because the *vibhakti* name applies to *prāgdiśo vibhaktiḥ*); *śucayantaḥ* (root *rucir prītau dīptau* [as printed]; *igupadhāt kit* (Uṇ. Sū. [?]) *in* suffix; no guṇa because *kit*; *śuciṃ karoti iti śucayati*; *tatkaroti tadācaṣṭe* [?], *ṇic*; loss of the *i* of *ṭi*; after *ṇijanta* the *laṭ* → *śatṛ*; the *ṇic* accent remains; nominative plural); *āyoḥ* (root *iṇ gatau*; *chandasīṇaḥ* (Uṇ. Sū. 2-[?]) *uṇ* suffix; *ājyād* [?] *vṛddhi*; *āyādeśa*; suffix accent: final *udātta*; *kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti* (Pā. Sū. 2-3-65) genitive in the sense of the object); *dadāśuḥ* (root *dāśṛ dāne*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* *liṭ*; *usādeśa*; doubling of the root; no *nighāta* because *pāda*-initial; suffix accent: final *udātta*); *vājebhiḥ* (*bahulaṃ chandasi*: *ais* optional; *bahuvacane jhaly et* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-103) *etva*).

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> बोधा मे अस्य वचसो यविष्ठ मंहिष्ठस्य प्रभृतस्य स्वधावः ।
> पीयति त्वो अनु त्वो गृणाति वन्दारुस्ते तन्वं वन्दे अग्ने ॥ २ ॥

> *bodhā me asya vacaso yaviṣṭha maṃhiṣṭhasya prabhṛtasya svadhāvaḥ |*
> *pīyati tvo anu tvo gṛṇāti vandāruste tanvaṃ vande agne ‖ 2 ‖*

> *bodha | me | asya | vacasaḥ | yaviṣṭha | maṃhiṣṭhasya | pra 'bhṛtasya | svadhā 'vaḥ |*

> हे यविष्ठ युवतम हे स्वधावो हविर्लक्षणान्नवन्नग्ने मे मदीयस्य मंहिष्ठस्य मंहतिशयेन पूजनीयस्य प्रभृतस्य प्रकर्षेण सम्पादितस्याद्येदानीं क्रियमाणस्य वचसः स्तुतिरूपस्य वचनस्य ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठी ॥ उक्तलक्षणं वचो बोध बुध्यस्व । स्तुतो भवेत्यर्थः । हे अग्ने लोके त्वः अत्र यास्कस्त्रयो [?] नेमे इत्यर्थः [?] (नि. ३-[?]) । एकोऽन्यो जनः पीयति हिंसति [?] ... यज्ञादिना त्वोऽनुगृणाति कश्चिदन्यः स्तौति [?] । वन्दारुः वन्दनशीलोऽहं ते तव तन्वं तनुं मूर्तिं वन्दे स्तौमि ॥ *[small type; several words doubtful]*

> *he yaviṣṭha yuvatama he svadhāvo havirlakṣaṇānnavannagne me madīyasya maṃhiṣṭhasya maṃhatiśayena pūjanīyasya prabhṛtasya prakarṣeṇa sampāditasyādyedānīṃ kriyamāṇasya vacasaḥ stutirūpasya vacanasya ‖ karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī ‖ uktalakṣaṇaṃ vaco bodha budhyasva | stuto bhavetyarthaḥ | he agne loke tvaḥ atra yāskastrayo [?] neme ityarthaḥ [?] (ni. 3-[?]) | eko 'nyo janaḥ pīyati hiṃsati [?] ... yajñādinā tvo 'nugṛṇāti kaścidanyaḥ stauti [?] | vandāruḥ vandanaśīlo 'haṃ te tava tanvaṃ tanuṃ mūrtiṃ vande staumi ‖ *[small type; several words doubtful]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *yaviṣṭha* — extremely young; *svadhāvaḥ* — having food in the form of oblation, O Agni; *me* — my; *maṃhiṣṭhasya* — extremely worshipful; *prabhṛtasya* — accomplished with great regard; *asya vacasaḥ* — this speech in the form of praise; *bodha* — understanding, accept (it; in the world); *tvaḥ* — some people; *pīyati* — (with the rites of sacrifice and the rest) revile you; *tvaḥ* — others; *anugṛṇāti* — (by performing the sacrifice and the rest) praise (you); *agne* — O Agni; *vandāruḥ* — I who worship you; *te* — your; *tanvam* — body, form; *vande* — praise.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, extremely youthful, having food in the form of oblations, accept this my praise, which is highly worshipful and made with great regard. In the world some revile you, and some praise you. But, O Agni, I, only worshipping you, praise your form.

**English Translation (as printed).** Youthful (Agni), to whom oblations are due, appreciate this my reverential and earnest praise: one men [sic] reviles (you), another propitiates (you); I, your worshipper, glorify your person.
