### Printed p. 410  (PDF 428)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 147".)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 2).** ***vandāruḥ*** — *vandanaśīlaḥ ahaṃ*: "I, one given to worshipping" — "one who has the habit of worshipping you; I", says the worshipper. In many places in the Ṛk-saṃhitā, the word *vandāru* is used in the sense "praise". Example:

> क उ श्रवत्कतमो यज्ञियानां वन्दारु देवः कतमो जुषाते । कस्येमां देवीममृतेषु प्रेष्ठां हृदि श्रेषाम सुष्टुतिं सुहव्याम् ॥

> *ka u śravatkatamo yajñiyānāṃ vandāru devaḥ katamo juṣāte | kasyemāṃ devīmamṛteṣu preṣṭhāṃ hṛdi śreṣāma suṣṭutiṃ suhavyām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks it means *vandanaśīlaṃ stotram*, "praise [that is] given to worship".

***tanvam*** — *tanuṃ tava mūrtiṃ vande*: "I praise your body, your form"; the worshipper says "I worship your form". What the forms of the gods are, in what way — *puruṣavidhāḥ syur ity eke* (Ni. 7-[?]): "some say they are of human form" — in this sense, the question on which view the Ṛk-saṃhitā rests is discussed in the Pīṭhikā section.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly).** *bodha* (root *budha avagamane*; *bhvādi*; *loṭ* 2nd sg.; *sip* → *hi*; *ato heḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-105) *luk* of it; *dhyeṇ…* [?] (Pā. Sū. 6-3-[?]) lengthening in the *saṃhitā*; *dyaucośṛḥ* [?]); *vacasaḥ* (root *vaca paribhāṣaṇe*; *uṇādi* *asun* suffix; being *nit*, first *udātta*; *kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti* (Pā. Sū. 2-3-65) genitive in the sense of the object); *yaviṣṭha* (*atiśayena yuvā yaviṣṭhaḥ*; *iṣṭhan*; *sthūladūrayuvahrasvakṣipra…* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-156) loss of *yuvan*'s *van*; guṇa of the preceding *u*; *āvādeśa*; vocative: *āmantritasya ca* gives the *nighāta* accent); *maṃhiṣṭhasya* (root *maha vṛddhau*; in the sense of the agent, *tṛc* suffix; *atiśayena maṃhitā maṃhiṣṭhaḥ*; *tuśchandasi* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-59) *iṣṭhan* after a *tṛjanta*; *teriḍi…* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-154) loss of *ti*; since the suffix is *nit*, first *udātta*); *prabhṛtasya* (root *bhṛñ bharaṇe*; passive: *niṣṭhā* suffix; *gatir anantaraḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) the *gati* (*pra*) keeps its natural accent; genitive sg.).

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: the protecting rays of Agni, seeing the blind son of Mamatā, saved him from distress; the all-knowing one protects those who do good, and the enemies who wish to harm them cannot.)*

> अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । उचथ्यबृहस्पतिनामानौ द्वावृषी आस्ताम् । तत्रोचथ्यस्य ममता नाम भार्या । सा च गर्भिणी । तां बृहस्पतिर्गृहीत्वा रमयामास [?] ... शुक्रनिर्गमनावसरे प्राप्ते गर्भस्य रेतः प्रावादीत् । हे मुने रेतो मा त्याक्षीः पूर्वमहं वसामि रेतःसङ्करं मा कार्षीरिति । एवमुक्तो बृहस्पतिर्बलात्प्रतिरुद्धरेतस्कः सन् शशाप । हे गर्भ त्वं यतो रेतोनिरोधमकरोः ... अतस्त्वं दीर्घं तमः प्राप्नुहि [?] जातमात्रो भवेति [?] । एवं शप्तो ममतायां दीर्घतमा आजायते । स चोत्पन्नः स्तन्योदधययोर्मुमुक्षः [?] ... स च स्तुत्या प्रीतमग्निमाह [?]... तेदीतमाह्वयते [?] । हे अग्ने ते तव सम्बन्धिनो ये पायवः पालयितारो रश्मयो मामतेयम् ममताया अपत्यं पुत्रं दीर्घतमसमन्धं पश्यन्तः ऽपश्यन्तोऽयम् [?] ... दुरितादुद्भूतात् [?] ... अरक्षन् रक्षितवन्तः तान्सुकृतः सुखकर्तॄन् विश्ववेदा विश्वज्ञो रक्षसि रक्षति । अस्मान्पालनेति भावः । ... एवं रक्षितास्मान् दिप्सन्तो दम्भितुमिच्छन्तो रिपवः कामादिरूपाः नाह देभुः अहेती [?] ... दंभेः ... देभुः । हिंसितुं शक्नुवन्ति ॥ *[small type; the story and the grammatical tail are only partly legible; many words doubtful]*

> *atretihāsamācakṣate | ucathyabṛhaspatināmānau dvāvṛṣī āstām | tatrocathyasya mamatā nāma bhāryā | sā ca garbhiṇī | tāṃ bṛhaspatirgṛhītvā ramayāmāsa [?] ... śukranirgamanāvasare prāpte garbhasya retaḥ prāvādīt | he mune reto mā tyākṣīḥ pūrvamahaṃ vasāmi retaḥsaṅkaraṃ mā kārṣīriti | evamukto bṛhaspatirbalātpratiruddharetaskaḥ san śaśāpa | he garbha tvaṃ yato retonirodhamakaroḥ ... atastvaṃ dīrghaṃ tamaḥ prāpnuhi [?] jātamātro bhaveti [?] | evaṃ śapto mamatāyāṃ dīrghatamā ājāyate | sa cotpannaḥ stanyodadhayayormumukṣaḥ [?] ... sa ca stutyā prītamagnimāha [?]... tedītamāhvayate [?] | he agne te tava sambandhino ye pāyavaḥ pālayitāro raśmayo māmateyam mamatāyā apatyaṃ putraṃ dīrghatamasamandhaṃ paśyantaḥ 'paśyanto 'yam [?] ... duritādudbhūtāt [?] ... arakṣan rakṣitavantaḥ tānsukṛtaḥ sukhakartṝn viśvavedā viśvajño rakṣasi rakṣati | asmānpālaneti bhāvaḥ | ... evaṃ rakṣitāsmān dipsanto dambhitumicchanto ripavaḥ kāmādirūpāḥ nāha debhuḥ ahetī [?] ... daṃbheḥ ... debhuḥ | hiṃsituṃ śaknuvanti ‖ *[small type; the story and the grammatical tail are only partly legible; many words doubtful]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *agne* — O Agni; *te* — your; *ye pāyavaḥ* — which protecting rays; *māmateyam* — the son of Mamatā, Dīrghatamas (the one named by the ṛṣi); *andham* — the person who is blind (thinking "he is blind"); *duritāt* — from the affliction (from blindness); *arakṣan* — protected; *tān sukṛtaḥ* — those good-doing rays; *viśvavedāḥ* — one who knows all; *rarakṣa* — protects (and so we too, protected); *dipsantaḥ* — (wishing to harm us) desiring to injure; *ripavaḥ* — enemies (of the form of desires); *nāha debhuḥ* — are unable to harm.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, your protecting rays, seeing Mamatā's son Dīrghatamas thus blind, protected him from blindness. You who know all protect those good-doing rays; so too, protected, the enemies who wish to harm us in the form of desires are unable to harm us.

### Printed p. 413  (PDF 431)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 29 [?].)*

**English Translation (as printed).** Your [printed "Ycur", sic] fostering (rays), Agni, beholding the blind son of Mamata, relieved him of the affliction: he who knows all things protects the pious, and (their) malevolent enemies are unable to do them harm.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***māmateyam andham paśyantaḥ duritāt arakṣan*** — "seeing Mamatā's son blind, they saved him from distress": in this, the protecting activity of Agni's rays is praised; Sāyaṇa narrates the *sannivēśa*-story (the background of the occurrence) here in this way:

> अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । उचथ्यबृहस्पतिनामानौ द्वावृषी आस्ताम् । तत्रोचथ्यस्य ममता नाम भार्या । सा च गर्भिणी । तां बृहस्पतिर्गृहीत्वा रमयामास [?] । शुक्रनिर्गमनावसरे प्राप्ते गर्भस्य रेतः प्रावादीत् । हे मुने रेतो मा त्याक्षीः पूर्वमहं वसामि रेतःसङ्करं मा कार्षीरिति । एवमुक्तो बृहस्पतिर्बलात्प्रतिरुद्धरेतस्कः सन् शशाप । ... स जातमात्रो [?] ... ॥

> *atretihāsamācakṣate | ucathyabṛhaspatināmānau dvāvṛṣī āstām | tatrocathyasya mamatā nāma bhāryā | sā ca garbhiṇī | tāṃ bṛhaspatirgṛhītvā ramayāmāsa [?] | śukranirgamanāvasare prāpte garbhasya retaḥ prāvādīt | he mune reto mā tyākṣīḥ pūrvamahaṃ vasāmi retaḥsaṅkaraṃ mā kārṣīriti | evamukto bṛhaspatirbalātpratiruddharetaskaḥ san śaśāpa | ... sa jātamātro [?] ... ‖*

*(The Kannada paraphrase of the story, in English:)* Ucathya and Bṛhaspati were two ṛṣis. Ucathya's wife was named Mamatā. When she was pregnant, Bṛhaspati forcibly took her and made love to her. At the moment of the emission, the embryo within said: "O sage, I am already living here first; do not mix seed [with mine]; leave your seed — have compassion on me." Bṛhaspati, angry that his seed was thus stopped, cursed the embryo: "Since you obstructed the seed, may you be born with long darkness (*dīrghatamas*) — be blind!" Thus the son was born to Mamatā named Dīrghatamas, "Long-dark". As soon as he was born, he, in the darkness, praised Agni; Agni, pleased with this praise, removed his blindness; and that incident is hinted at here.

The same story is told also by the author of the Bṛhaddevatā:

> द्वावुचथ्यबृहस्पती ऋषिपुत्रौ बभूवतुः । आसीदुचथ्यभार्या तु ममता नाम भार्गवी ॥

> *dvāvucathyabṛhaspatī ṛṣiputrau babhūvatuḥ | āsīducathyabhāryā tu mamatā nāma bhārgavī ‖*

> *tāṃ kanīyānbṛhaspatirmaithunāyopacakrame | śukrasyotsargakāle tu garbhastaṃ pratyabhāṣata ‖*
> *ahamasmi pūrvasaṃbhūto mā kārṣīḥ śukrasaṃkaram | tacchrutvā kṛtipratiṣedhaṃ tu na māmarṣadbṛhaspatiḥ [?] ‖*

> *sa jātyo [?] 'bhyatapaddevānekasandhaṃ [?] tamā gataḥ | dadurdevāstasmai netre tato 'ndho babhūva saḥ [?] ‖*
> *sa vediṣada itstutvā [?] ... ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 4-[?]-[?].) In this story, it is said that Bṛhaspati and Ucathya are brothers; and, as Sāyaṇa narrates, Dīrghatamas praised Agni; and here, the gods are praised, and it is also said that these gods gave him eyes. The story-background of *māmateyam duritād arakṣan* is this.

Concerning this sūkta, Oldenberg writes as follows:

Dirghatamas, the son of Mamata, is the reputed author of this section of the first Mandala which belongs indeed to a family of priests claiming descent from him. The story of the blindness of Dirghatamas and of the distress into which he fell is told in the Mahabharata I-4179 Seq.

Considering the construction of the whole verse from the grammatical point of view only, one will scarcely be tempted to translate otherwise than we have done. But it is rather strange that Agni is represented here as saving those very guardians by the aid of whom he has saved Mamateya. The meaning which one should expect to find expressed, is rather that Agni, as he saved Mamateya by his guardians, has saved also and will save, all pious worshippers. This meaning may be established if we consider the construction of the verse as similar to that of I-37-12.

Thus, we may, I believe, translate here, "Agni, with such guardians as thine who have seen and saved the blind son of Mamata from distress, he, the possessor of all wealth (i.e. Agni) has saved all those who have done good deeds".

(The Vedic Hymns, P. 171-2)

***duritāt*** — Nirukta author explains the word *durita* as *durgatigamanam* (Ni. 6-[?]); and

Citing this Śruti sentence, he explains the word *durita* in the sense "*duritāni — durgatiprāpakāṇi karmāṇi*" — "evil deeds that lead to a bad end" — ("*dussthitiṃ gatiḥ* [?] *tarataḥ*": the actions that are the means to a bad state are meant: they knew the *durita*, 'the evil acts', to be what is to be crossed over).

***dipsantaḥ*** — *dambhituṃ icchantaḥ ripavaḥ*: "enemies wishing to harm"; "the enemies of the form of lust and the like, who wish to injure us" is the meaning.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar page, noted briefly).** *pāyavaḥ* (root *pā rakṣaṇe*; *kṛvāpājimisvadisādhyaśūbhyaḥ uṇ* (Uṇ. Sū. 1-1) *uṇ* suffix; *āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-33) *yuk* for the root; the word *pāyu*; final *udātta* from the suffix); *māmateyam* (*mamatāyā apatyaṃ pumān māmateyaḥ*; *strībhyo ḍhak* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-120) *ḍhak* suffix; *āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ…* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-2) *eya*; *yasyeti ca* loss of the *ā*; *kiti ca* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-118) *vṛddhi* of the first syllable; accusative sg.); *paśyantaḥ* (root *dṛśir prekṣaṇe*; with *laṭ* → *śatṛ*, *paśya* substituted; *śap* vikaraṇa; as the root's *lasārvadhātuka* is *anudātta*, the root accent remains; *ugit* — nominative plural: *num*); *duritāt* (*dur* prefix + root *iṇ gatau*; *kta*; *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) *kṛdutarapada-prakṛtisvara*; ablative sg.); *arakṣan* (root *rakṣa pālane*; *laṅ* 3rd plural; owing to *yat* the *nighāta* is prevented; the *aṭ* augment being *udātta*, first *udātta*); *rarakṣa* (the root as above; *liṭ* 3rd sg.; no *nighāta* as *pāda*-initial; because of *ṇal* … *liti* (Pā. #### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यो नो अग्ने अररिवाँ अघायुरराती वा मर्चयति द्वयेन ।
> मन्त्रो गुरुः पुनरस्तु सो अस्मा अनु मृक्षीष्ट तन्वं दुरुक्तैः ॥ ४ ॥

> *yo no agne ararivā~ aghāyurarātī vā marcayati dvayena |*
> *mantro guruḥ punarastu so asmā anu mṛkṣīṣṭa tanvaṃ duruktaiḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यः । नः । अग्ने । अररिवान् । अघऽयुः । अरातिऽवा । मर्चयति । द्वयेन ।
> मन्त्रः । गुरुः । पुनः । अस्तु । सः । अस्मै । अनु । मृक्षीष्ट । तन्वम् । दुःऽउक्तैः ॥ ४ ॥

> *yaḥ | naḥ | agne | ararivān | agha 'yuḥ | arāti 'vā | marcayati | dvayena |*
> *mantraḥ | guruḥ | punaḥ | astu | saḥ | asmai | anu | mṛkṣīṣṭa | tanvam | duḥ 'uktaiḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

> हे अग्ने नोऽस्माकं यः शत्रुरघायुः पापेच्छुः [?] ... अररिवान् अस्मद्दानप्रतिबन्धकः [?] [...] रातेर्लुङ् [?] छान्दसः ... क्वसुः । अरातिवा अदातापि [?] ... स्वयमदावान् [?] ... यः शत्रुर्द्वयेन मानसवाचिकभेदेन द्विविधेन । न दद्यात् [?] मानसो मन्त्रः ... निन्दाभ्यां [?] ... स्वसन्तं [?] ... मर्चयति । उद्वेजयतीत्यर्थः [?] ... पुनरस्तु [?] ... तस्मै ... अनुमृक्षीष्ट अनुकरेण [?] ... दुरुक्तैः ... यद्वा । स द्विविधो मन्त्रः अस्मै प्रयोक्त्रैव गुरुर्गरीयान् [?] अस्तु ... दुरुक्तैः कोऽरातिः स्वतनुमेव [?] ... दहत्वित्यर्थः ॥ *[small type; largely illegible; only fragments read]*

> *he agne no 'smākaṃ yaḥ śatruraghāyuḥ pāpecchuḥ [?] ... ararivān asmaddānapratibandhakaḥ [?] [...] rāterluṅ [?] chāndasaḥ ... kvasuḥ | arātivā adātāpi [?] ... svayamadāvān [?] ... yaḥ śatrurdvayena mānasavācikabhedena dvividhena | na dadyāt [?] mānaso mantraḥ ... nindābhyāṃ [?] ... svasantaṃ [?] ... marcayati | udvejayatītyarthaḥ [?] ... punarastu [?] ... tasmai ... anumṛkṣīṣṭa anukareṇa [?] ... duruktaiḥ ... yadvā | sa dvividho mantraḥ asmai prayoktraiva gururgarīyān [?] astu ... duruktaiḥ ko 'rātiḥ svatanumeva [?] ... dahatvityarthaḥ ‖ *[small type; largely illegible; only fragments read]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *agne* — O Agni; *naḥ* — (your devotees) us; *aghāyuḥ* — the sinner; *arirvān* — who obstructs our offering of oblations; *arātī vā* — and himself without gifts; *yaḥ* — which enemy; *dvayena* — with a twofold, mental and verbal; (or) with two kinds of mantras; *marcayati* — (us) he harms, afflicts; *saḥ mantraḥ* — that mantra of his, fashioned by the mind; *asmai punaḥ* — to him again; *guruḥ* — heavy, burdensome; *astu* — let it be (so); *durukteḥ* [as printed *duruktaiḥ*] — by his evil words; *tanvam* — his own body; *anu mṛkṣīṣṭa* — let him be made to be burned.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, may the enemy who, sinful and obstructing our offering of oblations, himself giving nothing, harms us with a twofold, mental and verbal, evil spell — may that spell fall heavily back on its user; and may he himself burn his own body by his evil words.

### Printed p. 418  (PDF 436)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 147".)*

**English Translation (as printed).** When a wicked (man), with twofold (malignity of thought and speech), obstructing our offerings, and refraining from gifts (himself) reviles us, may his prayer be heavy on him and involve his person ( in the consequences of ) his evil works.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***aghāyuḥ*** — *māraṇādirūpāpecchāvān*: "one who wishes for the evil, in the form of killing and the like"; "one who looks to our destruction, of sinful mind". In present usage the word *aghāyu* is taken to mean "one whose life (*āyu*) is of the nature of sin (*agha*)", i.e. one who lives sinfully. Example:

> अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ।

> *aghāyurindriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati |*

(Bh. Gī. 3-16.) In this verse, for the word *aghāyuḥ* Śaṅkarācārya, explaining it as *agham pāpam āyur jīvanaṃ yasya saḥ aghāyuḥ pāpajīvanaḥ*, has given the meaning "one whose life is full of sin" in the commentary on the Gītā verse; but in the Ṛk-saṃhitā there is no such usage. Here it is *agham icchatīty aghāyuḥ*, "one who wishes evil" — one who wishes us harm, a sinner. As in:

> यस्ते इध्मं जभरत्सिष्विदानो मूर्धानं वा ततपते त्वाया । भुवस्तस्य स्वतवाँः पायुरग्ने विश्वस्मात्सीमघायत उरुष्य ॥

> *yaste idhmaṃ jabharatsiṣvidāno mūrdhānaṃ vā tatapate tvāyā | bhuvastasya svatavā~ḥ pāyuragne viśvasmātsīmaghāyata uruṣya ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks *aghāyataḥ* means "one who wishes to commit sin", "one who does evil" — hence, or *pāpam ātmana icchati* — "one who wishes sin for himself" — thus explained; the meaning in the earlier sense is the same. In the Ṛk at hand it means the sinner who wishes harm to the sacrificer.

***arirvān*** — *rarivān*, the sense *dānavān*, "one who gives". *Arirvān* means *adānavān*, "one who does not give". But since it is said *arātī vā*, and since it is *a-* *sneyam adānavān* [?], the word *arirvān* is explained by Sāyaṇa as "the obstructor of our offerings (*dāna*)".

***marcayati*** — *bhartsayati vidheyāṃ karoti vā asmān*: "he threatens us, or makes us subject to him". "By abusing us he makes us obedient to the enemy [i.e. harms us]" [partly unclear]; "that enemy's [?] harm — protect us — and may that mantra rebound upon him" is the prayer. Also in the other sense

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उत वा यः सहस्य प्रविद्वान्मर्तो मर्तं मर्चयति द्वयेन ।
> अतः पाहि स्तवमान स्तुवन्तमग्ने माकिर्नो दुरिताय धायीः ॥ ५ ॥

> *uta vā yaḥ sahasya pravidvānmarto martaṃ marcayati dvayena |*
> *ataḥ pāhi stavamāna stuvantamagne mākirno duritāya dhāyīḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उत । वा । यः । सहस्यः । प्रऽविद्वान् । मर्तः । मर्तम् । मर्चयति । द्वयेन ।

> *uta | vā | yaḥ | sahasyaḥ | pra 'vidvān | martaḥ | martam | marcayati | dvayena |*

> अतः । पाहि । स्तवमान । स्तुवन्तम् । अग्ने । माकिः । नः । दुःऽइताय । धायीः ॥ ५ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: whichever skilled mortal assails another with a twofold spell, protect us who praise you from that, O Agni, and do not put us into misfortune.)*

> पूर्वमन्त्रे द्विविधकुटिलमन्त्रेण कर्तारं तन्मन्त्रेण प्राप्नोत्विति [?] प्रार्थितम् । अत्र तु तन्मन्त्रेणात्मानं पाहीत्येवं प्रार्थ्यते । उत वा हे सहस्य बलनाम [?] ... सहः इति बलनाम । सहसः उत्पन्न [?] ... यः कश्चित् मर्तः प्रविद्वान् मायामन्त्रं प्रकर्षेण जानन् द्वयेन पूर्वोक्तरीत्या द्विविधेन मन्त्रेण मर्तं मनुष्यं मर्चयति विधेयं करोति भर्त्सयति वा । अतः तस्मात् हे स्तवमान स्तूयमान अग्ने स्तुवन्तं स्तुतिं कुर्वन्तं मां पाहि रक्ष । किञ्च नोऽस्मान् रिपुभिः [?] ... दुरितायेत्य [?] दुर्मन्त्रप्रयोक्तुर्दुःखाय [?] ... नः अस्मान् मा कीर्धायीः [?] ... धा धारणे । व्यत्ययेनेट् । सिचि वृद्धिः । न माङ्योगे [?] इत्यडभावः ॥ *[small type; partly legible]*

> *pūrvamantre dvividhakuṭilamantreṇa kartāraṃ tanmantreṇa prāpnotviti [?] prārthitam | atra tu tanmantreṇātmānaṃ pāhītyevaṃ prārthyate | uta vā he sahasya balanāma [?] ... sahaḥ iti balanāma | sahasaḥ utpanna [?] ... yaḥ kaścit martaḥ pravidvān māyāmantraṃ prakarṣeṇa jānan dvayena pūrvoktarītyā dvividhena mantreṇa martaṃ manuṣyaṃ marcayati vidheyaṃ karoti bhartsayati vā | ataḥ tasmāt he stavamāna stūyamāna agne stuvantaṃ stutiṃ kurvantaṃ māṃ pāhi rakṣa | kiñca no 'smān ripubhiḥ [?] ... duritāyetya [?] durmantraprayokturduḥkhāya [?] ... naḥ asmān mā kīrdhāyīḥ [?] ... dhā dhāraṇe | vyatyayeneṭ | sici vṛddhiḥ | na māṅyoge [?] ityaḍabhāvaḥ ‖ *[small type; partly legible]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *uta vā* — or; *sahasya* — Agni, born of strength; *yaḥ martyaḥ* — whichever human; *pravidvān* — knowing well the mantras of deceit; *dvayena* — mental and verbal, two kinds of mantras; *martam* — another man; *marcayati* — troubles; *ataḥ* — from the fear of this mantra-force; *stavamāna* — O Agni, who art worthy of praise; *stuvantam* — me who praise (you); *pāhi* — protect; (and) *naḥ* — us; *duritāya* — for the mouth of bad mantras; *mākiḥ dhāyīḥ* — do not make us a receptacle.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, born of strength, whichever wicked man, skilled in deceitful mantras, troubles another man by two kinds of mantra, mental and verbal — protect me, who praise you, from the fear of that mantra-force; and do not make us the receptacle of bad mantras.

**English Translation (as printed).** When, Son of Strength, a man skilful (in deception) assails another man with a doubly (malignant prayer), do you, Agni, duly propitiated, protect him who worships you ( from its effects ); consign us not to misfortune.

### Printed p. 422  (PDF 440)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 147".)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 5).** ***sahasya*** — *saha iti balanāma* — "*sahas* is a name of strength"; *tatra bhavaḥ sahasyaḥ* — "born in it, therefore *sahasya*": Agni is addressed as "O one born of strength". *yate kāraṇānmathanakāle baleneṣyate*: "because, at the time of churning, by strength he is wished for [?]"; since Agni is born from the power (*bala*) of friction, this adjective is given. *sahasaḥ putra*, *sahasā jāyamānaḥ* and many such adjectives show Agni's origin and birth in many places.

***duritāya*** — *śatrukṛtāya durmantraprayuktaduḥkhāya*: "for the suffering caused by a bad mantra applied by an enemy" — the sense is *śatruvinda ujjārita* [?] "a word produced by the enemy, and the sorrow arising from the mantra made by it".

***mākir dhāyīḥ*** — *mākiḥ* is of the group of words *sarvapadasūnām mnātam* (?): "*hikaṃ*, *nukaṃ*" and the like (Ni. 1-[?]); these are *nipāta* particles and are among the *sambandhasūcaka* *avyaya*s; *mākiḥ* belongs to that group. *mākir dhāyīḥ* means "do not make (us) the recipients (of the bad mantra)" (*mā kṣamasva*) — or "do not give anyone the opportunity to harm us" — such is the purport.

> प्रति ष्य शोको विश्वजन्यो [?] तोऽवि [?] भवा पायुर्विशो अस्या अदब्धः । यो नो दूरे अघशंसो यो अन्त्यग्ने माकिष्टे व्यथिरा दधर्षीत् ॥

> *prati ṣya śoko viśvajanyo [?] to 'vi [?] bhavā pāyurviśo asyā adabdhaḥ | yo no dūre aghaśaṃso yo antyagne mākiṣṭe vyathirā dadharṣīt ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks, as *mākiḥ* means "let none (harm)", so here too the prayer is made.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar page, noted briefly).** *sahasya* (*sahas* "strength"; *tatra bhavaḥ sahasyaḥ*; *bhave chandasi* (Pā. Sū. 4-4-110) *yat* suffix; in the vocative, *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198) accent: *nighāta*); *pravidvān* (*prakarṣeṇa vetti pravidvān*; root *vida jñāne*; *vido laṭo vā* … *vidaḥ śatur vasuḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-36) *vasu*; *prādisamāsa*: *kṛdutarapada-prakṛtisvara*); *martaḥ* (root *mṛṅ prāṇatyāge*; *asisaṃjimṛ…* (Uṇ. Sū. 3-[?]) *tan* suffix; on account of it guṇa of the root's *ṛ*; *ra* follows; being *nit*, first *udātta*); *pāhi* (root *pā rakṣaṇe*; *loṭ* 2nd sg.; *tiṅ*-*nighāta*).

## Sūkta 148

### Printed p. 423 (continued; PDF 441)

*(The Kannada heading reads "The 148th Sūkta".)*

*(Anukramaṇī, Sanskrit; not rendered in English. Gist: the sūkta of five Ṛks beginning "Mathīd yat" is the eighth sūkta, of Dīrghatamas, Triṣṭubh, Agni deity; its use, as the middle of the three sūktas, was stated earlier [by the third and last of the group].)*

> मथीद्यदिति पञ्चर्चमष्टमं सूक्तं दैर्घतमसं त्रैष्टुभमाग्नेयम् । मथीद्यदित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ सूक्तत्रयस्य मध्यस्य तृतीयेनान्त्येन [?] पूर्वं विनियोग उक्तः ॥

> *mathīdyaditi pañcarcamaṣṭamaṃ sūktaṃ dairghatamasaṃ traiṣṭubhamāgneyam | mathīdyadityanukramaṇikā ‖ sūktatrayasya madhyasya tṛtīyenāntyena [?] pūrvaṃ viniyoga uktaḥ ‖*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta *mathīd yat* is the eighth sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Agni is the deity; Triṣṭubh is the metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said to begin *mathīd yadīm*. As this sūkta is one of the three sūktas mentioned before, the use [of the group] has been stated already.

### Printed p. 424  (PDF 442)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 148".)*

**॥ ओम् ॥**

**Sūkta 148** — Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 21, Sūkta 148; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 31 [?]. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Ṛṣi: Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Devatā: Agni. Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> मथीद्यदीं विष्टो मातरिश्वा होतारं विश्वाप्सुं विश्वदेव्यम् ।
> नि यं दधुर्मनुष्यासु विक्षु स्वर्ण चित्रं वपुषे विभावम् ॥ १ ॥

> *mathīdyadīṃ viṣṭo mātariśvā hotāraṃ viśvāpsuṃ viśvadevyam |*
> *ni yaṃ dadhurmanuṣyāsu vikṣu svarṇa citraṃ vapuṣe vibhāvam ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> मथीत् । यत् । ईम् । विष्टः । मातरिश्वा । होतारम् । विश्वऽआप्सुम् । विश्वऽदेव्यम् ।
> नि । यम् । दधुः । मनुष्यासु । विक्षु । स्वः । न । चित्रम् । वपुषे । विऽभावम् ॥ १ ॥

> *mathīt | yat | īm | viṣṭaḥ | mātariśvā | hotāram | viśva 'āpsum | viśva 'devyam |*
> *ni | yam | dadhuḥ | manuṣyāsu | vikṣu | svaḥ | na | citram | vapuṣe | vi 'bhāvam ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: Mātariśvan, entering, churned out Agni, the invoker, many-formed, fit for all the gods, whom men established among human tribes, wonderful like the sun, for the sake of the sacrifice.)*

> होतारं देवानामाह्वातारं विश्वाप्सुं आप्स्निति रूपनाम । नानारूपं पार्थिववैद्युतजाठराद्भेदेनाहवनीयादिभेदेन वा । यद्वा । कालीकरालयादिरूपेण ज्वालानां वैरूप्याद्विश्वरूपत्वम् । विश्वदेव्यं सर्वदेवयोग्यक्रियासाधकम् । यदीं यमेनमग्निं मातरिश्वा वृष्ट्यादिनानाम [?] ... वायुर्विष्टः काष्ठे [?] ... मथीत् अमथ्नात् । प्रावर्धयदित्यर्थः ॥ मथे विलोडने । हृस्यन्तेक्षणेति वृद्धिप्रतिषेधः ॥ पुनः स एव विशेष्यते । यमग्निं मनुष्यासु मनुष्या [...] *[small type; largely illegible; the sentence continues on p. 425]*

> *hotāraṃ devānāmāhvātāraṃ viśvāpsuṃ āpsniti rūpanāma | nānārūpaṃ pārthivavaidyutajāṭharādbhedenāhavanīyādibhedena vā | yadvā | kālīkarālayādirūpeṇa jvālānāṃ vairūpyādviśvarūpatvam | viśvadevyaṃ sarvadevayogyakriyāsādhakam | yadīṃ yamenamagniṃ mātariśvā vṛṣṭyādinānāma [?] ... vāyurviṣṭaḥ kāṣṭhe [?] ... mathīt amathnāt | prāvardhayadityarthaḥ ‖ mathe viloḍane | hṛsyantekṣaṇeti vṛddhipratiṣedhaḥ ‖ punaḥ sa eva viśeṣyate | yamagniṃ manuṣyāsu manuṣyā [...] *[small type; largely illegible; the sentence continues on p. 425]**

### Printed p. 425  (PDF 443)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 31 [?].)*

*(Ṛk 1 bhāṣya, continued; small type, partly legible.)*

> ... कर्मे कुर्वतीषु विक्षु [?] प्रजासु पूर्वं वपुषे यज्ञसिद्ध्ये नि दधुः । धारयन्ति । मनुष्यस्य मनुषो वेति [?] ... ॥ मनुष्यास्तेजसां तेजोऽग्निं स्वर्णं स्वरेणेव सूर्यमिव चित्रं ... विभावं विविधप्रकारेण दीप्तिमन्तं [?] ... स्वश्शब्दो यास्कैवं निरुवाच ... स्वरादिक्मो भवति सु अरणः सु ईरणः स्वतो रसान्सृतो भासो ज्योतिरुत्सृतो भासते वा (नि. २-[?]) इति । ईदृशं यं निदधुस्तं मथीदिति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥ *[many words doubtful]*

> *... karme kurvatīṣu vikṣu [?] prajāsu pūrvaṃ vapuṣe yajñasiddhye ni dadhuḥ | dhārayanti | manuṣyasya manuṣo veti [?] ... ‖ manuṣyāstejasāṃ tejo 'gniṃ svarṇaṃ svareṇeva sūryamiva citraṃ ... vibhāvaṃ vividhaprakāreṇa dīptimantaṃ [?] ... svaśśabdo yāskaivaṃ niruvāca ... svarādikmo bhavati su araṇaḥ su īraṇaḥ svato rasānsṛto bhāso jyotirutsṛto bhāsate vā (ni. 2-[?]) iti | īdṛśaṃ yaṃ nidadhustaṃ mathīditi pūrvatrānvayaḥ ‖ *[many words doubtful]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *hotāram* — the one who invites the gods to the sacrifice; *viśvāpsum* — having many forms, by the differences such as earthly, lightning-born, belly-born, or from the dark-and-fierce flames, the many-formed; *viśvadevyam* — the representative worthy of the worship of all the gods (and); *yam* — whom; *manuṣyāsu* — in the human; *vikṣu* — the sacrificers' tribes; *vapuṣe* — for the sake of the sacrifice (for its performance) [or: for an embodiment of the accomplishment]; *citram* — one pleasing to the mind; *vibhāvam* — the one possessed of various kinds of radiance, as the *sūrya*; *svaḥ na* — like the sun; *ni dadhuḥ* — they establish, being well-founded in the human species (as one on whom the sacrifice rests); *yadīm* — whom indeed; *mātariśvā* — the wind that moves in the sky; *viṣṭaḥ* — having entered (into the fuel, etc.); *mathīt* — (Agni) he churned out, he kindled.

**Bhāvārtha.** The wind, entering the fuel, kindled Agni — the invoker of the gods, the many-formed, the worthy representative of the worship of all the gods — whom, for the sake of the sacrifice, the human sacrificers established among mortal men, like the wonderful, variously radiant sun, who is pleasing to the mind.

**English Translation (as printed).** The wind, penetrating ( amidst the fuel ), has excited ( Agni ), the invoker (of the gods) the multiform, the minister of all the deities, whom they have established amongst mortal worshippers for the accomplishment of sacrifice, like the wonderful and variously radiant sun.

### Printed p. 426  (PDF 444)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 148".)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***viśvāpsum*** — *āpsiti rūpanāma*: "*āpsa* is a name of form"; *nānārūpaṃ pārthivavaidyutajātharādibhedenāhavanīyādibhedena vā*: "of many forms, by the differences earthly, lightning, belly and the like, or by the differences of the Āhavanīya and the others"; or [*yadvā*] *kālīkarālyādirūpeṇa jvālānāṃ vairūpyād viśvarūpatvam*: "from the many forms of the flames, such as Kālī, Karālī, the all-formedness". *pārthiva*, *vaidyuta*, *jāṭhara* — with the differences earthly, in lightning and in the belly; or the Dakṣiṇāgni, Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya — and in the many-formed flames from Kālī and Karālī etc.: thus the adjective of Agni.

***trīṇi jānā*** (*trīṇi jānā vibhṛtā*) — in such passages the three different forms of manifestation of Agni, who reflect the root-principle of the world, are shown. What are they?

> त्रिस्थानं जैनमर्चन्ति [?] होत्रायामवृक्तबर्हिषः । इह्यैव पवमानोऽग्निर्मध्ये मोघे ग्निर्वनस्पतिः ॥ [?]
> अमुष्मिन्नेव विप्रैस्तु लोके ऽग्निः शुचिरुच्यते । इहाग्निर्भूतस्तु शिखिर्लोके स्तुतिभिरीळिते [?] ॥
> जातवेदाः स्तुतो मध्ये स्तुतो वैश्वानरो दिवि ॥

> *tristhānaṃ jainamarcanti [?] hotrāyāmavṛktabarhiṣaḥ | ihyaiva pavamāno 'gnirmadhye moghe gnirvanaspatiḥ ‖ [?]*
> *amuṣminneva vipraistu loke 'gniḥ śucirucyate | ihāgnirbhūtastu śikhirloke stutibhirīḷite [?] ‖*
> *jātavedāḥ stuto madhye stuto vaiśvānaro divi ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 1-[?]–[?].) Of these three kinds, Agni that manifests on earth is known as *Pavamāna* Agni; the Agni in the middle world as the *Vanaspati*-Agni [?]; the Agni in heaven as *Śuci* Agni. These three divisions are also given in the Taittirīya-saṃhitā:

> अग्नये पवमानाय पुरोडाशमष्टाकपालं निर्वपेदग्नये पावकायाग्नये शुचये ।

> *agnaye pavamānāya puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapedagnaye pāvakāyāgnaye śucaye |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?].) The divisions *Pavamāna, Śuci, Pāvaka* are read in it. Besides these, Agni, *Jātavedas* and *Vaiśvānara* are also names showing three kinds of forms of Agni; in some places *divas pari prathamaṃ jajñe* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?]; Tai. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?]) and the like, Agni, as the submarine fire (*baḍabānala*) in the water, as the Āditya in heaven [?], as lightning in the atmosphere, is said to be perceived. Likewise:

> विश्वरूपं हरिणं जातवेदसं परायणं ज्योतिरेकं तपन्तम् ।

> *viśvarūpaṃ hariṇaṃ jātavedasaṃ parāyaṇaṃ jyotirekaṃ tapantam |*

(Praśna Up. 1-8.) In such statements he is praised as the "all-formed", as having a thousand rays, as all-knowing, as the inner self of all beings. And:

### Printed p. 427  (PDF 445)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 31 [?].)*

> काली कराली च मनोजवा च सुलोहिता या च सुधूम्रवर्णा । स्फुलिङ्गिनी विश्वरुची च देवी लेलायमाना इति सप्त जिह्वाः ॥

> *kālī karālī ca manojavā ca sulohitā yā ca sudhūmravarṇā | sphuliṅginī viśvarucī ca devī lelāyamānā iti sapta jihvāḥ ‖*

(Muṇḍaka 1-2-4.) In such sentences, since the variform nature of the flames of Agni is said, the adjective *viśvāpsum* can be applied to this aspect of Agni's description. The all-formedness of Agni, who is all-formed, is described in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa:

> तमब्रवीद्रुद्रोऽसीति । तद्वाऽअस्य तन्नामाकरोद्यदग्निं रुद्रोऽभवदग्निर्वै रुद्रो यदरोदीत्तस्माद्रुद्रः । सोऽब्रवीज्ज्यायान्वा अतोऽस्मि धेह्येव मे नामेति ॥

> *tamabravīdrudro 'sīti | tadvā 'asya tannāmākarodyadagniṃ rudro 'bhavadagnirvai rudro yadarodīttasmādrudraḥ | so 'bravījjyāyānvā ato 'smi dhehyeva me nāmeti ‖*

Prajāpati, calling Agni "Rudra", [Agni] said, "I am greater than that; give me another name".

> तमब्रवीत्सर्वोऽसीति । तद्वाऽअस्य तन्नामाकरोदापोऽभवन्नापो वै सर्वोद्भ्यो हीदं सर्वं जायते । सोऽब्रवीज्ज्यायान्वा अतोऽस्मि धेह्येव मे नामेति ॥

> *tamabravītsarvo 'sīti | tadvā 'asya tannāmākarodāpo 'bhavannāpo vai sarvodbhyo hīdaṃ sarvaṃ jāyate | so 'bravījjyāyānvā ato 'smi dhehyeva me nāmeti ‖*

Then Prajāpati said to Agni, "You are Sarva"; Agni said that he was greater than that and asked for another name.

> तमब्रवीत्पशुपतिरसीति । तद्वाऽअस्य तन्नामाकरोदोषधयोऽभवन्नोषधयो वै पशुपतिस्तस्माद्यदा पशव ओषधीर्लभन्तेऽथ पतीयन्ति । सोऽब्रवीज्ज्यायान्वा ... ॥

> *tamabravītpaśupatirasīti | tadvā 'asya tannāmākarodoṣadhayo 'bhavannoṣadhayo vai paśupatistasmādyadā paśava oṣadhīrlabhante 'tha patīyanti | so 'bravījjyāyānvā ... ‖*

The forms of the plants, because they are of his inner nature [?], "you are Paśupati"; he said: "I am greater; give me another name."

> तमब्रवीदुग्रोऽसीति । तद्वाऽअस्य तन्नामाकरोद्वायुरभवद्वायुर्वा उग्रस्तस्माद्यदा बलवद्वात्युग्रो वातीत्याहुः । सोऽब्रवीज्ज्यायान् ... ॥

> *tamabravīdugro 'sīti | tadvā 'asya tannāmākarodvāyurabhavadvāyurvā ugrastasmādyadā balavadvātyugro vātītyāhuḥ | so 'bravījjyāyān ... ‖*

Being fierce, as the wind, "you are Ugra"; and again Agni asked for another name:

> तमब्रवीदशनिरसीति । तद्वाऽअस्य तन्नामाकरोद्विद्युदभवद्विद्युद्वा अशनिस्तस्माद्यं विद्युद्धन्त्यशनिरवधीरित्याहुः ... ॥

> *tamabravīdaśanirasīti | tadvā 'asya tannāmākarodvidyudabhavadvidyudvā aśanistasmādyaṃ vidyuddhantyaśaniravadhīrityāhuḥ ... ‖*

(Śa. Brā. 6-1-3-[?].)

### Printed p. 428  (PDF 446)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 148".)*

*(Ṛk 1, Special Topics continued; the Śatapatha-Brāhmaṇa narrative of the names given by Prajāpati to Agni.)* *(Prajāpati, calling him Aśani, because he was lightning:)* "…since you are Aśani, your name is Aśani" — Agni, again, [said he was] greater than that.

> तमब्रवीत्पर्जन्योऽसीति । तद्वाऽअस्य तन्नामाकरोत्पर्जन्यो भवत्पर्जन्यो वै [?] ... सोऽब्रवीत् ... ॥

> *tamabravītparjanyo 'sīti | tadvā 'asya tannāmākarotparjanyo bhavatparjanyo vai [?] ... so 'bravīt ... ‖*

To "you are Parjanya" [Agni, becoming Parjanya, the cloud, again said he was greater and asked for another name]:

> तमब्रवीन्महादेवोऽसीति । तद्वाऽअस्य तन्नामाकरोन्महादेवः प्रजापतिर्वै महान्देवः सोऽब्रवीत् ... ॥

> *tamabravīnmahādevo 'sīti | tadvā 'asya tannāmākaronmahādevaḥ prajāpatirvai mahāndevaḥ so 'bravīt ... ‖*

Prajāpati, being "the great god" (*mahādeva*): "you are Mahādeva"; Agni said: "I am still more; give me another name"; Prajāpati then said:

> तमब्रवीदीशानोऽसीति । तद्वाऽअस्य तन्नामाकरोदादित्यो वा ईशान आदित्यो ह्यस्य सर्वस्येष्टे [?] ... तान्येतान्यष्टावग्निरूपाणि ॥

> *tamabravīdīśāno 'sīti | tadvā 'asya tannāmākarodādityo vā īśāna ādityo hyasya sarvasyeṣṭe [?] ... tānyetānyaṣṭāvagnirūpāṇi ‖*

(Śa. Brā. 6-1-3-[?]–[?].) "You are Īśāna — the Āditya, lord of all the worlds" [says Agni]. The eight names — Rudra, Sarva, Paśupati, Ugra, Mahādeva, Aśani, Bhava and Īśāna — are the eight qualities-names of Agni; *tāny etāny aṣṭāv agnirūpāṇi*: "these are the eight forms of Agni", is the explanation in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. Hence the adjective *viśvāpsum* means "having the many forms described above".

***viśvadevyam*** — *sarvadevayogyakriyāsādhakam*: "the accomplisher of acts fit for all the gods"; the representative of the worship of all the gods.

> त्वामग्न आदित्यास आस्यं त्वां जिह्वां शुचयश्चक्रिरे कवे । त्वां रातिषाचो अध्वरेषु सश्चिरे त्वे देवा हविरदन्त्याहुतम् ॥

> *tvāmagna ādityāsa āsyaṃ tvāṃ jihvāṃ śucayaścakrire kave | tvāṃ rātiṣāco adhvareṣu saścire tve devā haviradantyāhutam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-13.) As described in such Ṛks, Agni, being the representative of all the gods, receives the oblations for all; hence this adjective.

***svaḥ*** — *svar ādityo bhavati*; *su araṇaḥ, su īraṇaḥ, svato rasān, svato bhāsaṃ jyotiṣām, svato bhāsate vā* (Ni. 2-[?]). Being extremely …

> वन्वासो ये स्रजः स्वतवः [?] इषं स्वरभिजायन्ते धूतयः । सहस्रियासो अपां नोर्मय आसा गावो वन्द्यासो नोक्षणः ॥ [?]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk *svar* is taken as "heaven", and in other places as "light". In the Ṛk at hand the sense "Āditya" is correct.

***mātariśvā mathīt*** — "Mātariśvan, the wind moving in the atmosphere, entered the fuel and kindled Agni": *mātariśvā guhā santaṃ havyavāhaṃ samīdhire* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-9-5) [as printed] — in such statements, the story of the churning of Agni by Mātariśvan was told before.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar page, noted briefly).** *mathīt* (root *mathe vilodane*; *luṅ* 3rd sg. *tip*; loss of *i*; *sic* with the *iṭ* augment; loss of *sic* by *iṭa īṭi*; *hmyantakṣaṇaśvasajāgṛ…* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-5) prohibition of *vṛddhi*; *bahulaṃ chandasy māṅyoge 'pi* no *aṭ* augment; no *nighāta* because *pāda*-initial; the augment is *anudātta*, hence the root accent remains); *viṣṭaḥ* (root *viśa praveśane*; *niṣṭhā* *kta*; *vraścabhrasjasṛj…* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-36) *ṣatva* of the *ś*; on account of it *ṭatva* of the suffix; suffix accent: final *udātta*); *hotāram* (root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; agent *tṛn*; *bahulaṃ chandasi*: *saṃprasāraṇa*; *pūrvarūpa*; *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ* guṇa; suffix being *nit*, first *udātta*); *viśvāpsum* (*viśvam āpo yasya saḥ viśvāpsuḥ*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* prior-member accent); *dadhuḥ* (root *dudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *liṭ* 3rd plural; *tiṅ*-*nighāta*).

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> ददानमिन्न ददभन्त मन्माग्निर्वरूथं मम तस्य चाकन् ।
> जुषन्त विश्वान्यस्य कर्मोपस्तुतिं भरमाणस्य कारोः ॥ २ ॥

> *dadānaminna dadabhanta manmāgnirvarūthaṃ mama tasya cākan |*
> *juṣanta viśvānyasya karmopastutiṃ bharamāṇasya kāroḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> ददानम् । इत् । न । ददभन्त । मन्म । अग्निः । वरूथम् । मम । तस्य । चाकन् ।
> जुषन्त । विश्वानि । अस्य । कर्म । उपऽस्तुतिम् । भरमाणस्य । कारोः ॥ २ ॥

> *dadānam | it | na | dadabhanta | manma | agniḥ | varūtham | mama | tasya | cākan |*
> *juṣanta | viśvāni | asya | karma | upa 'stutim | bharamāṇasya | kāroḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(printed under the Kannada heading "Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu" [sic] on this page; gist: let those who injure not harm me, who offer praise; Agni desires my praise; and all the gods accept the acts of the praiser and sacrificer.)*

> मन्म मननीयं स्तोत्रं हविरादिकं वा ददानमिदग्नये कुर्वाणमेव मां दम्भितारो वैरिणो न ददभन्त दम्भितुं हिंसितुं न प्रभवन्ति । दम्भेर्बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य श्लुः ॥ व्यत्येयेनान्तादेशः ॥ मम कोतिथ्ये [?] इति उच्यते । तस्य दातुःहविस्सस्य [?] प्रदातुर्मम वरूथं वरणीयं स्तोत्रादिरूपमयमग्निश्चाकन् आत्यर्थं कामयते । कनतेः कान्तिकर्मा अस्माद्यजन्तान्ताल्लुङ्सत्तेः [?] ... बहुलं छन्दसः ... केवलमग्निरेव कामयते किन्तु सर्वे देवाः कामयन्ते इत्याह । उपस्तुतिं भरमाणस्य कुर्वाणस्य कारोः स्तोतुरस्य यजमानस्य मम विश्वानि सर्वाणि हविष्पाकादिरूपाणि जुषन्ते सर्वे देवा । आदो न ददभन्तेत्यर्थः ॥ *[small type; many words doubtful]*

> *manma mananīyaṃ stotraṃ havirādikaṃ vā dadānamidagnaye kurvāṇameva māṃ dambhitāro vairiṇo na dadabhanta dambhituṃ hiṃsituṃ na prabhavanti | dambherbahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya śluḥ ‖ vyatyeyenāntādeśaḥ ‖ mama kotithye [?] iti ucyate | tasya dātuḥhavissasya [?] pradāturmama varūthaṃ varaṇīyaṃ stotrādirūpamayamagniścākan ātyarthaṃ kāmayate | kanateḥ kāntikarmā asmādyajantāntālluṅsatteḥ [?] ... bahulaṃ chandasaḥ ... kevalamagnireva kāmayate kintu sarve devāḥ kāmayante ityāha | upastutiṃ bharamāṇasya kurvāṇasya kāroḥ stoturasya yajamānasya mama viśvāni sarvāṇi haviṣpākādirūpāṇi juṣante sarve devā | ādo na dadabhantetyarthaḥ ‖ *[small type; many words doubtful]**

### Printed p. 431  (PDF 449)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 32 [?].)*

*(Ṛk 2 bhāṣya, end.)*

> केवलमग्निरेव कामयते किन्तु सर्वे देवाः कामयन्त इत्याह । उपस्तुतिं भरमाणस्य कुर्वाणस्य कारोः स्तोतुः [?] अस्य यजमानस्य मम विश्वानि सर्वाणि हविष्पाकादिरूपाणि [?] जुषन्ते [...] सर्वे देवाः ॥ *[small type]*

> *kevalamagnireva kāmayate kintu sarve devāḥ kāmayanta ityāha | upastutiṃ bharamāṇasya kurvāṇasya kāroḥ stotuḥ [?] asya yajamānasya mama viśvāni sarvāṇi haviṣpākādirūpāṇi [?] juṣante [...] sarve devāḥ ‖ *[small type]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *manma* — the praise accompanied with faith, or the oblation; *dadānam it* — (to Agni) the one who offers; *na dadabhante* — the enemies (as destroyers) are unable to harm; (the doubt thus: "in whom [?]"); *tasya* — he who offers thus; *mama* — my; *varūtham* — dear praise and the like; *agniḥ* — Agni; *cākan* — desires greatly (the root *kan*, "to desire"); *upastutim* — the praise of him; *bharamāṇasya* — I who bear; *kāroḥ* — who sings of fame; *asya* — of the sacrificer (me); *viśvā ni karma* — all acts (of offering oblations and praises); *juṣanta* — all the gods enjoy and are satisfied.

**Bhāvārtha.** Enemies are not able to harm me, who offer praises with faith to Agni. Indeed Agni with great regard desires my dear praise and the like; and the gods too, enjoying my praise, my fame-singing and all the acts of me, the sacrificer, are satisfied.

**English Translation (as printed).** Let not ( my enemies ) prevail against me, when presenting acceptable (oblations), for (Agni) is desirous of my so offered adoration, and all they (the gods) are gratified by the (pious) acts of me, the reciter of their praise, and the celebrator (of the sacrifice).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***manma*** — *mananīyaṃ stotraṃ havirādikaṃ vā*: "praise to be reflected on, or the oblation and the like"; "praise of which Agni is the object [?]"; it is explained as "the word (*manma*) *manasaḥ ṛddhiḥ* [?]" "prosperity of the mind"; in the Ṛk-saṃhitā the use of this word is seen where objects of desire are shown. The Nirukta author:

> उपे प्रागात्समन्मे धायि मन्म देवानामाशा उप वीक्षमाणः ।
> अन्वेनं विप्रा ऋषयो मदन्ति देवानां पुष्टे चकृमा सुबन्धुम् ॥

> *upe prāgātsamanme dhāyi manma devānāmāśā upa vīkṣamāṇaḥ |*
> *anvenaṃ viprā ṛṣayo madanti devānāṃ puṣṭe cakṛmā subandhum ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].)

### Printed p. 432  (PDF 450)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 148".)*

Citing this Ṛk, he shows the sense of the word *manma*. Durgācārya, explaining the word, says *manma = mananīyam ṛddhijātam* — "the thing that is a prosperity-product, to be thought of" — "the thing of *ādyut* [?] nature"; in the Ṛks *1-[?]*, *1-[?]*, *1-[?]*… the word, with the same sense, is applied to the praise or the oblation that is the object of the sacrificer's thought: "praise that is worshipped, desired and the like, which is dear" — in the Ṛk at hand also, both the praise and the oblation that is worshipful and to be meditated on. In sentences such as *agniḥ prajñena manmanā* (Ai. Brā. 1-[?]) too the extra sense of this word may be seen.

***varūtham*** — the word *varūtha* is read in the Nirukta among the names of houses (Ni. 3-[?]); this word is made from the root *vṛ varaṇe*, "to choose, to cover", meaning "that which is to be chosen, desired" or "that which protects"; the word is used in the Ṛk-saṃhitā in different ways, pointing to objects:

> तां ईयानो महि वरूथमूतये उप ब्रुवे नमसा गृणीमसि । त्रिषधस्थो न यान्संच [?] पोत्रानभिष्यय आवर्त [?] ... ॥

> *tāṃ īyāno mahi varūthamūtaye upa bruve namasā gṛṇīmasi | triṣadhastho na yānsaṃca [?] potrānabhiṣyaya āvarta [?] ... ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk *varūtham* is "that which is to be chosen" (*varaṇīyaṃ dhanam*), that is "excellent wealth"; and in

> मा ते अस्माँ सहसावन्परिष्ठावघाय भूम हरिवः परादै । त्रायस्व नोऽवृकेभिर्वरूथैस्तव प्रियासः सूरिषु स्याम ॥

> *mā te asmā~ sahasāvanpariṣṭhāvaghāya bhūma harivaḥ parādai | trāyasva no 'vṛkebhirvarūthaistava priyāsaḥ sūriṣu syāma ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?].) *vārayanty etāni* ... *varūthāni rakṣaṇāni* — "protections, which keep off; the protective [powers]" is the meaning, from *upapravartakāt* [?]. Thus, though used in different meanings, in the Ṛk at hand the sense is "the dear praise that is worth choosing".

***kāroḥ*** — *stotuḥ asya yajamānasya mama*: "of the praiser, the sacrificer, me": "of me, who praise, of the sacrificer". The Nirukta author reads the word *kāru* among the names of the praisers (Ni. 3-[?]); the author of the Bṛhaddevatā has used this word as the sense of "the ṛṣis who are the poets, the authors of the sūktas":

> अग्नेस्तु योनि सूक्तानि पञ्च नामानि कारवः । षड्विंशतिस्तु धेन्वस्य प्राहुः सूर्यस्य सप्त च ॥

> *agnestu yoni sūktāni pañca nāmāni kāravaḥ | ṣaḍviṃśatistu dhenvasya prāhuḥ sūryasya sapta ca ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-[?].)

### Printed p. 433  (PDF 451)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 32 [?].)*

> पृथक्त्वेन समास्तैस्तु यज्ञे यज्ञीयस्थे [?] नभः । स्तुवन्तश्चैषु तेनेमं नराशंसं तु कारवः ॥

> *pṛthaktvena samāstaistu yajñe yajñīyasthe [?] nabhaḥ | stuvantaścaiṣu tenemaṃ narāśaṃsaṃ tu kāravaḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 3-[?].) In such statements the word *kāru* is used with the nature of a synonym of the word "poet" (*kavi*), saying that the *kāru* praise (*stutisuttāre*). In the Ṛk-saṃhitā:

> प्रदक्षिणिद्धि गृणन्ति कारवो वयो वदन्त ऋतुथा शकुन्तयः । उभे वाचौ वदति सामगा इव गायत्रं च त्रैष्टुभं चानु राजति ॥

> *pradakṣiṇiddhi gṛṇanti kāravo vayo vadanta ṛtuthā śakuntayaḥ | ubhe vācau vadati sāmagā iva gāyatraṃ ca traiṣṭubhaṃ cānu rājati ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].)

> वि चेदुच्छन्त्यश्विना उषासः प्र वां ब्रह्माणि कारवो भरन्ते । ऊर्ध्वं भानुं सविता देवो अश्रेद्बृहदग्नयः समिधा जरन्ते ॥

> *vi ceducchantyaśvinā uṣāsaḥ pra vāṃ brahmāṇi kāravo bharante | ūrdhvaṃ bhānuṃ savitā devo aśredbṛhadagnayaḥ samidhā jarante ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks it means "the praisers". In the Ṛk at hand also the same meaning.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly).** *dadānam* (root *dudāñ dāne*; *śānac* in the sense of *laṭ*; *ślu* vikaraṇa; by *vyatyaya*, final *udātta*); *dadabhanta* (root *dambhu dambhane*; *leṭ* 3rd plural, by *vyatyaya* the ending *anta*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* *śap* → *śluḥ*; *ślau* doubling of the root; after a *tiṅanta*, *nighāta*); *manma* (root *mana jñāne*; *ṇādika*: suffix *man*; *ñnityādir nityam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197) first *udātta*); *varūtham* (root *vṛñ varaṇe*; *jvaryaivībhyāmūthan* [?] (Uṇ. Sū. 2-[?]) *ūthan* suffix; on account of the suffix guṇa of the *ṛ*; *ra* follows; suffix being *nit*, first *udātta*); *cākan* (root *kana kāntau*; *kānti* = wish; the root being *tṛpaṇārtha* [?] *dhātor ekāco…* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-22) *yaṅ* suffix; *yajluk* [?] (Pā. Sū. 2-4-74) *luk* of *yaṅ*; after *yaṅluganta*, *laṅ*; or *bahulaṃ chandasi*: *śap* → *śluḥ*; 3rd sg., *bahulaṃ chandasy māṅyoge 'pi* no *aṭ* augment; *tiṅ*-*nighāta*).

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> नित्ये चिन्नु यं सदने जग्रभ्रे प्रशस्तिभिर्दधिरे यज्ञियासः ।
> प्र सू नयन्त गृभयन्त इष्ट्वी अश्वासो न रथ्यो रराहाणाः ॥ ३ ॥

> *nitye cinnu yaṃ sadane jagrabhre praśastibhirdadhire yajñiyāsaḥ |*
> *pra sū nayanta gṛbhayanta iṣṭvī aśvāso na rathyo rarāhāṇāḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> नित्ये । चित् । नु । यम् । सदने । जग्रभ्रे । प्रऽशस्तिऽभिः । दधिरे । यज्ञियासः ।
> प्र । सु । नयन्ते । गृभयन्तः । इष्ट्वी । अश्वासः । न । रथ्यः । रराहाणाः ॥ ३ ॥

> *nitye | cit | nu | yam | sadane | jagrabhre | pra 'śasti 'bhiḥ | dadhire | yajñiyāsaḥ |*
> *pra | su | nayante | gṛbhayantaḥ | iṣṭvī | aśvāsaḥ | na | rathyaḥ | rarāhāṇāḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: the sacrificers lay hold of Agni in his own constant seat and keep him there with praises, then, as rapid horses draw the chariot, they lead him on to the sacrifice.)*

> यज्ञियासो यज्ञयोग्या यजमाना ऋत्विजो वा यं मथनेनोत्पन्नमग्निं नित्ये चित्सदने नित्य इव गार्हपत्यलक्षणेऽग्न्यासादनस्थाने नु क्षिप्रं जग्रभ्रे गृह्णन्ति । ग्रहेर्लिटीरो र इति रेभावः ॥ हृग्रहोर्भ इति भत्वम् ॥ नित्यं गतेः [?] ... धार्यते नित्यं गार्हपत्यमिति सूत्रार्थाद्गार्हपत्यो नित्यः ... तदाश्रयेत्यनन्तरं [?] ... प्रशस्तिभिः स्तुतिभिर्दधिरे [?] ... *[small type; the remainder continues on p. 435; many words doubtful]*

> *yajñiyāso yajñayogyā yajamānā ṛtvijo vā yaṃ mathanenotpannamagniṃ nitye citsadane nitya iva gārhapatyalakṣaṇe 'gnyāsādanasthāne nu kṣipraṃ jagrabhre gṛhṇanti | graherliṭīro ra iti rebhāvaḥ ‖ hṛgrahorbha iti bhatvam ‖ nityaṃ gateḥ [?] ... dhāryate nityaṃ gārhapatyamiti sūtrārthādgārhapatyo nityaḥ ... tadāśrayetyanantaraṃ [?] ... praśastibhiḥ stutibhirdadhire [?] ... *[small type; the remainder continues on p. 435; many words doubtful]**

> *mucyate [?] gṛhītvā praśastibhiḥ praśaṃsābhiḥ stutibhirdadhire | dhārayantyāhavanīyārthaṃ [?] tatraiva [?] sthāpayanti | tataḥ [?] yajñanimittabhūte sati yajñayitvā pra sū nayante [?] praṇayanti | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | rarāhāṇā raṃhasā gacchantaḥ | rahi gatau | chāndase liṭaḥ kānac | aniṭkamāgamaśāsanamanityamiti numabhāvaḥ ‖ rathyo rathavantaḥ [?] | yathā rathyānaśvāso nā aśvā iva | te yathā dhṛṣṭā rathasvāminamabhimatadeśaṃ nayanti tadvat ‖ *[small type; partly legible]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *yajñiyāsaḥ* — the sons fit for the sacrifice, or the sacrificers; *yam* — (born of the churning of the fire-sticks) whom, that Agni; *nitye cit sadane* — in the eternal abode, in the Gārhapatya; *nu* — quickly; *jagrabhre* — they lay hold of (and); *praśastibhiḥ* — with praises; *dadhire* — they keep him established, so that he remains (in the Āhavanīya also); *iṣṭvī* — for the sake of the sacrifice, [thus] having sacrificed; *gṛbhayantaḥ* — (thus) holding; *rarahāṇāḥ* — those who run speedily; *rathyaḥ* — the horses yoked to the chariot; *aśvāsaḥ na* — like mares; *pra su nayante* — they lead him eagerly to the place of the sacrifice.

**Bhāvārtha.** The sons fit to perform the sacrifice, or the sacrificers, quickly hold the Agni born of the churning in his eternal abode of the Gārhapatya and keep him established there with praises, for the Āhavanīya. After that, for the sacrifice, thus holding him, they lead him, as the speedily running chariot-horses, yoked, bear a rider to the place of the sacrifice.

**English Translation (as printed).** Him, whom the worshippers lay hold of in his perpetual abode, they detain by their praises, and the holders convey him diligently to the sacrifice, as rapid coursers, harnessed to a car, (bear the rider to his destination).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***rarahāṇāḥ*** — *gatyarthakavāda rahi dhātuvinda niṣpannavāgi raṃhasā gacchantaḥ*: "derived from the root *rahi*, in the sense of going; going with speed" — "moving rapidly" is an adjective of the horses.

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> पुरूणि दस्मो नि रिणाति जम्भैरादोचते वन आ विभावा ।
> आदस्य वातो अनु वाति शोचिरस्तुर्न शर्यामसनामनु द्यून् ॥ ४ ॥

> *purūṇi dasmo ni riṇāti jambhairādocate vana ā vibhāvā |*
> *ādasya vāto anu vāti śocirasturna śaryāmasanāmanu dyūn ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> पुरूणि । दस्मः । नि । रिणाति । जम्भैः । आत् । रोचते । वने । आ । विभावा ।
> आत् । अस्य । वातः । अनु । वाति । शोचिः । अस्तुः । न । शर्याम् । असनाम् । अनु । द्यून् ॥ ४ ॥

> *purūṇi | dasmaḥ | ni | riṇāti | jambhaiḥ | āt | rocate | vane | ā | vibhāvā |*
> *āt | asya | vātaḥ | anu | vāti | śociḥ | astuḥ | na | śaryām | asanām | anu | dyūn ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: the destroyer, Agni, burns many trees with his jaws of flame and shines in the forest; the wind blows after his flame, as an archer's arrow-flight, every day.)*

> अत्र दावाग्निरूपेणायं स्तूयते । दस्मः उपक्षयितायाग्निः पुरूणि बहूनि वृक्षादीनि नि रिणाति [?] निरेकत्र [?] हिनस्ति ॥ री गतिरेषणयोः [?] । प्यादीनां ह्रस्वः [?] । केन साधनेनेति तदुच्यते । जम्भैर्दन्तस्थानीयैर्ज्वालाभिः [?] । आदनन्तरं वने वृक्षाधाने [?] ... विभावा विविधप्रकाशयुक्तः सन्रोचते दीप्तो भवति । आदनन्तरमस्य ... वातो अग्निं सखिभूतो वायुर्द्यून् [?] ... *[small type; the remainder on p. 438; partly legible]*

> *atra dāvāgnirūpeṇāyaṃ stūyate | dasmaḥ upakṣayitāyāgniḥ purūṇi bahūni vṛkṣādīni ni riṇāti [?] nirekatra [?] hinasti ‖ rī gatireṣaṇayoḥ [?] | pyādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ [?] | kena sādhaneneti taducyate | jambhairdantasthānīyairjvālābhiḥ [?] | ādanantaraṃ vane vṛkṣādhāne [?] ... vibhāvā vividhaprakāśayuktaḥ sanrocate dīpto bhavati | ādanantaramasya ... vāto agniṃ sakhibhūto vāyurdyūn [?] ... *[small type; the remainder on p. 438; partly legible]**

*(Ṛk 4 bhāṣya, continued.)*

> प्रतिदिनमनुकूलं वाति । ज्वाला आदाय गच्छति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । अस्तुः प्रेषकः [?] सकाशादेषाणां [?] गच्छन्तीं शर्यां न । शरो नाम हिंसासाधनलोहमयमिषुमुखम् । तत्प्रचुरम् । यद्वा । शरो नाम वंशान्तरजातीयः काष्ठविशेषः [?] । तद्विकारमिषुमिव । शर्याम् इषवः [?] शरमय्यः [?] । यद्वा शरः शरमय्यः । शर इव शर्याः । अथवा शरो हिंसा तत्कारोतीति शर्याः इषवः । ... तां यथा वायुर्नोदेकजन्मोपेगो वानुकूलं प्रेरयति तद्वत् ॥ *[small type; partly legible]*

> *pratidinamanukūlaṃ vāti | jvālā ādāya gacchati | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | astuḥ preṣakaḥ [?] sakāśādeṣāṇāṃ [?] gacchantīṃ śaryāṃ na | śaro nāma hiṃsāsādhanalohamayamiṣumukham | tatpracuram | yadvā | śaro nāma vaṃśāntarajātīyaḥ kāṣṭhaviśeṣaḥ [?] | tadvikāramiṣumiva | śaryām iṣavaḥ [?] śaramayyaḥ [?] | yadvā śaraḥ śaramayyaḥ | śara iva śaryāḥ | athavā śaro hiṃsā tatkārotīti śaryāḥ iṣavaḥ | ... tāṃ yathā vāyurnodekajanmopego vānukūlaṃ prerayati tadvat ‖ *[small type; partly legible]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *dasmaḥ* — Agni, of the nature of burning; *purūṇi* — many trees; *jambhaiḥ* — by the flames that are like his teeth; *ni riṇāti* — burns up completely; *āt* — after that; *vane* — in the forest, [now] bare of trees; *vibhāvā* — shining with various kinds of light; *rocate* — shines; *āt* — afterwards; *vātaḥ* — (his friend) the wind; *astuḥ na* — like the arrow shot by an archer; *śaryām* — [at the speed] of a fast-moving arrow; *asanām* — an arrow going with speed; *anu dyūn* — every day; *asya* — of this Agni; *śociḥ* — the flame (bearing it along); *anu vāti* — blows favourably.

**Bhāvārtha.** The burning Agni completely consumes many trees with his tooth-like flames. After that, in the forest now bare of trees, he shines with many kinds of light. And his friend the wind, like a fast arrow shot by an archer, bears his flame along and blows favourably every day.

**English Translation (as printed).** The destroyer, (Agni), consumes numerous (tree) by his flames and shines with manifold radiance in the forest: the favouring wind blows (the flames) onwards day by day, like the swift arrows of an archer.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***dasmaḥ*** — the word *dasma* in the sense "burning" and "beautiful, to be seen" — both meanings are made known in the same section, in the Ṛk 1-[?]-[?].

***jambhaiḥ*** — the particular sense of this word is given in the Ṛk 1-[?]-[?]; in this Ṛk "by the flames, like teeth".

### Printed p. 439  (PDF 457)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 33 [?].)*

> शर्या अङ्गुलयो भवन्ति सृजन्ति कर्माणि । शर्या इषवः शरमय्यः । शरः शृणातेः ॥

> *śaryā aṅgulayo bhavanti sṛjanti karmāṇi | śaryā iṣavaḥ śaramayyaḥ | śaraḥ śṛṇāteḥ ‖*

(Ni. 2-16.) The Nirukta author has given two meanings for *śaryā*: first, "the fingers are called *śaryā* since they produce actions (*sṛjanti karmāṇi*)"; second, the derivation of *śaryā* in the sense "arrows" from the root *śṛ*, "to hurt", is given. Then —

> अभ्यभि हि श्रवसा ततर्दिथोत्सं न कं चिज्जनपानमक्षितम् । शर्याभिर्न भरमाणो गभस्त्योः ॥

> *abhyabhi hi śravasā tatardithotsaṃ na kaṃ cijjanapānamakṣitam | śaryābhirna bharamāṇo gabhastyoḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].) Durgācārya, explaining this Ṛk, says *śaryābhir na bharamāṇaḥ*: "bearing, as one bears with arrows" — *yathā kaścit kaṃcit abhighātāya iṣubhir yodhet* ("as someone fights someone with arrows to strike him"); for the word *śaryābhiḥ* he gives "by arrows". Sāyaṇa, however, gives "by fingers". Both are possible. In the Ṛk at hand Sāyaṇa explains *śaraḥ nāma hiṃsāsādhanalohamayam iṣumukham tatpracuram* — "*śara* is an iron arrow-head, a means of killing; one who is rich in these" — or "*śaraḥ nāma vaṃśāntarajātīyaḥ kāṣṭhaviśeṣaḥ*, a kind of wood, of a species of reed; arrows made of that"; or the sense that they are made as *śara*, "means of harm". This derivation he has shown.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar page, noted briefly).** *dasmaḥ* (root *dasu upakṣaye*, *antarbhāvitaṇyartha*; *iṣiyudhīndhi…* (Uṇ. Sū. [?]) *mak* suffix; suffix accent: final *udātta*); *riṇāti* (root *rī gatireṣaṇayoḥ*; *laṭ* 3rd sg. *tip*; *kryādibhyaḥ śnā*: *śnā*; *prādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-113 [?]) shortening of the root; *aṭkupvāṅ…*; the *vikaraṇa* accent; *tiṅ*-*nighāta*); *rocate* (root *ruca dīptau*; *laṭ* 3rd sg.; *tiṅ*-*nighāta*); *vibhāvā* (*vividhaṃ bhāḥ yasya saḥ vibhāvā*; *ato manin…* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-74) *vanip* suffix; being *pit*, it is *anudātta*; *kṛdutarapada-prakṛtisvara*).

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> न यं रिपवो न रिषण्यवो गर्भे सन्तं रेषणा रेषयन्ति ।
> अन्धा अपश्या न दभन्नभिख्या नित्यास ईं प्रेतारो अरक्षन् ॥ ५ ॥

> *na yaṃ ripavo na riṣaṇyavo garbhe santaṃ reṣaṇā reṣayanti |*
> *andhā apaśyā na dabhannabhikhyā nityāsa īṃ pretāro arakṣan ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> न । यम् । रिपवः । न । रिषण्यवः । गर्भे । सन्तम् । रेषणाः । रेषयन्ति ।
> अन्धाः । अपश्याः । न । दभन् । अभिऽख्या । नित्यासः । ईम् । प्रेतारः । अरक्षन् ॥ ५ ॥

> *na | yam | ripavaḥ | na | riṣaṇyavaḥ | garbhe | santam | reṣaṇāḥ | reṣayanti |*
> *andhāḥ | apaśyāḥ | na | dabhan | abhi 'khyā | nityāsaḥ | īm | pretāraḥ | arakṣan ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: no enemies, no harmful ones can harm Agni even in the embryo-state; the blind or sightless cannot dim his glory; his constant helpers protect him.)*

> यमग्निं गर्भे गर्भवद्र्चक्रे [?] अरणिमध्ये सन्तं वर्तमानं रिपवो नेरा [?] ... रेषयन्ति न दुःखयन्ति । कथा रिषण्यवोऽन्ये हिंसकाः । दुरस्मुर्दर्शिनः स्वयं पश्यन्तः [?] ... *[small type; the sentence continues on p. 441]*

> *yamagniṃ garbhe garbhavadrcakre [?] araṇimadhye santaṃ vartamānaṃ ripavo nerā [?] ... reṣayanti na duḥkhayanti | kathā riṣaṇyavo 'nye hiṃsakāḥ | durasmurdarśinaḥ svayaṃ paśyantaḥ [?] ... *[small type; the sentence continues on p. 441]**

> *riṣaṇyavaḥ | pā. 3-1-32 [?] iti kyaci nipātatvādriṣaṇyavaḥ [?] | kyacchandasyutkaḥ [?] | na hiṃsanti kīdṛśāste [?] reṣaṇā hiṃsanasvabhāvāḥ | yadvā | teṣāṃ kriyamāṇaṃ hiṃsanamaprakāraḥ [?] ... abhikhyābhikhyāṃ [?] māhātmyaṃ mandā avidvāṃsaḥ atra vināśayitvāraḥ [?] addhvā [?] ... vidvāṃso 'pyabhayāvidyātāraḥ [?] ... na dabhanti na dabhnuvanti na hiṃsanti lokopakāriṇāmapi prayojanaṃ cchāśātīti bhāvaḥ | tathyaṃ sapāramārthikaṃ rūpaṃ ke jānantīti cet ucyate | nityāso nityā aniletibhakṣyaḥ agnihotrādinityakarmaratā vā | agniṃ nugrahātyayamapi nityā bhaviṣyantīti bhāsi nityatvamāśritya nityā ucyante [?] | tādṛśā yajamānāḥ pretāro yajñādinā tameva tarpayitāraḥ santaḥ emenamarakṣan rakṣanti | yajñādirūpeṇa bhajante ityarthaḥ ‖ *[small type; many words doubtful]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *garbhe* — between the fire-sticks, like an embryo that is to be protected well; *santam* — being present; *yam* — whom, that Agni; *ripavaḥ* — enemies, of the sacrificers; *na reṣayanti* — cannot harm; *reṣaṇāḥ* — those whose nature is to cause damage; *riṣaṇyavaḥ* — other harmful ones too; *na* — cannot harm; (and) *andhāḥ* — those who are blind, like those without knowledge, the ignorant; *apaśyāḥ* — those who, with eyes, are unable to see; (or) those who, even with knowledge, by devotion and faith … worship; thus — these unwise ones; *abhikhyā* — his famous glory (greatness); *na dabhan* — cannot make dim; *nityāsaḥ* — those who are of constant faith in devotion; *pretāraḥ* — the sacrificers who please Agni by sacrifices; *īm* — this Agni; *arakṣan* — protect, serve.

**Bhāvārtha.** Agni, who is in the midst of the fire-sticks like an embryo to be protected, cannot be harmed by his enemies, the foes of the sacrificers, or by other harmful ones given to doing damage; and the blind, as men without knowledge, the ignorant, are unable to know him and cannot dim his famous glory. The sacrificers, of constant faith and devotion, who please Agni by sacrifices, protect and serve him.

**English Translation (as printed).** The blind (of intellect), or those who see not (physically), detract not from his glory, whom no enemies, no malevolent adversaries, harm, even whilst yet in (his) embryo (condition); for his constant encouragers defend him.

### Printed p. 442  (PDF 460)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 148".)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***garbhe santam*** — *garbhavad rakṣaṇīyaṃ*: "in the embryo, being a being protected well, between the fire-sticks, like an embryo", thus Sāyaṇa has explained it in this Ṛk too; and:

> गर्भो यो अपां गर्भो वनानां गर्भश्च स्थातां गर्भश्चरथाम् । अद्रौ चिदस्मा अन्तर्दुरोणे विशां न विश्वो अमृतः स्वाधीः ॥

> *garbho yo apāṃ garbho vanānāṃ garbhaśca sthātāṃ garbhaścarathām | adrau cidasmā antarduroṇe viśāṃ na viśvo amṛtaḥ svādhīḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-70-3.) In this Ṛk: (1) *apāṃ garbhaḥ* — *garbhavad antar vartī, apām napāt*, "like an embryo being within the waters, the Apāṃnapāt" — in the name of the Apām Napāt, the Agni who is in the form of an embryo within the waters; (2) *vanānāṃ garbhaḥ* — *araṇyānām garbhaḥ dāvāgnī rūpeṇa tanmadhye vartate*: "the embryo of the forests; in the form of the forest-fire he abides within them"; (3) *sthātāṃ garbhaḥ* — *sthāvarāṇāṃ kāṣṭhādīnāṃ garbhaḥ antaravasthitaḥ*: "the embryo of the stationary ones, wood and the rest, abiding within"; (4) *caratāṃ garbhaḥ* — *jaṅgamānāṃ garbhaḥ jāṭharāgnirūpeṇa dehamadhye sthitaḥ*: "the embryo of the moving, abiding within the bodies in the form of the digestive fire" — so in many things Agni's state of being an embryo within is described.

> के इमं वो निन्यमा चिकेत वत्सो मातॄर्जनयत स्वधाभिः । बह्वीनां गर्भो अपसामुपस्थान्महान्कविर्निश्चरति स्वधावान् ॥

> *ke imaṃ vo ninyamā ciketa vatso mātṝrjanayata svadhābhiḥ | bahvīnāṃ garbho apasāmupasthānmahānkavirniścarati svadhāvān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In this, *bahvīnāṃ garbhaḥ* — *meghasthānām apāṃ garbhaḥ vaidyutarūpeṇa garbhasthānīyaḥ saḥ agniḥ*: "the embryo of the many waters, abiding in the clouds in the form of lightning — that Agni is, as it were, in the position of an embryo"; or *bahvīnām oṣadhīnām diśāṃ vā garbhaḥ*, "the embryo of the many plants or quarters" (*oṣadhiṣu antarvartī*, "being within the plants"). Likewise in the Ṛk at hand also the embryo-form of Agni is spoken of.

***andhāḥ apaśyāḥ*** — here it is explained in two ways. First: *andhāḥ* — *jñānaśaktirahitā avidvāṃsaḥ*, "the ignorant, devoid of the power of knowledge"; *apaśyāḥ* — *anetrāḥ* [sic: *anakṣāḥ*?], "sightless"; because they are such, they cannot know the fire-sticks' churning and so on, i.e. are unable to understand the kindling of Agni and the like (the performance of rites); second: those who are not devoid of knowledge but, with devotion and faith, ... are yet unfit for the rite — the sense is "learned men [too] with faith and no devotion" [partly unclear].

***abhikhyā*** — the word is read among the names of understanding (Ni. 3-[?]); here, *abhitaḥ khyātiṃ māhātmyam*: "on all sides spread fame, greatness" — it is explained by Sāyaṇa: "(of Agni) the greatness which is famous everywhere".

Sū. 1-[?]) *u* suffix; *itva* of the root; *anistaṃ rapati iti ripuḥ*; suffix accent: final *udātta*); *riṣaṇyavaḥ* (root *riṣa hiṃsāyām*; *muraskṛdarciṣṭitiśarvarṣaṇ…* (Pā. ## Sūkta 149

### Printed p. 444  (PDF 462)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 149".)*

*(Anukramaṇī, Sanskrit; not rendered in English. Gist: the sūkta of five Ṛks beginning "Mahaḥ sa" is the ninth sūkta, of Dīrghatamas, in the metre Vairāja (Virāṭ), Agni deity; the Virāṭ metre is of ten syllables per pāda or eleven; its use is by indication.)*

> महः स इति पञ्चर्चं नवमं सूक्तं दैर्घतमसं वैराजमाग्नेयम् । दशकाश्रयो विराळेकादशका वा । अनु. [?] ... तथा चानुक्रान्तम् । महः स वैराजमिति ॥ विनियोगो लैङ्गिकः ॥

> *mahaḥ sa iti pañcarcaṃ navamaṃ sūktaṃ dairghatamasaṃ vairājamāgneyam | daśakāśrayo virāḷekādaśakā vā | anu. [?] ... tathā cānukrāntam | mahaḥ sa vairājamiti ‖ viniyogo laiṅgikaḥ ‖*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta *mahaḥ sa* is the ninth sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Agni is the deity. The metre is Virāṭ. In the Anukramaṇī it is said *mahaḥ sa vairājam*, with *daśakāśrayo virāḷ ekādaśakā vā*, stating also the characteristic of the Virāṭ metre. The use is by indication (*laiṅgika*).

**॥ ओम् ॥**

**Sūkta 149** — Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 21, Sūkta 149; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 34 [?]. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Ṛṣi: Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Devatā: Agni. Chandas: Virāṭ.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> महः स राय एषते पतिर्दन्निन इनस्य वसुनः पद आ ।
> उप ध्रजन्तमद्रयो विधन्नित् ॥ १ ॥

> *mahaḥ sa rāya eṣate patirdannina inasya vasunaḥ pada ā |*
> *upa dhrajantamadrayo vidhannit ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> महः । सः । रायः । आ । ईषते । पतिः । दन् । इनः । इनस्य । वसुनः । पदे । आ ।
> उप । ध्रजन्तम् । अद्रयः । विधन् । इत् ॥ १ ॥

> *mahaḥ | saḥ | rāyaḥ | ā | īṣate | patiḥ | dan | inaḥ | inasya | vasunaḥ | pade | ā |*
> *upa | dhrajantam | adrayaḥ | vidhan | it ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: Agni, lord of great wealth, comes giving desired things, and is at the place of wealth; the pressing stones, worshipping him as he comes near, please him.)*

> महो महतः पूज्यस्य रायो गवादिरूपस्य धनस्य पतिः पालकः स्वामी सोऽग्निर्दन् ददद्वाभिमतं प्रयच्छन् [?] ॥ ददातेः शतरि च्छान्दसः शपो लुक् । तस्य चच्छान्दस्यभयदित्यर्थधातुकत्वादातो लोपे इति चेत्याकारलोपः ॥ आ अभिमुख्येनास्मद्देशमायन्नुषते प्रतीषते गच्छति । ईषते गतिकर्मा ॥ इनः सर्वस्य परिमितो [?] ... किंचेनस्य स्वामिनोऽग्निः [?] वसुनो धनस्य पदे अस्मद्भूतो [?] वेदिस्थाने आ । अत्र आयो [?] उपसर्गव्यवहितः ... यद्वा वसुनो निवासयोग्यस्य धनस्वामिनः इति सम्बन्धः । यद्वा । वसुप्राप्ति प्रसिद्धा । किंच उप ध्रजन्तमुपगच्छन्तमेनमग्निं मर्मषः [?] ... अद्रयः ग्रावाणः सोमाभिषवार्थाः [?] यजमाना विधन् विधानं [?] ... परिचरन्ति ... *[small type; many words doubtful]*

> *maho mahataḥ pūjyasya rāyo gavādirūpasya dhanasya patiḥ pālakaḥ svāmī so 'gnirdan dadadvābhimataṃ prayacchan [?] ‖ dadāteḥ śatari cchāndasaḥ śapo luk | tasya cacchāndasyabhayadityarthadhātukatvādāto lope iti cetyākāralopaḥ ‖ ā abhimukhyenāsmaddeśamāyannuṣate pratīṣate gacchati | īṣate gatikarmā ‖ inaḥ sarvasya parimito [?] ... kiṃcenasya svāmino 'gniḥ [?] vasuno dhanasya pade asmadbhūto [?] vedisthāne ā | atra āyo [?] upasargavyavahitaḥ ... yadvā vasuno nivāsayogyasya dhanasvāminaḥ iti sambandhaḥ | yadvā | vasuprāpti prasiddhā | kiṃca upa dhrajantamupagacchantamenamagniṃ marmaṣaḥ [?] ... adrayaḥ grāvāṇaḥ somābhiṣavārthāḥ [?] yajamānā vidhan vidhānaṃ [?] ... paricaranti ... *[small type; many words doubtful]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *mahaḥ* — of the greatness (the great); *rāyaḥ* — of wealth in the form of cows and the like; *patiḥ* — the owner; *saḥ* — that Agni; *dan* — giving (the desired aims); *ā* — in the direction of the sacrificer; *īṣate* — comes; *inaḥ* — the mighty, though one who is powerful also; *inasya* — of the powerful; *vasunaḥ* — of wealth; *pade* — at the place of the abode (the altar); *ā* — coming and seated; *upa dhrajantam* — Agni who comes near; *adrayaḥ* — the sacrificers holding the stones that carry the Soma juice; (or) the stones that carry the Soma juice; *dhrajantam* — Agni, who comes; *upa* — near; *vidhanit* — by their [own] sounds, they please him with joy.

**Bhāvārtha.** Agni, owner of great wealth in the form of cows and the like, comes toward the sacrificer giving the desired things. Though mighty, he comes and sits at the place of wealth, the altar, and the stones that carry the Soma juice please him with their sounds as he comes near.

### Printed p. 446  (PDF 464)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 149".)*

**English Translation (as printed, Ṛk 1).** Agni, the lord of great wealth, the granter (of desires), comes (to the place of sacrifice) ; he, the lord of lords, comes to the place of affluence, (the altar) ; the stone prepares (the libation for him) as he approaches.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics, Ṛk 1).** ***inaḥ*** — this word is read among the names of the lord (Ni. 3-[?]); Agni is praised as *inasya inaḥ*, "the lord even of lords":

> प्र सम्राजो असुरस्य प्रशस्तिं पुंसः कृष्टीनामनुमाद्यस्य । इन्द्रस्येव प्र तवसस्कृतानि वन्दे दारुं वन्दमानो विवक्मि ॥

> *pra samrājo asurasya praśastiṃ puṃsaḥ kṛṣṭīnāmanumādyasya | indrasyeva pra tavasaskṛtāni vande dāruṃ vandamāno vivakmi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-[?]-[?].) In such Saṃhitā passages, and in Brāhmaṇa passages such as

> अग्निर्वै देवतानां मुखं प्रजनयिता स प्रजापतिः स उ एव यजमानः ।

> *agnirvai devatānāṃ mukhaṃ prajanayitā sa prajāpatiḥ sa u eva yajamānaḥ |*

(Śa. Brā. 9-[?]-[?]) too, Agni is praised as the highest.

***adrayaḥ*** — "(the stones that press) the Soma juice, or the sacrificers who hold them", is the sense given. In the section of the Ṛk 1-[?]-[?] the difference between the words *adri* and *grāvan* [both meaning stones] as the means for pressing Soma has been shown.

For this word, besides the sense of "means for pressing the juice", other senses too are seen in the Ṛk-saṃhitā:

> उत स्म ते परुष्णीमूर्णा वसते शुन्ध्युवः । उत पव्या रथानामद्रिं भिन्दन्त्योजसा ॥

> *uta sma te paruṣṇīmūrṇā vasate śundhyuvaḥ | uta pavyā rathānāmadriṃ bhindantyojasā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks, "mountain":

> ब्रह्माणि मे मतयः शं सुतासः शुष्म इयर्ति प्रभृतो मे अद्रिः । आ शासते प्रति हर्यन्त्युक्थेमा हरी वहतस्ता नो अच्छ ॥

> *brahmāṇi me matayaḥ śaṃ sutāsaḥ śuṣma iyarti prabhṛto me adriḥ | ā śāsate prati haryantyukthemā harī vahatastā no accha ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, "the bolt, the destroyer of enemies" (*śatrūṇāṃ bhakṣakaḥ vajraḥ*) — the weapon that destroys enemies; and

> इन्द्रस्याङ्गिरसां चेष्टौ विदत्सरमा तनयाय धासिम् । बृहस्पतिर्भिनदद्रिं विदद्गाः समुस्रियाभिर्वावशन्त नरः ॥

> *indrasyāṅgirasāṃ ceṣṭau vidatsaramā tanayāya dhāsim | bṛhaspatirbhinadadriṃ vidadgāḥ samusriyābhirvāvaśanta naraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-62-3.)

### Printed p. 447  (PDF 465)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 34 [?].)*

In such Ṛks, "*asura*" ("cloud"):

> प्र यद्वेषु पृषतीरयुक्षत वाजे अद्रिं मरुतो रंहयन्तः । उतारुषस्य वि ष्यन्ति धाराश्चर्मेवोदभिर्व्युन्दन्ति भूम ॥

> *pra yadveṣu pṛṣatīrayukṣata vāje adriṃ maruto raṃhayantaḥ | utāruṣasya vi ṣyanti dhārāścarmevodabhirvyundanti bhūma ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-5.) In this Ṛk it is "the cloud". And:

> महः स राय एषते पतिर्दन्निनस्य वसुनः पद आ । उप ध्रजन्तमद्रयो विधन्नित् ॥

> *mahaḥ sa rāya eṣate patirdanninasya vasunaḥ pada ā | upa dhrajantamadrayo vidhannit ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-149-1.) In such places, *adrayaḥ* has many senses — "the stones pressing, the sacrificers" (*grāvāṇaḥ*, *yajamānāḥ*).

The word *adri* has such senses as thunderbolt, rākṣasa, stone, mountain, cloud; the Nirukta author shows several derivations:

> अद्रिरादृणात्येतेन [?] अपि वा अत्तेः स्यात् ।

> *adrirādṛṇātyetena [?] api vā atteḥ syāt |*

(Ni. 4-[?].) "It may be from the root *dṝ* [or *dṛ*], 'to split', which gives the sense of splitting (*dṝ* + *ā*), or from the root *ad*, 'to eat'" — thus *adri*; because they split mountains and the like, the thunderbolt is called *adri*. Likewise:

> यदिन्द्र चित्र मेहनास्ति त्वादातमद्रिवः । राधस्तन्नो विदद्वस उभयाहस्त्या भर ॥

> *yadindra citra mehanāsti tvādātamadrivaḥ | rādhastanno vidadvasa ubhayāhastyā bhara ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].) Citing this Ṛk, the word *adrivaḥ* is explained: "O Indra, possessing the vajra". Thus, since the root of the word *adri* has several derivations, from different roots and several meanings are given, in the Ṛk at hand *grāvanato yajamānāḥ* — "the sacrificers who hold the pressing stones" — is the meaning given.

***dhrajantam*** — *dhraj* is read among the names of motion (Ni. 2-[?]); thence *upa dhrajantam* means "*upa gacchantam*, approaching, Agni".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 1; grammar page, noted briefly).** *mahaḥ* (*mahataḥ* with loss of *ta* in Vedic; or root *maha* with *kvip*; genitive sg., *mahaḥ*); *rāyaḥ* (genitive sg.; *ūḍidaṃpadādi* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) case-ending *udātta*); *īṣate* (root *īṣa gatau*, *tudādi*; *laṭ* 3rd sg.; *tiṅ*-*nighāta*); *dan* (root *dudāñ dāne*; *śatṛ* in the sense of *laṭ*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* *śap* → *luk*; *chandasy ubhayathā* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-117) the *śatṛ* suffix is both *sārvadhātuka* and *ārdhadhātuka*; *ā to lopa iṭi ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-64) loss of the root's *ā*; in the nominative sg. *ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne* [?] *num* augment; loss of the final conjunct, being *asiddha*, *nalopa* does not occur; suffix accent: final *udātta*); *inaḥ* (root *iṇ gatau*; *iṇsiñjidīṅbhyaḥ kan* [?] (Uṇ. Sū. 3-[?]) *nak* suffix; no guṇa since *kit*; suffix accent: final *udātta*); *ā* (this particle, always seeking the verb, is joined [as *upasarga*] as there is no verb separately and no *kriyāpada* here; the verb *eti*, "comes", is to be supplied); *dhrajantam* (root *dhṛja gatau*; *śatṛ* in the sense of *laṭ*; *śap*; the *lasārvadhātuka anudātta*, so the root accent remains; accusative sg., *ugit*: *num*); *adrayaḥ* (root *adaṃ bhakṣaṇe*; *ādiśiṭibhūṣubhyaḥ kran* (Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]) *kran* suffix; *ñnityādir nityam* first *udātta*); *vidhan* (root *vidha vidhāne*, *tudādi*; present sense *luṅ* [*laṅ*] in *chandasi* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-6); 3rd plural *jhi* → *ant*; loss of *i*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* *luk* of the vikaraṇa; *bahulaṃ chandasy māṅyoge 'pi* no *aṭ* augment; after a *tiṅanta*, in Vedic, *nighāta* does not occur; or since *yat*… the word *yat*, as *tat* is a heard (*śrutavat*) word [?], *yaccha*-… the *nighāta* is not applied by the supplied *yo*…; suffix accent: first *udātta*). ‖ 1 ‖

### Printed p. 449  (PDF 467)

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स यो वृषा नरां न रोदस्योः श्रवोभिरस्ति जीवपीतसर्गः ।
> प्र यः सस्राणः शिश्रीत योनौ ॥ २ ॥

> *sa yo vṛṣā narāṃ na rodasyoḥ śravobhirasti jīvapītasargaḥ |*
> *pra yaḥ sasrāṇaḥ śiśrīta yonau ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । यः । वृषा । नराम् । न । रोदस्योः । श्रवःऽभिः । अस्ति । जीवऽपीतऽसर्गः ।
> प्र । यः । सस्राणः । शिश्रीत । योनौ ॥ २ ॥

> *saḥ | yaḥ | vṛṣā | narām | na | rodasyoḥ | śravaḥ 'bhiḥ | asti | jīva 'pīta 'sargaḥ |*
> *pra | yaḥ | sasrāṇaḥ | śiśrīta | yonau ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: Agni, the showerer, like the male of men and of heaven and earth, abides with his glories, the begetter whose creation is filled with living beings; he enters all wombs and produces all living creatures.)*

> स ताद्दृशो योऽग्निर्नरां न मनुष्याणामिव रोदस्योर्द्यावापृथिव्योरपि वृषा सेक्ता । उत्पादके इत्यर्थः । एवं सर्वोत्पादकः श्रवोभिः सर्वत्र श्रूयमाणैर्यशोभिर्युक्तः सन् अस्ति वर्तते । सर्वोत्पादके इत्युक्तं तत्रोपपत्तिमाह । यस्य जीवपीतसर्गः । जीवैः पीतः आस्वादितः सर्गः सृष्टिः । ... जीवानां पानार्थे ... पीतसर्गः जीवरसपीतसृष्टिः [?] ... प्रसृत्य [?] ... अयमग्निः स्वदेहं [?] हविर्द्रव्यादित्यादि प्राहुः [?] ... वृष्ट्याद्यर्थ [?] ... इदानीं साक्षादुत्पादकत्वमाह । योऽग्निर्योनौ गर्भाशये सस्राणः प्रविष्टः सन् शिश्रीत निषिक्तं रेतः पायोति [?] ... यद्वाग्निर्योनौ पर्जन्ये [?] ... तस्मादयं सर्वदेवोत्पादकः [?] ... महानुभावो वर्तते ॥ *[small type; many words doubtful]*

> *sa tāddṛśo yo 'gnirnarāṃ na manuṣyāṇāmiva rodasyordyāvāpṛthivyorapi vṛṣā sektā | utpādake ityarthaḥ | evaṃ sarvotpādakaḥ śravobhiḥ sarvatra śrūyamāṇairyaśobhiryuktaḥ san asti vartate | sarvotpādake ityuktaṃ tatropapattimāha | yasya jīvapītasargaḥ | jīvaiḥ pītaḥ āsvāditaḥ sargaḥ sṛṣṭiḥ | ... jīvānāṃ pānārthe ... pītasargaḥ jīvarasapītasṛṣṭiḥ [?] ... prasṛtya [?] ... ayamagniḥ svadehaṃ [?] havirdravyādityādi prāhuḥ [?] ... vṛṣṭyādyartha [?] ... idānīṃ sākṣādutpādakatvamāha | yo 'gniryonau garbhāśaye sasrāṇaḥ praviṣṭaḥ san śiśrīta niṣiktaṃ retaḥ pāyoti [?] ... yadvāgniryonau parjanye [?] ... tasmādayaṃ sarvadevotpādakaḥ [?] ... mahānubhāvo vartate ‖ *[small type; many words doubtful]**

### Printed p. 450  (PDF 468)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 149".)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *yaḥ* — which Agni; *narām na* — as in the case of men; *rodasyoḥ* — of heaven and earth, both; *vṛṣā* — the generator; *jīvapītasargaḥ* — whose creation, all of it, is filled with the essence of living beings (is the subject of the savour of living beings); *saḥ* — that Agni; *śravobhiḥ* — with famous glories; *asti* — grows exceedingly. *yaḥ* — which Agni; *yonau* — in (all) the wombs; *pra sasrāṇaḥ* — entering; *śiśrīte* — causes the seed to ripen (all) — makes the creatures spring forth. [Or: *yaḥ* — which Agni; *narāṃ na* — as to the sacrificers diligently engaged in the sacrifices, the giver of desired aims; *rodasyoḥ* — of heaven and earth, both; *vṛṣā* — the one who rains oblations and who showers on men; *saḥ* — such Agni; *jīvapītasargaḥ* — (the sacrifices that the sacrificer makes) all the sacrifices offered, of the others, together with serving the other creatures with his own power of feeding them; *śravobhiḥ* — with famous glories; *asti* — shines; *yaḥ* — which Agni; *yonau* — on his own place, the altar; *pra sasrāṇaḥ* — entering; *śiśrīte* — causes his own offered *purodāśa* and the like to be cooked.]

**Bhāvārtha.** Agni, who is the generator of men and of heaven and earth, shines with his famous glories, having made all creation filled with the essence of living beings; and entering all wombs, he makes all living creatures spring forth.

**English Translation (as printed).** He, who is, as it were, the generator of men as well as of heaven and earth, of whom creation has imbibed life, abides with his glories: he it is who, entering into the womb (of being), procreates (all living creatures).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** For this Ṛk two kinds of meaning are given. First, *vṛṣā* is explained as "generator", and *yonau* as "in the womb": Agni, who is the generator of heaven and earth as of men, filled the whole creation with the essence of living beings, and entering all wombs, procreates all living creatures. Second, *vṛṣā* is explained as "the sprinkler, one who showers desired aims", and *yonau* as "in his own place, the altar": the sense is that Agni, the giver of desired aims to the sacrificers engaged in the rites, who by oblations and showers [rain] pleases men, enters the place of the altar and cooks the *purodāśa* and the like offered to him — so Sāyaṇa has explained —

---

### Printed p. 451  (PDF 469)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 35 [?].)*

*(Special Topics, continued.)* that Agni who gives the desired aims to the sacrificers diligently engaged in the sacrifices, who by oblations rains upon heaven and earth and pleases the divine and human beings and the rest, is, in the place of his own, the altar, entering the *purodāśa* and the like and causing them to be cooked — thus a second meaning too is possible, says Sāyaṇa.

***vṛṣā*** — the word *vṛṣan* can have both the above meanings; and the uses of this word in the Ṛk-saṃhitā in many places, with examples, have been shown in the special topics of the Ṛk 1-[?]-[?] of this section.

***yonau*** — the word *yoni*, besides its sense of "place of birth", also has the meaning of "dwelling-place, house, and the like". It is read in the Nirukta among the names of water — *arṇaḥ*, *kṣodaḥ*, etc. (Ni. 1-[?]).

> ऋतस्य देवा अनु व्रता गुर्भुवत्पतिर्द्यौर्न भूम । वर्धन्तीमापः पन्वा सुशिश्विमृतस्य योना गर्भे सुजातम् ॥

> *ṛtasya devā anu vratā gurbhuvatpatirdyaurna bhūma | vardhantīmāpaḥ panvā suśiśvimṛtasya yonā garbhe sujātam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, "in the water, which is the cause of the sacrifice or of food"; and

> देवं वो देवयज्याग्निमीळीत मर्त्यः । समिद्धः शुक्र दीदिह्यृतस्य योनिमासदः सस्य योनिमासदः ॥

> *devaṃ vo devayajyāgnimīḷīta martyaḥ | samiddhaḥ śukra dīdihyṛtasya yonimāsadaḥ sasya yonimāsadaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, *yoni* means "cause", "means to heaven"; and

> दुरोकशोचिः क्रतुर्न नित्यो जायेव योनावरं विश्वस्मै । चित्रो यदभ्राट् छ्वेतो न विक्षु रथो न रुक्मी त्वेषः समत्सु ॥

> *durokaśociḥ kraturna nityo jāyeva yonāvaraṃ viśvasmai | citro yadabhrāṭ chveto na vikṣu ratho na rukmī tveṣaḥ samatsu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) in such Ṛks, "house"; and

> यमीं द्वा सवयसा सपर्यतः समाने योना मिथुना समोकसा । दिवा न नक्तं पलितो युवाजनि पुरू चरन्नजरो मानुषा युगा ॥

> *yamīṃ dvā savayasā saparyataḥ samāne yonā mithunā samokasā | divā na naktaṃ palito yuvājani purū carannajaro mānuṣā yugā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-144-4.) In such Ṛks it means "the place of origin of the fruit", and so on.
