### Printed p. 452  (PDF 470)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 149".)*

> वेदिषदे प्रियधामाय सुद्युते धासिमिव प्र भरा योनिमग्नये । वस्त्रेणेव वासया मन्मना शुचिं ज्योतीरथं शुक्रवर्णं तमोहनम् ॥

> *vediṣade priyadhāmāya sudyute dhāsimiva pra bharā yonimagnaye | vastreṇeva vāsayā manmanā śuciṃ jyotīrathaṃ śukravarṇaṃ tamohanam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-140-1.) In such Ṛks *vedyāśryaṃ sthānaṃ* ("the place resting on the altar") — "the place that is of the form of the altar" — have many senses; therefore in the Ṛk at hand the sense of "the place of origin" or "the sacrificial altar" can be given.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly).** *vṛṣā* (root *vṛṣu secane*; *kasin* after *yuvṛṣi…* (Uṇ. Sū. 1-[?]) *kasin* suffix; being *nit*, first *udātta*); *śravobhiḥ* (root *śru śravaṇe*; *asun* suffix; word *śravas*; *nit*: first *udātta*; instr. plural); *asti* (root *as bhuvi*; *laṭ* 3rd sg.; owing to *yat*, no *nighāta*; the root accent remains); *jīvapītasargaḥ* (*jīvaiḥ pītaḥ jīvapītaḥ*; *jīvapīte sargo yasya saḥ jīvapītasargaḥ*; the root in the passive, *niṣṭhā* suffix *kta*; *ghumāsthāgā…* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-66) *ī* for the root; in the first member the natural accent; as a bahuvrīhi, *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the first-member accent remains); *sasrāṇaḥ* (root *sṛ gatau*; *liṭaḥ kānajvā* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-106) *liṭ* → *kānac*; doubling of the root; *urat* for the reduplicate; *ādivat* [?]; since the suffix is *kit* guṇa does not occur; *aṭkupvāṅ…* *ṇatva* of the suffix *n*; *cit*: final *udātta*); *śiśrīte* (root *śrā pāke*; *laṭ* 3rd sg.; *śluḥ* vikaraṇa in *chandasi*; *śnābhyastayor ātaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-112) loss of the root's *ā*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* *itva* for the reduplicate; because *yat* is connected, no *nighāta*; suffix accent: final *udātta*). ‖ 2 ‖

### Printed p. 453  (PDF 471)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 35 [?].)*

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> आ यः पुरं नार्मिणीमदीदेदत्यः कविर्नभन्योनार्वा ।
> सूरो न रुरुक्वाञ्छतात्मा ॥ ३ ॥

> *ā yaḥ puraṃ nārmiṇīmadīdedatyaḥ kavirnabhanyonārvā |*
> *sūro na rurukvāñchatātmā ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आ । यः । पुरम् । नार्मिणीम् । अदीदेत् । अत्यः । कविः । नभन्यः । न । अर्वा ।
> सूरः । न । रुरुक्वान् । शतऽआत्मा ॥ ३ ॥

> *ā | yaḥ | puram | nārmiṇīm | adīdet | atyaḥ | kaviḥ | nabhanyaḥ | na | arvā |*
> *sūraḥ | na | rurukvān | śata 'ātmā ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: Agni, the wanderer, wise, like a swift sky-wind, has lit up the delightful place [the altar]; many-formed, he shines like the sun.)*

> योऽग्निर्नार्मिणीं नर्मवतीं यजमानानां सम्बन्धिनीमुत्तरवेदिं । यद्वा । नृणां मनसि स्थितां यजमानानां यज्ञार्थं यां भूमिं प्रत्यग्न्यागमनमनीषया विद्यते तां । पुरं तत्र्यनामादीदेत् [?] दीपयति । कीदृशोऽयं । अत्यः अत्यतनशीलः कविः क्रान्तदर्शी । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । अर्वा रणकुशलो नभन्योः न नभस्याकाशे भवो नभस्यो नाभ्यायोरिव । किञ्च शतात्मा शतं सहस्रमित्यपरिमितवचनः । तत्रेदृजमानगृहेक्षयेऽआहवनीयगार्हपत्यादिनाना रूपात्मकः । अथवा मित्रावरुणाद्यनेकदेवतात्मकः । यद्वा शतसंख्याकात्मवान् [?] ... स सूरो नेव सूर्य इव रुरुक्वान् दीप्यमानः । रुच दीप्तौ । छान्दसः क्वसुः ॥ अतः स शतात्मा अग्निरस्ति उत्कृष्टं वर्तते इति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥ *[small type; many words doubtful]*

> *yo 'gnirnārmiṇīṃ narmavatīṃ yajamānānāṃ sambandhinīmuttaravediṃ | yadvā | nṛṇāṃ manasi sthitāṃ yajamānānāṃ yajñārthaṃ yāṃ bhūmiṃ pratyagnyāgamanamanīṣayā vidyate tāṃ | puraṃ tatryanāmādīdet [?] dīpayati | kīdṛśo 'yaṃ | atyaḥ atyatanaśīlaḥ kaviḥ krāntadarśī | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | arvā raṇakuśalo nabhanyoḥ na nabhasyākāśe bhavo nabhasyo nābhyāyoriva | kiñca śatātmā śataṃ sahasramityaparimitavacanaḥ | tatredṛjamānagṛhekṣaye 'āhavanīyagārhapatyādinānā rūpātmakaḥ | athavā mitrāvaruṇādyanekadevatātmakaḥ | yadvā śatasaṃkhyākātmavān [?] ... sa sūro neva sūrya iva rurukvān dīpyamānaḥ | ruca dīptau | chāndasaḥ kvasuḥ ‖ ataḥ sa śatātmā agnirasti utkṛṣṭaṃ vartate iti pūrvatrānvayaḥ ‖ *[small type; many words doubtful]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *atyaḥ* — one who goes (in the place bound for the sacrifice); *kaviḥ* — the wise one; *yaḥ* — which Agni; *nārmiṇīm puram* — the delightful, the Uttaravedi; or (that which the sacrificers have in mind and have desired for the sacrifice) the place; *arvā* — one who moves about (by his nature); *nabhanyaḥ na* — like the wind that moves in the sky; *ā adīdet* — shines in a special way; *śatātmā* — (and) having a hundred bodies — with many forms, as Āhavanīya, Gārhapatya and so on — Agni; *sūraḥ na* — like the sun; *rurukvān* — shines.

### Printed p. 454  (PDF 472)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 149".)*

**Bhāvārtha.** Agni, who moves of his own will, wise, brightens the delightful altar-place, which gives joy, specially, like the wind that moves in the sky. And Agni, having many forms, shines like the sun.

**English Translation (as printed).** He who is wise, and goes (wheresoever he will), like the rapid ethereal ( wind ), has lighted up the delightful spot, (the altar), and, identical with many forms, is radiant as the sun.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***nārmiṇīm*** — it is somewhat difficult to give the meaning of this word. Even Sāyaṇa has given non-obvious meanings. First, *narmavatīṃ yajamānānāṃ sambandhinīm uttaravedim*: "possessed of delight, belonging to the sacrificers: the Uttaravedi", i.e. "the Uttaravedi that gives joy"; and then *nṛṇāṃ manasi sthitāṃ yajamānānāṃ yajñārthaṃ yāṃ bhūmiṃ prati agnyāgamanamanīṣayā vidyate tāṃ* — "the place which, as the sacrificers think, will be, for the sake of the sacrifice, the place of Agni's arrival" — as the sacrificial ground that he comes to; to the wish in the mind of the sacrificer "let Agni come here" — thus explained [partly unclear]; of the two, *nārmiṇī* means *narmavatī*, i.e. "(the delightful)", or "that which is set in the mind of men (*nṛṇāṃ manasi sthitā*)"; this word is made an adjective of *puram*; the sense is "the place called the Uttaravedi".

Monier Williams, in his Sanskrit-English Dictionary, gives for this word "*na* + *ārman*" (a negative, *ārman* = a town; "a *pura* that is not a *ārmaṇa*, i.e. loose, *śithila*), "*Name of a Town*" — he conjectures a town's name; the *nāra* [sic] "*pāṭaliputra*"; in Pāṇini, *dattarma*, *guptarma*, *bṛhadarma* are words [of the kind]. For *nārmiṇī* no proper meaning is given in Pāṇini or the Nirukta; so, of the two meanings given by Sāyaṇa, one should be accepted.

***atyaḥ*** — *āsekṣitadeśaṃ prati atanaśīlaḥ*: "one who is wont to go to the place he desires" — an adjective of Agni; in general the word is an adjective of horses and the like, which are ever on the move:

> एष प्र पूर्वीरव तस्य चम्रिषोऽत्यो न योषामुदयंस्त भुवनेः । दक्षं महे पाययते हिरण्ययं रथमावृत्या हरियोगमृभ्वसम् ॥

> *eṣa pra pūrvīrava tasya camriṣo 'tyo na yoṣāmudayaṃsta bhuvaneḥ | dakṣaṃ mahe pāyayate hiraṇyayaṃ rathamāvṛtyā hariyogamṛbhvasam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].)

### Printed p. 455  (PDF 473)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 35 [?].)*

> अस्य श्लोको दिवीयते पृथिव्यामत्यो न यंसद्यक्षभृद्विचेताः । मृगाणां न हेतयो यन्ति चेमा बृहस्पतेरहिमायाँ अभि द्यून् ॥

> *asya śloko divīyate pṛthivyāmatyo na yaṃsadyakṣabhṛdvicetāḥ | mṛgāṇāṃ na hetayo yanti cemā bṛhaspaterahimāyā~ abhi dyūn ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, *atyaḥ* is used as a synonym of "horse"; in other places the word gives the sense "one who goes always" — Āditya, thus:

***nabhanyaḥ*** — *nabhasi ākāśe bhavo nabhasyaḥ vāyur iva*: "born in the sky; like the wind"; an adjective of the wind, called *nabhasya*, because it is "of the sky". The Nirukta author puts the word *nabhati* among the names of killing-actions: *nabhati*, *ardati* (Ni. 2-[?]); according to this Sāyaṇa takes *nabhanya* from the sense of killing — here and elsewhere:

> गायेत्सामा नभन्यं यथा वेरर्चाम तद्वृन्यासानः स्वर्वतः [?] । गावो धेनवो बर्हिष्यदन्वा आ यत्कश्यानां दिव्यं विवासन् ॥

> *gāyetsāmā nabhanyaṃ yathā verarcāma tadvṛnyāsānaḥ svarvataḥ [?] | gāvo dhenavo barhiṣyadanvā ā yatkaśyānāṃ divyaṃ vivāsan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk the word *nabhanya* he explains as *nabhasyaṃ nabhasi bhavanam* ("existing in the sky"), "*nabhonyaṃ himsakaṃ vā rākṣasādikasya*" — "a destroyer of Rākṣasas and the like"; and:

> प्र ब्रह्माणो अङ्गिरसो नक्षन्त प्र क्रन्दनुर्नभन्यस्य वेतु । प्र धेनव उदप्रुतो नमन्त युज्यतामद्री अध्वरस्य शेषः ॥

> *pra brahmāṇo aṅgiraso nakṣanta pra krandanurnabhanyasya vetu | pra dhenava udapruto namanta yujyatāmadrī adhvarasya śeṣaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, *nabhanyasya* he explains as *asmadīyaṃ stotram*, "our hymn, [of him who has?] the sky-birth".

***arvā*** — *araṇakuśalaḥ* ("skilled in the field") — "one who moves swiftly, quickly"; in the sense of the horse, "*arvā*" as an adjective of the wind. In general, the *-t*-ending and *-n*-ending words *arvat*, *arvan* are synonyms of horse; in some places they have also the sense of "enemy". The Nirukta author puts *atyaḥ*, *hayaḥ*, *arvā* among the names of horses (Ni. [?]); in the Ṛk-saṃhitā both words *arvat* and *arvan* have their uses.

> यस्मै त्वमायजसे स साधत्यनर्वा क्षेति दधते सुवीर्यम् । स तोत नैनमश्नोत्यंहतिरग्ने सख्ये मा रिषामा वयं तव ॥

> *yasmai tvamāyajase sa sādhatyanarvā kṣeti dadhate suvīryam | sa tota nainamaśnotyaṃhatiragne sakhye mā riṣāmā vayaṃ tava ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, *anarvān* is explained as "without enemies" (*aśatru*); in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā:

> अनर्वा प्रेहीत्याह भ्रातृव्येभ्यो वा अर्वा भ्रातृव्यमेवासुत्ते श्रीः ॥ [?]

> *anarvā prehītyāha bhrātṛvyebhyo vā arvā bhrātṛvyamevāsutte śrīḥ ‖ [?]*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?]) —

### Printed p. 456  (PDF 474)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 149".)*

— citing this sentence of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (*bhāṣya* of the Ṛk 1-[?]-[?]), after showing that *arvan* has in such passages the meaning "enemy" (*bhrātṛvya*), it is shown that in the Ṛks too this meaning has been given: in many other places Sāyaṇa's explanation shows "enemy". In the derivation of this word, Wilson and Max Müller state different opinions; on the occasion one may not blame either. Wilson —

> श्रीलं वः शर्धो मारुतमनर्वाणं रथेशुभम् । कण्वा अभि प्र गायत ॥

> *śrīlaṃ vaḥ śardho mārutamanarvāṇaṃ ratheśubham | kaṇvā abhi pra gāyata ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-37-1.) In explaining the word *anarvāṇam* in this Ṛk, the scholar comments on Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya thus:

*(English, as printed:)* The phrase is *anarvāṇam* which the scholiast explains *bhrātṛvyarahitam* (*sic*, with the Devanagari). Literally without a brother's son, which would be a very unintelligible epithet. Arvan is in its usual acceptation a horse ; and being without horses would not be inapplicable to the Maruts whose chariot is drawn by deer. *bhrātṛvya* may mean an enemy, but it is doubtful if *arvat* can admit of such an interpretation.

(Rig-Veda Translation. Vol. 1 P. 258)

[The Kannada text remarks:] Since the Maruts' vehicle is deer, the explanation "without horses" cannot be improper — thus the scholar thinks; but against this, when interpreting this same sūkta, Max Müller says the word *anarvan* cannot mean "without horses"; that is the remark:

*(English, as printed:)* Wilson translates *anarvāṇam* by without horses, though the commentator distinctly explains the word by without an enemy. Wilson considers it doubtful whether *arvan* can ever mean enemy. The fact is, that in the Rig-Veda *an-arvan* never means without horses but always without hurt or free from enemies, and the commentator is perfectly right, as sense is concerned, rendering the word by *apratiprahata* [?] ('without an enemy or unopposed'). (*aśatrukṛtam* [?])

(Sacred Books of the East. Vol. 32. P. 65)

Even so, the use of the word *arvan* as a synonym of horse is the more frequent; in the Ṛk at hand, to show that the word is used also as an adjective of the wind, it is made an adjective of the *vāyu*.

### Printed p. 457  (PDF 475)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 36 [?].)*

***śatātmā*** — in explaining the Ṛk 1-[?]-[?] of this section, the word *viśvāpsu* showed that the Agni has many kinds of forms; in the Ṛk at hand also, with the adjective *śatātmā* the greatness of Agni is shown. *śataṃ sahasram ity aparimitavacanaḥ*: "*śata*, a thousand — this is the word for the unlimited"; *tattaddyajamāna gṛhāpekṣayā āhavanīya-gārhapatyādyapekṣayā vā nānārūpātmaḥ*: "of many forms according to the houses of the respective sacrificers, or according to the Āhavanīya, Gārhapatya and so on". The word *śata* here does not mean a hundred only: it indicates an unlimited number. The various forms of the fire, like the southern fire, Āhavanīya, Gārhapatya, in the houses of the sacrificers, serve each according to the rites, so this adjective is applied. Or:

> इन्द्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमाहुरथो दिव्यः स सुपर्णो गरुत्मान् । एकं सद्विप्रा बहुधा वदन्त्यग्निं यमं मातरिश्वानमाहुः ॥

> *indraṃ mitraṃ varuṇamagnimāhuratho divyaḥ sa suparṇo garutmān | ekaṃ sadviprā bahudhā vadantyagniṃ yamaṃ mātariśvānamāhuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-46.)

> त्वमग्ने वरुणो जायसे यत्त्वं मित्रो भवसि यत्समिद्धः । त्वे विश्वे सहसस्पुत्र देवास्त्वमिन्द्रो दाशुषे मर्त्याय ॥

> *tvamagne varuṇo jāyase yattvaṃ mitro bhavasi yatsamiddhaḥ | tve viśve sahasasputra devāstvamindro dāśuṣe martyāya ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-1.) In such Ṛks, and also in

> त्वमग्ने रुद्रो असुरो महो दिवस्त्वं शर्धो मारुतं पृक्ष ईशिषे । त्वं वातैररुणैर्यासि शंगयस्त्वं पूषा विधतः पासि नु त्मना ॥

> *tvamagne rudro asuro maho divastvaṃ śardho mārutaṃ pṛkṣa īśiṣe | tvaṃ vātairaruṇairyāsi śaṃgayastvaṃ pūṣā vidhataḥ pāsi nu tmanā ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?].) and so on in the sentences of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā too, Agni is described as being the all-formed (*viśvātmaka*), hence here he is praised as *śatātmā*.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar page, noted briefly).** *nārmiṇīm* (*yuṇeḥ…* [?] (Pā. Sū. 4-1-[?]) *ṅīp*, *ñīp* in the feminine; *ṅīp* being *pit*, *anudātta*; accusative sg.); *adīdet* (*dīdi* is Vedic root; used in the sense of *dīpti*, "lustre"; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-6) *laṅ* in the present sense; by *chandasi* the *śap* *luk*; the suffix being *nit* [?] guṇa; augment *aṭ*; owing to *yat* [connected], no *nighāta*); *atyaḥ* (*atati iti atyaḥ*, root *ata sātatyagamane* [as printed: *āṅ*]…, the form *aty*, "*atyaḥ*" is Vedic: *ata* + *yat*, *ac* [?], the root-sense *vega-sāmya* "equality of speed" [?]; "*atyaḥ*" (Nir. 1-[?]) "horse", as the swift one — and here used for a wise one, a poet [*kavi*]).

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अभि द्विजन्मा त्री रोचनानि विश्वा रजांसि शुशुचानो अस्थात् ।
> होता यजिष्ठो अपां सधस्थे ॥ ४ ॥

> *abhi dvijanmā trī rocanāni viśvā rajāṃsi śuśucāno asthāt |*
> *hotā yajiṣṭho apāṃ sadhasthe ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अभि । द्विऽजन्मा । त्री । रोचनानि । विश्वा । रजांसि । शुशुचानः । अस्थात् ।
> होता । यजिष्ठः । अपाम् । सधऽस्थे ॥ ४ ॥

> *abhi | dvi 'janmā | trī | rocanāni | viśvā | rajāṃsi | śuśucānaḥ | asthāt |*
> *hotā | yajiṣṭhaḥ | apām | sadha 'sthe ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: the twice-born Agni stands shining over the three luminous worlds and all spaces; the invoker, best of sacrificers, in the gathering-place of the waters.)*

> अयमग्निर्द्विजन्मा द्वाभ्यामरणिभ्यां जायमानः । यद्वा । मथनात्प्रथमं जन्म । उत्पत्त्यनन्तरं पावमानेष्ट्याहि [?]संस्काररूपं द्वितीयं जन्मेव । एवं द्विजन्मत्वम् । अथवा द्यावापृथिवीभ्यामुत्पन्नत्वात् । तादृशोऽग्निः त्री रोचनानि त्रीणि [?] रोचनानि त्रीन् दिशः [?] ... गार्हपत्यादीनि वा भाभिः शुशुचानोऽभितः प्रकाशयन् । न केवलं त्रीन्येव किन्तु विश्वा रजांसि सर्वाण्यपि रञ्जनात्मकानि क्षित्यादिलोकान् शुशुचानोऽभितः प्रकाशयन् दीपयन् होता देवानामाह्वाता यजिष्ठो यष्टृतमः सन्नपाम् प्रोक्षणाद्युदकानां सदस्थे सहस्थाने यागदेशे अस्थात् तिष्ठति ॥ *[small type; partly legible]*

> *ayamagnirdvijanmā dvābhyāmaraṇibhyāṃ jāyamānaḥ | yadvā | mathanātprathamaṃ janma | utpattyanantaraṃ pāvamāneṣṭyāhi [?]saṃskārarūpaṃ dvitīyaṃ janmeva | evaṃ dvijanmatvam | athavā dyāvāpṛthivībhyāmutpannatvāt | tādṛśo 'gniḥ trī rocanāni trīṇi [?] rocanāni trīn diśaḥ [?] ... gārhapatyādīni vā bhābhiḥ śuśucāno 'bhitaḥ prakāśayan | na kevalaṃ trīnyeva kintu viśvā rajāṃsi sarvāṇyapi rañjanātmakāni kṣityādilokān śuśucāno 'bhitaḥ prakāśayan dīpayan hotā devānāmāhvātā yajiṣṭho yaṣṭṛtamaḥ sannapām prokṣaṇādyudakānāṃ sadasthe sahasthāne yāgadeśe asthāt tiṣṭhati ‖ *[small type; partly legible]**

### Printed p. 459  (PDF 477)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 36 [?].)*

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *dvijanmā* — Agni who has two kinds of birth; *trī rocanāni* — the three shining realms; *viśvā rajāṃsi* — all regions made of colour (the worlds, all around); *abhi śuśucānaḥ* — shining all around; *hotā* — the invoker of the gods to the sacrifice; *yajiṣṭhaḥ* — the most excellent sacrificer; *apām sadhasthe* — in the place of sacrifice where the waters of sprinkling and the like are collected; *asthāt* — has taken his place.

**Bhāvārtha.** Agni, who has two kinds of birth, makes all the shining worlds and regions of colour shine all around; as the invoker of the gods to the sacrifice, the best of sacrificers, he has taken his stand in the place of sacrifice where the waters of sprinkling and the like are collected.

**English Translation (as printed).** He, the twofold-born, illuminating the three bright (regions), and shining over all the lustrous spheres, the adorable invoker of the gods, is present at the place where the waters are collected.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***dvijanmā*** — *dvābhyām araṇibhyām jāyamānaḥ*; *yadvā mathanena ādhānasaṃskārena ca utpannatvāt dvijanmatvam*, *athavā dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ jāyamānaḥ araṇyor vā jāyamānaḥ* — "born from two fire-sticks; or twice-born because produced by churning and then by the consecration of establishment; or born of heaven and earth, or from the two fire-sticks": thus the manner of Agni's origin is described in the section of the Ṛk 1-[?]-[?] of this part; see there.

***trī rocanāni*** — here *rocana* is taken as "the lustrous sphere". Agni has three luminous places of his own — earth, atmosphere and heaven; or the Gārhapatya, Āhavanīya and Dakṣiṇāgni, Sāyaṇa has explained. *Trimūrdhānam* in the Ṛk 1-[?]-[?] of the same section has also suggested this subject; and:

> त्रीणि जाना परि भूषन्त्यस्य समुद्र एकं दिव्येकमप्सु । पूर्वामनु प्र दिशं पार्थिवानामृतून्प्रशासद्वि दधावनुष्ठु ॥

> *trīṇi jānā pari bhūṣantyasya samudra ekaṃ divyekamapsu | pūrvāmanu pra diśaṃ pārthivānāmṛtūnpraśāsadvi dadhāvanuṣṭhu ‖*

(Yaj. Saṃ. [?]-[?].) In the special topics of this Ṛk too (in the Ṛg-Veda Saṃhitā part, page [?] onward) this subject has been explained.

### Printed p. 460  (PDF 478)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 149".)*

***rajāṃsi*** — *sarvāṇy api rañjanātmakān kṣityādilokān śuśucānaḥ*: "shining on all the worlds of the earth and the rest, which are of the nature of being coloured"; the Kannada: "the worlds of the earth and the rest which draw the mind"; the word *rajas*, in the sense of "world", "water" and so on, its uses with examples are shown in the special topics of the Ṛk 1-[?]-[?] of this section.

***apāṃ sadhasthe*** — *sahasthāne* (Ni. 4-[?]): "in the place where all come together", i.e. "in the house, in the dwelling [?]". Or *saha tiṣṭhanti yasmin devatāḥ sa sadhasthaḥ yajñaḥ* — "that in which the deities stay together is a *sadhastha*, the sacrifice". *apāṃ sadhasthe* means "in the place of sacrifice, where waters are collected, as for sprinkling, consecrating, etc." — since the place of sacrifice is in the nature of purifying waters, the sacrificial ground has the name *apāṃ sadhastha*; "in the sacrificial ground" is the sense. And:

> इमं विधन्तो अपां सधस्थे द्विता दधुर्भृगवो विक्ष्वप्स्वा । एषं विश्वान्यभ्यस्तु भूमा देवानामग्निररतिर्जीरराश्वः ॥

> *imaṃ vidhanto apāṃ sadhasthe dvitā dadhurbhṛgavo vikṣvapsvā | eṣaṃ viśvānyabhyastu bhūmā devānāmagniraratirjīrarāśvaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks, *apāṃ sadhasthe* means "in the atmosphere"; "in the atmosphere, which is the house-form of the lightning and the fire".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4; grammar page, noted briefly).** *dvijanmā* (*dve janmanī yasya saḥ dvijanmā*; *pāradiśchandasi bahulam* [?] (Pā. Sū. 6-2-[?]) the later-member first *udātta*); *rocanāni* (root *ruca dīptau*; *anudāttetaś ca halādeḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-149) *yuc* suffix; *yuvor anākau* *ana*; *cit*: final *udātta*); *viśvā* (*viśvāni*; *śeṣaṃ chandasi bahulam* loss of *i* of *śi*); *śuśucānaḥ* (root *śuca dīptau*; in Vedic *liṭ*; *liṭaḥ kānajvā* *kānac*; doubling of the root; *cit* — final *udātta*); *asthāt* (root *ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* present sense *luṅ*; 3rd sg. *tip*; loss of *i* by *itaś ca*; *cli* → *sic*, *gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ…* (Pā. Sū. 2-4-77) *luk* of it; augment *aṭ* to the stem; *tiṅ*-*nighāta*); *yajiṣṭhaḥ* (root *yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu*; agent *tṛc*; *atiśayena yaṣṭā yajiṣṭhaḥ*; *tuśchandasi* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-59) *iṣṭhan*; *teriḍi* loss of *tṛc*'s *ti*; suffix is *nit*, so first *udātta*); *apām* (*ūḍidaṃpadādi* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) case-ending *udātta*); *sadhasthe* (root *ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*; *supi sthaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-4) *ka*; *sadhamādasthayoś chandasi* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-96) *sadha* for *saha*; *ā to lopa iṭi ca* loss of the root's *ā*). ‖ 4 ‖

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अयं स होता यो द्विजन्मा विश्वा दधे वार्याणि श्रवस्या ।
> मर्तो यो अस्मै सुतुको ददाश ॥ ५ ॥

> *ayaṃ sa hotā yo dvijanmā viśvā dadhe vāryāṇi śravasyā |*
> *marto yo asmai sutuko dadāśa ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अयम् । सः । होता । यः । द्विऽजन्मा । विश्वा । दधे । वार्याणि । श्रवस्या ।
> मर्तः । यः । अस्मै । सुऽतुकः । ददाश ॥ ५ ॥

> *ayam | saḥ | hotā | yaḥ | dvi 'janmā | viśvā | dadhe | vāryāṇi | śravasyā |*
> *martaḥ | yaḥ | asmai | su 'tukaḥ | dadāśa ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: this is the invoker, the twice-born, who holds all desirable riches through desire for food; the mortal who gives him oblations has excellent offspring.)*

> यो द्विजन्मा स एव होता होमनिष्पादकः । अरणिभ्यामुत्पन्नस्यैव गार्हपत्यादिरूपाहवनीयत्वात् [?] आह्वाता वा देवानां सोऽयं विश्वा विश्वानि वार्याणि वरणीयानि [?] ॥ ईडेदन्ते वृत्र... सुषामादिः [?] इत्यादिनोदात्तत्वम् ॥ श्रवस्या श्रवस्यया श्रोत्रेन्नं हविर्लक्षणम् [?] तदिच्छया ॥ श्रवःशब्दात् क्यजन्तात् आ प्रत्ययाद्यतीति [?] भावे अप्रत्ययः ॥ दधे धारयति । अस्मा उक्तस्वरूपायाग्नये यो मर्त्यो ददाश ददाति स सुतुकः शोभनपुत्रो भवति ॥ *[small type; partly legible]*

> *yo dvijanmā sa eva hotā homaniṣpādakaḥ | araṇibhyāmutpannasyaiva gārhapatyādirūpāhavanīyatvāt [?] āhvātā vā devānāṃ so 'yaṃ viśvā viśvāni vāryāṇi varaṇīyāni [?] ‖ īḍedante vṛtra... suṣāmādiḥ [?] ityādinodāttatvam ‖ śravasyā śravasyayā śrotrennaṃ havirlakṣaṇam [?] tadicchayā ‖ śravaḥśabdāt kyajantāt ā pratyayādyatīti [?] bhāve apratyayaḥ ‖ dadhe dhārayati | asmā uktasvarūpāyāgnaye yo martyo dadāśa dadāti sa sutukaḥ śobhanaputro bhavati ‖ *[small type; partly legible]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *yaḥ* — which Agni; *dvijanmā* — born in two ways; *saḥ* — that; *hotā* — the accomplisher of the *homa* or the invoker of the gods to the sacrifice; *ayam* — this Agni; [continues on p. 462]

### Printed p. 462  (PDF 480)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 149".)*

*(Pratipadārtha continued.)* *śravasyā* — desiring the oblation in the form of food; *viśvā* — all; *vāryāṇi* — most desirable [?] riches; *dadhe* — holds; *asmai* — to this Agni; *yaḥ martaḥ* — which mortal; *dadāśa* — offers (oblations); *sutukaḥ* — will be the father of children of excellent worth.

**Bhāvārtha.** The Agni who has two kinds of birth is the accomplisher of the *homa*; this Agni, desiring oblation in the form of food, holds all excellent riches that are desirable. The mortal who offers oblations to this Agni becomes the father of sons of excellent worth.

**English Translation (as printed).** He is the offerer of oblations, who is of twofold birth; and, through desire for (sacrificial) food, has in his keeping all good things: the man who presents offerings to him is the parent of excellent offspring.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***sutukaḥ*** — *śobhanaputraḥ*, "one having excellent children" — the owner of excellent progeny [thus Sāyaṇa]. The word *toka* has been explained in the special topics of the Ṛk 1-[?]-[?] of this part: "children of worth, descendants". The Nirukta author:

> स आ वक्षि महि न आ च सत्सि दिवस्पृथिव्योररतिर्युवत्योः । अग्निः सुतुकः सुतुकेभिरश्वै रभस्वद्भी रभस्वाँ एह गम्याः ॥

> *sa ā vakṣi mahi na ā ca satsi divaspṛthivyoraratiryuvatyoḥ | agniḥ sutukaḥ sutukebhiraśvai rabhasvadbhī rabhasvā~ eha gamyāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) Citing this Ṛk, he explains here the word *sutuka*: *sutukaḥ sutūrī* [?] *nirīti vā* / *supraja supraja[?]* — "*sutuk* is one who has [good] offspring"; or: (Ni. 4-[?]). From the root *tuk*, in the sense of going, the word *sutuka* is derived — "one who has splendid motion, a good mover". In the Ṛk here quoted it is said, as the epithet of Agni, "one who has splendid-going horses", or *sutukaḥ* "one having splendid births, one of excellent origin" — thus Sāyaṇa; two senses are possible. Sāyaṇa, however, explains *tuk* here as *tukkṛtyārthaḥ* [?]: "one who is *sugamaḥ*, *stotṛbhir yajñaiś ca sukhena prāpyaḥ*": "easily reached by praisers and by sacrifices", i.e. "by those who praise with hymns, he can be pleasantly approached":

> न घा राजेन्द्र आ दभन्नो या नु स्वसारा कृणवन्त योनौ । आपश्चिदस्मै सुतुका अवेषन्गमन्न इन्द्रः सख्या वयश्च ॥

> *na ghā rājendra ā dabhanno yā nu svasārā kṛṇavanta yonau | āpaścidasmai sutukā aveṣangamanna indraḥ sakhyā vayaśca ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].)

---

### Printed p. 463  (PDF 481)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 36 [?].)*

In this Ṛk, *sutukāḥ* is explained as *śobhanabalahetūni*, "being the cause of good strength": the oblations which are causes of excellent strength; and:

> आ संयमिन्द्र णः स्वस्तिं शत्रुतूर्याय बृहतीममृध्राम् । यया दासान्यार्याणि वृत्रा करो वज्रिन्त्सुतुका नाहुषाणि ॥

> *ā saṃyamindra ṇaḥ svastiṃ śatrutūryāya bṛhatīmamṛdhrām | yayā dāsānyāryāṇi vṛtrā karo vajrintsutukā nāhuṣāṇi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, *sutukāni* means *śobhanahiṃsopetāni*, "[armies] with good capacity for killing": an adjective of the enemies' [hosts] — "may they be made capable of being slain" — thus the epithet of foes.

In the situation described in the Ṛk at hand, the sense is "that mortal, the sacrificer, who offers oblations to Agni, becomes *sutuka*, one with excellent sons and grandsons" — this meaning is the fit one.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar page, noted briefly).** *dadhe* (root *dudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* *liṭ*; 3rd sg.; owing to *yat* [connected], no *nighāta*; suffix accent: final *udātta*); *vāryāṇi* (root *vṛñ varaṇe*; *ṇyat* suffix by *ṛhalor ṇyat* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-124); *ac ṇṇiti* *vṛddhi*; *ūḍidaṃpadādi*…; first *udātta* by *ṇyat* accent); *śravasyā* (*śravasyati* → *śravasyā*; *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-8) *kyac*; *apratyayāt* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-102) *a* suffix after *kyajanta*; *ajādyataṣ ṭāp* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-4) *ṭāp*; *supāṃ sulug* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) *ā* for the instrumental ending; from the *kyac* accent final *udātta*); *martaḥ* (root *mṛṅ prāṇatyāge*; *asihasimṛ…* (Uṇ. Sū. 3-86) *tan* suffix; on account of the suffix, guṇa of the *ṛ*; because of *nit*, first *udātta*); *sutukaḥ* (*śobhanaṃ tokaṃ yasya saḥ sutukaḥ*; by Vedic *u*-substitution; *dvaitoḥ-…-sṛjiḥ* [?] (Pā. Sū. 6-2-[?]) later-member first *udātta*); *dadāśa* (root *dāś dāne*; in Vedic *liṭ* 3rd sg.; no *nighāta* owing to *yat*; *liti* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) *udātta* before the suffix). ‖ 5 ‖

## Sūkta 150

### Printed p. 464  (PDF 482)

*(The Kannada heading reads "The 150th Sūkta"; page header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 150".)*

*(Anukramaṇī, Sanskrit; not rendered in English. Gist: the sūkta of three Ṛks beginning "Puru tvā" is the tenth sūkta, of Dīrghatamas, Agni deity, Uṣṇih metre; its use at the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra, for the Uṣṇih Ṛks, is given by the Āśvalāyana sūtra "puru tvā tvām agne".)*

> पुरु त्वेति तृचात्मकं दशमं सूक्तं दैर्घतमसमाग्नेयमौष्णिहम् । पुरु तृचमौष्णिहमित्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोरौष्णिहे छन्दस्यस्य सूक्तस्य विनियोगः । अथैतस्या इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । पुरु त्वा त्वामग्न इति । आ. [?] इति ॥

> *puru tveti tṛcātmakaṃ daśamaṃ sūktaṃ dairghatamasamāgneyamauṣṇiham | puru tṛcamauṣṇihamityanukramaṇikā ‖ prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayorauṣṇihe chandasyasya sūktasya viniyogaḥ | athaitasyā iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | puru tvā tvāmagna iti | ā. [?] iti ‖*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta *puru tvā* is the tenth sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has three Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Agni is the deity. The metre is Uṣṇih. In the Anukramaṇī it is said *puru tṛcam auṣṇiham*. For the Prātaranuvāka and Āśvina-śastra mantra recitals the use of this sūkta, for the Ṛks in Uṣṇih metre, is explained by the sūtra *puru tvā tvām agne* in the section *athaitasyā* of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra.

**॥ ओम् ॥**

**Sūkta 150** — Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 21, Sūkta 150; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 37 [?]. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 3. Ṛṣi: Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Devatā: Agni. Chandas: Uṣṇih.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> पुरु त्वा दाश्वान्वोचेऽरिरग्ने तव स्विदा ।
> तोदस्येव शरण आ महस्य ॥ १ ॥

> *puru tvā dāśvānvoce 'riragne tava svidā |*
> *todasyeva śaraṇa ā mahasya ‖ 1 ‖*

---

### Printed p. 465  (PDF 483)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 37 [?].)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> पुरु । त्वा । दाश्वान् । वोचे । अरिः । अग्ने । तव । स्वित् । आ ।
> तोदस्यऽइव । शरणे । आ । महस्य ॥ १ ॥

> *puru | tvā | dāśvān | voce | ariḥ | agne | tava | svit | ā |*
> *todasya 'iva | śaraṇe | ā | mahasya ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: I, who have given many oblations, speak many things to you, O Agni; as a servant born in the house, comes before a great master, I come before you.)*

> हे अग्ने त्वा त्वां पुरु बहु वोचे । यद्वा । बहु दाश्वानि सम्बन्धे । पुत्रं देहि वित्तं देहीत्याद्याशासनानि ब्रवीमीत्यर्थः । किं कोऽस्मि नेत्र्याह [?] । यतो दाश्वानभिमतं हविर्दत्तवानस्मि अतो वोचे । ईश्वरावधारणेन [?] ब्रुवतः कथं दातव्यमिति न मन्तव्यम् । यतोऽहं हे अग्ने तव स्वित् स्वैव अभिमुख्येनारिर्हविरादि प्राप्तिप्रापणेन सेवकोऽहम् । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । महस्य महतस्तोदस्येव शिक्षकस्य स्वामिनः शरणे गृहे यथा गर्भदासादिर्[?] ... समन्ताद्यतो वर्तते तद्वदेहमसि । यस्मादेवं मुक्त्वोपे ... (नि. ३-२) इति ॥ *[small type; partly legible; the end of the bhāṣya quotes Ni. 3-2: *bahudāśvāṃs tvām evābhiprayāmy ariḥ ... todasyeva śaraṇa ā mahasya tudasyeva śaraṇe 'dhi mahataḥ*]*

> *he agne tvā tvāṃ puru bahu voce | yadvā | bahu dāśvāni sambandhe | putraṃ dehi vittaṃ dehītyādyāśāsanāni bravīmītyarthaḥ | kiṃ ko 'smi netryāha [?] | yato dāśvānabhimataṃ havirdattavānasmi ato voce | īśvarāvadhāraṇena [?] bruvataḥ kathaṃ dātavyamiti na mantavyam | yato 'haṃ he agne tava svit svaiva abhimukhyenārirhavirādi prāptiprāpaṇena sevako 'ham | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | mahasya mahatastodasyeva śikṣakasya svāminaḥ śaraṇe gṛhe yathā garbhadāsādir[?] ... samantādyato vartate tadvadehamasi | yasmādevaṃ muktvope ... (ni. 3-2) iti ‖ *[small type; partly legible; the end of the bhāṣya quotes Ni. 3-2: *bahudāśvāṃs tvām evābhiprayāmy ariḥ ... todasyeva śaraṇa ā mahasya tudasyeva śaraṇe 'dhi mahataḥ*]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *agne* — O Agni; *tava sviḍ ā* — standing facing you (as your own); *mahasya* — in the place of the great one; *todasyeva ā śaraṇe* — as one born in the house of the sacrificer, before him; (like a servant) who stays in the house; *ariḥ* — I, your devotee; *puru* — in great number; *dāśvān* — offering oblations; *tvā* — to you; *voce* — I pray (to give sons and wealth).

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, as a servant born in the house of the master, in a great place, stands before him in supplication, I, your servant, offering you oblations, stand facing you and ask of you sons and wealth.

**English Translation (as printed).** Presenting many offerings, I address you, Agni, ever coming into your presence (like a servant) in the dwelling of a mighty master.

### Printed p. 466  (PDF 484)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 150".)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** Here the relationship of Agni to the sacrificer is compared with that of a master and his servant, to show the sacrificer's humility.

***todasyeva*** — in explaining the meaning of this word, the Nirukta author has cited this very Ṛk and explained it. His explanation is as follows:

> बहुदाश्वांस्त्वामेवाभिप्रयाम्यरिरमित्रमुच्यते । ईश्वरोऽप्यरिरीत्येतस्मादेवेदेनस्मै देवतस्या अग्न्याहुतयो हूयन्ते इत्येतद्दृष्ट्वैवमुपमामैक्षत [?] तोदस्येव शरण आ महस्य तुदस्येव शरणेऽधि महतः ॥

> *bahudāśvāṃstvāmevābhiprayāmyariramitramucyate | īśvaro 'pyarirītyetasmādevedenasmai devatasyā agnyāhutayo hūyante ityetaddṛṣṭvaivamupamāmaikṣata [?] todasyeva śaraṇa ā mahasya tudasyeva śaraṇe 'dhi mahataḥ ‖*

(Ni. 3-2.) "Agni is the giver, I am the one who asks for sons and the like; I am the one without a rival" — thus after describing, the author states the explanation of *ari*: "*ari*, from the root *ṛ*, 'to go' [or *iṇ gatau*], is a word that gives the sense of 'enemy' — and the sacrificer, too, in the same way, being a harmer, is called *ari*", i.e. hostile to enemies, and the like. The word *ari* is also "lord" as well; the Nirukta author says *īśvaro 'pi arir ity etasmād …*.

As Agni, by his oral service, carries the oblations to the other gods, and as the stomach of a great well is a well of great capacity, he explains the word *toda* by the comparison "as a well".

Durgācārya explains this comparison thus:

> "तोदस्येव शरणे आ महस्य"—तुदस्येव विदीर्णस्य कस्यचिच्छ्वभ्रस्य कोपस्योपरि । शरणे बिले । यथा हि श्वभ्रे बिले कस्मिंश्चिद्दर्वस्य [?] आपो गच्छन्ति । न च तस्मै श्वभ्रस्य महतो ग्रहणशक्तिपरिहानं भवति । एवं तेनानेकाश्चानेकदेवशास्त्राहुतीरभ्याभिः प्रदत्ताः प्रतीच्छतो न सामर्थ्यपरिहानमस्ति । अतो देवतानामस्माकं स्नेहेनातिनिक्षेपोपकारे प्रवृत्तेः अतः श्यामेनाप्ययोमि [?] ।

> *"todasyeva śaraṇe ā mahasya"—tudasyeva vidīrṇasya kasyacicchvabhrasya kopasyopari | śaraṇe bile | yathā hi śvabhre bile kasmiṃściddarvasya [?] āpo gacchanti | na ca tasmai śvabhrasya mahato grahaṇaśaktiparihānaṃ bhavati | evaṃ tenānekāścānekadevaśāstrāhutīrabhyābhiḥ pradattāḥ pratīcchato na sāmarthyaparihānamasti | ato devatānāmasmākaṃ snehenātinikṣepopakāre pravṛtteḥ ataḥ śyāmenāpyayomi [?] |*

Meaning: "Since I have the strength to praise you, I can call you; as for your pouring oblations in abundance, I am able: the reason for calling only Agni is that his stomach, like a well, can take in much oblation, and fill it" — [partly unclear].

Therefore, according to the explanation in the Nirukta, *toda* means a well [*kūpa*], and *śaraṇa* a hole. But Sāyaṇa's meaning is contrary to this.

### Printed p. 467  (PDF 485)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 37 [?].)*

Sāyaṇa explains *toda* as "a master who teaches" (*śikṣaka svāmin*), *śaraṇa* as "house", *ari* as "the sacrificer who is a servant, one who gives oblations, and is a worshipper".

> मध्ये होता दुरोणे बर्हिषो राळग्निस्तोदस्य यज्यै । अयं स सूनुः सहस ऋतावा दूरात्सूर्यो न शोचिषा ततान ॥

> *madhye hotā duroṇe barhiṣo rāḷagnistodasya yajyai | ayaṃ sa sūnuḥ sahasa ṛtāvā dūrātsūryo na śociṣā tatāna ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-1-1 [?].) In this Ṛk, Sāyaṇa explains the word *toda* as *tudyate tapasā pīḍyate iti todaḥ yajamānaḥ* — "one who is goaded, afflicted by austerity, the sacrificer"; since the sacrificer is strong in carrying out the Agni-rites, *toda* means "the sacrificer". In the same sūkta:

> तेजिष्ठा यस्यारतिर्वनेराट् तोदो अध्वस्य वृषभानो अव्यात् । अद्रोघो नु प्रवणीता चेतति तन्न मर्त्यो वव्रिशत् [?] ॥

> *tejiṣṭhā yasyāratirvanerāṭ todo adhvasya vṛṣabhāno avyāt | adrogho nu pravaṇītā cetati tanna martyo vavriśat [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, *todaḥ* he explains as "*sarvasya prerakaḥ sūryaḥ*" — "the Sun, the impeller of all". And:

> यासि कुत्सेन सरथमवस्युस्तोदो वातस्य हर्योरीशानः । ऋज्रा वाजं न गध्यं युयूषन्कविर्यदह्न्पार्याय भूषात् ॥

> *yāsi kutsena sarathamavasyustodo vātasya haryorīśānaḥ | ṛjrā vājaṃ na gadhyaṃ yuyūṣankaviryadahnpāryāya bhūṣāt ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-16-11.) In this, *todaḥ* is explained as *śatrūṇāṃ hiṃsakaḥ*, "slayer of foes".

***śaraṇe*** — following the author of the Nirukta, Durgācārya has explained this word as "a hole"; since it has a wide place and gives shelter, it may be given the meaning "a hole or house", according to the context.

> प्रियोस इत्ते मघवन्नभिष्टौ नरो मदेम शरणे सखायः । नि तुर्वशं नि याद्वं शिशीह्यतिथिग्वाय शंस्यं करिष्यन् ॥

> *priyosa itte maghavannabhiṣṭau naro madema śaraṇe sakhāyaḥ | ni turvaśaṃ ni yādvaṃ śiśīhyatithigvāya śaṃsyaṃ kariṣyan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-19-8.) In this Ṛk, "house"; and

> उदुष्य शरणे दिवो ज्योतिरयंस्त सूर्यः । अग्निर्न शुक्रः समिधान आहुतः ॥

> *uduṣya śaraṇe divo jyotirayaṃsta sūryaḥ | agnirna śukraḥ samidhāna āhutaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].) In this the word *śaraṇa* means *ādityasya sthāne nabhasi*: "in the sky, the place of the Āditya, since it is a wide dwelling-place for the Āditya", they have explained.

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> व्यनिनस्य धनिनः प्रहोषे चिदररुषः ।
> कदा चन प्रजिगतो अदेवयोः ॥ २ ॥

> *vyaninasya dhaninaḥ prahoṣe cidararuṣaḥ |*
> *kadā cana prajigato adevayoḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> वि । अनिनस्य । धनिनः । प्रऽहोषे । चित् । अररुषः ।
> कदा । चन । प्रऽजिगतः । अदेवयोः ॥ २ ॥

> *vi | aninasya | dhaninaḥ | pra 'hoṣe | cit | araruṣaḥ |*
> *kadā | cana | pra 'jigataḥ | adevayoḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: I seek your favour for the sacrificer; ward off the godless rich man, who gives nothing at the sacrifice, and who does not praise the gods.)*

> पूर्वमन्त्रे स्वाभीष्टं बहु विज्ञापयामीत्युक्तम् । अत्र तु स्वनिलप्रेभ्यो [?] दानादिरहितेभ्यो दानं न दातव्यमिति प्रार्थ्यते । हे अग्ने त्वां निशेषेण ब्रवीमि । उपसर्गस्तेर्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः । अथवा सन्निहितद्योतक इत्यनुषज्यते । अस्मदर्थं यद्वा । विज्ञ ... तद्विरुद्धं वोचे । वक्ष्यमाणस्वरूपस्य न दातव्यमिति ब्रवीमित्यर्थः । तेषां स्वरूपमाह । अनिनस्य [?] स्वामिनं कुर्वाणस्य कथा धनिनः समुग्रदानवतो [?] । पूर्वमेव धनवतो दानस्य निरर्थकत्वात् नार्य्यतेः । यद्वा । योगात्मनुपयोग्यार्थतः [?] इत्यर्थः । किंच प्रहोषे प्रहोषोऽत्र । प्र क्षीयत [?] ... तत्र दक्षिणारूपेण । यद्वा । प्रहोषे ऽत्र सम्बन्धः । प्रकर्षेण होतुमं समुद्यतेः इत्यर्थः । अत्र रेतब्बेन तस्मिन् सामर्थ्यं लक्ष्यते । जिज्ञ ... समुच्छ्येनायोः । किंचे केव चन प्रजिगतः कदाचिदपि प्रकर्षेण देवानस्तुवतः । अत्र चेनेति निपातसमुदायः । तत्र चेतशब्दः समुच्छ्ये नसब्ज्ञो विशेषः । किंचानेवोऽदेवयोः । देवानात्मनोऽनिच्छतः । एवमेषां न दातव्यमिति विब्रीवे [?] इत्यर्थः । निन्दितानां स्वरूपनिरूपणेन स्वस्य तादृशत्वाभावे [?] बहु वोचे इत्येतदुत्तरं [?] ॥ *[small type; many words doubtful; only the sense is given]*

> *pūrvamantre svābhīṣṭaṃ bahu vijñāpayāmītyuktam | atra tu svanilaprebhyo [?] dānādirahitebhyo dānaṃ na dātavyamiti prārthyate | he agne tvāṃ niśeṣeṇa bravīmi | upasargasteryogyakriyādhyāhāraḥ | athavā sannihitadyotaka ityanuṣajyate | asmadarthaṃ yadvā | vijña ... tadviruddhaṃ voce | vakṣyamāṇasvarūpasya na dātavyamiti bravīmityarthaḥ | teṣāṃ svarūpamāha | aninasya [?] svāminaṃ kurvāṇasya kathā dhaninaḥ samugradānavato [?] | pūrvameva dhanavato dānasya nirarthakatvāt nāryyateḥ | yadvā | yogātmanupayogyārthataḥ [?] ityarthaḥ | kiṃca prahoṣe prahoṣo 'tra | pra kṣīyata [?] ... tatra dakṣiṇārūpeṇa | yadvā | prahoṣe 'tra sambandhaḥ | prakarṣeṇa hotumaṃ samudyateḥ ityarthaḥ | atra retabbena tasmin sāmarthyaṃ lakṣyate | jijña ... samucchyenāyoḥ | kiṃce keva cana prajigataḥ kadācidapi prakarṣeṇa devānastuvataḥ | atra ceneti nipātasamudāyaḥ | tatra cetaśabdaḥ samucchye nasabjño viśeṣaḥ | kiṃcānevo 'devayoḥ | devānātmano 'nicchataḥ | evameṣāṃ na dātavyamiti vibrīve [?] ityarthaḥ | ninditānāṃ svarūpanirūpaṇena svasya tādṛśatvābhāve [?] bahu voce ityetaduttaraṃ [?] ‖ *[small type; many words doubtful; only the sense is given]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *(O Agni —)* *aninasya* — one who does not worship you as master; *prahoṣe* — in the performing of the sacrifice; *dhaninaḥ* — rich, possessing wealth; *cid ararūṣaḥ* — even when [he is] one who does not give (at the dakṣiṇā); *kadā cana* — ever; *prajigataḥ* — one who praises you; *adevayoḥ* — those who have no devotion to the gods; (in this way) the two types of people: *vi* — withhold (your favour); — [lit.] "O Agni, be devoted to the two sorts of people [with whom I contrast myself]".

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni, there are two kinds of people who have no devotion to the gods: one kind is the rich man who does not worship you as master and is chary of giving the fee for the sacrifice; the other, who never praises you. Do not show your favour even to these two sorts of people.

### Printed p. 470  (PDF 488)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 150".)*

**English Translation (as printed).** ( I ask you also to withhold your favour ) from ( those ) two godless ( persons ), from the rich man, who, acknowledging you not as his lord, is chary of gifts at sacred rites, and from him who rarely praises (the gods).

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***prahoṣe*** — *prakarṣeṇa hotum*: "to offer in an excellent manner"; he explains "at the sacrifice at which the offerer offers oblations in abundance"; those who offer such oblations are called *prahoṣin*:

> अपादु शिप्र्यन्धसः सुदक्षस्य प्रहोषिणः । इन्दोरिन्द्रो यवाशिरः ॥

> *apādu śipryandhasaḥ sudakṣasya prahoṣiṇaḥ | indorindro yavāśiraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk, as for *prahoṣiṇaḥ*, it is explained "*prakarṣeṇa devān havirbhir juhvataḥ*" as an adjective of *sudakṣasya*, i.e. of the sacrificer "who offers oblations", in the sense of the offerer.

***aninasya*** — for this word two kinds of meaning have been made. First, taking the word as it is: *tvāṃ asvāminaṃ kurvataḥ* — "one who does not make you his master", i.e. one who does not worship you as master; and the second, taking the two words *prahoṣe aninasya* together: *ina* means "one with capacity, the lord", *ananiṣya* [aninasya] "one who has no capacity [*sāmarthya*] like that of the powerful" — "to the man who lacks capacity, who cannot offer oblations at the sacrifice" — so he has explained.

***prajigataḥ*** — *kadācid api devān astuvataḥ*: "one who does not praise the gods at any time", the non-believer.

***adevayoḥ*** — *devān ātmano 'nicchataḥ*: "those who do not desire the gods"; "the two [persons] who have no devotion and faith in the gods", the unbelievers.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar page, noted briefly).** *vi* — because it is in connection with a verb, the *upasarga* is used, so a suitable verb, "I speak" (*bravīmi*), is to be supplied; or it is understood as *voce* with the *anuvṛtti*; *aninasya* (*na vidyate inaḥ svāmī yasya saḥ aninaḥ*; *nañsubhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) *uttarapada-antodātta*; genitive sg.); *dhaninaḥ* (*dhanam asyāsti iti dhanī*; *ata ini…* (Pā. Sū. 5-2-115) *ini* suffix in the sense of *matup*; suffix accent: first *udātta*).

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स चन्द्रो विप्र मर्त्यो महो व्राधन्तमो दिवि ।
> प्रप्रेत्ते अग्ने वनुषः स्याम ॥ ३ ॥

> *sa candro vipra martyo maho vrādhantamo divi |*
> *praprette agne vanuṣaḥ syāma ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सः । चन्द्रः । विप्र । मर्त्यः । महः । व्राधन्ऽतमः । दिवि ।

> *saḥ | candraḥ | vipra | martyaḥ | mahaḥ | vrādhan 'tamaḥ | divi |*
> *pra 'pra | it | te | agne | vanuṣaḥ | syāma ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: O wise Agni, the mortal who worships you becomes, in heaven, a moon, greater than the great; may we, too, be your excellent worshippers.)*

> हे अग्ने विप्र मेधाविन् यो मर्त्यस्त्वां यजते स मर्त्यो यजमानो दिवि द्युलोके चन्द्रः सर्वेषामाह्लादकश्चन्द्रसदृशो भवति । यद्वा । चन्द्र एव भवति यजमानानां चन्द्रत्वप्राप्तिं छन्दोगा आमनन्ति । पितृलोकादाकाशमाकाशाच्चन्द्रमसमेष सोमो राजा (छां. उ. ५-१०-४) इति । सोमलोके विभूतिमनुभूयेति च । तथा मुण्डके [?] ... सुवर्णवर्णः सूर्यरश्मिभिर्वहन्ति ... किञ्च महो महतोऽपि व्राधन्तमः प्रवृद्धतमः । इतरदेवानामपि श्रेष्ठ इत्यर्थः । अतोऽग्ने ते तव प्रप्रेत् प्रकर्षेण [?] ... वनुषः संभक्तारः स्याम । यद्वा । प्रीणयित्वा प्रप्रेत् स्याम ... प्रकृष्टा भवेम ॥ *[small type; partly legible]*

> *he agne vipra medhāvin yo martyastvāṃ yajate sa martyo yajamāno divi dyuloke candraḥ sarveṣāmāhlādakaścandrasadṛśo bhavati | yadvā | candra eva bhavati yajamānānāṃ candratvaprāptiṃ chandogā āmananti | pitṛlokādākāśamākāśāccandramasameṣa somo rājā (chāṃ. u. 5-10-4) iti | somaloke vibhūtimanubhūyeti ca | tathā muṇḍake [?] ... suvarṇavarṇaḥ sūryaraśmibhirvahanti ... kiñca maho mahato 'pi vrādhantamaḥ pravṛddhatamaḥ | itaradevānāmapi śreṣṭha ityarthaḥ | ato 'gne te tava prapret prakarṣeṇa [?] ... vanuṣaḥ saṃbhaktāraḥ syāma | yadvā | prīṇayitvā prapret syāma ... prakṛṣṭā bhavema ‖ *[small type; partly legible]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *vipra* — O wise Agni; *martyaḥ* — which mortal; (worships you with sacrifices and the like); *saḥ* — that mortal; *divi* — in the heaven; *candraḥ* — takes the place of the moon, which delights; *mahaḥ* — becomes also greater than the great gods; *vrādhantamaḥ* — extremely grown; *agne* — O Agni; *prapet* — in the most excellent way; *te* — you; *vanuṣaḥ* — as worshippers; *syāma* — may we be (be gracious) [or *prapet syāma* — worshipping you, may we also attain, in the highest manner].

**Bhāvārtha.** O wise Agni, the mortal who worships you with sacrifices and the like attains in heaven the place of the delight-giving moon, and becomes greater than the gods who are great. Therefore, O Agni, may we too, worshipping you in the most excellent way, attain the best place.

### Printed p. 473  (PDF 491)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 38 [?].)*

**English Translation (as printed).** Sage Agni, the mortal ( who propitiates you ) becomes a moon in heaven, the most eminent of the great (deities): may we, therefore, ever be in an especial manner your worshippers.

*(The printed heading of this block reads "English Tranlation" [sic].)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***vrādhantamaḥ*** — this word is read among the names of the great (Ni. 3-[?]). It means "exceedingly great"; this adjective is used in the Ṛk-saṃhitā, in the sense of "strong", as praise of one of great power, and in some places as a synonym of "enemy". Examples:

> इमे ये ते सु वायो बाह्वोजसोऽन्तर्नदी ते पतयन्त्युक्षणो महि व्राधन्त उक्षणः ।

> *ime ye te su vāyo bāhvojaso 'ntarnadī te patayantyukṣaṇo mahi vrādhanta ukṣaṇaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk the word *vrādhantaḥ* is an adjective of the bulls (*ukṣaṇaḥ*) of Vāyu: *mahi vrādhantaḥ* — "greatly increasing (growing)" — gives "greatly grown". And:

> स व्राधतो नहुषो दंसुजूतः शर्धस्तरो नरां गूर्तश्रवाः । विश्वस्पर्वतरातियाति वाळ्हैः सत्वा विश्वासु पृत्सु सदमिच्छूरः ॥

> *sa vrādhato nahuṣo daṃsujūtaḥ śardhastaro narāṃ gūrtaśravāḥ | viśvasparvatarātiyāti vāḷhaiḥ satvā viśvāsu pṛtsu sadamicchūraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In this Ṛk *hiṃsakān mahataḥ asi*: "you are a destroyer of the great enemies"; the word as a synonym of "enemy". As in

> शत्रूयन्तो अभि ये नस्ततस्रे महि व्राधन्त ओगणास इन्द्र । अन्धेनामित्रास्तमसा सचन्तां सुज्योतिषो अक्तवस्ताँ अभि ष्युः ॥

> *śatrūyanto abhi ye nastatasre mahi vrādhanta ogaṇāsa indra | andhenāmitrāstamasā sacantāṃ sujyotiṣo aktavastā~ abhi ṣyuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) the word *vrādhantaḥ* is "those who are harming us (*asmān bādhamānāḥ*)", i.e. those who greatly afflict us.

In the Ṛk at hand the word *vrādhantamaḥ* is an adjective of the mortal who worships Agni, in praise of his greatness: *pravṛddhatamaḥ*, "most grown"; "he becomes still greater than the other gods who are greater than all".

***candraḥ*** — *candra* has two meanings. First: "for Agni's worshipper, *sarveṣām āhlādakaḥ candrasadṛśo bhavati*, the delight-giver of all, like the moon" — since the moon is said to be "bright with beauty (brilliant and delightful)": from the root *cand*, "to delight". Following this meaning the Nirukta derivation:

---

### Printed p. 474  (PDF 492)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 150".)*

> चन्द्रश्चन्दतेः कान्तिकर्मणः ।

> *candraścandateḥ kāntikarmaṇaḥ |*

(Ni. 11-[?].) "Since it gives the meaning of shining (*kānti*), *candra* is formed from the root *cand*", thus it is said; hence that Agni has the meaning "of one who delights (*āhlādaka*)" and "bright"; second: the sacrificer himself "becomes the moon" — "*chāndogāḥ*, the Sāmavedins, state that the sacrificers attain the state of the moon through the sacrifice":

> पितृलोकादाकाशमाकाशाच्चन्द्रमसमेष सोमो राजा ।

> *pitṛlokādākāśamākāśāccandramasameṣa somo rājā |*

(Chāṃ. Up. 5-10-[?].)

> सोमलोके विभूतिमनुभूय ।

> *somaloke vibhūtimanubhūya |*

(Praś. Up. 3-[?].) Sāyaṇa has cited these sentences.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar page, noted briefly).** *candraḥ* (root *cadi āhlādane*; *sphāyitañci…* (Uṇ. Sū. 2-13) *rak* suffix; *idito num dhātoḥ* *num* augment; suffix accent: final *udātta*); *vipraḥ* (root *ḍuvap bījasantāne* [sic: *ḍuvapa*]; *ṛjendrāgravajra…* (Uṇ. Sū. 2-28) *ran* suffix, *nipātita*; in the vocative, *āmantritasya ca* *nighāta*); *mahaḥ* (root *maha pūjāyām*; *kvip ca* *kvip*; genitive sg.; *sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168) case-ending *udātta*); *vrādhantamaḥ* (root *vṛdhu vṛddhau*; *oṇādika* suffix *atiśayena*; lengthening of the *ṛ*; *atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau* (Pā. Sū. 5-3-55) *tamap*); *divi* (*ūḍidaṃpadādi* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) case-ending *udātta*); *vanuṣaḥ* (root *vana sambhaktau*; by the power of *bahulagrahaṇa*, the *oṇādika* *usi* suffix; suffix accent: first *udātta*; nom. plural); *syāma* (root *as bhuvi*; *vidhiliṅ* 1st plural; *tiṅ*-*nighāta*). ‖ 3 ‖

*Here the 150th Sūkta ends.*

## Sūkta 151

### Printed p. 475  (PDF 493)

*(Page header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 30, 31 [?]. The Kannada heading reads "The 151st Sūkta".)*

*(Anukramaṇī, Sanskrit; not rendered in English. Gist: the sūkta of nine Ṛks beginning "Mitraṃ na yam" is the eleventh sūkta, of Dīrghatamas, Jagatī, Mitrāvaruṇa deity; the Anukramaṇī word is "mitraṃ nava maitrāvaruṇaṃ hi jāgatam"; its use is by indication.)*

> मित्रं न यमिति नवर्चमेकादशं सूक्तं दैर्घतमसं जागतं मैत्रावरुणम् । आद्या मैत्रेव । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । मित्रं नव मैत्रावरुणं हि जागतं मैत्र्याद्येति ॥ विनियोगो लैङ्गिकः ॥

> *mitraṃ na yamiti navarcamekādaśaṃ sūktaṃ dairghatamasaṃ jāgataṃ maitrāvaruṇam | ādyā maitreva | atrānukramaṇikā | mitraṃ nava maitrāvaruṇaṃ hi jāgataṃ maitryādyeti ‖ viniyogo laiṅgikaḥ ‖*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta *mitraṃ na yam* is the eleventh sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has nine Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Mitra-Varuṇa are the deities. The metre is Jagatī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said *mitraṃ nava maitrāvaruṇaṃ hi jāgataṃ maitryādyeti*. The use is by indication (*laiṅgika*).

**॥ ओम् ॥**

**Sūkta 151** — Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 21, Sūkta 151; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 30, 31. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 9. Ṛṣi: Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Devatā: 1 Mitra; 2–9 Mitrāvaruṇau. Chandas: Jagatī.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> मित्रं न यं शिम्या गोषु गव्यवः स्वाध्यो विदथे अप्सु जीजनन् ।

> *mitraṃ na yaṃ śimyā goṣu gavyavaḥ svādhyo vidathe apsu jījanan |*

> अरेजेताम् । रोदसी इति । पाजसा । गिरा । प्रति । प्रियम् । यजतम् । जनुषाम् । अवः ॥ १ ॥

> *mitram | na | yam | śimyā | goṣu | gavyavaḥ | su 'ādhyaḥ | vidathe | ap 'su | jījanan |*
> *arejetām | rodasī iti | pājasā | girā | prati | priyam | yajatam | januṣām | avaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(gist: the cattle-seeking, well-meditating worshippers produced Agni in the waters by their rites, like a friend; heaven and earth trembled with his strength and his roar; he is the dear, worshipful protection of living beings.)*

> यमग्निं शिम्या कर्मनामैतत् शिमीति शक्ति [?] तन्नामसूक्तत्वात् । प्रकाशवृष्ट्यादनादिकर्मणा मित्रं न मित्रमिव स्थितम् । यद्वा । शिम्येत्येतत् क्रियया सह सम्बध्यते । गोषु बह्वीषु निमित्तभूतासु गव्यवः गा आत्मन इच्छन्तः । अत्र यद्यपि गव्यमिवालं न गोश्चित्तं तथापि गव्यन्ति इत्यनेनात्मनो गोस्पृहा प्रतीयते [?] ... स्वाध्यः सुष्ठु ध्यातारः फलस्योत्पादयितारः शोभनध्याना वा ... विदथे यज्ञे [?] ... अप्सु अप्शब्दः [?] अन्तरिक्षनाम आपः । पृथिवीति तन्नामसूक्तत्वात् ... अग्निं जीजनन् जनयन्ति यजमानाः [?] ... अरेजेतां कम्पेते रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ पाजसा बलेन गिरा [?] भयंकरशब्देन च ... प्रति प्रियं ... यजतं यजनीयं जनुषामवः जनानां प्राणिनां रक्षणं निमित्तीकृत्य [?] ... शिम्या मथनादिकर्मणा जीजनन् जनयन्ति यजमानाः । यद्वा । अप्सु निमित्तभूतासु जीजनन् सर्वप्राणिमात्रोपकारार्थं [?] वृष्ट्यर्थम् ... *[small type; many words doubtful; this bhāṣya continues on p. 477]*

> *yamagniṃ śimyā karmanāmaitat śimīti śakti [?] tannāmasūktatvāt | prakāśavṛṣṭyādanādikarmaṇā mitraṃ na mitramiva sthitam | yadvā | śimyetyetat kriyayā saha sambadhyate | goṣu bahvīṣu nimittabhūtāsu gavyavaḥ gā ātmana icchantaḥ | atra yadyapi gavyamivālaṃ na gościttaṃ tathāpi gavyanti ityanenātmano gospṛhā pratīyate [?] ... svādhyaḥ suṣṭhu dhyātāraḥ phalasyotpādayitāraḥ śobhanadhyānā vā ... vidathe yajñe [?] ... apsu apśabdaḥ [?] antarikṣanāma āpaḥ | pṛthivīti tannāmasūktatvāt ... agniṃ jījanan janayanti yajamānāḥ [?] ... arejetāṃ kampete rodasī dyāvāpṛthivyau pājasā balena girā [?] bhayaṃkaraśabdena ca ... prati priyaṃ ... yajataṃ yajanīyaṃ januṣāmavaḥ janānāṃ prāṇināṃ rakṣaṇaṃ nimittīkṛtya [?] ... śimyā mathanādikarmaṇā jījanan janayanti yajamānāḥ | yadvā | apsu nimittabhūtāsu jījanan sarvaprāṇimātropakārārthaṃ [?] vṛṣṭyartham ... *[small type; many words doubtful; this bhāṣya continues on p. 477]**

### Printed p. 477  (PDF 495)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 31 [?].)*

*(Ṛk 1 bhāṣya, end.)*

> ... निरुद्धम् । यद्वा । मित्रं न सखायमिव स्थितं मित्रनामकं देवं यज्ञीयैः [?] ऋत्विग्भिः [?] प्रादुर्भावयन्ति । शिप्रान्तेदन्ये शेषेण तत्र्येयोजनीयम् ॥ *[small type; partly legible]*

> *... niruddham | yadvā | mitraṃ na sakhāyamiva sthitaṃ mitranāmakaṃ devaṃ yajñīyaiḥ [?] ṛtvigbhiḥ [?] prādurbhāvayanti | śiprāntedanye śeṣeṇa tatryeyojanīyam ‖ *[small type; partly legible]**

**Pratipadārtha (Kannada).** *goṣu* — in order to get cows in abundance; *gavyavaḥ* — those who desire cows; *svādhyaḥ* — worshippers of good meditation, or devotees; *vidathe* — in the sacrifice; *apsu* — in the atmosphere (and in the sacrifice); *priyam* — dear, or benefactor of the world; *yajatam* — worshipful; *mitraṃ na* — like a friend, the god named Mitra, who is like the friend of living beings; *yam* — whom (Agni) — [or *mitraṃ na* — like Agni, the friend; *yam* — whom, Mitra-deity (Agni's friend)]; *janūṣām* — for the sake of the protection of living beings, produced; *avaḥ prati* — for protection; *śimyā* — by the acts of churning or by the acts that cause rain; *jījanan* — [they] cause to be born; (so that) *pājasā* — by his strength; *girā* — by his terrifying sounds; *rodasī* — heaven and earth; *arejetām* — tremble.

**Bhāvārtha.** Worshippers, of good meditation, who desire to acquire many cows, make [the god] Mitra, or Agni, who is dear, worshipful, and a benefactor of the world, to be born in the sacrifice and in the atmosphere, by their acts of churning and the like, for the protection of all living beings, as a friend; and heaven and earth tremble by his strength and by his terrifying sounds.

**English Translation (as printed).** Heaven and earth have been terrified by the strength and the noise (of him), whom pious worshippers, desirous of acquiring cattle, have generated by their (sacred) acts, amidst the waters (of the firmament), at the sacrifice, as a friend for the preservation of living beings, the benefactor (of man), and entitled to adoration.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).** ***svādhyaḥ*** — *suṣṭhu ādhyātāraḥ phalasya utpādayitāraḥ, śobhanadhyānā vā*: "those who are of good meditation, who produce the fruit; or those with excellent meditation" — in the commentary, the two meanings are given: "those who produce the desired fruits"; or "devotees of excellent meditation" (*śrīmanta dhyānāsakta*); of these two meanings the second is the more fitting. Moreover —

### Printed p. 478  (PDF 496)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 151".)*

> तव व्रते सुभगासः स्याम स्वाध्यो वरुण तुष्टुवांसः । उपायन उषसां गोमतीनामग्नयो न जरमाणा अनु द्यून् ॥

> *tava vrate subhagāsaḥ syāma svādhyo varuṇa tuṣṭuvāṃsaḥ | upāyana uṣasāṃ gomatīnāmagnayo na jaramāṇā anu dyūn ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].)

> युवा सुवासाः परिवीत आगात्स उ श्रेयान्भवति जायमानः । तं धीरासः कवय उन्नयन्ति स्वाध्यो मनसा देवयन्तः ॥

> *yuvā suvāsāḥ parivīta āgātsa u śreyānbhavati jāyamānaḥ | taṃ dhīrāsaḥ kavaya unnayanti svādhyo manasā devayantaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-4.) In all such Ṛks, the word *svādhyaḥ* is explained as *śobhanadhyānāḥ* ("of excellent meditation"; "those who, with intense attention, are fixed in the thought"); by this the sense in the Ṛk at hand also is fitting.

***vidathe*** — the word *vidatha* has many senses, such as work (*karma*), sacrifice, sacrificial assembly; with examples, and also with the criticisms of Western scholars, this has been explained in the section of the Ṛk 1-[?]-[?] in this part.

***mitraṃ na*** — *mitraṃ na* has two meanings: first, "like a friend", a synonym of *sakhā*; second, the sense that the god Mitra, who is the friend of all.

> न वै मित्रं किंचन हिनस्ति न मित्रं कश्चन हिनस्ति नैनं कुशो न कण्टको विभिनत्ति नास्य व्रणश्च नास्ति सर्वस्य ह्येव मित्रो मित्रम् ।

> *na vai mitraṃ kiṃcana hinasti na mitraṃ kaścana hinasti nainaṃ kuśo na kaṇṭako vibhinatti nāsya vraṇaśca nāsti sarvasya hyeva mitro mitram |*

(Śa. Brā. [?]-[?]-[?].) In such sentences too, the element of Mitra as the friend of all beings is mentioned here too.

***gavyavaḥ*** — *gāḥ ātmana icchantaḥ*: "desiring cows for themselves"; the first sense is "those desirous of getting cows". Or, *gavyavaḥ* — *ity ātmīyāṃ gāṃ svāmitvaṃ pratipadyate* — "in the sense of making [the cow] one's own, the lordship" — Sāyaṇa explains that by the word *gavya*, the sense "the state of being lord of the cows" is also suggested:

> तवेदं विश्वमभितः पशव्यं यत्पश्यसि चक्षसा सूर्यस्य । गवामसि गोपतिरेक इन्द्र भक्षीमहि ते प्रयतस्य वस्वः ॥

> *tavedaṃ viśvamabhitaḥ paśavyaṃ yatpaśyasi cakṣasā sūryasya | gavāmasi gopatireka indra bhakṣīmahi te prayatasya vasvaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-[?]-[?].) The reference to the lordship of cows in this Ṛk has been shown there.

***śimyā*** — *śaktyā*: "by the power; either of the nature of churning and the like, or the power of the lightning-fire, which is the work of rain-giving": this is the sense here.

***apsu jījanan*** — *antarikṣe utpannam* — "they caused him to be born in the atmosphere":

> यदग्ने दिविजा अस्यप्सुजा वा सहस्कृते । तं त्वा गीर्भिर्हवामहे ॥

> *yadagne divijā asyapsujā vā sahaskṛte | taṃ tvā gīrbhirhavāmahe ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha).** (O Mitra-Varuṇa!) *yat* — for which reason; *vām* — for you two; *purumīḷhasya* — abundantly pouring (making desired things rain down); *sominaḥ* — filled with Soma-juice; *svābhuvaḥ* — arisen of its own gladness, together with the oblation; *tyat* — that sacrificial rite; *pra mitrāso na* — excellent priests, who are like friends; *dadhire ha* — perform. [Alternatively: *sominaḥ* — possessing Soma; *purumīḷhasya* — of the king called Purumīḷha; *pra mitrāso na* — priests like excellent friends; *svābhuvaḥ* — competent in their several duties; *tyat* — the well-known rite; *dadhire ha* — perform.] *adha* — therefore; *gātum* — your coming; *arcate* — of the sacrificer who awaits (you) and worships; *kratum* — rite; *vidatam* — knowing …

### Printed p. 482  (PDF 500)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 151".)*

*(Pratipadārtha continued: …) accept and praise it ("koḍu ślāghisiri" as printed); *uta* — moreover; *vṛṣaṇā* — O bestowers of wishes, O Mitra-Varuṇa; *pastyāvataḥ* — (of the sacrificer) whose house is furnished with sacrificial wealth, (his praise); *śrutam* — hear.*

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha).** O Mitra and Varuṇa, the priests, who are like excellent friends, perform for you both the sacrificial rite — abundantly flowing, filled with Soma, arisen out of the heart's own joy, with oblation. Therefore know the rite of the sacrificer who awaits your coming and worships you, and take it up. And, O bestowers of wishes, Mitra-Varuṇa, listen well to the praise of the house-holding sacrificer endowed with sacrificial wealth.

**English Translation (as printed).** Since they, (the priests), like friends, have prepared for you both, Mitra and Varuna, a libation) [sic: closing parenthesis without opening] of the abundantly-flowing and spontaneous Soma juices, therefore do you consent to come to the rite of the worshipper, and listen, showerers (of blessings) to the (prayers of the) householder.

**विशेषविषयाः (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Special Topics).** For the first half of this Ṛk two meanings are given. First: the word *purumīḷhasya* — "of the abundantly sprinkled / of the one pouring out wishes" — although in the genitive, qualifies the word *tyat* "rite" (the verb being *dadhire*). *Svābhuvaḥ* means "of Soma, of what comes into being of itself": a sacrificial rite with oblation arisen of the heart's own joy. Such a rite the excellent priests perform.

Second: *purumīḷhasya* is a proper name, "of King Purumīḷha," and *svābhuvaḥ* means priests competent each in their own functions; such priests perform the well-known rite. Purumīḷha is famous in some places as an ancient sage, in others as a king. His story is told in the *Bṛhaddevatā*; although the story there is chiefly about Śyāvāśva, since it relates the connection between Śyāvāśva and Purumīḷha, the story as the *Bṛhaddevatā*-author tells it is given here:

> राजर्षिर्भ[?]द्दार्भ्यो रथवीतिरिति श्रुतः ।
> स यज्ञमानो राजात्रिमभिगम्य प्रसाद्य च ॥
> आत्मानं कार्यमर्थं च ख्यापयन् प्राञ्जलिः स्थितः ।
> अन्वयाचद्[?]षिमात्रेयमार्त्विज्यायार्चनानसम् ॥

> *rājarṣirbha[?]ddārbhyo rathavītiriti śrutaḥ |*
> *sa yajñamāno rājātrimabhigamya prasādya ca ‖*
> *ātmānaṃ kāryamarthaṃ ca khyāpayan prāñjaliḥ sthitaḥ |*
> *anvayācad[?]ṣimātreyamārtvijyāyārcanānasam ‖*

Rathavīti Dārbhya, a royal sage, wishing to perform a sacrifice, went to the sage Atri, honoured him, and requested that his son Arcanānas accept the office of priest at his sacrifice and help him in the sacrificial work. He agreed, and with his son Śyāvāśva went to the king's house for the sacrifice and carried it out. While the sacrifice was going on, Arcanānas saw the king's daughter and, attracted, desired her as a bride for Śyāvāśva. Śyāvāśva too was enamoured of her. When father and son made their wish known to the king, he too agreed to the alliance, but said he would give his answer after asking his wife; his wife did not consent: Śyāvāśva was not a *ṛṣi*, and she would not give a daughter born in a line of sages to a non-*ṛṣi* — so she told them. In the same way the king too gave father and son his answer, after which they returned to their own place. Their …(continued overleaf: "ಅವರ" as printed)

### Printed p. 485  (PDF 503)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 2 Va. 30"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

Śyāvāśva alone remained with his mind fixed on the king's daughter. On the way back, along the road, he met Śaśīyasī [as printed "ಶಶೀಯಸೆನ್ನೂ"], Taranta and the king Purumīḷha. Taranta and Purumīḷha were both sons of a king and also sages; both bowed to the two arrivals, honoured and worshipped them. The women of the inner apartments also honoured them with gifts of cattle, horses and the like. Śyāvāśva alone, brooding that he had not got a beautiful wife, wandered in the forest and met the Maruts. Knowing them to be the sons of Rudra, the Maruts, he praised them. He became the seer of the hymn beginning *kva nara…* [as printed "ಕೀ ಫ್ಯಾ ನರಃ"; ṛ. saṃ. 5-61-1 as printed, [?]]. Learning this, Rathavīti, son of [?] (as printed "ವರ್ಷಿಗ" [?]), had his daughter brought and begged forgiveness for having refused to give her before, and asked that Śyāvāśva, who was now a *ṛṣi* himself, be pleased to accept his daughter. Śyāvāśva and his father agreed; then he gave the maiden with *arghya*, *pādya* and the like. Then Śyāvāśva, in return for the help Purumīḷha and the others had given him, bowed to them and composed six Ṛks praising them. Among them:

> उत म्ये रेद्वतीर्मन्मन्दीषी [?] प्रति श्यावाय वर्तनिम् ।
> वि रोहिता पुरुमीळ्हाय येमतुर्विप्राय दीर्घयशसे ॥

> *uta mye redvatīrmanmandīṣī [?] prati śyāvāya vartanim |*
> *vi rohitā purumīḷhāya yematurviprāya dīrghayaśase ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-61-5 [?].) This Ṛk praises Purumīḷha.

> युवां गोतमः पुरुमीळ्हो अत्रिर्दस्रा हवन्तेऽवसे हविष्मान् ।
> दिशं न दिष्टामृजूयेव यन्ता मे हवं नासत्योप यातम् ॥

> *yuvāṃ gotamaḥ purumīḷho atrirdasrā havante 'vase haviṣmān |*
> *diśaṃ na diṣṭāmṛjūyeva yantā me havaṃ nāsatyopa yātam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-183-5 [?].) In this Ṛk it is known that Purumīḷha praised the Aśvins and obtained their protection. Sāyaṇa tells the same story with some differences, thus:

> अत्राश्वार्क्षं पुरावृत्तमाहुरागमपारगाः ।
> अर्चनानाः पुरात्रेयो दार्भ्येण रथवीतिना ॥
> आर्त्विज्याय वृतो यज्ञे विततेऽहौत्र आस्थितः ।
> रथवीतिसुतां कन्यां ददर्श सितुरन्तिके ॥
> यियोज [?] स्वकुमाराय श्यावाश्वाय च तां सुताम् ।

> *atrāśvārkṣaṃ purāvṛttamāhurāgamapāragāḥ |*
> *arcanānāḥ purātreyo dārbhyeṇa rathavītinā ‖*
> *ārtvijyāya vṛto yajñe vitate 'hautra āsthitaḥ |*
> *rathavītisutāṃ kanyāṃ dadarśa siturantike ‖*
> *yiyoja [?] svakumārāya śyāvāśvāya ca tāṃ sutām |*

### Printed p. 487  (PDF 505)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 2 Va. 30" as printed, [?]; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 2 continued.)* … [the story] of Śyāvāśva's marriage is told; and since it tells of the help Purumīḷha gave Śyāvāśva and that his wish was fulfilled by that help, it is an occasion for praising Purumīḷha's greatness too. The Ṛk of the hymn (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-61) in which Śyāvāśva praises Purumīḷha has been quoted above.

**पस्त्यावतः** — *pastyā*, *duroṇe* (Ni. 3-4) etc. are read among the house-names (*gṛhanāmāni*). The meaning is "of one whose sacrificial house is furnished with sacrificial wealth".

> इन्द्र[?]न् बृहद्भ्यः पर्वतेभ्यः क्षयां विभ्यः सुवसि पस्त्यावतः ।
> यथायथा पतयन्तो विमीमिर एवैन [?] तस्थुः सवितः सवाय के ॥

> *indra[?]n bṛhadbhyaḥ parvatebhyaḥ kṣayāṃ vibhyaḥ suvasi pastyāvataḥ |*
> *yathāyathā patayanto vimīmira evaina [?] tasthuḥ savitaḥ savāya ke ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?], as printed, numerals not legible.) In such Ṛks *pastyāvataḥ* means "of the house-owner", and so it is understood in the present Ṛk too.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; grammar pages 487–488, noted briefly).** *purumīḷhasya* (root *miha secane*; the *niṣṭhā* suffix; *ho ḍhaḥ* — *ḍha* for *ha*; *ḍho ḍhe lopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-13) loss; *ḍhralope pūrvasya* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-111) lengthening; accent of the *kṛdanta*); *sominaḥ* (*somaḥ asya asti*; the *matvartha* suffix *ini*, Pā. Sū. 5-2-115, cited as printed; genitive sg.); *mitrāsaḥ* (*āj jaser asuk*, Pā. Sū. 7-1-50 — *asuk* augment of *jas*); *dadhire* (root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *liṭ* in the Veda; 3rd pl.; no *nighāta* since connected with *yat*; *ite*, Pā. Sū. 6-1-[?], final *udātta*); *svābhuvaḥ* (root *bhū sattāyām*; *kvip*; *karty-ekakarmaṇoḥ* … locative/genitive for the agent); *vidatam* (root *vida jñāne*; *loṭ* 2nd dual; the augment lacking …; *vyatyayo bahulam*; *ap*/*śap* = *śa*; *sārvadhātukam apit* — no guṇa; *nighāta* accent). Further small-type numerals not legible. ‖ 2 ‖

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> आ वां भूषन्क्षितयो जन्म रोदस्योः प्रवाच्यं वृषणा दक्षसे महे ।
> यदीमृताय भरथो यदर्वते प्र होत्रया शिम्या वीथो अध्वरम् ॥ ३ ॥

> *ā vāṃ bhūṣankṣitayo janma rodasyoḥ pravācyaṃ vṛṣaṇā dakṣase mahe |*
> *yadīmṛtāya bharatho yadarvate pra hotrayā śimyā vītho adhvaram ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आ । वां । भूषन् । क्षितयः । जन्म । रोदस्योः । प्रवाच्यम् । वृषणा । दक्षसे । महे ।

> *ā | vāṃ | bhūṣan | kṣitayaḥ | janma | rodasyoḥ | pravācyam | vṛṣaṇā | dakṣase | mahe |*

### Printed p. 489  (PDF 507)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 2 Va. 30" as printed, [?]; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥** *(continued)*

> यत् । ईम् । ऋताय । भरथः । यत् । अर्वते । प्र । होत्रया । शिम्या । वीथः ।
> अध्वरम् ॥ ३ ॥

> *yat | īm | ṛtāya | bharathaḥ | yat | arvate | pra | hotrayā | śimyā | vīthaḥ |*
> *adhvaram ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*(Gist: the Mitra-Varuṇa pair, bringers of what is desired, are praised for their birth from heaven and earth; the sacrificers praise it because the pair receive the sacrifice with praise and oblation. Small type, read with doubt.)*

> हे वृषणा कामानां वर्षितारौ हे मित्रावरुणौ वां युवयोः संबन्धि जन्म जननमुत्पत्तिं रोदस्योर्द्यावापृथिव्योः सकाशात् । द्यावापृथिवीभ्यामेव सर्वेषामुत्पत्तेः । यद्वा । मित्र इति सर्वोपकारी अग्निरुच्यते । वरुण इति तमोनिवारक आदित्यः । उभयोः पृथिवीद्युस्थानत्वात् । तत्र पूर्वमन्त्रे मित्र[?]ब्यान् स्मृतः । अत्र इदमधिगम्यते अग्निरेव मित्र इति । तथान्यत्रापि । अग्निं मित्रो न क्षितिषु प्रशंस्यम् । ऋ. ३-२-३ । मित्रं न यं सुधितं भृगवो दधुः । ऋ. ६-१५-२ । इति च । प्रवाच्यं स्तुत्यं तादृग्मित्रावरुणयोर्जन्म मह्ये महते दक्षसे सर्वविषयबलाय क्षितयो मनुष्या यजमाना आ भूषन् । सर्वतोऽलंकुर्वन्ति । श्लाघन्ते इत्यर्थः । जन्मनः प्रवाच्यत्वमाह । यदीं यस्मादेव कारणात् । अथवा । ईमित्यनर्थकः । [?] ऋतायेत्यर्थक्रमिदितीत्यादि [?] । ऋताय यज्ञाय भरथः सामर्थ्यं । यद्यस्माच्च कारणादर्वते युष्मान् प्राप्नुवते यजमानाय च भरथोऽभिमतं फलम् । अथवा । उभयत्र कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्चतुर्थी । यज्ञं यजमानं च भरथ इत्यर्थः । यस्माच्च होत्रया स्तुतिरूपया वाचा शिम्या हविःप्रदानादिकर्मणा च प्र वीथः प्रकर्षेण प्राप्नुथः । तस्मात्तद्वाच्यं जन्म भूषयन्तीत्यर्थः । होत्रेति वाङ्नाम होत्रा गीरिति तन्नामसु पाठात् ॥

> *he vṛṣaṇā kāmānāṃ varṣitārau he mitrāvaruṇau vāṃ yuvayoḥ saṃbandhi janma jananamutpattiṃ rodasyordyāvāpṛthivyoḥ sakāśāt | dyāvāpṛthivībhyāmeva sarveṣāmutpatteḥ | yadvā | mitra iti sarvopakārī agnirucyate | varuṇa iti tamonivāraka ādityaḥ | ubhayoḥ pṛthivīdyusthānatvāt | tatra pūrvamantre mitra[?]byān smṛtaḥ | atra idamadhigamyate agnireva mitra iti | tathānyatrāpi | agniṃ mitro na kṣitiṣu praśaṃsyam | ṛ. 3-2-3 | mitraṃ na yaṃ sudhitaṃ bhṛgavo dadhuḥ | ṛ. 6-15-2 | iti ca | pravācyaṃ stutyaṃ tādṛgmitrāvaruṇayorjanma mahye mahate dakṣase sarvaviṣayabalāya kṣitayo manuṣyā yajamānā ā bhūṣan | sarvato 'laṃkurvanti | ślāghante ityarthaḥ | janmanaḥ pravācyatvamāha | yadīṃ yasmādeva kāraṇāt | athavā | īmityanarthakaḥ | [?] ṛtāyetyarthakramiditītyādi [?] | ṛtāya yajñāya bharathaḥ sāmarthyaṃ | yadyasmācca kāraṇādarvate yuṣmān prāpnuvate yajamānāya ca bharatho 'bhimataṃ phalam | athavā | ubhayatra karmaṇaḥ saṃpradānatvāccaturthī | yajñaṃ yajamānaṃ ca bharatha ityarthaḥ | yasmācca hotrayā stutirūpayā vācā śimyā haviḥpradānādikarmaṇā ca pra vīthaḥ prakarṣeṇa prāpnuthaḥ | tasmāttadvācyaṃ janma bhūṣayantītyarthaḥ | hotreti vāṅnāma hotrā gīriti tannāmasu pāṭhāt ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha).** *vṛṣaṇā* — O Mitra-Varuṇa, who shower down (wished-for things); *yad īm* — for which reason; *arvate* — for the sacrificer who worships (you); *ṛtāya* — for the sacrifice (its fruit); *bharathaḥ* — you bear (and); *yat* — for which reason; *hotrayā* — by the praise-speech; *śimyā* — by the acts (of presenting the oblation etc.), (accompanied); *adhvaram* — the sacrifice; *pravīthaḥ* — you accept: (therefore) *vām* — of you two; *pravācyam* — to be extolled; *rodasyoḥ* — arisen from heaven and earth; *janma* — the birth; *mahe* — great; *dakṣase* — for (all-round) power; *kṣitayaḥ* — human sacrificers; *ā bhūṣan* — glorify with adorned words.

### Printed p. 490  (PDF 508)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 151".)*

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha).** O Mitra and Varuṇa, bestowers of what is wished: you bear the fruit of the sacrifice for the sacrificer who worships you, and you accept the sacrifice with its praise-words and oblation-rites; therefore human sacrificers extol your birth from heaven and earth, which is great and all-powerful, with adorned words.

**English Translation (as printed).** For the sake (of obtaining) great vigour, showerers (of benefits), men glorify your birth irom [sic: from] heaven and earth, which is to be extolled, inasmuch as you bestow (his desires) upon the worshipper (as the reward) of his sacrifice, and accept the rite (that is solemnized) with praise and oblation.

**विशेषविषयाः (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Special Topics).** **रोदस्योः जन्म क्षितयः आ भूषन्** — Human sacrificers glorify the birth of you two, arisen from heaven and earth. To the question "whose birth?", Sāyaṇa first (in explaining the word *vṛṣaṇā*) takes it as the birth of Mitra and Varuṇa; then, "or" (*yadvā*): "Mitra" is said of Agni, the benefactor of all; "Varuṇa" is the Āditya (sun), who removes darkness; both have their place on earth and in the sky. Or, since Agni is the benefactor of everyone, Agni may be called Mitra, and since the sun destroys darkness, the sun may be addressed as Varuṇa; for this he gives the support of Vedic passages:

> तं देवा बुध्ने रजसः सुदंससं दिवस्पृथिव्योररतिं न्येरिरे ।
> रथमिव वेद्यं शुक्रशोचिषमग्निं मित्रं न क्षितिषु प्रशंस्यम् ॥

> *taṃ devā budhne rajasaḥ sudaṃsasaṃ divaspṛthivyoraratiṃ nyerire |*
> *rathamiva vedyaṃ śukraśociṣamagniṃ mitraṃ na kṣitiṣu praśaṃsyam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-2-3 [?].)

> मित्रं न यं सुधितं भृगवो दधुर्वनस्पतावीड्यमूर्ध्वशोचिषम् ।
> स त्वं सुप्रीतो वीतहव्ये अद्भुत प्रशस्तिभिर्महयसे दिविदिवे ॥

> *mitraṃ na yaṃ sudhitaṃ bhṛgavo dadhurvanaspatāvīḍyamūrdhvaśociṣam |*
> *sa tvaṃ suprīto vītahavye adbhuta praśastibhirmahayase dividive ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-15-2 [?].) Quoting these Ṛks, he shows that, as Agni is described in them as Mitra, so in the present Ṛk too the meaning may be taken in the same way. Further, likewise:

> स जिह्वया चतुरनीक ऋञ्जते चारु वसानो वरुणो यतेनरिम् ।
> न तस्य विद्म पुरुषत्वता वयं यतो भगः सविता दाति वार्यम् ॥

> *sa jihvayā caturanīka ṛñjate cāru vasāno varuṇo yatenarim |*
> *na tasya vidma puruṣatvatā vayaṃ yato bhagaḥ savitā dāti vāryam ‖*

### Printed p. 491  (PDF 509)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 2 Va. 30" as printed, [?]; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Quotation reference at the foot of p. 490 not legible: "(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?])".)*

In such Ṛks, where Agni is praised, Agni too carries the epithet "Varuṇa", and *varuṇaḥ tamo-nivārakaḥ* (Varuṇa, remover of darkness) is said [as printed, wording uncertain]; therefore in the present Ṛk *vṛṣaṇā* may be taken as Mitra and Varuṇa, or as Agni in the form of Mitra and the Āditya in the form of Varuṇa — so Sāyaṇa has shown.

**अर्वते** — *yuṣmān prāpnuvate yajamānāya*: "for the sacrificer who approaches you" is the sense. The word *arvan* indicates a special motion, and its usage as a synonym of "horse" in the ordinary way was explained in detail earlier. Because (the sacrificer) approaches the gods quickly with devotion, the word is used also as a synonym for the oblation and for the sacrificer.

**क्षितयः** — *manuṣyāḥ (yajamānāḥ)*. It is read among the 22 names of men beginning *nare* (Ni. 3-2), so the meaning is "men".

> अग्निर्नेता भग इव क्षितीनां दैवीनां देव ऋतुपा ऋतावा ।
> स वृत्रहा सनयो विश्ववेदाः पर्षद्विश्वाति दुरिता गृणन्तम् ॥

> *agnirnetā bhaga iva kṣitīnāṃ daivīnāṃ deva ṛtupā ṛtāvā |*
> *sa vṛtrahā sanayo viśvavedāḥ parṣadviśvāti duritā gṛṇantam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-20-4 [?].) In such places, where a difference is shown between men and the divine peoples, the word *kṣiti* indicates the people of the earth, men.

**शिम्या** — *śimī iti karmanāma*; from the root *śam* or from *śak* (Ni. [?]); "to take pains" or "power" — it becomes "action". These can be actions that display power, such as dance; or actions of bringing rain. In the present Ṛk it means actions such as presenting the oblation.

**होत्रया** — *hotrā*, *gīḥ* are read among the names of speech (Ni. 1-11 [?]); the sense is "speech in the form of praise".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar pages 491–492, noted briefly).** *bhūṣan* (root *bhūṣa alaṅkāre*; *chandasi luṅ-laṅ-liṭaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-6) in the sense of past *laṅ*; *luk* [?]; 3rd pl.; no augment *aṭ* in the Veda; *tiṅ*-accent: *nighāta*); *kṣitayaḥ* (root *kṣi nivāse*; *kṣiyaḥ ktin* …/*kṛ-cakṣi-… -mṛ* [as printed, "kṛc kṣi-… saṃjñāyām"]; *ktic* suffix; final *udātta*; 1st pl.); *pravācyam* (root *vaca paribhāṣaṇe*; *ṇyat* by *ṛhalor ṇyat* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-124); *ato upadhāyāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116) *vṛddhi*; *yajacyācaprav…* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-[?]) no *kutva*; *tit svarita* accent; or *yat* by *aco yat*, *ṇeranii*…).

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 151".)*

*(Grammar page continued, noted briefly.)* *vṛṣaṇā* …; *dakṣase* (root *dakṣa vṛddhau śīghrārthe ca*; *asun*, *nityād…* first *udātta*; dative sg.); *mahe* (*sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-[?]) — final *udātta*).
