*(Gist: the sacrificial ground is well prepared; you who take up the sacrifice, proclaim it; you two yoke the heaven-wide, all-pervading sacrificial work as one harnesses a cow to a load. Small type, read with doubt.)*

> हे असुरा सुरौ [?] बलवन्तौ मित्रावरुणौ युवयोर्या क्षितिर्देवयजनरूपा मही महती प्रिया प्रियकरा प्रीणयित्री वा सा क्षितिः प्र प्रकर्षेण संपादिता । उपसर्गश्रुतेः क्रियाध्याहारः । तामासीदतमिति शेषः । यागभूमिर्देवानां प्रीयते [?] प्रसिद्धेः । अस्माच्च ते हे ऋतवानौ यज्ञवन्तौ युवं बृहत् [?] ऋतं यज्ञमा घोषथः । आस्तेल्येन [?] संपादिते इति स्तुतिमित्यर्थः । यतो ययोर्युवां युवां बृहतो महतो दिवो द्युलोकस्य धुरि दक्षं तर्पणसमर्थम् । अथवा बृहतो दिवो महतो द्युलोकस्य देवान् दक्षं प्रीणयितुमिति शेषः । यद्वा । कर्मणि षष्ठी । दिवो द्योतनात्मकं बृहतः प्रभूतं दक्षमभिमतसाधनसमर्थम् । आभुवं सर्वतो भवनशीलमपः कर्म सोमयागादिरूपमुप युञ्जाथे सेवेथे तत्कर्म हविः स्वीकुरुथ इत्यर्थः । दृष्टान्तः । धुरि शरीरबलस्य निर्वाहे [?] गां न धेनुमिव । उसे योजयन्ते तद्वत् । यद्वा । विकारे प्रकृतिशब्दः । क्षीरादिकमिव । तस्मात्तेन घोषथः ॥

> *he asurā surau [?] balavantau mitrāvaruṇau yuvayoryā kṣitirdevayajanarūpā mahī mahatī priyā priyakarā prīṇayitrī vā sā kṣitiḥ pra prakarṣeṇa saṃpāditā | upasargaśruteḥ kriyādhyāhāraḥ | tāmāsīdatamiti śeṣaḥ | yāgabhūmirdevānāṃ prīyate [?] prasiddheḥ | asmācca te he ṛtavānau yajñavantau yuvaṃ bṛhat [?] ṛtaṃ yajñamā ghoṣathaḥ | āstelyena [?] saṃpādite iti stutimityarthaḥ | yato yayoryuvāṃ yuvāṃ bṛhato mahato divo dyulokasya dhuri dakṣaṃ tarpaṇasamartham | athavā bṛhato divo mahato dyulokasya devān dakṣaṃ prīṇayitumiti śeṣaḥ | yadvā | karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī | divo dyotanātmakaṃ bṛhataḥ prabhūtaṃ dakṣamabhimatasādhanasamartham | ābhuvaṃ sarvato bhavanaśīlamapaḥ karma somayāgādirūpamupa yuñjāthe sevethe tatkarma haviḥ svīkurutha ityarthaḥ | dṛṣṭāntaḥ | dhuri śarīrabalasya nirvāhe [?] gāṃ na dhenumiva | use yojayante tadvat | yadvā | vikāre prakṛtiśabdaḥ | kṣīrādikamiva | tasmāttena ghoṣathaḥ ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha).** *asurā* — O powerful Mitra-Varuṇa; *yā* — which sacrificial ground; *mahi* — great; *priyaḥ* — dear, (is); *sā* — that earth in the form of the sacrifice; *pra* — has been supremely well prepared; *ṛtavānau* — you who accept the sacrifice; *bṛhat* — widely;

### Printed p. 494  (PDF 512)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 151".)*

*(Pratipadārtha continued:)* *ṛtam* — (our) sacrifice; *ā ghoṣathaḥ* — (declare, announce that it has been performed splendidly); *yuvam* — you two; *bṛhataḥ* — of the vast; *divaḥ* — of the region of heaven …; *dakṣam* — (capable) of satisfying (living beings); *ābhuvam* — pervading all regions; *apaḥ* — the rite (in the form of the Soma sacrifice); [or *divaḥ* — shining; *bṛhataḥ* — very great; *dakṣam* — capable (of supplying what is wished); *ābhuvam apaḥ* — the all-pervading sacrificial rite]; *dhuri* — in the yoke/burden; *gāṃ na* — as one joins a cow; [or as one joins milk-products with the cow]; *upa yuñjāthe* — you join together.

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha).** O powerful Mitra and Varuṇa, the great and pleasing sacrificial ground has been supremely well prepared. You who accept the sacrifice, announce our sacrifice, widely performed, as performed with the sacrifice's splendour. You two, moreover, join together the sacrificial rite — able to supply what is wished and pervading all regions — with the vast heaven, for the satisfaction of the gods, as one joins milk with the cow, together.

**English Translation (as printed).** Powerful divinities, most acceptable to you both is that spot, (where you are worshipped): accepters of sacrifice, proclaim the great ceremoney [sic] (as duly performed); for you two connect the efficacious and comprehensive rite with the vast heaven, like a cow with a burthen.

**विशेषविषयाः (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Special Topics).** **असुरा** — *asurau balavantau mitrāvaruṇau* (powerful Mitra and Varuṇa): the word *asura* is given the sense "possessed of power". In contexts where this power is displayed, the word is used with a sense suited to the particular place. For example:

> अर्चा दिवे बृहते शूष्यं वचः स्वक्षत्रं यस्य धृषतो धृषन्मनः ।
> बृहच्छ्रवा असुरो बर्हणा कृतः पुरो हरिभ्यां वृषभो रथो हि षः ॥

> *arcā dive bṛhate śūṣyaṃ vacaḥ svakṣatraṃ yasya dhṛṣato dhṛṣanmanaḥ |*
> *bṛhacchravā asuro barhaṇā kṛtaḥ puro haribhyāṃ vṛṣabho ratho hi ṣaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-3 [?].) In this Ṛk the word *asura* is an epithet of Indra. Here *asuraḥ śatrūṇāṃ nirasitā* (the thrower-down of enemies); or *asuḥ* = life (breath) or strength, and *asura* = one who has it (*-ra* in the possessive sense); or "one who gives those (waters)" [as printed, partly uncertain]; …

### Printed p. 495  (PDF 513)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 2 Va. 30" as printed, [?]; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

… "one who drives away enemies" is the meaning. Or, since *asu* has the meanings life (breath) and strength, "one who has life, one who has strength". Or *asu* = waters; since he gives them, *asura* is an epithet of Indra. Since Indra has many and various powers, the word can be an epithet of him in all these senses.

> प्र वेधसे कवये वेद्याय गिरं भरे यशसे पूर्व्याय ।
> घृतप्रसत्तो असुरः सुशेवो रायो धर्ता धरुणो वस्वो अग्निः ॥

> *pra vedhase kavaye vedyāya giraṃ bhare yaśase pūrvyāya |*
> *ghṛtaprasatto asuraḥ suśevo rāyo dhartā dharuṇo vasvo agniḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-[?]-[?], numerals not legible.)

> अहा यदिन्द्र सुदिना व्युच्छान् यो यक्षेतुमुपमं सनुत्सु ।
> न्यग्निं सीददसुरो न होता हुवानो अत्र सुभगाय देवान् ॥

> *ahā yadindra sudinā vyucchān yo yakṣetumupamaṃ sanutsu |*
> *nyagniṃ sīdadasuro na hotā huvāno atra subhagāya devān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-[?]-[?], numerals not legible.) In such Ṛks the word is used of Agni in the sense "powerful". In Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-3 [?] and similar Ṛks it means "intelligent" ("*prajñāvān*"); in 1-114-3 [?] and similar, "munificent"; in 4-[?]-[?] and similar, "the year, time-self" in the sense of time; in 8-[?]-[?] and similar, as a synonym of cloud; in 10-[?]-[?] and similar Ṛks, as a synonym of demon (*daitya*).

> वि सुपर्णो अन्तरिक्षाण्यख्यद्गभीरवेपा असुरः सुनीथः ।
> क्वेदानीं सूर्यः कश्चिकेत कतमां द्यां रश्मिरस्या ततान ॥

> *vi suparṇo antarikṣāṇyakhyadgabhīravepā asuraḥ sunīthaḥ |*
> *kvedānīṃ sūryaḥ kaściketa katamāṃ dyāṃ raśmirasyā tatāna ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-35-7 [?].) Here *āsuraḥ sarveṣāṃ prāṇadaḥ* — "the giver of life to all" — is an epithet of the sun.

> आव ते हेळो वरुण नमोभिरव यज्ञेभिरीमहे हविर्भिः ।
> क्षयन्नस्मभ्यमसुर प्रचेता राजन्नेनांसि शिश्रथः कृतानि ॥

> *āva te heḷo varuṇa namobhirava yajñebhirīmahe havirbhiḥ |*
> *kṣayannasmabhyamasura pracetā rājannenāṃsi śiśrathaḥ kṛtāni ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-14 [?].) In this Ṛk, *abhipta-kṣepaṇa-śīlaḥ* — "one whose nature is to cast off what is undesired" [as printed, uncertain]; since he has the power to destroy what is unwished, the epithet *asura* belongs to Varuṇa. In the present Ṛk too, *balavantau mitrāvaruṇau* — "O Mitra-Varuṇa, possessed of manifold power" — is the address.

**ऋतवानौ** — *ṛtavantau*. Possessing *ṛta* means "having the rule that is *ṛta*" or "having the sacrifice". The connection of Mitra-Varuṇa with *ṛta* has been explained at length earlier.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 4).** *asurā* (root *asu kṣepaṇe*; *asser uran* (Uṇ. Sū. 1-[?]) *uran* suffix; vocative dual: *supāṃ sulug* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) *ā* for the ending; *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198): *nighāta* accent); *mahi* (root *mah pūjāyām*; *sarvadhātubhya in* *in* suffix; *ñniṣṭhaśa* … first-*udātta* accent); *ṛtavānau* (*ṛtam asti anayoḥ*; *chandasi vanip ca* — *vanip* in the sense of *matup*; lengthening by *anyeṣām api dṛśyate* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-137); no *āmantrita*-*nighāta* since at the head of the *pāda*; *āmantritasya* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-78) *śnam* suffix; *śnasor allopaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-111) loss of the *a*; *n* → *anusvāra*, *parasavarṇa*; *tiṅ*: *nighāta*).

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> मही अत्र महिना वारमृण्वथोऽरेणवस्तुज आ सद्मन्धेनवः ।

> स्वरन्ति । ताः । उपरऽताति । सूर्यम् । आ । निम्रुचः । उषसः । तक्वनीःऽइव [?] ॥ ५ ॥

> *mahī iti | atra | mahinā | vāram | ṛṇvathaḥ | areṇavaḥ | tujaḥ | ā | sadman | dhenavaḥ |*
> *svaranti | tāḥ | upara 'tāti | sūryam | ā | nimrucaḥ | uṣasaḥ | takvanīḥ 'iva [?] ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*(Gist: O Mitra-Varuṇa, here on earth you drive the cattle to their dear stall; the cows return to the stall unharmed and cry to the sun at dusk and dawn. Small type, read with doubt.)*

> हे मित्रावरुणौ युवां मही महत्यौ [?] ॥ सप्तम्येकवचने पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः । ईदूतौ च सप्तम्यर्थे । पा. १-१-१९ । इति प्रगृह्यत्वम् । अत्रास्यां पृथिव्यां महिना महत्त्वेन यो धेनूनां वारं वरणीयं प्रदेशं ऋण्वथः गमयथः ॥ अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थः । गमनादिव्यवहारस्य तयोर्हीनत्वात् द्यावापृथिव्योरभिमानिदेवतात्वाच्च मित्रावरुणयोः । ता एता धेनवो गावः सायंकाले युष्मन्महत्त्वेन [?] ...रेणवो रेणुरहिताः [?] तुजः क्षीरदातारः [?] सद्मन् गृहे आ[?] ...प्रापिताः सत्यः स्वरन्ति शब्दं कुर्वन्ति । उपरताति उपरतातौ [?] उपरमकाले सायंकाले सूर्यमा सूर्यं प्रति । निम्रुचः निम्लोचन [?]कालाः [?] उषसः उषःकाले च । स्वरन्ति ... तक्वनीरिव तक्वा स्तेनः । तस्य वेत्ता गन्ता मनुष्यः । स यथा क्रोशति तद्वत् । एवं निरुद्धानां गवां सुखचारो युष्मद्दायत्त इति तयोः स्तुतिः ॥

> *he mitrāvaruṇau yuvāṃ mahī mahatyau [?] ‖ saptamyekavacane pūrvasavarṇadīrghaḥ | īdūtau ca saptamyarthe | pā. 1-1-19 | iti pragṛhyatvam | atrāsyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ mahinā mahattvena yo dhenūnāṃ vāraṃ varaṇīyaṃ pradeśaṃ ṛṇvathaḥ gamayathaḥ ‖ antarbhāvitaṇyarthaḥ | gamanādivyavahārasya tayorhīnatvāt dyāvāpṛthivyorabhimānidevatātvācca mitrāvaruṇayoḥ | tā etā dhenavo gāvaḥ sāyaṃkāle yuṣmanmahattvena [?] ...reṇavo reṇurahitāḥ [?] tujaḥ kṣīradātāraḥ [?] sadman gṛhe ā[?] ...prāpitāḥ satyaḥ svaranti śabdaṃ kurvanti | uparatāti uparatātau [?] uparamakāle sāyaṃkāle sūryamā sūryaṃ prati | nimrucaḥ nimlocana [?]kālāḥ [?] uṣasaḥ uṣaḥkāle ca | svaranti ... takvanīriva takvā stenaḥ | tasya vettā gantā manuṣyaḥ | sa yathā krośati tadvat | evaṃ niruddhānāṃ gavāṃ sukhacāro yuṣmaddāyatta iti tayoḥ stutiḥ ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha).** (O Mitra-Varuṇa) *mahī* — vast; *atra* — here on this earth; *mahinā* — by your greatness; (*dhenoḥ* — of cattle); *vāram* — to the dear (pen)

### Printed p. 498  (PDF 516)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 151".)*

*(Pratipadārtha continued:)* *ṛṇvathaḥ* — you bring; *dhenavaḥ* — those cows; *areṇavaḥ* — unharmed (by thieves and the like), or not stolen; *tujaḥ* — as givers of milk; *sadman* — in the pens; *ā* — come and gather; *tāḥ* — such cows; *nimrucaḥ* — at evenings; *uṣasaḥ* — at dawn also; *ā sūryam* — towards the sun; *takvanīr iva* [?] — as one who detects a thief (cries out loudly for the help of others); *svaranti* — cry out (for the light needed for their pleasant movement).

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha).** O Mitra and Varuṇa, you bring the cows, which have gone to graze over this wide earth, by your greatness to the pen dear to them. Those cows, unharmed by thieves, giving milk, return to the pens; at evening and at dawn they cry out towards the sun for light, for the help of … as one who detects a thief cries out.

**English Translation (as printed; begins thus on the page).** you bring (the cattle) to their acceptable (pasture) upon earth, whence the milk-yielding cows, protected by your power, return unharmed to their stalls: they cry to the sun (in heaven) above, both at evening and at dawn, as one (cries aloud) who detects a thief.

**विशेषविषयाः (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Special Topics).** **आरेणवः** — The word *reṇu* means dust. In an extended sense the word is used for dirt, impurity, sin and the like. The word *areṇavaḥ* qualifies the *antarikṣa* (atmosphere): "the atmosphere free of dust". It is also used in the sense "inviolable, not liable to harm".

> आव स्वयुक्ता दिव आ वृथा ययुरमर्त्याः कशया चोदत त्मना ।
> अरेणवस्तु विजाता अचुच्यवुर्ध्वानि जिन्मरुतो भ्राजदृष्टयः ॥

> *āva svayuktā diva ā vṛthā yayuramartyāḥ kaśayā codata tmanā |*
> *areṇavastu vijātā acucyavurdhvāni jinmaruto bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-168-5 [?].) In this Ṛk the word *areṇavaḥ* is an epithet of the Maruts: "free from toil, sinless, pure of self".

### Printed p. 499  (PDF 517)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 2 Va. 31" as printed, [?]; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

> त्वं जिहेषं न वाजिनमरेणवो यमत्सत ।
> दृळ्हं ग्रन्थिं न विष्यकमत्रं यविष्ठ मानु [?] एजः ॥

> *tvaṃ jiheṣaṃ na vājinamareṇavo yamatsata |*
> *dṛḷhaṃ granthiṃ na viṣyakamatraṃ yaviṣṭha mānu [?] ejaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-3, as printed, numerals uncertain.) In such Ṛks *ahiṃsyamānāḥ* — "those not subject to harm, the mighty *asuras*" — shows the power of the *asuras*. Likewise in the present Ṛk this word, as an epithet of the word *dhenavaḥ*, is explained in one way as *anavadyāḥ* — "blameless, pure", that is, "not carried off by thieves" — and in another way as *taskarādy-upaharaṇe anaṣṭāḥ* — "not lost by the thieves' taking, not stolen by robbers and the like".

**तुजः** — the word *tuj* is read among the names of the thunderbolt (Ni. 2-20 [?]), since it means "to injure". *Tujatiḥ dānakarmā* — "it also has the meaning of giving".

> आ नस्सुजं रयिं भरांशं न प्रतिजानते ।
> वृष्णं पक्षं फलमङ्केव धूनुहीन्द्र संभारणं वसु ॥

> *ā nassujaṃ rayiṃ bharāṃśaṃ na pratijānate |*
> *vṛṣṇaṃ pakṣaṃ phalamaṅkeva dhūnuhīndra saṃbhāraṇaṃ vasu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?], numerals not legible.) In such Ṛks *tujaḥ* means *śatrūṇāṃ bādhakam* — "one who injures enemies" — an epithet of the son (as printed, [?]).

> ज्योतिर्यज्ञाय रोदसी अनु ष्यादारे स्याम दुरितस्य भूरेः ।
> भूरि चिद्धि तुजतो मर्त्यस्य सुपारासो वसवो बर्हणावत् ॥

> *jyotiryajñāya rodasī anu ṣyādāre syāma duritasya bhūreḥ |*
> *bhūri ciddhi tujato martyasya supārāso vasavo barhaṇāvat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. [?]-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks *tujataḥ* means: for the sacrificer who gives abundantly, "who bestows abundant wealth" is the sense. In the present Ṛk too, the word *tujaḥ*, in the sense of giving, is an epithet of the cows that give milk and the like.

**ऋण्वथः** — from the root *riv* in the sense of motion, it means: "cause to reach, bring, make go".

> पवमानो अभि स्पृधो विशो राजेव सीदति ।
> यदीमृण्वन्ति वेधसः ॥

> *pavamāno abhi spṛdho viśo rājeva sīdati |*
> *yadīmṛṇvanti vedhasaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks *gamayati preṣayati* — "makes go" — is the sense; likewise in the present Ṛk the meaning is "you bring (the cows to their pen)".

### Printed p. 500  (PDF 518)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 151".)*

**निम्रुचः** — *mruc gatyarthaḥ*; *sūryasya nimrocane nitarāṃ gamane*, *sāyam ity arthaḥ*: the root *mruc*, meaning motion, joined with the prefix *ni*, means the final going (setting) of the sun, and so gives the sense "evening".

> यदेद्य सूर्य उद्यति प्रियक्षत्रा ऋतं दध ।
> यन्निम्रुचि प्रबुधि विश्ववेदसो यद्वा मध्यंदिने दिवि ॥

> *yadedya sūrya udyati priyakṣatrā ṛtaṃ dadha |*
> *yannimruci prabudhi viśvavedaso yadvā madhyaṃdine divi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].)

> श्रद्धां प्रातर्हवामहे श्रद्धां मध्यंदिनं परि ।
> श्रद्धां सूर्यस्य निम्रुचि श्रद्धे श्रद्धापयेह नः ॥

> *śraddhāṃ prātarhavāmahe śraddhāṃ madhyaṃdinaṃ pari |*
> *śraddhāṃ sūryasya nimruci śraddhe śraddhāpayeha naḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-151-5 [?].) In these Ṛks *asta-maya-velāyām*, *sāyaṃ samaye*, "at sunset time, in the evening hour," is the sense; so also in the present Ṛk.

*(Correction to pp. 497–498: the word I read there as "तक्वनीः [?]" is *takvavīḥ* — so written in the commentary and grammar on pp. 500–501 — i.e. Saṃhitā "तक्ववीरिव".)*

**तक्ववीः** — *taitpuḥ* (?), *takvā* etc. are read among the names of the thief (Ni. 3-18 [?]); the word *takvan* means a thief. *Tasya vetā gantā manuṣyaḥ* — the man who goes seeking such a thief.

> त्वां त्सारी दसमानो भगमीट्टे तक्ववीये ।

> *tvāṃ tsārī dasamāno bhagamīṭṭe takvavīye |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], numerals not legible; as printed, reading uncertain.) Here, as *taskarāṇāṃ gamanam*, so in the present Ṛk *taskarān uddiśyāgamanam* — "going in pursuit of thieves" — is the sense.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 5; grammar pages 500–501, noted briefly).** *mahī atra* (the locative sg.: *supāṃ sulug* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) *luk*; then *īdūdeddvivacanaṃ pragṛhyam* (Pā. Sū. 1-1-11) *pragṛhya*, so *plutapragṛhyā aci nityam* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-125) no *sandhi*); *mahinā* (since *mah* is read among the *pṛthvādi* words, *pṛthvādibhya imanij vā* (Pā. Sū. 5-1-122) *imanic* in the sense "its state"; *ṭeḥ* loss of the *ṭi*; *cit* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) final *udātta*; in the instr. sg. *ā* … the *ā*-loss, lengthening-reversal; in Vedic, loss of the *m*) — [continued on the next page].

*(Grammar page continued, noted briefly.)* *ṛṇvathaḥ* (root *riv gatau*; *idito num dhātoḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-58) *num* augment; *vyatyaya*, *samprasāraṇa*; *laṭ* 2nd dual; *tiṅ*: *nighāta*; the *ṇic* sense of "causing" (*prayojaka-vyāpāra*) is included in the root); *areṇavaḥ* (*reṇuḥ yeṣāṃ te areṇavaḥ*; *nañ subhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) final *udātta*; nominative pl.); *tujaḥ* (root *tuja dānārthe*, used causally; *kvip ca* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-76) *kvip*; nominative pl.); *sadman* (*supāṃ sulug* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) *luk* for the locative; *upasargaśruteḥ* "gacchanti" must be supplied); *svaranti* (root *svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ*; *bhvādi*; *laṭ* 3rd pl.; no *nighāta* since at the head of the *pāda*; *tāsyanudāttet* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) — *lasārvadhātuka* *anudātta*, so the root accent remains); *uparatāti* (*supāṃ sulug* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39); locative); *nimrucaḥ* (root *mruc gatau*, *bhvādi*; *kvip ca* — *kvip*; *kṛdutarapada* with the stem accent); *takvavīḥ* (*takvaṃ stenaṃ veti gacchati iti takvavīḥ*; the root *vī* with *kvip*, as before, *kṛdutarapada* stem accent). ‖ 5 ‖

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> आ वामृताय केशिनीरनूषत मित्र यत्र वरुण गातुमर्चथः ।
> अव त्मना सृजतं पिन्वतं धियो युवं विप्रस्य मन्मनामिरज्यथः ॥ ६ ॥

> *ā vāmṛtāya keśinīranūṣata mitra yatra varuṇa gātumarcathaḥ |*
> *ava tmanā sṛjataṃ pinvataṃ dhiyo yuvaṃ viprasya manmanāmirajyathaḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

### Printed p. 502  (PDF 520)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 151".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आ । वाम् । ऋताय । केशिनीः । अनूषत । मित्र । यत्र । वरुण । गातुम् । अर्चथः ।
> अव । त्मना । सृजतम् । पिन्वतम् । धियः । युवम् । विप्रस्य । मन्मनाम् । इरज्यथः ॥ ६ ॥

> *ā | vām | ṛtāya | keśinīḥ | anūṣata | mitra | yatra | varuṇa | gātum | arcathaḥ |*
> *ava | tmanā | sṛjatam | pinvatam | dhiyaḥ | yuvam | viprasya | manmanām | irajyathaḥ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*(Gist: O Mitra-Varuṇa, flames of Agni honour you at the sacrifice; as you accept the sacrificial ground, of your own accord send rain and prosper our rites, for you are masters of the praises of the wise sacrificer. Small type, read with doubt.)*

> हे मित्रावरुणौ केशिनीः केशवत्योऽग्नेर्ज्वाला वां युवामृताय यज्ञार्थमानूषत । हविःसमर्पणेनाभिपूजयन्तीत्यर्थः । कुत्रेति तदुच्यते । हे मित्र हे वरुण युवामुभौ यत्र यागे गातुं गमनं देवयजनदेशं वा । गातुरिति पृथिवीनाम गातुः पूषेत्यक्षत्वात् [?] । अर्चथः पूजयथः । स्वीकुरुथ इत्यर्थः । आगत्य च तैः त्मनात्मनैवाव सृजतं वृष्टिमवाजुखं [?] विसृजतम् । तथा कृत्वा धियः कर्माणि पिन्वतं वर्धयतमित्यर्थः । एवं कृत्वा विप्रस्य मेधाविनो यजमानस्य मन्मनां मननवतीनां स्तुतीनां युवं युवमिरज्यथः । ईश्वरौ स्वामिनौ भवथः । इरज्यतिरैश्वर्यकर्मा इरज्यति पत्यते इति तन्नामसूक्तत्वात् ॥

> *he mitrāvaruṇau keśinīḥ keśavatyo 'gnerjvālā vāṃ yuvāmṛtāya yajñārthamānūṣata | haviḥsamarpaṇenābhipūjayantītyarthaḥ | kutreti taducyate | he mitra he varuṇa yuvāmubhau yatra yāge gātuṃ gamanaṃ devayajanadeśaṃ vā | gāturiti pṛthivīnāma gātuḥ pūṣetyakṣatvāt [?] | arcathaḥ pūjayathaḥ | svīkurutha ityarthaḥ | āgatya ca taiḥ tmanātmanaivāva sṛjataṃ vṛṣṭimavājukhaṃ [?] visṛjatam | tathā kṛtvā dhiyaḥ karmāṇi pinvataṃ vardhayatamityarthaḥ | evaṃ kṛtvā viprasya medhāvino yajamānasya manmanāṃ mananavatīnāṃ stutīnāṃ yuvaṃ yuvamirajyathaḥ | īśvarau svāminau bhavathaḥ | irajyatiraiśvaryakarmā irajyati patyate iti tannāmasūktatvāt ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha).** *mitra* — O Mitra; *varuṇa* — O Varuṇa, (both of you); *yatra* — in which sacrifice; *gātum* — (your) coming or the sacrificial ground; *arcathaḥ* — you accept and honour, (there); *keśinīḥ* — the hair-like flames of fire; *vām* — you two; *ṛtāya* — for the sake of the sacrifice; *ā anūṣata* — serve (by offering the oblation); (you, coming,) *tmanā* — of your own accord; *ava sṛjatam* — cause (the rain) to pour down; *dhiyaḥ* — our rites; *pinvatam* — cause to prosper, (for) *yuvam* — you both; *viprasya* — of the wise sacrificer; *manmanām* — of the reverent praises; *irajyathaḥ* — are the lords.

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha).** O Mitra and Varuṇa, at whatever sacrifice you adorn and honour the sacrificial ground by your coming, there the hair-like flames of Agni serve you both with oblations and the like. Graciously, of your own accord, send down the rain that benefits us and make our rites prosper; for you are lords of the reverent praises of the wise sacrificer.

### Printed p. 503  (PDF 521)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 2 Va. 31" as printed, [?]; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

**English Translation (as printed).** The tresses of Agni minister, Mitra and Varuna, to your sacrifice, when you honour (with your presence) the sacrificial chamber: send down of your own accord (the rain) and prosper our offerings, for you have command over the praises of the pious men.

**विशेषविषयाः (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Special Topics).** **गातुम्** — *gamanaṃ devayajanadeśaṃ vā*: "the coming (of Mitra and Varuṇa) or the sacrificial ground" — two meanings are given. Even when it means "going", two kinds of sense are possible: "the path of observance (*anuṣṭhāna*)" or "the path to the world of the gods". Like the word *sugam*, this word too has physical and moral meanings.

> ऊर्ध्वो वां गातुरध्वरे अकारि ऊर्ध्वा शोचींषि प्रस्थिता रजांसि ।
> दिवो वा नाभा न्यसादि होता स्तृणीमहि देवव्यचा वि बर्हिः ॥

> *ūrdhvo vāṃ gāturadhvare akāri ūrdhvā śocīṃṣi prasthitā rajāṃsi |*
> *divo vā nābhā nyasādi hotā stṛṇīmahi devavyacā vi barhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks it is meant as "path", and:

> आर्यमा नो अदितिर्यज्ञियासो अद्रेबाद्र [?] देव्यानि वरुणस्य व्रतानि ।
> युयोत नो अनपत्यानि गन्तोः प्रजावान्नः पशुमाँ अस्तु गातुः ॥

> *āryamā no aditiryajñiyāso adrebādra [?] devyāni varuṇasya vratāni |*
> *yuyota no anapatyāni gantoḥ prajāvānnaḥ paśumā~ astu gātuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-[?]-[?].) In such passages *stuvantīndrādīn atreti gātur gṛham* — "the house in which Indra and other gods are praised" — is the meaning, a house;

> न्यैष्टै [?] देवी स्थिबिर्जहेते इन्द्राय गातुरितीव येमे ।
> सं यदोजो युवते विश्वमाभिरनु स्वधाव्ने क्षितयो नमन्ते ॥

> *nyaiṣṭai [?] devī sthibirjahete indrāya gāturitīva yeme |*
> *saṃ yadojo yuvate viśvamābhiranu svadhāvne kṣitayo namante ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-32-10 [?].) In such passages, "the earth" (the word *gātu* is read among the names of the earth, Ni. 1-3 [?]):

> स ते जानाति सुमतिं यविष्ठ य ईवते ब्रह्मणे गातुमैरत् ।
> विश्वान्यस्मै सुदिनानि रायो द्युम्नान्यर्यो वि दुरो अभि द्यौत् ॥

> *sa te jānāti sumatiṃ yaviṣṭha ya īvate brahmaṇe gātumairat |*
> *viśvānyasmai sudināni rāyo dyumnānyaryo vi duro abhi dyaut ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-[?]-[?].) Here *gīyate uccāryate iti gātuḥ — stotram*: the word is used as a synonym of "praise-song". In the present Ṛk the meaning is given as a synonymous pair: "going or the sacrificial ground".

### Printed p. 504  (PDF 522)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 151".)*

**इरज्यथः** — the word *irajyati* is read among the names of acts of lordship (Ni. 2-11 [?]) and also among the names of acts of service (Ni. 3-[?]); but the use of the word in the first sense is the commoner.

> इरज्यन्नग्ने प्रथयस्व जन्तुभिरस्मे रायो अमर्त्य ।
> स दर्शतस्य वपुषो वि राजसि पृणक्षि सानसिं क्रतुम् ॥

> *irajyannagne prathayasva jantubhirasme rāyo amartya |*
> *sa darśatasya vapuṣo vi rājasi pṛṇakṣi sānasiṃ kratum ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-[?]-[?].) In explaining the meaning of the word *irajyan* in this Ṛk, first, from the root *iraj* in the sense of jealousy, *īrṣyan* = *spardhāṃ kurvan* — "vying with other powers and splendours you shine" — is one meaning; second, *yadvā irajyatir aiśvaryakarmā jantubhir jāyamānair ātmaiśvaryo…* [text partly legible] *irajyan īśvaro bhavan* — "being lord of all creatures by your own splendour" — is explained. Likewise:

> यस्य श्वेता विचक्षणा तिस्रो भूमीरधिक्षितः ।
> त्रिरुत्तराणि पप्रुवर्वरुणस्य ध्रुवं सदः स सप्तानामिरज्यति नभन्तामन्यके समे ॥

> *yasya śvetā vicakṣaṇā tisro bhūmīradhikṣitaḥ |*
> *triruttarāṇi papruvarvaruṇasya dhruvaṃ sadaḥ sa saptānāmirajyati nabhantāmanyake same ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-[?]-[?].) In such Ṛks too *irajyati* means *īśvaro bhavati*, "is lord"; likewise in the present Ṛk Mitra and Varuṇa are described as lords of all the hymns of praise and of the praisers.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6; grammar pages 504–505, noted briefly).** *keśinīḥ* (*keśā āsāṃ santīti keśinyaḥ*; here with *jas* following, *supāṃ sulug* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) *pūrvasavarṇa* lengthening); *ānūṣata* (root *ṇu stutau*; *vyatyayo bahulam* — *ātmanepada*; in Vedic, *luṅ*; *ru*-suffix: *āt* substitution; *cli* → *sic*; *gāṅkuṭādibhyo 'ñṇin ṅit* (Pā. Sū. 1-2-1) it becomes *ṅit*, so no *guṇa*; in Vedic the root takes long and *iṭ*; *tiṅ*: *nighāta*); *gātum* (root *gai śabde*; *kamimanijani…* (Uṇ. Sū. 1-[?]) *tu* suffix; *ādeca upadeśe 'śiti* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-45) *ā* for the root's final; suffix accent: final *udātta*; accusative sg.; *gātuḥ*, *pūṣā* (Nir. 1-1-[?]) is read among the names of the earth).

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 2 Va. 31" as printed, [?]; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Grammar of Ṛk 6, concluded, noted briefly.)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 6, continued).** *arcathaḥ* (root *arca pūjāyām*; *laṭ* 2nd dual; *nipātair yad yadi…* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-30) — prohibition of *nighāta*, the root accent remaining); *tmanā* (*mantreṣv āṅy ādeḥ…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-[?]) loss of the *ā*); *sṛjatam* (root *sṛja visarge*; *loṭ* 2nd dual; *lasārvadhātuka* *anudātta*, so the *śa*-suffix keeps the accent; *cādilope vibhāṣā* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-63) no *nighāta*); *pinvatam* (root *pivi secane*; *loṭ* 2nd dual; *iditvāt* *num* augment; *nighāta* prohibited since it stands before a *tiṅanta*; *śap anudātta*, the root accent remains); *manmanām* (root *mana jñāne*; *manin* suffix; *nit*: first *udātta*; genitive pl.); *irajyathaḥ* (the root *iraj* is read in the sense of the action of lordship; *laṭ* 2nd dual; *nighāta*). ‖ 6 ‖

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यो वां यज्ञैः शशमानो ह दाशति कविर्होता यजति मन्मसाधनः ।
> उपाह तं गच्छथो वीथो अध्वरमच्छा गिरः सुमतिं गन्तमस्मयू ॥ ७ ॥

> *yo vāṃ yajñaiḥ śaśamāno ha dāśati kavirhotā yajati manmasādhanaḥ |*
> *upāha taṃ gacchatho vītho adhvaramacchā giraḥ sumatiṃ gantamasmayū ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यः । वाम् । यज्ञैः । शशमानः । ह । दाशति । कविः । होता । यजति । मन्मऽसाधनः ।

> *yaḥ | vām | yajñaiḥ | śaśamānaḥ | ha | dāśati | kaviḥ | hotā | yajati | manma 'sādhanaḥ |*

### Printed p. 506  (PDF 524)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 151".)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥** *(continued)*

> उप । अह । तम् । गच्छथः । वीथः । अध्वरम् । अच्छ । गिरः । सुऽमतिम् । गन्तम् । अस्मऽयू इति अस्मऽयू ॥ ७ ॥

> *upa | aha | tam | gacchathaḥ | vīthaḥ | adhvaram | accha | giraḥ | su 'matim | gantam | asma 'yū iti asma 'yū ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*(Gist: the sacrificer who praises and offers to you, the wise Hotṛ with his means, to him you go and accept his sacrifice; so, favouring us, accept my praises too. Small type, read with doubt.)*

> यो ह यः खलु यजमानो वां युवामुद्दिश्य युवाभ्यां वा यज्ञ[?]योगैरग्निमित्रभूतैः शशमानः शंसमानो दाशति हविरादिकं स्वस्वक्रमं निर्वर्त्य युष्मत्तृप्त्यसाधनं करोति । य एव कविर्मेधावी । अथवा कविर्मेधावी होता सम्यग्ज्ञोऽनिष्पादकः [?] यजमानो मन्मसाधनो मनसेनीय[?]द्रव्यदक्षिणादिसाधनोपेतः सन् यजति सोमयागादिकं कर्म करोति । तमेव यजमानं सुमतिं शोभनप्रज्ञां [?] मुपलक्ष्य गच्छथः । प्राप्नुथः खलु । अध्वरं तदीयं यज्ञं वीथः । कामयेथे । किंचास्मयू अस्मान्कामयमानौ युवां गिरः स्तुतीरच्छाभिलक्ष्य गन्तं गच्छतम् । ताभ्यां मां प्राप्य स्तुतीः स्वीकुरुतमित्यर्थः । अत्र युष्मदि तमिति सामान्यनिर्देशः प्रतिभाति तथाप्यस्मयू इत्युक्तत्वाद्दीर्घतमाः स्वात्मानमेव परोक्षतयोक्त्वानीति गम्यते । यद्वा । यो दाशति यष्टा यजते तमुपेत्य तदीयं यज्ञं कामयेथे । अतोऽस्मयू युवां सुमतिं मां मदीया गिरः स्तुतीरच्छाभिलक्ष्य गच्छतम् ॥

> *yo ha yaḥ khalu yajamāno vāṃ yuvāmuddiśya yuvābhyāṃ vā yajña[?]yogairagnimitrabhūtaiḥ śaśamānaḥ śaṃsamāno dāśati havirādikaṃ svasvakramaṃ nirvartya yuṣmattṛptyasādhanaṃ karoti | ya eva kavirmedhāvī | athavā kavirmedhāvī hotā samyagjño 'niṣpādakaḥ [?] yajamāno manmasādhano manasenīya[?]dravyadakṣiṇādisādhanopetaḥ san yajati somayāgādikaṃ karma karoti | tameva yajamānaṃ sumatiṃ śobhanaprajñāṃ [?] mupalakṣya gacchathaḥ | prāpnuthaḥ khalu | adhvaraṃ tadīyaṃ yajñaṃ vīthaḥ | kāmayethe | kiṃcāsmayū asmānkāmayamānau yuvāṃ giraḥ stutīracchābhilakṣya gantaṃ gacchatam | tābhyāṃ māṃ prāpya stutīḥ svīkurutamityarthaḥ | atra yuṣmadi tamiti sāmānyanirdeśaḥ pratibhāti tathāpyasmayū ityuktatvāddīrghatamāḥ svātmānameva parokṣatayoktvānīti gamyate | yadvā | yo dāśati yaṣṭā yajate tamupetya tadīyaṃ yajñaṃ kāmayethe | ato 'smayū yuvāṃ sumatiṃ māṃ madīyā giraḥ stutīracchābhilakṣya gacchatam ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha).** *yaḥ ha* — whichever sacrificer; *vām* — you two, addressing; *yajñaiḥ* — with sacrifices; *śaśamānaḥ* — praising; *dāśati* — offers the oblation, (and); *kaviḥ* — the wise; *hotā* — the performer of the *homa*; whichever sacrificer; *manmasādhanaḥ* — provided with his own means (of the offering and gifts); *yajati* — performs the sacrifice, (such); *sumatim* — one of excellent understanding; *taṃ upa* — to that sacrificer, aiming at him; *gacchathaḥ* — go; *adhvaram* — his sacrifice; *vīthaḥ* — desiring, accept; (and likewise) *asmayū* — favouring me; *giraḥ accha* — (my) hymns also, regarding them; *gantam* — come (accept).

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha).** Whichever sacrificer praises you two with sacrifices and offers the oblation, and the wise Hotṛ who performs the sacrifice with his means of gifts and the like — go to him, that excellent and understanding sacrificer, and accept his sacrifice; and likewise, favouring us, accept our praises as well.

### Printed p. 507  (PDF 525)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 2 Va. 31" as printed, [?]; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

**English Translation (as printed).** Come to the devout (worshipper), who, glorifying you, and providing (all that is) acceptable, presents you with oblations; (to him), the sage, the invoker, who offers you worship: accept his sacrifice; favourably disposed towards us, (accept our) praises.

**विशेषविषयाः (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Special Topics).** **शशमानः** — this word is read among the names of the act of worship (*arcati-karmanāmāni*). The *Nirukta*-author, quoting this very Ṛk (6-8 [?]), explains this word as *śaśamānaḥ śaṃsamānaḥ (stuvan)* — "the sacrificer who praises".

**मन्मसाधनः** — it was said earlier that the word *manma* has the meanings "agreeable to the mind", "meditative", "praiseworthy". *Manmasādhanaḥ* here means *manasīya-dravya-dakṣiṇādi-sādhanopetaḥ san*: the sacrificer provided, at the time of the sacrifice, with the gifts and materials he heartily wants. In this Ṛk this word is an epithet of the sacrificer.

> रायो बुध्नः संगमनो वसूनां यज्ञस्य केतुर्मन्मसाधनो वेः ।
> अमृतत्वं रक्षमाणास एनं देवा अग्निं धारयन् द्रविणोदाम् ॥

> *rāyo budhnaḥ saṃgamano vasūnāṃ yajñasya keturmanmasādhano veḥ |*
> *amṛtatvaṃ rakṣamāṇāsa enaṃ devā agniṃ dhārayan draviṇodām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?], numerals not legible.) In this Ṛk, as an epithet of Agni, *mananīyasya abhilaṣitasya sādhayitā* — "the accomplisher of what is thought of and desired" — is the sense, as is said in explaining that Ṛk [as printed, wording uncertain].

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 7; grammar pages 507–508, noted briefly).** *śaśamānaḥ* (root *śaśa plutagatau*; since the roots are of manifold meanings, here used in the sense of praise; *tācchīlyavayo-vacana-śaktiṣu cānaś* (Pā. Sū. 3-2-129) *cānaś* suffix; *śap* … *luk*; *anyeṣām api* augment *mukāgama*; *cit*: final *udātta*); *dāśati* (root *dāś dāne*; *laṭ* 3rd sg.; *yady-anyā*… no *nighāta* since connected with *yat*, the root accent remains).

*(Grammar of Ṛk 7, continued.)* *kaviḥ* (root *ku śabde*; *acāyiṅ* … (Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]) *i* suffix; *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ* guṇa; suffix accent: final *udātta*); *manmasādhanaḥ* (root *sādha saṃsiddhau*; *lyuṭ* suffix; *yuvor anākau* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-1) *ana* for *yu*; *liti* (Pā. #### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> युवां यज्ञैः प्रथमा गोभिरञ्जत ऋतावाना मनसो न प्रयुक्तिषु ।

> *yuvāṃ yajñaiḥ prathamā gobhirañjata ṛtāvānā manaso na prayuktiṣu |*

### Printed p. 509  (PDF 527)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 2 Va. 31" as printed, [?]; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(continued)*

> भरन्ति वां मन्मना संयता गिरोऽदृप्यता मनसा रेवदाशाथे ॥ ८ ॥

> *bharanti vāṃ manmanā saṃyatā giro 'dṛpyatā manasā revadāśāthe ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> युवाम् । यज्ञैः । प्रथमा । गोभिः । अञ्जते । ऋतऽवाना । मनसः । न । प्रऽयुक्तिषु ।
> भरन्ति । वाम् । मन्मना । सम्ऽयता । गिरः । अदृप्यता । मनसा । रेवत् । आशाथे इति ॥ ८ ॥

> *yuvām | yajñaiḥ | prathamā | gobhiḥ | añjate | ṛta 'vānā | manasaḥ | na | pra 'yuktiṣu |*
> *bharanti | vām | manmanā | sam 'yatā | giraḥ | adṛpyatā | manasā | revat | āśāthe iti ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*(Gist: O Mitra-Varuṇa, owners of the sacrifice and of rain: they anoint you first with the produce of the cow, as the mind is put first in actions; give wealth with gracious minds. Small type, read with doubt.)*

> हे ऋतावाना यज्ञवन्तौ वृष्ट्युदकवन्तौ वा मित्रावरुणौ युवां प्रथमा प्रथमौ यज्ञैर्यजनसाधनैर्गोभिर्गोविकारैः पयआदिभिरञ्जते । व्यञ्जयन्ति यजमानाः । देवभागं याग्येषु क्षीरादिभिर्युञ्जन्ते [?] इत्यर्थः । यद्वा । गोभिः रञ्जते स्रवन्ति [?] । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । प्रयुक्तिषु प्रयोगेषु मनसो न [?] कर्मणि षष्ठी । मन इव । तद्यथा प्रथमं व्यञ्जयन्ति मुख्यं कुर्वन्ति तेनैवोर्ध्वव्यवहारस्य [?] । किं च वां युवयोर्मन्मना मननवेत्ता [?] संयता सम्यग्यताश्चित्ता [?] चित्तेन गिरः स्तुतीर्भरन्ति संपादयन्ति । यस्मादेवं तस्मादद्यूप्यता [?] अनुग्रहपूर्वकेण मनसा प्रकृष्टेन चेतसा येन [?]रेवद्धनयुक्तं कर्म आशाथे । व्याप्नुथः । ददाथे इत्यर्थः । अश्नोतेर्लिटि नित्यमागमशासमिति वचनादिडभावः ॥

> *he ṛtāvānā yajñavantau vṛṣṭyudakavantau vā mitrāvaruṇau yuvāṃ prathamā prathamau yajñairyajanasādhanairgobhirgovikāraiḥ payaādibhirañjate | vyañjayanti yajamānāḥ | devabhāgaṃ yāgyeṣu kṣīrādibhiryuñjante [?] ityarthaḥ | yadvā | gobhiḥ rañjate sravanti [?] | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | prayuktiṣu prayogeṣu manaso na [?] karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī | mana iva | tadyathā prathamaṃ vyañjayanti mukhyaṃ kurvanti tenaivordhvavyavahārasya [?] | kiṃ ca vāṃ yuvayormanmanā mananavettā [?] saṃyatā samyagyatāścittā [?] cittena giraḥ stutīrbharanti saṃpādayanti | yasmādevaṃ tasmādadyūpyatā [?] anugrahapūrvakeṇa manasā prakṛṣṭena cetasā yena [?]revaddhanayuktaṃ karma āśāthe | vyāpnuthaḥ | dadāthe ityarthaḥ | aśnoterliṭi nityamāgamaśāsamiti vacanādiḍabhāvaḥ ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha).** *ṛtāvānā* — O Mitra-Varuṇa, who accept the sacrifice or are lords of rain-water; *prayuktiṣu* — whenever (in any work, through the organs) one has to act; *manaso na* — as the mind is given first rank (for the judgment of good or bad); *yuvām* — you two; *yajñaiḥ* — with the means of sacrifice; *gobhiḥ* — with milk and the like; *prathamā* — making you chiefs (placing you at the head); *añjate* — (the sacrificers) worship; (and) *vām* — you; *manmanā* — with reverent meditation; *saṃyatā* — with the concentrated mind; *giraḥ* — hymns; *bharanti* — compose; (therefore) *adṛpyatā* — without anger (with graciousness); *manasā* — with the mind; *revat* — wealth-bearing rites; *āśāthe* — bring about (for them).

### Printed p. 510  (PDF 528)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 151".)*

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha).** O Mitra and Varuṇa, fit to receive the sacrifice: just as in any work one gives first place to the mind that deliberates whether it is good or bad, so the sacrificers put you two at the head and worship you first; and they compose hymns with a mind that is wholly given to you in reverent meditation. Therefore, without anger, with a gracious mind, bring them wealth-bearing rites.

**English Translation (as printed).** Accepters of sacrifices, you are the first whom (worshippers) propitiate with offerings, the produce of the cow, like (the application of) the mind (in the first instance) to the results (of the senses), hymns (prompted) by thoughts wholly intent upon you, celebrate (your praise): do you with humble minds, bestow upoo [sic: upon] us wealth.

**विशेषविषयाः (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Special Topics).** **ऋतावाना** — *yajñavantau vṛṣṭyudakavantau vā mitrāvaruṇau*: Mitra and Varuṇa are addressed as "possessors of the sacrifice" or "lords of rain-water".

> अधारयतं पृथिवीमुत द्यां मित्रराजाना वरुणा महोभिः ।
> वर्धयतमोषधीः पिन्वतं गा अव वृष्टिं सृजतं जीरदानू ॥

> *adhārayataṃ pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ mitrarājānā varuṇā mahobhiḥ |*
> *vardhayatamoṣadhīḥ pinvataṃ gā ava vṛṣṭiṃ sṛjataṃ jīradānū ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-62-3 [?].)

> ऋतस्य गोपावधि तिष्ठथो रथं सत्यधर्माणा परमे व्योमनि ।
> यमत्र मित्रावरुणावथो युवं तस्मै वृष्टिर्मधुमत्पिन्वते दिवः ॥

> *ṛtasya gopāvadhi tiṣṭhatho rathaṃ satyadharmāṇā parame vyomani |*
> *yamatra mitrāvaruṇāvatho yuvaṃ tasmai vṛṣṭirmadhumatpinvate divaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-1 [?].) In such Ṛks Mitra and Varuṇa are the deities of rain, and the prayer is that they pour rain and protect the world; here too the same rain-deities, Mitra and Varuṇa, are petitioned for help.

**गोभिः** — *govikāraiḥ paya ādibhiḥ*: the word *go* is used even for the products of the cow, milk and the like. The *Nirukta*-author has shown that the word *go* has the meanings "earth" (2-3 [?]), "sun" (2-6 [?]) and so on; in the present passage it is to be understood that the chief meaning of *go* is the cow and the milk and the like obtained from it. In the *Nirukta*:

> आ धावता सुहस्त्यः शुक्रा गृभ्णीत मन्थिना ।
> गोभिः श्रीणीत मत्सरम् ॥

> *ā dhāvatā suhastyaḥ śukrā gṛbhṇīta manthinā |*
> *gobhiḥ śrīṇīta matsaram ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-46-4 [?].)

### Printed p. 511  (PDF 529)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 2 Va. 31" as printed, [?]; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 8, continued; the Nirukta quotation introduced on p. 510 ends with the Ṛk below.)* Quoting this Ṛk, he explains that *gobhiḥ* here means *gobhir abhiniṣpannena kṣīreṇa* — "with milk produced from cows"; so in the present Ṛk too it means "with milk and the like, products of the cow".

**अञ्जते** — *vyañjayanti*: they make manifest. The sense is that the sacrificers display their devotion by worship and the like. For the derivation of this word, the *Nirukta*-author:

> एता उत्या उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमञ्जते ।
> निष्कृण्वाना आयुधानीव धृष्णवः प्रति गावोऽरुषीर्यन्ति मातरः ॥

> *etā utyā uṣasaḥ ketumakrata pūrve ardhe rajaso bhānumañjate |*
> *niṣkṛṇvānā āyudhānīva dhṛṣṇavaḥ prati gāvo 'ruṣīryanti mātaraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-1 [?].) In this Ṛk *rajaso bhānum añjate* shows that Uṣas lights the whole atmosphere with her radiance, and so it is understood rightly; likewise in the present Ṛk the sense is that the sacrificers make manifest their devotion through the means of worship.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 8; grammar pages 511–512, noted briefly).** *prathamā* (root *pratha prakhyāne*; *prather amac* (Uṇ. Sū. 5-[?]) *amac* suffix; *cit*: final *udātta*; *supāṃ sulug* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) *ā* for the dual ending); *añjate* (root *añju vyaktimrakṣaṇakāntigatiṣu*; *laṭ* 3rd pl.; *nighāta* since after an *atiṅanta*); *ṛtāvānā* (*chandasīvanip* — *vanip* in the sense of *matup*; lengthening by *anyeṣām api dṛśyate* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-137); the dual *ā* by *supāṃ sulug*); *prayuktiṣu* (root *yujir yoge*; *striyāṃ ktin* (Pā. Sū. 3-3-94) in the sense of action; *coḥ kuḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-30) *kutva*, *carttva*; *tādau ca niti* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-50) the preceding … *udātta* accent); *bharanti* (root *bhṛñ bharaṇe*, *bhvādi*; *laṭ* 3rd pl.; no *nighāta* at the head of the *pāda*; *lasārvadhātuka* *anudātta*, the root accent remains; the root has the *ṇic* sense included); *saṃyatā* (root *yatī prayatne*; *kvip ca* — *kvip*; instr. sg.; *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) the *kṛdanta* keeps its stem accent).

*(Grammar of Ṛk 8, concluded; noted briefly.)* *adṛpyatā* (*na dṛpyat adṛpyat*, *tena*; root *dṛpa harṣamohanayoḥ*; *śatṛ* in the sense of *laṭ*; *tasparaśe tulyārthāḥ*… *naña* — *tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…* (Pā. **॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे मित्रावरुणौ युवां रेवद्धनवद्वयोऽन्नं दधाथे । उभयं च धारयथः [?] । यस्मादेवं तस्मादेवं [?] सहजसृष्ट्याध्वर्य [?] इति गम्यते । धनसिद्धिः [?] । हे नरा नेतारौ युवां मायाभिर्युवयोः प्रज्ञाभिरुत ऊतिभी रक्षणैश्च [?] आशाथे । अश्नुथः । अस्मभ्यं ददाथे इत्यर्थः । कीदृशं । मायाभिर्युवयोः प्रज्ञाभिरुतेऽस्मदभिमुखं गमनवत् इतो रक्षणवद्वा माहिनं महत् [?] अतिमहत् । उद्द्योर्द्योलोकर्युवयोर्देवत्वं माहात्म्यं [?] कुत इत्येक आह । वां युवयोर्देवत्वमहभिरहोभी रात्रिभिः । अत्राहोरात्रशब्देन रात्रिर्लक्ष्यते [?] । द्यावो दिवसा नानशुः । न प्राप्नुवन्ति । अहभिः रात्रिश्चेभे न तरते इत्यर्थः । उतापि च सिन्धवः स्यन्दनशीला नद्यो न व्याप्नुवन्ति । तथा युवयोर्देवत्वं पणयोऽसुरा अपि नानशुः । मघं धनं च नानशिरे । लोकत्रये युवयोः पराभविकारो न केऽपि सन्तीत्यर्थः ॥

> *he mitrāvaruṇau yuvāṃ revaddhanavadvayo 'nnaṃ dadhāthe | ubhayaṃ ca dhārayathaḥ [?] | yasmādevaṃ tasmādevaṃ [?] sahajasṛṣṭyādhvarya [?] iti gamyate | dhanasiddhiḥ [?] | he narā netārau yuvāṃ māyābhiryuvayoḥ prajñābhiruta ūtibhī rakṣaṇaiśca [?] āśāthe | aśnuthaḥ | asmabhyaṃ dadāthe ityarthaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ | māyābhiryuvayoḥ prajñābhirute 'smadabhimukhaṃ gamanavat ito rakṣaṇavadvā māhinaṃ mahat [?] atimahat | uddyordyolokaryuvayordevatvaṃ māhātmyaṃ [?] kuta ityeka āha | vāṃ yuvayordevatvamahabhirahobhī rātribhiḥ | atrāhorātraśabdena rātrirlakṣyate [?] | dyāvo divasā nānaśuḥ | na prāpnuvanti | ahabhiḥ rātriścebhe na tarate ityarthaḥ | utāpi ca sindhavaḥ syandanaśīlā nadyo na vyāpnuvanti | tathā yuvayordevatvaṃ paṇayo 'surā api nānaśuḥ | maghaṃ dhanaṃ ca nānaśire | lokatraye yuvayoḥ parābhavikāro na ke 'pi santītyarthaḥ ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha).** (O Mitra-Varuṇa) *revat* — wealthy; *vayaḥ* — food; *dadhāthe* — you hold (therefore); *narā* — you, guides; *māyābhiḥ* — with your wisdom; *ita ūti* — coming here to us with your protection; *māhinam* — great; *revat* — wealthy food; *āśāthe* — bring (to us); *vām* — of you two; *devatvam* — divine worthiness; *dyāvaḥ* — days, together with *ahabhiḥ* — nights; *na ānaśuḥ* — do not attain; *uta* — and; *sindhavaḥ* — rivers; *na* — do not (attain); *paṇayaḥ* — the Asuras too; *na* — do not attain (nor) *magham* — (your) wealth.

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha).** O Mitra and Varuṇa, you are lords of food with wealth. Therefore you, the guides of the sacrifice, come to us with the help of your wisdom and your protection, and bring us great and wealthy food. Neither days nor nights, nor the flowing rivers, nor the Asuras attain your divine worthiness; nor do they attain your wealth. There are none in the three worlds who surpass you.

**English Translation (as printed; the page break falls mid-sentence).** You distribute food, accompanied by riches; you bestow upon us, leaders (of sacrifice); wealth, ample, and defended by your wise provisions

### Printed p. 514  (PDF 532)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 151".)*

*(English Translation continued:)* the days with the nights have not attained your divinity; neither have the rivers, nor have the Asuras, and they have not obtained (your) wealth.

**विशेषविषयाः (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Special Topics).** **मायाभिः** — *māyeti prajñānāma; māyā, vayunam iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt* (Ni. 3-9 [?]): the *Nirukta*-author, quoting the Ṛk beginning *māyābhir mama tu yajñiyānām* (10-83-3 [?]), explains *sa eva prajñām tv etāṃ manyante*, and so shows that the word *māyā* has the meaning "wisdom, intelligence" (Ni. 2-26 [?]). Moreover:

> शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यद्विषुरूपे अहनी द्यौरिवासि ।
> विश्वा हि माया अवसि स्वधावो भद्रा ते पूषन्निह रातिरस्तु ॥

> *śukraṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyadviṣurūpe ahanī dyaurivāsi |*
> *viśvā hi māyā avasi svadhāvo bhadrā te pūṣanniha rātirastu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-58-1.) Quoting this Ṛk (Ni. 11-[?]), here too he takes the word *māyā* to mean "wisdom". This word is used in the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā some ninety times. It may be said broadly that it is used in four chief senses: as a supernatural creative power, as a merely material power, as trickery, or as magic (*indrajāla-vidyā*). It may also be said to be derived from the root *mā* in the sense of creation. This word, indicating the special power of Mitra-Varuṇa, is an epithet of them in many places:

> ऋतस्य बुध्न उषसामिषण्यन् वृषा मही रोदसी आ विवेश ।
> मही मित्रस्य वरुणस्य माया चन्द्रेव भानुं वि दधे पुरुत्रा ॥

> *ṛtasya budhna uṣasāmiṣaṇyan vṛṣā mahī rodasī ā viveśa |*
> *mahī mitrasya varuṇasya māyā candreva bhānuṃ vi dadhe purutrā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-61-7.) Here Uṣas is the supernatural creation of Mitra-Varuṇa.

> माया वां मित्रावरुणा दिविश्रिता सूर्यो ज्योतिश्चरति चित्रमायुधम् ।
> तमभ्रेण वृष्ट्या गूहथो दिवि पर्जन्य द्रप्सा मधुमन्त ईरते ॥

> *māyā vāṃ mitrāvaruṇā diviśritā sūryo jyotiścarati citramāyudham |*
> *tamabhreṇa vṛṣṭyā gūhatho divi parjanya drapsā madhumanta īrate ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-4.) Here too the extraordinary wisdom and creative power of Mitra-Varuṇa are described. Likewise:

### Printed p. 515  (PDF 533)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 2 Va. 31" as printed, [?]; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

> पूर्वापरं चरतो मायया एतौ शिशू क्रीळन्तौ परि यातो अध्वरम् ।
> विश्वान्यन्यो भुवनाभिचष्ट ऋतूरन्यो विदधज्जायते पुनः ॥

> *pūrvāparaṃ carato māyayā etau śiśū krīḷantau pari yāto adhvaram |*
> *viśvānyanyo bhuvanābhicaṣṭa ṛtūranyo vidadhajjāyate punaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-18.) Here it is said that the Sun and the Moon move in the atmosphere by their special power of wisdom. Thus in many Ṛks this word shows the power of the gods to bring about the welfare of the world. But in some other places it is an epithet showing the power of the Asuras — deceit, fraud and the like.

> त्वं मायाभिरनवद्य मायिनं श्रवस्यता मनसा वृत्रमर्दयः ।
> त्वामिन्नरो वृणते गविष्टिषु त्वां विश्वासु हव्यास्विष्टिषु ॥

> *tvaṃ māyābhiranavadya māyinaṃ śravasyatā manasā vṛtramardayaḥ |*
> *tvāminnaro vṛṇate gaviṣṭiṣu tvāṃ viśvāsu havyāsviṣṭiṣu ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-147-2.) Here, the deceitful enemy was destroyed "by your special wisdom", so Indra is praised. In the same way the epithet *māyābhiḥ* in the present Ṛk shows the extraordinary power of Mitra-Varuṇa; by this wisdom they have obtained power beyond that of the *sindhus* [sic: as printed], the rivers and the Asuras, so it is explained.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 9; grammar pages 515–516, noted briefly).** *dadhāthe* (root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *laṭ* in the Veda; 2nd dual; *tiṅ*: *nighāta*); *narā* (root *ṇī nayane*; *kvip ca* — *kvip*; before the dual ending *ṛto jāsvanāmasthānayoḥ* … guṇa; *supāṃ sulug* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) *ā* for the ending); *itaūti* (*itaḥ ūtiḥ yasya tat*; *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the first member keeps its accent); *māhinam* (root *maha pūjāyām*; *mahe rinan ca* (Uṇ. Sū. 3-[?]) *inan* suffix; *ato 'pupadhāyāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116) *vṛddhi* of the penultimate; by *vyatyaya*, *ā* is *udātta*); *devatvam* (*devānāṃ bhāvaḥ devatvam*; *tasya bhāvas tvatalau* (Pā. Sū. 5-1-119) *tva* suffix in the sense of state; suffix accent: final *udātta*).

## Sūkta 152

### Printed p. 516 (continued; PDF 534)

*(The Kannada heading reads "The 152nd Sūkta".)*

*(Anukramaṇī, Sanskrit; not rendered in English. Gist: the sūkta of seven Ṛks beginning "Yuvaṃ vastrāṇi" is the twelfth sūkta, of Dīrghatamas, Triṣṭubh by the general rule, Mitrāvaruṇa deity "as said"; use is by indication; the first Ṛk is the offering-verse of the Mitrāvaruṇa animal sacrifice and is also used at the *samāvartana* when new garments are put on, by the Āśvalāyana sūtras cited.)*

> युवं वस्त्राणीति सप्तर्चं द्वादशं सूक्तं दैर्घतमसम् । अनादेशपरिभाषया त्रैष्टुभम् । मैत्रावरुणं हीत्युक्तत्वात् । सूक्तविनियोगो लैङ्गिकः । मैत्रावरुणे पशुवाजयाज्या । प्रदानानामिति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । युवं वस्त्राणि पीवसा वसाथे प्र बाहवा सिसृतं जीवसे नः । आ. ३-८ [?] इति । सैव समावर्तने नववस्त्रधारणे विनियोक्ता । सूत्रितं च । युवं वस्त्राणि पीवसा वसाथे इत्यहते वाससी आच्छाद्य । आ. गृ. ३-९-८ [?] इति ॥

> *yuvaṃ vastrāṇīti saptarcaṃ dvādaśaṃ sūktaṃ dairghatamasam | anādeśaparibhāṣayā traiṣṭubham | maitrāvaruṇaṃ hītyuktatvāt | sūktaviniyogo laiṅgikaḥ | maitrāvaruṇe paśuvājayājyā | pradānānāmiti khaṇḍe sūtritam | yuvaṃ vastrāṇi pīvasā vasāthe pra bāhavā sisṛtaṃ jīvase naḥ | ā. 3-8 [?] iti | saiva samāvartane navavastradhāraṇe viniyoktā | sūtritaṃ ca | yuvaṃ vastrāṇi pīvasā vasāthe ityahate vāsasī ācchādya | ā. gṛ. 3-9-8 [?] iti ‖*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The sūkta *yuvaṃ vastrāṇi* is the twelfth sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Dīrghatamas, son of Ucathya. As stated before, Mitra-Varuṇa are the deities. The metre is Triṣṭubh. The use is by indication; in the animal sacrifice made to Mitra-Varuṇa, the first Ṛk of this sūkta is to be used as the *yājyā* mantra at the *vapā* offering, as the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra explains in the section *pradānānām*, by the sūtra *yuvaṃ vastrāṇi pīvasā vasāthe pra bāhavā sisṛtaṃ jīvase naḥ* (Ā. 3-8 [?]). And the same Ṛk is prescribed, in the household rite called *samāvartana*, to be recited when putting on a new garment, by the Āśvalāyana sūtra *yuvaṃ vastrāṇi pīvasā vasāthe ity ahate vāsasī ācchādya* (Ā. Gṛ. 3-9-8 [?]).

**॥ ओम् ॥**

**Sūkta 152** — Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 21, Sūkta 152; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 32 [?]. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Ṛṣi: Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Devatā: Mitrāvaruṇau. Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*(Gist: you two wear robust garments, or garments of abundant radiance; your creations are flawless; you destroy all untruths and join us to sacrifice and its fruit. Small type, read with doubt.)*

> हे मित्रावरुणौ पीवसा पीवसा [?] युवं युवाम् । यद्वा । पीवसा पीवसानि [?]च्छिन्नानि वस्त्राणि वसाथे आच्छादयेथः । यद्वा । पीवसा स्थूलेन प्रभूतेन तेजसा वस्त्राणि दधाथे । अविच्छिन्नानि वस्त्रस्थानीयानि तेजांसि धारयेथ इत्यर्थः । किंच युवयोः सर्गाः सृष्टयः अच्छिद्रा अच्छिन्ना मन्तवो मननीयाश्च । उद्वौ [?] युवां विश्वा विश्वानि सर्वाण्यनृतान्यसत्यान्यप्रियाणि पापानि अवातिरतं नाशयतम् । विश्वेत्यत्र संहितायामुत्वक [?] इति प्रकृतिभावो ह्रस्वश्च । ऋतेन फलेन तत्सत्यभावेन [?] यज्ञेन वा सचेथे । संगच्छेथे । अस्मभ्यं योजयथ इत्यर्थः ॥

> *he mitrāvaruṇau pīvasā pīvasā [?] yuvaṃ yuvām | yadvā | pīvasā pīvasāni [?]cchinnāni vastrāṇi vasāthe ācchādayethaḥ | yadvā | pīvasā sthūlena prabhūtena tejasā vastrāṇi dadhāthe | avicchinnāni vastrasthānīyāni tejāṃsi dhārayetha ityarthaḥ | kiṃca yuvayoḥ sargāḥ sṛṣṭayaḥ acchidrā acchinnā mantavo mananīyāśca | udvau [?] yuvāṃ viśvā viśvāni sarvāṇyanṛtānyasatyānyapriyāṇi pāpāni avātirataṃ nāśayatam | viśvetyatra saṃhitāyāmutvaka [?] iti prakṛtibhāvo hrasvaśca | ṛtena phalena tatsatyabhāvena [?] yajñena vā sacethe | saṃgacchethe | asmabhyaṃ yojayatha ityarthaḥ ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha).** *mitrāvaruṇā* — O Mitra-Varuṇa; *pīvasā* — robust-bodied; *yuvam* — you two; [or *yuvam* — you two; *pīvasā* — unwearing, fit for covering; *vastrāṇi* — garments; or *pīvasā* — with abundant (radiance), (radiant) *vastrāṇi* — garments;] *vasāthe* — you wear; *yuvoḥ* — of you two; *sargāḥ* — creations; *acchidrā* — flawless; *mantavaḥ ha* — and charming, are they not; (you two) *viśvā* — all; *anṛtāni* — untruths or unpleasant sins; *ava atiratam* — destroy; *ṛtena* — with the sacrifice or its fruit; *sacethe* — join (us).

### Printed p. 518  (PDF 536)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 152".)*

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha).** O Mitra and Varuṇa, robust-bodied as you are, you wear garments of abundant radiance. Your natures are flawless and charming. You destroy all sins; you join us with the sacrifice, so that we enjoy its fruit.

**English Translation (as printed).** Robust Mitra and Varuna, you wear vestiments (of light); your natures are to be regarded as without defect; you annihilate all untruths; you associate (us) with sacrifice.

**विशेषविषयाः (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Special Topics).** Sāyaṇa shows the construction of the word *pīvasā* in three ways. First, as an epithet of *yuvam*, so that Mitra-Varuṇa are addressed. Second, as an epithet of *vastrāṇi*, with two senses: *pīvasā vastrāṇi pīnā acchinnāni ācchādanayogyāni vāsāṃsi vasāthe* — "you wear garments fit for covering, that do not tear" — one sense; or *pīvasā sthūlena prabhūtena tejasā vastrāṇi dadhāthe; avicchinnāni vastrasthānīyāni tejāṃsi dhārayetha ity arthaḥ* — "with abundant radiance you wear garments: you bear unbroken splendours in the place of garments" — another, namely that Mitra-Varuṇa wear garments abundant and made of their own radiance. Generally the word *pīvas* is used in the sense "stout, thick":

> अग्नेर्वर्म परि गोभिर्व्ययस्व सं प्रोर्णुष्व पीवसा मेदसा च ।
> नेत्त्वा धृष्णुर्हरसा जर्हृषाणो दधृग्विधक्ष्यन् पर्यङ्ख्याः ॥

> *agnervarma pari gobhirvyayasva saṃ prorṇuṣva pīvasā medasā ca |*
> *nettvā dhṛṣṇurharasā jarhṛṣāṇo dadhṛgvidhakṣyan paryaṅkhyāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-16-7 [?]; reading of the second line uncertain.) In such Ṛks everywhere *pīvasā* is explained as *sthūlena*. In the present Ṛk it means garments very extensive and made of radiance.

**अव अतिरतम्** — *avatiratiḥ vadhakarmā*: "you destroy untruths, unpleasant sins" is the sense. In sum the form of Mitra-Varuṇa is made of radiance; their creations are flawless and charming; they destroy untruths and spread truth and purity in the world.

Sū. 7-2-88): *āva* is prescribed only in the language, so none here); *vastrāṇi* (root *vasa ācchādane*; *sarvadhātubhyaḥ ṣṭran* (Uṇ. Sū. 6-1-70 [?]) *luk* of *śi*); *vasāthe* (root *vasa ācchādane*; *adādi*; *ātmanepada*; *laṭ* 2nd dual; the form *vasāthe*; *tiṅ*: *nighāta*); *yuvoḥ* (*yuṣmad*; genitive dual: *supāṃ suluk* … *yoci* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-[?]) *yatva* does not occur; *śeṣe lopaḥ* loss of *ṭi* (*ad*); *ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-5) *udātta*); *acchidrā* (*na cchidram acchidram*; *tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-128) *prakṛtibhāva*; Vedic shortening); *mitrāvaruṇā* (*devatādvandve ca* (Pā. Sū. 6-3-26) *ānaṅ* in the *dvandva*; dual: *supāṃ suluk* *ā*; *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19) *nighāta*).

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्रिरश्रिं हन्ति चतुरश्रिरुग्रो देवनिदो ह प्रथमा अजूर्यन् ॥ २ ॥

> *etaccana tvo vi ciketadeṣāṃ satyo mantraḥ kaviśasta ṛghāvān |*
> *triraśriṃ hanti caturaśrirugro devanido ha prathamā ajūryan ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> एतत् । चन । त्वः । वि । चिकेतत् । एषाम् । सत्यः । मन्त्रः । कविऽशस्तः । ऋघावान् ।
> त्रिःऽअश्रिम् । हन्ति । चतुःऽअश्रिः । उग्रः । देवऽनिदः । ह । प्रथमाः । अजूर्यन् ॥ २ ॥

> *etat | cana | tvaḥ | vi | ciketat | eṣām | satyaḥ | mantraḥ | kavi 'śastaḥ | ṛghāvān |*
> *triḥ 'aśrim | hanti | catuḥ 'aśriḥ | ugraḥ | deva 'nidaḥ | ha | prathamāḥ | ajūryan ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*(Gist: among these two (or among the pious) one truthful, wise, praised, slaying one performs this deed of power; though armed with three- or four-edged weapons he kills; revilers of the gods, strong at first, decay by themselves. Small type, read with doubt.)*

> एषां मित्रावरुणयोर्मध्ये । बहुवचनं पूजार्थम् । यद्वा । तदनुचरापेक्षया बहुवचनम् । एतयोर्मध्ये त्वः श्रेष्ठस्य [?] कश्चित् एक एव यजमानस्य सामर्थ्यरूपं कर्म वि चिकेतत् । विशेषेण चेतति । अनुतिष्ठतीत्यर्थः । स विशेष्यते । स एकः सत्यः अबाध्यः सत्सु भवो वा मन्त्रः मननीयः [?] कविशस्तः कविभिर्मेधाविभिः शंसनीयः ऋघावान् हिंसकः शत्रूणाम् । अनेन वक्ष्यमाणस्य सामर्थ्यस्य सम्भावयिता प्रतिपादितवदित्युत्कृतम् [?] । किं तदित्याशङ्कायां । त्रिरश्रिम् । अश्रित्रयोपेतमायुधं त्रिरश्रिस्तद्वन्तम् [?] । मत्वर्थो लुप्यते । उपलक्षणमेतत् सर्वायुधसंपन्नमित्यर्थः । एतन्नामानं वा । चतुरश्रिस्तोपै [?] चतुरस्रायुधवान् । न केवलमायुधसामर्थ्यं किंत्वुग्रः स्वयमुग्रबलो हन्ति । हिनस्ति बलं शत्रुम् । किंच युवयोरेकस्यैव सामर्थ्येन देवनिदो ह देवनिन्दका एव प्रथमाः समर्थाः सन्तोऽपि अजूर्यन् स्वयमेव जीर्णा भवन्ति ॥ जीर्यतेः क्र्यन् बहुलं छन्दसीत्यत्वं [?] ॥ युवयोर्मध्ये एकोऽपि महाबलः । मिलितयोस्तु सामर्थ्ये किमु वक्तव्यमिति भावः ॥ अथवा । एषां युवयोरेतेषामुत्[?] उत्तरत्र वक्ष्यमाणं सामर्थ्यमेकः सत्यादिलक्षणो वि चिकेतत् विशेषेण जानाति । शेषं पूर्ववत् ॥

> *eṣāṃ mitrāvaruṇayormadhye | bahuvacanaṃ pūjārtham | yadvā | tadanucarāpekṣayā bahuvacanam | etayormadhye tvaḥ śreṣṭhasya [?] kaścit eka eva yajamānasya sāmarthyarūpaṃ karma vi ciketat | viśeṣeṇa cetati | anutiṣṭhatītyarthaḥ | sa viśeṣyate | sa ekaḥ satyaḥ abādhyaḥ satsu bhavo vā mantraḥ mananīyaḥ [?] kaviśastaḥ kavibhirmedhāvibhiḥ śaṃsanīyaḥ ṛghāvān hiṃsakaḥ śatrūṇām | anena vakṣyamāṇasya sāmarthyasya sambhāvayitā pratipāditavadityutkṛtam [?] | kiṃ tadityāśaṅkāyāṃ | triraśrim | aśritrayopetamāyudhaṃ triraśristadvantam [?] | matvartho lupyate | upalakṣaṇametat sarvāyudhasaṃpannamityarthaḥ | etannāmānaṃ vā | caturaśristopai [?] caturasrāyudhavān | na kevalamāyudhasāmarthyaṃ kiṃtvugraḥ svayamugrabalo hanti | hinasti balaṃ śatrum | kiṃca yuvayorekasyaiva sāmarthyena devanido ha devanindakā eva prathamāḥ samarthāḥ santo 'pi ajūryan svayameva jīrṇā bhavanti ‖ jīryateḥ kryan bahulaṃ chandasītyatvaṃ [?] ‖ yuvayormadhye eko 'pi mahābalaḥ | militayostu sāmarthye kimu vaktavyamiti bhāvaḥ ‖ athavā | eṣāṃ yuvayoreteṣāmut[?] uttaratra vakṣyamāṇaṃ sāmarthyamekaḥ satyādilakṣaṇo vi ciketat viśeṣeṇa jānāti | śeṣaṃ pūrvavat ‖*

### Printed p. 521  (PDF 539)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 2 Va. 32" as printed, [?]; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha).** *eṣām* — among these Mitra-Varuṇa (or in the company of other devotees); *satyaḥ* — truth in form (or following the path of truth, or belonging to the company of good men); *mantraḥ* — thoughtful; *kaviśastaḥ* — praised by the wise; *ṛghāvān* — one who harms (enemies); *tvaḥ* — one alone; *etat* — this deed accompanied by power; *vi ciketat* — performs in a special manner; (what is it?) *trirasrim* — even one furnished with all weapons (or the enemy called Trirasri); *caturasriḥ* — having still more weapons [as printed, reading uncertain]; *ugraḥ* — formidable; *hanti* — slays; *devanido ha* — and the revilers of the gods; *prathamāḥ* — though powerful at the start; *ajūryan* — (in the end, of themselves) waste away.

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha).** Among these Mitra-Varuṇa, one — of truthful nature, thoughtful, praised by the wise, a harmer of enemies — performs this deed of power in a special manner. For example, though the enemy be furnished with all weapons, he, with still more weapons and formidable, slays the enemy. And although revilers of the gods are powerful at the beginning, through his influence they waste away of themselves at the end.

**English Translation (as printed).** He amongst those (who are your followers), who observes truth, who is considerate, who is commended by the wise, who is able to (inflict) harm carefully weighs (the means whereby), fierce and well-armed, he slays (a foe) less efficiently accoutred, and (by which) the revilers of the gods, however mighty, may perish.

**विशेषविषयाः (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Special Topics).** **सत्यः** — *ābādhyaḥ satsu bhavo vā*: "one beyond harm, or one who is among the good" — the word gives its purport. Though he must be beyond harm, he cannot be of an untrue nature; he must be of the form of truth and follow the path of truth. The word *satya* throughout the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā is used with a sense that sets forth a superior, moral worth and power. The actions done by people of such excellent worth are also of the nature of truth. The *Nirukta*-author too has given a derivation of the word *satya* expressing this meaning,

### Printed p. 522  (PDF 540)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 152".)*

> सत्यं कस्मात् सत्सु तायते सत्त्वभवनं भवतीति वा ।

> *satyaṃ kasmāt satsu tāyate sattvabhavanaṃ bhavatīti vā |*

(Ni. 3-13 [?].) "It spreads among the good, or arises among the good; therefore it is called *satya*," the *Nirukta*-author explains. According to this derivation, since the fruit of the nature of truth too must come to the good, the idea that good intentions have a fruit that is good, fit for good works, is suggested by this Ṛk's description. The difference between the God-fearing man who follows the path of truth and the God-reviler who follows the path of untruth is shown here: however great the power of the God-reviler at the start, it wastes away of itself at the end, while the capacities of the God-fearing man increase, and that increase is the fruit of his truthful conduct. So, since here the word *satya* is used both in the sense of action and in the sense of fruit, one must explain what universal principle this idea reflects in both settings.

> ते देवा उत्सृज्यानृतं सत्यमन्वालेभिरे ।

> *te devā utsṛjyānṛtaṃ satyamanvālebhire |*

(Śa. Brā. 9-5-1-13 [?].)

> तद्यत्त्रय्यै [?] तत्सत्यम् । त्रयी सा विद्या ते देवा अब्रुवन् यज्ञं कृण्वेदं सत्यं तेनामाहा इति [?] ।

> *tadyattrayyai [?] tatsatyam | trayī sā vidyā te devā abruvan yajñaṃ kṛṇvedaṃ satyaṃ tenāmāhā iti [?] |*

(Śa. Brā. 9-5-1-19 [?].) The gods gave up untruth and firmly held to truth. Since the Vedas, called *trayī*, are themselves of the nature of truth, the gods hoped, "Let us perform the actions prescribed by the Veda and keep truth." Thus, besides showing the real connection between truth and conduct, the passage implies that by such pure actions one may obtain full length of life, all prosperity and welfare.

> नाभिर्ह तस्य सप्रथा इति । सत्यं ना ऋतं वा ऋतं सत्यस्य नाभिः सप्रथा इत्येषैवैकदाह स नो विश्वायुः सप्रथा इति स नः सर्वायुः इत्येषैवैकदाह ।

> *nābhirha tasya saprathā iti | satyaṃ nā ṛtaṃ vā ṛtaṃ satyasya nābhiḥ saprathā ityeṣaivaikadāha sa no viśvāyuḥ saprathā iti sa naḥ sarvāyuḥ ityeṣaivaikadāha |*

(Ṛ. Brā. 14-3-14 [?].) By such explanations, showing the identity of the world-order with truth, it is indicated that by following such truth and performing truthful actions one obtains full length of life as fruit, even the joy of liberation [as printed, uncertain]; the causal relation between truth and truthful action is made known.

*(Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued.)* … it is necessary to know even for truthful conduct the world-order and the nature of the deities who are its cause; and that this knowledge too is possible only through truth is explained in detail in many contexts.

> सत्यं तदिन्द्रो दशभिर्दशग्वैः सूर्यं विवेद तमसि क्षियन्तम् ॥

> *sakhā ha yatra sakhibhirnagmabhirjñātvā satyebhirgā anugman |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-31-[?], numerals uncertain.)

> स इद्देवानां सधमाद आसन्नृतावानः कवयः पूर्व्यासः ।
> गूळ्हं ज्योतिः पितरो अन्वविन्दन् सत्यमन्त्रा अजयन्नुषासम् ॥

> *sa iddevānāṃ sadhamāda āsannṛtāvānaḥ kavayaḥ pūrvyāsaḥ |*
> *gūḷhaṃ jyotiḥ pitaro anvavindan satyamantrā ajayannuṣāsam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-76-4.)

> अधा यथा नः पितरः परासः प्रत्नासो अग्न ऋतमाशुषाणाः ।
> शुचीदयन् दीधितिमुक्थशासः क्षामा भिन्दन्तो अरुणीरप व्रन् ॥

> *adhā yathā naḥ pitaraḥ parāsaḥ pratnāso agna ṛtamāśuṣāṇāḥ |*
> *śucīdayan dīdhitimukthaśāsaḥ kṣāmā bhindanto aruṇīrapa vran ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-2-16.) In all such Ṛks, passages are numerous which tell how the sages also, knowing the nature of the truthful deities and performing the rites, obtained wealth, and with them goes the prayer that "by truth may it be well with us". The truthful nature of Agni and other deities, whose law is truth, is described in such prayers as "as our fathers, by truthful sacrificial conduct, obtained whatever fruits, so now too may the fruits of our rites be true…" [as printed, partly uncertain].

> आजो न क्षां दाधार पृथिवीं तस्तम्भ द्यां मन्त्रेभिः सत्यैः ।

> *ājo na kṣāṃ dādhāra pṛthivīṃ tastambha dyāṃ mantrebhiḥ satyaiḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-67-3 [?].)

> कविमग्निमुपस्तुहि सत्यधर्माणमध्वरे ।
> देवममीवचातनम् ॥

> *kavimagnimupastuhi satyadharmāṇamadhvare |*
> *devamamīvacātanam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-7 [?].)

> देवो न यः सविता सत्यमन्मा क्रत्वा निपाति वृजनानि विश्वा ।
> पुरुप्रशस्तो अमतिर्न सत्य आत्मेव शेवो दिधिषाय्यो भूत् ॥

> *devo na yaḥ savitā satyamanmā kratvā nipāti vṛjanāni viśvā |*
> *purupraśasto amatirna satya ātmeva śevo didhiṣāyyo bhūt ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-[?]-[?].) In many such places it is shown that Agni and the other deities uphold earth and the other worlds, and carry out the protection of the worlds, by *truth*, and that men too should follow that path of truth.

### Printed p. 524  (PDF 542)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 152".)*

If one follows this path, *tvaḥ cana etat vi ciketat* — one man alone, without needing the help of others, endowed with every capacity, wins the victory: this assurance is given in the present Ṛk.

**ऋघावान्** — for the word *ṛghā*, Monier Williams's *Dictionary* gives "violence, passion"; the purport may be "a violent power". The word *ṛghāvān* occurs not only in this Ṛk but also in

> इन्द्रः सुशिप्रो मघवा तरुत्रो महाव्रातस्तुविकूर्मिर्ऋघावान् ।
> यदुग्रो धा बाधितो मर्त्येषु क्व त्या ते वृषभ वीर्याणि ॥

> *indraḥ suśipro maghavā tarutro mahāvrātastuvikūrmirṛghāvān |*
> *yadugro dhā bādhito martyeṣu kva tyā te vṛṣabha vīryāṇi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-30-9 [?].) In that Ṛk too, as in the present one, Sāyaṇa explains it *śatruviṣaye hiṃsāvān* — "one capable of harming enemies"; the stress may lie on the power to inflict harm.

**त्वः** — *tva iti vinigrahārthīyaṃ sarvanāmānupāttam arthānām eteke* (Ni. 1-7 [?]): the *Nirukta*-author quotes

> ऋचां त्वः पोषमास्ते पुपुष्वान् गायत्रं त्वो गायति शक्वरीषु ।
> ब्रह्मा त्वो वदति जातविद्यां यज्ञस्य मात्रां वि मिमीत उ त्वः ॥

> *ṛcāṃ tvaḥ poṣamāste pupuṣvān gāyatraṃ tvo gāyati śakvarīṣu |*
> *brahmā tvo vadati jātavidyāṃ yajñasya mātrāṃ vi mimīta u tvaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-71-11.) and explains the word *tvaḥ* here as "one" (*ekaḥ*). Besides, *athāpi samuccayārthe bhavati*: the word is also used in the sense of "and" (Ni. 1-9 [?]).

**त्रिरश्रिम्** — Sāyaṇa gives two senses: "an enemy with three edges (*aśri*)", or "an enemy by the name Triraśri". No authority is found for this word as the proper name of a person.

**देवनिदः** — the *Nirukta*-author:

> स्वयं सो अस्मदा निदो वध्रैरजेत दुर्मतिम् ।
> अव स्रवेदघशंसोऽवतरमव क्षुद्रमिव स्रवेत् ॥

> *svayaṃ so asmadā nido vadhrairajeta durmatim |*
> *ava sravedaghaśaṃso 'vataramava kṣudramiva sravet ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-38-5 [?].)

### Printed p. 525  (PDF 543)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 2 Va. 32" as printed, [?]; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Grammar page, noted briefly.)*

Explaining that Ṛk, he takes *nidaḥ* as *nindhitāraṃ* — "those who blame" — from the root *nid* in the sense of contempt. In the present Ṛk *devanidaḥ* means "those who revile the gods".

**अजूर्यन्** — *svayam eva jīrṇā bhavanti*: they decay of themselves.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 2; noted briefly).** *ciketat* (root *kita jñāne*; *laṭ*, *tip* → *e*; *iketi lopaś ca*, *letoḍāṭau* (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94) *aḍāgama* … *śap* doubling; *laghūpadhaguṇa*; *nighāta*); *tvaḥ* (*viśāmāt*?: the plural in the sense of worship, or by reference to followers); *satyaḥ* (*sat* + *bhave*; *bhave chandasi* (Pā. Sū. 4-4-110) *yat* suffix; suffix accent); *kaviśastaḥ* (root *śaṃsu stutau*; *kta*; *anidit* — loss of the nasal; *kavibhiḥ śastaḥ*, the *kṛdutara* member keeps the stem accent); *ṛghāvān* (root *ṛgha hiṃsāyām*; *ṛghā asya asti*; *matup*); *triraśrim* (*trayaḥ aśrayaḥ yasya tat triraśri*; *tadasya asti*; in the Veda *matvartha* suffix dropped); *hanti* (root *han hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *adādi*; *laṭ* 3rd sg.; *nighāta*); *ugraḥ* (root *ujha samavāye*; *ṛjendrāgra*… (Uṇ. Sū. 2-[?]) *ra*, as a *nipātana*; *cakāra* to *gakāra* by *vyatyaya*; suffix accent: final *udātta*); *devanidaḥ* (*devān nindanti*; root *nidi kutsāyām*; *kvip ca* — *kvip*; *āgamānuśāsanam anityam* — *num* augment; the *kṛdutara* member keeps the stem accent; nominative pl.); *ajūryan* (root *jṝṣ vayohānau*; *laṅ* in the Veda; 3rd pl. *jhi* → *ant*, loss of the final; *divādibhyaḥ śyan* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-69) *śyan*; *bahulaṃ chandasi* … *ut* for the root; *hali ca* lengthening; *nighāta*). ‖ 2 ‖

### Printed p. 526  (PDF 544)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 152".)*

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अपादेति प्रथमा पद्वतीनां कस्तद्वां मित्रावरुणा चिकेत ।
> गर्भो भारं भरत्या चिदस्य ऋतं पिपर्त्यनृतं नि तारीत् ॥ ३ ॥

> *apādeti prathamā padvatīnāṃ kastadvāṃ mitrāvaruṇā ciketa |*
> *garbho bhāraṃ bharatyā cidasya ṛtaṃ pipartyanṛtaṃ ni tārīt ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अपात् । एति । प्रथमा । पत्ऽवतीनाम् । कः । तत् । वाम् । मित्रावरुणा । आ । चिकेत ।
> गर्भः । भारम् । भरति । आ । चित् । अस्य । ऋतम् । पिपर्ति । अनृतम् । नि । तारीत् ॥ ३ ॥

> *apāt | eti | prathamā | pat 'vatīnām | kaḥ | tat | vām | mitrāvaruṇā | ā | ciketa |*
> *garbhaḥ | bhāram | bharati | ā | cit | asya | ṛtam | piparti | anṛtam | ni | tārīt ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*(Gist: the footless Dawn goes first of all footed beings — who understands that this is your work? And your embryo, the Sun, bears the burden of this world, fills it with truth and removes untruth. Small type, read with doubt.)*

> हे मित्रावरुणा मित्रावरुणौ पद्वतीनां मनुष्यादीनां प्रजानां प्रथमा प्रथमभाविन्यपात् पादरहितोषाः । प्रतिदिनं सूर्यचन्द्रादिवत् स्वस्वाः [?] परिभ्रमणाभावात् सूर्यगमनेनैव स्वगमनादपादिति चैती [?] । इत्युपचर्यते । तत्प्रादुर्भावं [?] युवयोः प्रसिद्धं कर्म कः आ चिकेते । कः अभिमुखेन जानाति ॥ कित ज्ञाने ॥ तत्प्रत्यक्षं त्वमित्यर्थः । मित्रावरुणयोरहोरात्रदेवत्वादहोरात्रयोरेतरा [?] स्थानत्वादित्यर्थः । किंचास्य लोकस्य भारं निर्वाहं गर्भो युवयोर्गर्भस्थानीयः शिशुरादित्यः । अहोरात्रयोर्मध्यकाल उत्पत्तेरुभयोरेव मित्रावरुणात्मकत्वात् । अहोरात्रे वै मित्रावरुणाविति श्रुतेः । स आभरति आहरति [?]: समानान्यान् [?] हरति नास्य भारं जाड्यं । चिदित्यवधारणे । तक्ष्ण [?] तमुच्चैः ऋतं सत्यं जगते प्रकाशगमनादिरूपं पिपर्ति पूरयति । अनृतमुक्तविलक्षणमन्धकारं गमनादिनिरोधं च नि तारीत् नितरां तारयति नामयति नाशयतीत्यर्थः । शिशोर्जगद्भारवहनरूपं कर्म युष्मत्कर्मानुकृतीति [?] ॥

> *he mitrāvaruṇā mitrāvaruṇau padvatīnāṃ manuṣyādīnāṃ prajānāṃ prathamā prathamabhāvinyapāt pādarahitoṣāḥ | pratidinaṃ sūryacandrādivat svasvāḥ [?] paribhramaṇābhāvāt sūryagamanenaiva svagamanādapāditi caitī [?] | ityupacaryate | tatprādurbhāvaṃ [?] yuvayoḥ prasiddhaṃ karma kaḥ ā cikete | kaḥ abhimukhena jānāti ‖ kita jñāne ‖ tatpratyakṣaṃ tvamityarthaḥ | mitrāvaruṇayorahorātradevatvādahorātrayoretarā [?] sthānatvādityarthaḥ | kiṃcāsya lokasya bhāraṃ nirvāhaṃ garbho yuvayorgarbhasthānīyaḥ śiśurādityaḥ | ahorātrayormadhyakāla utpatterubhayoreva mitrāvaruṇātmakatvāt | ahorātre vai mitrāvaruṇāviti śruteḥ | sa ābharati āharati [?]: samānānyān [?] harati nāsya bhāraṃ jāḍyaṃ | cidityavadhāraṇe | takṣṇa [?] tamuccaiḥ ṛtaṃ satyaṃ jagate prakāśagamanādirūpaṃ piparti pūrayati | anṛtamuktavilakṣaṇamandhakāraṃ gamanādinirodhaṃ ca ni tārīt nitarāṃ tārayati nāmayati nāśayatītyarthaḥ | śiśorjagadbhāravahanarūpaṃ karma yuṣmatkarmānukṛtīti [?] ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha).** *mitrāvaruṇā* — O Mitra-Varuṇa; *padvatīnām* — of footed beings such as men; *prathamā* — the first-going herald; *apāt* — the footless goddess Uṣas; *tat* — this truth; *vām* — your work (that it is); *kaḥ* — who; *ā ciketa* — fully understands; (and moreover) *asya* — of this world; *bhāram* — the burden of its upkeep; *garbhaḥ* — the infant in (your) womb, the Sun; *ā bharati cit* — bears completely; *ṛtam* — truth (of light etc.) for the world; *pipartti* — fills; *anṛtam* — the untruth of the form of darkness; *ni tārīt* — destroys.

### Printed p. 527  (PDF 545)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 2 Va. 32" as printed, [?]; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha).** O Mitra and Varuṇa, who can understand that this truth — that the footless goddess Uṣas is the herald, the first of all beings with feet, men and the rest — is your work? And, filling the world with the truth of light and the like and destroying the untruth of the form of darkness, the Sun, the infant in the womb of you two, bears and fully carries the burden of this world's upkeep.

**English Translation (as printed; heading misprinted "English Tranlation").** Who knows, Mitra and Varuna, that it is your doing, that the footless [sic: "footles s", split by line break] dawn is the precursor of footed beings; and that your infant (progeny, the sun), sustains the burthen of this (world): he diffuses (the) truth (of light) and disperses the falsehood (of darkness).

**विशेषविषयाः (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Special Topics).** **पद्वतीनां प्रथमा** — *pādavatīnāṃ manuṣyādīnāṃ prajānāṃ prathamabhāvinī*: she appears before all beings that move on earth or in the atmosphere, and wakes them.

> आ घा योषेव सूनर्युषा याति प्रभुञ्जती ।
> जरयन्ती वृजनं पद्वदीयत उत्पातयति पक्षिणः ॥

> *ā ghā yoṣeva sūnaryuṣā yāti prabhuñjatī |*
> *jarayantī vṛjanaṃ padvadīyata utpātayati pakṣiṇaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-48-5.) In such Ṛks it is indicated how Uṣas is described as appearing before the dawn and rousing all sleeping birds and moving creatures, as a housewife skilled in household work rises first of all and wakes the others.

**अपात्** — *pādarahitā uṣāḥ*; Sāyaṇa tells us that because, unlike the sun and the moon, she has no daily independent circuit of her own but joins her movement to the sun's rising, this epithet (*apāt*, footless) is used.

---

### Printed p. 528  (PDF 546)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 152".)*

**अस्य भारं गर्भो आ भरति चित्** — the infant in the womb of the two, the Sun, carries completely the whole burden of this world. *Ahorātrayor madhyakāle utpatteḥ tābhyām eva mitrāvaruṇātmakatvāt*: since it is born in the time between day and night, and is thereby of the nature of Mitra-Varuṇa.

> अहोरात्रे वै मित्रावरुणौ ।

> *ahorātre vai mitrāvaruṇau |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-10-1 [?].) By this scripture, Mitra is known as the deity presiding over day, and Varuṇa over night. These deities too:

> त्री रोचना वरुण त्रीरुत द्यून् त्रीणि मित्र धारयथो रजांसि ।
> वावृधानावमतिं क्षत्रियस्यानु व्रतं रक्षमाणावजुर्यम् ॥

> *trī rocanā varuṇa trīruta dyūn trīṇi mitra dhārayatho rajāṃsi |*
> *vāvṛdhānāvamatiṃ kṣatriyasyānu vrataṃ rakṣamāṇāvajuryam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-69-1.) In such Ṛks Mitra-Varuṇa bear the burden of the three worlds; and that they are the cause of the Sun and other luminaries to give rise to the worlds and help the worldly activities is also described, and is here mentioned.

**ऋतम्** — *jagataḥ prakāśagamanādirūpaṃ satyam*: the word *ṛta* has many meanings, "sacrifice", "water" and others; here it means "truth". The truth that is reflected in the world's light and all kinds of activity has been explained. The Sun, the representative of Mitra-Varuṇa, is the cause of the growth of truth and the destruction of untruth.

**पिपर्ति** — *pipartti pṛ prīr iti syutra nigamau vā prīṇāti nigamau vā* [as printed, uncertain]: "make grow" or "make obtain" — the use of these words in that sense was shown earlier on the authority of the *Nirukta* (Ni. 3-38 [?]).

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Ṛk 3; grammar pages 528–529, noted briefly).** *apāt* (*na vidyate pād yasya* — *apāt*; *bahuvrīhi*, *nañ subhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) final *udātta*); *eti* (root *iṇ gatau*; *laṭ* 3rd sg.; *nighāta*); *padvatīnām* (*pat pādo 'syāḥ asti*; *matup*; *ṛśyaḥ*-rule *ṛtvā* [?] (Pā. Sū. 6-1-[?]) *ma* to *va*; by *vyatyaya* the *matup* ending is *udātta*); *ciketa* (root *kita jñāne*; *chandasi liṭ*; 3rd sg., *ṇal* → *ā*…; reduplication; *nighāta*).

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> प्रयन्तमित्परि जारं कनीनां पश्यामसि नोपनिपद्यमानम् ।
> अनवपृग्णा वितता वसानं प्रियं मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धाम ॥ ४ ॥

> *prayantamitpari jāraṃ kanīnāṃ paśyāmasi nopanipadyamānam |*
> *anavapṛgṇā vitatā vasānaṃ priyaṃ mitrasya varuṇasya dhāma ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्रऽयन्तम् । इत् । परि । जारम् । कनीनाम् । पश्यामसि । न । उपऽनिपद्यमानम् ।
> अनवऽपृग्णा । विऽतता । वसानम् । प्रियम् । मित्रस्य । वरुणस्य । धाम ॥ ४ ॥

> *pra 'yantam | it | pari | jāram | kanīnām | paśyāmasi | na | upa 'nipadyamānam |*
> *anava 'pṛgṇā | vi 'tatā | vasānam | priyam | mitrasya | varuṇasya | dhāma ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*(Gist: we see the Sun, the lover of the maiden-like dawns, always going, never sitting down even for an instant, wearing unattached, wide-spread rays, the dear abode of Mitra and Varuṇa. Small type, read with doubt.)*

> कनीनां कमनीयानां दीप्तानां कन्याकास्थानीयानामुषसां [?] ॥ कनतेः कान्तिकर्मणः [?] ईप् [?] । कृदिकारात्केः [?] इति ङीप् । अमी कन्याशब्दस्य वा छान्दसो रूपं [?] ॥ तासां जारमाप्रियत्वं [?] प्रयन्तमित् प्रगच्छन्तमेव परि पश्यामसि । वयं परितः पश्यामः । उपनिपद्यमानं क्षणमात्रमपि निविश्यन्तं न पश्यामः । एतदेव तयोः सामर्थ्यम् ।

### Printed p. 530  (PDF 548)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; "Maṃ. 1 A. 21 Sū. 152".)*

*(Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, continued from p. 529:)*

> पुनस्तदेव विशेष्यते । अनवपृग्णानवपृक्तानि अत एव विततानि तेजांसि वसानमाच्छादयन्तं प्रियं सर्वेषां प्रियभूतं मित्रस्य वरुणस्य च धाम तेजःस्थानभूतम् । यद्वा । धामेति संबध्यते । तयोः प्रेमस्थानम् । ईदृशमादित्यं युष्मदनुज्ञया संचरन्तं पश्यामसि ॥

> *punastadeva viśeṣyate | anavapṛgṇānavapṛktāni ata eva vitatāni tejāṃsi vasānamācchādayantaṃ priyaṃ sarveṣāṃ priyabhūtaṃ mitrasya varuṇasya ca dhāma tejaḥsthānabhūtam | yadvā | dhāmeti saṃbadhyate | tayoḥ premasthānam | īdṛśamādityaṃ yuṣmadanujñayā saṃcarantaṃ paśyāmasi ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha).** *kanīnām* — for the dawns, lovely in the form of maidens; *jāram* — the beloved; *anavapṛgṇā* — not clinging to one another; *vitatā* — widely spread rays; *vasānam* — wearing; *priyam* — wanted by all; *mitrasya varuṇasya* — for Mitra-Varuṇa; *dhāma* — being their abode; [or *priyam dhāma* — the dear abode (of Mitra-Varuṇa)]; (the Sun) *prayantam it* — as one always going; *pari paśyāmasi* — we always see; *upanipadyamānam* — (even for an instant) as sitting down to rest; *na* — we never see.

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha).** The Sun, the best beloved of the dawns that are lovely in maiden form, who wears rays spread widely and not clinging to one another, and who is the dear abode of Mitra-Varuṇa, we see always as one going. We never see him sit down to rest even for an instant.

**English Translation (as printed).** We behold the lover of the maiden (dawns), ever in movement, never resting for an instant, wearing inseparable and diffusive (radiance), the beloved abode of Mitra and Varuna.

**विशेषविषयाः (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Special Topics).** **कनीनाम्** — *kanyakānām*: *kanyā kamanīyā bhavati; kṣeyaṃ [?] neśam eti vā; kamane nānīyute iti vā; kanater vā syāt kāntikarmaṇaḥ* (Ni. 4-15 [?]) — the *Nirukta*-author gives this derivation of the word, either because the maiden is "to be desired", or because she "shines" (root *kan*, in the sense of brightness) [text partly illegible]. And (the Ṛk quoted at the top of the next page):
